Hades is an amazing experience. One that I wholeheartedly recommend. The art, the sound design, the characters and the narrative are all top notch.
Arguably some of the best I've seen in a game. It hits all the right notes for me.

I'm hesitant to call it an amazing game though.
Why?
Well, I have absolutely no complaints with the way the game handles. Everything is solid, controls are tight, there's no sliding. Action animations last just long enough that it usually doesn't interfere with you're need to control when things get hectic. If this was an Action RPG I'd say this is an amazing game.
It's not an Action RPG though.

It's a rouge-lite. (Like? What the difference is exactly still eludes me.)

You play through the same short amount of content repeatedly.
Room layout, and enemy variance is staggering when you first start playing.
Then you're on run 40. You've seen all the gameplay content the game has back at run 20. (Unless there are some really late game unlocks that shake things up that I haven't encountered yet)
Yeah there are minor variants that can be unlocked via the weapons and boons (or difficulty modifiers after your first clear). But they're subtle changes, really.

So here's the thing, you've got to enjoy doing the same thing over and over and over again.
This game really does rely on you getting hooked and invested in the characters and narrative.
If you like visual novels, or games with the "story rich" tag, and you enjoy rogue-like/lites then you will almost certainly love this game.

Hades however just doesn't have the depth of gameplay and game content to really sink your teeth into if that's the biggest thing you care about in a game.

So I'll sum Hades up like this.
It's a solid game. As far as I can tell bug free too! (When does that happen anymore?)
A good deal better than other games at a similar full price.
But if it's gameplay you care about I think you're only going to get ~15 odd hours out of the game. (less if you're good at these kinds of game)
If you get invested in the story and the characters though... oh you're in for a treat.

The game has a lot of hype. Well deserved too. It hits the sweet spot of a game that has bold and unique aesthetics, solid controls, engaging gameplay and almost no bugs. So it will appeal to, and be fun for a lot of people.
Just keep in mind that Hades doesn't reinvent the wheel. It's not some new mind-blowing thing. It's a game that a lot of love and care went into in developing, and people see that and respond well to it. But it's definitely not a game that everyone is going to love, or enjoy.

If you're on the fence read some of the game's negative reviews. Some of them raise some fair points.
Or you know.. instead of eating out a few times use that money and pick up this gem of an experience that's in a video game format instead.
'Cause that's Hades.
It's more of an experience than a game.

Come a long way since it's initial release.  I saw one other review call it "Animal Crossing in Space" and while it may not have the same social interactions it does possess a good gameplay of base building, resource management and most definitely, exploration.  
  For anyone who's primary draw is "what's over that next ridge" this is a good game.  It suffers from what plagues all sequentially created open world games, that being a sort of 'sameness' that can crop up after a while despite their best efforts for variety.
  Making one's own base is also a big bit of fun in this game.  You can be quite creative in designing your space home.  And if having it planet side isn't enough, there's freighters you can structure the interior of almost to your heart's content.
  Resource acquisition can be a bit of a drudgery (grind).  There's a lot of mods out there though and once you learn how those function, it may take a lot of the hum-drum away.
  Recommended if you're into:  Sci-Fi, First Person Exploration, Base Building

The most recent (so far) Nep Nep game is very good. Idea Factory changed a lot of stuff from previous games, and most of the changes were good. Firstly, I feel that the series has finally catch up with this current gen in the graphic aspect. The models look nice and the enviroment looks detailed enough, specially comparing to Megadimension Neptunia. They finally updated and made a 100 % new soundtrack. In the other Nep games, the soundtrack was basically recicled each year. Which is not totally bad, considering the fact that the soundtrack was very good, but it got old and repetitive. This time the soundtrack is entirely new, which is good. The biggest problem that I see people complain on the reviews is the game's combat system, and I agree with them. Idea Factory implemented a new combat system, which is similar to some of the Neptunia games spin-offs, like MegaTag Blanc and NepU. Cyberdimension Neptunia is an action RPG, or a hack'n slash, or both if you prefer. Of course the combat tends to get way more fuild in this kind of game than the Turn-Based RPG systeem used on the other main games of the series. The problem is that the system is not good enough. There is literally just one "action" button, that you spam through the entire game. And another button designated to cast spells. It's really simple and it tends to get boring after a while. They could have implemented a slightly more elaborated system. About the story, this is high point the game. Idea Factory focus on the whole meta game they always liked it. This time they go really far. On the main story, you(the player) is playing a game that is about videogame characters playing a videogame. Yes, and this works out just fine. Also, the NEP NEP classic lewd moments are here, and a lot of past games characters are on the game. This game game could have easily been one of the bests NEP games If ID Factory improved the gameplay mechanics. Still, worth playing if you are a fan of the series. If you are not, wait for sale.

I first played this game on the alpha release on itch.io. i remembered liking this game. when i saw this came to steam, i had to buy it. i didn't remember what it was about this game that i liked, but boy did i like it again, and of course, now i remember what it was i liked. this game has controls that feel like those of a platformer like celeste. you have a dash, which renders you invulnerable, an infinite slide across the ground for moving faster, a stop which can launch enemies in the air or even kill them, and the ability to wall jump 3 times before hitting the ground. this allows for insanely in-depth movement that feels like second nature after 10 minutes with the game. the doom-like gameplay encourages the player to constantly move and take advantage of their moveset. 
Blood refuels the player's health, which encourages close-quarter combat. The combat in this game is brutal and edgy as fuck. blood flies everywhere, covering the walls and floor, but all this blood doesn't replenish you. it has to have come from an enemy not even a second ago. if there were intestines, this would feel like a brutal doom for quake. 
Most important to the combat is the weapons, and these feel fucking awesome to use. i haven't gotten all the weapons yet, but i'll talk about the ones i have. you start with a pistol that feels kind of gimped, but it's not a terrible weapon. later, you get a shotgun, which already feels powerful enough that you think you could get through the whole game with it. the last weapon i have so far is the chaingun, and it feels like a weapon from brutal doom. all the weapons can be upgraded, and the upgrades add so much. i won't go into detail for them, but they rock.

TL;DR: This game is the best FPS i've played since doom: project brutality 3.0. please, for the love of god, get this game!

So what is this game?

An action-RPG lite, game.  It features 4 classes, each glass had 3 weapon choices, your weapon chooses the bulk of your attacks.  There is also a specialization that then sets up some passive ability based on the class.  As an example the mage class can go between a high damage spec, or one that heals as well as does damage.

The game world is broken up into several regions of land with you starting off inside of a random region.  As you travel the region you will face enemies broken up into 5 catergoes of difficulty, talk to NPCs, do quests (kill enemies in area, kill a boss, and similar).  Equipment will also drop, usually of the category of the enemy/quest, or one category higher.  As you travel the area you will collect neat items like a hang glider, sail boat, climbing spikes, reins (to use to ride your pet).  As you explore you will eventually uncover the location of artifacts in your current region, which are your main goal per region.  These artifacts, once collected, will make you ride your pet slightly faster, sail slightly faster, glide slightly better, dive slightly longer.  In general helping you explore.

So I obviously don't recomend this game, what is wrong with it, I'm sure it sounds ok so far.

First, difficulty scaling is rather crazy.  Enemies are either too tough and you MUST exploit game mechanics to beat them, or the enemy is just cakewalk easy.  Gear is your main way of becoming stronger, and a good weapon dropping for you will utterly wreck all but the toughest of enemies.

Notice I've said nothing about leveling up, there is not really a level system.  You gain a 'level' by collecting earlier mentioned artifacts.  The level does nothing but show how many artifacts you've collected.

Once you leave a region with your reward of an artifact.  Your gear, becomes usless low level stuff, unless you found very very rare gear called + gear.  Which will keep full effect up to one region away from wherever you found it.

All of the utility stuff you found (gliders, reins, etc) also disapear, so you can't even use the artifact you found until you manage to find them again in the new region.  And again you need to put up with the bad difficulty progression.  The loop itself can get quickly boring, but it could play slightly better if you are in a group.

But the game has a big issue with rewarding you for your time.  As the artifact is your only true permanent reward, and not only is the effect tiny, but you need to find an item in each and every region for most of the effects to actually be of use.  So despite the fact that I personally want to like this game, I can't suggest it for anyone to buy it, unless it gets some massive changes.

Rocket League is a completely physics-based fast-paced sports game where cars play soccer. A very simple concept, but it's the most fun you could ever have in a video game. The learning curve is very steep, so you might struggle when you begin, but the game's addictive nature will probably grab you anyway and make you play for hours until you're too tired to even go to sleep, so you play more and you realize you've been playing 5 days non-stop and you're dead. Even though it's such a simple idea, there's so much you can do in this game. If you're a newcomer, don't forget to try flying! (Spoiler alert: It's f***ing awesome!)

It also has great potential to become a big e-sports game, something that I'm really looking forward to.

The list of features at the moment isn't huge, but hopefully the devs will add more things in future updates like they've promised. (Psyonix always keeps their promises, so I wouldn't worry about it!) The season mode is a great place for new players to practice their skills against the AI, but the online mode is where most of the fun of the game lies. And, the customization is sick. Oh and the insanely cool replay editor! Also new free maps in the future confirmed!

All in all this game is very solid, very competitive and fun, and I would recommend it to anyone who likes skill-based games or is into sports.

You remember XCOM:EU? That game of the year 2012 and still ever since in it's genre? XCOM2 not only manages to be a worthy successor to it, but far overwhelmingly surpasses the first's game to take it's throne and be "The" turn based strategy for the years to come.

Firaxis took everything that was good in the first game, implemented it to the second one almost unchanged (don't fix what isn't broken as they say), and vastly expanded on it.

[b]Combat System:[/b] Unchanged cover system, completely randomly generated maps for each mission (important story missions are of course exceptions), new type of soldier classes with many more strategies and tactical options. You often start the mission concealed, meaning the tables are turned and you can set up ambuses. More type of weapons and abilities.

[b]Map design[/b] More interactable objects: risky hackable towers, explosives, new types of doors and windows (some you can see through, some are laser and cannot be run through), great new sci-fi cities and other various biomes (such as forests, deserts, snowy tundra, small towns in all of them, ADVENT fortresses and more!), the maps often include holographic advertisements such as ADVENT propaganda, scrolling news of our customized characters being labelled as terrorists. The graffities of resistance and logos of the Elders are always representing the global status of the area you landed in.

[b]World map[/b] A new type of turn based "adventure" where you free regions from the occupying power. A vast amount of randomly generated missions, new mechanims that based on your choices take serious effects on upcoming combat scerianos. Finally no more permanent nonsense loss of support, UFO encounters has been reworked and overall the whole world map part of the game is much more important, strategic and enjoyable to play.

[b]Customization[/b] Everything you loved before, just more of that and more on top of that! You have about a dozen layers to customize your characters' faces only, customizeable hand, chest and leg armor for each different armor type, voices of a few languages, armor and weapon patterns, helmets, hoods, face accessories, everything can be recolored, renamed, whatever you want.

[b]Story[/b] Huge improvements here aswell. Being honest, nobody ever bought XCOM:EU for the story, and nobody will buy XCOM2 for the story. Still, there are more cutscenes, more likeable and recognizable characters. XCOM: The Bureau tried to drag down the perspective to a more personal level but doesn't come even close to XCOM2 that also remains to be the good old XCOM:EU gameplay, while the overall playtime is increased from 20-25 hours to a healthy 27-30, filled up with more engaging scenes, more type of mission objectives and more varied gameplay in general.

[b]But there are some negatives[/b], really minor things but worth to mention. Loading screens are mostly hidden behind cutscenes that is a common thing nowadays, but sadly there are performance / stuttering issues of the engine rendered cutscenes (pre-recorded videos are fine though), and very-very rarely it can couse an exe crash. Customization while being a massive improvement over XCOM:EU, could have used more hairstyles, face paints and some things here and there. The last thing is entirely a subjective topic, but most of the game is attached to various type of timers during missions and outside missions (pretty much a doom timer that you can roll back if you play well), that puts constant pressure of the wrong type on those who don't like being time restricted, and it also kind of works against the new ambush setup allowing concealment mechanism too. The engine in general could be better optimized, which was an unpleasant surprise given XCOM2 is PC exclusive, though Firaxis is actively working on improvements. Don't worry, it's nothing like the sadly widespread terribly optimized unstable garbages, it's a decent game that could be better on some points.

However, there is steam workshop perfectly integrated to the game (Skyrim-level of integration), and the modding community is already making oceans of additional customization content, voiceovers, and even gameplay changing mods such as new enemies, new balance, new weapons, different or disabled timers, whatever you are looking for is either already made or is likely under development already. Add this to the randomly generated maps and even after the first "pure" / "vanilla" playthrough you have a MASSIVELY replayable game that always has new surprises to kill you with.

In Outlast (which, btw, sounds like a 'try not to fap challenge') you play a journalist/ex long jumper who came to investigate some seriously shady dealings in an abandoned asylum/battery factory. So jumping and battery collecting are definitely among the top things you'll be doing.

Asylums are generally boring and safe places, especially at night, but our hero nonetheless came armed to his teeth with his camera, just to be safe. 

Like most modern games, Outlast is entirely too simple. There's no fighting, the puzzles are more chores than puzzles and the same few elements are repeated over and over again.

The theme, plot elements and enemies are unimaginative to the highest degree.
Worst of all, the game is not very scary as there really is nothing to lose if you die. The jump scares are the only thing that might get you (until you come to expect them as they are rather regular) and even though I would not ban jump scares from horror, I prefer when they are the icing on the cake, not the whole cake.

Anything positive I can say about it? Well, it looks good and I get 60+ FPS on a crap PC, so that's great. It would be hard to argue Outlast is a very good game, but its simplicity and inability to truly scare the older player do add up to a relaxing action-walking simulator, like a virtual house of horror: get scared, but not really, enjoy the siliness of it all and then quickly forget about it.

Really fun shooty-bang-bang game.

There is loot and collectibles everywhere. You're characters have levels which increase with progression, from what I've seen each level gives you a permanent 2% damage boost. There are a couple different currencies in the game which you collect and use to upgrade your characters and unlock abilities. Enemies have health bars which the game says have different resistances to different weapons, but on the 2nd hardest difficulty, at least early on, the sturmweger and shotgun seem to be strong enough to quickly take down anyone, except for the huge robot dogs which require a laser turret.

I'm playing solo and the AI partner is actually pretty good at distracting enemies, and has revived me more than I've revived her! It never gets in the way and when you're crouching it just turns invisible.

The game takes place in an underground hub and you just fast travel to different areas to carry out missions. Even in the first level, there are rooms that require a specific ability to open that you couldn't possibly unlock early on, so obviously the game wasn't designed for linear progression, but rather an arcade approach.

I'm having an awesome time with it and I'm very interested to see this story through.

Dark Souls sonunda hakkettiği "Remastered" halini alabildi mi bu soruya cevabım hem evet hem de hayır olur bunun sebebi ise bu remastered versiyonu biraz sorunlu öncelikle bu sorunlar hakkında konuşmamız lazım öncelikle çevrim içi özellikler çok sıkıntılı geldi birisinin oyununa işgale gittiğimizde acayip derecede takılmalar oluyor ve bunun sonucunda bir kişi ile savaşmaya çalıştığınızda sinir bozucu şeyler olabiliyor. Hatta bundan acayip derece bana oldu adama vurup duruyorum adam sadece sarsılıyor canı hiç gitmiyor kan çıktığını görmeme rağmen hasar görmüyor. Bir diğer sıkıntı ise hileyi çevrim içi halde kullanan insanlar sinirlenmenize sebep olabiliyor. Ben bir çok kez karşılaştım böyle oyuncular bir şeyler yapılıyor genel de ama bu hile kullanıcıları bir e-posta ile yasaklamalarını açabiliyor bu da onlara hile açmasınlar diye değil de sadece göstermelik bir uygulama olarak yapılmış bu da diğer oyuncuların haklarını suistimal ediyor. 

Sadece oyunun grafiklerini geliştirip bırakmışlar çevrim içi oyun özelliklerini sorunlu bırakmışlar bu büyük bir eksi sorunları yaşadığımda genel de İnternet'imin bir sorunu olduğunu görmedim çünkü sorunu yaşadığımda genel olarak karşı taraf acayip derecede çok takılmalı ve hızlı hareketler ile öldürülmüş oluyordum. Son olarak da remastered hakkında bir kaç şey konuşup oyunun kendisi hakkında konuşabilirim şimdi bu halinde oyunun grafiklerini geliştirmişler fakat oyunda görüntü yavaşlaması, gölgelendirme sorunları gibi hatalar ile karşılaştım. 

Özellikle bu görüntü yavaşlaması acayip saçma bir durum ben motion-blur özelliği açıkken bu sorun acayip derecede oluyordu fakat bu özelliği kapattığımda daha az karşılaştım ama bir remastered'a yakışır bir şey değil bu. Gölgelendirme hakkındaki hatalarından bahsetmek gerekirse Ash Lake yolunda iken The Great Hollow isimli bir ağacın içinde yol alırken dalların gölgesi gözükmez iken üstümde duran canavarların gölgesi gözüküyor normal şartlarda dalın gölgesi gözükmeli ve cidden bu gölgelendirme sorunu da remastered diye çıkarılan bir versiyona büyük bir eksi. Şimdi oyunun gerçek içeriği hakkında konuşabiliriz. 

Dark Souls benim acayip derecede sevdiğim ve bitirdiğimde muhteşem derecede tatmin olduğum nadir oyunlardan birisidir. Ben normalde Souls oyun serisine serinin 2.oyunundan başladım ve bildiğiniz üzere pek sevilmedi serinin diğer oyunlarına göre ben beğenmiştim fakat 1.oyunu oynayınca 2.oyundan daha çok beğendim bunun sebebi aslında 1.oyunun çoğu özelliği 2.oyuna göre daha çok etkileyiciydi. Konuya 2.oyunu dahil etmemin sebebi ona daha önce oynamam ve bazı yönleri 2.oyunla karşılaştıracağım için 2.oyunu dahil ettim.
 
O zaman konuşmaya bölüm tasarımları ile başlayalım oyunun çoğu bölümü farklı birbiri ile bağlantısı olmayan ve üzerine çok düşünülmüş tasarımları var fakat 2.oyunda genelde bölüm tasarımları koridorlardan ibaret olduğu için böyle bölüm tasarımlar cidden çok hoşuma gitti. Oyunun bölüm tasarımları çok iyi ve bu bölümleri muhteşem şekilde destekleyip atmosfer yaratabilen müziklere sahip. Müziklere o kadar bayıldım ki ara sıra açıp dinlemeye devam ediyorum müzikler cidden şaheser olmuş. Oyunu zevkli kılmak için bu özellikler yeter mi yetmez iyi bir oynanış olmalı ki tekrar tekrar oynamalısın işte bu özelliğe sahip bir oyun Dark Souls. Oynanış kısmında tatmin edici, oturaklı ve zevkli bir oyunu zor bulursunuz. 

Bu muhteşem oynanışa üstüne bir de kaliteli bosslar ile olunca tadından yenmez bir eser oluyor Dark Souls. Bosslar ise bir kaç tasarım haricinde çoğu boss kaliteli yapılmış zorlukları da dengeli hazırlanmış fakat 3 bossun 3 de aynı olur mu bu arada bahsettiğim bosslar [spoiler]ilk karşılaştığımız boss olan Asylum Demon ile Stray Demon ve Demon Firesage isimli klonları ile tekrar savaşıyor bu biraz tasarımda ucuza kaçmak gibi olmuş [/spoiler] bunlar dışında cidden çok kaliteli bosslara sahip örnek olarak vermem gerekirse Sif, Artorias, Ornstein ve Smough gibi bir sürü kaliteli bosslara sahip bir yapım Dark Souls. Hikayeden de biraz bahsetmek gerekirse bir kadere göre seçilmiş ölmeyen Undead Asylumdan kaçıp sönmeye başlamış olan ateşi yakmak için yolculuğuna başlayacak. Genelde hikaye eşyaların içine saklanmış şekilde ve araştırılarak bulursanız çok zevkli oluyor fakat bunlarla uğraşmak istemezseniz çeşitli içerik üreticilerinin videolarını izleyebilirsiniz. 

Son olarak rol yapma oyunlarda büyük etkisi olan NPCler hakkında konuşmamız gerekirse serinin bu oyunu ikonik karakterlerinin neredeyse hepsinin bulunduğu tek oyun (Solaire, Siegmeyer, Oscar...) ve bu karakterlerin özel görev çizelgelerine sahip. Bu görevleri yaparsanız karakterlerin hikayesini az çok öğreniyor ve karakterlerin son kaderi ile karşılaşabiliyorsunuz.

XCOM 2 is a turn-based combat action game that both rewards and punishes the player for their tactics, improvisation and game knowledge. Despite removing some of the more strategic aspects from its predecessor, this iteration of XCOM is a vast improvement that is well worth the time and investment. 

[h1]Positives[/h1]
(+) [b]Rewarding combat:[/b]
Many mechanics, skills and weapons that work in different ways when applied to the diverse enemy types. 

(+) [b]Immersive experience[/b]:
It is easy to become attached to the staff and soldiers at your command. Successful missions feel exhilarating, while losing your favourite soldiers is traumatising and full of grief. 

(+) [b]Easy to learn and get addicted to[/b]:
The gameplay is relatively intuitive and the process of trial and error will provide adequate experience to plan around each enemy and situation. The base management aspect has been simplified where money is not the sole focus, as opposed to the predecessor. 

(+) [b]Mods[/b]:
Mods range from Quality of Life improvements to aesthetic customisation as well as gameplay enhancing. This addition vastly improves the gameplay experience, and longevity of the game. 

(+) [b]DLC provides excellent value and immensely improves the base game[/b]

(+) [b]Soldier customisation[/b]:
Adds an element of role-playing and narrative creating, as you are able to give soldiers particular personalities, physical traits and customise them in any way desired. 

(+) [b]Graphics[/b]:
The game looks spectacular in general combat, but especially during the cutscenes. However, more powerful systems may be needed to achieve a smooth graphical experience. 


[h1]Negatives[/h1]
(-) [b]Unexplained and unfair mechanics[/b]:
Some mechanics and enemies feel unbalanced and can induce rage-quitting from sheer frustration. 
[list]
[*]Enemy Field of Vision and detection upon movement is not explained. Enemies also get to move for free, regardless of their turn, when they are detected, which can ruin your set-up plan to attack them as a group. 
[*]RNG is calculated before the turn starts, which makes the outcome predetermined unless you try another move.
[*]Exploding cars, destructible environment, fall damage.
[*]Lancers, Alien Kings and the Chosen are extremely powerful. 
[*]Mission timers make the game feel hasty and sometimes impossible to complete.
[/list]

(-) [b]End game becomes too easy, even on harder modes[/b]:
When the strongest weapons and soldier skills have been unlocked, missions begin to feel like a nuisance as you advance time to progress the story. As long as you have the strongest equipment, the only way to lose is making extremely poor decisions. 

(-) [b]Lack of QoL UI and gameplay settings[/b]:
Simple things such as enemy numeric health, information about their skills, movement capabilities and damage are not readily accessible. Viewing the types of enemies expected to be encountered during the mission planning screen is also not available. Mods fix this problem, but it should be in the base game.

(-) [b]No safeguards to misclicks[/b]:
Accidentally clicking on an open space or not selecting the correct ability can derail the entire mission. This is especially distressing on Ironman mode experiences, as manual saves are not allowed.  

(-) [b]Full stealth not possible[/b]:
Despite being in full stealth, the enemy will always know where you are and will move to deny undetected paths. Some actions always alert enemies, such as planting bombs, hacking objects and securing hostages; this makes quick and efficient missions difficult, but not impossible .

(-) [b]Animations jarring and drop framerate[/b]:
Cut scenes are not always smoothly transitioned, are unable to be skipped and take a while to finish. Other cumbersome events include enemies taking too long to finish their turn and the transition between XCOM forces and enemy’s turns. 

 (-) [b]Bugs[/b]:
Be sure to frequently save and make backups, as mods will eventually corrupt save files.

app_name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
review:
This game is honestly a masterpiece,it pretty much takes the first one and makes it better in a lot of aspects. I never review games, but I love this one too much not to review it.

The visual design and music are just what you'd expect from Ori. They are mindblowingly good and one of the biggest reasons why this game is so charming and immersive. There have been times where all I wanted to do was stop, take in the scenery and listen to the beautiful soundtrack.

The platforming and level design are also really good. Each level brings something new with its own gimmicks and abilities required to overcome the obstacles in said level. Speaking of abilities, they are very fun and feel smooth and polished. However, I highly recommend that you change some keybindings, since some abilities overlap and there are times where you'll accidently use an ability that you didn't want to which could possibly lead to your death.

The story is by no means anything complex, but it's the perfect example of simple yet effective. It's a cute adventure on the surface that tells the tale of loss, love and sacrifice.

And last but not least, the combat. This has to be my favorite part, as it's the most unique and really separates this game from the last one. I'll start off by mentioning that you have a weapon wheel and that you can have 3 weapons equipped at a time. While at first this might seem very restricting, it's actually a really nice piece of design, since you can swap weapons in the middle of battle, depending on what you need. There are enough weapons in the game to suit multiple playstyles and experiment with different synergies.  The one minus I have however, are the shards. A lot of them feel somewhat unimpactful and boring, mostly giving you damage, damage resistance, cells etc. Though with how polished and smooth the combat is, and also all of the previous pros, I didn't care about the shards all that much.

The one single major con I have about this game is the fps drops and the sound stutters. Those can break the immersion from time to time, so if you really wish to immerse yourself I'd suggest waiting for patches.

All in all, I loved this game. It's hands down one of the best games I've ever played, and I can highly recommend it to anyone who loved the first game, or loves metroidvanias in general.

Прошел я наконец всеми любимую игру под замечательным названием Bisohock Infinite.

Скажу сразу считаю эту игру одной из самых переоцененных в игровой индустрии.
Какие же чувства у меня возникали в процессе прохождения данной игры? Я боюсь что мне не хватит эпитетов, чтобы описать свою реакцию, дабы не держать вас здесь долго я все-таки позволю себе сказать, что она ужасно скучная, унылая, однообразная и сама идея далеко не самая новая и уникальная (совершенно не понимаю тех людей, которых чуть ли не инфаркт хватает, когда они переваривают мысль о механизме использования времени в данной игре, существует огромное количество проектов, которые работают с этой идеей намного лучше). Одним словом, они просто взяли самую популярную и избитую концепцию мультивселенных, параллельных и миров и не справились с ней, а все потому что подкованный и насмотревшийся не одним таким сюжетом человек предугадает абсолютно все сюжетные твисты ещё задолго до их наступления. Хочу отметить один из многочисленных примеров подобного: гг  надо заполучить оружие для Фицрой (очередной пластмассовый персонаж), спустя продолжительное время неинтересных пострелушек с помощью способностей Лизы выясняется, что оружие, которое им надо было доставить было уже доставлено в другом мире, в которое Лиза и открыла портал (ВОТ ЭТО  ПОВОРОТ) И это должно нас удивить? В этом вся сложность и запутанность сюжета?? В изначальной концепции параллельных миров?? Это же смешно.

Мертвая и лишенная каких-либо шероховатостей, которые делают игру более живой, именно так я могу отозваться о мире игры.

Псевдолинейность, которая никак не отражается на сюжете игры. К чему в этой игре предоставляется выбор, если он приводит к абсолютно такому же исходу??

Все персонажи шаблонные и абсолютно не запоминающиеся(их даже не было по сути), что касается Лизы, то я также, не понимаю всеобщего обожания в её сторону, что же в ней такого??Это просто красивый манекен без каких-либо чувств и внятной мотивации. Если говорить о геймплейных моментах связанных с ней, то она может привести вас в раздражение потому как ИИ в этой игре на посредственном уровне, да и частое нажимание кнопки F для того, чтобы открыть запертую дверь или сундук вряд ли сделают игру интереснее. 

В мире игры есть энергетики с помощью которых можно получить сверхъестественные способности, у меня вопрос, а почему враги не используют их??what??

Что касается технической части, то тут все на довольно среднем для того времени уровне, звёзд с неба не хватает. 1) Paciencia o fasito

3) 60 dolares...
4) Experiencia en los Early access ya que este juego es una beta disfrazada de un Release.

Ya que aclaramos los terminos vamos a explicarlos.

1) Vas a esperar a veces 10 minutos para comenzar una partida, y ademas de que los miembros de tu equipo factiblemte abandonen la partida cuando se sientan "REKT" o mejor dicho violados, la comunidad de este juego basicamente proviene de los CoD, muchos niños ratas, mucha gente que se frustra rapidamente y no busca remontar una partida despues de un mal comienzo. En el tiempo que jugue tengo muchos ejemplos para darlos, por ejemplo del lado CT: Partida de rehen, pickean fuze(bombas clusters), localizamos rehen en un cuarto acompañado de 3 terroristas, Fuze pone cluster, Rehen muere, LOST ROUND.
Otra mas, Sniper en tejado alejado del objetivo, compañero rompiendo ventana, sniper ve enemigo por el agujero de la ventana pero el compañero sigue enfrente, sniper dispara, doble kill, compañero y enemigo(a veces solo el compañero)
OTRA MAS!!
Dos escudos intentan entrar por una puerta sin antes utilizar un dron, Lanzas un dron para marcas enemigos dentro del cuarto, los marcas, escudos entran aputando para el lado contrario, partida 3vs5, LOST ROUND.
Ahora vamos con los terroristas:
Rehen en medio de la sala, smoke tira granada de humo alado del rehen, cuando estan por entrar la activa, muere rehen, LOST ROUND.
Rehen en una habitacion cerrada, refuerzan esa habitacion hasta los muebles, nadie adentro de la habitacion, Rehen rescatado y nadie se entero, LOST ROUND.
Empieza la partida,2 bombas, haces un agujero entre A y B para curir terreno mas ampliamente, compañeros TAPAN el agujero, te activan A cuando estabas en B, nadie puede entrar porque solo tenes una entrada y esta siendo cuidada. LOST ROUND.
Pero hey, no todo es malo, Empieza una partida, te prendes un faso, el equipo es estable mentalmente, 4-3 defienden la bomba, 2-1 lobos solitarios corren por el edificio buscando realizar emboscadas, Resultados: Flawless victory!!
Muchas tacticas diferentes, muchas formas de jugar diferentes, muchas erradas que se van a ir modificando con el tiempo, el problema es que hay poca gente jugando y hablan todos diferentes idiomas en su mayoria, no existe una comuniacion con el equipo, no existe un sistema de "ping" para poder marcar donde reforzar, donde mirar, donde romper, donde tener cuidado (al estilo del lol en todo caso), solo tenes un PING que todo el mundo ignora....

Esto no lleva al punto

Castle Crashers is a 2D Hack n Slash/ Brawler game which in my opinion worked perfectly on so many levels. The story is quite simple: You and other four knights chase through various levels a mysterious villain who just snatched an equally mysterious crystal and four fair maidens from your castle. 
If you're looking for dramatic, story-rich content this is not the game for you. BUT if you're keeping an eye out for a fun filled, challenging multiplayer game then definitely yes.

The controls are quite simple, I easily managed to play more than 30 hours of the game on just my keyboard. Though if you want to make life a bit easier for yourself then I would suggest a controller. It's a game where timing and cooperation with other players is essential.

What really got me into the game was the Unique Art style. The Game Artist, Dan Paladin, made an excellent job in creating a cartoonish, colourful (and in many ways cute) world. Even the monsters look pretty. The game is rich with humour and the Style conveys that perfectly.
Excellent graphics combined with an Epic soundtrack make this game entertaining and glorious for both eyes and ears.

The game can work for both Solo players and Co-op Players, though I would really suggest it for the latter. This is the kind of game you want to laugh about and yell to when you're with friends. It's a great experience, better shared with someone that likes the game's... shall we say... extreme humour.

In order to not make the game repetitive and eventually boring, the game developers made an excellent job in adding ways to enhance your character and give you different abilities to choose from. There are many ways to fight the hordes of enemies in each level, and it's so rewarding to see your character progress and become a bad-ass by the end of it. And if that wasn't enough, there are 28 animal spirit that you can acquire throughout the game. Not only they're adorable, they're also useful for boosting your character's stats.

In conclusion, this is definitely the one I can suggest to everyone, regardless of age. 
Though it might look simple, it's a well made, challenging game. And no matter what, you will want to play it over and over again.

[b]Summary:[/b] Definitely recommend for the engaging gameplay, but the game can get a bit scary at times. However, Valve does an excellent job of providing affordances for players to play to their physical and emotional comfort level.

HL Alyx is an incredible achievement from a technical and gameplay design perspective. It delivers an engaging and simple full-length narrative that can be enjoyed multiple times. The tactile nature of the game adds new depth to the Half-Life universe. I marveled at how the environments enabled all sorts of emergent gameplay: from leaning or opening doors with my weapon all the way to literally lying on the floor to shoot through a narrow space, Alyx is a game that rewards creative thinking.

That said, I don't think it's a game for everyone. VR adds a barrier to entry, and not everyone would be able to cope with the horror aspects to this game. However, Valve does an expert job at adding difficulty and accessibility settings to allow more people to play At the outset of playing, I was concerned I was going to be too frightened by the headcrabs and zombies, but again, Valve cleverly designs the environments so the first time you engage with a new enemy, you can observe and defeat them in a controlled setting. All this together allows you as a player to move Alyx at your own pace and by your own rules.

I play games for fun.

Very rarely do I play a game in order to experience and enjoy what the story has to offer. Sure, the story is often a huge plus (Portal and Portal 2), and perhaps [i]afterwards[/i] I will see the story as something that should be recommended (Drawn to Life). However, even then, stories very rarely leave an impression on me that I feel as a person in the real world, rather than a character within a game.

Then, there's Undertale.

Perhaps committing some sort of horrible taboo, I must admit I went into Undertale knowing what most of the story entailed. Without hoping to spoil anything, I knew about Sans and "having a bad time." I knew about Flowey, and why you should never give Toby Fox the ability to use Photoshop. I knew that I would have to choose to befriend or kill every enemy in the game.

What I didn't know is how the game would mark me.

Undertale is a game that is very self-aware. Not that it necessarily breaks the fourth wall often, but your playthrough(s) and the story go beyond what is on your current save file. Some characters may remember what you've done on previous runs, what you've done may affect what you are now able to do, etc.

At least, this is what I've been told. I wouldn't really know.

You see, beating Undertale for the first time has left an impression on me. The characters you meet, the story you experience, ingrains itself within your mind and prevents you from continuing afterwards, at least with me. After what I've experienced, I'm not sure I will be able to complete the game. I'm not sure I could bring myself to restart and do a genocide run - to kill these characters, to prevent the relationships from growing, the love from spreading, and the story from unfolding in a way that allows everyone, even including the main villain, to be happy.

Yes, I know it's "only a game," but I believe my point still stands. Heck, even if I plan on doing another pacifist run, I'm not sure I can bring myself to reset the game and start over, knowing that the happy ending I've worked so hard to create will have essentially been evaporated.

Undertale has changed my outlook on games and their stories in general. The story does a great job of making you feel responsible for what happens. And right now, I'm struggling with what to do with that responsibility.

Play this game. Please. It's an experience you need to have.

P.S. Playing it with friends in the room makes for an even more enjoyable experience. Especially when things get weird. [spoiler]And they will.[/spoiler]

When I was 11 years old my dad took me to an amusement park next to my hometown. Was fun as far as I remember. Pretty exciting for a kid my age. Two years later, my parents took me to Disneyworld. After visiting the most famous and greatest amusement park in the world, I never felt the urge again to go back visiting the one next to my hometown. 

“Hades” is now Disneyworld in the world of roguelike amusement parks. I’m not gonna be surprised if we're gonna experience now a baby boom of roguelikes in the steps of Hades - even more then before - trying to cash in on this massive achievement of gameplay. 

I feel like the word “Masterpiece” is a bit overused in our times, taking out the real meaning of the description. I am not a kid anymore. Games don't tend to make me bust a nut so easily like 20 years ago or so. Hades is my first Steam game that made me care about getting all the achievements, and obviously any other nook and cranny it has to offer. After more than 200hrs of gameplay and more than 200 runs, I am still coming back to it for a new run, now as a morning ritual with my coffee.

I’m not gonna use the word masterpiece again. But with Hades, it feels like a new standard has been established in the genre.

Watching the hivemind nostalgia circlejerk down here is both amusing and disturbing at the same time. 

I have an additional 50+ hours in the closed & open betas and have been playing Dawn of War since the original release. Personally, Dawn of War 1 was more my style, though I did enjoy Dawn of War 2 quite a bit as well. Consequently, I sunk quite a few more hours into the first game than the second game. Hence I have a greater affinity for this title given it's more traditional RTS setup compared to DoW2.

At any rate, people claiming lack of tactical depth compared to previous titles need to take their rose saturated hipster glasses off. I suspect there are several problems at work here, the first being complete lack of understanding of the current game. It reeks of people presuming to understanding every facet of balance and stragety the instant they install the game (almost as if they'd made up their minds before the game even released... hmm).

Second, given the age of the previous titles I suspect a lot of people were children when they played DoW 1 and 2. This is leading to some grotesquely inflated notions of what was actually in those games.

Whatever the case FAR too much of the discussion is being centred around what the previous games were. DoW3 is, surprise, not DoW 1 or 2 (though it does more closely resemble 1 than 2). This revelation may piss off some of the fanatical, niche playerbase left in those games, but DoW 3 needs to be judged on it's own mertis.

In that respect DoW3 has been a highly enjoyable experience both in terms of it's single player (so far, as I am currently on mission 6) and multiplayer. Personally, MP is more my bag, but SP people will get quite a challenging campaign if played on hard. Winning requires both strategy and micro. You WILL lose to a competent player if you just blob and move about the map without tactical consideration. 

Perhaps some of the more pompus fringe elements of the warhammer fanbase just needs to accept that shoving around some figurines while spending 2hours to take their god damned turn does not make them the unparalleled strategy master-gods of gamingdom. Nothing against most TT players (I have Dark Eldar and Dwarf armies myself), but this is an RTS. It will demand actual mechanical competence and quick reaction speed from you (both in terms of decision making and unit micro). It's demanding and requires concentration, but difficult skills are rewarding to master.

Being new and inexperienced is fine, but pretending to understand every facet of the game on day 1 while mindlessly blobbing against other new players is exceptionally disingenuous. The gameplay has been brought into a modern context where balance is actually a primary consideration. 

I see a lot of "e-sports" buzzwords being thrown around, but people don't seem to be taking the time to consider what that even means. If "e-sports" means moving away from the janky, bug ridden, haphazardly balanced games of the past perhaps more games should strive for "e-sports" professionalism. 

As funny as release state bugs and balance issues that hung around for AGES could at times be (kruutox daemon armour, vanilla fireprisms, release honour guard, monolith duplication bug, sisters of battle infinite resource bug, tyranid balance, release warpspider exarch, etc et etc) gaming needs to keep moving forward beyond this. Some crotchety "old" 20-30 year olds mumbling "back in my day when gaming was great.." are just going to have to be carried along with it.

At the end of the day, this is Dawn of War 3. People who want Dawn of War 2 should keep playing Dawn of War 2 (or wait for CoH3... though I'm sure that too will get it's fair share of endless complaining :P) and stop expecting that everyone should/wants to play "their" game. The people who want Dawn of War 1... well, go back and play that? It's plainly evident most people droning on and on about the glory days of tactical depth and unparalleled imersion haven't touched the game since some time back in 2006 :P

An amazing game pureley based on survival of the fittest. The game is only an alpha build, so it has many bug fixes to be made, and many updates to be added on. When we say bugs, we dont mean "the whole world has turned to hell, there are indestructable bears duplicating and teleporting, help god PLEASE!" No, we mean the accasional bear walks to base, bear walks through wall, bear mauls and kills player, bear walks away. Thats about it, with a few texture bugs every now and then, if you are unlucky. The game focuses on surviving in the wilderness alone, no food, no water, no home, just a torch and your lovely rock. It is completely free roam, no story or quest line what so ever. You start out gathering resources, and finding supplies to stay alive. You get your nice little house set up, and go offline thinking of how safe you are in your nice wooden cottage, full of food and water :) But this is far from the reality of rust. The burn the house down, take everything useful, and run back to their base. Its kill or be killed. Trust no one. How ever, this is not the case all the time, you may run into a few friendly people on the way. You get online, your house and supplies are gone, and you are back to square 1. With your new found blood lust- I mean knowledge of the world of Rust, you decide to take a more... dangerous approach, to anyone near. You build a stone (or steel) fortress, ready to defend what is rightfully yours. Occasionally, airplanes will come by and drop parachute boxes full of items, such as food, meds, junk, armor, and the most delicious loot, guns. People will have the same intention as you getting the loot first, so if you are there before anyone else, be ready to fight, or run. You can set up an ambush, but be warned, other survivors may have the same bright idea as you. You grab your things, and run home as bullets fly by your presumably beautiful face, and you get inside. You plan a raid in the day for the upcoming night. As the sun sets, you set out on your journey. You find the horrible people who broke in, and you give them  a taste of their own medicine. Luckily, the stone walls are no match for a good helping of C4 and timed explosives. You get in, grab loot, and get out. Congrats, you are now a "professional" Rust player. Until someone breaks in again, kills you, and you are back to the start, with your rock and torch.
Once you download beatsaver, this game is totally worth it. Couldn't have picked a better first game to get on VR.

Edit:
Dec 26, 2018
Post Launch Review;

Everything I said about this game above was ture for the first year of Early Access. Since then my view about the game and the developers behind the game has changed dramaically. This game is not worth the price hike. It's not worth the 60$ in it's current state.

After the honeymoon phase I have come to dislike this game more and more. Nothing foundationally has changed since Early Access and some how this game plays worse than it did a year ago. I have a pretty high end computer, that according to the store page and in game default settings, my rig should be more than enough to play on high settings. They have yet to address the memory leak and a pethora of glitches and bugs that have been in the game since day one. The constant CTDs due to memory being eaten up has imbittered me. Undermeshing is the new flavor of the month and they have done little to fix it. 

WildCard would rather add new shiny things into the game instead of fixing the broken foundation. They should have never ported this to switch or mobile either. It's buggy and unoptomized regardless of platform. They allocated their human resources in all the wrong areas of development and the state that Extinction released in really shows that they lost their way since early EA. I was a idiot to think this game would be fully optomized and smooth post launch. After two years of EA, I regret defending it on the forums.

I will admit I had fun in EA with some great friends, but I can NOT recommend this game until they fix the foundation, and I will not buy any more games made by Instinctgame/WildCard/GrapeShot until these problems are fixed aswell.

Hey Leute,


Nach schon bald einem Jahr im Early Access scheint mir, dass genau jetzt der Zeitpunkt für eine Review gekommen ist. My Time At Portia ist schlicht und ergreifend ein atemberaubendes Spiel. Es handelt sich um eine Art von Aufbau und Simulationsspiel, welches man grob mit Stardew Valley und ähnlichen Ablegern vergleichen kann. Trotz der Ähnlichkeiten, die sich hauptsächlich auf das Prinzip beschränken, ist My Time At Portia ein komplett eigenes Open World Abenteuer, welches von Jung und "Alt" genossen werden kann.

Nach kurzer Einleitung werde ich im folgendem meinem Stil treu bleiben und My Time At Portia anhand der gängigsten Kriterien bewerten. Die Kriterien lauten hierbei: [b]Gameplay, Entwicklung, Preis und die Grafik.[/b]

Nun also zur Einleitung, was genau ist My Time At Portia überhaupt? In diesem Spiel schlüpft ihr in die Rolle eines jungen Abenteurers/in, landet am Strand von Portia und werdet umgehend in die vorhandene Gesellschaft integriert. Ihr seid der Nachfahre eines Builders/Handwerkers der schon vor vielen Jahren der Stadt treue Dienste geleistet hat. Wie es der Zufall so will, hat euer Vater euch eine Werkstatt hinterlassen die ihr nach eigenem Gutdünken gestalten, umbauen oder sonst wie verschönern könnt (Kennt man irgendwoher oder?). Im folgenden ist es an euch die Bewohner kennen zu lernen, ihre Aufträge entgegen zu nehmen oder bei sonstigen Problemen zu helfen.... Soviel zur Einleitung man muss ja nicht alles vorweg nehmen.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

Im gesamten Spiel bewegt ihr euch in Third-Person durch die Welt, erkundet das Land, diverse Höhlen und die ein oder andere Stadt. Das Spiel legt viel Wert auf Interaktionen um also verschiedene Boni oder Special Items, zum Teil auch Zugänge zu neuen Gebieten zu bekommen, müsst ihr mit den NPCs gut auskommen und teilweise auch Aufträge erledigen die nunmal nicht ganz so spannend sind. Das Kampfsystem ist angemessen, es ist jetzt nicht so herausfordernd wie bspw Dark Souls aber auch kein luschiges Point&Click Adventure somit sollte jeder auf kurz oder lang damit klarkommen. Mitunter kann das Spiel ein wenig grind lastig werden aber lasst euch davon nicht abschrecken, selbst schnöde Erze in düsteren Höhlen abzubauen kann wirklich interessant werden.

[h1]Entwicklung[/h1]

Wie zu Beginn bereits gesagt, dass Spiel nähert sich seinem Einjährigen Jubiläum. Zufälligerweise habe ich das Spiel bereits in den ersten Tagen erworben und angespielt, kann also durchaus etwas zur Entwicklung sagen. Zuerst einmal sollte festgehalten werden, dass wir hier kein typisches EA Game vor uns haben. Selbst kurz nach Release deutete nur wenig darauf hin, dass sich dieses Spiel überhaupt im Early Access befindet. Ein wenig Content fehlte und mitunter waren einige Dialoge, sowie Übersetzungen noch nicht implementiert. Inzwischen, knapp ein Jahr später, wurde viel Content nachgesteuert, sowohl was Items angeht als auch Quests und NPC Dialoge. Die deutsche Übersetzung lässt noch zu wünschen übrig aber hauptsächlich was Dialoge angeht, Items und Quests sind zu 95% vorhanden davon sogar um die 70% von der Grammatik und Rechtschreibung her korrekt^^

[h1]Preis[/h1]

Einer der Streitpunkte in jedem Spiel und eindeutig individuell zu betrachten. Um den Punkt allerdings trotzdem zu beschreiben hier meine eigene Meinung, die derzeit 20 Euro sind wirklich gut angelegt. Wie bereits erwähnt hier hat man nicht das übliche EA Game vor sich, dass vor Bugs strotzt und durch inaktive Devs glänzt. Das Spiel hat schon sehr viel zu bieten und wird stetig weiter entwickelt, also greift lieber jetzt zu bevor es teurer wird. Im Zweifel auf einen Sale warten, dass Spiel hat bisher keinen ausgelassen.

[h1]Grafik[/h1]

Der letzte Punkt, für den einen komplett nachrangig für den anderen das Totschlagkriterium. My Time At Portia ist meiner Meinung nach auf jedenfall ansehnlich designed und der Stimmung im Spiel mehr als angepasst. Das Spiel sollte auf den gängigsten Gaming System im bereich der mittlere Hardware problemlos laufen, ohne arge Einbußen in Sachen FPS und Detailgrad.

[b]Fazit[/b]

Ich kann das Spiel jedem empfehlen ,egal in welcher Altersklasse man angesiedelt ist. Mir persönlich macht es viel Spaß und es ist extrem entspannend. Das Spiel verlangt keine durchgehende Aufmerksamkeit, es bombardiert einen auch nicht unentwegt mit Action. Man kann es einfach starten, ein bisschen durch die Welt wandern, vielleicht einfach nur ein bisschen Angeln und dann wars das wieder und trotzdem hat man das Gefühl etwas geschafft zu haben.
Der Preis ist mehr als angemessen, die Reviews sprechen für sich und die Entwicklung schreitet stetig voran. Jeder der also etwas entspanntes sucht ist hier genau richtig.
Bevor die Frage auftaucht, Multiplayer ist nicht vorhanden und soweit ich weiß derzeit auch nicht in Planung.
Das einzige was ich als etwas störend empfinde ist, dass das Spiel automatisch speichert und auch nur beim Wechsel auf den nächsten Tag. Zum Teil sorgt das für ärgerliche Ereignisse.

Ich hoffe die Review konnte dem ein oder anderen weiterhelfen. Danke fürs lesen und eventuell viel Spaß beim spielen :)

Я еще с детства люблю приключения о Ларе Крофт. Все эти тайные знаки, гробницы, загадочные места и прочее, будили во мне большую любовь и интерес к этой игре. Эта часть Tomb Raider очень захватывающая. В ней Лара с командой отправилась в морскую экспедицию на поиски страны Яматай, где правила имератрица Пимико. Пимико (также известна как Химико) — первая и последняя Императрица Солнца. По легенде, она передавала свою душу избраннице, которую воспитывала и учила как родную дочь. Последней избранницей была Хоси, которая покончила с собой, дабы предотвратить ритуал. Также в легенде говорится, что она могла управлять погодными условиями. Когда Лара с командой взяла курс на треугольник дракона, она попала в шторм, после чего ее корабль потерпел крушение и она вместе с остальными, таким образом, оказалась на загадочном острове Яматай. Этот ужасный шторм и мешает выбраться людям с острова. Также Пимико служат, так называемые, Штормовые стражи или же Воины Они, которые являются воинами самураями. Я очень люблю Японию и японскую культуру, и возможно, именно это сыграло ключевую роль в формировании моего мнения об игре. Скажу сразу, что игра мне сильно понравилась. Эта игра увлекательная и интересная, я рекомендую пройти ее всем. Геймплей очень классный. Окружающий мир в игре уж слишком красивый, а все эти древние пагоды и замки, навевают некую мистическую атмосферу Японии того времени. Взаимодействие Лары с окружающим миром и ее поведение очень реалистично сделаны. Помимо сюжетной линии в игре можно изучать мир, а также находить тайники и расхищать тайные гробницы, что не менее важно. Оружие в игре можно всячески модифицировать, собирая запчасти, а умение по выживанию Лары, прокачивать, что делает прохождение игры более интересным. Минусы в игре также присутствуют, их очень и очень мало, но на фоне такого круто геймплея и всего остального их просто не замечаешь, а впечатление от игры никак не портится, да и для игры 2013 года все просто идеально, поэтому говорить о них в своей рецензии, я не вижу смысла. 
   Подводя итог хочу сказать, что игра действительно достойная и заслуживает вашего внимания. Рекомендую ее к прохождению!

This game really is awesome!  Before you say "DayZ rip-off!! BURN IT!!!"  Just remember, DayZ, while yes being the first, is now part of a genre.  The open world survival horror genre.  Nether does that, with a twist.  Instead of zombies, it's these freaky mutated humans that can teleport.  The teleporting REALLY adds to the intensity when you know they're coming for you, after another player opens fire on you!  So even if you manage to disbatch the player..... They're still coming.

While still providing plenty of wide open space, Nether as brought the combat MUCH closer to home.  While someone sniping from one of the many explorable 20+ story buildings is a VERY real danger, the real danger could be coming around the next corner.  It takes place in a city some what based on Detroit I believe.  It has a very "close quarters" feel to it.  Seriously, at any point another player could come running around a corner.  Then you have to decide... Do you Kill him on sight?  Do you let him live?  Do you hope to all that is good and holy in this world that he didn't spot you and sneak away?  

There's a LOT of cover, so stealth and camo are important to survival.  There are highways full of vehicles, fences, buildings and alley ways.  I have yet to find a building that I COULD NOT enter.  Seriously, EVERY building that I have so far see I have been able to go inside!

Height is a big deal too.  As I mentioned before, there are some buildings that go up and up and up and up and up!!  It's awesome!

Death is a big deal.  As you kill the Nether you gain experience. As you gain experience you level.  As you level you earn stat points.  You may apply these points to different skills.  When you die...... You start back at zero, as well as lose everything you had on your person.  So make bank trips as often as is logical.

The game is in early access.  There has been a whole lot of witch hunting surrounding this game.  If you don't feel comfortable with it, you don't enjoy the open world survival horror genre or you just plain hate fun... Then do not get this game.  But if you're into the idea of a game where survival is actually fairly difficult to do, where you could suddenly get one shot by a crawler and lose everything...  Where the PVP is made that much more intense because you know a fair amount of  unpredictable enemies are teleporting toward you, and then arrive before your fight is even over....  

Man it's cool...

DMC3 is enjoyable for most people, and I highly recommend atleast playing that one to see if the series really interests you as it is essentially a prologue to the whole series.

Čo o tejto hre povedať?  Payday 2 je co-op akčná FPS hra o vykrádaní bánk a celkovo o [i] robení [/i] kriminálnej činnosti. V hre sa nachádza veľmi veľa DLC, ktoré si zamilujete ([spoiler] Hotline Miami, Big bank, Assault pack, Clover character pack [/spoiler]), ale záreň je v hre aj pár DLC, po ktorých kúpe sa budete sami seba spytovať, čo naozaj tých pár euro nemohlo ísť na niečo užitočnejšie ([spoiler] Ano hovorím o strašnom Goat Simulator DLC a o otrasnom h3h3 character pack DLC [/spoiler]). 
V hre funguje level systém. Postupne sa pribúdajúcimi levelmi hráčovi odomykajú rôzne zbrane, ale aj Skill Pointy, ktoré môže hráč zainvsetovať do Skillov, aby získal rôzne vylepšenia svojho charakteru alebo nejaké schopnosti, ktoré by dokázali pomôcť jemu alebo jeho spoluhráčom.
Gameplay je fantastický. V PD2 sú 3 tipy misií:
1. Stealth only - misia sa dá dokončiť len potichu. Stealth je v tejto hre sice docela ne-realistický, ale o to dosť zábavný.
2. Loud only - misia sa dá dohrať len "hlučne", to znamená, že si so sebou treba pribaliť batohy s muníciou, armor a gulomety :)
3. Stealth possible - misia sa dá dohrať aj na Loud aj na Stealth. 
Hra má perfektne utvorený "wave" systém počas Loud misií, ktorý sa doslova prispôsobuje tomu, čo sa v hre deje, či sa hráčom darí alebo nie  a teda sa nejedná len o nejaký obyčajný plošný "wave" systém. 
Komunita je príjemná, veľmi zriedka sa dá naraziť na vyslovene (((TOXICKÉHO))) hráča.

Doporučujem túto hru? Určite áno, ale....
Nekupujte si "len" základnú hru. Ak budete môcť, tak si počkajte na zľavu na Steame a kúpte si kompletnú edíciu so všetkými DLC, naozaj to stojí za to. [spoiler] (Podľa mojich informácií ani kompletná edícia neobsahuje nehorázny h3h3 character pack, toto DLC rozhodne nedoporučujem). [/spoiler]

- No ultra-widescreen support currently
- Some people have had issues with stuttering and crashing (I've not experienced either of these issues personally)
- Gameplay can feel a little slow at times

Now, let's talk about the pros.
- Fantastic turn-based strategy
- Roleplaying aspects are very well done
- UI gives all information you could want without bombarding you with it; it's very intuitive in my opinion
- Giant walking tank robots, loaded down with missles, lasers, and eletricity cannons
- The mercenary company simulation/base management are very nice and streamlined
- Tons of freedom

In summary, there are a few issues which I imagine will be fixed with patches sooner than later, but the core gameplay is spectacular, especially if you are a fan of the Battletech tabletop game. 10/10, would stomp tanks with an eighty ton 'Mech again.

Exploring into a new area removes all of your previous progress and starts you over from the beginning, also taking away your travel gadgets so you're back to plain old walking. About the best thing you can hope to "progress" with is a permanent 2.5% climbing speed boost after 5 hours of gameplay. You've accomplished nothing else.

Balance is all over the place, with you either dying in one hit or being wildly more powerful than everything else in the area. Power jumps around sporadically with each piece of dropping gear, instead of having a logical, gradual progression to the top. Ultimate abilities are about the only thing that matters, and combat largely revolves around abusing design flaws, cheesing, or one-shotting everything. There's no skill customization, no skill progression, and very little reason to do combat at all. So far, nearly all bug fixes from the dev have either failed entirely or made things worse, and the game is still rampant with EXTREMELY game-breaking bugs.

Even the most hardcore lovers of this genre (if you can even fit this "game" into a genre) like myself will seriously struggle to find their enjoyment. In all, this is a slap in the face to any followers of the game, because after 6 years all the developer has managed to do is stroke his own ego by removing old, good features and thinking he had struck gold with this inane concept. And after 6 years of playing this game, about the only thing you'll manage to accomplish is getting an extra +1 meter to your lamp light radius. Don't waste your time.

(Let me just also point out that I don't want the alpha game back. This is not a comparison review. This release, completely disregarding the alpha build, is not fun. I am basing the game on what it is now, not what it COULD be).

I really love this game. The art style is awesome and has a lot of range when you enter different ships. There's so many great details on the ships and everywhere that show a lot of care went into the artistic and logistical design of it all. At the same time it doesn't take its sci-fi too seriously- which is a good compliment to the art and tone of the game. Like the fuel your space ship uses to jump from site to site is just scattered about in red jerry cans in ships' engine rooms. And like the fact there are so many varying ships (like luxury spaceships, prison ships, medical ships, bureaucracy ships, etc.) just abandoned and full of whatever the citizens are. Or like how the clients/prisoners are literally just like dehydrated in little bags, being stored in a filing cabinet. There's just so much charming creativity here. The world is appropriately tongue and check comical but also fairly interesting. I very much enjoy thinking about how things in this world operate. It's great fun to upgrade your character- scavenging wrecked ships throughout the nebula hoping there isn't a ridiculous amount of enemies waiting to f your shi up. I also enjoyed the combat. It's satisfying to kill certain enemies and watch them explode into turquoise goo and body parts (although I do wish there was some type of melee kick back option for those desperate situations). Having to ration ammo makes engagements tense and sometimes undesirable. It's also gratifying to feel like you are playing intelligently. Planning out routes, dishing out the merits you have to get a bit of an advantage, quarantining areas that are problematic (rifts), maneuvering the security system. The modifiers for locations also give the gameplay a nice twist. For example, I thought I had adequately quarantined a rift, but I forgot that the ship's power would go out, unlocking all of the ships doors, and giving me quite a surprise when I thought I had the ship to myself. The menu ui is efficient, cool, and I like it. The starmap is a cool aspect of the game. The sardonic, and a bit absurd, humor is great. Excited to put a good amount more time into this game.

This is a really good port, finally a persona game for PC.
The graphic on PSV is actually really good, but on PC it obviously improved a lot. I can now see what's actually going on with the graphic thanks to better resolution, and smoother frame rate makes it really good and satisfying to see. It does feel like playing P4G in a bigger screen, since the game being the exclusive of PSV making it identical with the handheld. When playing a good game, rpg genre to be specific, you've spent 10 hours on the game without realizing it, because it's just enjoyable and bring you into the game.

You can having a simulation by interacting with people, doing certain activities, improving your personal skills, and they aren't done for nothing. It affects, and can actually make your actual gameplay much more easier.
-Deepen your relationship with your teammates gives you an ability bonus for their persona. And can evolve the persona into a more powerful version.
-Interacting with people with social links makes it possible for you to unlock and fuse more powerful persona.
-Social link ranks will give bonus level when you're fusing a persona who the same arcana as the social links.
-Your personal skill can help you interact better with the social links, in some social link, it requires some personal skills to unlock. Like enough knowledge or courage.
-Side quest aren't that great, but they actually give you something useful that help you in the gameplay, like healing items, unique items too (assault signals, diamond shield, etc.), money, and I find many times, I do need them. Most of them aren't tedious to do too.
In conclusion, there's no activity that's just a waste of time in this game, they all almost matters (except you are in new game+ with maxed stats). Dialogues and event are also interesting, not sounds awkward nor forced, it feels like you are watching an anime show, a good anime show which enjoyable. So it's worth to own I almost can assure, especially if you are new to this game, you will enjoy your time a lot. I've beaten this game many times, from start to the end it always feels full. Not rushed, and didn't feel like a half assed game until the end. Moreover golden add more of event and contents which aren't available on the OG p4.

Would I recommend the game for new players? Yes. It's a good starting point if you want to play the series backwards.
Would I recommend it to hardcore, Demons' Souls/Dark Souls players? No. It was tuned down so much... and some solutions...

I've finished the game in far under 20 hours while exploring nearly every corner of it, failing some quests but not caring much. Exploring entire maps. And there's just so much wrong with what it became. DS 1 felt like a very, very giant, open world filled with intersections between maps. DS 3 doesn't give that feeling anymore, to a point it hurts me actually. You are given a feeling that you've got a choice, I mean if you're good you can kill Dancer instantly and go to castle at once right? Except you will get murdelized by high-end monsters. But in end, any side-areas you enter, you enter once and leave them for good unless a quest orders you otherwise. Smouldering Caves? Went there once, gotten everything I needed, never returned again. This was never a case of DS1, I kept travelling past all the maps.

Difficulty? Far, far below expected. Out of 18 bosses (if I count it right) I've had issues with only 4 using my PVP focused build. Ever tried beating Seath or Four Kings using a bleed/backstab dex dagger build in DS 1? No? Try it, tell me how it went. It is a challenge. And don't get me started on Orstein... but here? I understand I used greatsword+shield, but still no boss took me more than 3 tries solo (except the ones mentioned) and I think at least 8 died at first try. Where's difficulty in that? Especially that you can summon an army of sun-praising fantoms nowadays.

Then there's the fact that a lot of mechanics that allowed for build customization around armors and poise were overhauled to a point in which you are nearly forced to resign from playing certain builds. (Staggerlocking Havel armor with a mediocre-enchanted Katana pays its respects...)

There's a lot I could go into detail which I didn't like and which I did, but it would take a long time.

I can say for absolute certainty that this game is a hidden gem from 2017. Releases like Super Mario Maker probably contributed to its lack of coverage, which is a real shame because this game is fantastic, well designed, thought-provoking, inspiring, and creative on almost every level. With tight and fluid gameplay, intelligent level design, amazing music, challenging boss fights and platforming sections, and hours upon hours of optional content that you can completely miss if you aren't looking carefully. I've played through the entire game and can easily recommend it, especially at such a low price. Knowing what I know, I would have bought this game even if it wasn't on sale.

***SPOILER WARNING***

The only thing I felt truly frustrated by in the game was access to the game's secret final boss, The Radiance. In order to fight it and access the game's true ending, you need to complete a great deal of extra content with no obvious hints towards it. I had to look up a guide after I completed the game for the first time because it was clear that I got the "bad ending". Even after you complete these challenges, you still need to get past the Hollow Knight, the game's not-so-final boss. This is true for EVERY time you want to fight the Radiance, meaning that if you die, you need to fight the Hollow Knight again just to make another attempt a The Radiance. This was extremely aggravating to me, but having something like that happen only once during the entire game speaks to the game's good design.

Despite this, I still highly recommend the game to anyone who loves games that are challenging, tightly designed, explorative, aesthetically pleasing, and well worth the price.
