A worthy follow up to Enemy Unknown. This time around the missions and objectives are more varied, with less 'go to new map and kill all enemies' missions and more objectives around protecting or eliminating certain objects or people. The enemies now have a little more variety between them as well, with later hostiles having different abilities rather than just more health and damage. 

Being able to customise you squads weapons with mods you find adds a nice layer of specialistion to individuals. You'll need to aquaint yourself with all of your teams abilities and stats more carefully this time as well, as the difficulty seems raised. Injured teammates are out for much longer and most missions have some kind of turn timer, adding a level of urgency to each objective. You can't just overwatch and creep forward anymore.

There is also more to do while not on an active mission this time, with you tasked with building a resistance network. This will have you flying around to various locations to set up communications arrays and invesigate supply caches or rumors. This extra layer adds a bit more interest to some of the downtime, while also giving you important tactical advantages.

My main issue with the game is that by adding a few different kinds of objectives they've made each mission a little more distinct, which means when you inevitably play another 'protect the radar dish' mission you feel like you've done that already. This paradoxically seems to have reduced the replay value, as even by the end of the first playthrough you already feel like your repeating yourself. Admittedly I have played through the campaign twice, but I think it'll be a while before I can go back and play again.

I recommend it, but before you get it you should know some stuff. 
One: It's a platinum game so the combat is pretty good. It's not quite Bayonetta or DMC but it's still really fleshed out considering that it's an EXP-based RPG. 
Two: It's a JRPG. There are no autosaves and you can't manually save everywhere. You need to be within close proximity to a savepoint to do so. The game is not well optimized on PC and you'll need install mods to get the game running to a level of quality comparable to the console versions, even then there are some annoying bugs exclusive to the PC version that were never patched.
Three: This game is very story-based and can feel preachy and heavy handed at times. If you don't like Kojima games (More MGS than Death Stranding), there is a decent chance you'll hate it.
Four: There are three main 'routes' you take in the story. Two of them are very similar. I won't spoil it but if you despise backtracking, one of them is going to be hair-pulling.

The line of sight mechanic is genius (hold down 'c') to see what any unit can see from where your mouse cursor is) 

The animations, soundscape and terrain are well done.

There really is a ton to like - but this is not a casual lets have a beer and play some steel division..type of thing...it's a process...and if you love wwII units, the history of it,  the cool vehicles and tanks, the planes - well it's just a delight.  

one last thing - it's going to take you awhile to master this game...try to be patient

Mount & Blade, un jeu qui 8 mois plus tôt m'était complètement inconnu...  aujourd'hui, je suis triste de ne pas l'avoir eu dans mes mains avant!
Pour être un grand fan de jeux médiévaux, stratégiques avec une sauce open world.. j'ai enfin trouvé un jeu qui regroupe toutes les choses que j'aime!
On commence comme un moins que rien, avec un bâton et une tunique pour zigouiller un ivrogne mécontent. La petite intrigue du début n'a franchement pas un réel intérêt, c'est le commencement d'une longue survivance dans un monde féodal simple (Enfin!!) où le but est de servir ou asservir les puissances de Calradia.
Ce jeu va vous faire pousser une âme de royaliste monarchique totalitaire hors du commun si vous décidez d'emprunter le chemin royal. Mais vous pouvez aussi bien servir le peuple, faire du commerce, des petites quêtes, version mercenaire... Le jeu est complet, même si au début il parait un peu maigrichon, il faut juste savoir ou aller !

[b] Les plus: [/b]

-Qualité/prix : Largement correct, même si pour certains ce genre de graphismes vieillit le jeu, personnellement ils ne me dérangent pas du tout, ça donne même un certain charme !

-Durée de vie: Le temps s'écoule dans votre royaume, les jours passent, les guerres, les morts, les pillages... parler d'une durée de vie est compliqué dans ce genre de jeu.. Si votre but est de conquérir le royaume entier, il vous faudra environ une trentaine d'heures si vous êtes vraiment à fond et très motivé! Mais entre les petite quêtes et la vie du royaume, les heures de jeu ne se comptent plus! surtout avec les DLC et le multijoueur.

-Multi: Le mode multijoueur de se jeu est très positif, une communauté parfaite, avec de vrai passionnés de guerre Napoléonienne (DLC), des stratégies complètement contrôlées et une immersion totale dans les champs de bataille. 

-La baston: Mon Dieu! La jouissance totale d'une armée de chevaliers qui foncent en ligne droite contre une troupe de bandits en haillons! Ou des batailles épiques de prises de forts et de villes. Les batailles de ce jeu peuvent être vraiment superbes! "PEUVENT".. parfois c'est l'anarchie totale quand on perd le contrôle de nos troupes.. cela devient ridicule!

-L'ambiance: Dès mon arrivée dans ce royaume, j'ai compris que j'étais parti pour PLUSIEURS heures de chevauchée dans les plaines, galopant sur les tête de mes ennemis...
Non sérieusement ce jeu vous place vraiment dans une ambiance médiévale (d'ailleurs les différentes contrées représentent plusieurs "types" de Moyen-Age = Européen, Nordique, Oriental...).

[b] Les moins: [/b]

-L'IA de ce jeu est vraiment...VRAIMENT stupide! Attention, seulement à certaines occasions...
Les combats d'escarmouches sont importants et l'IA bourrine absolument tout...même les arbres...
En arène et dans les prises de territoires.. c'est un spectacle presque comique, c'est affligeant de voir des troupes s'entraîner durant des heures sur le terrain, et se faire tuer de manière ridicule...

-Le "farming": Le plus gros problème de ce jeu pense,  c'est le temps qu'il faut pour créer et avoir une armée de style "puissante"... entre les combats qui sont normalement gagnés par votre armée, mais qui au final, sont perdus à cause de votre mort sur le champ de bataille.. Avec en plus votre long emprisonnement au sein d'un groupe de bandits inattrapable... C'est LONG.
En bref le déroulement du jeu: Création personnage, blablabla, village recrutement, bataille, recrutement, bataille, recrutement... Pour enfin avoir une armée potable!

-La difficulté: ATTENTION, je m'adresse aux novices de ce genre! Ce jeu est "dur" dans sa durée.. plus vous irez loin, plus la chute sera difficile. Jouez calmement et intelligemment! si vous jouez bourrin dans ce genre de jeu... Soit vous êtes comme moi, ou soit vous allez ragequit à cause de la perte de la totalité de votre armée (true story)

-Multi: Le seul gros problème du multi, et la tristesse des serveurs vides :'( Souvent, c'est un seul gros serveur avec 200 personnes, et le reste compte dans les environs d'une trentaine de personnes...

En bilan, achetez ce jeu! Regardez des extraits, des images... si les graphismes ne vous coupe pas, GO! C'est une très bonne expérience que je conseille à tout fan de ce genre!                         (surtout en solde avec DLC)

Et surtout! BON JEU !

Terraria

Terraria is a 2D, platformer, sandbox game. The idea being that they place you in the "16 bit" world and your goal is to survive. The game becomes fairly easy to understand and thus fun is insured. 


Story (Positives)

The story of terraria is...

There is no story. Your goal is to simply survive in the fantasy world that is very similar to earth. Defend yourself from the threats of the environment, craft and create new materials, and enjoy finding the mysteries of this world. With a simplistic idea as this you can any where. From a realism survival game such as The Forest, or to the extreme opposites such as Grand Theft Auto V(given we are talking about the sandbox part of the game). This keeps the game exciting because there a mysteries to be explored and found out by the gamer.

Story (Negatives)

Lots of games today are compelled by a fantastic story, excellent scripting, and grade A voice acting. Terraria lacks all of these, which is somewhat okay for it being a sandbox. But people looking for game where they have a plot, or reasoning, won't be pleased by this. 

Graphics and Sound (Positive) 

Let me first say this, good graphics doesn't necessarily mean the next Crysis 3, or creativity as Limbo, but a game can have charming and appropriate graphics. Being a 2D platformer in 2011 would expect something equivalent to Super Mario Land 2.1, but they go on the whole opposite side of the spectrum. When asked to describe the graphics I would say imagine 16 bit Mario games you played as a kid, but better looking with more color. Sounds pretty bad in today's age but it matches the game so well. It keeps things basic in this extremely complex world. I'm not saying the graphics are 16 bit, cause they are a much higher resolution, but they resemble them. It has a certain charm which makes the game unforgettable. The music also has this charm in which you can turn on the ambient, music, and sound. It fits and matches the situations you are in. Like the graphics not being triple A, the music is chosen perfectly which can make or break a game for people. 

Graphics and sound  (Negative)

For those looking for triple A graphics from publishers like Bethesda and DICE, you will be disappointed. But for how unique this game looks, you can't really go wrong. The sound of other things besides music in the game is average.

Gameplay (Positive)

While the game seems to be lacking in the story and graphics, the gameplay nearly instantly makes up for this. The idea being, kill this, mine that, fight that boss, find this, do that... Wash rinse and repeat sounds boring, bland, and uninteresting. But what changes this from bland to interesting is the abundance of items/blocks, unique biomes, and challenging bosses/enemies. When you get in the game you crave for the next ore, next item, and more money. Understanding the game at the beginning is fairly basic and most gamers would enjoy to play this. Even to introduce people to video games they would be able to understand. The mobs of enemies and difficult bosses make you feel accomplished when you get that next upgrade of armor or weapons. You feel as if you have gotten stronger and progression is made. It's almost ridiculous how fun this grind is. The replay ability of small scale situations in the game is very high, but the large scale is average. If asked to play this game again after around 3 months of beating it, I probably would. 

Gameplay (Negative)

I mentioned how most people would be able to grab this game and start playing, but the problem that it runs into is that it has so much content that it can get confusing to a point of not knowing where to go. With having thousands of items and hours of hours of gameplay available, where do you go, how do you craft that, where is that boss? Late game you will find yourself on Terraria Wiki searching for what to do next and what does the next damage instead of naturally funding it /searching for it. 

Verdict

Costing under $10, it's practically a free game. The amount of hours/fun you can have on this game makes it a must buy.

Bonus: I didn't review multiplayer and single player because the game on multiplayer plays like the single player, pretty much making it seem like a co-op.

Where to even start with Terraria.

Let's start at the price, $10 American , for 1 copy, and $30 American for 4 copies. At that price you'd expect a game to be maybe, mmm 5-10 hours long? if that? You might expect the game to be fun with friends but kinda boring alone but hey, it was cheap, what do you care if it's crap? and besides if it's as short as you think it is you can just return it! ( you shouldn't do that by the way, it makes Valve angry, and developers sad) 

So you buy the game, maybe even throw down a few copies for a few friends, and you get in the game and think, okay so i chop trees? Then you find your first slime, and get a taste of the combat to come, you think "no problem, this game is EZ" a few nights later your friends and you have a pretty slick base built up, you've got some copper armor, maybe even an iron sword! Then a Blood moon happens, You and your friends don't know what that is, so you treat it like any other night, at first your killing zombies left, right and center. But hey these zombies just keep coming, maybe we should hold off for tonight, so you all retreat back into base, safe behind your wooden walls, and sturdy wooden doors, Right? WRONG before you and your friends know what's happening there are zombies breaking down your doors, eyeballs flying in unfettered and your guide just exploded into a pile of gore! After a long battle your little group decides to take a break, thats when you realize you've been playing for 10 hours straight, and oh how little progress you've made. 

For the next several weeks your group keeps coming back, slowly working your way up the food chain, no longer are you afraid of a few dozen zombies, slimes cower in fear when you walk by. You've even beaten the eye of cthulu and the eater of worlds! Clearly nothing can stop your party. And then you come to this large blue brick structure on the edge of the world, No problem, nothing your group can't handle you walk by the silly old man without heeding his warning, Who needs to? you can't be stopped. Deeper in the massive structure you go, the atmosphere is ominous, one party member suggests turning back, but he is outnumbered and you press on. Suddenly you hear a roar from the deeps of the dungeon, you ready your weapons for a fight, and before you know what happened you've been splattered all over the walls, your friends retreat but they aren't fast enough. 

The next night your group sits on top of the dungeon and beckon the old man's warnings this time, And you face his curse together. After your hardest fight yet you've finally done it, you've won, you summarily loot the dungeon and split up the loot. Well that was fun right? Your party has a good time, you've won the game! A celebration occurs. Soon you realize, your only getting started in this crazy world of Terraria.

This is Terraria.


On a less lyrical term, Terraria is a free form sandbox RPG with an aircraft carrier's worth of things to do. You want to fight awesome bosses? You got it. Want to build a crazy house? You got it. Want to PVP with your friends? You got it. Want to explore a diverse and amazing world? You bet your ass you've got it. you want to make pixel art? YOU CAN DO THAT. Do you get the picture yet?

EDIT: i recommend voting for Terraria for the Stands the test of time Award, i'm certainly still playing it to this very day.

Like Paradox' other titles, this game is made with a lot of love and attention to detail, while still providing a fun gameplay experience with almost infinite replayablity. The personal empire creation and expansion gives the player the perfect pioneer feeling, while the mid-game politics aspects turn the game into a whole new experience. 
Mentionable features are the alien race creation with its ethics and the indept ship customization. 
Yet, there are stilll some flaws with it. while other paradox titles give you great and well positioned information, once the player got to know the interface, stellaris lacks this comfort. Here you have to do perform 2-5 clicks more to find the info you need. in the mid to late game, the game tends to lag in big universes, even with a decent pc (gtx 980, i5 4690k, 16GB RAM), which makes it less enjoyable.

All in all, this game is totally worth your money, if you like strategy games. it is, in contrast to other paradox titles, very easy to get into, yet lets you improve your skills each time you try a new start. If you are looking for a space exploration and politics game, there are no better alternatives than this!

What can I say? This game is a real gem. Granted, the base game is small and buying all the DLC can be frustrating, but it's more than worth it in the end. There're so many civs and maps to choose from, every kind of play style is well-supplied and every player can find the civ that resonates with them.

No game is without its flaws, and there are some that were rather glaring in my eyes:

1. AI civs make no sense sometimes. They will extend a trade offer, then refuse when you accept and demand more. They will refuse fair trade deals even when they need the help.

2. Combat information can be misleading. All too many times have I lost a unit because the game told me it was a decisive victory...only to have the enemy unit survive with 1 HP left. Just like that, 12 promotions I've been building since the Ancient Era are gone.

3. The game is very insistent sometimes. While it's nice for the camera to snap to a unit that needs orders, I'm often trying to do something else when I'm ripped away to look at a unit I was going to deal with after. It can be frustrating to be at war and have an important unit start traveling the wrong way.

Despite these flaws, the game has enough value for me to sink hundreds upon hundreds of hours into the game. Some of my personal favorite highlights are:

1. Civ diversity. With 43 different civs to choose from, history buffs can play out an alternate history for their favorite empires, and everyone else can find a civ that they can enjoy. And if you don't? That's addressed later.

2. Scenarios. While it is jarring to revert to the base game or G&K for some scenarios, it's a breath of fresh air to play them. They're short and include civs specially made for these, and offer a unique experience for the civ player who's grown tired of the same game.

3. Diplomacy and espionage. These two systems introduce a whole new layer to the game, enacting policies that affect the world, stealing tech from others, rigging elections and staging coups in city-states, and even winning the game if you have it enabled. City-states play an entirely new role in the game, providing a civ with more world congress votes later on if they're allies. If played right, one player can dictate what does and doesn't pass without fail.

4. This is quite possibly the biggest draw, despite being something most PC games have now: mods. The Workshop has a plethora of mods ranging from new civs and gameplay changes, to quality of life improvements and bug fixes. A common complaint with the game was that games would take far too long becuase AI turns played out at regular speed. So someone developed a mod for Quick Turns, meaning that all AI turns are now sped up unless they interact, whether friendly or hostile. Playing with mods disables achievements, but most will find it a reasonable trade.

Overall I would give this game an 8.5/10. It's rich in content, has a diverse cast (all the leaders speak in their native tongue by the way), and provides the replay value that has players finishing a game that took place over 2 weeks and say, "I want to play again." However, points were docked for the flaws listed above, but at a lesser degree because of mod support. While I wish the annoyances weren't there in the first place, it's nice to know that there's a free fix for a lot of them to install for a smoother, more enjoyable experience.

Sama gra miała bardzo ciężki i mroczny klimat, a szaro-szary świat nie rozjaśniał się nawet na chwilę. Dodatkowo doskonały wybór muzyki i ponura powojenna Anglia wzmacniały poczucie mrocku świata, w którym Johnathan, wampir-lekarz przeżywa swoje wewnętrzne niejasne moralnie spory.

Dla wielu system walk będzie siermiężny i nieprzyjemny, ale dla mnie bardzo wpasował się w imersję historii, która była dość ciekawa, nie wybitna, ale też nie "płaska".Do tego płynna i zwarta. Ciekawy zarys niektórych postaci i ich historii.

Do tego kilka dodatkowych spraw takich jak przyjemny system "exploringu" i "craftingu", czy system rozwoju umiejętności postaci. System podnoszenia poziomu zdrowia pojedynczych ludzi i całych dzielnic jest bardzo dużym plusem tej gry,ale niestety...

Gra cierpi na jeden problem, jej twórcy obiecali nam znacznie, znacznie więcej i to w tym miejscu mam problem przy recenzowaniu gry. Ja osobiście nie liczyłem na "masterpiece" ale na przyzwoitą grę z mroczną fabułą i światem widzianym oczyma potwora targanego człowieczeństwem, co oznacza że nie zawiodłem się produktem, bo dostałem naprawdę przyzwoitą grę, ale rozumiem też oburzenie, zniechęcenia, czy nawet głęboki zawód grą.

O ile sama metoda rozdawania umiejętności jest ciekawa, to ilość umiejętności i zestaw kombinacji nie "powala na kolana", co potwierdzi nieomal każdy kto zagrał w tą grę. Tak faktycznie isnieje tylko jeden działający system skilli z miejscem na personalizację. 

Nadto jak już jesteśmy przy kwestii levelowania to dobrze, że nareście punkty XP nie służą w bezpośredni sposób do przeliczania poziomu wampira. Tylko ilość XP przelanych i wydanych na umiejętności podnosi poziom naszej bestii.
Tu jednak pojawia się problem. Twórcy obiecali przy pozyskiwaniu owych litrów ludzkiej krwii dwie kwestie, które nie do końca wyglądają jak w obietnicach, czy marzeniach gracza. 

Po pierwsze można wypić krew z każdego NPC-a w grze. To tylko poczęści prawda, gdyż do momentu, gdy boleśnie w tym aspekcie zderzyłem się z grą myślałem, że będzie można za pomocą  XP rozwinąć Hipnozę, czy jakąś charyzmę wampiryczną, ale niestety nie. Za podnoszenie tej umiejętności odpowiada tylko i wyłącznie rozwój fabuły, co oznacza, że gdy zdobędziemy odpowiednio wysoki poziom, by pochłonąć naszą ofiarę albo nie będzie nam się chciało wracać do lokacji albo skończy się gra. Dodatkowo bonus za wypicie do dna człowieka zwłaszcza na początku gry jest nieopłacalny. moim zdaniem powinien być znacznie większy, by bardziej kusić gracza do skorzystania z tej opcjii.

Po drugie kwestie związane z moralnością pochłaniania ludzi i ich związkiem z fabułą jest co najmniej nie dopracowany tzn. każda dzielnica ma swoją zakładkę w menu i z niej dowiadujemy się 3 informacji, ilu jest mieszkańców dzielnicy(jak się nazywają, na co chorują, dostęp do wskazówek), kto jest postacią kluczową dla całej dzielnicy i o zgrozo, jaki jest poziom zdrowia dzielnicy. To właśnie cały poziom absurdu, gdyż większość NPC-ów może nam utrudnić grę po śmierci tylko w taki sposób. Jeżeli poziom zdrowia dzielnicy spadnie poniżej 50% dzielnica wpadnie niejako w stan anarchii i zwiększy się liczba przeciwników itd. itp. Rzadko kiedy śmierć postaci wpływa na fabułę bezpośrednio naprzykład posiadając kluczową informację dla opcjii dialogowej decydującej o losach tego NPC-a. Za małe jest też powiązanie między mieszkańcami Londynu i śmierć takiej postaci właściwie nie wpływa na nas negatywnie.

Dam prosty przykład nie związany bezpośrednio z grą ale wpisujący się w to jak powinny wyglądać te zależności. Są mąż i żona na pozór wydaje się, że się nienawidzą, postanawiasz, więc uśmiercić jedno z nich, by podnieść swoje statystyki. W konsekwencji dowiadujesz się to drugie wiedziało, że rozmawiałeś z małżonkiem przed śmiercią a po ranach można stwierdzić wampira, oczywiście nikt tej osobie nie wierzy, gdyż jesteś protegowanym Swansea i wielkim Johnathanem Reidem, więc zastawia na ciebie pułapkę w czasie linii fabularnej jednocząc się z kimś kto stał się twoim wrogiem.

Gra jest dosyć mocno bym powiedział liniowa, a niektóre postacie, zwłaszcza wątek jejdnej z kluczowych postacii jest bardzo płytki a szkoda, bo ten akurat mógłby być więcej niż ciekawy...

Jak chodzi o postacie to dla fanów filmów-gier mam złe wieści, postacie prawie nie grają ( mam namyśli grę aktorską) poza naszym protagonistą, a w dialogach pojawiają się karygodne uproszczenia u niektórych postaci, sprawiając, że czesem chce się przewinąć kwestię dialogową danej postaci ( później także u tych ciekawszych postaci) i tu pojawia się niespodzianka, gdyż można przewinąć dialog postaci ale tylko i wyłącznie jako cały blok dialogowy tzn. jeśli mówi nasza postać i chcemy przyspieszyć to zniknie nam nie tylko to co widzieliśmy na ekranie przed chwilą ale wszystko co chciała postać powiedzieć do momentu zakończenia dialogu lub zmiany rozmówcy.

Na koniec tej recenzji, żeby nie masakrować tej i tak już niszczonej gry dodam, że gra jest naprawdę fajna, mroczna siermiężna, niezbyt zróżnicowana w systemie walkli to fakt, ale to również zapewnia dodatkowy "smaczek" w rozgrywce.
Mogłaby być bardziej rozbudowana w poruszonych przeze mnie aspektach, ale nie ulega wątpliwości, że jest grą dobrą, ale nie wybitną, czy przełomową i to na tym polu jest masakrowana.

Mogę bez cienia wątpliwości powiedzieć, że 1. twórcy mają nad czym pomyśleć, by grę dopracować lub wydać sequel, który jak doktor Reid leczył chorych w Londynie, tak oni mogli uleczyć choroby swojej gry; 2. Polecam, zwłaszcza gdyby miała spaść cenowo, gdyż jest naprawdę przyzwoita a dobrej gry o wampirach dawno niebyło; 3. Mam nadzieję, że twórcy nie zostawią swojej gry samej sobie teraz i spróbują poprawić ją sami nim nastąpi efekt Diablo III i to fani stworzą grę bijącą Vampyra tak, że już z trumny nie wyjdzie. 4. Vampyr będzie tą grą, która przypomni graczom jaki ta bestia (tj. wampir) ma potencjał gamingowy i dalej pokaże twórcom, że gracze wcale nie widzą nieszczęsnego "Zmierzchu" w każdej grze czy filmie itd. dotyczących wampirów i ich mrocznego rozumienia świata, ergo będą chcieli więcej gier osadzonych w tym klimacie lub gry w świecie gdzie te potwory nie są mitem niezależnie od stylistyki.

I tą nadzieją i pozytywnym akcentem zakończę moją recenzję!

关于难度问题：似乎很多人对这一代的评价是像魂……其实怎么说呢，我记得我在打暴食的时候死了十次左右，算是次数最多的boss了，连死两次没有捡魂，然后boss身边飘着两朵魂，之后打了，似乎也没什么损失吧。这和过去的不一样之处又有哪些？怒意形态和爆气也都在，该割草割草，该打精英当然还是需要技巧，而且这武器射程还比原来长了，怎么就不知道满足呢？也就是少了很多招式的学习这一点确实变化很大，但我觉得这到省的我练习各种复杂到然并卵的连招了（毕竟也没有评分系统）。另外这一部有一个缺点，有的武器之间的战斗区别不是很大，也没有使用优势（除了大锤和冰刀），鞭子够用的时候我为啥要用副武器呢？当然除了锤子，锤子反击和打盾是真的好（不用也不行）。
而且完美闪避不要太简单，跟黑魂比起来容易太多了。其实黑魂我不喜欢，因为盾反的手感太难受，闪避无敌时间又觉得不够，敌人出招节奏又怪，根本不是靠反应而是需要长久的背板，熟悉招式。而暗黑血统3我基本上每个怪都不需要预先熟悉，看起手就知道大概什么时候攻击会到，稍微打两次熟悉了各种完美闪避不要太容易。（虽然我玩的并不是天启）
剧情上，填了一些坑，但挖了更多坑，护符是干啥的，荒魂之主自爆了还是变成什么别的形态了，最后的传送门对面有啥？祸乱又都干了啥？总体来说倒也不是什么都没说，但是果然还是得下一部出来才能评价整个故事。
关于角色上，反派上嫉妒给人感觉出场有点唐突，别的反派咱就不提啦。女主人公神怒人设真的太棒！一开始的无脑暴走大姐大形象到后来学会反省冷静，哼我才不管你们这些人类渣滓！~真香！怎么就这么可爱！
不过模型上我觉得还能再精致些的，毕竟距离上一部已经那么久过去了，神怒的模型精度感觉并没有得到应该有的提升（尤其是头发和脸）希望下一部能有所进步吧，期待着。
并不完美但是并没有愧对我对这个系列的喜爱，感谢制作组！

This game is amazing. It is a refreshing and challenging take on the classic Japanese rpg (jrpg). 

  I wont describe the whole game, since its been a while now from its release and info on that is plenty. What I will do, is clarify a lot of the misleading reviews out there, that are drenched in emotions (mainly rage lol).

The “grind” people cry about

  For starters, this game is as much “grinding” as pokemon, fireemblem, xcom, final fantasy… Its not grinding lol. Grinding is when you do something repeatedly in order to acquire or progress on a game, which does not have that Action as a main component. Simply put, fighting different trainers in pokemon, is not a grind, it is the main point of the game so you either enjoy it or not. 

  In the darkest dungeon, you will explore different areas and fight different creatures, with different heroes, gear them, upgrade your town and use your resources wisely. It has many different spices (like town events) to mix things up, but in the end this “grind” lol, is the whole point of the game.

Difficulty and RNG

  As a gamedesigner I can tell you that, there is a difference between well placed rng and filler (cheap) rng. Cheap rng is the one you see in most tcgs, where you have no control over it and it is there to spice things up, but is usually frustrating. 

  Smart RNG, is the one that tells the player that, if he does X, he might get Y or W… In other words, if the player wants to interact with the coffin, he might find rewards or he might get poisoned…. This smart placement evokes the “risk over reward” idea, which is basically the vibe of this game. They even have a intro message stating “this game is about making a bad situation less… bad…”, so you can expect challenges and tough decisions, but nothing out of the blue.

  The game is in fact, unfair in favor of the player… Yes. For example, when your hero gets killed, he does not die immediately, he stays in a “death’s door” debuff, where the next damage he takes, MAY or may NOT kill him… If you think about XCOM or Fire Emblem, you will remember that those games were way less forgiving.

  Another fact is the amount of things the game offer the player in order for him to feel more secure towards a decision he has to make. Potions, bandages, food, buffs, %+ for almost everything, guaranteeing that your success chance is actually high. This is more than we can say about Darksouls for instance, since there is no potion in RL for twitch reflexes…

  This is a thinking game and it will challenge the player like no other, because of an extremely well designed game, that forces the player to accept bad results and move on immediately. That is the roguelike spirit. However, unlike FTL (which I love) this game places really smart rngs and a continuous progression system, so the player does not have to restart the game, only take a few steps back.

Znáte ten typ člověka, co je hodně ošklivý a nikdo se s ním kvůli tomu nebaví (a přitom může být skvělý)? Tak to jsem já... a i tato hra je taková. U tohoto akčního RPG se pozná, komu skutečně nezáleží na grafice, ale hratelnosti a atmosféře.
+ nejlépší zpracování jízdy na koni
+ atmosféra středověku
+ soundtrack
+ dobývání a bránění hradů a měst
+ turnaje a zápasy
+ spousta oldschool RPG prvků a statistik
+ úkoly (pouze jako doplněk, ne jako hlavní náplň hry)
+ obrovský živý svět
+ funkční obchodní model a spousta věcí (zbraně, štíty, oblečení, koně, jídlo, materiál)
+ management vojáků
+ volitelná obtížnost (nejsou tu typické obtížnosti, ale prvky, které si můžete kdykoliv změnit, např. počet vojáků na poli...)
+ možnost připojit se k jedné ze šesti unikátních frakcí, každá s jinou kulturou a jinými bojovými návyky
+ možnost stát se lordem nebo mít dokonce vlastní království
+ možnost oženit se
+ na vyšší obtížnosti nutnost taktizovat
+ žádné fantasy prvky, je to čistě středověké RPG
+ čeština (i když občas krkolomná)
+ spousta módů
+ multiplayer
+ a spousta dalších výborných věcí

- zpočátku je hra extrémně těžká (a tím myslím opravdu EXTRÉMNĚ)
- hra se s nikým nemazlí a nikomu nevysvětlí své mechaniky, na které si člověk musí přijít sám
- grafika (ale mě osobně to vůbec nevadí)
- úkoly tu jsou, jen aby se neřeklo (je jich jen pár a pořád se opakují)

CuteFish Review: Longish review, pro/con list, closing thoughts. Just skip ahead if you don't like reading! :3

   FFXIV: A Realm Reborn is a game that aimed to polish and refine the 'WoW-era' MMO instead of hamfisting in a slightly different spin of the genre. A story based leveling system (at first) that leads into a content rich MMO that has appeal to, quite literraly, any form of player who likes the genre. Very challenging group-based endgame PvE, good PvP, and an abundance of 'things to do' that makes for a very gratifying time sink. 

   Aesthetically, the game has a clean look similar to the other current-gen Final Fantasy games. It runs rather well on my machine and pretty decently on lower end machines, but it's definitely an art style that loses quite a lot of its charm when you start setting graphical settings to 'low'.

   The combat system is the standard tab-targetting most of us are likely accustumed to but actually at a slower pace. The game has a 2.5 second global cooldown between abilities. Early on, this feels incredibly slow (because it is) but later on it feels much more meticulous since each ability use is quite a time commitment. I feel much more weight to use the 'right' ability than any other MMO I've ever played, and a big part of using the 'right' ability lies in understanding the fight. This makes the game far less 'go through your rotation based' and just thought-provoking enough to make you forget you're even waiting 2.5 seconds between spells and it's wonderful.

   The game has a unique system in which 100% of the content the game contains can be completed on one single character. Every class, job, craft, quest, etc can be completed on one character to the point where there is genuinelly no practical reason to ever make a second. This makes for a unique attachment to that one special character who will likely be with you from beginning to end. All classes (including crafts) can be changed at a whim (outside of dungeons and PvP) by simply changing your weapon. You're given a bonus 25 slots per gear slot to hold every single piece and an easy 'gear set' system to quickly swap between entire sets of gear for your variety of classes.

  FFXIV has a pretty decent story with likeable characters and hit-or-miss voice acting. The only major complaint is how you're supposed to be the 'hero of light'... along with all the other thousands of players on your server. Even looking past that, it delivers a classical Final Fantasy adventure that hits all the right notes possible in the MMO setting.

   Leveling is rather easy and straightforward; but at the same time allows for an impressive amount of freedom in how you want to go about it at all. Your first class/job will primarily follow the main story line supplemented by FATEs (randomly spawned group content in the world) and dungeon queues to level at a solid pace. The pacing was excellent and was a rather mild curve in the time between levels as you progress. Part of what makes leveling great is that after progressing a little bit into the game you gain access to 'Duty Roulette', which allows you to queue for a random dungeon and upon completetion, receive a tremendous surge in xp on top of the already solid dungeon xp. This allows people on time restraints to level at a very reasonable pace as all you really need is about 35 minutes. After having one max level class, all future classes gain +100% xp to almos everything, partly because they dont get the main story and partly to speed you along.

  This is an MMO with a definite PvE focus, as the dungeons are execellently crafted progression of difficulty from the start to the end. A complaint does lie in the first set of dungeons aquired very early on as they were very devoid of mechanics and give a bad impression of future content. Lategame PvE offers a multitude of challenge tiers to accomadate what you as a player are looking to do. Duty Finder raids, unlike other MMO counterparts, don't offer an easy mode, and its nice to see the game respect the playerbase by demanding a minimum skill requirement to start getting your hands on decent gear pieces.

   A special mention should go out to this games crafting system. While earlier I mentioned this game has a strong sense of polish to the genre, this area was given a revamp compared to virtually every other MMO with a focus of creating depth, choices, strategy, and a purpose. The crafts are actually classes with their own gear avaiable to them to boast the crafting potentional. Every craft class has their unique spells used during the hard-to-describe act of actually crafting, which plays almost like a classical turn based game balancing many factors such as the progress towards actually finishing the item vs the actual quality of it, among other factors. Craft classes also have certain abilities that benefit other crafts, encouraging you to do them all even if you only really want to use one. Honestly if you've ever wanted to go hard on some crafts, this is DEFINITELY the game to do it.

   On a final note, this game has the best soundtrack and the most cinematic, epic bosses in any MMO I've played. I genuinelly don't want to really spoil any of by showing you, but it's pretty freaking great.

Pros
+ Single-character system builds strong bond with your player character.
+ Content that will appeal to any audience that already likes the MMO genre, and many newcomers (are there still any?)
+ Combat that requires some actual mental usage regarding what abilities you're using.
+ Best MMO on a console (but you're reading this on steam...)
+ Great story that blends into the game almost seamlessely.
+ Heavily teamwork-based group PvE content.
+ The content updates are HUGE. The latest one (3.2) required a hefty time investment just to read through all the patch notes.
+ Heavy timesink game based around progressing the overall state of your character rather than locking you behind time/grindgates. Always something to do~
+ Most fun I've had crafting in an MMO to date.
+ Amazing soundtrack that makes bosses feel larger than life. Many bosses have multiple songs, with one even having 5 whole songs. FIVE SONGS!
+ System in place to help new players learn the game, from decent tutorials to a whole network of matching new players with highly experienced ones for guidance.
+ Amazing community from my personal experience.

Cons
- There's a large divide between emptier and fuller servers. Definitely do your research before commiting to a server.
- Early game dungeons are pretty awful.
- Endgame gear/stat choices for each job is very linear. This is lessened since you can play all 13 classes on 1 character.
- The gathering classes are really runescape-y in their grind... but I mean theres not much you can do with collecting rocks.
- Some of the voice acting in English sucks. Some of it is pretty great. But mostly mediocre.
- When you reach level 50 theres a 100 quest slog to get through before you can start the Heavensward (50->60 content.) It's pretty rough, not gonna lie. At least you only have to do it on one character!

Closing thoughts: This game is epitome of taking the fundamentals of a game type and making them perfect. If you're feeling a little burned out by games like WoW or any of its plentiful clones, it may be time to give FFXIV a whirl. If you're just looking for a really comfy game to play and always have stuff to do when you log on, this game is great for that. If you want that classic hardcore PvE content found in the earlier days of WoW, this game delivers on that front too!

40 weeks into my first game and it no longer feels insanely hard. Its actually a nice blend of very unforgiving yet very patient.  

My graveyard is stuffed full of dead and failed heroes. I ran out of money several times. I lost whole parties of my favourites. I invested in new weapons and skills only for them to die on the next mission. Sometimes missions go well only to deliver so many diseases and flaws randomly at the end that financial diastser arrives anyway. Thats the unforgiving bit.

Once you embrace the idea that things are going to go badly, heroes are going to die, money is going to run out regularly, the patient bit of the game starts to become clear: there is no crushing difficulty curve ramping up in the background. A disastrous mission or even three or four in a row does not kill the game... your town upgrades remain, new adventurers arrive every week and you can always train and equip another team. And you can (almost) always retreat. 

Dont overcommit to a mission or any one character. Dont pressure yourself into thinking every mission has to succeed and it starts to make sense and the game becomes hugely addictive fun.

Thus far, in my opinion, Paradox has not yet released a single DLC that I thought was overpriced or useless, and that goes for Hearts of Iron IV, Stellaris, Cities: Skylines, all of which have excellent DLC, HoI4 developing further its mechanics to enrich all the playable possibilities in the ww2 scenario, Stellaris giving an awesome space strategy experience with colorful laser battles, and no doubt the Colossal step above city building games that is Cities: Skylines, leaving All of the other city builders in the dust.
Hear my words, on top of absolutely fantastic initial releases, Paradox does DLCs just the right way, and they're often on sale.

"Buchen Sie jetzt bei The-Forest-Tours und wir bietet Ihnen: Eine einmalige Höhlen-Expedition mit erfahrenen Guides, einen "freundlichen Austausch" mit den Höhlenbewohnern, gemütliches Essen zusammengekauert in engen Höhlengängen, sowie als Bonus finden wir endlich dieses drecks Gör. Frühbucher erhalten ein Katana. Taucherfahrung vorausgesetzt."

->So oder so ähnlich könnte eine Werbeanzeige für eine Höhlenbesichtigung in The Forest lauten. xD

Als ich mir das Spiel bereits Ende 2014 gekauft habe, war ich sofort von der wunderschönen Grafik, Baumechanik und dem Spielprinzip begeistert. Als dann noch der Coop-Modus released wurde, konnte ich mit Kumpels gemeinsam Lager bauen und diese vor den Kanibalen verteidigen und es hat immer mehr Spaß gemacht. Außerdem kamen immer mehr Tiere und Items ins Spiel und die Crafting-Möglichkeiten wurden stetig erweitert. 
Es gab bald die Möglichkeit Höhlen zu erforschen und unter Zuhilfenahme von Kletterhaken und Taucherausrüstung konnte man bis zu einem bestimmten Punkt vor einem großen Tor sehr tief in das verzweigt Höhlensystem vordringen. Dort ging es aber zu dem Entwicklungs-Zeitpunkt noch nicht weiter. Wir hatten aber trotzdem in einer Gruppe dann riesigen Spaß sämtliche Höhlen zu erforschen und hatten so grandiose Momente wie z.B., wo mir alle nach einem längeren Tauchgang in den Höhlen direkt in dem See, an dem wir unser Lager errichtet hatten, wieder herauskamen und von der unterirdischen Verbindung nicht wussten.

Ich habe mit einigen Freunden, dann vor wenigen Wochen seit längerer Zeit mal wieder mit The Forest angefangen und wir hatten viel Spaß beim Errichten mehrerer Lager. Leider gibt es immer noch einige Bugs im Coop, sodass z.B. nur der Host ab einer bestimmten Anzahl an Bauelemente, diese sehen kann oder dass das Spiel einfach manchmal abstürtzt, wenn man ab und zu speichert, ist das aber kein großes Problem.

Nachdem das Haupt-Lager größtenteils fertig gestellt war und wir schon recht gut ausgestatte waren, bin ich mit einigen Leuten aufgebrochen, die Höhlen erneut zu erforschen und ich muss sagen seit Release hat sich storytechnisch einiges getan. Was ihr hinter dem verschlossenen Tor in der Tiefe erlebt ist der Wahnsinn und habe ich in noch keinem anderem Spiel erlebt - vorallem nicht mit gerechnet. Als Survival-Game alleine ist The Forest, meiner Meinung nach, schon ganz vorne und als ein Spiel dieser Art auch noch mit so einer genialen Story, ist es absolut empfehlenswert - für so einen geringen Preis sowieso. Andere AAA-Titel könnten sich da mal eine Scheibe abschneiden!
Für die wenigen negativen Stimmen sag' ich nur: Ihr UNWISSENDEN, ihr habt nicht mal nur ansatzweise das gesamte Spiel gesehen. Es ist klar, dass das Spiel jetzt schon sehr lange im EA ist, was nicht unbedingt was Schlechtes ist, denn das kleine Entwickler-Team aktualisiert, fixed und erweitert immer noch häufig das Spiel. (Es gibt sogar einen Counter im Menü, wann der nächste Patch ansteht). Auch klar ist, dass das Spiel im Coop selbst auf "hart" relativ einfach ist und man gemeinsam die stärkeren Mutanten recht erfolgreich bezwingen kann. Da wird es bestimmt auch noch ein Balancing geben. Wenn man allerdings alleine von mehreren Mutanten umzingelt ist, kann es dennoch sehr schnell zum Tode führen.

Ich bin sehr begeistert von dem Spiel und hätte eine derartige Story in einem Indie-Survival-Game niemals erwartet. In keinem anderem Spiel habe ich die Story auf diese tolle Weise bisher erlebt und The Forest ist noch nicht mal fertig. 

Wer auf Erforschen, Craften, Lagerbau in einer Idylle, die schnell mal in eine beklemmende Atmosphäre umschwingt und eine kinoreife Story rund um Kanibalen-Mutanten und einem verlorenen Sohn steht, der kommt um The Forest nicht herum.

我要向大家推荐这款游戏《波西亚时光》，我在这款游戏刚刚发行测试版时就已经入手，并且已经玩了176小时了。可以说，我是见着《波西亚时光》的成长，从第一版内的不完善，剧情欠缺，地图不完整，到如今的正式版1.0的发布。在此，我希望这款游戏能够受到玩家的欢迎，并且希望创作者的不断更新。

在这里，我还想向开发者提一些小小的建议，希望能够改善。
1.希望能够稍微修改一下家园的大小，因为我个人觉得家园的大小在中后期已经基本满足不了我的需求，工厂，房屋，马棚，建造台等占得地方太大了，这样就无法使用道具装饰家园。
2.支线任务的欠缺比较大，希望能够完善支线任务。
3.在个个NPC的家里面除座椅外，并没有其他的功能，使得非常漂亮温馨的家只能观看，白白浪费了那么好的资源。
4.游戏中的“我”的样貌太过抽象化，希望美工能在游戏中“我”的嘴唇、眉毛、鼻子、眼睛上多下些功夫，是任务更加美观，也让中国大陆的玩家看着更加顺眼。（在正式版1.0更新后的角色样貌可以说无法达让玩家看着顺眼，在此之前还是比较中国化的）
5.在一些看似可以进入的场景中增加可进入的场景，使游戏的体验更加完美
6.希望在除波西亚城镇之外再沙漠，高地，沼泽在建立几个比较大的城镇场景，使游戏的建筑密度与小镇特色更加凸显。
7.希望游戏中的可互动的建筑更多一些，更加便捷一些，增强游戏体验。
8.希望游戏内置一个游戏内道具，材料，服装，场所，NPC住址，材料具体掉落场景、任务等一套完全的图鉴，省的游戏玩家在百度上找来找去浪费时间了。（这是我十分强烈希望的一个功能，能省不少时间，对于肝《波西亚时光》来说可以是非常便利的一个小功能）
9.希望游戏内能在此吧硬木转化为木头，这样最基础的材料就不会造成不足还要浪费时间去砍伐了。
10.希望在家园中，加入吊顶，这样就可以吧美丽的水晶吊灯，风扇等悬吊的装饰物装饰家园了。
11.希望后面的更新可以更新更多的服装，是游戏的角色更加具有个性，并且可以给NPC加入不同的服装，是NPC在不同时间穿着打扮不一样，使得游戏体验更加具有随机性与个性。
12.希望游戏内加入股市系统，让玩家可以在肝游戏时增加一个赚钱的渠道，让游戏更加具有可玩性。
13.希望在游戏的小镇中增加灯光效果，让夜晚波西亚小镇更加美轮美奂。
14.在游戏中增加一个统计板块，可以向主线完结后的那样总结在波西亚的时光。
15.希望新的坐骑飞天猪可以向小米平衡车一样可以跟随，这样就不用打哪里都要亲自驾驶飞天猪了。也希望飞天猪在平面可以加速并且力气条可以更加耐用，而不是点一下就没了。

以上就是我对《波西亚时光》的建议，希望《波西亚时光》这款有戏可以更加完美，让中国人自己的RPG游戏迈向世界的大舞台。

Undertale is a quirky millennial fairytale. With its MIDI soundtrack, pixel art, endearing NPCs and cosy villages, it is teeming with charm. And despite exuding the warmth of your nana's handknitted woollen jumpers, the game fails to provide a compelling reason to keep moving forward other than finding the next easter egg or zany encounter. Overall, Undertale is a comforting lockdown game that I would have quit under better circumstances.

Do I recommend this game overall? Yes. Definitely Yes.

Before kicking off with the Pros, and Cons, I would like to emphasise what an incredible job the devs have done on this game. At the first initial thought of a fully open-world Witcher game, I was very skeptical, however I feel that this game deserves a positive review from me, and what seems like the majority of the community due to the following positive aspects.

[b] Positives	[/b]
- Stunning Visuals (Even from a low settings viewpoint it is still quite amazing / From an ultra settings viewpoint? Suprised my eyes didn't bleed.)
- Interesting Story (Personal Opinion)
- Likeable Characters (Zoltan, and let's admit it we sort of like Dandelion) 
- Gwent! (The only game I have ever witnessed come out of a minigame)
- Interesting References / 'Easter Eggs' 
- Breathtaking Environments
- Perfected Ambient Sounds
- Multiple Endings (No spoilers for you) 
- Extensive Skill Tree
- I wish I could spend a few hours in the sun and get a beard as lovely as Geralt's

[b] Negatives	[/b]
- Very little game to game domino effect (Choices in one game have little impact on the next)
- A few bugs (What can be expected from a game of this multitude)
- Battle system could do with some improvements (Personal Opinion)
- Can't find that many negatives

[b] Conclusion	[/b]

If you're a man like me and have very little time to play games, perhaps invest your money elsewhere because the likelihood is that you will require alot of free time to appreciate this game fully. However, I do feel that the game meets that standard I have which justifies the price tag.

[b] Side Note	[/b]

I do not own any of the DLC, however I would be interested in hearing what people have to say about it! I suppose that also makes this review relevant to only the base game, otherwise that would be biased! ;) So please take that into account.

Edit: Since writing this review, I have now played all the DLC for this game. I can confidently say that all of them offer a gripping story along with breathtaking environments for you to explore. I fully recommend them.

This game has easily become one of my favourites of all time. I was surprised at how cool it made playing as a bug feel. The gameplay is fun and the controls are tight and responsive. The large array of bosses and enemies introduce new challenges throughout the game, and learning the right technique to defeat them helps keep the gameplay fresh. The atmosphere really makes the world come to life thanks to the amazing sounds (both soundtrack and sound effects) and visuals. The attention to detail really shows when you play the game, and the story had me constantly coming back to learn more about the world the game inhabits. The game uses its open world perfectly so that you always feel like you have something to do but you don't feel forced in one direction like in more linear games. This makes the story feel more like a natural result of your actions as you explore the world. You really feel connected to the world and the characters in it. As I think has been said in other reviews, the game has a lot of content for its price, and the devs are still adding more content post-release in the form of free DLCs so I'd say it's a pretty good deal. I would have definitely been willing to pay more for something of this calibre, though the low price is what made me willing to try it out in the first place.

Grand Theft Auto V, as well as GTA Online, (although one can argue that they are the same game, just different modes), is a pretty good game. My review says that I "recommend" this game; in truth, I only chose that because there is no middle option. The game itself is fun, with many game modes, missions, and fun stuff to do. However, there are many, many problems with the game. 

1. Hackers
On GTA Online, hackers are a serious problem. basically when you join a session, you have aa 50/50 chance of having a hacker on the server. Now, I am going to say this; not all hackers are bad, and not all hackers ruin the gaming experience. The problem is with the few that do cause issues. For example, the ones that repeatedly kill everyone on the server, or the ones that turn people into Christmas trees. These are huge problems. R* just makes it worse by lumping both hackers and victims together. My friend once was playing GTA Online, when a hacker dropped about $3,000,000 onto his character. At first he was overjoyed;that is, until he was banned for "hacking in money" a couple days later. All in all, the support for the hacking problem needs to be fixed.

2. Shark Cards
Making money in GTA isn't exactly difficult, but it sure isn't easy. Shark cards are R* way for players to spend real money for ingame currency. This wouldn't be so bad, if only the shark  cards gave more money. In the game, there is a vehicle, a plane to be precise, that costs $10,000,000 of the games currency. The largest shark card you are able to purchase costs $99.99, and gives you $8,500,000 in game dollars. Let me rephrase that; There is an object, a virtual object, in a virtual game, that costs more than $100 real dollars. For that much money, you could buy a couple new games. Shark cards are probably the biggest reason for the hacking problem. If money was easier to obtain, there would be no need to cheat it in. The whole money making system could use a rework.

Your interaction with the world depends on you, you can build one base, or move like a nomad with just the cyclops. I myself built like 2 full bases just because I liked the base building part.

Subnautica is the only survival game I have played to completion, it has a story, and you are not there just to fuck around in a sandbox. I. Love. This. Game. IT IS AWESOME!!! One Finger Death Punch is like this: Take a rythm game, remove every button except for 2 of them, and make every correct button press kill/or cause unbelievable pain to someone else. I love that every single button press matters. If you miss you give up the chance of getting a good medal and also you leave yourself vunerable to attacks, giving away your perfect as well. And the best part about this game is that it never gets repetitive , as it keeps itself fresh by throwing different twists to an otherwise simple formula. You got regular mob rounds where you beat the ever loving s#@! out of some poor fellows (about 100-200 of them). You got boss rounds where you fight one on one with another enemy. You got defender rounds where you defend against a volley of knifes. You got dagger/bomb rounds, where you have to time each shot so the enemy never gets close enough. And then... there are Lightsword/Nunchaku rounds. Where you can just kick ass while the enemies speed up the longer you play. It just never gets boring and it has the right amount of challenge all the way through. Sometimes you might get frustrated at the speed because you gotta pull off some really impressive moves just to move on. But it still is motivating. You may play a round and get a silver medal and the game doesn't make you think 'Well thats good enough'. Instead it makess you think 'Silver? Pffft! I can do way better than that! Bring it on!'. And when you're 'in the zone' you get to do some insane moves! Once i killed a guy who was holding a throwing knife and a ball of death, I threw the knife to the left killing a dude, then I kicked the ball, it bounced against a wall and hit the last guy on the screen! Or one time when I threw a spear and hit two guys, killed a guy on the left and the spear went through the guy behind him! Just buy it and see what crazy things you can pull of yourself.

     What is Undertale? Undertale is a role-playing video game created by indie developer Toby Fox. The player controls a child who has fallen into the Underground: a large, secluded region under the surface of the Earth, separated by a magic barrier. The player meets various monsters during the journey back to the surface. Some monsters might engage the player in a fight. The combat system involves the player navigating through mini-bullet hell attacks by the opponent. They can opt to pacify or subdue monsters in order to spare them instead of killing them. These choices affect the game, with the dialogue, characters, and story changing based on outcomes.

     Outside of some artwork, Fox developed the entirety of the game by himself, including the script and music. The game took inspiration from several sources, including the Brandish, Mario & Luigi, and Mother role-playing series, bullet hell shooter series Touhou Project, role-playing game Moon: Remix RPG Adventure, and British comedy show Mr. Bean. Originally, Undertale was meant to be two hours in length and was set to be released in mid-2014. However, development was delayed over the next three years.

     The game was released for Microsoft Windows and OS X in September 2015. It was also ported to Linux in July 2016, PlayStation 4 and PlayStation Vita in August 2017, and the Nintendo Switch in September 2018. The game was acclaimed for its thematic material, intuitive combat system, musical score, originality, story, dialogue, and characters. The game sold over one million copies and was nominated for multiple accolades and awards. Several gaming publications and conventions listed Undertale as game of the year. The first chapter of a related game by Fox, Deltarune, was released in October 2018.

Rant time. These are purely my own gripes with the game. They do not make the game bad. These are mainly just QoL changes or additions that should have been added before the 1.0 release.

Physics/Terrain & Fall Damage

The game's physics system is horrible. Sometimes, you get flung off of teammates or terrain and fly off into a random direction and die from fall damage. Using Scout's grappling hook will get you killed a lot because of the terrain being weird and uneven and the physics system thinking you're inside the terrain, causing you to be launched tens of meters away. Just try jumping on a barrel in the pre-mission starting area and you'll see exactly what I mean.

Speaking of fall damage, if you fall more than a meter, you end up losing half your shields. Either tone down the amount of damage you receive from fall damage or increase the height on how far you can fall before you receive damage. For a game with a lot of verticality, you sure do die way more from fall damage than from the actual enemies.

Spawn Rates & Locations

Sometimes, things just won't spawn that are supposed to. For example, when there's a mission to repair some machines, sometimes not all the machine parts spawn, so there aren't enough parts to actually complete the mission.

Sometimes, you will traverse the entire level searching for the full amount of minerals to mine and turn in, and there aren't enough spawned.

Sometimes, reward stations won't spawn either, so you will find 2 batteries that will open a vault with an unlockable cosmetic item inside and the actual station won't spawn. 

The worst one is when the objective is to kill 3 specific boss enemies and sometimes only 2 actually spawn in the entire level, so you can't complete the level.

Connection

Connections are always laggy. Even with low ping (20-30 ping) the game still lags a lot in online games, sometimes I would freeze in the air when my ping was only around 30 or 40, which is still pretty low.

Team Chat

Team voice chat is almost non-existent, those that do use voice chat are usually only using it to tell you if they died. No one is calling out anything. This isn't the game's fault, just an observation.

Ping System

Ping system (holding control and pressing left-click will ping an item or a specific area) is very non-intrusive, which is horrible for this type of game because it's all about teamwork and communication. Someone will be grabbed by a a grabber enemy and/or get downed and you won't realize for a minute or 2 until the person is typing in chat that they are down because there's no real attention-grabbing sound to let you know that someone needs help.

A perfect example of this done right is Vermintide 2. When a teammate is grabbed by an assassin character in that game, there's an audible sound and a bright outline on the enemy AND teammate signifying that they are captured and need help. Multiple times have I been stuck in the air by a ceiling leech, being stabbed over and over and yet the team doesn't realize it until I'm already down.

This is also just a problem with the HUD/ UI, for example: teammates and friendly machines should have outlines on at all times, or at least have the option turn that on in the settings. Also, when pinging an enemy, their outline should not go away over time, like it is now. It should be permanent unless you move too far away from the enemy or the enemy dies. 

Pinging the Molly (the walking mine cart that you turn your minerals into) or any friendly items/machines and teammates should go away over time, but not enemies. Pinging an enemy and pinging an item or mineral should also be considered different, meaning pinging one should not cancel the other. There's shouldn't be a 1 ping limit, maybe 3-5 objects or enemies should be pingable at the same time for each person.

Also, just give the option to keep the mineral page on all the time. I don't want to have to keep pressing CTRL just to see what minerals we've collected, where the mine cart is, where my teammates are, where the enemy grabber is, just keep those on. Keeping teammate/machine outlines on all the time should be an option in the settings.

Main Starting Area & Walking

The main pre-mission waiting area is quite large, so the stations where you change your gear or make weapon upgrades/modifiers are farther apart than they need to be. It tends to be a lot of walking. It should instead be different keyboard shortcuts that open the weapon/crafting/cosmetic menus even if you aren't near the physical station.

This is especially annoying when prestiging your characters (every 25 levels you can prestige and earn a border with stars on your character's icon, signifying your time put into that character) as you have to go to a separate room on a different floor, that you have to wait for a lift to take you to called the memorial room just to prestige, wasting a lot of time walking, as well as an unskippable cutscene after you finally pay the fee to prestige where the radio comms guy will tell you the same thing every time about how they are proud of you for leveling up that lasts a good 2 minutes.

There also shouldn't be a fee when prestiging in the first place. The point of prestiging is that, by doing so, your overall level is increased (there's 2 progression bars in this game, you character level which resets to level 1 when you prestige, and your overall level, which keep increasing as long as you keep leveling up) and you unlock a new, different mode (called Deep Dives) where you can unlock matrix cores, which are essentially weapon upgrades/modifiers. Eventually, as time goes on and you prestige more and more, you also unlock missions that reward you with cosmetic helmets and interchangeable pickaxe parts that are also purely cosmetic.

Those cosmetic items are not worth it. Because they are just cosmetic items, if you don't care about cosmetics, then prestiging would simply be a waste of time for you. The Deep Dives, however, ARE worth prestiging for but you only need to prestige once to unlock them. That shouldn't cost you thousands of coins and minerals just to unlock a completely optional mode in the first place. At the very least, your first prestige should not cost anything. Afterwards shouldn't either because you are just wasting money and minerals for nothing more than making a number go up. Grindy.

At the Abyss Bar, having only 1 worthwhile specialty beer that gives you a buff is not smart. Sometimes, the specialty beer you happen to get a beer that gives you an increased drop rate for a specific mineral that may not even be in the mission you are going on. If you are going on a mission to collect Eggs, and the specialty beer you get is to have more Morkite drop when you mine it, then the specialty beer is useless, as Morkite is a specific mineral that only shows up when you go on missions where the actual main objective is to collect Morkite in the first place.

There needs to be a variety of beers you can buy at the bar that aren't just multiple gag beers that do nothing except make you fart, or breath fire, or freeze in place, or make you small. These don't do anything in the missions themselves. They are just there to make you laugh while waiting for the mission to start or just mess around. They are amusing maybe the 1st time you try them and then you already know the punchline, so it becomes a waste of materials just to use them.

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Gameplay loop is fun and addictive though.

Gunplay is solid and the guns feel powerful and they really pack a punch when fully upgraded.

Overall, it's a great game to pass the time, with some minor flaws.

Again, these are just my gripes with the game and you should ignore this rant if you just want a fun game to play with friends, because it is exactly that, a fun game to play with friends.

Just needs more improvement that probably should have been implemented before going 1.0.

review:
Could be great, but it is just silly. As if the makers of this game never shot an arrow, slinged a rock, handled swords, spears and shields, let alone read about historical battle formations, tactics, campaigns and battles, and how battles played out in general. It could take hours to break a phalanx, in this game it takes 5 seconds.

Battles that in history lasted hours, you can now play in 50 seconds, if you have the APM (actions per minute) for it in clicking power. Formations are superfast, yet they tire immediately. Arrows have tracers behing them. If an enemy convoy gets ambushed while on quick march through a forest, it will still have assembled trebuchets ready to fire massive boulders that are magically supplied to it.

Also the size of a Roman legion was around 4000-5000 + equal amount of auxiliary allies. Usually two legions were dispatched to deal with just about anything. No more, sometimes only one. In this game you can wield only an "army" of around 1500-3000 men, and if they march together, the other one takes time to arrive, yet it can arrive from behind the enemy? Then all goes wild with the control groups.

Cavalry are invincible, even against phalanxes that have their pike ranks deployed to face them. However they always stop, unless they are in diamond formation (which they cannot form "on the move" but have to stop to form).

Water fights are such BS that you will want to auto them, not to mention sieging major cities. Just gather enough numbers and let computer deal with that glitchy madness.

I expect so much from this, but it seems to have gone worse with every update. Last fix was "adding scorpion pot ballistas"- Really? No need to answer that.

(This is for the NA server, I have never played on any other servers, mainly because I live in the NA place, and because it's hard enough to figure out things without trying to learn korean on the fly on top of that)

Is Black Desert more confusing than trying to watch an episode of Twin Peaks without knowing anything about it? - Yes

Is is a PvP centered game? - It can be, but I would say you need to be in a guild that does a lot of node wars.  If not, the PvP is minimal.  You'll get as much PvP as you want, from nearly zero to omgzorz why are these guards killing me why why.

Do you have to spend money beyond the initial game?  Absolutly not.  However, $100 for the largest pearl pack certainly makes a big difference.  Save your money for special sales, they happen all the time.  For instance, there is usually a big pet pack at halloween, and the black friday sale after thanksgiving.  Pets will vastly improve your play experience as there are only a token few free ones here and there (you want 4, at a minimum)  Wait for sales, patience is a virtue.

If you don't like crafting, you can purchase almost everything off the auction house.  The game is designed for crafting though, and it's not bad at all once you figure out what the heck you're doing.  You can have an army of peons scratching in the dirt for everything from wood to pumpkins, while only having to throw them vast quantities of beer.  So much beer.    It could be called Beer Distribution Online.

If you are AFK for long periods, you can still be playing BDO the entire time.  You can fish afk, you can turn raw metal into melted raw metal, you can drive horses around until they get stuck on a rock because you failed to make sure the path you chose was rock free.

Item upgrading - probably the biggest source of frustration in this game.  You will fail at upgrades ALL THE TIME.  You will curse the people at Pearl Abyss, you will call them terrible things.  You may possibly rage quit.  Upgrading is the source of all that is evil in the world.  Your friend will upgrade with no effort and shove the results in your face.  Don your tinfoil cone of shame, you'll need it.

In summation - this is the most single player MMO I've ever played.  You can pretty much look at other players as computer AI with a penchant for occasionally killing you for no good reason (only after level 49, and you should level beyond that, there's almost no reason not too).  You can't trade with anyone for the most part.  You can join guilds (definitly worth doing for the perks) and group up but there are not really any "dungeons" per se, and the boss raids are a huge ffa, where you'll die a lot if you don't know how any particular world boss operates (they smash in your face, for free).

All in all I really like BDO.  I get far more out of it than I ever did playing WoW, I get more satisfaction than I ever did playing Everquest.  It is not the game for everyone.  If you do not enjoy extreme tedium at times, or RNGesus slapping you about the face-head-chest-neck you won't get much enjoyment from BDO.  

Buy it, watch lots of videos (there is a ton of outdated info out there, things have vastly changed, become an internet Sherlock Holmes to get current info, you'll be glad you did) and give it a good hundred or so hours, then you can decide if it's for you.  You will be completely lost for a while.  It gets better, knowledge is power, reading is fundamental, the more you know, reading rainbow, g.i.joe, porkchop sandwiches.

app_name: South Park™: The Stick of Truth™
review:
Just finished thoroughly playing through this game. It is absolutely brilliant. A lot of reviews remarked on how short it was - I disagree. It really isn't that short at all. If you like, or have ever liked South Park, this game is for you. If you don't like the humor even slightly - I wouldn't get it.

I normally don't giggle at games, but I found myself laughing rather often through the game. It is far more funny than even the best episodes offer. Nearly every character or sets of characters from the entire series is either referenced or shows up at some point. Nearly every area of south park is used at some point, and some of the plot twists or surprises actually left me delighted.

Normally a game will fail to keep me interested or engaged throughout itself, but this game is extremely dynamic. It changes ALL the time. Goals change, areas change, scenery, enemy types, gameplay changes - it is WONDERFUL. There is SO much packed into this game, it certainly shows me why it had such a high initial price tag. I got it on sale for a little over $10 and it is worth far far more than that. A great game, one that I cannot praise enough.

Buy it, you seriously won't regret it. It's very fun, and only gets more and more fun and engaging as the game goes on. There's a TON of content, and characters to play with.

I usually don’t write reviews for stuff, but I am a diehard Borderlands fan and would like to share my opinion after seeing some of the reviews on here. I will start with my overall opinion on the game followed by the most important points. I am assuming that if you are reading this you would have at least played Borderlands 2, if not start with that game before Borderlands 3. This will be spoiler free, get ready for a wall of text!

TLDR: The story is no where near as bad as people make it out to be, I enjoyed it a lot and it doesn’t deserve the massive flak it is getting, I personally believe the story is the second best in the franchise. The NPCs are hit or miss, some are some nice new additions, and some are not so welcomed. Overall, the gameplay is exactly what you would expect out of a borderlands game, and with some of the new weapon changes (explained below) it makes for a fun new experience. Overall, I would give the game a 9/10. 

The story: The story is not well received from the community, read most of the steam reviews and the story is always criticized. If you go into this game expecting a story on par or better than BL2, you will probably be let down. Borderlands 2 is the best story out of the FPS Borderlands game, and in my opinion, I do not think that BL2s story will ever be matched by Gearbox. That being said, BL3 is a very good story, the antagonists are great (IMO), side characters are mostly good (a couple of exceptions), and the missions themselves are decent. The cutscenes are well done (30 fps though), and the new and returning characters are nice to see. I cannot stress this enough though, the story is no where near as bad as everyone says it is, if you liked any of the FPS Borderlands games so far, the story in BL3 is about what you would expect, and IMO I thought it was the second best story in the franchise (Behind BL2). 

The NPCs: New and returning NPCs are present in BL3, the usual characters that we are used to at this point, plus some from Tales from the Borderlands, and new characters all together. The main new characters are the antagonists, which a lot of people do not seem to like. People seem to compare the antagonists to Jack, which IMO is unfair to the new antagonists. They are obviously different than Jack, and they are better and worse in some aspects, but they should not be compared to arguably one of the best antagonists of all time. Its like comparing Heath to Joaquin for their Joker roles, they are both different and should be treated as such. The story has some characters that are definitely not the best, but that’s every game. I despised Tina in BL2, and there isn’t a character in BL3 that is nearly as bad as she was in BL2. 

General Gameplay: The gameplay itself is exactly as you would expect a borderlands game to be. The new playable characters are fun and each of them now has quite a bit of variety, leading to great replay ability. The combat is fast paced and is very engaging, and there isn’t really a point where the combat isn’t fun (expect maybe vehicle combat). Legendary guns are way more common now, farming them is a lot easier than past games (especially considering more than one legendary can drop from a single kill). The gun manufacturers have all gotten some changes as listed below, along with if they got a buff or a nerf from BL2. These are not legendary guns or red text guns, just the manufactures new “base” gun, legendary guns can obviously vary from these:

Maliwan: Guns now need to charge up before the first shot comes out, but they also usually come with two elements that you can switch between with a press of a button. (Nerfed but also buffed)

Jakobs: Different guns have different reloads, some you load one bullet at a time, some have a stripper clip, some have a speed loader etc. Jakobs reloads are the only thing changed. (Slight nerf in some situations) 

Vladof: The main firing function is unchanged; however, they now have an under-barrel attachment like a shotgun or a grenade launcher etc. (Buff)

Torgue: Torgue is the same, however they also now have an alternative firing mode “Sticky” in which shots stick to and enemy then blow up later. (Buff)

DAHL: DAHL is no longer restricted to burst fire, DAHL guns now can switch their firing mode between full auto/semi auto/burst, depending on your gun you have, the firing mode will have two of the three modes previously stated. (Buff)

Hyperion: Stayed unchanged, however you now get a shield when ADSing that does different things depending on the gun. (Buff)

Tediore: Tediore is the same gimmick its always been, now they are just more things that the guns do when you reload them. If you liked old Tediore you will love new Tediore. (Change)

Atlas: Atlas is back! Atlas has two fire modes, one marks enemies with a shot, then the other mode will automatically hit your target when you shoot (pretty much) anywhere. 

COV: A new contender, COV guns need to “start up” before you can shoot them. Think of it as starting your lawnmower, just faster and more reliable. COV guns use ammo straight from your inventory, no need to reload. However, after a certain number of shots, the gun will overheat in which you basically have to reload.

Darkest Dungeon is a beautiful nightmare. Red Hook means it when it says at the start that this game is about making the best of a bad situation.

The art, narration, and story are all fantastically made to immerse you in this Lovecraftian world. The gameplay is fun and strategic relying on your ability to properly use positioning, skill sets, and turn timing. You'll also need to carefully manage your more-flawed-by-the-day heroes and a crumbled estate. Overall, the name of the game here is proper planning for the horrors you're going to face. If you make sure to bring the provisions and heroes you need to succeed in a dungeon then things should work out alright. Of course, learning what's best for the dungeons will take some time. 

One thing to note is that people tend to point at the RNG in this game saying that it's too unfair. However, I don't think people recognize how often the RNG works in your favor. For example, there were several different times when I'd be starting a fight and suddenly have my heroes do 3 critical strikes on different enemies in a single turn. Things don't always go your way either, but there are so many ways you can mitigate that through heroes' skills, items, or trinkets. 

Some tips for anyone struggling or just starting out:

1. Upgrade your stagecoach first. In the beginning it's much easier to just dismiss heroes when they get too many bad quirks or are too high stress and hire new ones.

2. Bleed skills work well in the Warrens and the Weald (and the Courtyard). Blight skills work well in the Ruins and the Cove.

3. Antiquarians will help you when you're low on gold. They increase how much gold can stack by 750. So, having one in your party increases the maximum gold stack from 1750 to 2500. They also find antiques that are worth a lot. JUST MAKE SURE TO USE THEM WHEN INTERACTING WITH OBJECTS.

4. Don't try Champion missions until you're able to do four level 5 heroes with fully upgraded skills and armor/weapons. Those dungeons are no joke.

Most of all, just remember (as you'll often be told)... Overconfidence is a slow and insidious killer.
