It's reasonably entertaining, but the leveling and crafting systems are pretty tedious and are very clearly designed to keep you grinding in order to use anything interesting.  You run into typical greifers on most servers, including some admins who use the console to antagonize people, so the multiplayer is more or less what you'd expect from the genre. The building system is pretty wonky since it uses a grid/tile snap mechanic, which you have to fit into the terrain and learn all the quirks of by trial and error (lots of clipping issues, mismatched snap points, and poor meshing with the terrain).  Performance is pretty spotty and not very optimized, some graphics options don't always play well with each other, and multiplayer uses a lot more bandwidth than most games (some of my friends used their whole months service over a weekend).

Both of the core maps have issues with terrain collisions (falling/teleporting through cliffs, hitboxes extending past ledges, levitating rocks/foliage). Dinos will clip into almost everything, causing your dinos to get stuck together or inside wild carnivores, and to rarely teleport through walls. You can travel fast enough to fly through a wall before it has finished loading into the game. If you lose connection to a server while flying your character will dismount and fall to their death upon reconnecting, similar to what happens when the terrain hasn't finished loading when you connect to the server. Very fast land animals (like alpha raptors) can run up near-shear cliffs, terrain, and rocks.  Singleplayer isn't very interesting as there isn't a good save management system, and most of the allure to the game comes from playing along with freinds anyway.

The survival aspects are becoming fairly well-developed, and you can set custom values for needs and other multipliers that affect overall difficulty on your own servers. The dino breeding mechanic is interesting, but isn't really useful since it requires you to actively feed the hatchlings over the course of up to 18hours for permanent-tame creatures before they can begin to eat by themselves (10% of the total maturation time). You can build crazy and useful contraptions on mobile platforms (rafts and certain dino saddles), which is great even if you have to deal with the building system. There are lots of areas to explore, but be careful of carnivores that spawn too close to you.

It's a very promising early access title, but it has a lot of quirks with the game. Wildcard pushes through updates fairly regularly, which are usually less than half a gigabyte.  They are a little behind on their projected release date of June 2016, but they are gradually adding things from the planned features list in the game description. It will probably be worth it when they finish up the features list, squash most of the bugs, and make a lot of performance optimizations. There are community mods which have other maps and content developed by the community for free, and Wildcard occasionally bundles some of them into the core game.  They have recently started charging for a DLC pack (game map, unique items, and unique dinos that can then be transferred into other maps) while the game is unfinished, so you should base your decision to purchase on the features and performance already present and not what has been promised in the description. There's no telling when/if you'll actually get the promised features since they were splitting development into other projects even though they were coming up on their projected release. I don't really see the appeal in getting another map that has the same issues as the others, but I'll probably take another look once the game is finished and they decide on what they want to charge for the whole thing.

由于首席设计师是万智牌的创始人，因此Artifact包含了很多MTG的元素，比如色卡，比如轮抽制，比如卡牌买卖（虽然没法直接交换）这让Artifact既拥有了卡组和卡池的丰富性，可能性，又让玩家可以‘经营’这个‘购物车’。

而Dota2的要素也被很好的体现，比如装备系统，比如英雄牌自带的绑定技能和绑定技能卡，再比如三路兵线及带来的各种战略，战术思考。举个例子，我方某一路已经铁定被破的情况下，可以战略放弃这一路，把兵力调往其他两路，而如果对方缺乏换线的机动性，那么可能会导致重兵堆于一路，而被我方分头带线带死，有点像DotaA2种的rat打法。通过战略战术战胜对手是Artifact比起炉石传说的机制（趋向于简单的大压小，以及一些对局和牌组种完全无法预测的随机性）更吸引我的一点。

当然这个游戏才刚刚推出，有很多不完美，不平衡的地方，比如小黑和斧王的imba，一些低费小兵的超模，当然，对于TCG游戏来说，并不是所有的卡都是“有用”的，反过来讲，有些当前环境冷门英雄，冷门卡可能会随着更多的拓展而重新有价值起来（比如黑鸟将来可能就会改动？）。对无氪金玩家的‘不友好’也是为人诟病的一点，但相信随着Artifact的发展，这些问题都会得到一定程度的解决。

They now have base building, and a home planet. But even that has unexpected limitations.

AND, I feel that it’s very important that a multiplayer aspect is added to this game, for example being able to work together with/ trade with/ fly with other players. Honestly that should have been the case from the get go, no matter how unlikely they say it is to meet someone else, you should be able to go to a galactic hub and meet with people to play with. This would add a whole new and exciting aspect to the gameplay of this otherwise secluded feeling game.

But in the meantime, I paid full price for what’s basically and incomplete, early access game.

이제는 사실상 온라인 게임이 되어버렸지만 싱글 기준,
게임 미션의 다양성과 여전한 통수쟁이들에 재미를 느끼고,
여러 주인공이 협력하는 플레이 역시 색달랐으며,
더군다나 패드 부드럽게 찍히는 자동조준과 조작감은 내 심금을 조져놓았다. 

다만 GTA 4에 비해서 안타까운점이 많다.
GTA 4는 어둡고 진지했던 스토리에 비해 당시 미션의 단조로움이 발목을 잡았으나(살인후 도망치기 끝)
이번 GTA 5에는 미션은 다양하나 기본적인 조작이나 시스템적 퇴보가 심각하다.

윾튜브 조회수 1500만 가량을 받은 "GTA IV is better than GTA V" 란 영상만 봐도
GTA4보다 미션의 다양성은 높으나 시스템적으로 너무나도 삭제된게 많다. 
앉기는 엄폐를 하지 않으면 안되고, 전투는 너무나도 쉬워졌다.
개활지에서 쓰래기통, 가판대에 엄폐해 무너지기 전까지 임시로 사용 가능한 여러 엄폐물 오브젝트는
GTA5에서 그저 벽,차로만 한정되게 바뀌어 전투가 캠핑과 다름없다.

AI는 사람을 왕따를 시킨다. 그저 정상인 플레이를 하면서 신호등 앞에 서있으면,
웬 미친새낀가 하면서 주인공을 피해버린다. 길따라 걷고있으면 따라오는줄 알고 도망도 친다.
그러다가 앞에 차에 박고 뒤지는게 이게임 AI의 전부이다.

문제는 GTA4와 GTA5의 엔진은 RAGE 엔진으로 빌드버전만 다르지 뼈대는 같다.
즉, GTA5에서도 GTA4같은 세부적인 물리표현과 캐릭터 동작이 가능하다는 것이다.
분명 그 5년간의 기간동안 수많은 기기적 성능, 엔진의 최적화가 있었음에도 불구하고, 시스템의 퇴보가 발복을 잡는다. 
물론 이부분에서는 GTA4,GTA5가 콘솔 기반으로(PC는 PS판 포팅) 제작된 게임이며
두게임 모두 PS3,XB360 대응이였기에 반박은 가능하다.
하드웨어적인 성능은 달라진게 없었고, 발전된 그래픽을 TV 해상도에서 48~60fps로 담아내야하니 말이다.

이제는 PS4가 아닌 PS5 출시도 거론되는 시점이니 락스타에게 바라는건,
GTA4의 섬세한 게임 디테일과 GTA5의 다채로운 색감과 미션+그리고 살짝의 약!,
또다른 혁신적인 무언가로 무장한 GTA의 신작을 바란다.

Fallout 4 had high expectations all around. And in many ways this game has delivered, and beyond. But what I want to touch down on is what you don't see on the cover. Bethesda's constant failing in delivering on a good story and their lies on the size of the game.

It was stated in several official areas that the game should run up to hundreds of hours, easily. But here is the problem, unless you are dungeon crawling every one of the numerous locations, you will struggle to even reach that third digit. It just wont happen. Why? because bethesda doesnt give you any reason to go there. None at all. Its all the same, repeated over and over, and with the EXTREMELY small selection of quests(of which mostly comprise of repeative radiant missions, and we all know how boring those are) you just will be running thru the motions of rinse and repeat.
This game also failed to capture the feeling of a wasteland wanderer... the one thing ALL people go to for in a fallout series. The wasteland might as well not exist and we have butterflies and unicorns prancing around, because none of it MATTERS. Bethesda didnt take the time to make a wasteland. What they did was make very little of some high quality content and spread it all over in vast quantities and give very little gameplay incentive to explore it.
And why would you? its the same shit, rather you turn left or right. Their best opertunity to change this, quests, was thrown right out the window.
Believe me, I been feeling this very shortly in,.. and I took a GOOD long time thinking it over and making sure I wasnt over-reacting.

With that said,... I am sure there are many people who will reach that third digit of hours played. But if they fail to see how shallow the game is by then, I question how blindly they are going thru the motions of repeative gameplay. Bethesda needs to wake up. This trend of theirs to take 2 steps forward and 2 steps backward for every new game is bullshit and normally I enjoy the fuck out of their games, but this time if I could get a refund I most definately would.
Don't get me wrong, its a good game, and the mods will make it all worth it in their own way. The problem is that this isnt the game that was advertised.
Expect to run out of things to do, and fast.

As a long time AC fan I felt the franchise had really lost its way with AC Unity and AC Syndicate, being just very mild, bland games. 
So I skipped Syndicate partly and skipped the whole of Origins.
AC Odyssey comes along and I was hooked by the setting, ancient Greece, perfect for AC. 
Full of intrigue, the origins of many political philosophies thanks to the great philosophers.

Ohn boy did the game deliver, I was afraid that stealth would be impossible, which isn't true at all.

Stealth can be a lot easier than previous games, but it requires some serious investment into the skill tree and what type of gear you'll favour, which honestly makes it that much more rewarding at the end.
There are some "bosses" who are simply impossible to kill stealthily but those are always 1v1 fights, so that's nothing new nor disturbing.


Combat is awesome, it just is. Sure you can cheese your way through opponents who are 4 or more levels higher by endlessly dodging and doing 'light/fast attacks', however it only takes one mistake to mess it all up, which I'm totally okay with.
The staleness of combat in previous AC games has largely been broken by the influx of abilities (haven't even used them despite the 99 hours), nothing quite beats "spartan kicking someone of a cliff" or "hero striking for that quick instant-kill".

The story is honestly very good, I did see the ultimate boogey coming however there's a very nice twist at the end which really made you stop and think about the core message of both the Templars and the Brotherhood of Assassins. 
The fact that you can quite heavily impact some aspects of the story by your choices are a nice addition and despite my initial concerns doesn't go overboard much.
Sidequests are besides some bounty missions very interesting with a lot of them being tied back into the main story, perhaps even affecting it somewhat. 

Overall it's a great game, in my opinion worth every penny, even at full price (was lucky enough to buy it in sale)

I'm a huge fan of the art, as well. It's all low resolution, but crisp, colorful, and intentional. The animations give Into the Breach a much more lively feel than FTL had. The Kaiju destroying humanity look almost... adorable, as they sit there menacing entire city blocks.

Celeste é uma grata surpresa na minha vida. Jogo fantástico, lindo e bem feito. Até nas horas de raiva e ódio, é difícil não amá-lo justamente por isso. Há uma experiência aqui: a dificuldade do game, te ensina e te molda. Você vai sendo forjado ao longo das fases, numa progressão de dificuldade muitíssimo bem pensada. Morrer faz parte do processo e a sensação de recompensa é uma das maiores que eu já experimentei no mundo dos games. Há frustração, não tem como fugir dela. Mas até isso faz parte dessa experiência. 
Um jogo que fala sobre depressão, ansiedade, aceitação... E a gameplay te faz viajar por todas as sensações que essas condições infringem. Você sente raiva. Você surta. Você quer desistir. Você desiste. Mas volta, luta, aprende e passa por aquela etapa. E esse ciclo vai sendo repetido. É essa mensagem que o jogo quer te passar: que há esperança em meio as dificuldades da vida.
Outra coisa incrível é que conforme você avança no jogo, vai descobrindo que há quase que uma infinidade de coisas pra fazer. Os 7 capítulos que formam a história base do jogo são a ponta de um iceberg que vai longe.
Enfim, já posso dizer que Celeste é um dos jogos da minha vida.

Total war: Warhammer

 -Jugabilidad: Este es el primer total war que he jugado que al pasarme la campaña con una facción nada más acabar quería jugarla con todas las demás facciones ya que cada raza tiene una jugabilidad diferente y que se adapta a cada tipo de jugador. Han metido al juego misiones especiales para los héroes que son personalizadas para cada uno y están chulísimas y al cumplirlas te dan un objeto que mejora al héroe en la campaña. Las batallas son alucinantes ya que son más dinámicas gracias a la magia y a todos los tipos diferentes de unidades. Los puntos negativos de este juego son que muchas veces no hace falta jugar las batallas en la campaña ya que el auto resolver esta muy a tu favor. Una de las cosas que se echan en falta son las batallas navales aunque se sabe que la compañía tiene problemas con eso por problemas de copyright aun así es algo que sería un puntazo si estuviese implementado. La diplomacia a mi parecer flojea un poco.También es un punto muy malo el que hayan solo 4 facciones jugables en el juego base. Por todo ello puntúo este apartado con un 8,5.  .  
 
-Tecnología: La tecnología en general está muy bien. Los efectos de luz y sombreado son alucinantes en las batallas además de que el tema de las físicas es muy bien logrado. La pega que tiene este juego en este apartado es que está un poco mal optimizado ya que cuando se juntan muchas unidades pega un bajo muy grande de frames que mi ordenador podría haber aguantado esa exigencia grafica si perder tanto frames y que a muchos amigos le ha pasado así que  por eso bajo tanto la nota en este apartado a pesar que lo demás este muy bien hecho. Puntúo este apartado con un 6.5.

-Gráficos: Los gráficos en esta entrega de total war son maravillosos, las unidades están muy detalladas y los mapas están muy bien logrados ya tanto por las texturas como por la distribución de los elementos en ellos. Los efectos tanto de luces, sombras, fuego, magia y explosiones  están hechos de una manera muy realista. Las animaciones de los soldados luchando, caminando y hasta las nuevas animaciones de carga son muy buenas. Puntúo este apartado con un 8.5.  

-Sonido: En esta entrega de total war en el tema de efectos sonoros se han superado ya que el sonido de las espadas, de los disparos, los cañonazos de la artillería, disparos mágicos, etc… están tan logrados que te sumergen totalmente en la batalla. La banda sonora que tiene esta entrega es la que más me ha gustado de lejos. Puntúo este apartado con un 9.  

-Innovación: En esta nueva entrega de total war por primera vez se mete el tema de la fantasía y por mí ha sido un respiro de aire fresco. Es la primera vez que meten unidades aéreas y magia que a mi parecer han implementado ambas perfectamente. Las mecánicas diferentes de cada raza en las que al ser tan diferentes entre ellas te puedes adaptar muy bien con tu forma de jugar a alguna de ellas. Puntúo este apartado con un 6,5.

 Finalmente este juego recibe, desde un punto de vista crítico, un merecido 8.06

Nota: La historia del juego me encanta aunque a muchos fans de la saga total war esta entrega les ha defraudado por no ser un juego histórico y porque falta en estrategia según ellos.

Excellent, excellent game.

DOOM 2016 shows that you don't have to follow the trend (military shooter, open-world, battle royale, games as service etc.) to achieve success and please gamers. You just have to give them what they actually want. Take note you C-level morons sitting at the top of most publishers / development studios.

DOOM does all that in spades. You get some guns, a boat load of ammo and then you go and kill demons with extreme prejudice. It's that simple. You don't even ponder stuff like where the hell does the Doom Guy hide all of those weapons because you're having too much fun blowing up enemies.

The graphics are nice and not too taxing on the system. Players can actually play at high settings even on mid-range setups. While graphics aren't everything it's allways nice to be able to experience the world in full detail. And the world in DOOM is ripe for exploring. Granted it's not an open world game but there are many secrets to find of the beaten path. It also helps that game controls and mechanics (ledge grabbing, double jump etc.) make platforming/exploring quite fun.

The audio is also a strong point. Let's start with the gem that is the soundtrack. Oh my god, it is freaking awesome ! It's loud (unless you turn it down ofc but why would you ?!), it gets you pumped, it makes you feel even more of a badass and it's just so in tune with the carnage happening on the screen. I absolutely love the soundtrack.
Gun sounds are also a strong point. All of them sound cool and heavy, thumpy/bassy giving you the feeling that they actually pack a heavy punch. Voice acting is done well enough.
The only nitpick I could find are demon sounds. They're not really that distinct from one another and they easily get drowned in the rest of the sounds. Other games communicate which enemies are where much better than DOOM.

The story in the game is OK but let's be honest, it's not why you play this game now is it ? :) I like that it's there, I like that it's competent because otherwise you'd just be playing an arena shooter. It gives the gamne structure, some backstory on the history of hell, the doom guy etc. Although most of it is in the data logs. Still, the lore is quite interesting so thumbs up.

Mechanically the game is quite simple but in that simplicity lies it's success. You don't have ARMA-like controls because this is not ARMA. You have your standard WASD, normal fire, secondary fire, melee attack/glory kill, duck, jump, and a grenade. That's it, that's all you need. There isn't even a realod mechanic. The game is about going fast, not stopping in one place for more than a few seconds shooting while you move and the control scheme is perfectly adjusted for that.
Even the glory kills which I had my doubts about don't distract or impact the flow of the game. They actually enrich the experience and I quite like them.

All in all a fantastic game, fantastic reboot of a beloved franchise. If only a similar bunch of competent people would do that with Duke Nukem... One can dream :)

As someone who is familiar with the Civ series - I played with each one of the series, except Beyond Earth - this game is a worthy pretender of the throne. The game kept the hexagonal, one combat unit / tile system of the 5th game, which was probably the best thing among all the things Civ 5 introduced. The AI agendas are giving the AI players a lot more character than before, and the inspiration / eureka system certainly provides a lot more dynamic and situational progress throughout the ages.
The game is not perfect tho', as someone who is struggling with Deity level AIs in Civ 5 (I mostly played on Immortal difficulty, and I have ~1000 hours+ of gameplay), in Civ 6, i am confident of beating a random game in Civ 6 on Deity (after ~200hours of gameplay). It kinda feels like playing on Immortal on Civ5, with the last difficulty setting is missing somehow. 
The communication with the AI feels deeper, and the Cassus Belli system is interesting to play with, however with the absence of diplomatic victory you probably never care to liberate city states or keep them out of harms way. They are just there for the taking in most cases. Hopefully an upcoming expansion pack of some sort will bring back that victory type, because without that the existence of CS-s are not really relevant. 

Overall the game is OK, I would recommend to fans of the series - but I alos have to highlight that it does not feel like a complete game at this point.

I want to like this game, I really do.  Most of the characters are interesting with good voice acting, the combat has depth, and the story has a good amount of fantasy with some twists thrown in.  Unfortunately, most of the characters have plot armor thicker than Naruto with little to no relatability to any of them.  The combat, for all it's depth, is actually about as wide as a pothole in execution.  And the story quickly turns into one where I actually started wanting to see the main cast fail for how ridiculous they were becoming.  

The MC, Velvet, starts off an edgelord, continues to be an edgelord, and after 25 hours of story content still continues to be a brainless embodiment of "I hate the world, I'm gonna go write a dark poem now."  Most of the supporting cast all have interesting backstories but seemingly throw said stories to the side of the road for the tiniest reason to follow our MC along on what they all fully understand could end all life as they know it.  Makes sense. 

The combat offers tons of options to customize your combos and button configs to suit your playstyle only for it all to boil down to: "enter combat, spam the controller face buttons until the bad guys stop moving."  25 Hours in and there is little to no reason to do anything more than simply spam random buttons to win as even on the highest difficulty available, everything ends by even so much as a sneezing in the general direction of the target being fought.  This is made even worse by the horrendous "tutorials" that get constantly thrown in your face to explain the convoluted system.  This is a perfect example of how throwing an encyclopedia at a player is the wrong way to teach a game's mechanics.  Especially when half the mechanics have similar if not identical terminology.  

All in all, for a Tales game, most of these things are par for the course.  If you've played, and enjoyed, Tales games before and want more, you might like this game.  For everyone else I don't think I can recommend this one.

There's nothing I can say about this game that all the other steam reviews won't tell you, so I'll just got over the cliff's notes for you.

Positives:
Beautiful aesthetic that no other game has.
Tight controls that mean, theoretically, all damage you take is your own fault.
Challenging, almost punishing difficulty will test your patience but ultimately leave you with a sense of satisfaction.
Levels are short so dying doesn't feel like that big a deal.
Equipment, weapon, and super selection let you feel like you're not just playing as a specific archetype, and allow you to mix up combinations for different challenges if that's how you want to play the game.
Megaman players will feel right at home with the Charge shot, knowing they need to pay attention to yet another layer of gameplay, the rhythm of charging up an attack, in order to gain a damage advantage. (If Charge is ever nerfed it will be worthless, since it is only better than other shots if you land its once-every-couple-seconds blast.)

Negatives:
Too many attacks don't give you any warning as to their area of effect until it occurs, making too many first tries only trial runs you know you'll fail on. (See the double flamethrower on Werner or the tugboat's chargin' mah lazor attacks for instance.)
Chaser is both bad at chasing and bad at damage, and if you are even moderately skilled at moving and shooting, you'll always want the pea shooter instead for sustained rapid-fire damage.
Some projectiles are difficult to see or approach from unexpected directions or far too quickly. (Bone wheel on the train boss, flames from said boss.)
Unexpected interactions with various parryable items/creatures. The octopus for instance most players will assume would hurt to touch.
Parrying objects above you feels off. When it's underneath you can tell when to press the button, but above it's almost like Cuphead's hitbox extends too far vertically to reliably parry anything with ensuring it will collide into you mid parry, instead of parrying as you collide into it.
Short. My playtime as of my first complete Regular playthrough was 4.6 hours.
Some weapons or items have limited or seemingly no worth. I used lobber once, on the bee, and didn't even need to.
Scrolling in multiplayer run n' gun levels is awful, as if players are too far apart the player in the lead will often take damage before being able to dodge out of the way.

All of this said, this is the first game I have paid full price for in a long time without feeling ripped off, and if you have any confidence in your hand-eye coordination I think you should give it a shot.

Edit: As of the recent update supposedly the developer did indeed nerf Charge, as well as apply a few other nerfs to existing strategies. The ones which were clearly exploits like the switching weapon bug are fine, but some of them make the game a less interesting and less fun experience. This is still a thumbs up for me but less enthusiastically than before.

Stardew Valley é basicamente um simulador de vida na fazenda,  é um jogo difícil, e tem alguns elementos de simulação que não são realista. Por exemplo: se não alimentarem os animais, eles não vão morrer, apenas vão ficar mais aborrecidos com o jogador(a). O progresso do personagem segue uma prática de evolução das habilidades que o jogador(a) utiliza enquanto se joga. incluindo a pesca, a agricultura, a recolha de minério, e até o combate. No progresso do jogo precisa-se de lucro para fazer melhorias na fazenda, comprar novas ferramentas, e aumentar mais os lucros.

Começamos o jogo sem tutoriais e sem um objetivo principal a ser seguido. Desde então você segue a sua nova vida de fazendeiro(a) aproveitando o dia plantando suas sementes e quebrando madeira para obter lenha para fazer seu próprio cercado. Há também mais de 30 personagens para você se socializar e 10 desses personagens podem ter uma relação amorosa com você independentemente do sexo. Existe um quadro onde podemos ver pequenos objetivos, porém é escolha do jogador(a) faze-los.

*Stardew Valley um relaxante e divertido simulador de fazenda.

Sabe aquele doce que você saboreia com grande deleite? Como se fosse o último do mundo? Pois bem, é mais ou menos assim que você se sentirá ao jogar DOOM Eternal, o mais novo rebento da id Software, empresa que é também a responsável pela criação do gênero FPS.

Wolfenstein, Quake, Doom: todas são franquias oriundas do estúdio fundado em Fevereiro de 1991 por John Carmack, John Romero, Tom Hall e Adrian Carmack.

E em DOOM Eternal, jogo lançado em 20 de Março de 2020, para PC, PlayStation 4 e Xbox One, a empresa conseguiu, por incrível que pareça, se superar em relação a seu trabalho anterior no DOOM de 2016.

O Doom lançado em 2016 conseguiu em diversos aspectos revitalizar a renomada série, iniciada em 1993. Ele também fundamentou um novo patamar para jogos de tiro em primeira pessoa, com ação bastante frenética, gráficos de ponta e níveis enormes.

Já DOOM Eternal, é um jogo claramente superior a seu antecessor, e não apenas no quesito “gráficos”, mas também em questões de personalização de armamento, níveis muito maiores, maior tempo de duração (analistas chegaram a estimar o dobro de duração em relação a Doom – 2016), etc.

Vale também lembrar que o shooter será lançado para Nintendo Switch, e segundo pude averiguar, ainda em 2020. Vamos torcer para ver o quanto antes este verdadeiro petardo no console híbrido da Nintendo.

Como em todo bom Doom que se preze, Eternal tem uma história, digamos, um tanto quanto rasa. Digo isto a princípio, digamos. Para tentar “enganar” você: pois conforme você avança na campanha, acaba percebendo que há ali muito material para entreter e informar.

Além disso, se você coletar os diversos pergaminhos espalhados pelo mundo do jogo, os quais são então adicionados ao “Códice”, conseguirá obter informações bastante aprofundadas a respeito de tudo o que está acontecendo, bem como a respeito de acontecimentos anteriores, no universo da franquia.

Aliás, há em DOOM Eternal uma certa surpresa para os jogadores que acompanham a franquia há anos, algo que por si só pode representar motivo suficiente para que você adquira o jogo.

Também existem vários flashbacks bastante interessantes a respeito do Doom Slayer. O “Cara do Doom”, ou “Doomguy”, acaba se lembrando de momentos antiquíssimos de seu passado, de momentos que, de certa forma, ajudaram a moldar a máquina de massacrar demônios em que ele se transformou.

Acredite: vale a pena coletar os inúmeros pergaminhos espalhados pelos mapas de DOOM Eternal para conhecer mais a respeito do jogo e também a respeito do universo no qual ele está inserido.

Basicamente, no jogo, a Terra foi invadida por demônios. Logo de início, cerca de 60% do planeta foi consumido pelas forças infernais. A maioria da população morreu no primeiro dia da invasão.

3 Sacerdotes Infernais comandam tais forças, e o primeiro deles, o primeiro alvo do protagonista do jogo, chama-se Deag Nilox.

Há muito material para lermos. Existem informações aos montes, sobre as forças infernais, sobre o passado do Doom Slayer, sobre o próprio universo em si, e sobre a própria existência como um todo. É extremamente interessante dar uma olhada em tudo isto.

DOOM Eternal é um jogo brutal. Frenético. Violento. Visceral. Hardcore. Um dos melhores (senão o melhor) jogos de tiro em primeira pessoa já lançados.

A id Software realmente se superou, neste título, e o que temos em mãos é algo que pode muito bem durar entre 20 a 40 horas de gameplay, dependendo do estilo do jogador, do nível de dificuldade escolhido, etc.

O título está repleto de novidades, e sua jogabilidade é verdadeiramente desenfreada. Porém, não tenha medo: o jogo te força a matar, matar, e matar. A dilacerar demônios com rapidez e fluidez.

A fazê-los sofrer em suas mãos, ao mesmo tempo em que você obtém recursos necessários para continuar progredindo, como por exemplo vida/sangue e munição.

Doom Slayer, como nos jogos anteriores da franquia, é um personagem mudo. E isto não é ruim: digamos que ele se expressa através de sua violência, forjada há bastante tempo.

Ele se manifesta com grande pompa no campo de batalha, explodindo e dilacerando demônios com as próprias mãos, e com grande ódio. Confesso que em grande parte do tempo me senti quase que um semideus; isto porque o jogo faz com que o Doomguy consiga se manter quase sempre um passo adiante dos demônios que tanto odeia.

Uma das mecânicas mais interessantes de DOOM Eternal está relacionada ao fato de que o jogo nos obriga, de certa forma, a sofrermos dano. Claro, dentro de certos limites, para evitar a morte.

Sofremos danos e logo utilizamos a motosserra (a qual requer combustível), para partir demônios mais fracos ao meio, para que possamos então obter a valiosa munição para nossas armas (além de sangue).

Também devemos utilizar uma mecânica semelhante, em demônios inertes, cambaleantes (próximos de morrer): com o botão “E”, literalmente os destroçamos, e então são liberados cristais azuis que preencherão nossa barra de vida.

app_name: Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy
review:
This game is terrible.
Not because it's difficult, I'm a huge fan of difficult, punishing games, and it was never resetting itself that annoyed me, it's easy to get into a zen state where you simply stop caring about progress.
But unfortunatley, it's also very easy for that state to be shattered by the game's intrinsic low quality.
This is a shameless rip of an old gamemaker studio game "sexy hiking", and Foddy is very open about that, calling this an "homage". Now, the mechanics and visuals are all much more polished in this game than in sexy hiking, but it still feels like a newgrounds game, something you'd have a bit of fun with screwing around with for 10 minutes before forgetting about it forever.
It feels like QWOP, one of Foddy's earlier projects, another hard-to control mess that is fun for all of 30 seconds. Clearly Foddy was annoyed by how disposable QWOP felt to people, and so devised a way to turn any shitty unplayable flas/unity/GMS game into ""art""
A: Add an annoying narrator
   "Oh dear, you fell, well here's an inspiring quote somebody else said. Now keep going"
   "Something something consumerism"
   and that's foddy's entire contribution as a narrator
B: Sell it for €8
   Shitty unplayable free game? Abandon after 10 minutes
   Shitty unplayable €8 game? Better get your money's worth!

And that's it. It's a game of lower content than the vast majority of free browser games out there, the only things this game adds to the table are a pricetag trying to get you emotionally invested through your wallet, and a narrator trying to distract you from the game's unplayablility through going on about how you can never give up!


I suppose I should explain exactly how the game is unplayable. I've established it doesn't do anyhting new, so let's see how bad the old is:
First and foremost, it does not feel like it was made for mouse controls. It really doesn't. Your only feedback on where the cursor is is a vague white blob on the screen that sometimes completely disobeys you. The movement of this blob is essentially tied to the hammer and the pot man through some arcane bonding that obeys no laws of science or logic.  Sometimes you'll quickly move your mouse to preform a speedy maneuver, and the blob will fly off while the hammer sluggishly trails behind, barely moving pot man an inch, causing him to slowly roll down a furniture ladder. Sometimes you'll pull drastically on your mouse and nothing will happen, the blob will remain stationary, if the hammer is in a position where it isn't really able to move much. Sometimes you'll nudge the mouse and the blob will fly off, hammer in tow, chucking pot man off a cliff. Sometimes the hammer follows the cursor, sometimes the cursor follows the hammer, but both are linked to pot man, who moves around the screen a lot, causing the positon of the cursor to vary depending on the movement of pot man. So halfway though a difficult maneuver the scrren might shift a little, and pot man will do a somersault off a cliff because the cursor moved relative to him when the screen shifted.
I haven't even mentioned the hundreds of times I've wanted to retract or extend the hammer and it's rotated instead, or vice-versa, but you already get the picture. It feels like a mechanic designed solely for analog sticks, with their constant relative positioning and off-axis accelleration, so why the game is mouse only boggles the mind.

So other than the controls being broken, the only other element of gameplay is the environment, and Foddy himself states in-game that it recieved zero playtesting. When he made an addittion, it stayed, regardless of internal balance of difficulty, and ohh boy it shows. I spent roughly 50% of my time playing this stuck on a single rock. There is a chimeny of sorts bridging the rocky segment to the industrial segment, where even the slightest false move can mean getting stuck in the chimney or falling straight back down, instead of grappling a lantern. And in order to get to an ideal position to jump into this chimney, you need to climb a short slope and a knee-high rock, and these had the worst collision detection and grip I've ever seen in a game. I literally spent upwards of 15 minutes stuck trying to climb the slope, with the hammer just failing to grip and me sliding down, crawling up a little, slipping, falling, over and over again until it just works. This happened every single run, where I would fall to the bottom, climb the rocky segment fine, and then spend far too long on a clearly untested segment. It gave my arm serious cramps just performing the same actions over and over again until it finally just works.

Of course, the biggest issue is that the game seems to free itself from any and all criticism by way of advertising "It's difficult! It's painful! You gotta keep going!" But nowhere does it actually say what the point of doing any of this is. I don't care what's on top, and the journey is just bad. I can't find any redeeming aspects about the game itself, and if you consider that, all the "prepare to die" just seems to be trying to make the most out of a bad game. "It's not low quality, it's post-modern!"



Game gotta be good if you want me to never give up, never surrender. Acres of slapped-together low resolution assets with ridiculous untested hitboxes and janky, unresponsive controls that just feel horrendous to play, with a nice big dollop of pretentious irony on top, make this a poor, poor affair.

The Room....

Un jeu de PUZZLES et non d'énigmes. Comme cela est beaucoup indiqué dans les évaluations pré-existantes, la réflexion demandée est faible pour résoudre ces puzzles...voire très faible. On voit une pièce, on cherche où la mettre et c'est résolu. Ce n'est qu'au prologue où la complexité des mécanismes m'a demandé quelques instants de triturages de neurones, ce qui est assez décevant. 
Les indices (symboles et autres marques en tout genre, je ne parle par du point d'interrogation "Aide") sont presque insultants tant ils vous sautent au nez à la moindre avancée. Le joueur est clairement souestimé et je pense que le jeu aurait gagné en intérêt s'il n'y avait eu aucune bulle d'informations à popper au moindre clic. Certains puzzles sont tellement évidents qu'il m'est arrivé à plusieurs reprises d''en avoir résolu avant qu'un mécanisme ne se déclenche.

Concernant l'histoire du jeu, j'étais émoustillée à l'idée que de l'alchimie soit abordée et j'espère fortement que la suite développe un peu plus ce sujet car en finissant ce premier opus, on a un goût amer en bouche. L'alchimie et toute sa complexité symbolique sont à peine effleurées sans que l'univers en soit correctement retranscrit ici. The Room est plus proche du cabinet de curiosité pour l'instant.

Pour finir l'adaptation sur PC est médiocre. Mon temps de jeu reflète beaucoup plus le temps que la caméra passait à switcher d'un élément à un autre que la durée de ma progression (en étant sur un pc capable de supporter TESO, The Witcher II, III et autre poids lourds). Cela engendre une frustration constante où l'on sait exactement où aller, quoi faire, mais où l'on doit attendre que la caméra daigne se bouger au prochain mécanisme...

En dehors de tout ceci, le jeu est beau, très beau, c'est certain. Mais je reste perplexe sur l'ambiance louée un peu partout dans les évaluations. A part quelques cliquetis, la musique d'ambiance n'est présente QU'AU MENU et aux chapitres de transition. L'univers mystique, qui pourrait avoir une belle influence, est à peine suggéré et est complètement mis en retrait par les lenteurs atroces de la caméra. 

Bref, un beau loupé à mes yeux. J'ai surtout l'impression, au final, de me retrouver devant un mémoire de fin d'année, certes bien peaufiné, mais qui n'a eu le mérite que de bénéficier de chapitres supplémentaires pour en devenir un produit commercial. 

J'espère sincèrement changer d'avis pour la suite.

I can whole-heartedly recommend this game, provided it is on sale for 10 dollars. The campaign on normal difficulty will take about 8-12 hours to complete, even faster if you go "guns blazing". This game was only fun to replay (for me) 2 times .  Everything in this game is spot on except 4 things:

1. Feels like a console port- Frankly the graphics  are disgusting if you get up close. All of the textures in this game are pretty mediocre for pc master race standards, but if you are playing on a laptop or toaster you can probably run this without difficulty. This game has a cool style and is optimised well though.

2. Enemies are totally blind to anything above them- Not even joking, you can drop bottles on people's heads without them having the slightest clue where they came from. For some reason places to hide above people are super common too, light fixtures, pipes, vents, the works. Once you find out how to exploit this stealth is too easy for the most part.

3. With practce it is really easy to fight everyone. This might have been a design choice so that people could go non steath and have fun, but if I wanted a brain dead action fps I woud play CoD or something. Thankfully this problem is pretty much solved by swithing the difficulty to hard, still seems a tad easy though.

4. Blink, the teleport spell, is very OP- It does not use much magic and can be spammed to speed through areas without being noticed. Blink can also be used to get to higher places and avoid everyone.  Reason #2 and blink when used together are pretty game breaking. 

Overall I give it 8/10. Pretty fun, not much replay value unless you are the kind of person who goes around looking for hidden stuff and collectables.

While some games are easily memorable for their gameplay, others will stood out by their Story. To the Moon is a game where the story is clearly the winner and it’s the reason why everyone should spend their time playing it. I’ll start by saying that it may not be a game that will please most of the players but consider starting the game with an open heart and the experience will be a remarkable one. The two main characters are doctors who go by the name of Watts and Rosalene and their jobs can be many things, but common isn’t one of them. They can provide an alternative, a different path to the ones whose life is approaching the end. During the story, your role is to help your patient to fulfil his wish: going to the moon. While it may seem an odd thing to wish for, there may be a reason for it, but that, is up to you to find out. 

You start by going from the most recent memories to the older ones, until you reach the point where you may find key-points in the Johnny’s past. But as you advance in the game you start to create a bond to his memories which can be odd, considering it’s just a job and Johnny is a stranger for you, but remember, if you let yourself immerse into the story you will end playing a much better game this way. There’s not much to be said about the Story itself without spoiling most of it to be honest. The game is very straight to the point, hence its short length but this can be a good thing because there won’t be any unnecessary time spent doing pointless quests or wandering off for long. You have a goal, this is your job and emotions should be left aside, but play this game as intended and emotions will surely make part of this experience. As they should.

The music/soundtrack is as much important as the story because during certain events you will be listening to a nice piano tune that will provide warm feelings or a sense of loss, sadness and curiosity. I don’t believe the game to be any sort of depressing, as humor also plays an important role in To the Moon. Small conversations with some jokes and jests will arise from time to time to create a lighter mood since, after all, this is your goal and you shouldn’t let your personal feelings obstruct your intents. While I’m sure many will leave satisfied with the story (weather you end up liking the very end or not) and the music as well, do not come expecting some heavy gameplay mechanics or a rather lengthy game. I believe its short size can be a strong point this time because it takes you right where you need to be so I would advise to not measure your time and money invested with the length of the game but rather in its storytelling. If you are able to past the simple visuals with almost no gameplay mechanics, and if you let yourself engage in the Story while listening to the wonderful soundtrack then To the Moon will be a perfect fit to play in the between of any other lengthier games you are currently playing. It’s a respectable violence-free game, short but sweet experience filled with some humor, remarkable music and probably some tears as well. Play the game as intended, do not haste, do not do anything else while playing it and I’m sure your money will be a good investment. Enjoy the story. 

PS: As you may have noticed, English is not my first language so I apologize for the lack of a better grammar and steady writing.

Vor einigen Monaten ist Dishonored 2 erschienen, weshalb ich nicht umhinkomme, den brillanten ersten Teil anzupreisen!

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

Dishonored ist ein aus der Ego-Perspektive gesteuertes Schleichspiel, welches man auf zwei Arten spielen kann: Entweder man schleicht sich an den Gegnern vorbei und tötet möglichst wenig bis gar keine Personen, oder man kämpft sich mit Pistole, Schwert und Magie durch die feindlichen Reihen. Je nachdem für welche Spielweise man sich entscheidet, wird der sogenannte "Chaosfaktor", eine Art Karmasystem, niedrig oder hoch. Dieser Chaosfaktor hat nicht nur Einfluss auf die Schwierigkeit, sondern auch auf das Verhalten anderer Personen dem Spieler gegenüber und auch das Ende des Spiels, von diesen gibt es nämlich insgesamt drei Mögliche. Das Gameplay ist ziemlich an das von Thief oder Dark Messiah of Might & Magic angelehnt.

[h1]Story[/h1]

Dishonored spielt in einer fiktiven Steampunkwelt, genauer gesagt im Kaiserreich der Inseln. In der Hauptstadt Dunwall grassiert eine Seuche, welche im Spiel aber nur am Rande vorkommt und den Spieler auch nicht betrifft. Man selbst spielt Corvo Attano, den "Kaiserlichen Schutzherren", also den Leibwächter der Kaiserin. Zu Beginn des Spiels kehrt man von einer erfolglosen Suche nach einem Heilmittel zurück nach Dunwall. Kurz nachdem man der Kaiserin davon berichtet hat, wird diese von Unbekannten ermordet und ihre Tochter Emily entführt. Corvo wird für den Mord fälschlicherweise verhaftet, und das ausgerechnet von den tatsächlichen Drahtziehern, jedoch gelingt es ihm, mit fremder Hilfe aus dem Gefängnis zu fliehen. Er wird in den "Hound Pit's Pub" gebracht, wo sich eine Bewegung formiert hat, die die Herrschaft des Lordregenten, also jenes Mannes, der Corvo hat verhaften lassen, beenden will und stattdessen die entführte Prinzessin Emily auf den Thron setzen will. Also ist es nun an Corvo, die junge Emily zu retten und die Verschwörer entweder zu töten oder auf andere Weise handlungsunfähig zu machen. Vom sogenannten "Outsider", einer in einer Zwischenwelt namens "Nichts" wandelnden Entität, erhält Corvo magische Kräfte, welche er durch das finden von Runen weiter ausbauen kann. Weiter gehe ich nicht auf die Story ein, da ich sonst zu viel dieser großartigen Handlung spoilern müsste.

[h1]Grafik[/h1]

Die Grafik ist für ihre Zeit in Ordnung, jedoch sehen die Figuren, insbesondere die Gesichtsanimationen, sehr hölzern aus, außerdem trifft man auf viele Doppelgänger. Die Spielwelt ist der Stimmung des Spiels angemessen, jedoch auch recht statisch. Trotzdem gibt es im Punkt Grafik wenig zu beanstanden.

[h1]Fazit[/h1]

Für Fans von Schleichspielen ist Dishonored ein Muss! Wer ausschließlich auf Action steht, wird mit Dishonored allerdings wenig Freude haben, da selbst die Kämpfe wenig Actionreich sind, wenn man sich denn für die kämpferische Variante entscheidet. Müsste ich das Spiel bepunkten, so würde ich ihm 9/10 Punkten geben, da die Level etwas weniger linear sein könnten.

To start off ark you are stranded on the shores of the island. You have no items, No engrams no nothing. You have to start with punching a tree and making yourself a stone pickaxe. Then you level up by getting some wood and thatch and make yourself a hatchet and a campfire. As you level up you get to level things such as Heath Stamina Food and others. Absolutely incredible game & one of the best I've played in years! For me, in terms of engagement and fun, I would rank this up there with Red Dead Redemption and Fallout 4 (disclaimer: I have not played Witcher III or Skyrim -- but I'd imagine this is comparable with those as well)

I recommend watching https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JyWqCew1g-A to get an idea of everything that went into this game.

As far as storyline, it's fairly predictable, but entertaining nevertheless. There's more pages of script in the story than the first two Game of Thrones books combined and over 3.5 hours of cut-scenes. It's really an amazing accomplishment.

Regarding the visuals & scenery: I read other reviews about how people would just look at the surroundings. I had my doubts... but I really do find myself just looking around -- they did an absolutely incredible job at making the landscape seem alive & real. As someone who's hiked many miles, this has been one of the best simulations of forest & trails I've seen in a game.

In addition to the setting and landscape, the world itself feels alive. Lots of games claim to have this "living world", but they really make it happen here (with the exception that all the townsfolk are just... really happy to see you all the time). The towns, characters, shops, and weather are quite immersive; and your ability to sit around and read, eat, or play dice adds quite a bit in terms of creating an environment for relaxed-paced gameplay. 

As for the gameplay itself, it felt very much on rails at the beginning, but I later learned this was a "prologue" to the main game, so made sense. The latter parts of the game opened up more and allowed for multiple ways of completing or bypassing some objectives. And although you can drift a bit more evil or more good; in the end the results & questline seem be pretty much the same, which is to be expected for an RPG rather than sandbox. Nevertheless, I do find that my Henry character develops a distinct personality, and I look forward to doing another playthrough with a different style/personality, which is quite doable in this game.

The biggest shock was the learning curve -- not for the player, but for the character you play. In the beginning, your character really sucks. At first I agreed with many other posts -- combat & lockpicking are impossible! But, then I learned that the failures weren't all my fault as the player, but rather the game actually alters the mechanics of the mini-games to make it near impossible for someone with 0 lockpicking skills to pick a lock. After leveling up and training, the mechanic itself changes to allow for an easier time. It's a really well-done concept which forces the player to assume the role of someone with limited skills.

That's not the only concept that was well done, though. I feel the sleep day/night cycles are excellently balanced, the ability to sit & wait and/or read are done well; and the combat system is one of the better implementations I've seen. It definitely can be frustrating, but I think it's well-done. The fact that you can't easily take on a group of 4-5 bandits by yourself really puts you in your place in the world. 

The armor/clothing mechanic is also very well done. I get a pretty customization appearance, my clothes get dirty and require cleaning/mending (although they do get dirty WAY to fast).

The walking/horse riding is another mechanic I think they nailed. I can just walk or ride my horse around and really feel immersed in the game.

Finally, the sound is superb. Not just the music, but they've clearly sunk some resources into making sure that the ambient sounds are immersive.

All in all, an incredible buy and totally worth it -- will easily sink hundreds of hours into this.

街中でできるビリヤードやカラオケなどのミニゲームも多数あり物凄く作りこまれていたりするのだが、別にこのゲーム中でこれをやる意味があるかといわれるとそうでもないのでやる気はしない。
サブクエストをそこそこ消化していったけどやらなくても良かったなと途中から後悔したので、さっさと本編だけ進めることを推奨する。

銃で撃たれてもすぐに回復するやつが多すぎるのには笑って流す必要があるが。
Ｗ主人公のひとりである真島の方は何したいのかよくわからないし、シリーズ本編につなげるための物語でこの作品単品としてみるといまいちなところがある。

app_name: Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy
review:
Beaucoup de rage, beaucoup de frustration, beaucoup d'insultes envers l'auteur de cette abomination sadique et de ses interventions des fois irritantes (à cause du contexte...). Une concoction soigneusement préparée pour susciter l'impatience, la colère et la mise sur les nerfs, grâce à un gameplay impardonnable et une prise en main absolument immonde.

Merci à mes ventilateurs pour m'avoir soulagé pendant cette ascension et mes excuses à ma souris et à mon clavier qui ont pris de sale coups.

Sinon, très bon jeu, je recommande.

Edit: 8 heures ont été nécessaires à ma première ascension, suite à quoi j'avais rédigé cette évaluation, et juré de ne plus revenir sur ce jeu. Puis je suis revenu le lendemain - pour de nouveau atteindre le sommet, cette fois en 2h30.

Puis j'ai encore recommencé. Cette fois, seulement 30 minutes. Puis 20 minutes. 15 victoires plus tard, ça continue, et mon record est de 13 minutes, mais je pense pouvoir descendre à 7 ou 8 avec un peu de chance. Et je rage toujours autant sur les obstacles, et à violenter sans modération ma souris - mais non plus parce que je n'y arrive pas, mais parce que je n'y arrive pas du premier coup.

En effet, passé les premières parties, si vous êtes d'humeur à retenter cette pénible épreuve, vous allez commencer par vous apercevoir que certaines mécaniques ne sont pas aussi indomptables qu'elles en avaient l'air au départ, et certains passages, sur lesquels vous auriez pu passer des heures (et qui pour moi restaient tous simplement insurmontable après 5-6 heures de jeu) ne deviennent plus qu'un détail.

Tous les obstacles ne se domptent pas au même rythme cependant, certains se jouant à la pratique rigoureuse, avec d'innombrables échecs frustrants - par centaines, voir milliers de fois, avant que vous ne maîtrisiez enfin le fichu mouvement de souris.

Ainsi, aujourd'hui, je continue d'essuyer des chutes incessantes sur le tout dernier obstacle et à en pleurer comme si c'était la première fois que je perdais ma progression, et je considère me racheter une souris pour remplacer celle que j'utilise, parce qu'elle semble vieillir prématurément - allez savoir pourquoi.

Edit 2: Je l'ai fait. 25 jours après être grimpé pour la première fois, j'ai terminé l'impensable exploit de finir le jeu 50 fois. Ma souris a tenu bon, même si j'ai du la dépanner une fois suite à un coup de rage violent. Mon record est de 7 minutes et 18 secondes.

Ce jeu m'a rendu marteau. Merci Bennett Foddy

World and general mood:
The term "grimdark" is very apt. Everything is shite. Plague, war, monsters and a crazy destructive cult as delicious frosting on a massive cake of misery. You recognise a well-traveled road by the corpses piling up beside it and the national sport seems to be hangings.

Combat:
It is intense in a Dark Souls kind of way. Do your homework and fight smart or what ever you go up against will make you its prison wife.

Story and interaction: The world is insanely huge and feels very alive. Villages and cities feel like people actually live there and have realistic amounts of inhabitants. The story is very well written and choices you make might come back later to bite you in the ass, or line your pockets, or both at once.

Pros:
- Good G-man acting
- Lots of weapons
- Lots of intresting new dialogue
- Beautiful graphics
- Lots of graphic customisation

Cons:
- Most weapons have sight aims. (-_-)
- The file is 21.3 gb to download (This can change if they make updates)
- Horrible story
- Annoying weapon sounds
- A knife is used to hit crates and makes metal noises.
- G-man has material texture on shirt and tie which is weird.
- Mobs spawn in the most rediclous places as if someone was making a 5 minute Garry's Mod map.
- Poor dialogue made and with the cutscenes and the story it's just a waste of your time.

- The maps are buggy and even mobs and their dead bodies known as "ragdolls" are flying everywhere across the map giving you a feeling as if you will die or get stuck.
- Props block your way.
- There is no actual objective per location since this gaming feels as if it should be something to a typical Call of Duty or Battlefield campaign.
- Black Mesa sound effects at the start are made poorly.
- The maps, designs and stuff feel as if they were made cheapily. 
- You have to buy this game. (This game is a joke to even cost money)

Overall, is it worth it?

Fallout 4 is definitely Bethesda's most ambitious game to date. At times the game can look magnificently beautiful for a game set in the post-apocalyptic Boston. The World-building is some of the best to date, expanding on the already rich lore of the Fallout universe. Some of the characters you meet in this game are also written quite well, and the quests associated with them are therefore interesting and worth your time. Additionally, the game's combat is the best it has ever been, even if it detracts the game away from an rpg-style combat to more of an action rpg flavour.

This isn't to say the game doesn't have it's flaws. When the game first came out, it was riddled with many bugs and performance issues, which is a standard for Bethseda games now a days, but still unacceptable for a Triple AAA company with such a reputation. While some of the characters are genuinely interesting (Nick Valentine, Kellog), other characters either fall flat on their face with a boring personality or simply not enough characterisation/development (don't get me started on Presley). The voice acting is nice, but ultimately hinders the game's dialogue system, which has been extremely simplified to a dialogue wheel with 4 distinct ways to express your character (most of the time the way you express yourself doesn't matter). This brings me to the removal of skills, which is once again another simplification of the rpg elements that were present in previous games. Most of the stat bonuses that you would normally recieve from leveling skills, is instead implemented into F4's perks, which takes away from the creativity and unique bonuses they gave you in previous games.

While Fallout 4 is still a great action rpg game, it ultimately does not feel like a "traditiional" fallout game, and thus subjects the game to heavy criticism from hardcore fans. Most of these criticisms are true, and if you are diehard fan and can't imagine a fallout game without the core mechanics which the previous games of the franchise was known for (speech checking, skills, high level of player agency etc.), than I ultimately cannot recommend this game, since you will surely dislike the game. For everyone else however, despite this game's flaws, it's still a great game knowing how simplified it is. You will definitely get your time and money's worth.

Я конечно прекрасно понимаю, что этот коммент затеряется в лавине одинаковых рассуждений о деньгах, но все же напишу его для тех кому интересна сама игра, а не её модель монетизации. Сам бывалый любитель ККИ, начинавший в дремучие годы с "Берсерка". Дальше была "MTG", потом уже пошли онлайновые ККИ аля "ХС" и иже с ней, в общем жанр повидал. Потому "Artifact" ждал с момента его анонса на "The International 2017". Располагая суммой денег достаточной лишь на покупку самой игры, я решился несмотря на негативные отзывы приобрести её и самому посмотреть что тут происходит. И спустя 5 часов игры могу с уверенностью сказать, что с точки зрения механики, на данный момент, это самая лучшая онлайновая ККИ за все время жанра. Да, рандом всё ещё решает во многих игровых ситуациях, однако в отличие от того же "ХС" с которой игру принято сравнивать, здесь он играет куда менее значительную роль. Система с героями и цветами реализована очень изящно, для тактических приемов крайне большие перспективы. С графической и музыкальной составляющей всё тоже неплохо. Думаю любые ролики или стримы расскажут об этом куда лучше меня, потому не буду углубляться в анализ этих критериев. А вот интерфейс не слишком удобный и приятный. Конечно сравнивать приходится с реальной жизнью, но того приятного чувства при сборе колоды и её просмотре не получаешь. Вообще не хватает какого-то ощущения целостности. То есть в погоне за функциональностью растеряли тот самый коллекционный элемент и удовольствие от него. Что же по поводу самой важной части и камня преткновения для многих желающих поиграть - массовых истерик на тему Pay2Win. Имеют ли они место быть? Скорее нет, чем да. Спорить с тем, что стартовыми колодами практически невозможно обыграть ребят с колодой за 4к бесполезно. Это факт. Однако из полученных паков вам выпадет более сотни карт и несколько из них скорее всего окажутся ценными. Если вы конечно не "победитель по жизни", то из полученного материала, продав пару карт и закупив новых, можно собрать колоду. Буквально из говна и палок, смастерив красно-черную пачку на пуш общей стоимостью около 400 рублей, помучал бота и пошёл играть в паб. Пока не потерпел ни единого поражения. В экспертный драфт ещё идти не рискую, но вроде как там все в одинаковом положении, а значит при должном изучении всех карт и механик, побеждать также не составит труда. Так что если вы знакомы с ККИ непонаслышке, то "Artifact" - качественный и интересный продукт, стоящий своих денег. Если вы только познакомились с жанром или до этого играли лишь в "ХС", то на свой страх и риск, ибо пока что "Artifact" слишком нишевый. А вот когда подвезут ладдер и систему достижений, а также добавят пару дополнений, игра раскроется уже для более широкой публики. Думаю, оценка критиков на Metacritic справдедлива и игра заслуживает своих 8 баллов.

This game is really funny, but even more sad, especially on the True Pacifist route that I just finished. At the time of writing this review, I haven't completed the genocide route, and I'm planning on taking a break from this game before I return to it because yes, I am emotionally attached to the characters. But for me, that's just the kind of game this game is; the game itself is not as fun as the characters are, and all the dialogue you have with them, and how you get to know them and all their problems as you tried to solve them. Overthinking it, I guess this game is about solving everybody's problems.

But despite that, it's really fun helping them solve their problems, and it's one of the things that make this game stand out from all others. It's never ever too difficult, it's very fair; the most difficult aspect is memorizing bosses' attack patterns, and you have infinite retries, so you should manage to get all the way through the game. Like I keep stressing, this is more of an exposition game than it is about features. The emotional attachment you-or at least I-had to the characters at the end were so touching it inspired me to write this review. The game isn't perfect in all ways, but in terms of setting up a universe like this one where the characters actually have relationships with you, and you can manipulate them however you want; really this game just gives you [i][h1]the feels[/h1][/i]

In [i]HuniePop[/i] you play as an anonymous man or woman who is not having much luck with picking up the ladies. After another failed attempt at a bar, you meet the love fairy Kyu who promises to help you improve your social skills with the ultimate goal of bedding more women than you could ever imagine.

[i]HuniePop[/i] is primarily a puzzle-type game with some dating simulator elements included. The core of the game is a [i]Bejeweled[/i]-type puzzle game where you need to move and match symbols on a grid to score points. But there are added layers of complexity such as items to use and power-ups to gain. Indeed, I actually found this puzzle aspect to be quite addictive when I was playing. As the game progresses and more points are required to pass levels, you need to think more strategically about which moves to play and what the effects will be.

In addition to the main puzzle game, [i]HuniePop[/i] is also about a dating simulator-style of play. You will meet several women during the course of play and you can buy them gifts to unlock new outfits or earn Hunie points which can be used to increase your stats. Or you might have to answer questions to earn points based on each woman's unique characteristics and personalities.

The art does an okay job for the game. The background art all around is very well done and the CGs (which are mostly very lewd) are professionally done as well. The style is anime inspired for the characters. While it looks nice, and each character has multiple outfits and hairstyles that can be unlocked, the style is still not particularly distinctive nor memorable.

While the puzzle game is fun, what really got me interested in this game is the unusual and often funny writing. The game's description notes that it includes an "abrasive western writing style." Unlike other games with a dating aspect that often contain a slew of women with cute and/or bubbly personalities, [i]HuniePop[/i] includes a far larger range of character types. This runs the gamut from the sweet and demure Beli, the shut-in, video game nerd Nikki, to the very foul-mouted and narcotics-loving Audrey. I found this aspect of the game to be quite hilarious and really added to my enjoyment of it. There is just something very comedic, for example, about dating Audrey who clearly has nothing but contempt for the player-character, but she goes along with it anyway.

In addition to the writing, all of the women in the game are fully voiced. The voice acting, in my opinion, was a bit hit-and-miss. Some of the voice actors did an excellent job of imbuing their characters with personality. I particularly enjoyed the work done for Audrey and Kyu in this regard. But some of the acting felt a little wooden, such as the work done for Nikki which often sounds like someone just reading off of cue cards.

It should be noted that this is most definitely an adult game with nudity and sexual content. Even the "censored" Steam version is still very much NSFW. There is a [url=http://www.teamhijack.com/huniepop/patch/uncensor.html]free patch available[/url] from the developer's website that will unlock all of the art. If hentai is not your cup of tea, you will not like this game.

Overall, I found this game to be fun. The puzzle aspect was more involved than I thought it would be which kept me playing for hours while the writing was often hilarious. If you are looking for a puzzle game with some hentai aspects, this is for you.

Story wise, Half-Life focuses on a silent protagonist, which may seem strange for a story rich game. However, Half-Life's character's silence causes the player to react rather than the character, letting the player feel as if they were in the game, and make choices that reflect on themselves not on the character, which really causes the player to feel as if they form a part of the story. I won't spoil the story but I have to say it is unique for its time, and not everyone will be attracted to it, but it's worth a play from my side. :D

Dirt Rally was in Early Access for a while. There was a lot of bug fixing during that time, plus they were taking feedback from the community and tweaking the handling model, resulting in a model that's challenging but adrenaline pumping. It was their first sim focused rally game, and they took their time to nail down the driving feel.

Dirt 4 was released as a 1.0 game, no Early Access. It's larger in scope than Rally, but it's not as finely polished. The launch version was not very stable with frequent crashes. The crashes seem to have been addressed, but some bugs never have, like alt tabbing causes the game to drop out of full screen and display in a small window. Some features from Dirt Rally were missing, like VR support.

While it launched with lots of synchronous multiplayer options, it lacked the Clubs system for asynchronous racing. In contrast, Dirt Rally had almost no synchronous multiplayer (other than for Rallycross mode), but you could join clubs and compete against others in custom asynchronous tournaments. (Both featured developer-ran daily/weekly/monthly competitions at launch though)

Clubs were eventually added to Dirt 4.

The simulation handling model has been changed quite a bit going from Dirt Rally to Dirt 4 - modelling of suspension articulation, frame flex, and aerodynamics have all been noticeably improved. The real controversy comes from the tire grip model, especially the lateral tire grip. For Dirt 4, Codemasters purchased tire grip data from a tire manufacturer (Continental IIRC) and gathered test data with a real world (AWD) rally car. Perhaps the supplied tire data was a bit optimistic or flattering, but in any case there's no denying that sidewalls now dig into gravel far more during a slide. This makes glorious sweeping slides much harder to pull off, and in many ways makes the handling feel "safer" than Dirt Rally.

Personally I think the AWD and FWD cars feel pretty good, and tarmac and other hard surfaces are much improved from Dirt Rally for all car types, but I do think RWD cars have too much grip on loose surfaces. Dirt Rally is the opposite, RWD cars are almost comically difficult to control on some tracks. The community wanted the tire model patched to feel more like Dirt Rally, but the devs never responded and the Steam page got review bombed by sim fans.

In the arcade handling mode, Dirt 4 is better than Dirt 3 in every way except for lacking split screen, but the arcade fans never really showed up (maybe due to negative reviews from the sim crowd?).

The procedural generation has also drawn some criticism. It uses hexagon segments across large prebuilt maps. Some of the scenery is built into the tiles and some into the the maps, this helps keep things somewhat varied visually, and there are a few possible variations of some corners. The downsides is that some tiles can only connect to a limited number of other tiles, so some of them usually show up in pairs. This makes them more recognizable and undermines the "don't know what's around the next corner" feel they were going for. I think the severity of this problem is overblown, but it's there.

Another problem is that Dirt Rally baked a lot of shadows into the textures of the scenery, making the graphics look better than they really were. This isn't possible with procedurally generated tracks, and the tracks in Dirt 4 look less dramatic as a result. (Look at screenshots of Sweden in both games, you'll see.) There are also only 5 locations for rally stages, vs six in Rally (plus there was a good amount of variety within each location, like snowy sections of Monaco vs dry tight sections of Monaco), so even though you never drive the same track twice, it does feel less varied than Dirt Rally.

I do miss Pike's Peak in Dirt 4 (especially because the tarmac model is so much better than Dirt Rally), but Land Rush is kind of a neat replacement, it's a lot of fun. And Dirt 4's Rallycross mode is far better than that in Rally.

Some of the criticism is valid, but Dirt 4 doesn't get enough credit for what it does right. If you can forgive it for not being Dirt Rally, it's a fantastic racing game. I can't pick a favorite, but I'd sum it up as Dirt 4 is the better game and Dirt Rally is the better experience.

Графика слабовата, но глаз не режет, выглядит органично.
 Но, атмосферы в игре совсем нету. В то время, когда Беседка в серии TES наполняла кучу городов кучей НПС, у каждого из которых было имя и какая-то своя небольшая история, то в Фоллауте 4 НПС кроме главных почти нету. Все абсурдно настолько, что в городе (единственном нормальном городе в игре - Даймонд Сити) рядом могут стоять два НПС с именами "Гражданин 1" и "Гражданин 2". Серьезно? Нумеровать НПС - это что-то новое, реально. Неужели так сложно было хоть какие-то рандомные имена дать им, чтобы не так бросалось в глаза.
 Так же, стоит отметить прославленные Беседковские кривые уровни сложности. Т.е. вся сложность игры на высокой сложности - это то, что тебе за удар будут отрывать по пол лица гули (даже если ты в силовой броне), а ты должен им вжарить обойму из винтовки в лицо, что бы убить. Это еще при том, что на вас начнут сыпаться всякие "Легендарные дикие гули-охотники" или "Легендарные ядовитые радтараканы" из которых вам будет выпадать "Термоядерная свинцовая броня для правой руки", которая дает обычно какой-то юзлесс бафф.
Так же, очень раздражает система улучшения оружия, когда ты можешь взять пистолет, добавить на него ложе и БАМ - у тебя уже винтовка. Ну отлично.
Вообщем, игра оставляет очень смешанные чувства. Вроде играть и приятно, но при этом на каждом шагу видно, что разработчики делали игру "наотъебись". Куча механик не доработаны, убогие диалоги в стиле "Да, Нет, (Сарказм)", мало оружия, слишком много однотипной брони.  Что безусловно понравилось, так это система "quickloot", когда тебе не нужно открывать 100500 контейнеров для сбора всяких ништяков, и реализация силовой брони. Все остальное либо "нормально", либо плохо. Если вы любите постапокалипсис - лучше поиграть в Сталкер или Метро какое-нибудь, но уж точно не в это.

The combat has devolved into a big boring mash of garbage.  Just pick whichever classes, it's all the same thing now.  Cipher/Druid/Loremaster/Dragon Disciple/Flamethrower Man/Half-Drow Spellshaper? Let's be honest, the new RPG mechanics in this game are everything that's bad about Real Time With Pause combined with everything that's bad about failed Tabletop RPG systems in one neat package. Barf.

Celeste is a tough yet forgiving platformer with a very charming aesthetic. The controls are very tight and fuild with the mechanics revolving around the player's dashing ability. The game presents a decently difficult challenge but as with many such platformers, your downtime is extremely low, you're back in the action seconds later and you rarely need to replay huge sections of platforming too. Because of this, I never felt like the game was TOO difficult, but instead I felt more satisfyed when moving to the next screen.

Each of the 7 zones use the dash ability in different ways keeping gameplay fresh and exciting. Tons of collectibles and secrets can be found by the more curious of players. It's a relatively short game, but there's a fair bit to do too. Including a hard version of all the zones for that added challenge, so I'd say it's worth the money.

The story isn't too much to write home about. Without spoiling too much, this game appears to be tackling the topic of depression. The events in the game are sort of acting as a giant metaphor for how a person with depression might feel; hell, two characters straight up talk about one of them having depression later in the game, just in case you missed the memo.

Like a bunch of popular indie adventure games (Undertale, Cave Story, Owlboy etc.) on top of the very solid and satisfying gameplay is a cast of characters who hold up the story all by themselves. No matter what is going on you can't help but love them all in the end. Everyone is written very well is what I'm saying, and Celeste is no different. The banter between both the player and guy with his "instagram" followers or with the player and the old lady who lives on the mountain. I just never wanted them to stop talking! The little mumbled speech (Reminisant of Animal Crossing) that can be heard is super cute and in one certain case added to the humor. The characters had so much... character!

I almost shred a tear 2 seperate times while playing this, just seeing what the small cast of characters had gone through, both the good and the bad. I'm a pretty big wuss, but still :')

I HIGHLY recommend this game, it hooked me from start to finish.

Half-Life. The very first game Valve made. Without this game we wouldn't have all of Valve's other games, and neither would we have Steam. And besides that, it layed much of the groundworks for 3d first person shooters. Because of all of this, Half-Life may very well be one of the most important games ever. 

I got Half-Life in the Valve Complete Pack, on a summer sale, so it was more of a bonus than anything. This is probably how most people will want to get Half-Life, since it will cost next to nothing and comes bundled with some more popular games (cs:go, l4d2, etc). If you look at it that way, the question becomes more if it's even worth your time anymore, since the game is more than 20 years old at this point. I'm going to say Half-Life is definitely worth your time, if only just to get a greater understanding of Valve and its games. Just know that Half-Life has become slightly antiquated over the years , and some sections are a bit unfair (mainly on the last levels), but it'll give you enough good gameplay and a solid, though simplistic, story to enjoy to keep you going for the 30 of so hours it lasts.

- Good shooting mechanics

- Good enemy variety
