Assassins Creed Origins, the latest game of the AC franchise, the fresh air that we need. This game has potential despite the flaws. Lets start with the review.

Graphic
Man, this is the prettiest AC I've ever player besides Syndicate. The lighting, heat effect, the draw distance and the water, oh god the water, are the most thing I like in ACO's graphic. Didnt know desert could be that pretty, and the water looks natural especially when I was on a boat. I still remember when I was in Siwa and on the way to Giza, I could see the shape of the pyramid from afar, like very far and got excited. When I reached the pyramid I climbed it straight to the top, and the view is amazing. Furthermore, once you progress the story further, you can see the Roman style building, which are also beautiful. Conclusion, ACO's graphic is the biggest improvement of the series.

The World
Well, I am happy that this time Ubisoft did it perfectly regarding the game's world. Egypt is alive gentlemen, when you are walking the road, you can see people minding their own business, from smithing, riding a carriage, children playing on the street, a group of flamingos flying through the air, animals rampage on nearby village, people singing together in group, so many diversities. Not like in other AC games where people just sort of walking and riding a vehicle, and simply talking to each to each other. The world in ACO is full of details, like animals, you can pet cats, dogs, when you walk in the field of flowers, Bayek put down his hands, reaching and feeling the flowers of wheats on his hands, when nightfall villagers will going back to their house, even the guards, and when you put something on fire, either guards of villagers will try to put it off. This makes exploring the world, going from one location to another location more interesting. And Bayek is an interesting man, the protagonist is likeable, he has personalities.

Story
This is my personal opinion, the story is the usual Ubisoft style, good at the beginning, but forced at the end, seriously, the ending is kinda forced to end, but its not a big problem, at least for me.

Combat
ACO is an rpg now, and combat is kinda sloppy. You have 2 attacks, light and strong. Keep pressint the light attack button for a string of combo, and for the strong attack, its used to break enemies's shield or to know them down. You can also guard using your shield, but honeslty, I rarely guard, the game isnt that hard, unless the enemies are gangin up on you. Another one is dodge, this is the one I use the most. Though more often than not, enemies still can hit you when you dodge. Also there are onlyseveral killing animation that you will see over and over on the course of the game, some good some just plain boring. Besides melee combat, there's a range combat, which is the most satisfying combat in ACO. Aiming is done by holding the RMB, and depends on whick type of bow you are using, each bow has different aiming mode, more will be explained in the gameplay section.

Gameplay
This is where I tell you the game's mechanic, combat is for combat only, while this is for everything AC:O has to offer. For starter, the stealth. Stealth is there, but its dumbed down, you cant merge with poeple to hid anymore, even the hiding spot is somewhat lacking, but bushes are abundant. Yeah, stealth is simplified in Origins. Next, the parkour, in Origins, you dont have to hold certain button in order to run/parkour/free run like previous AC games, Bayek is always running, and you can climb by pressing a button, again simplified. This can be bad or good depends on your taste, I am neutral regarding stealth and free run. But, fun thing is, you can climb almost anything in this game, which is nice.

Equipments, for weapons, you can several types of weapons such as, swords, sickle sword, dual sword, mace, axe, staff, predator bow, light bow, warrior bows. For melee weapons each has their own style and finishing animation, they even has different overpower move, some just give you adrenaline to attack and move faster, some will attack enemy and kill the in one hit. For bows, you have predator, light and warriors bow, as I stated before, when you aim down while using bow, the types of bow depends the aim interface. For light bow, its like a normal bow,but you can charge your shot; for warrior bow, its normal aim, but you cant charge your shot, instead it fires several arrows in quick succession (at most 3), and for predator, when you aim, it will give you a zoomed aim, its easier to hit further target with these bow, and with certain skill, you can guide your arrow into the enemy's head.

For armors, you got shield, which is pretty useless for me, outfits, your 5 basic equips brace, quiver, breastplate, tool pouch and hidden blade, each can be upgraded into legendary using materials and will increase their corresponding atributes. Upgrade them based on your playstyle, either full frontal combat or stealth combat. Outfits can be bought from the weaver shops, sometimes you can buy legendary outfit from the shops, other legendaries can be gotten by completing certain events like chariot race, arenas, daily quests from Reda, or by Heka Chests you bought from Reda with 3000 drachmas (contains random loot).Every outfits can be gotten from the Heka chests, but it need tons of drachmas, except for the Isu Armor, you have to get all the zodiak circle, has 50 silicas and enter the Sphinx, you will get the armor there.

Mounts, since Egypt is massive, you will need mounts. There are 3 types of mounts, chariot, horse and camels. Chariot is faster than the other 2, while horses and camles are similar. Mounts also has quality, but even if you get legendary mount, it wont affect anything aside from getting an achievement for it. 

Materials can be gotten by exploring the world and looting everything, or by killing the guards whom are transporting the resources you want. You can find the transporters by scouting with Senu and mark them so that they can appear on your screen. Be careful, if you are in the middle of a fight with the transporters, other guards transporting another resources may pass and enjoy your party, so you might end up against 8-12 enemies. The transporting guards only transports resources like metals, drachma and woods, for skins you have to hunt animals, such as hyenas, crocodiles, hippos, and lions. 

Skill, AC:O has 3 skills category, warrior, hunter and seer. Warrior is obvious, Hunter is for bow and stealth mainly, and Seer's skills affecting tools damage and unlock, shop unclock, breathing, taming animal etc. I recommend getting the bow or warrior skills first, especially the bow. Guiding arrow through the enemies head never gets old.

The microtransaction is there, but its not lootboxes, but its not as intrusive and the game doesnt constantly reminding you of its presence like in Shadow of War, the store even located on its own section, and Ubisoft sells you an item for a price, not being randomized, its an item, like the mummy outfit, unicorn mount, time saver pack, etc. I am not defending this, I am just stating a fact.

Optimization
Now this is one of the bad of Origins, because the game is plagued by DRM fest, VMProtect, Denuvo, Uplay and Steam, it affects the game's performance. WIth i5-6600k 1070 16GB, I can get Ultra setting with 30-50ish fps, unstable. After I bought i7-7700k, I got 60-80ish fps. I will test the free version once it's released.

Conclusion:
Origins is a good game despite of the flaws, it has moderate to a lot of content (this is purely subjective), pretty graphic, a lively world, ok story, you get your money's worth. But all of those are ruined by performance issue, after the patch it helps a bit, but still freezing sometimes with my i5-6600k, I dont know if its because of the DRM or other things. 
Wait until this problem is fixed, if its not fixed then I recommend get this on sale.

Vous existez dans la peau d'un docteur durant la Première Guerre mondiale, en pleine épidémie de grippe espagnole…

Vous avez été laissé pour mort… dans la peau d'un vampire et votre première action en revenant à vous : tuer votre propre sœur ! On pouvait espérer mieux comme départ non ?

Bref !

Vous partez donc en quête de renseignements, d'indices et d'exploration pour comprendre qui vous a transformé et lui rendre la monnaie de sa pièce.

Encore très loin d'avoir fini le jeu, mais déjà une très bonne impression.

Vampyr ne possède pas de niveaux de difficulté en tant que tels. Ici, vous avez le choix de la facilité ou non.

La facilité en suçant le sang des civils, augmentant ainsi votre expérience très rapidement et de fait l'accès à de bonnes compétences rapidement.
La difficulté réside justement dans le fait de ne pas s'abreuver de plasma frais, tout au moins celui des civils et d'avancer en essayant de réaliser le moins de victimes innocentes possible.

D'après ce que j'ai compris, le jeu a prévu deux fins selon vos choix qui ont des conséquences.

J’affronte deux parties en parallèle :

Une première en mode je suis un gentil et je ne mords que les méchants, et une seconde où je suce le sang des innocents dès l'instant où je n’obtiens plus d'indice à en tirer.

Je joue d'abord la complexité, puis la simplicité sans aller plus loin que l'autre partie. Ainsi, je terminerais le jeu en partie difficile et je verrais aussi la fin qui m'attend en mode facile.

On peut supposer, bien que je puisse me tromper, que je trouve une manière de me guérir du vampirisme dans la partie difficile, et que je meurs. Je suis condamné à errer dans l'ombre dans la partie facile.

Ich bin eigentlich nicht der Fan von RTS, aber Northgard hat etwas unglaublich fesselndes, was wohl nicht zuletzt am Setting liegt. Das ganze Wikingerthema ist liebevoll umgesetzt und es macht tierirsch Spaß die einzelnen Clans zu bespielen. Charmant sind auch die vielen Andeutungen und Zitate, die bei den ersten Spielen ein Schmunzeln entlocken.

Jedoch, das Spiel hat es in sich, sprich: Der Schwierigkeitsgrad ist ungemein happig auf den höheren Stufen. Praktisch steht in diesem Spiel alles gegen den Spieler und seinen Clan. Von den Wetterbedingungen, über die angreifenden Mobs bis hin zu der Verfügbarkeit der Ressourcen. Obendrein ist es ein ewiger Balanceakt den Clan bei Laune und in positiver Stimmung zu halten. Sprich: Es gibt immer was zu nörgeln. Mitunter kann ein Spielzug über Wohl und Wehe des Clans entscheiden. Diese Faktoren jedoch machen es zugleich auch extrem unterhaltsam und fordernd. 

Jeder Clan hat seine Stärken und Schwächen. Manche sind einsteigerfreundlicher als andere, aber nie wirkt es unbalanced. Der Spieler selbst hat es in der Hand und je öfter man spielt, desto leichter geht es auch von selbiger. Man hat eine stetige Lernkurve die belohnt und motiviert.  

Kurz: Northgard ist ein liebevoll desingtes Spiel, welches versteht Einsteigter als auch Veteranen zu bedienen weiß und ist seinen Preis auf alle Fälle wert. Auch wenn ich nie der RTS-Gott werde (solche Ambitionen sind mir fremd), so verbringe ich dann und wann gerne ein paar Stunden mit meinen wuseligen Wikingern in den eisigen Weiten des hohen Norden.

First of all, I have been a faithful fan of the TES series since I was a wee lad and I was wetting myself in the streets of Whiterun where my family lived.

I thought that [b]Oblivion[/b] was one of the best RPGs ever made. And then, this bad boy hits us in 2011.

Skyrim basically [b]knocked down our front doors, grabbed us from the hair and dragged us out in its magnificient, detailed and incredible world[/b]. You [b]just can't resist it[/b], it's an addiction. The more you play it, the more you want it.

Oh, and to make something clear: [b][u]THIS REVIEW IS SPOILER-FREE[/u][/b]. Got that? Let's get to work then, you filthy milk-drinkers.

TESV introduces the province of Skyrim, the home of the Nords in this universe. It's the northern territory of Tamriel and it's full of dense forests, green hills, snowy mountains, beautiful rivers and frozen lakes. All of them, and more, are depicted [b]with an amazing detail[/b] that will immerse you as soon as you make your character.

As soon as the tutorial finishes, you will be shocked by the sheer scale of freedom you have. Nothing constraints you, you can be a mage with heavy armor, a necromancer, an archer, a hunter, a paladin, a healer, anything. You can even [b]destroy your foes with a fork[/b] for all I care. The complex and diverse landscape makes exploring seem endless, but not boring or weary. You will find yourself finding new areas even after your 5th playthrough.

That's Skyrim's magic. These places are exciting to explore. Your only sound is the cave's drippings, or the howling winds as you discover old legends, lost artifacts, forgotten cities, haunted tombs, even ancient civilizations.

As for the gameplay, [b]your actions determine your proficiency[/b]. Your character gets better at whatever you do: from firing arrows and magic to swinging huge battleaxes or sharp daggers. In Skyrim, [b]your talents are unrestricted[/b], there's no class to determine your playstyle. No words are enough to express how good this gameplay is, you just have to see for yourself and test the endless combinations that exist.

Story-wise, there are tons and tons of quests. From fetching wood and ingredients to hunting down the Nordic Dragon God of Destruction, you will never be disappointed by the quest quality and diversity in the way you can finish them. Everywhere you go, you will find new missions to complete that will introduce you to Skyrim's history and lore or the tragedy of the civil war that has struck it. the content simply feels endless.

And the best part: [b][u]MODS![/u][/b] Since 2011 the community does its best to improve Skyrim and add new content. New questlines, weapons, armors, locations, houses, characters, gameplay elements and many, many more are present in both [b]Skyrim Nexus[/b] and the [b]Steam Workshop[/b]. Personally, I finished the game in around 50 hours and then moved on to modding. Mods kept me busy for [b]250[/b] extra hours. That's just crazy. And it's magnificient to see the quality many of the mods have, it's simply astonishing. And, what's best, new stuff are coming out every week. It feels like this game will never die.

Even though there are some drawbacks, like an easy to deal with AI once you learn the game and some quests might feel unsatisfying compared to other RPGs or previous installments, mods are there to improve these flaws and make the game even more perfect than it already is.

I was always given the impression that these were low-quality romance baiting games, but Dan Salvato showed me otherwise.

Dan Salvato did quite a good job on the music, each one fits the scene, and makes you double take on the fact that they're not placing a price tag on it.
The scene detail looks hand drawn and like there was actual care placed into the environment, like the school, or the club itself.

I spent a lot of time [b]hanging[/b] out with Sayori, the first girl you meet and It's pretty obvious that she has a crush on you..albeit, I found it a bit [b]depressing[/b] that there weren't more than 4 girls you could speak to, but Sayori made it all worth it.
She shows genuine care about the player character, and even though you're roped into a lot of situations and how the game tries to "push" the obvious romance, you can still hang out with the others but I highly recommend Sayori.

Yuri is another case entirely, her [b]sharp[/b] wits and shyness were to be expected, but the way she [b]opened up[/b] to me caught me off guard and I found myself loving her all the more as I took a [b]stab[/b] in the dark I went for her on my second run.

[h1] Rust Long Review [/h1]

[b] What is Rust? [/b]

Rust is a survival game, where you find resources and craft guns, build bases and kill other players. The game is only multiplayer
and works with a system that uses servers (like ark). Everyone can make one of these server (you can also make a private one, for you and your friends). The game also includes animals, random buildings to explore, AI vechiles to take down and grab the loot from, and ofcourse the other players

[b] Why did i buy it? [/b]

Its a great game to play with loads of friends, and very time consuming, i really enjy games where i can put 100+ hours in and still play with the same excitement as when i started playing. i would really recommend the game if you have some friends that can buy it too, its deffenitly not expensive for this type of game

[b] Whats the goal of the game? [/b]

Build a base, make guns, and kill everybody then you can capture their items or base, and use the items that you find to raid the next one. At first, it might look repetitive, but its always fun to explore new bases and find new loot!

[b] How does this game stand out? [/b]

first, The players. You can meet so many new players that eventualy become your friends. as example at my favourite server, where i buyed vip at that server and meeted 4 people, we started to skype together and joined the same clan, now after 50+ hours with that people, their almost my best friends :)

[b] How are the graphics, the music and the world?[/b]

The graphics are very good and its nice to run around in the game, there are a lot of biomes to explore and every biome has diffrent cave's, buildings and other cool stuff, the music is a little dowpoint... let me put it this way, there's almost no music.
 
[b] Whats bad about it? [/b]

The music is bad, the lag can sometimes be annoying, but that depends on the server you are playing on.

[b] How are the devs/community?/b]

They're fantastic, like i said, its fun to meat new people in the game. there are a lot of people who are glad to help you :)
and the devs constantly add new content and make the game greater!

[b] How about mods/workshop content? [/b]

you can buy some pretty nice skins in the steam market, there are no other workshop things.

[h1] Is it worth the price? [/h1]

Yep, i cant recommend the game more, its just so good!

[h1] Thanks for reading, and i hope you buy the game! [/h1]

app_name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
review:
A great game. Start as a low-level adventurer and become a legendary hero. Or become a world-renowned thief. Maybe you will become an assassin that kills for gold? How about a powerful mage that can make the very ground tremble with a flick of your wrist. 

These and other choices are available to you as you explore this amazing sand-box RPG. The quests and stories of the game are not at the level of The Witcher 3; however, that has never been what The Elder Scrolls are about. TES are about forging your own path and creating your own incredible story.  Even with all the content packed into the land of the Nords why are people still returning to Skyrim again and again? 

The reason the game is still being played nearly nine years after release - mods.  Skyrim is the game that keeps on giving. Learn how to mod your game and you will enter a world full of near limitless potential. Don't like the leveling system? Change it. Want a quest line that is actually epic and well written, there are several user-created quest mods that blow everything Bethesda did away. How about an Indiana Jones style game where you tracers the land gathering artifacts for a museum. Check out my favorite quest mod - The Legacy of the Dragonborn. It's like a whole new game. 

Every modded Skyrim is different and you can really tailor the experience to suit your personal tastes. Seriously, if you are not playing Skyrim with mods, then you are doing it wrong. 

Happy gaming everyone!

TLDR: Currently broken beyond repair gameplay and a player base that will make you ask God why he hates you.

This is my fifth time rewriting this review, with every rewrite still ending in a Not Recommended ruling. This one, however, will be my final revision as I have just played what is to be my last game of Hunt - a decision I have made for my personal health.

Go over to the For Honor page, read the negative reviews, especially the ones from people with hundred of hours on that game, and you will understand what is wrong with this game. If that sounds like too much work, then you can just read the negative reviews on this game; I assure you that they are all entirely accurate and justified, while the positive reviews are either naive due to lack of exposure or have a case of battered wife syndrome.

Hunt is a game that if it handled as well as it looks it would be one of the greatest games I have ever played, instead it is one of the most broken and disheartening gameplay experiences I have ever made myself suffer through; and suffer through I did, as I was convinced that this game was worth the effort.

Every about this game screams potential, yet despite the overwhelming odds of this being fantastic, it pulls a Destiny and drops the ball on even the simplest of concepts. To know that the people who gave us Crysis and the original Farcry are behind this is baffling.

A game that relies on the  idea of hardcore dynamics as a means of justifying having broken elements that exist solely to punish you; newcomers are immediately turned off, if not by the game itself then the player base that consists of players who are either hackers or have played to such excess that they only find joy in 360 no scoping you in a half second flat; whatever the case they have ruined any chance of this game having a community at this point.

This is further exacerbated by what has to be THE MOST broken gameplay elements of any high production quality game I have ever seen:  the game was originally in third person (look up Hunt: Horrors of the Gilded Age) and when they switched it to first person they never changed the aiming system, so it feels like you're trying to play Gears of War without aim assist, in a game that is heavy on precision; add to that the fact that 90% of the weapons are unusably weak or inaccurate and you have a never ending flow of "what - are you serious?!" moments that are sure to ruin your game night. All of these issues are known to the devs who belligerently  ignore them or willfully make them worse e.g. they took a shotgun that took three point blank shots to kill and nerfed it to require six point blank shots to kill - remember that the aiming is still broken while you're trying to kill someone with your marshmellow gun.

I want nothing more than this game to be good; as my playtime suggests I have already tried extensively to git gud and just enjoy and absolutely gorgeous game with a really slick and enticing premise. Alas, this is a classic case of developer arrogance and a fractious player base leading a wonderful game to ruin.

If you've ever read any Brothers Grimm Fairy tales and enjoyed it then you will love the story line and universe that The Wolf Among Us has and is set in.

The Wolf Among Us puts you in the shoes of Bigby Wolf, or better known as The Big Bad Wolf that tried to have Little Red Riding Hood for supper, the sheriff of Fabletown. Fabletown is a town where a community of fairytale immigrants take refuge in 1980s New York. Being as this game has a very dark theme to it you can already guess what kind of sheriff Bigby is. He doesn't like liars and people who waste his time, which you find out very quickly when questioning Mr. Toad from The Wind in the Willows in the very beginning of the game.

If you were a fan of Telltale Games The Walking Dead then you will see familiar button prompts with that simple line of text stating "So-and-so will remember that choice..." that might make you second guess yourself as soon as you select it. Just like The Walking Dead The Wolf Among Us has appealing graphics and an impressive storyline that will have you immersed the whole time and will more than likely make you start to develop actual feelings for characters in the game just as The Walking Dead made you with its wonderful caricature. This will have an effect on the choices you make in the future of your game.

Telltale decided to use the same episodic theme as they did in The Walking Dead and to some gamers this was unfortunately dispiriting when The Walking Dead first was released. Although The Wolf Among Us is using the same idea, it's definitely still worth picking up. If you're an inpatient person then I would suggest just picking it up when all of the episodes are released, because it will capture you and have you on the edge of your seat and ready for the next episode, if you're patient and don't mind waiting a little then definitely pick it up as soon as possible and experience Telltale's excellent storytelling. Waiting for the next episode will only make it THAT much sweeter when it's finally released.

Overall if you were an admirer of The Walking Dead's gameplay and mechanics, loved any noticeably dark fairy tale by The Brothers Grimm, or really just love a fantastic story line with in-depth caricature and beautiful artwork that makes you feel like you're in a comic book then you will LOVE The Wolf Among Us. I would definitely recommend this game to all of my friends.

Very well done sequel to Shadow of Mordor. Game is basically SoM but with just about every aspect improved. Nemesis system is more present this time even at lower difficulties. Some orcs will become very well known to you because they keep popping up all over the place ambusing you unless you finish them off once and for all and even then they sometimes return from the grave to hinder your progress.

Fortress sieges are fun, fortress defense, not so much. Castle sieges can be made a lot easier by running quests that help reduce the upgrades that a fortress has in place so you are not charging into a wall of poison or trying to batter down a solid iron door.

The story line is okay. The main quest line is short and not that impressive. Sim City ist Vergangenheit. Cities Skylines hat alles besser gemacht, was EA beim "neuen" Sim City falsch gemacht hat. 
Ein sehr detailreiches und liebevoll gestaltetes Spiel, mit viel Spielspaß und das über lange Zeiträume. Und wer etwas mehr Geld in die Hand nehmen möchte, kann sich eines der vielen DLCs kaufen, die durchaus einiges an Inhalt mitliefern, aber definitiv kein Muss sind.
Die Benutzeroberfläche ist übersichtlich und sofort verständlich. Tutorials gibt es nicht wirklich, sondern lediglich einen "Hilfe-Knopf", der allerdings vollkommen ausreicht und in Textform Tipps und Unterstützung gibt. Darüber hinaus gibt es unzählige weitere Tipps im Ladebildschirm, die ebenso hilfreich sind. 
Schönes Feature: Man kann so gut wie alles umbenennen. Von Straßennamen über Häuser, sogar bis hin zu einzelnen Bürgern.
Ich denke, das Spiel ist definitiv empfehlenswert und ein Must-Have für alle, die schon die alten Sim City Teile gemocht haben und nun einen aktuellen Teil suchen.

WICHTIG: Das Game ist sehr RAM-hungrig und frisst locker mal 8-9 GB, sobald die Städte größer werden.

Tipp: Die Maps umfassen 25 Quadrate, wovon man maximal 9 Stück erwerben kann. Wem das nicht ausreicht, kann durch einen kostenlosen Steam-Workshop-Inhalt alle 25 Quadrate erwerben und bebauen. Und das vollkommen Bug-Frei:

review:
Mutant Year Zero is a interesting title that blends post-apocalyptic Earth complete with crumbled structures and relics of a world that no longer thrives.  It does this with a linear storyline.  Guiding you through a plot revolving around a group of mutants called Stalkers.  People that salvage metals for a settlement called the Ark.  Where they go out into the ruined world dubbed, "The Zone" and bring back items that help to keep the last bastion of civilization chugging along.  

As for the game, it blends tactical turn-based combat like XCOM but also has an interesting stealth-mix with light exploration.  Overall, I found the mechanics solid and the RPG elements rewarding.  The faults are minor stuttering and poor difficulty scaling.  I found that the attrition rates when going with a higher difficulty didn't make sense with a static amount of items generated in the world.  It didn't seem fully fleshed out.  As if they could use some help making the balance make more sense.  But, on Normal mode the game is quite enjoyable with lightly moderate difficulty.

This is a tentative review at the moment to help counteract all the kneejerk negative reviews over minor port issues.

The game itself has been amazing so far. Platinum's combat does wonders to make the moments inbetween Yoko Taro's amazing writing enjoyable. The game, like the first Nier, enjoys mashing together various styles of gameplay from shmup to action, though you are primarily playing it as an action game.

As for the port, FPS is capped to 60, with prerendered cutscenes capped to 30. There are also a lot of in-game cutscenes that happen at 60 FPS, so you don't have to worry about it dropping to 30 every time there's story.

The game supports resolutions beyond 1920x1080, although they will not show up in the menu unless you have a higher resolution monitor hooked up (I believe the highest resolution option is just an adaptive resolution that adjusts to your monitor, but don't quote me on that as I only have 1080p monitors). However, the fullscreen option currently doesn't work properly, and will actually render the game at a lower resolution than specified (how much lower I don't know, but it's enough to be noticeable). Unfortunately while the game will run at the proper resolution in windowed mode, there is also no borderless window support, and in order to have the game run at the proper resolution in fullscreen you will need to use another program to force the game into borderless window mode. I've been using Borderless Gaming (the free version you can find through a google search, not the one on steam) and haven't had any issues.

Beyond those issues and some lackluster graphic options the game is an alright port.

And honestly the quality of the game itself (or at least what I have played of it so far, I plan to update this review at a later date when I've beaten it) more than makes up for the port's shortcomings.

you're looking for a game review you've come to the wrong place. But if youre looking for a fantastic ravioli recipe you've come to the right place.

Ingredients
- To Make the Dough
375 grams (3 cups) plain flour
1/2 teaspoon salt
2 eggs
1/4 cup (50 ml / 3½ tablespoons) olive oil
1/2 cup (120 ml / 8 tablespoons) water
Extra flour for dusting 


- To Make Cheese Filling
15 ounces (425 grams) container Ricotta cheese
5 ounces (142 g/about 1/2 cup plus 2 tablespoons) "3 Cheese Italian Blend" (Parmesan, Romano & Asiago)
Note: grate these cheeses yourself and create your own custom blend.
1/2 cup cheddar cheese
2 eggs, lightly beaten
1/2 teaspoon salt
1/2 teaspoon pepper


- Extras
Your favorite sauce for the ravioli (i.e. marinara/ marijuana)
Parmesan cheese
Basil
Fried vegetables
Shrimp
Fish slices
Chicken pieces 
Make the Ravioli filling.

- In a small mixing bowl, add the ricotta and mash with a fork.
- Add in the 3-cheese blend, Cheddar cheese, eggs, salt, and pepper.
- Mix all ingredients thoroughly until you have a smooth, paste-like consistency.
- Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes. 

Make the Ravioli dough.

- Crack eggs into a large mixing bowl and beat them with a fork. Add water, oil, and salt. Mix.
- Add 1 cup flour to the bowl. Use a fork to mix the flour with the eggs, water, oil, and salt. Repeat with the rest of the flour. Mix until a smooth dough is formed.
- Clear and clean off a large work surface and dust it with flour. This is where you are going to roll out your dough.
- Take the dough out of the mixing bowl, shape it into a ball, and place it on your work surface. Knead for at least 10 minutes or until it becomes elastic.
- Dust a rolling pin with flour to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll out the dough until it is about 1/8 inch (1/3 cm) thick, or about the thickness of 2 stacked quarters.
- With a cookie cutter or upside-down water glass, cut out circles in the dough (will make about 15-20 dough circles).
- Ball up the unused dough and either roll it out and make a couple more raviolis, or wrap it and put in the freezer for another time. Dough can keep for weeks when frozen. Just make sure to wrap well so that it doesn’t suffer from freezer burn or absorb freezer odor. 

Fill the Ravioli shells.

- Take the ravioli filling out of the refrigerator and place a tablespoon of it in middle of a dough.
- Fill a small bowl with water, dip your fingers in, and moisten around the outer edge of the dough circle.
- Fold the dough in half over the filling, making a half-moon shape. Be sure all the filling stays inside. Pinch the edges together and then seal the edges of the ravioli with a fork. Make sure to press firmly and go all the way around. This will add a “homemade” touch as well.
- Repeat this process for all your dough circles.
- Dust the finished ravioli with flour to keep them from sticking together. 

Form the Shells and Fill Using a Ravioli maker.

- Roll the dough into two sheets
- Place one sheet on the ravioli maker, and form the filling cups.
- Fill with the ravioli mixture.
- Lay the second sheet of dough on top, and roll it out. This will seal in the filling.
- Remove and separate the finished raviolis.

Cook the Ravioli.

- Fill a large pot with water and bring to a boil.
- Place the ravioli in boiling water for 5-6 minutes, or until they float. You can also test for doneness by nibbling on the edges to test.
- If you don't want to make all the ravioli at one time, you can freeze the rest 
- Take ravioli out of boiling water with large slotted spoon and place on warmed plates

Serve it up.
Top with your favorite sauce, grate some fresh cheese over it, and enjoy!

This is a third person action adventure where you impersonate a half human half wraith character that fights to free well known 'lord of the rings' locations from the grip of sauron. You do so by fighting with a plethora of skills and using sword,  bow and stealth, versus countless 'grunt' orcs and their 'captains'.
There are a few side challenge-quest types that reveal the story or expand on the lore and they're all well made.
This is bascially it, but naturally the game's quality shows through the implementation.

Fine combat mechanics, enormous enemy variety, great playstyle and skill combinations, interesting story and great graphics (albeit the engine is a bit dated, and this shows both in performance and texture / lighting quality).

Despite the game's positive aspects though, I must say I appreciated it for the abandon with which you'll be slaughtering orcs left and right. In fact, even in normal difficulty, even the most stupid of captains will often be so abundantly surrounded by their grunts, that you'll repeatedly have to back off, become stupid looking for a way to heal, and the get into the fray again: the character doesn't heal automatically and can only use skills as a source of health which in certain situations is as a matter of fact a showstopper.
Additionally, there are many enemies with 'special' dynamics that mean you can't attack them normally, and you must wait for THEM to attack, like this was a fucking 80's nintendo game.
So at a point, I turned down the difficulty to EASY, and actually enjoyed advancing through the quests without the actual hassle and bother of near-invulnerable enemies and their infinite waves of quicktime-event enemies.

So to summarise: a great game for the lord of the ring fans, and a great follow to its predecessor, but don't expect GTA5 quality missions or Batman melee combat quality. Additionally, if you can cope with the artificial difficulty in fights (don't even get me started on the 6 to 12 max arrows in the quiver), you'll at least enjoy this as I did.

Sekiro is a challenging game that will reward patient and determined players with a personal and poignant tale of loyalty.

The combat system bears very slight similarities to the Souls series. There are no heavy attacks here, you can swing your sword or thrust with it (not a smart idea) by holding down the button. You have one button for your off-hand weapon, one button for your grappling hook, and one button for blocking. 

You possess the same two resources as your enemies, Vitality and Posture. Vitality is most easily understood as HP, posture plays a similar role that stamina did previously. Posture is a bar that slowly fills from blocking attacks, taking damage, and having your attacks deflected (think perfect blocking, or parrying). If your posture bar overfills, you will be posture-broken, and unable to take any actions for a moment. 

When an enemy is posture broken, they become vulnerable to deathblows. A deathblow instantly empties an enemies health bar, killing most weaker enemies. Stronger enemies have multiple health bars, in my first playthrough some incredibly strong foes had 3. 

The beauty of the posture mechanic comes from its interaction with vitality. Posture will start to recover after a few moments of not taking any posture damage. The lower your vitality, the slower it will refill. Guarding causes it to refill faster, but this also applies to your enemies. Combat then often becomes a balancing act between maintaining pressure on your enemies to prevent their posture from recovering, and being careful to not attack recklessly, lest your attacks be deflected and thus fill your own posture bar.

Combat in Sekiro also contains several types of unblockable attacks. Sweeps, Thrusts, and Grabs. 
-Sweeps cannot be deflected or guarded against, and must be jumped over. If you steel your nerves, and jump straight up instead of away (as your instinct is going to tell you to do), you can kick off of the enemies head to do massive posture damage.
-Grabs cannot be deflected, parried, or countered in any way. You must avoid them, or suffer massive (and usually fatal damage). They have long recovery frames if they miss however, giving you an option to retaliate.
-Thrusts cannot be guarded or jumped over, but they can be deflected if you have perfect timing. You can obtain a skill called the mikiri counter, where instead of blocking, if you dodge towards the thrust at the last second, you will step on the point of the attack, and do massive posture damage. This is one of the coolest and most satisfying things to pull off in Sekiro in my opinion. Certain enemies also possess this skill, and thrusting at them will result in them countering you, killing you instantly. Never thrust.

Death in sekiro is an obstacle to be overcome, not the end of an attempt. You possess limited ability to revive on the spot after being killed, through nodes of resurrective power. These nodes are refilled through deathblows and killing enemies, but your first node can only be refilled by resting at a sculptors idol (think a bonfire from dark souls).

I finished my first Sekiro playthrough in about 30 hours, with a decent amount of that time spent exploring and looking for secrets. There seems to be a new game+ option that i have not yet started. There are multiple endings.

Update on this game: I bought this game back when it was Early Access, back in 2015. At the time, I knew that the game was heavily unoptimized and it was most likely due to the devs just putting a lot of effort into looking to make the game pretty. I gave them a chance to optimize their game, and waited.

And waited.

Skip forward 4 years later, 2019, and the game is still as unoptimized as the very first day I bought the game, 4 years ago. It still feels like an Early Access game, except with more things tacked on to it.

I am currently playing on a GTX 1060 graphics card, and the game still runs like it was dunked in molasses and fresh black tar. Compared to the GTX 660 back when I first tried out the game, and running it on Low settings. I stilled tried running the game on low settings and it's still an awful mess. 

I don't know if Studio Wildcard as a whole lacks the ability to make their game run smoothly, or they don't care to make it run smoothly, or a mixture of both, but it's been 4 years, and it still runs awfully. If the developers do not know how to make their game run smoothly, they should outsource that kind of technical work to a company that knows how to do it, because it's pretty obvious (at least on their own official servers) that they don't know how to do it, and 4 years of the game being in the same unstable state proves this. 

Other edits I have made were about how buggy the game is, and thankfully, it's not as buggy as the day I bought it, but given how I can't even run the game on a semi-powerful card on the lowest settings of this game without the game almost blue-screening my computer, I don't know if they fixed the bugs, or the bugs all amalgamated together to make the game what it is today.

Either way, I heard that this game is going free soon, which means that the developers are really desperate to gain back lost players to their game. The main thing they should do is the same thing that I put on my very first review of the game: Fix the game, make it stable, and stop adding things into it that'll break it even more. 4 years of lessons should be enough, but that ball is in the developers' court.

Highly demanding and equally rewarding.

Unlike previous Souls-like games, Sekiro requires you master the games combat in order to progress. There are no attributes to sink points into as stat boosts are linked to bosses and challenging enemies, and there are no weapons to hunt for and upgrade. To advance in the game is almost entirely down to your ability to outclass your opponent in swordsmanship. Fortunately Sekiros combat is intensely satisfying. 
If you are a Soulsborne veteran this entry will require you to rethink your approach and shed off your old habits, as fights require an almost rythymic quality to parry, attack and evade your enemies attacks and crush their posture, allowing for a single killing blow. 

The stealth mechanics while basic add another dimension to tackling difficult areas and the verticality awarded to you via the grappling hook allows you to survey the challenge from above and plan your approach and the story is engaging and unlike previous from software games is told fairly straight, however there is plenty of lore to discover if you look for it.

Sekiro is an excellent addition to From Software's catalogue of granite hard RPGs and also has some of the series most rewarding and intense 1 on 1 boss duels yet.

As for the software side, Sekiro runs like a dream, however it is capped at 60fps. I have had no trouble running it, the game never dipping below that 60fps cap.
The game also looks outstanding, the backgrounds and levels (especially one level that has you running through a burning village at night) can be breathtaking, but the major standout is the quality of animation, even after the 100th deathblow animation is still enjoyed seeing it.

Sekiro is a truly great game, but admittedly may not be for everyone even including fans of previous games. 

If you enjoy crafting the perfect character build and equipping them with the ideal weapon and armour so that they can overcome any challenge then you may find Sekiro lacking.

If you want to play a focused and pure combat action/rpg that will test your skills then don't hesitate!

Divinity: Original Sin 2 is one of the best, if not the best, turn based strategy fantasy RPG there is right now.

8/10 Combat - The combat in Divinity is AMAZING, for a turn based one, that is. The whole concept of Divinity's combat system is "skill combos".  
Throw a giant boulder, that leaves an oil puddle behind, at a group of enemies and follow it up with a fireball for a nasty explosion. Quench the flames with rain, which will leave steam behind, then hurl a lighting bolt at it to create a thunder cloud. 
Rupture your victims tendons then literally turn them into a scared chicken and give them a speed boost so you can watch them run away and bleed to death. 
There are so many creative and fun ways for you to approach a problem, sadly not all of them work as well as you would want them to, and on higher difficulty only a handful of strategies are actually viable. 

9/10 Character progression/Builds - You start the game as a regular level 1 soldier, rogue, pyromancer, whatever you chose at the beginning, but you are not bound to your starting class. Started as a zweihander wielding soldier? Why not get yourself a pyromancer's staff and put your attribute points into intelligence, pyrokinetic and two handed weaponry and become a close range, fire swinging battle mage that can utilize both pyromancer and soldier skills! It might not be the optimal combination but it still works well! The only complaint I have is that hybrid builds are somewhat limited due to the fact that each weapon type only scales with one attribute. 

9/10 Exploration - I'm on my fourth playthrough right now and I still stumble upon things I haven't known about. There are 4 world maps, tied to the 4 story arcs of the game, and each one is unique, looks different from the last and has dozens of quests and secrets, although some of the riddles you need to solve to get to those secrets felt somewhat arbitrary or are easily forgotten while you're exploring and finding new ones, 

8/10 Story - It's your classic "You're the chosen one and have to save the world from the bad guys" plot. However, Divinity puts a unique spin on it. The bad guys aren't just bad because they're bad guys, although those types still exist, but rather have good, or at least relatable, intentions. And the way you save the world, or if at all, is up to you, as well. There are a lot of interesting and funny NPCs with a lot of story on their own and depending on who and how you talk to them the story can unravel itself in different ways. 

10/10 Overall - Despite nothing being a 10/10, I would still give Divinity: Original Sin 2 a perfect score. It is rare, maybe even impossible, to find a game that doesn't have any short coming, but imo Divinity comes very, very close to that. If you like or are interested in turn based strategy, are a fantasy RPG fan or want to try one out, definetly give this one a shot. It even has multiplayer, both online and local, and mod support!

Hands down, the best turn based strategy fantasy RPG there is right now.

app_name: Total War: ROME II - Emperor Edition
review:
Ben lontano dalla qualità del primo, nonostante tutto si fa valere. D'accordo, sono servite 12 patch per renderlo un gioco all'altezza, e a parte alcune mancanze di intelligenza della CPU, è molto apprezzata la collaborazione con lo Steam Workshop, la grafica, ovviamente, è superba, la storia delle tecnologie e ottima, la gestione delle tasse forse poteva rimanere da provincia a provincia, metodo di gestione degli insediamenti invece carino...i dlc si potevano evitare, ma oramai è una prerogativa dei giochi di oggi...alla fine, 4 stelle se le merita...più 3,5 che 4 però XD

[AGGIORNATO: EMPEROR EDITION]
Alla luce dell'uscita della "edizione definitiva" di Rome II, si può dire che questo era il gioco che sarebbe dovuto uscire quell'ormai lontano 3 Settembre: molti meno bug, la politica resa finalmente utile (nonostante ci si debba mettere d'impegno per fare le guerre civili), delle campagne con la C maiuscola (oltre alla Grande, la Imperator Augustus promette moolto bene), e la fluidità migliorata.
Andiamo, chi non ha mai voluto immedesimarsi in uno dei tre triumviri? Io avrei, personalmente, adorato una storia su TUTTE le guerre civili da Mario e Silla, ma questo è già tanto. I dlc si potevano evitare...come al solito. Manca (sigh, oh se manca!) la funzione dilpomatica di "scambiare" territori, in effetti oltre i soliti 3/4 trattati non ha molta originalità. A parte ciò e altre piccole cose che ci si ricorda da Rome I, questo è davvero Rome II Total War. Qualcuno direbbe "alla buon'ora!", ma CA non ha mollato nonostante l'avvio a rallentatore e pieno di bug e si è impegnata, patch dopo patch, a dimostrare che la colpa, in fondo, è più di SEGA che di CA. Ora ha 4 stelle meritate.
P.s.: un po' più di battaglie storiche però...xD

My wife's Uncle Ken was a navigator in a Liberator bomber with the 8th Airforce, so this game has an oddly personal feeling to it.  It looks cute, at first, and during the training missions, it feels a touch cartoony - though that does not detract like it does in Civ VI.  This cartoon bobblehead gives you the illusion of security - even when your gunners first give Jerry what-for.  

That illusion is dispelled when you really head out over the Channel.  The Sweaty Betty's first mission was easy enough - bomb stuff.  But the second quickly went FUBAR - though not SNAFU - because I know the name of who, ahem screwed up.  First I dropped all my bombs on a single target - there were two bombing sites - then I didnt tag the enemy fighters fast enough, didnt dispatch my mechanic to repair the engines quickly enough - I was loosing the four fast enough that it was damn near a count-down.  I finally said "bugger it" - lets see if Steam catches that one - and told the pilot to take us back to Ol' Blighty.  Which, I suppose, he successfully did.  Unfortunatly, a Lancaster doesnt maintain altitude very well on a single engine, so as soon as we found England, we promptly landed.  Face first.  Which I do not recommend as a landing proceedure.  Two of my crew lived to see the Sweaty Betty II.

This is a hard, unforgiving multi-tasking game.  I'm looking forward to more of 1942, though hopefully I've seen the last of roman numerals.  Wishful thinking, which, incidentally, was the name of my training bomber.

As for the fabled online experience, it's hands-down the most sluggish multiplayer I have ever seen. Only recently have I been able to use it as more of my steam friends have the game in their library as well and we simply decided to put our heads together. If one is attempting to try the multiplayer be prepared for the slowest loading times you will ever see. Even with an SSD, great WiFi, and other high-end factors; you will still find your self in a loading screen staring at the heavens of Los Santos in a gamble if you're able to join your friends session or not. Speaking of which, online is genuinely better with friends.

Multiplayer (Hard Sell, Best trashed around with friends)

Музыка, детально проработанный город, цвета и сама стилистика, дух игры – вот что формирует ощущение свободы в первую очередь. Сан-Франциско и его пригороды – это оттиск реальных мест, на которых затерлись все скучные кварталы и остались только самые живые и интересные места. Поэтому город занятно изучать. Просто бродить, глазеть по сторонам, фотографироваться с достопримечательностями (для их поиска даже приложение в смартфоне главного героя есть) и людьми.  Посмотрите любое геймплейное видео или запись  и увидите, какой живой в игре мир.
Залипнуть на таких делах можно на долгие часы, и дело не только в городе. К прожиганию виртуальной жизни располагает сама атмосфера игры. Тут нет ни капли нуарного тона оригинальной Watch Dogs.
Погружению в атмосферу бесконечного жаркого лета способствуют и герои. В их образах совершенно не хочется копаться, потому что это слепок нас самих. Маркус (главный герой) и его друг Рэнч по пути на очередное опасное задание обсуждают вовсе не детали операции. Они заводят спор о том, кто круче: Хищник или все-таки Чужой. Спорят они так живо, что так и разбирает свои пять копеек вставить. В итоге сходятся на том, что Хищник круче, потому что дрался с Шварценеггером, и переходят к обсуждению кроссовера вселенной Чужих и Бэтмена. И да, никакого пафоса с официальных артов в образах героев нет, выдохните.
Побочные задания – тема вообще отдельная. Невероятно, но до Ubisoft, кажется, наконец-то дошло, что проходить одинаковые миссии десятки часов – скучно. Watch Dogs 2 постоянно подбрасывет что-то интересное, и даже привычные рутинные вещи преподносит с фантазией.

[b]DISCLAIMER[/b] - I bought this game wanting a Monster Hunter clone.

So is this a bad game? No, but I will do my best to describe exactly "what" kind of game this is so no one is mislead like I was. 

If you like Dynasty Warrior then I think you will enjoy this. It is a hybrid between that kind of hack n slash OP gameplay and the grind/crafting that a Monster Hunter game would show off. Unfortunately that's where the similarities end. Expect a casual auto-pilot story where you are supposed to care about a village and your romantic interest all while be told to kill the same monster over and over again in different locations. I never felt accomplished after beating a boss or scared to face anything whilst playing the game. The crafting allows a lot of options but the art style/ over all graphics of the game make me not care about when and what I will craft to replace my current gear.

[*] What I was expecting was a thrilling challenge, a variety of different monsters and animals, a living breathing outdoors to weather and visuals that make me proud of my kills/ gear.

[*] What I got was a demon slaying cruise including the drink package, the same monster over and over again, a map that made me question the entire premise of the game and boring boss battles wear we gang raped every challenge and received the same weapons and move sets with different color palates.

It's not bad, but it's not a Monster Hunting game by any means.

It's here. Prepare to die again in what may be (subjective opinion) best SoulsBorne game to date.

If you ever played any game of this series you will feel right at home here. From Software took an “if it ain't broke, don't fix it” approach so gameplay stayed the same with few minor tweaks. Spell charges are gone replaced with much more flexible magic bar and you can switch between covenants at will with a simple menu switch. There are a lot more bonfires this time around and you can warp between them almost from the get go. It cuts on unnecessary running and shifts focus on what is most important here: exploring new beautifully interconnected world filled with traps and aggressive enemies eager to turn you into a bloody pulp. Combat now feels faster while still retaining its tactical side with newly added Weapon Skills - special moves that are determined by the weapon you have equipped.

My first playthrough was an enjoyable experience and I'm already experimenting with new builds. Perhaps DS3's biggest drawback is that it is yet another iteration of Demon's Souls, refined in some areas yet oddly conservative in others. However, it is an iteration I had a lot of fun with. Highly recommended.

游戏时间已近百小时，主线还没通关，突然发现自己还没有为WITCHER3写点什么。

WITCHER这个系列，我是从一代开始接触，一路玩下来的。不敢说自己多资深吧，因为入手一代的时候STEAM上已经不知是第几次打折了。不过，如果没有记错的话，至少是在二代上市之前，所以相比大多数从三代才开始接触这个系列的玩家来说，我深知这个系列是如何一步一个脚印走到今天这个地位的。

根据一般经验，系列游戏的评分，如果和上一代相比没什么新的亮点出来的话，评分会较低。如果评分持平，那说明新作已经有可观的进步了。而WITCHER三部曲的评分是一部比一部更高，这里面蕴含了多大的进步可想而知。

技术进步和投资增加带来的效果我就不多讲了，一代进间屋子都要读盘，还经常看到长的完全一样的NPC，即便如此我还是玩通关了，因为游戏自始自终都非常吸引我玩下去。最近在补原著小说，感觉二代三代的剧情跟原著联系多一些，一代则像个独立外传（上来就失忆什么的）有些重要人物如叶奈法、希里竟然是三代才第一次登场，不知道是不是后来和作者重新谈过改编的权限之类，抑或是有意为之？

游戏对杰洛特这个人物的塑造非常成功，很好地还原了小说里那个有一点点侠义色彩的猎魔人形象，台词设计也是如此，有些选项虽然是玩家的，但不管选什么杰洛特说出来都让人拍案叫绝。RPG游戏预设主角性格的话会减少玩家的代入感，但如果做得足够有魅力，玩家还是会买账。

看了小说之后还发现，游戏的支线任务设计与世界背景的基调与原著也十分契合，通过这些大量的支线任务，把这些内容生动地表现出来，传递给玩家，丝毫也不单调乏味。以至于，每当骑马经过一个有新任务的告示板（地图上显示为金色）或看到金色感叹号时，都会忍不住停一停，好奇会遇到什么样的故事。现在有些RPG支线任务虽多，但都是些滥竽充数的玩意儿，让人根本提不起兴趣，相比之下本作支线任务质量之高，堪称业界模范。

战斗系统方面延续了二代的ARPG套路，轻-重攻击配合法印，新增的是小跳步闪躲，不像二代只能翻滚。透射武器在二代的炸弹基础上又增加了弩，但在大多数战斗中都不怎么好用……值得一提的是一代其实是传统RPG，战斗也就是点鼠标，分快击（猫）强击（狼）群伤（狮鹫）三种模式，到了三代发展成了轻甲（猫）中甲（狮鹫）重甲（熊）为基础的人物培养思路，挺有意思的。法印从一代到三代都是这五种，但具体效果有所微调。还有嗑药抹油这些原著中的猎魔人特点在三部游戏中都有很好的还原。

小游戏方面，昆特牌闻名天下，甚至专门出了独立的卡牌游戏，但真正从一代传承到三代的小游戏其实是酒馆搏击……一代特有的骰子游戏、二代特有的扳手腕，还有三代特有的赛马，差不多就这些了。

关于开放世界，最初听说WITCHER3会做成开放世界时我是十分期待的，但同时也有点不安，因为开放世界是把双刃剑，对于剧情叙述方面，开放世界接任务肯定比不上章节式推进来得紧凑。事实也确实如此，我经常会把主线晾在一边去清支线，说好了午夜在十字路口碰头也不知NPC等了杰洛特多少天。这种叙事上说不通的地方，就当是白玉微瑕吧。

废话了这么多，其实游戏都已经这么便宜了，买一个来体验一下比看评测强多了，大不了退款呗。而且CD社自家的GOG平台上卖的还是无DRM硬盘版，简直是太有自信了，我服。再说个题外话，其实CD社很早就声明WITCHER3会有多少多少个免费DLC，我一直以为会自动添加进去，其实需要到商店页面点一下的，可别错过了。

Was soll ich sagen?

Sid Meiers Civilization VI! Mal abgesehen davon, dass ich diesen Namen in meinem Leben wohl hundertfach falsch geschrieben habe, hat mich diese Tatsache nicht davon abgehalten, mich in dieses Spiel regelrecht zu verbinden. Suchtpotential auf höchstem Niveau! 
Ich bin seit dem fünften Teil dabei und muss sagen, dass mich der sechste wesentlich länger gepackt hat, was aber auch daran liegt, dass ich seither Civ 5 nicht mehr gespielt habe.
Man kann definitiv sagen, dass Civ 6 ein gelungener Nachfolger ist, wenn nicht sogar der bessere Teil. Ich kann die Leute nicht verstehen, die sich über den Comic Look beschert haben und es immer noch tun. Was Civ denn je das Non-Plus-Ultra Realismus Strategie Spiel? Nein!
Mir gefällt sowohl der Look des Vorgängers, als auch dieser hier und fügt sich einfach perfekt ins Spielgeschehen ein. Civ 6 sieht einfach Bombe aus!

ABER: 
Ich kann alle Leute verstehen, die zurecht die DLCs kritisieren. Die Haupterweiterungen (Rise and Fall nicht zu empfehlen, da man bei Gathering Storm alle Inhalte dazu bekommt, außer die Anführer aus Rise and Fall) sind meiner Meinung nach alles in allem noch Lohnenswert, aber die Preispolitik von Civ 6 ist alles andere als gerechtfertigt, außer in der Hinsicht, dass Sid Meiers im "Action-Strategie" Genre einfach ein Machtmonopol vertritt, welches sich hoffentlich mit Humankind endlich etwas in eine andere Richtung lenken lässt. 
Ich hatte mir im Sale (welche mit gut Glück 20% Rabatt bieten) sämtliche Inhalte angeschafft, nur damit zwei Monate später ein Season Pass angekündigt wird. 
Sid Meiers versucht also konstant nach Wegen zu suchen um den Käufer noch mehr Geld aus der Tasche zu ziehen und das währe ja an sich gar nicht mal so schlimm, ABER es wird an den falschen Stellen gearbeitet. Statt immer weiteren Szenarien und Anführern sollte man an der KI arbeiten. Doch diese hat man ganz offensichtlich schon aufgegeben und somit zu scheitern der Armee des Spielers vor die Kanonen geworfen. 

Ich kann dazu nur sagen: Ein MUSS für jeden Fan und Strategie Liebhaber. BESONDERS für all jene, die eben nicht das komplexeste Spielgefühl brauchen, sondern auch mit kleinen Schritten und wenigen Entscheidungen große Reiche formen können. Das motiviert und macht jede Menge Spaß!
Zu leicht war mir persönlich das Spiel dann doch nicht, aber das liegt nicht daran, dass die KI auf höheren Schwierigkeitsgraden besser ist, sondern so viele Boni erhält, dass ich als Spieler die Kontrolle verloren habe und mich das mehr frustriert, als fordert und anspornt. 

Wer aber mit dem Genre absolut nichts anfangen kann und rundenbasierte Strategie nicht zuspricht, der sollte entweder gänzlich die Finger von diesem Spiel lassen, oder sich einen der früheren Teile zu Gemüte ziehen. 
Beste Empfehlung: "Sid Meiers Civilization V"

[i]Duck game- хорошая игра за разумные деньги, в которой можно провести не один свободный вечер.[/i]  

[h1]Что же такого особенного в ней?[/h1] 
1. Наверное, одна из немногих игр, в которой наличие багов являются плюсом, нежели минусом. Например на некоторых картах при помощи нескольких ящиков  можно пройти сквозь стену( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)
2. Незамысловатый сюжет. Ходи, бегай, убивай.  Игра проходит в темпе, раунды длятся по 15-20 секунд. За пол часа можно отыграть с десяток игр. 
3. Хорошая оптимизация игры, игра не требует особо мощного железа и пойдет у всех, даже если у вас средневековый ПК. 
4. Огромное количество карт и разнообразных видов оружия, начиная от простого однозарядного пистолета -“Пукалки”, так я его называю, и заканчивая огромным лазером, который [strike]ху*ри[/strike] стреляет через стены. Так же в игре можно встретить различные виды метательного оружия, такие как гранаты, мины и даже ЯЩИК. Да-да, врага можно убить просто кинув ему на голову ящик :)   
5. Шапки. За выполнение различных ачивок в игре выдаются шапки, в которых можно бегать. Более того, с помощью редактора можно самому создавать их, и убивать противникам скажем, с холодильником на башке.

Таким образом, Duck game-великолепная игра, непохожая на другие игры, если вы ищете что-то новое, смело берите ее.

Playing Persona 4 again really drives home to me just how good of an rpg it is. The Dungeon's aren't nearly as fun and unique as the ones in Persona 5, due to their nature of being random generated floors much like the Mementos is in P5, but the fights shine just as much and sometimes outshine those in its successor. The social links feel very personal and tell very fullfilling and complete stories that really get me invested in the characters they involve. Only a few of the characters in this story I find flat or annoying which is a testament to its writing as there are a LOT of characters in this game that all have their own little stories and hangups to experience. The story moves a satisfying and active pace and it really feels like the team in this game are working hard to figure out a mystery bigger than themselves instead of just reacting to situation as they happen, which is more than I can say for a lot of other mystery rpgs. Really enjoyed this game far more than I expected to considering I had played the original Persona 4 back when I was a kid.

Music: 9/10, so many goods songs on this soundtrack like "Angus Story" and "Church Hill". All the background tracks are very calming and zen, but some of the best songs are the more upbeat and lively ones that you get to play on the Bass minigame. A list of bangers for sure.

Graphics: 10/10, some people may be off put by the graphics of this game, but I absolutely love them. The very cartoony, imperfect design of all the characters and environments really ties the game together and makes it feel complete and cozy. 

Characters: 10/10, all of the characters in the game felt like real people with actual personalities. It was very obvious that a bunch of time was put in to the characters backstories and how they fit into the world. The relationships that are made between the characters throughout the game is absolutely precious, especially the sister bond that develops between Mae and Bea. But, the best character, without a doubt, was my boy Angus. 

Story: 10/10, at first I was somewhat reluctant about the story, because within the first hour or so of the game not much is revealed to the player. But as the game progresses the overarching story, as well as the small side stories that encapsulate the lives of the cast of characters, bloom into full effect and take you on a wild and emotional ride, especially in the later half of the game. On top of that the use of real life problems, such as emotional and mental issues, loss of a loved one, and the idea of just getting by day to day, are expertly placed throughout the story, and show the different ways people cope. The last thing I will touch on is the dialogue, because oh my god, is it amazing in this game. The interaction between characters is so real, and the way in which they talk to one another feels very natural, and not fabricated at all, like many current day games do.

Summary (Minor Spoilers): In Night in the Woods you play as Mae Borowski, a 20 year old recent college dropout who has moved back to her hometown and is now living with her parents once again. As you play through the game you meet old and new friends of Mae, explore her cozy little hometown, and plunge down a dark path secrecy as not everything in the town is as it seems.  

Gameplay: 8/10, the only thing lacking in this game is true gameplay, but that is because is a story and dialogue driven game. However, the little gameplay that is scattered throughout the game, like the Bass playing, Knife Fighting, and Crossbow shooting, are fun and extremely wholesome.

Honestly, the story was amazing, the gameplay is great and the class trials are fair and challenging. I haven’t played through the second mode, but I’m definitely going to give it a try. I fully recommend this game to literally anyone. It’s one of the best games you can get, you’ll fall in love with the characters, and you’ll learn to deal with the despair. 10/10

Ok, mon avis est celui d'une personne ayant suivi une formation en archéologie et histoire de l'art. Alors je le recommande, mais sous réserve. 

Pour reprendre ce que disent les trois quarts des semi-illettrés ayant donné leur avis sur ce jeu sans savoir parler le français,
-oui c'est beau
-oui c'est bien conçu
-oui, c'est un vrai RPG
-oui, on sent que la communauté a été écoutée
-oui, on prend son pied à découvrir la Grèce à l'époque classique à travers les yeux d'un personnage pour une fois pas trop cliché (avec un vrai challenge comme je les aime en mode cauchemar, bravo !)
-oui, c'est juste sublime à quel point le jeu a été bossé dans les moindres détails.

Alors vous me direz, "mais alors pourquoi, espèce de triple imbécile, le recommandes-tu sous réserves ?" 

Parce que l'intrigue, du début à la fin du 6e épisode, est parfaite. Oui, parfaite. Mais arrive un moment où les gens tels que moi décrochent complètement. 

*Alerte Spoiler *Alerte Spoiler*

A un moment donné, on se retrouve propulsés devant l'Atlantide (ouai ouai rien que ça, c'est pas comme si c'était un sujet piège qui avait déjà été surexploité...) et attention, tenez-vous bien, Pythagore qui vous sort un vieux "Je suis ton père" suivi d'un "En fait avoir des gosses je m'en fous, mais toi t'es né parce qu'il fallait bien que notre lignée se perpétue, et puis de toute façon personne d'autre pourrait zigouiller les tordus du culte de kosmos".

Alors non, mesdames et messieurs, je dis un non catégorique à ce vieil atlantide réchauffé, justifié par une civilisation ancienne disparue qu'on veut à tout prix voir comme un ciment rattachant toutes les cultures mystérieuses et grandes interrogations de notre histoire. Vous valez mieux que ça les gars, votre scénario était tellement plus prometteur que ça. Vous vous êtes jetés tête baissée dans un sujet déjà tourné et retourné dans tous les sens, par tous les types d'individus ayant réfléchi dessus. 

A la limite je pardonne vos incohérences historiques, légères et liées à un besoin de faciliter l'écriture du récit.

Mais vraiment votre jeu a perdu toute crédibilité à mes yeux en voyant que parmi TOUTES LES POSSIBILITES QUE VOUS OFFRAIT LA GRECE A L'EPOQUE CLASSIQUE il a fallu que vous choisissiez cet immondice d'atlantide, symbole cuisant pour vous d'un choix de facilité ridicule.

Oui, votre jeu m'a transporté, carrément, je vais même le finir, mais vraiment, en traînant les pieds depuis que j'ai rencontré Pythagore, tellement l'histoire a tourné au ridicule.

Comme quoi, foirer un bon scénario, ça peut reposer sur quatre secondes et un "je suis ton père".

Alors voilà, j'ai fini le jeu, et j'ai eu l'ending "câlin en famille et 'tite session de lutte entre Stentor et Alexios".

Je voudrais pourrir le jeu une dernière fois, mais franchement ça me semble compliqué. Une fois passée la souffrance de voir l'Atlantide, on se rend compte qu'il n'est qu'un prétexte à des bossfight captivants et réellement compliqués (Méduse et le Minotaure, franchement, que du bonheur) et nous emmène dans des lieux dont le level-design est au top. Vraiment, voir les ruines de Minos, de Mycennes, et des toutes ces civilisations extraordinaires qui ont précédé les âges sombres (je parle de la période historique), d'en côtoyer des représentations, même si elle relèvent de l'interprétation la plus subjective, ça n'a pas de prix. 

Lisez des articles sur Mycennes et Minos, cultivez-vous et apprenez du peu que nous savons de ces artisans extraordinaires, Odyssey vous y encourage et rien que pour ça j'applaudis des deux mains. 

Au-delà de ça, une fois que vous avez zigouillé tous les planqués en masque, le jeu s'essouffle un peu. Heureusement qu'on peut se taper une bonne grosse baston de conquête de temps à autres, ou qu'on peut flinguer un mercenaire à droite ou à gauche, se faire les poches en pillant le trésor public (le rêve chers amis...)... 

La fin est la conséquence directe de toutes vos décisions dès le chapitre 7 voire bien avant, alors gare aux dialogues passés trop vite !

Venons-en maintenant aux dlc. 
Ouai, je sais, j'suis un vendu, j'ai raqué 100 balles en précommande pour avoir le season pass. Mais regardez le compteur: 200h de jeu et j'y reviens quasiment tous les jours en ce moment alors que j'ai fini le jeu. Vous expliquez ça comment, les râleurs ? 

Même sans aucune quête à suivre et la carte complètement explorée, le jeu est tellement immersif qu'on se prend à revenir dessus pour faire un contrat par-ci par-là, se balader en mer pour traquer des navires légendaires et piquer leurs skins pour repeindre l'adrestia avec des couleurs toujours plus improbables...

Et les Lost Tales of Ancient Greece, sortant régulièrement, sont plus que sympa, même si un peu brefs. 

(Avertissement : pour une raison que j'ignore, steam sensure le mot Perse ou perse, c'est pourquoi je mettrai un espace entre le P et le e. Très franchement j'ignore pourquoi on n'a pas le droit de parler d'un empire antique dans une critique de jeu, à croire que ça doit vexer des gens de les remettre sur le tapis. Qu'un modérateur m'explique pourquoi s'il vous plaît, je ne vois pas en quoi "perse" est un mot grossier, en tout cas pas en français.)

Pour ce qui est de Legacy of the First Blade, on n'a pour l'instant eu droit qu'au premier épisode, et à défaut de rajouter un peu de map à explorer, met l'eau à la bouche avec une nouvelle histoire plutôt sympa, mettant l'accent sur le lien étrange entre Grèce et P erse dans l'antiquité, et ce à la période Classique, qui je le rappelle a démarré en 480 av J.-C. avec la défaite des forces d'invasion P erses sur le Péloponnèse, et prendra fin à la mort d'Alexandre le Grand en 323 av. J.-C., lorsqu'il aura conquis l'intégralité de l'empire P erse. Entre ces deux dates, Grèce et P erse entretenaient des relations tantôt cordiales et commerciales, tantôt hostiles, mais les flux de population et les flux culturels entre les deux nations étaient extrêmement importants. Ce point est très bien mis en avant par Odyssey et son premier dlc, qui sort au compte-goutte, est très prometteur, mais espérons qu'il ne s'arrêtera pas à de simples promesses. 

Bilan des courses : le jeu en lui-même sans Legacy of the First Blade vaut très largement 100 balles, et oui les amis, c'est un fait, on ne peut pas dire le contraire. Le contenu qu'il propose est simplement stratosphérique, et surpasse tous les AC sortis jusque-là. Je ne parle pas du scénario mais bien du contenu. Il vous occupera au moins 100h en mode cauchemar, et ne cessera de vous occuper si comme moi vous vous plaisez à faire le lien entre archives historiques et interprétation vidéoludique. 

Malgré un raté appelé Atlantide qui fait comme une grosse tache de matière fécale sur une page de roman, il suffit de tourner la page et on s'aperçoit qu'on ne s'est pas fait voler et que le reste du roman est une véritable pépite. Que voulez-vous, quand on savoure un bouquin, on ne peut pas empêcher un pigeon de passer au-dessus et de lâcher un étron, la nature et les lois de la statistique sont ainsi faites.

Jouez-y, rejouez-y, il est excellent.

Ah Battlegrounds.  You are a tempting lady to say the least.  I love to love you and I love to hate you.  Well, hate your maker, rather. 

PUBG as a game is really fun in my humble opinion.  Sure it has it's share of bugs (some that are getting more annoying by the day), but all in all, it's a great experience with friends.

The Good:
* Overall game play is addicting
* Variety of situations you can and will find yourself in are never ending
* The pacing of the game is really good for those of us that enjoy both intense and laid back gameplay
* Gun play is really fun and very satisfying when you get a kill
* New content (maps and loot) are only getting better as the game matures
* Cheaters were rampant.  Nearly every game I played I saw or was killed by one.  However, PUBG Corp's initiative to diminish their impact seems to be working as I rarely encounter one these days.

The Bad:
* Bluehole / PUBG Corp. are now starting to treat this game as a cash grab and it's really starting to show.  They are fixing bugs, which is nice, but they are creating more annoying bugs in the process.
* Lag is getting worse.  It cancels jumps, teleports you meters away from where you thought you were and kills you after you've been behind cover for even as much as a second or two.
* Can not connect to lobby without several retries
* Not being able to see all your friends on the in-game friends/team UI is really annoying
* Did I mention this game is turning into a cash grab?
* Updates are rolled out during North America prime time of play and with very little warning.  This shuts down the servers for 3 - 4 hours and no play is possible.  They offer regional servers so why not roll out the update regionally during each regions lowest activity time?  Software Deployment 101.
* With the exception of the newest map, Sanhok, testing of patches is barely given adequate time before rolled out to the production servers.  Sometimes only a day on the test servers before moved to production.  As a software engineer, this is bothersome.  Especially for a user-base as large as PUBG has.
* Speaking of Sanhok and testing: PUBG stated several times that they are going to be spending lots of time and testing cycles on it so it is as perfect as possible.  And for the most part, they have succeeded.  It's is a well designed and beautiful map.  My favorite experience yet.  HOWEVER, there are very obvious cosmetic flaws in the form of floating assets all over.  If this is PUBG Corp's idea of perfect, then I'm not surprised the game and company are in the states they are.
* They are working on optimizing the game, but still a long way from it.  I receive FPS drops frequently on my mid-range rig.  I don't expect to achieve a steady 144 FPS the entire time, but going from 110 FPS to 45 FPS just by looking a different direction is jarring and limits my ability to win a fire fight

Conclusion:
This game is really fun if you can take it light heartedly and enjoy it for what it is.  It is no where near a Triple-A title and I suppose it's priced as such, but with how popular it was, and still is, you'd think they would have been able to make it better than it currently is.  All in all, I will say I recommend it because I still have a lot of fun in it, but PUBG Corp is really starting to sour my taste of it.

[h1]充满野心的作品[/h1]
AKA：法国佬的大招

其实早在去年，育碧就放出话来说"2016年没有刺客信条"。理由大概是他们要花更多的时间用心培育打磨下一部作品。并暗示新的AC将是不同于以往巨作。

为了土豆和更好地阅读体验[url=https://cowlevel.net/game/Assassin_s_Creed_Origins/review/2802249]图文版[/url]

如今看来育碧所谓的巨作，果然名副其实。《起源》颠覆了很多旧有设定，并加入了很多新的机制，很多被玩家吐槽的系列祖传老毛病也多数进行了改进。总体而言：尽管与以往的刺客风格基调略有不同，但综合来看这可能是育碧这两年内最完美的作品。


[h1]鲜活的埃及[/h1]
AKA：克丽奥佩特拉的下巴

曾经有个笑话，叫育碧的沙盒。意在吐槽育碧的沙盒游戏无聊没有特色。可能这个笑话传到育碧员工耳朵里，于是他们决定：为了做得更像沙盒，最新的刺客信条里将有大量的沙子。哪的沙子多？非洲！好，新作舞台就选埃及！

于是他们真的做了一个伟大的沙盒...

新的刺客信条地图面积要比以往历代都大上几倍，但是场景细节却没有因此打折扣。好吧，我承认，荒山野岭大沙漠占了地图大多数。但是就算是沙漠，老家希瓦和吉萨的景色也有明显不同。同是绿洲，尼罗河泛滥区和马留提斯湖畔又是两种光景。

当然《刺客信条》系列不同于其他沙盒的地方就在于它对文化的复原。罗马之所以罗马，埃及之所以埃及，可不单单只是盾上画个橄榄鹰，或是垒个土山旁边放个狮子怪那么简单。如果留心观察的话，会发现各类NPC无论埃及或是罗马人，衣装，行为都会因所在地区和身份有所差异，而且细节精致。亚历山大港的希腊化时期建筑和雕塑，衰落到只能在村落和古庙才找的埃及古文字和神祗。以及"刺客"世界观特色的各种（演绎加工过的）名人，或是市井民众在讨论当下时事的只言片语。都在讲述那个时代，正在落败的埃及王朝...

育碧用埃及人最原始也最有效地方法：放好每一块石砖，最终垒砌自己的金字塔。

[h1]游戏机制的改变[/h1]

AKA：尼罗河的战神

(提前说明啊：我可没有黑这游戏的意思啊，你们不要弄个大新闻，给我扣个育碧黑+二代吹的帽子，把我批判一番......)

育碧开发游戏的套路，喜欢把一个作品中的特色，搬到其他系列里重复使用。比如，这部起源里就包括了《荒野》刺杀名单。《看狗》的无人机（鹰），《FH》的打击感，以及鬼知道什么时候就开始（大概是《远哭2》）的据点。以及创新的加入了RPG的装备数值元素。总体来说融合的还不错，就是有点找不到老刺客系列的感觉了。

按照育碧的说法，他们想让狂战玩家和潜入玩家都能找到自己的游戏方式。但是你摸着良心说：就这技能树，单独为战士流列出一个系，和潜入有关的技能加起来也没有5个。

袖剑刺杀的动画也少了不少，藏匿点也简化到只有稻草堆和衣柜，以及.....草丛。在地图设计上确实是有不少帮助"潜行过关"地形。但是到了中后期据点内敌人密度大，想不被发现实在太难了，况且有时需要收集材料必须要正面肛罗马鬼子的武装运输队。而且最重要的是，本作基调上就少了那种作为刺客，神出鬼没的风格，还记得《刺客》初代CG里最后二太爷面对追兵藏到朝圣者人群里的"装完逼还能跑"的画面吗，《起源》里是彻底没了...

(当狂战不好吗？辣么多技能加持，辣么多武器招式，不好吗？不好吗？）

其实也并不是很好。

相比前作，本作确实强调正面肛，出现了轻重攻击，破盾，盾反，闪避，绕背等值得研究的操作。但是和同类游戏比起来手感就弱很多了。战斗的时候动作很笨拙，视角和锁定控制等问题让敌人的正面肛起来也并不是很爽（但总比潜入爽）。

作为本作最大的变化，RPG机制。这个机制在E3上展示之后确实让人眼前一亮。但是实际玩起来却没多大存在感。所有人物有各自的等级，装备也有各自的属性和稀有度，连地图和任务都按照等级区间做了划分。可是，（也可能是我个人对RPG游戏要求太高），《起源》里的RPG元素实在禁不起推敲。一个可玩的RPG不只是给人物加个等级和攻击力数值那么简单，还需要各类属性选择或是技能组合起来的BUILD，显然《起源》里没有。


（那至少玩可以刷武器啊，有人就喜欢刷刷刷）

也不行...游戏中所有武器都可以升级，随着游戏的进行，可以直接找铁匠把低等级的武器升级到符合当前难度的状态，也就是说一把橙武你可以用到游戏结束。因为它们属相要全面高于同等级紫装和蓝装，于是多样的装备也就失去了意义。

总体来说RPG机制实在是太过鸡肋，只有通过等级限制玩家流程和活动区域的作用。或许是鼓励玩家做支线任务的手段，因为等级的存在，玩家必须要完成支线任务获取经验升级才能跟上主线任务的等级要求。

好在，本作中可探索元素和支线任务比前作有趣....了那么一丁点。如果你喜欢研究历史的话，可能会看到这些任务背后的历史背景。但我想大多数人都不是，那么这些任务就像历代前作一样，不过是去A杀X人，然后偷走B交给C。

[h1]画质和摄影模式[/h1]
AKA：非洲的记者

我也不太想浪费口舌夸3A游戏的画面。（画面都够搞不好还做什么3A？）

我只是想说：摄影模式，它太棒了。我把我自觉还不错的照片放在后面了...

[h1]内购，内购，GO[/h1]

AKA：商人的贪婪

是的，这游戏有内购。是的，它不影响游戏流程。

有人在意这个，单独提一下。游戏中确实提供了了内购来解锁皮肤，橙武和游戏币...事实上正常流程下玩家是不需要内购项目的帮助。只是偶尔做做支线任务和偶尔刷刷素材足以保证游戏流程顺畅，普通或者是紫色装备对难度影响也不会太大，况且他们升级费还便宜。也不会有人非酋到一整个流程下来一个橙武都不爆（哎？埃及就在非洲...嗯）。所以就一周目来说，如果你没有收集强迫症的话，有没有内购完全是无所谓的。可能二周目懒得刷素材的时候会用得到吧...不过那都是后话了...

当然了，我确实担心日后育碧更新个多人模式什么的来勾引你预购，毕竟已经有开箱子和"世仇任务"了,《狗2》里也确实见过了无缝联机的玩法....但愿只是杞人忧天。

[h1]TL；DR[/h1]
AKA：太长不看

++生动的世界
+优秀的画面
+摄影模式
=差强人意的变革，喜忧参半
-没太大进步的任务

[b]总结[/b]：作为系列变革的一作，《起源》在游戏风格和机制上的变化可能会引起老玩家不适。而且其变化的内容虽然很难说是成功，但也处在合理范围内。但是育碧一如既往认真塑造的世界着实为游戏增色不少

3.个人认为盾是个没用的东西
4.技能还是带冰冻弹和闪光弹双控比较靠谱
5.前期卷轴力量为主，如果对操作没信心的话可以点几级生命
6.前期细胞升级推荐血瓶>远程（个人是先点的初始远程武器随机）>金币收集
7.中毒和流血的伤害是可以叠加的而且很高
8.饰品减伤其实没多大用，一般死亡都是被无限连击致死
9.在墓地关卡有一个特别恶心的怪可以让其他怪隐身，注意看水花
10.BOSS用远程慢慢磨死是要磨一年的，但是最稳。（第一个只打一次获得藤蔓符文的BOSS除外，堡垒后面（貌似是黑桥来着）的BOSS注意跳跳跳）
11.不要作死去什么下水道，你会遇见手残的噩梦
12.（敲敲敲）知识点来了！前两关的出生点左边是各有一个图纸（不是下水道），地图名我忘了反正就是正常路线。按这情况来说应该每个地图都会有一个图纸（我猜的），目前只找到这两个，没有任何需求就可以拿的（如果你手残二段跳都上不去我也没辙），其他如果有找到的欢迎补充~
13.如果为了通关就不要着急赶时间房间（本人是个手残，每次冲过去就差几秒钟或是死于不知名AOE，就从来没赶上过，所以不知道里面有啥，新手不推荐打这么快，不如熟悉一下操作和武器）

以上！

小贴士补充：
14.如果身上带着一堆图纸只想活着过关的话推荐箭塔+磁雷配合无伤慢慢打通关，注意这个配合最好不要惹精英怪，碰到跑的快打的快的精英怪就绝对没救了，原因参考下一条。
15.精英怪属性大致为减少攻击前摇（增加攻击速度），增加移动速度，血厚。半血后进入狂暴状态会瞬移到玩家附近。
