They say war never changes but that universal truth does not apply to Total War. The series has the well-known core gameplay of a campaign map and isometric army clashes. This has changed relatively little over the years, but it has evolved considerably. I found the series in the Medieval times and remained a dedicated fan up to Shogun 2. With Attila and Rome 2 I felt the long-standing flaws, franchise fatigue and general DLC policy had finally ended the war for me. Sometimes it is good to be wrong: the matrimony of the two titans in the game title is a blessed one indeed.

On the surface things are the same as before: you still recruit a general and a stack of 20 units for him and build up your cities to climb the tech tree and pay for the proceedings. The surface is where all old familiarity ends, however. All the core systems have been changed, but not for the sake of changing, as often happens in old, succesful series. Take agents, for example. In Empire you would stack them in universities and forget them there. Now you can build them for campaign map support or helping your Lord in combat and give them followers and magic items familiar from the table-top. This familiar RPG system feels so fresh here, I hope Total War will never let go of it. The spirit of carefully weighed innovation is present in all things. Your provinces are made up of a capital citadel and 1-3 settlements and building them into a web of benefits is challenging, rewarding and above all fun. With Total War: Warhammer, you get to feel like a true head of state, making plans for a payoff as in nowhere else.

With many other Total Wars, Empire in particular, the AI had great difficulties in building intelligent armies and leading them into battle. No more. The Great Powers can put up a good fight on Normal and become true headaches on Very Hard and Legendary. The battles with piling corpses look fantastic, as usual, but you can feel how the change from history to fantasy has liberated Creative Assembly's collective imaginations. The addition of flying units and sorcerers feels new, but organic, like long-awaited additions. Warhammer Fantasy also has such a deep fount of lore and history to draw from and CA has truly embraced the creation. All the little details feel tasteful and correct, completely in place. The factions above all are what makes TW:W the diamond it is. All of them play unique and feel balanced. Even better than this, the quest systems, Legendar Lords and general feuds mean great opportunity for emergent storytelling. In my Empire game, Volkmar the Grim was tasked with defending the northern coast from Norsca raiders. In his first encounter with Throgg, the Troll King, Volkmar was bested and wounded, his army destroyed. But he staged a comeback, beating back Throgg and Wulfrik again and again, until victory was secure. The game did not have a feud system between Volkmar and the Norsca, it simply emerged in my head and made the troll burning feel like happiness.

The tradition of bugs has ended as well and the wait between turns is remarkably brief. Considering how good the game looks, the lightness feels truly respectable. The DLC policy has often been criticized and for good reason. A fan could pay the retail price again if he wants to try all the factions and this is not respectable. On the other hand, CA has released great free DLCs too and paid ones are worth getting, but minding your budget is a must. Other than that, the perfectly captured Warhammer spirit, seamless technical execution, aerodynamic Total War gaming mechanics and vivid presentation all make Total War: Warhammer an instant classic, one no strategy lover should do without.

Какая-то недоработанная система одевания героя. Теперь как в великом Морровинде можно облачиться в разномастную броню, собранную из over9000 кусочков, но они почти никак не отображаются и сравнение статов сделано очень неудобно. Как будто бы вам нужно было одеться в абсолютно тёмной комнате, ища всю одёжку наощупь.

Система прокачки. Это просто ночной кошмар любого любителя RPG в целом и Фолла в частности. Ты Особенный!(S.P.E.C.I.A.L.) Правда, видимо в понимании разработчиков это стало значить что-то вроде "Альтернативно одарённого", так как это просто издевательство. Любой пункт Спешл теперь можно прокачать с помощью скилл поинта, как обычный навык. Вместо навыков теперь сраный постер, который можно крутить туда-сюда и как слабоумный отмечать крестиком 1-2 полезных навыка из 10 представленных в каждой ветке(это не описать словами, загуглите как теперь стала выглядеть система перков). И да, теперь Харизма вообще не упёрлась, потому что единственное её назачение - доп.лайн в диалоге, который можно с помощью комбинации save/load активировать даже с 1 ХАР. Зато ИНТ теперь даёт ничего кроме очков опыта за каждое действие, и как по мне, немного читерный, ибо с ним за любой локпик получаешь очень много экспы. Короче, похерили ролевую систему, изнасиловали её, повесили, сожгли труп и помочились на могилу.

Крафт оружия. Вот тут конечно было видно желание сделать как лучше, но получилось как обычно. Куча всяких апгрейдов, которые теперь отображаются в названии оружия(??) и из-за обилия лёгких тактических штыковых шоковых гладкоствольных пистолетов, которые один хрен выглядят как кусок ржавого говна ориентироваться в неудобном соснольном интерфейсе стало абсолютно невозможно.

Диалоги.
[Да] Они полностью озвучены, включая речь ГГ.
[Нет] Они убогие до невозможности.
[Не понял?] Если что, а сейчас наглядно объясняю систему асболютно ЛЮБОГО диалога в игре.
[Сарказм] Лучше разговорное RPG ever!

Карта. Это скорее не карта, а полигон для игры в пейнтбол. Потому что на ней дохрена всякого мусора, который никак не задействован и полтора значимых места, в которых есть что-то кроме ссаных рейдеров и гулей.

Кстати о врагах. Они тут все как Флэши, объёбанные спидами и героином, потому что по ним нельзя как нормально попасть, так и убить. На личном примере: стрелял обычному человеку в фетровой шляпе в голову из снайперки. Убил с 4 патрона... WTF?!
Система VATS теперь абсолютно бесполезна. Нынче время лишь замедляется, но в виду вышеозначеннвых фактов это помогает примерно никак.

Все задания в игре теперь сводятся к "Убей Х рейдеров/гулей и иди нахуй". 

Короче, подведём итоги:
Игра красивая, но пустая. Простая, но в итоге абсолютно убогая. Хотели сделать что-то новое, но абсолютно забыли о старом. 
Знаете, она как Fallout: Tactics. Вроде бы и Фолл, вроде бы и норм, но по факту- абсолютно чужая и лишняя в этой вселенной игра.

И не взять уже ружья и верного пса в долгую дорогу, заканчивающуюся на горизонте мира.
А так хотелось...

Pros
1. Huge learning curve (Paradox games are renowned for incredible depth to every game's mechanics.)

5. Extensive community providing guides, mods, multiplayers game.
6. It feels like the 2020 version of Axis and Allies.

Cons
1. A never ending game means you are bond to dislike some changes, but you can always revert to an older version of the game. Altough it sucks since you then  miss new DLC and tweaks, most mods and guides.

DOOM Eternal is an action packed first person shooter that has you killing demons left and right! It differs from DOOM 2016 when it comes to difficulty. You need to be more tactical in this game. For example, you can't just spray and pray. If you do this you will die. Instead you should prioritize each enemy and know what their weaknesses are (which all of them have). The only gripe I have is the ammo issue. You simply run out of ammo too fast. You can use the chainsaw to get more ammo but this happens way too often to be a fun game mechanic. The plus side to this is that you are going to be using your abilities all the time compared to DOOM 2016 where you can just beat the game with the shotgun.

Apart from that, the secrets in this game are a blast to discover and the rewards you get for finding them make it worth it to do a second play through of the game.

As of now, I am still stuck on the last level because it is really hard for me but I will finish it at some point.

All in all, the game does not take itself too seriously at some points but all around it is a great game and a worthy followup of DOOM 2016.

This is a really fun game to play with friends. What sets PUBG apart from other battle royale's is the strategy. You are to use your weapons, equipment and environment to get an advantage over your opponent. I recommend playing with friends since that makes the game more tactical, and the tactics are what make me want to play PUBG over something like Day Z, Fortnite, Apex Legends, Blackout, or Warzone. This game also includes a variety of maps to choose from, ranging from small maps to big maps. I wish there was more gun variety as it seems I rarely ever use anything different. You should be able to run this game on low settings if your PC is not that powerful, although I don't recommend playing this game with a slow computer as you may experience frame drops pretty much every time you fire your weapon and loading times are annoying. I will sometimes tab out of my game to talk on Discord while I wait for the game to load, but I'm pretty sure the game either takes longer to load or won't load at all if you're not tabbed in. Sometimes I will be on Miramar and I haven't loaded in, so the plane automatically kicks me out and I will parachute all the way to the bottom. I was alive for around five minutes until a guy came and shot and downed me. As soon as I got down the game decided to load me in. I also don't really like Kraken that much because of the small size. I guess it works for people who want a quickie, but there's no option to take it out of the search or search exclusively for it. The zone sometimes moves too fast and is fairly small for the first phase. However, as I played the game more it is less annoying because vehicles compensate for it. Overall, I give this game 8/10.

Darkest Dungeon от Red Hook Studios зарекомендовала себя как один из лучших представителей жанра crpg, с элементами rogue-like, за последние несколько лет и в приведенном ниже обзоре я поясню, почему же я так считаю.

Данный симулятор нежданных критов и неочевидных промахов предлагает игроку погрузиться в атмосферу отчаяния и ужаса, взяв под свое командование четверых авантюристов, которых вы можете отбирать на свое усмотрение, ведь игра предлагает вам 14 классов, а это, в свою очередь, дает огромный простор для комбинаций, тактики ведения боя и делает каждый забег по подземельям уникальным. Говоря о подземельях в Darkest Dungeon, следует упомянуть о такой важной, и довольно популярной в современных играх, детали, как процедурная генерация мира, добавляющая игре элемент неожиданности и держащая игрока в постоянном страхе перед каждой новой «комнатой», а страх смерти одного или всех членов команды — это именно то, что будет преследовать вас на протяжении всей игры и неминуемо настигать, особенно учитывая здешний рандом во время боя. Битвы проходят в пошаговой форме (подобно той, что присутствует в жанрах jrpg), где очередность ходов будет зависеть от показателя SPD, который может постоянно изменяться, особенно если у вас в команде есть Jester.

Атмосферу разработчики задали как надо, начиная от закадрового голоса, дающего вам надежду, либо отнимая последние частицы оной, до гротескно нарисованных персонажей, монстров, подземелий и саундтрека под авторством Стюарта Чатвуда, который прекрасно вписывается в игру и задает нужный темп.

В игре присутствуют приятные отсылки к творчеству Лавкрафта. Взять, к примеру, самую явную – локация «Бухта(Cove)» монстры в которой, будто сошли со страниц рассказов «Тень над Иннсмутом» и «Дагон». Присутствует, ко всему прочему, вероятно косвенная отсылка — оккультист, большинство его умений имеют вид щупалец (излюбленная или даже неотъемлемая часть монстров у Лавкрафта), и в названии присутствуют такие слова как «Abyssal/глубинный», «Abyss/Бездна» и «Unspeakable Commune/Тайный разговор». Подобные наименования являются излюбленным приемом описания у Лавкрафта, когда речь идет об обители тех или иных чудовищ или связи человека с древними существами. Но самое главное, как я думаю, это сам персонаж оккультиста – араб, который вполне может быть отсылкой к вымышленному персонажу Абдулу Альхазреду, создателю некрономикона (вымышленная книга во вселенной Мифов Ктулху). Также следует упомянуть систему «стресса» у персонажей, аналогичная система, но не в таком, конечно же, виде, присутствует практически во всех играх, которые так или иначе опираются на мифологию Лавкрафта.

Из недостатков можно отметить одно: рандом. Это, на мой взгляд, единственное, что может подпортить впечатление от игры, так как порой промахи с вашей стороны могут длиться 3 раунда подряд, в то время как ваши враги будут прописывать вам криты, но это так – единичные случаи и придирки.

Что мы имеем в итоге: замечательную игру на десятки часов, способную удержать игрока своей атмосферой и не отпускать до самой последней вылазки наших отважных и немного безумных героев.

Capolavoro! Il miglior acquisto del 2019. La versione Black Mesa di Half Life non è un semplice remaster, poichè i capitoli, seppur fedeli alla versione del 1999, sono stati ricostruiti in maniera precisa e accurata, senza lasciare nessun dettaglio al caso. Alcune parti del vecchio Half Life sono state snellite e rese decisamente più interessanti, come il capitolo "Su un binario", che nella vecchia versione era piuttosto noioso.

Ma il vero capolavoro è stato fatto col tanto atteso macrocapitolo di Xen. Essendo stato introdotto successivamente rispetto al resto della storia, si notano un lavoro e una grafica davvero sbalorditive. Il pianeta stesso è stato ricostruito da zero: gli ambienti sono completamenti diversi dalla versione del '99 che, pur mantenendo alcuni riferimenti, rendono l'avventura tutta da scoprire come fosse la prima volta. La ricostruzione di Xen, inoltre, ha contribuito (a mio parere) e rendere più chiara la storia e il legame con Half Life 2. Un esempio? Su HL2 non si capiva come mai i Vortigaunt fossero diventati improvvisamente buoni e collaborativi, cosa che si capisce con HL Black Mesa. 

Tocco di classe che accompagna tutto il gioco, l'ambientazione resa decisamente più horror, la quale ha reso nuovamente magico una storia che ha 20 anni.

I have very mixed feelings about this game.
The campaign was decent, and I enjoyed going through it.

The multiplayer... is something. I often find myself getting killed in situations you'd expect to have an advantage in. Like shooting a guy in the face with a rocket, twice, only to get turned on and one-shot by a shotgun despite having full health and substantial armor.

A sniper that requires a charge to do high damage, but then some guy with a gauss cannon one-shots you with no delay despite you having gotten a plain-as-day headshot on them, only to realize it did a whole 40 damage due to a low charge. And the heavy machine gun! In the campaign, it was awesome! Nice accuracy and power! But in multiplayer, you'd probably get more damage out of throwing it at a player instead of shooting it.

I feel for powerups, demon runes, etc, that the losing team should get first view of it. What fairness is it that a crushing team gets to see it at the same time and can much more easily get ahold of it? Especially if it's quad damage or the demon possession.

I do have fun with the multiplayer, don't get me wrong. But I feel like there are plenty of things that need balanced. But hey, maybe I just need to drink an 8 ounce glass of Git Gud first.

Pour un mélange de plateformes, d'infiltration, de survie et de petites énigmes, Little Nightmares est une de ces petites perles originales se démarquant des standards et plongeant le joueur d'emblée dans une ambiance sombre et collant parfaitement à un univers cauchemardesque enfantin, parfois malsain. Avec pour seul outil, un briquet, les environnements devront toujours être utilisés à bon escient pour échapper aux assaillants. Dans cette aventure, personne ou presque n'est votre ami et le personnage incarné devra parfois faire des choix de survie cruels.
Une patte graphique plus qu'enchanteresse et des musiques doucement angoissantes maintiennent le rythme de votre fuite avec brio sans jamais le casser net, tant le chemin est facile à trouver, sans jamais tout à fait se montrer.
Il sera parfois nécessaire de répéter quelques scènes pour en saisir le déroulement et observer les patterns des antagonistes qui, une fois qu'ils vous auront repérés, vous fonceront dessus sans vous lacher jusqu'à ce que vous trouviez une issue ou cachette, que ce soit au sol, ou en hauteur.
D'une patte Burtonesque ou bien tout droit sortis du pays des merveilles, les univers sont étranges, dérangés et mystérieux mais jamais ennuyeux.
Le voyage est une petite surprise bien agréable dont on regrettera seulement sa durée franchement courte.

[b] Alright, I am aware of how many good things have been said about the game, another positive review might be pointless. I am here just to point out some things that are rarely said and to let off steam from playing this game. I am going to divide the review in parts that I wanted to point out so that it's more digestible. [/b]

[b] [u] MAIN STORY [/u] [/b]
This game's story is prett-ty dark. Like I'll gladly categorize this as a dark fantasy rpg kind of story. You often don't quite expect the outcome of certain actions that is often done in other games, and I'll have to say it's somewhat [b] realistic [/b] because the outcome is probably what would happen if said scenario were to happen in the real world, and as a [i] witcher [/i] (oversimplified, a monster bounty hunter) you'll come across A LOT of grim situations. Lemme give you an example: [spoiler] "You were tasked to get back a certain person loved ones that have been gone for 2 days in the woods." In the real world you'd might expect the worst already but this is a game right? haha surely they'll be alive... NO. 90% of these encounters the realistic thing happened, the loved ones dead and the quest giver will begin their 5 stages of grief right in front of you before you received your payment in which it would be very awkward to ask. [/spoiler] 
Don't worry though, there are quite a few of happy moments, it's not a completely dark story after all, and these moments don't last forever, so you'll be sure to cherish these!
Oh, I also want to give a new player a tip in making decision, be carefree. You might never expect what would happen y'know :)

[b] [u] GAME ACCESSIBILITY [/u] [/b]
This is a big point that haven't been said enough to a player wanting to pick up this game.

If you're an [b] outsider of The Witcher franchise [/b], you might be asking, "is it okay to just jump into The Witcher 3 without ever knowing the previous games and books?", the answer is a YES. It's okay to just play this game, although, as expected, you might be confused in the early hours of the game. Don't worry though, you got a Character Book (default key: G.) that'll tell you what there is to know about the character to fully enjoy the game, after some reading you won't feel quite left out anymore when the characters are talking. Besides that, there are YouTube videos online that'll cover The Witcher lore, but beware, as for this game is quite spoiler heavy, meaning there's a lot of story points that can be spoiled and it can happen easily.

Now, in my opinion, the biggest barrier that made me cannot recommend this to everyone is the [b] language barrier. [/b] This game, I think, uses a lot of Old English phrases that can be quite hard to understand for the Modern English speaking folk. I personally HAVE to play it with Google Translate in the Steam Overlay just to understand what're these [i] ploughing [/i] phrases mean! Although I am not a native English speaker, so that may be a factor in my difficulty. If your native tongue is lucky enough available as a subtitle, you can go ahead not do that translating deed. But, at the other end, this game can be quite a source to understand plenty heavy, majestic, master looking words, like [i] colloquially, frippery, [/i] and others that you can use in the internet to virtually raise your social status!

Game difficulty's fine... you can change it in the middle of a playthrough, so don't worry about that. You can look up others take on difficulty if you're still curious.

[b] [u] THE BUGSSSSSSSSSSSS [/u] [/b]
Oh god, the bugs. How the hell did people not see Cyberbug 2077 coming?! This game, after 5 years and more, IS STILL riddled with bugs. Mind you, it's not game breaking bugs that you can see in Cyberbug, but still, I'd say the amount of it is similar to recent Assassin's Creed games! You got the input bug, such as not being able to attack in the middle of a fight, not being able to sprint horses, alt+tab sometimes doesn't work, to graphical bugs, such as texture pop in (quite rare), hair and tree flailing around in cutscenes at an unrealistic rate, and lots, lots of clipping the latter of which can be fixed with mods thankfully (gonna talk more about this). The solution of most of these bugs are just reloading your saves (enabling autosave is a must for this reason) which can take variably depending on your system, if you got HDD, well, you're in for a long time of waiting.

[b] [u] MODDING DIFFICULTY [/u] [/b]
Alright this will be my last point, won't bore you too long with reading, the modding in this game is pretty accessible, not as much as to say, Skyrim, but still pretty friendly nonetheless. After 2 hours of straight reading (i think? i dunno i was immersed in modding) of multiple instructions on how to mod the game, I already got the gist of it and pretty much able to troubleshoot any mod installed. Why? well I'd love to kinda roleplay and do my own thing, wheras I would be very much attacked by anyone on the street, I just wanted to make friends, man! but I guarrantee you if you go up to 5 people and honk your horn, atleast 1 will shoot you, take your car and give you the finger... pretty rude, huh?

[b]Assassin's Creed Origins[/b] as the name suggest aims to show the beginning of the Assassin's Brotherhood, over a thousand years prior to Altaïr.
In this game you play as Bayek, an Egyptian Medjay who is on a personal quest for revenge. As a Medjay (a protector of the people) he also encounters a lot of people in need whom he feels is his duty to protect and aid.
During the game you'll visit famous landmarks in the BCE Egypt such as the Sphinx, the great pyramids of Giza, Alexandria, Memphis and etc, you'll also meet important historical characters such as Cleopatra, Julius Caesar and others, as is custom in the AC series.
The game was beautifully designed and the Egypt was amazingly well recreated by Ubisoft using many resources, even NASA satellite images.

The game is demanding, my computer doesn't max it, but that was expected, I can still play decently on high settings.
A lot of people and websites are claiming the game to be having performance issues because of Ubisoft's decision to include up to 4 layers of DRM protection in the game. Unfortunately due to my computer not meeting the requirements to max the game graphics I cannot test that by myself, but there's a lot of evidence online suggesting that the claims may be true.

Now I'll list some pros and cons, keep in mind these are my personal opinions and they may and certainly will differ from other players.

[b]Pros:[/b]

- Beautiful graphics
- Ancient Egypt (I've been crazy for the mysterious land of Egypt since I was a little kid, so playing one of my favorite series on Egypt is a huge plus for me)
- Great characters (especially Bayek, he's a fantastic character)
- Historical locations and characters wonderfully added to Ubisoft's fictional setting
- A lot of stuff to do beside the main content
- Free DLC to be added by Ubisoft next year

[b]Cons:[/b]

- 4 layers of DRM protection (3 if you do not purchase on Steam)
- Bugs (they're slowly being worked on though)
- Extremely high CPU usage even on 8+cores CPUS
- Not very well optimized (but still playable)
- While the game and map feels huge, a good part of it is actually empty desert (that was expected really)

As you can probably see I had to stretch on the cons a bit so people can't say I only listed positive things, that is because for me the game is fantastic and I am loving every minute I am expending on it.
I completely recommend buying it if you the like series or the historical elements it has to offer.

C est Ubisoft, c est un AAA, c est Assassin's Creed
Plus, Uplay, Denuvo, micro transactions, nécessite un bon PC (en bon ordre de marche...)

Tout pour déclencher la haine...

Et pourtant …
Le jeu est réellement bon


C est un jeu de type aventure / RPG léger, oriente action
Un peu comme The Witcher 3 (mais beaucoup moins RPG, plus action), qui se déroule en Grèce antique, en pleine guerre, le tout sur une carte immense

Assez peu connecte aux anciens AC, un moins pour les fans, un gros plus pour les nouveaux venus
Vous pouvez commencer par celui la si la franchise AC ne vous intéresse pas vraiment et que vous voulez juste un action RPG / open world se déroulant en Grèce (mon cas...)


Vous incarner un mercenaire en plein milieu de la guerre Athènes / Sparte
En tant que mercenaire, vous allez aider et combattre les 2 camps
N espérer pas vous allier avec un des adversaires, c est impossible dans le jeu

Homme ou femme au choix (j’ai joue Kassandra)
Des NPCs historiques et charismatiques

Le jeu est beau et le monde est vaste, très vaste, avec pas mal d eau et une bonne composante navale

Open world, vous pouvez aller ou vous voulez...si vous avez le level

Le gameplay est bon, nerveux, rapide et fluide, avec de nombreuses manières d aborder les situations, mêlée, distance, furtif, mixte
Plus, du parkour, mais facile

La partie navale est bien sympa

Quelques composantes RPG, des quêtes plutôt sympa et bien écrites, un peu d humour, quelques choix (pas trop…), stats, levelling...mais ça reste un jeu d action et d aventure avant tout

Concernant les quetes, ne pas se focaliser sur les répétables évidemment….
Celles ci sont très peu intéressantes...et infinies

Des romances...plutôt bof pour tout dire, et toutes bi-neutre
Tout NPC romancable sera OK pour y aller avec le joueur, peu importe son sexe

Le Grèce est plutôt bien retranscrite
Attention, ce n est pas une simulation historique et des concessions on été faite pour le gameplay (pas de boucliers pour le joueur par exemple) ou pour le 'politiquement correct' (quelques femmes warriors, ça en fait rager certains…)
Dans l ensemble, ça reste néanmoins cohérent

Le jeu est long, une bonne soixantaine d heures pour finir, 200-300 pour tout retourner
N espérer pas rusher et finir en 15 heures…

Difficulté correcte avec 4 niveaux, peut être trop facile en end game, même en Nightmare

Level scaling
Marche très bien, mais certains n aiment pas ça

Jouable clavier / souris sans problème (souris gamer avec beaucoup de boutons…)

Tout en vocal et en français

Micro transactions totalement optionnelles, essentiellement des skins, que l on peut gagner en jeu eventuellement
J ai tout fait dans le jeu, en difficulté max, pas une seconde je me suis dis que j avais besoin de quelque chose du magasin

Aucun gros bug pour moi , jeu stable
Attention encore, il nécessite un bon PC...et en bon ordre de marche

Quelques bugs ennuyeux, corriges au fur et a mesure
Jeu suivi par Ubisoft, avec patches et correctifs

Des DLCs a prévoir...

I still keep firing it up every few months because random stuff just keeps being fun, interesting, and memorable. Kiedy już wszystko działa okazuje się, że jest niedobór prądu, a do elektrowni atomowej jeszcze daleko, rzucasz się z misją samobójczą na osadę biter'ów (kąsaczy).

[h1]CZYLI O CO TAK NAPRAWDĘ CHODZI[/h1]
Generalnie chodzi o to, że wszystkiego jest za mało, a fabryka musi się powiększać więc tworzymy więcej kopalń, hut i rafinerii aby niczego nie brakowało, a jak jest trochę więcej niż mało to fabryki robią fabryki, które tworzą wszystko, co nam potrzeba. Dzięki temu mamy bez przerwy jakieś zajęcie i gra nam się nie nudzi, ale jak satysfakcjonuje. Moment, w którym droidy wykańczają nową hutę lub fabrykę i wszystko pięknie działa (do czasu). Można znaleźć kilka sekund na popatrzenie jak wszystko się rusza i produkuje. Tylko, że to za mało. Patrzymy na produkcję. Ładna wszystko idzie, ale wciąż mało. I budujemy więcej tworzymy nowe produkty lub powielamy stare projekty, aż w pewnym momencie nie jesteśmy zapamiętać układu całej bazy na pamięć.

Podsumowując gra jest jednym wielkim "city build'erem" z dużą ilością grind'u (budowa wszystkiego), w której  staramy się osiągnąć pełną automatyzację, gdzie my, malutki człowieczek wszystkim zarządza. To kłamstwo, że mamy uciec rakietą z tej planety, nie wierzcie twórcą.

[h1]GRAFIKA I DŹWIĘK[/h1]
Grafika i animacje są proste, ale ładne. Cieszy oko bardziej to, że wszystko się rusza niż to, w jaki sposób wykonucje ruch, czy jak wygląda obiekt, który wykonuje daną czynność. Dźwięk jest bardzo dobry. Podchodzisz do rafinerii, słyszysz jak ropa płynie. Podchodzisz do hut, słyszysz jak wszystko się przetapia, a podajniki wszystko wykładają na taśmę. Drony lecą do Ciebie z item'ami albo wydajesz im polecania i przyglądasz się im, wydają słodki robotyczny pisk, a przynajmniej ja tak uważam. W skrócie, dźwięk jest zrobiony perfekcyjnie.

[h1]OPTYMALIZACJA[/h1]
Skoro tyle się tworzy, cały czas coś się dzieje, wszystko się oblicza, przetapia, wydobywa, produkuje to bardzo wymagająca musi być ta gra. Otóż nie do końca. Gra jest naprawdę dobrze zoptymalizowana i nawet grając na serwerze częściej spadają klatki z powodu internetu niż przez to, że nasza fabryka zajmuje hektary i ciężko jest to obliczyć. Jednak przy już naprawde dużej fabryce (i nie, nie o takiej, co myślisz, wyobraź to sobie 100 razy większe) to faktycznie im bliżej centrum, czy miejsc, w którym dużo się produkuje mogą spaść klatki, ale na ogół gra chodzi płynnie.

PLUSY:
- wciąga, wciąga i jeszcze raz wciąga
- satysfakcjonuje już od pierwszej zautomatyzowanej fabryki
- chęć "przejścia" gry wiele razy, na różne sposoby
- błędy tylko motywują do poprawy
- grind nie przeszkadza
- przyjemna grafika
- dźwięk jest wszędzie
- optymalizacja (czego brakuje niektórym grą z większym budżetem)

MINUSY:
- ciężka do zrozumienia
- generator map (mała ilość lub brak surowców aby móc dobrze zacząć grę)
- chyba zapomniałem pójść do łóżka od dobrych trzech dni

Certainly a game that warrants a greater audience than the current one it has now. This little gem was sadly overshadowed by Celeste that came only 2 days after the release of this title, so it's understandable how it went a bit under the radar. Aside from this, let me list what I enjoyed about this game.

The visual art style was very enjoyable for me, sure there is a case to be made about the oversaturation of pixel art style games in the indie market, but each title never ceases to amaze me how they can all look so beautiful and can be so different. Games such as this one, hyper light drifter, celeste, and shovel knight are all fantastic examples of the diversity of the pixel style and the jaw dropping visuals they may have despite their simplicity.

The music is top notch, there was not one track I did not enjoy in my entire playthrough, they all had their place and fulfilled their purpose, a few of which amped up the thrill of a scene, generated great suspense, or just really tug at my heart strings. 

The story was quite enjoyable for me, may have been weak at some parts but the other aspects of the game really come into full force to compensate for it. after finishing the game 100%, I just craved for some more about this world the developer created, it has a genuinely interesting premise that I hope is explored more in the future... hopefully not another 8-10 years this time.

Now for the fundamental aspect, the GAMEPLAY. The gameplay reminds me alot more of megaman then it does of a metroid or castlevania game. Sure there may be SOME backtracking, but 90% of it is for collectibles and not for actual progression, still fun to backtrack and find new secret paths with your acquired goodies though. Puzzle solving is very enjoyable, nothing too stellar but it was def a highlight of the game for a few portions. Now for the action and platforming, both of them are top tier for me, the speed, the little mechanics here and there and some of the tweaks you earn really make maneuvering and combat a blast, especially for the boss fights where each and every one is memorable and thrilling! I just crave MORE and a sequel just can't come soon enough, I'd certainly get some DLC if the option was ever given to me.

Do yourself a favor and get this game, you won't regret it!

Провёл в игре более 200 ч, практически, сюжетную линию прошёл. Очень противоречивые впечатления: сюжет и графика без нареканий, боевая система вполне приемлемая, багов много и они раздражают, но при таком объёме они неизбежны. Если бы была какая-то нейтральная оценка, выбрал бы её, но есть только "рекомендую" и "не рекомендую".  Самый главный недостаток: примерно между 15 и 20 уровнем резко снижается интерес к игре. Все эти тупые звери и чудовища, путающиеся под ногами, начинают восприниматься, как спам, за их уничтожение, всё равно, никаких очков не получаешь; потом и однообразные несюжетные задания становятся спамом, за них можно получить от 2-х до 20 очков. Зато после длиннющих сюжетных заунывных видео, на которые никак не влияешь, неожиданно получаешь 500- 1000 очков умений и, как правило, следующий уровень. Охренительно интересно. Обилие образцов оружия и брони совершенно бессмысленно, по причине того, что они привязаны к уровням, и крафтить их, за исключением ведьмачьих сетов, невозможно; доходит до смешного, когда тебе с благоговением передают какой-нибудь "легендарный" клинок или броню, а они годятся только для того, чтобы их продать  по дешевке в ближайшей лавчонке. Битва за Каэр Морхэн - отдельная песня. Чисто для прикола, практически ничего не делал, всё-равно, там сплошные видеовставки, ведущие к решительной победе. Итог: познакомиться с игрой и поиграть какое-то время можно, и даже нужно, но недолго. Желания переигрывать снова и снова, как это было со "Скайримом", не возникает.
    Нужно отметить и положительные моменты, вернее, момент: это гвинт. Действительно, интереснейшая игра в игре, превосходящая по интересу саму игру; выполнил всю линейку заданий, собрал все колоды и получил при этом максимальное удовольствие.
     P.S. Прошёл дополнения "Каменные сердца" и "Кровь и вино" и решил изменить оценку на "рекомендую". Всё-таки, объём работы проведён огромный и над ошибками определённая работа проведена. Несомненно, положительного гораздо больше отдельных огрехов, в целом игра хороша и стоит внимания.

Simply Put Quite The Journey for this game

the game itself from the start is quite ambitious and promised us with many that didnt lived to its hype.The Devs made many mistakes including Features that werent there and a world that is void and feels liveless BUT the game still deserves some support from us the gaming community because although The Devs made a Catastrophic Mistake they did something thats rarely done by the devs these days They still Continue theyre support for this game even after a HUGE Backlash from the Gaming Community and The Media and that is something quite rare for instance im gonna make a Sample Case of the new Mass Effect Andromeda they receive quite the number of Backlash from eveybody and within a Couple of Monthes they stopped theyre support for the game of course this had to do with certain variables such as Economy and Publisher.

Of Course The Game itself is far from perfect and still needs numorous Patches and Constant Updates but its improving little by little here are The Current Pros and Cons of the game with its Current State So Far:

CONS

1) Based on my aproximatelly 10 hours of gametime the game is really Shallow sure its Vast and theres a Gigantic amount of planets and star system to explore but they all felt really simillar for instance i travel to a nearby star system about 65 light years away and grind there travel to another system which is about 100 light years further and i found a very very simillar planet with some incremental changes to the habitats and habitants and this is kinda frustrating Also theres a storyline that feels somewhat less important and not really noticeable its interesting but its not really achieved the goal that its trying to which the goal is trying to gave us a sense of how big the Universe or Multiverse is.

2) Grinding feels really Monotonous sure theres a diffrent type of resources but the game doesnt give you any reward system to compensate this Grinding even though theres a Huge amount of variety of Resources you just basically grinds and buy a new ship equipments and etc with very little pleasing effect for instance the Sample Case im gonna use is RS6 Siege ive played a lot of that game and i can tell you the grinding feels worth it the operators or characters is pretty expensive but with diffrent play style and gunplay it makes you feel refreshed and rewarded and top of that new cosmetics from the character itself such as new guns, looks and etc sure this is two diffrent case but what i wanna point out is if you have to make the player grind so much The Devs should made it Rewarding and Pleasing and this is something that the game in its current state fails to Deliver.

3) Clunky Navigation its still to me a Major Issue of the Game for a game that relies heavily on navigation the navigation system is literally bad the first time ive played this game it literally took me 5 - 10 minutes to figure out how to rotate the star system map and figuring out which button does what in general this broke the immersion 


PROS

1) A Decent Optimization i played it on a budget rig with 3rd gen I3 and a RX470 and encounter no input lag and fps drop ive encountered some stuttering but this is probably caused by my poor cooling solution

2) the Vastness of the game is quite stunning and mesmerizing although this is one of its current weakness but is also one of its strong cards ive found the best ways of playing this game is through only visit a a planet for a brief moment listen to the soundtack while exploring for a small amount of time and grind for a small amount of time and immidietly sets on your way again ive found this to be the best way to counteract the monotonous grind while still Appreciating the scale of the game which is while shallow still really MASSIVE

3) A Decent soundtrack thats fit for the mood if you enjoy a nice walking moody Simulator this is for me one of the recommended the soundtrack itself is pretty decent it creates a suiting mood for the current environment and ive found this entertaining while exploring

4) A Decent Base Building the Base Building itself is pretty basic in its Current State but its got a Great Foundation to build upon just a few updates and patches it will be really Decent 

CONCLUSION

Overall though the game has made a big leap in terms of improvements based on what i heard from the initial reviews and also the fact that The Devs still support it even after a Huge Backlash from eveyone is something to be Credited and Applauded.The only thing i can Recommend you when to buy is when the Price Range is Around 10 - 15 Dollars because at its Current State the Emptiness of the game tends to overshadow its Vast and big Atmospheric Themes.

Bear in mind when a Huge Improvements is introduced i will update this Review

And the balancing is really, REALLY off.  Want to win?  Go Germany, forgo religion, and put everything into science, money, and production.  About the time everyone else is entering the Renaissance era, you're most of the way through the Industrial revolution and rounding the corner for the Modern era.  While I appreciate the irony of no religion equaling a massive science advantage, it kind of throws the game off.
I like some of the concepts here and with some expansions, this game can be saved and brought into the pantheon of the truly great Civilization games.  But for $60 bucks?  Pass until they put it on sale with an expansion release.  At a minimum.

When it comes to Early Access games, there a lot of stigma to it and with good reasons, Quite often, us consumers sometimes feel that the developers are coming with empty promises, unclear directions on developing, or plainly just putting the label Early Access as an attempt to "steal our wallets", but Slay the Spire and the developers, Mega Crit Games, are quite on the other side of the spectrum.

As for the gameplay, I'll keep it simple and quick. There are 3 classes to the game (with more to come), all having diverse playstyles as each character has their own collection of cards to pick. In Daily mode, people are ranked amongst each other to gather the most point and to spice the gameplay, there are multiple modifers that changes the game. In Custom mode, you can freely select any modifiers and try out the endless mode where you'll keep on climbing floors on floors.  

When actually playing the game, it is extremely easy to pick up with short description of what each status does and though the game has RNG, I felt that almost every death was not random and was because of my decision making. The game is fair but also brutally hard and it doesn't get any easier with ascension mode. There is a total of 20 Ascension levels where each ascension, makes the game harder. Harder enemies, heal less, less potion etc.

Overall, I paid this game during the steam sales and with the amount of content and addicting gameplay, this game is well worth the price and is one of the best rogue-like you can buy. Just look at the amount of hours I have.

I got Rust on the tails of watching Hasan Piker's Twitch stream. I figured I'd join the tide of new blood getting farmed by the veterans, but I also figured it wouldn't be as unforgiving as it was memed to be.

As it turns out, the memes were more-or-less true. Rust at its worst is a brutally unforgiving, hope-shattering pit of despair that will absorb valuable hours of your life and mock you for spending them playing the game. Most players will attack you on sight, your base will be harassed constantly and attacked daily, all your resources will be stolen, your gear looted, and your farms stripped of everything like they were attacked by locusts. If you want to put your trust in the goodwill of your fellow players, prepare for disappointment.

But Rust at its best is also incredibly rewarding, in a way that both nullifies and contextualizes the "bad" parts, making them an integral part of the experience. You will beat players in a gunfight, stumble across an advanced rifle at random, execute a good ambush, create a genetically perfect strain of hemp, build a progressively more fortified base, and meet a few people worth running around with. Every time I succeeded in a project I set out for myself, or won an engagement, I felt a visceral sense of accomplishment very few games manage to evoke.

It is that sense of reward, attained through brutal, senseless violence, that makes this game a definite recommend for me.

Overall:

+Game is immensely rewarding.
+Building a base and your equipment is fun and straightforwards. The electrical and hydraulic elements of building are pretty in-depth, surpassing ARK but falling short of Minecraft redstone stuff.
+Progression has a very tangible effect on your playstyle and how you approach engagements.
+Exploration is rewarding, has obvious objects of interests and ties into the other parts of the game well.

+/-Combat is engaging and brutal, but leaves little room for error and can be frustrating. Almost all fights will be determined by positioning. Beware roof campers and people camping your front door.
+/-Socializing with other players is a decisively poor decision about 80% of the time.
+/-It takes a pretty long time to reach the third (the last you can make) tier of items, but it's easy to maintain tier 1 and 2 items and replace them if you die.
+/-Stealth is very important if you're alone, and often the only way.

-Default drop rates are too low. They should be 2 or 3 times higher by default. Communtiy servers with boosted rates are better.
-PvE (i.e. combat against AI animals and humans) is almost laughably bad at times. The human enemies in particular effectively have aimbots, and are annoying as all hell to fight. Fortunately the game is focused on fighting other players.
-The semi-automatic rifle and assault rifle are overbearing in the weapon sandbox and should be given a slight nerf to their effectiveness at range.
-The diversity of biomes is disappointingly limited compared to other games. Temperate, Snowy and Desert. Temperate has rolling plains and some dense forests, Snowy has... snow and hills, and Desert is an American semiarid desert. You might find a swamp sometimes.

The only reason I'm not recommending the game is because I don't think it's worth 1000 dollars. Lets be honest, most people don't have a headset yet, and this game is still not enough reason to spend that kind of money.  

I've let the main story settle for a couple weeks. As well as the gameplay and graphics. And these are my final thoughts. 

Half life: Alyx is the BEST VR game to date. Is it a good game though? Yeah, it is. It's just good though. It's not great or amazing and I think that VR still has a long way to go before really reaching a polished state that really immerses the player. I think people are giving this game way too much credit. Lets start with the worst part.

The pacing is sometimes watered down whenever you hit the same puzzle for the 5th, 6th, 7th and 8th time. This is not what made Half: Life popular. No puzzle was the same in the previous games and it shows here. You were constantly going and whenever you did hit a puzzle in the previous games it was nothing like the ones before. They aren't even puzzles to be honest. More like advancing levels of challenges that bog the pace of the game because you already know the answer to them. This is, without a doubt, the WORST part of the game. Out of the 10 hours of the game, they take up, at the very least 2 hours. Which leaves you with....


The story and gameplay. Make no mistake, half life's gameplay is far and away outstanding and polished down to a diamond. Catching things in VR has never felt so satisfying, and when you compare it the other popular games in the genre, the two are polar opposites. Everything has a "weight" to it and every object you interact with behaves as it should. I'm actually afraid to go and play some of the other previous games in VR simply because of how I remember how clunky they are compared to this. 

It's not like it doesn't have its faults when playing it though. I had trouble opening doors sometimes because of bodies getting clipped inside of them. As well as other minor issues where my guns wouldn't work as intended. These issues were minor though, and they almost should not be mentioned because of how little it happened (Once or twice). 

graphically, no other VR game can compare. It's just the best. No other like it. 

VR has come a long way. A REALLY long way. And it still has a long road ahead of it. This game is not a headset seller, but it is worth the price if you already have the setup. I've always based my reviews off of the amount of hours invested (1 hour = 1$) and the experience I've had with them. The experience I've had with Alyx is like no other in VR and worth 60$. At the end of the day though, the game is just good and nothing more.

Original Review:

I'll start with all the issues I have with the game:

- Smoke is [b]always[/b] bugged. When I started playing this game in spring, smoke would just vanish suddenly. They claimed to have fixed it (they didn't), then when they managed to fix it, they introduced a new bug: At random occasions some players can see silhouettes through the smoke, giving them a huge advantage. This is very frustrating and completely unacceptable in a game which requires you to use smoke.

- The game is terribly optimized. After some fixes I found in the forums and guides I could get it to run well, but at first I had around 100 fps (on medium, with an RTX 2070 Super) with sudden drops to below 30 fps. Then the game would just run at 25-50 fps until I restarted the game.

- The PvP mode Push is the only game mode which is fun for me. Competitive mode only exists for one of the main game modes.

- Cheaters can reach lvl 72 (for reference, I'm lvl 85 or so after 100 h) without getting banned. There's nothing you can do about it either, since they can just rejoin after getting kicked.

- Low player count. In Europe, it can happen that there is only one server with people on a workday. I have never managed to play a round of Competitive, because it is never populated.

- Lvl is purely time-based. No matter how good or bad you are, 99% of your XP gain is determined by the time you spend playing.

- Customization is either ugly, or will lead to you having a disadvantage because you stand out.

- Fun heavily depends on how well your team works together (at least for me). This can make the game incredibly fun, or very frustrating.

- Vaulting is a pain and often doesn't work properly.

- You will frequently get killed by completely random grenade (launcher) and RPG spam.

- Might be hard to get into at first.

(Edit: Almost forgot this:
- There are "restricted zones" in which you cannot shoot (so as to prevent spawnkilling probably), but they're very weirdly placed. Spawnkilling is still possible, however flanking can be hard on some maps due to this. As an example, on one map the zone starts immediately behind the building in which the objective is, which means you cannot enter from behind or briefly go outside to kill incoming defenders.)

Now for the good things:

+ Requires teamwork, and most of the community is willing to work together and to aim for the win, rather than the highest K/D rate.

+ Commander/Observer combo is an amazing idea and feels so...strategic.

+ Great gunplay, nice feeling of recoil and big differences between weapons.

+ Weapons have different customization and make them feel even different.

+ Classes have distinct equipment and roles.

+ The two factions feel different.

+ Sound is great, nice directionality of footsteps etc.

+ Maps are quite nice.

Overall it's a great game and I definitely recommend it, but it is far from perfect. Consider all the negative points before buying this game.

Negatívum: 
A felülnézet miatt "sokszor" forgatni kell a kamerát, ami nem lenne zavaró ha folyamatosan szükség lenne erre az opcióra azonban a játék során 5-6-szor kell csak ezt megtenni, de ekkor kissé szokatlan vagy elfelejtődik és emiatt lehet valaki elakad. Je n'avais jamais joué à Don't Starve avant de me saisir de l'offre Bundle de Don't Starve Together. Bien que les commentaires précédents conseillent d'avoir joué en solo, je vous affirme que ça n'est pas une nécessité.
Bien sûr, c'est plus difficile de prendre en main la totalité des possibilités du jeu. Mais ça vient tout de même rapidement et le mode social est parfait pour débuter.

L'intérêt du pack bundle était de l'offrir à ma copine, qui a été tout de suite séduite par les vidéos du jeu. Nous avons donc lancé et découvert le jeu en même temps et la surprise est à la hauteur des notes et commentaires donnés : +60 heures de jeu en 1 semaine.

Les mécaniques du jeu sont excellentes. Bien que frustrant lorsque la partie est mal paramétrée au niveau des ressources, de la quantité des monstres, de la durée des saisons... le jeu n'en reste pas moins excellent.

Les créations (crafts) sont nombreuses. Pour vous dire, nous n'avons pas encore fait une partie dans laquelle nous avons créé la moitié de ce qui est possible à faire. Sûrement parce qu'à chaque fois que nous pensons être en mesure d'asssurer la suite, nous nous faisons dépop à grande vitesse par une créature que nous ne connaissions pas encore.

Les combats sont basés sur le kitting (Hit and Run). Mais attention, certains ennemis savent très bien "kitter" eux aussi ! Et là où vous pensez qu'il faut courir pour ne pas mourir, il faudra bien souvent combattre pour récupérer des matières rares et intéressantes pour la suite.

L'exploration est un point essentiel du jeu. Les maps sont grandes ou immenses et les ressources dispatchées aléatoirement. Recherche et découverte oblige !

Côté gameplay, je note tout de même de petites choses désagréables :
- le petit lag lors de la sauvegarde automatique qui se passe au début de journée, si vous êtes en train de combattre, vous prendrez des coups gratuits, même de très loin, et ne donnerez pas ceux que vous aurez pourtant bien portés aux ennemis.
- il y a aussi les hitbox qui sont un peu abusives concernant certains mobs ou objets (par exemple les pièges à dents qui s'activent sur une toute petite hitbox par rapport à la taille du graphisme).
- pour finir, ce randoming qui va vous faire détester le jeu : lorsqu'on a bien géré sa base, qu'on voit venir une attaque de chiens (hounts) et que surviennent (en même temps) une pluie de météorites, une attaque d'abeilles tueuses et un cerfclops... C'est une mort en boucle assurée pour le mode sans fin et une fin de partie pour le mode survie.

Pour les graphismes, il suffit de voir les vidéos qui vous montrent tout. C'est propre, bien représenté et souvent les réactions des personnages sont assez drôles (surtout quand ils sont équipés de bonnets d'hiver, de jupettes et talons haut, même pour les hommes ^^).

Je termine sur le point le plus positif : le coopératif. Don't Starve est un jeu particulièrement difficile. Tout est fait pour vous emmerder, concrètement. Lorsque l'on joue à plusieurs, il ne faut pas oublier qu'il faut nourrir chaque personne. Les ressources alimentaires doivent donc être rassemblées pour autant de joueurs qu'il y en a dans la partie. Il est nécessaire de coordonner les déplacements, la recherche des ressources et les combats importants.

Pour conclure, si vous cherchez un survival coopératif qui vous donnera du fil à retordre, je crois bien que Don't Starve Together est LE titre qu'il vous faut dans votre bibliothèque.

Zacznijmy jednak tradycyjnie, czyli od fabuły. Techland zdecydował się tym razem na porzucenie "sandboksowego" pomysłu na kilku bohaterów, wprowadzając jedną, odgórnie narzuconą postać. Skupienie się na jednym bohaterze, a więc brak konieczności stworzenia scenariusza uniwersalnego, zaowocowało intrygującym w pierwszej chwili zawiązaniem historii. Dobrym pomysłem okazuje się tutaj zredukowanie wiedzy gracza do absolutnego minimum. Niezbyt wiele wiemy o bohaterze, również jego zleceniodawcy (do miasta trafiamy z tajną misją) przedstawieni są w bardzo zdawkowy sposób, nie mamy też żadnej precyzyjnej wiedzy na temat sytuacji w Harran. Całość podana nam została jednak w taki sposób, że nie podważamy wiarygodności sytuacji.

Szkoda tylko, że sama historia nie jest może przesadnie oryginalna i korzysta z wielu motywów charakterystycznych dla gatunku, mając jednak swoje momenty i kilka zwrotów akcji. Najbardziej podobał mi się pod tym względem chyba początek rozgrywki, kiedy byłam nieco zdezorientowana niejednoznacznymi sytuacjami i reakcjami bohatera. Niestety po tym obiecującym wstępie historia rozwinęła się w łatwo przewidywalny sposób, tracąc nie tyle rozpęd, co potencjał. Fabuła, choć pełna kalek, sprawdza się więc całkiem nieźle, pozostawiając jednak pewien niedosyt - tutaj naprawdę można było "pojechać" jeszcze mocniej. Twórcy zdawali się jednak - mimo tych fabularyzujących zabiegów - nie ukrywać, że Dying Light to produkcja, w której największy nacisk położony został na rozgrywkę. Olbrzymi plus należny się natomiast za masę świetnych, pełnych aluzji oraz nawiązań małych epizodów i scen, na które natrafić możemy podczas eksploracji.

Oczywiście Dying Light to nie tylko główny wątek fabularny, ale również całkiem spora liczba różnorodnych zadań pobocznych. Te z grubsza podzielić można na dwie grupy - fabularne i wyzwania. Druga grupa obejmuje przede wszystkim dwie formy aktywności - "biegi przełajowe" na czas oraz wyzwania związane z walką. Mówiąc krótko w wyznaczonym limicie czasu musimy pokonać zadaną trasę bądź też zabić określoną liczbę zombiaków. Poziom tych wyzwań jest rozsądny - wymaga pełnego skupienia i koncentracji oraz doskonałej znajomości mechaniki rozgrywki, jednocześnie nie zmuszając nas do kilkudziesięciu nieudanych prób. Dodatkową motywacją są atrakcyjne nagrody: unikalne przedmioty, czy pokaźne kwoty pieniędzy.

app_name: Total War: ROME II - Emperor Edition
review:
I never write reviews but I feel like I have to do it for this one. This is right now a great game, no matter what anyone says. So far the best TW maybe with the exception from Attila. I have over 300 hours on Rome 1 so I know what the franchise was. 

The problem about this game (and subsequent TW games) its his very greedy publisher decisions. Too many minor DLCs to a very high price, we can all agree it is outrageous. On the other hand we are on Steam and this game is on sale quite often, I've purchased it and all the DLC that interested me for about 30-40€, which is a fair price for the product.

The game es very stable now, still looks really good and it's really optimized. Some mechanics have poor balancing, like spies that can starve to death small factions without any cost is a good example, but for the most part they are engaging and fun, I think it was a good step overall and a breeze of fresh air. Right now also diplomacy works pretty well, it was not the case on near release. Battles are really fun and fluid and you can work out many strategies, the best ones in the series for me. Also the faction pool imo it's awesome and the campaign map feels huge, also there is a ton of NPC factions which makes you appreciate the diversity in tribes back then. 

The mixed reviews are deserved for it's disastrous release and greedy DLC policy, but that doesn't change the fact that it is the best TW experience right now for me.

Everything was going smooth, passing Virals was easy, they scream all the time so you can stay out of their sight without much problem. The slow ones were taken care by the firecrackers, handy tool I'm telling you.
Finally I've found some energy bars, bread, bottled water to satisfy hunger and thirst and gauze with alcohole just in case if something would happen.
Well...
Taking a different route back was a bad idea, got too close to Rais place and some thugs attacked me. I had no chance since there were 3 of them and I was alone weak and tired from lack of food and water. I thought it was over, you know. I'll never see my son or my dear wife again but something happend.
As I was getting kicked to death I covered my head and other vital points to I guess endure a little longer but then I've heard a sound of metal slamming on the walls and screams of virals in pain. The sound of metal smashing on walls and wooden boxes was closing in.
Then suddenly... 
After a moments of silence I heard a loud noise...
BONK!
Then couple more of those...
BONK! BONK BONK!
Everything went silent and no one was hitting me anymore.
After getting of the ground I've noticed a MAN, a single man with a FRYING PAN.
He said:
-Are you alright?
I said that I can manage if I can just bring the food to my family and save them.
Then he said:

... This is what happend friend. Now we can be safe with a community of great people in the Tower, my family is safe and I don't have to worry about anything anymore.
Sometimes you can still see Kyle Crane running around playing Checkers on the roof with someone, and weapons at the shop.

Whoo boy, where to even begin?  I guess a TL;DR description?  Basically, this feels like what you'd get if you took some older style CRPGs, like Baldur's Gate, and modernized them.  Add in a ton of character customization, online multiplayer, built-in mod support, and quest decisions that'll leave permanent impacts on the plot.  The game is long, has a pretty good plot, lots of side-plots, and a ridiculous amount of replayability.  If that sounds good to you, then get this game!

Also, this game is really long.  Expect a normal playthrough to take 50+ hours.


This game, while not perfect, is freaking great.  Why?  Let me try to keep this brief, since I'd probably write pages going into detail on things.  This game can be played solo, with friends, or drop-in/drop-out public and you can switch at any time on any given save.  There's four difficulty modes, ranging from casual "just here for the plot" to hardcore "delete your save if you wipe".  You start by choosing your character, either selecting from one of the canon characters who have their own in-game storylines and some unique skills, but can't have their name or appearance changed, or you can make your own character.  Regardless of what you pick, you're free to assign their skills, traits, and stat points as you please and, if you make mistakes, you can respec freely starting in Act 2.  (And, I do mean freely.)

Once you're started, you're free to go about your business.  It's a little confined at first, given the plot, but it'll quickly open up.  Half of this game is the exploration and interaction with NPCs.  Your choices in conversation often have permanent impact and cannot be taken back except by reloading.  What quests you take, which of conflicting quests you do, and even how you solve the quest or report your success can alter things for the better or worse.  Kill a NPC you don't like and maybe you'll meet their wife later in the game and can tell her you killed him.  Help a guy out and he might return the favor later.  

Or he might stab you in the back down the road.

Yes, that may happen.  Things are not cut and dried in Divinity and you should always question whether you should trust someone.  Some people are there to help, some to take advantage of you, and some may shift dispotions depending on how you interact with them.  Likewise, you're free to help or betray whoever you please and whether you make it to the end as a saint seeking to save the world or the epitome of evil leaving a trail of bodies seeking to take all power for yourself is entirely up to you.

The story might follow a given path through the whole game, but the branches it takes, the way it unfolds, and how it ends is entirely up to you.  Apparently, even some ending options are only available if you make certain choices or play certain characters.

The other half of the game is combat.  You'll have a massive array of options of how to approach it due to the sheer amount of customization available and synergies available.  Wanna be a bow-wielding summoner?  Wanna sprout wings and fly behind someone to stab them in the back?  Do you wanna throw a fireball at someone, then douse water on them to make steam, and then electrify the steam and turn it into a thundercloud?  You can do all of that.  Not every choice is the most optimal, but if you're not playing on Honor difficulty, who really cares?

Combat is turn-based with initiative (and status effects) determing turn order.  Everyone gets a certain number of action points to use per turn and can carry some of them over to their next turn (in most cases).  Moving uses differing action points depending on your move speed and how far you're going.  Using abilities, attacking, using items, and so forth all also use differing amounts of AP as well.  Two unique things about this game, however, is the armor and the terrain systems.  Characters and most NPCs are protected by Physical and Magic Armor that basically act as extra hit points.  In order to damage health and inflict status effects, you'll have to break through the respective armor (with some exceptions).  It's a neat system, but it does make status effects a bit binary, either really weak or really strong depending on if armor is up or down.

Terrain though... is a whole 'nother beast.  Many attacks will leave "surfaces" or "clouds".  A fireball, for example, will burn the ground for a couple of turns, damaging people who move in it and igniting anyone who's magic armor is down.  Once the fire goes out on its own, it'll make a brief smoke cloud that prevents people from seeing through it.  These terrains interact with skills and each other, which is where things can get crazy.  That fireball will ignite and detonate any oil surfaces, instantly damaging anyone standing on them and setting them ablaze.  Likewise, dropping a pool of oil next to open flame will explosively spread that fire.  Water, meanwhile, can put out fire and create steam.  And both water and steam can be electrified to shock anyone passing through them.  Water can also be frozen into ice, which might make people crossing it slip and fall.  You can also corrupt water and turn it into poison, which will damage and poison people moving on it.  You can then curse the poison to turn it into acid, which will erode physical armor.  You can then detonate the acid with fire and... yeah, we're just scratching the surface and haven't even touched on other synergies.  The number of ways abilities can interact with each other is pretty crazy and I'm really, really confident I've hardly figured them all out.

Also, yeah, there's mods, which lets you add a ton to the game.  Or you can fix things you don't like about the game.  So, have a problem with something, like no respec in Act 1?  There's a mod for that.


Like I said, the game does have its fair share of flaws.  One would probably be crafting.  It's neat, but it feels unfinished.  If you're not using potions, scrolls, and grenades a lot, most of it seems frivolous beyond the early game.  The game's number scaling is also a bit off.  For most of the adventure, it's fine.  But by Act 4, it kinda just... explodes to the point where items start to double in effectiveness every level and a rusty sword costs more gold than is in the entirety of the first half of the game.  (Gold wasn't a problem for me at that point, thankfully.)  There's also a ton of items that seem like they'll be important or useful, but aren't, and ended up clogging my inventory.  Backpacks help with this immensely since I can at least shove the clutter into its own space.  There was also an end-game fight I had to use cheese tactics to pass since enemies killed respawned instantly and got a free turn in before the round ended.  And because there were traps, they'd run on them, suicide, respawn, run on them suicide, respawn, and repeat for minutes on end.  It was hilarious at first.  But when they started attacking and then killing themselves.... yeah...

Biggest complaint though?  Effects like confusion.  They're usually preventable, but not always.  Anything that makes you lose control of your character is a super pain in the butt.  Your character can take any action on their own within the parameters of the status effect.  Which, in my case, included chugging tons of potions or using lots of scrolls.  I'd be okayish with it if they didn't use consumables.  But them effectively throwing wasting items was infuriating.

Anyway, I'm literally out of space.  Despite the flaws, I seriously recommend this game!  Just make sure to keep up with your Real Life™ obligations when playing!

I've got to say... I'm very impressed. Never have I played a game so many times in such a short time span. 305 hours spent on this game since I bought it, and I'm still having a blast!
This is probably the only game I'd consider "Horror" in any way that I still truly love to play (I'm a massive wimp). It terrifies me to no end, especially the Leviathans, but something keeps pulling me back every update...

This is a very beautiful game with brilliant visuals and sound design to really pull you in and make you feel like you're there. There's lots of content and many hours of fun on any given save file, even if you've memorized many parts of the game. At first I was concerned that having a single map instead of a procedurally generated one would decrease replay value in an adventure/survival game, but it actually helps out a lot on following play-throughs.
The different biomes and wildlife felt diverse and interesting, especially as you get farther in the game and deeper into the ocean.
The story is pretty intriguing, but not intrusive. If you want to ignore it, you can. For however long, or at whatever point in the story, you want.
Certain parts of the game, such as exploring wrecks, can be confusing and disorienting at times. Thankfully they never felt too frustrating to me, and the sense of accomplishment after every successful trip makes it all worth it.

Now, this game does have quite a few issues. 
First of all, it is buggy. REALLY buggy. Some bugs are even game-breaking. I can't name the number of times I had to abandon a save file because it got corrupted for no reason, or I got caught in an endless death loop. It's possible to avoid such problems (Mainly through backing up your save files and/or heavily researching the known bugs and what causes them), but I can totally understand this turning people away from the game.

Second of all, lag. While I don't really have the best computer, I've never had this much trouble with lag in any game. (Aside from Dishonored 2 I guess, but that's an entirely different story.) I have to play the game on the absolute lowest visual settings in order for the game to even run. (Yes, I'm within the system requirements.) Some areas are especially bad and I've had to learn to move very cautiously through them. Not because of any monsters, mind you, but simply because objects will load out of nowhere right in front of me and severely damage my submarine. Even from a simple aesthetic perspective, this is pretty bad. Remember how I said the game fealt really realistic and pulled you into it's world? Yeah, well that applies only when the creatures and environments don't pop into existance 3 meters away from you. It's frustrating and pulls you out of the experience, even when technically harmless to your gameplay.

Last of all, the A.I. This is yet another thing that kinda pulls you out of the game. While the AI seems acceptable or even good at first, the longer you play the more start to notice how fake it all feels. It's hard to be scared of the big scary sea monsters when you realize you can just move a certain way or get too close to a certain thing and make it's AI flip out, turning it into a giant flailing spaghetti noodle. It again takes you out of the experience far too often, ruining what the sound and art design managed to achieve. This is a problem with a lot of games, so maybe I only noticed it here because I play Subnautica way too much. I don't really know. Either way, once you notice it, it makes it harder to feel immersed in the world, which is essential to a game fo this nature.

Some of these issues have been improved upon in recent updates, but so far there hasn't been anything so drastic as to change my opinions on these issues. I sure hope these are just problems with my computer, but considering the large amount of people who seem to agree with me, I don't think it is. I understand that the game is in development, but it's getting kind of ridiculous at this point. These issues NEED to be fixed, or at least majorly improved upon before release.

Now, I've gotten pretty negative by this point, but it's really only because I want anyone who reads this to know what they're getting if they buy this game. 

Tl;Dr 
Subnautica is fun, with lots of play time. It's highly immersive, beautiful, and an over-all blast. In the end, I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys the survival, adventure, and sci-fi genres. Just be prepared for some pretty nasty bugs that probably won't be fixed any time soon.

Edit Review:

My original review of this game was negative due to the planned ( not bugged) movement changes that were introduced with the latest mount update.  

For me, it was so very frustrating- it reminded me of the Star Wars Galaxies revamp when everyone quit.  Very similar feeling.  (SWG was a game I loved and hated to leave.  I think about it still.)

 The previous Conan update felt like I was fighting a gimped movement system.  It was like moving your character through mud with ankle weights on vs being able to enjoy all the other wonderful features in the game.  ( I LOVE this game. It's amazing, quirky bugs aside.  My kid can play the theme song on her trumpet, she hears it so often.)

The official forums blew up about the movement changes.  It was nuts. 

Since then, Funcom has reviewed a lot of the issues that had come up (sluggish movement, the long ramp-up to full run speed, jumping/falling and the turning /walking small movements).

Funcom held their Conan Thursday stream 12/12/19.   It looked like they had as rough as a week as the rest of us did.   It probably didn't help that they were also sick.  That's a lot to deal with when also being under the weather.  I get the human side of it.

They announced the failure of the lack of communication.  The 'why' the movement was adjusted the way that it was.  They explained that it was a more "sledgehammer" approach to a fix vs a "scalpel" adjustment.   And Funcom apologized. 

Wow.  I honestly didn't see that coming. A company taking responsibility for not something I'd say was a mistake, but more a rash change that blindsided a lot of players.  Well done. 

Today, Fri 12/13, they introduced a hotfix which included refinement to the movement system.

It feels great.  Not the same.. it's not a rollback.  But different and playable. 
Quicker response time.   I can move around my base again without dragging my feet.  I can jump off a cliff and grab back onto the ledge again.  I can control the character sprint much more fluidly than before.

Thank you Funcom for adjusting the movement system!

Thank you Funcom for the stream explaining what happened!
