Über DbD:
Dead by Daylight bietet ein bisschen von allem: Hide and Seek, Jump & Run, Strategiespiel, tw. Roleplay und: viiiel Spaß! Keine Runde läuft wie die andere dank unterschiedlicher Charaktere mit den verschiedensten Möglichkeiten aber auch dank der Personen hinter den Bildschirmen. Es kann sowohl zu gruseligen oder anstrengenden, als auch zu extrem lustigen Runden kommen. Auch vier Jahre nach Release schläft das Spiel und seine Community nicht ein und es kommt ständig zu Updates, neuen Spielfeatures und neue Killer oder Survivor bringen ständig neuen Schwung ins Spiel.

Gameplay an sich:
Wie das Spiel funktioniert, erkläre ich jetzt mal nicht. Die meisten Leute wissen es schon oder können es in anderen Reviews lesen. Hier möchte ich nur persönliche Eindrücke erwähnen. 
Durch Challenges und tägliche Rituale (verschiedene Aufgaben, die man machen DARF für zusätzliche Punkte) kommt Abwechslung in den Spielealltag und durch die kaufbaren Cosmetics kann man sich recht individuelle Spielecharaktere erstellen. Jeder kann sich eigene Strategien überlegen, wie er/sie spielen möchte. Manchmal dauert es kurz ein paar Minuten bis man in eine Lobby mit vier Survivorn und einem Killer kommt aber dafür werden in der Regel die Level der Spieler aufeinander abgestimmt, sodass man als Neuling (meist) nicht mit oder gegen Profis spielen muss. Das vereinfacht auch den Einstieg ins Spiel.
Zu den Bugs... ja, es gibt sie, aber nicht allzu viele. In der Regel (und nach Möglichkeit) werden sie schnell gefixt. Wobei ganz ehrlich: manche Bugs sind auch einfach nur lustig und es ist fast schon schade, wenn sie gefixt werden!

In-Game-Käufe:
Das negativ behaftete "Pay to win" gibt es hierbei nicht. Nur manche Klamotten und ein paar der Survivor und Killer müssten, wenn man selbst damit spielen möchte, mit "Echtgeld" bezahlt werden, sind aber nicht nötig, um im Spiel Erfolge zu erzielen. Vieles kann man sich auch kaufen ODER einfach freispielen. Ich persönlich habe nur einen Survivor mal mit Echtgeld geholt, als er im Angebot war, alle übrigen Charaktere und Outfits freigespielt und nun 16 von 22 Survivorn. Es gilt also: wer mehr möchte oder manche Dinge schneller haben möchte, kann dafür bezahlen, ansonsten kann man fast alles mit der Zeit auch einfach freispielen.

Community:
Auch wenn manche Spieler leider meinen, sich toxisch verhalten zu müssen und manche leider so spielen, als wären sie die Einzigen, die Spaß am Spiel haben dürfen (derart sozial unterentwickelte Personen findet man wohl überall), ist und bleibt das Gesamterlebnis doch sehr positiv. Viele meiner Steam-Freunde habe ich über DbD kennen gelernt und spiele inzwischen regelmäßig mit ihnen. Mit Freunden zu spielen macht das Spieleerlebnis um so lustiger.

Schlusswort:
Ich würde sagen, knapp 1.450 Spielstunden und 2,5 Jahre regelmäßigen DbD-Spielens sagen genug darüber aus, ob ich das Spiel weiter empfehlen kann: Nein.
Quatsch, natürlich ganz klar JA. Für 20€ (oder im Sale tw. sogar für nur 10€) bekommt man hier viel geboten. Für mich hat sich das investierte Geld definitiv gelohnt!

Hai mai pensato di, che so, vivere la vita di un ladro professionista e avere un aiutante hacker, che pur cliccando a caso nella tastiera, riesce a trovare persino i contatti per creare un conto estero per poter, dopo fatto il colpo, inserire parte dei soldi che rubi che se no ti ritrovi un controllore bancario delle entrate che ti mette nei casini più assurdi?! BENE, questo è il gioco che fa per te!

PAYDAY 2 è il gioco FPS d'eccezione andando da semplici rapine a mano armata a missioni stealth dove bisogna rubare un DIAMANTE. Tutto condito con un sistema di strutturazione del personaggio in stile GDR tramite ramificazioni di abilità per qualsiasi specializzazione tu preferisca. Vuoi fare tutto in maniera stealth e bypassare sicurezze con un jammer? Fai lo Spettro! Vuoi fare il carry per tutta la mappa con una armatura da transformers e la vita di un dinosauro? Fai lo Specialista!

Il gioco è veramente di bel impatto, grafica ben ottimizzata e bella da vedere, varie armi, personalizzazioni sia delle armi che delle maschere, varie missioni dinamiche dove può variare persino la posizione di una telecamera. Ottimo da giocare in compagnia, oltre alle tante risate si crea un bel gioco di squadra necessario, addirittura essenziale. 

Non ho parole per i DLC. 0.99 centesimi è la maggioranza del prezzo di un contenuto aggiuntivo che sblocca nuove armi e accessori, qui non c'è nulla di male, peccato che in ogni DLC danno al massimo 3 armi e 2 maschere. E i dlc sono almeno più di 20. Una cosa positiva è che anche se non hai il DLC di una nuova missione ci puoi giocare comunque se l'host della partita ha acquistato quel dlc, ma tu non puoi hostare o creare una partita con quel contratto del contenuto aggiuntivo.

Consiglio questo gioco, ma purtroppo avviso che è facile stancarsi!

You might be wondering whether to buy this game or not. Do it. It's $20. 

It's one of the most addicting games you'll ever play. The more competitive you are, the more you'll be hopelessly addicted (which actually isn't a bad thing when it comes to playing this game). After all, it is just so much fun.









Why, you ask?

The skill ceiling in this game is insanely high... meaning, you can dump over 1000 hours of play time into the game and still have much to get better at. At the time of this review, I'm at about 650 hours, and I haven't even gotten close to Grand Champion, which is the highest competitive-mode rank in the game. And even when you reach Grand Champ, there is still so much to get better at.

The trading system in this game is a world of it's own. If you want, you can just play matches. But when you put money into the game, you have entered into the realm of trade. You can trade anything you have with other players to get an item you want to use to customize your car. How cool is that?

The one downside to this game is the "toxicity" of a lot of players. Sometimes you'll play worse than you usually do, maybe because your co-workers pissed you off today, maybe because you didn't get much sleep the other night, etc. This is when you will see players, mostly your teammates, who relentlessly try to put you down and express how horrible you are just for the sake of it. It's gotten me raged before, but other times I just shrug it off. It really isn't that bad, especially since you can mute them, and if you can realize that they are probably just annoyed kids anyways.

Like I said: just buy it. You won't regret it.

Listen BlueHole, just because someone makes the same style of game as you doesn't mean they flat out copied you. You don't own the Battle Royal genre, no one does. If it were the case that Medal of Honor's developers would've sued the living Hell of out of studios like Infinity Ward, Treyarch and Activision for making Call of Duty. Blizzard would've sued Jagex over the MMO genre claiming Runescape ripped off World of Warcraft, and Valve would've probably sued Blizzard on the grounds that Overwatch copies Team Fortress 2. No one own a game genre. The reason you're losing to Fortnite is because your game is more or less an asset flip with hardly any identity at all. Fortnite on the other hand has its assets made by competent artists and a very talented team of programmers and games designers. It's neither their fault, nor their problem that you got salty because they out sold you. It's not their fault they were able to take a simple mechanic and do it better as well as give it its own identity. The most you own rights to are your Title screen and a few pieces of in game art that aren't even featured in the main portion of the game. Let's explore their talent vs your own shall we?

In PUBG, how do players drop into the map at the start of each match? They parachute in after leaping out of the back of a C-130 gunship. Okay, pretty standard, pretty generic. Not very exciting but not exactly appaling either.

Now in Fortnite how do they do the same exact mechanic, which you don't own btw BlueHole don't get it twisted that you own the mechanic of dropping into a map from the sky. How does Fortnite accomplish that? One jumps out of a bus carried by balloons and use a glider to land safely in the play space. That's unique. That's pretty exciting too. It stands out among other drop in sequences by being anything but run-of-the-mill. Point for Fortnite.

In PUBG, aside from the Storm and shooting other players what unique mechanics do players work with? Well you can drive motorcycles and cars in PUBG. Some of them. Not all of them. Okay, once again, pretty run-of-the-mill for a standard multiplayer focused shooter. Can be exciting to turn someone into paste if they step in front of you but nothing that most gamers haven't seen before.

In Fortnite, however they said to hell with vehicles (unless you count rocket hopping) and gave you a Minecraft-esque building mechanic that lets you create structures, cover, and ammunition if you have the right materials on the fly and pretty damn quickly. Building properly is almost as important as being able to land shots on a target in Fortnite as it can mean the difference between defeat and Victory Royale.

That previous point is up to the player preference. I personally prefer PUBG in this regard as it is a much more straight forward concept. However, straightforwardness doesn't ship units and sadly Fortnite simply beats out PUBG in the realm of unique mechanics, building mechanics like the ones displayed in Fortnite are really only seen in crafting heavy games such as Terraria and Minecraft.

What's the art style for PUBG? And I mean the in game assets that players will be seeing from the moment they open the game to the moment they close to desktop (or shut of the console if they perfer to play there). Well PUBG has a somewhat "in your face" logo that shows up in the main menu and in some of the loading screens. The in game assets are...well generic. It looks like what it sets out to be. A map of a generic island in the middle of nowhere with a base a port a few small towns a school etc. But there's not a lot else there to set it apart from other games thrown together with store bought assets. PUBG's world is very bland and run-of-the-mill and in my opinion boring.

Fortnite on the other hand reminds me strikingly of a Saturday Morning Cartoon. It's art style is colorful and vibrant, and with the addition of Save the World mode, there's actually a narritive here, a story that one can follow along and appreciate for what it is. The way the story is handled in Fortnite actually reminds me of how Titanfall 2 handled its story. The Campaign was designed to equate one to the mechanics of the Battle Royale mode. In this regard the world really shines when suddenly the whole mape is full of grotesque creature that wish nothing but ill towards the players that defend the generators.

Art assets definitely go to Fortnite, Fortnites style, from its cartoony aesthetic to how it implements emotes and cosmetic items for its player base simply out classes and out paces PUBG piece for piece.

How much is PUBG? ~$20 US plus any microtansactions made there in.

How much is Fortnite? Anywhere from Free to Play to $30 if you want to play story mode.

PUBG spends no time teaching you how to play it, but then again, if you're going the Free play route, neither does Fortnite. However only ones of these games bothers to teach you how to play at all. The first 3 or so mission of Fortnite campaign are the essentials. It teaches you the basics all the way up to building entire structures, laying traps and crafting items.

The concensus here is that, if you're good at learning stuff on the fly, Fortnite is the way to go. If you wanna be taught through an in game tutorial, Fortnite will cost you $30 US for the full campaign even though you only really need the first three missions.

Conclusion, while I would prefer to play PUBG over Fortnite, I cannot recommend PUBG in its current state. It has no identity, it's servers go unmonitored so cheaters run rampant, and its developer is more focused on sueing the competition than actually competeing. I don't recommend this game at all. If you want THE premire Battle Royale game, go play Fortnite.

(Initial Review)
As a long time fan of both the Battletech and Mechwarrior franchises I have been looking forward to this game since it was announced. I was not able to participate in the Kickstarter due to a spending moratorium imposed by my better half so launch day was my first exposure to it. I purposely kept myself from spoiler videos and early reviews so that I could approach the game with a clean slate.

Spoiler-free section: The first thing we are exposed to in most games is a cinematic introduction. This game sticks to the standard introduction formula and does not disappoint in the lore, or in its presentation. I particularly like the art style and while, yes, the voice acting is not AAA, it also does not take away from the game when viewing the game through the lense that it is a translation of a tabletop RPG. With this mindset the voice acting gives the impression of what playing a roleplaying game would be like if my game group was filled with voice actors. The voice work in Battletech is professionally done and gives the game a tone that is equal parts Battlestar Galactica (dark, serious and direct) and Starship Troopers (whimsical military-light). The battle chatter is to the point and serves as a functional play-by-play, though response driven commentary can become repetitive in any game. There is a good variety of situational pilot reactions to in-battle events and only at the very end of a several hours long play session did I find the battle dialogue repetitive.  I would like the option to adjust the frequency of comms chatter to reduce the repetitiveness over long play sessions, but this is far from being a deal breaker.

The battles are fluid and intuitive. Objectives are clear and make sense within the flow of the game. There is plenty of tactical depth here as well. Unit positioning is important, as is your patience as a player. The game rewards a thoughtful commander with reduced repair bills, but not to the extent that it encourages turtling and hiding behind terrain for the entire battle. Anyone who has played tabletop wargames before will appreciate the balance that has been struck here in Battletech between movement and cover, poking and alpha strikes, holding objectives and acceptable losses. This is where Battletech truly shines. The commander who brings a balanced lance is better able to respond to varied threats (queue the Steiner scout jokes) and is going to have the most enjoyable experience as the 4 different mech skills synergize well. Also, the activatable skills, once unlocked, improve situations rather than simply allowing you to immediately destroy your oppenent. Balance. Battletech is well tuned.

Graphics. They are good. Anyone who has played PGI's Mechwarrior online will know the mechs from their silhouette alone. Textures and models are above average for a strategy game. The environments deserve a special mention. The terrain and environments are varied and believable. What I mean by that is the terrain doesn't feel like it was simply painted on and plopped into place. Roads and buildings are placed logically and the whole of each location feels natural. It doesn't look like terrain was added just to create a barrier between points A and B. The level of environment design execution present in Battletech goes a long way toward immersion and their efforts here pay dividends throughout the game. Truly exceptional.

Mech customization and task management. You have all of the mech customization options you would expect from a Battletech game. Add/remove weapons, armor, heat sinks, jump jets, etc. What makes this aspect different from other battletech/mech games is the time component. Each change made to a mech requires time and will take the mech out of service until those changes have been completed. How you manage your mechs and what you choose to make available for each drop is important. You will find yourself  taking unrepaired mechs into battle out of necessity due to financial and time constraints. Pilots can be injured or killed  in battle as well. The timing aspect of the game borrows heavily from the XCom series in that regard and it works perfectly here as well.

As of this writing I have logged 7.5 hours into the game less than 24 hours after launch. The story works, it creates a sense of immediate peril and sets the stage for long-term drama. The combat is engaging, requires planning, and can be difficult  if you find yourself out of position. The presentation (audio/visual) is good and serves its intended purpose.

When I first saw this game, I didn't think much about it. Just another indy game, whatever. Then I watched playthroughs of it and thought it was awesome, and started wanting to play it for myself. Then, unfortunately, I saw some of the community around this game and how cringey it can get. Then it sort of faded into obscurity, I hadn't heard anything about it in like a year or two really, and a friend even wound up gifting me a copy for the holidays. Months later I'm playing it on multiple platforms and I can definitively say...

It's okay. Not the greatest game of all time, nor the dumpster fire that you might here contrarian types say it is. It's just good. There are a lot of likeable characters throughout, pretty good dialogue and jokes here and there, an intriguing story found if you look for it, and the combat? is a pretty nice twist on traditional rpg style fighting. 

That said, it doesn't have very gripping gameplay. Sure, there are puzzles here and there, and the bullet hell-esque defense is pretty challenging at times, but these just serve as a means to an end in hearing more from characters you like. This is especially true of Pascifist and Genocide runs of the game, with the former being annoying due to the complete lack of any sort of progression as a character, and the latter being a simple grind-fest until you clear an area and are ready for moving on to the next part. The fights themselves aren't all that fun, with the exception of a boss fight or two per route. In addition, the keyboard controls just feel clunky, using the arrow keys to move and interact with the world using "z" "x" and "c." Maybe it's just because of the amount of games I play, but using WASD is a lot easier to handle, and you can easily use other buttons for interactions, maybe even integrate a mouse into it for selecting in menus and possibly simplifying controls. I realize I'm having gripes about a game made by one dude that runs fairly well and is in all fairness pretty fun, but it's still worth noting its issues.

Like I said though, it's a good game, and I'd really recommend trying it out especially if you somehow haven't heard of it. A community shouldn't prevent a player from enjoying a single player game, so by all means enjoy.

I'm a strategy buff mostly into RTS and Turn based strategy with the occasional action shooter or rpg thrown in for good measure. I picked this game up looking for a versatile real world stategy game much like Civilization or the Supreme Ruler series (also by Paradox). What I've received thus far is a in depth strategy game with oodles of options for each and every turn, from administration to commerce to diplomacy to military tactics, everything is there. Prestige and rivalry is also a big element here between yourself and your immediately neighboring countries, provinces/states or factions. If you're looking to take a step from Civilization towards a more complex strategy title I'd recommend something like this as it has all of the bells and whistles that you're looking for at the cost of learning curve. That cost mind you is a steep but rewarding one that I've seen so far.

Pros
 - Detail (Choose from nearly 300 different nations to run from many different time periods in sand box or in scenarios)

 - Scenarios allow for story and event based timeline experience.

 - Events that happen in other parts of the world affect other nations according to how well they're connected (ie through trade routes, proximity and relevance). A major event that has happened far away might not be known to you but it may affect your interactions with other countries or even later when you make contact with other countries through trade and diplomacy.

 - AI is not easy nor a push over. Don't expect going into the game and taking a military victory with ease. Your neighbors opinions and relations are very important in this one.

 - Colonialism and confederation. You can expand your empire when and if powerful enough and found other nations, like the United States or Canada assuming you use those names. You could literally found such a colony in any unoccupied part of the world (after you clean it out of pesky Aboriginal peoples).

 - Play as Aboriginal nations. That's right. If you want a really hard core game you can play as an Aboriginal nation and attempt to organize your Aboriginal neighbors into an empire of your own. Have real negotiating power when colonists arrive or just crush them with your military might so long as you have enough prestige and trust of your neighboring Aboriginal partners.

 - Rewrite history. The game is very flexible and somewhat generic in some aspects allowing you to rewrite history with a little bit of effort and time.

 - Scalable. With DLC content the game includes some great addons some of which are necessary to enjoy the game fully. They also add historical events originating from nations in the game adding greater detail to the immense historical aspect of the game.

 - Workshop. Lots of Steam Workshop content.

Cons
 - Generic. It sometimes can feel a bit generic when playing with some nations that do not have content specific to their civilization. DLCs bridge this a bit but some can be a bit expensive as well. The Workshop content helps out in this end as well at the risk of incompatibility.

 - Learning Curve. I'd consider this a con if you don't invest the time it takes to learn this title. If you're like me you'll likely play it in stretches until frustrated by the learning curve only to return a month later with renewed vigor and curiosity.

 - Tutorials. There are many in game helpers and I'd recommend playing some of the easier scenarios at first to learn. It needs a one or two hour game tutorial that guides the player to building from a weak to modestly powered and prestigious nation to a powerful contender in the region of the country played.

Gameplay: 8.5/10 - Turns can be a little bit confusing at first thanks to the learning curve.
Interace:  9/10 - For all of the game's complexity, the interface brings it all together surprisingly well.
Graphics: 9/10 Don't expect a lot of animation but the board artwork and event artwork is great.
Audio: Great soundtrack and many DLCs add to this experience proving period music from a variety of civilizations. Sound FX are fairly good considering the genre.

Recommended if you're ready to expand from Civilization to something a bit more complex that isn't going to hold your hand as much.

Highly Recommended if you are very familiar with the strategy genre and loved the Supreme Ruler series or any other involved strategic simulation.

Having a lot of fun with it though. Would really recommend it to others, especially MonHun fans with no consol. It's interresting for them to try an actual story that they haven't really given a shot before in this series, and they got a lot of voice actors I love in here. 
Hearing a lot of issues with online but I've been playing with friends on and off since launch with no troubles either so I have no idea what everyone is talking about in those negative reviews. There's no harm playing this game single player, either. It is tuned to be played alone as well as with others and I've done just as much content solo as in multi. 
Also hearing that the keyboard/mouse controls are bad but like if you're gaming on PC why don't you have a USB controller of SOME KIND by now anyways? Like for those layback chill game not like a FPS where you need super tight mouse tier aiming?
If you care about your 4K monitor and the pixel perfect graphics, well this isn't supposed to be that. It's pretty as is and there's a lot of places I like to just go and look around. That high place in Wildspire, pretty much anywhere in Highlands, that first area in Forest where those Aptonoth hang out. 
Just enjoy things, folks. Really is not that hard to just... have fun and enjoy something without picking it apart. And hell, if you don't like it, Steam gives refunds. No harm no foul. Hang out with the Wigglers and the Kepli and just have a good time.

This entry to the series does away with a lot of that. Lots of trees have very similar looking weapons (the same bone base but with fur from whatever mob's parts are added to it, basically). This makes for a more 'realistic' look, I suppose, where you probably wouldn't re-work an entire weapon's form just to add an element to it, ya know? Would love some more cool weapon designs is all but it's fine, just thought I'd say.

Going into this game, I was on and off. In the beginning, I hadn't been charmed yet by the game's potential and quality; for around 100 hours. This time was spent mostly playing invade and annex and other miscelaneous endeavors within the game, but I hadn't really gotten devoted to one mode or playtype in general. 
    
    This, I think, is what the casual, sale purchaser will do, as I did, because there is not much that prompts you to delve into such communities as the zeus servers or custom modding communities; you have to discover these sections, with the drive to doing so only coming from your own interest and inquiries rather than from any queues from the game itself. 
    
    I found it very grouling to have to dig and search for all this myself. But why do I? In other games, 'if you want to find communities and like minded people, it is your job to go and find those.' Now I would agree with that perspective on most games, but not this one. 

    With ARMA III, The entire ideal game experience, is the community and what it makes of Arma. For example: modding, role play groups, milsim groups, just casual mod groups all give you options to explore vast arrays of amazing experiences with this game. But that's it. It is just these communities adding to the game that give it life. If this game had no modding and no option for custom sessions, it would have died a long time ago. The vanilla game itself has a lifespan, of like what happened when I first played, of about a hundred hours, until you yearn for more. 

    The Single Player Campaign is truly unextraordinary. It is a series of tutorials, that all tie together in a narrative, but still only serve to show you how to play the game. You will learn (sort of) how to pilot vehicles, from helicopters to submarines... which only really serves to help you not get yelled at by annoyed teammates trying to accomplish an objective. Of the almost 2k hours I have, not 10 hours went into the campaign. Even with the new DLC's bringing in something new to the single player scene, they still act like tutorials for the new gadgets and toys brought in.

    This game was really hyped up when it came out, and rightfully so. The graphics were beautiful for a game in 2013. I saw instagram posts captioned: [i] "Think this is a real life picture? No, it's the game ARMA III with ultra graphics turned on." [/i] It was amazing. And I remember playing one of the free weekend sessions in 2014, going into an invade and annex server and being amazed at the immersion and complexity of the game. I thoroughly enjoyed waiting for a transport chopper to pick me up from base to bring me to the battlefield and in the process, deciding with a recently acquired buddy that we were going to go in as a sniper/spotter duo and pick them off from afar. Approaching the island, I yelled over the wurr's of the helicopter blades to the pilot that we would be dropped off a bit prematurely, as we'd spotted a nice vantage point. So he set us down and we got set up a [i] kilometer [/i] away from the battlezone, just the right range before the enemies would start to disappear from rendering. I was blown away by the fact that I had to adjust my range and have my spotter call out targets to me. It was so much fun.

    But even that after a while -- after I had learned all there is to learn and mastered the unnecessarily complicated UI and systems -- started to become stale. So this amazing mode where I could insert myself tactically with friends and clear out objectives like true soldiers that truly captivated me for hours on end would too dwindle away like the campaign's fire did; granted, at a much slower rate, but still. And even that mode was not made by Bohemia Interactive. Invade and Annex or Liberation servers, etc. all are made by the peers and consumers of the game alike. The most amazing and interactive parts of this game, are not even given to us by the developers. An analogy could be: Bohemia are the teachers who give the kids (modders and coders) the crayons and markers (tools) to make cool things, but don't actually do it themselves.

    So after playing other games for a bit or just not even playing games at all, I came back to ARMA, craving those amazing experiences I had once gone through. That is when I discovered the Zeus gamemode. Zeus was a DLC added to ARMA not long after it's release which gave players the ability to create their own scenarios to let players, like little green soldiers, play on the battlefield.

    It was so genius, I thought. I joined and immediately loved it, as the scenarios and missions were player made, and new every single time. I then got my hands on the player slot of Zeus and created my own mission. The players all hated it of course, as it was my first time and had no idea what I was doing.

    It was at this moment that I found a new respect for other people that I had never felt in a video game before. I felt, then, that it is a responsibility of the player in Zeus' chair to make fun experiences for the other players, if not from a solely ethical standpoint, then from the concern that comes from zeus servers' closley knit communities, which is that your reputation as a mission creator may be tarnished.

    So here was this new mode I had been playing, where, even in the loading screen as you joined a Zeus server, you were reminded with a caption preaching that [i] "In Zeus, no scenario is predetermined, everything is made by you, the Zeus." [/i] I was having so much fun from the satisfaction I got from making amazing missions for people who wanted amazing missions. People commenting on my profile saying "how good of a zeus I am" felt awesome. But again, I realized, none of this was coming from Bohemia. This was all us, the players, taking what Bohemia layed down as a foundation and building a skyscraper from it. They did nothing. And that thought really did and still does bother me.

Dead by Daylight é um jogo que superou minhas espectativas, principalmente pelo fato de que me falaram mal do jogo, disseram-me coisas como "Ah é cheio de bugs", "Não funciona corretamente", "Mal otimizado", porém o jogo é excelente, principalmente para um jogo na versão 1.3.1(versão que eu comecei a jogar), o que as pessoas não entendem que raramente um jogo que não tem um enorme fiador, dificilmente é lançado sem um ou outro bug ou falta de otimização, calma ai gente não é a Rockstar, Blizzard ou Valve, por exemplo, fazendo o jogo, não foram gastos 200 milhões para fazer o jogo.

E com a experiencia de atualmente 148 horas de jogo, me fez perceber que os unicos bugs que aparecem no jogo são na tela inicial, e durante a escolha da posição que você quer jogar(Be a Survivor ou Be a Killer), que as vezes buga e você fica preso em um looping, mas isso é fácilmente arrumado reiniciando o jogo ou reiniciando a Steam.

Uma coisa que me deixou desapontado é o jogo não ter um servidor fixo, o que faz com que algumas partidas fiquem com a latência(ms) alta pois o host da partida é o Killer, que muitas vezes ou é de uma região longe como América do Norte, Europa Ocidental ou Oriental, ou Oriente mesmo, o que te leva muitas vezes a abandonar o Lobby e procurar outro, mas não é algo que atrapalhe tanto meu julgamento sobre o jogo.

O jogo é muito bom em praticamente todos os aspectos, os sobreviventes jogam em terceira pessoa o que dá certa vantagem sobre o assassino, ja que você pode girar a camera e não apenas ficar preso no que esta fazendo(geralmente reparando os geradores, que são os objetivos principais do jogo), e ver o assassino antes que eles os vejam e se mover sorrateiramente para longe dali sem ser visto e tendo noção de onde se encontra o perigo.

A visão em primeira pessoa do assassino o atrapalha um pouco na hora de procurar os sobreviventes mas a velocidade dos assassinos compensa isso, pois eles são moderavelmente mais rápidos que os sobreviventes, fazendo com que os sobreviventes sejam o mais silencioso possivel e os mais astutos na hora de utilizar o mapa a seu favor para atrasar ou despistar os assassinos, fora que os assassinos com suas caracteristicas únicas conseguem mais vantagem ainda, sendo colocando armadilhas, desenhos mágicos ou utilizando de motosseras para conseguir surpreender e pegar os sobreviventes.

Outra coisa sensacional sobre o jogo, que me surpreendeu, é que cada sobrevivente ou assassino tem seu próprio kit de habilidades(perks e/ou itens nos casos dos assassino) exclusivos os tornando melhores que os outros em certos aspectos, como, por exemplo, a sobrevivente Meg que corre ligeiramente mais rápido que os outros personagens sem utilizar de qualquer adicional ou o assassino The Shape que tem 3 níveis, e em cada nível ganha algum atributo a custo de perder outros, em seu nível 1, ele é inauditivel a longa e a média distancia, o que na maioria das vezes resulta em sustos e surpresas, e em seu nível 3 fica extremamente rápido e derruba os sobreviventes com apenas 1 ataque.

Contém uma variedade grande de mapas, e esses mapas, principalmente os mais antigos(Autohaven Wreckers, Coldwind Farm e The Macmillian States) tem várias versões do mesmo mudando a forma com que você tem que jogar, pois alguns tem mais ganchos, menos ganchos, geradores em locais diferentes, tem mais espaços de campo aberto, menos e assim por diante, testando ao limite suas habilidades de sobrevivencia e de investigação de rastros e vestigios deixados pelos sobreviventes.

Os itens e add-ons no jogo são outra coisa que me deixaram impressionado, tendo vários níveis e utilidades, e sendo variados, desde mapas, e caixas de ferramentas até chaves que abrem uma porta secreta para você sair de fininho pelas costas do assassino enquanto ele acha que você vai consertar os geradores e sair pela porta da frente.

O jogo é incrivel, eu super recomendo, vão ser os R$36,99 mais bem gastos que vocês irão gastar!

[b]La viva imagen de los juegos Indie desarrollados correctamente, fundando a partir de Kickstarter este juego lucho su camino hacia Steam armado con impresionantes gráficos hechos a mano, interesante y brutal sistema de combate y por ultimo un narrador con uno de los mejores voice acting que he tenido el placer de escuchar en años, considerado por muchos como el "white Morgan Freeman"[/b]

[b]Dicho eso pasemos a las características.[/b]
[olist]
    [*]Increíbles gráficos, muy agradables de ver con un toque tenebroso y oscuro que encajan al dedillo con la temática del juego.

    [*]Interesante historia que engancha desde la mismísima intro del juego narrada con una de las mejores voces que he escuchado en años en un videojuego, esta voz también pasara a narrarte los eventos que vayan ocurriendo en el juego, ya sea un crítico, la muerte de un enemigo o aliado o cosas por el estilo.

    [*]Jugabilidad roguelike a más no poder, Darkest Dungeon es un juego que no perdonara tus errores, su sistema de autoguardado te impedirá rehacer tus errores añadiendo tensión a las batallas y la preparación para estas, exprimiendo cada recurso que tengas para no afrontar la derrota aunque en el fin, la suerte determinara tu destino más de una vez.

    [*]Sistema de combate en escuadrones 4vs4 por turnos con posicionamiento clave, el posicionamiento es crucial en este juego pues ciertas habilidades solo pueden utilizarse desde ciertos puntos del grupo como por ejemplo que un mago solo pueda atacar desde la parte trasera y un melee desde la delantera, para añadir dificultad y variedad los enemigos y ciertas clases poseen habilidades que cambiaran el posicionamiento de sus aliados o enemigos creando posibles estrategias.

    [*]Impresionante e innovador sistema de cordura para tus héroes, conforme pases tiempo en las Dungeon tus héroes perderán la cordura, volviéndose cada vez mas paranoicos con el mundo que les rodea y sus compañeros, llegando a volverse locos una vez llegado al máximo, cuando esto pase ignoraran ordenes, rechazaran curaciones o habilidades de otros compañeros o se negaran a utilizarlas sobre otros, complicando mas el combate.

    [*]Rasgos beneficiosos y perjudiciales permanentes aleatoriamente asignados a tu personaje después de cada Dungeon, si el personaje pierde la cordura dentro de una Dungeon recibe aparte otro rasgo perjudicial, estos rasgos varían desde reducciones de estadísticas hasta trastornos como la Cleptomanía o Ludopatía que deberán ser curados más adelante mediante edificios como Iglesias donde rezar o meditar para recobrar la cordura, Centros Médicos para curar los trastornos y otras desventajas o una taberna donde apostar y beber para restablecer cordura, los personajes están vinculados a ciertos tipos de "placeres" para restablecer la cordura, con lo que un Cruzado o una Hermana de Batalla preferirán rezar antes que beber para recobrar su cordura.

    [*]Variedad de clases y habilidades, el juego contiene más de 10 clases diferentes, cada una con "skill sets" variados, cada personaje es creado aleatoriamente con rasgos aleatorios y le son asignadas varias habilidades de su clase, con lo que varios personajes de la misma clase pueden tener habilidades diferentes entre ellos y desarrollar roles diferentes, además de habilidades de combate también se implementan habilidades de "campamento" que serán utilizadas durante las acampadas que desarrolles en las Dungeons y que también son diferentes en cada clase y cada personaje tendrá varias de ellas seleccionadas aleatoriamente.

    [*]Campamentos y habilidades de campamento, este juego posee Dungeons muy largas con caminos variables y generados aleatoriamente cada vez, la Acampada hace que tu grupo monte una hoguera y descanse un rato recuperando salud y cordura mediante las habilidades más arriba dichas, cada clase tiene sus habilidades y algunas pueden variar desde restablecer la cordura o darle un buff a un aliado para el resto de la Dungeon, pero hay que elegir bien pues solo dispones de 12 puntos para gastar entre los 4 personajes añadiendo decisiones críticas a tu acampada.

[b]En definitiva Darkest Dungeon ofrece casi todo lo que alguien esperaría de un juego a un precio ridículamente asequible, gráficos atrayentes y agradables, historia original y bien narrada, combate divertido y difícil y por ultimo una gran cantidad de contenido con dungeons aleatoriamente generadas que instan a la rejugabilidad, gran cantidad de enemigos diferentes y jefes que derrotar.[/b]
[/olist]
[b]Mi valoración no es otra que un absoluto y total 10/10, por su precio y estado (Early Access) ya contiene más contenido y empeño que otros juegos mucho más caros.[/b]

After spending a few hundred hours in this video game, I decided to quit spending my life in a cubicle. I traded my dreary desk job for the fresh air of a country farm. 

Last year, I divorced my house and sold my wife. I moved from the anaesthetic idyll of suburbia to the anaesthetic idyll of a small midwestern town. 

I purchased a farm from an estate sale, just like in the game. I renamed it "THE FARM OF THE VALLEY OF HATRED" just as I had in this game. I spent tens of thousands of dollars on gold tools (which I then spray-painted purple so they would essentially be iridium).

Soon, it became clear that I was in over my head. I walked to the general store to purchase seeds, but they didn't have anything good like Starfruit. I then decided to make one of the townsfolk my wife, but she quickly filed for a restraining order after I gave her some whole, raw fish that I caught in the sewers for the third day in a row. The community center had no magic gnomes, and I was not able to find a contractor to complete renovations in exchange for several pieces of fruit. I have been arrested several times for crawling around a local park swinging a sword looking for a ladder down to the good loot below.

Stardew Valley presents itself as an educational game, designed to teach an aspiring farmer the ropes. I write this review to you as a warning--it is no such thing. As I sit here under the fluorescent lights of the local library, squinting into a flickering CRT monitor, I am ashamed to say I am flat broke and destitute. The FARM OF THE VALLEY OF HATE has been repossessed by the county, my ex-wife is now married to my high school bully. Stardew Valley will NOT prepare you for the life of a real farmer--it's just a fun game.

Pros
+Fun and unique game mechanics that feel well designed and fleshed out
Diving off of walls to stop the other team's game winning goal is satisfying everytime.
+graphics look nice and game runs well
60 fps, nice interface etc.
+No issues with lag from servers (although some have complained about it)
+Split-screen multiplayer
Speaks for itself
Cons
-Lack of game modes/variety
This is my biggest complaint about the game. The game only has one standard game mode, there's no differences between cars other than visuals, and only a handful of arenas to play at, which again, do not affect gameplay.
I understand the game is trying to create a competitve experience, which means skill has to come before luck and in-game car upgrades, however, I feel this is a valid complaint.
-Lackluster single player mode
I understand, again, that this is a primarily multiplayer, competitive game. However, the singleplayer modes offered are extremely shallow. The primary modes are exhibition (a single match) and a league mode. However, the league mode struggles because all of the cpu teams are set to the same difficult setting (easy, medium or hard). This means that once I beat one team, the other matches should generally go the same way, as none of the cpu characters play different from one another (from what I've seen).  The league mode ends up feeling more suited towards the multiplayer game because of this but is not available in multiplayer.
-Controller support
Many controllers generally do not work with this game. While there is a fix on the forums to correct this, the fix brings up a new issue. For example, if I have an xbox controller (which, by default works with the game) and my friend has a logitech controller (which, by default does NOT work with the game) and I attempt the fix posted on the forum, at best I can allow my friend's logitech controller to work, however, my controller will no longer work. The fix only corrects the problem if all players are using the same type of controller. I returned the game because of this issue.


Overall, for 20 dollars I think the game provides an enjoyable that will ultimately end up being hit or miss for a lot of people. Personally, I felt the lack of variety in the game took away from it's lasting appeal and I didn't feel the core gameplay was enough to keep me playing.This, in addition to the controller support issue, leads me to not recommend this game. While I know many people may enjoy it, I feel a large number of people may also feel similarly to me, and a majority of the reviews neglect to point out the issues with single player and variety as a whole within the game.

I bought this game at launch and it runs very well.

If you're new to the genre then you have quite a lot to look forward to and if you're familiar with the Wargame series then this will all feel very familiar to you.

The tutorial is quite basic but it does go and teach you the mechanics of the game and pushes you to you combined arms, cover mechanics, surrender systems and more.

The game's different systems that they have used are a welcome change from the wargame series, the use of tiered vehicles and 3 phase system works quite well and adds quite a lot of strategy to an already intricate game.

The campaign provides a constant challenge and certain units from previous missions carry over to the next for you depending on how well you perfromed, the only downside here is that there are very few missions. 12 in total split between Allied and Axis.

The multiplayer is where this game really shines, it allows 1v1 games up to 10v10 games and communcation is key in everything! You can choose from either Allied or Axis decks and each side has a number of divisions to choose from that dictate the type of units you can bring to the field. Each division will have a focus e.g. infantry, mechanized or armored that will add unique units to their respective decks.
This allows quite a lot of customisation and different strategies to employ.

Overall it's a fantastic RTS with quite a lot of depth and challenge.

Beware a lot of the negative reviews from people in the wargame community that are upset that Eugen aren't adding any new content to that game (Wargame: Red Dragon released in April 2014) and the developers themselves commenting how they are constantly abused from particular community members regardless of what they do.
Relax, take your time, make some tea/coffee, let this game give you peace.

Игра отличная, но кампании очень короткие.

Фон Карштайны и Хаос очень простые. Если есть хоть какой-то опыт, то лучше брать очень тяжелый или легендарный уровень сложности. Дерево развития сформировано по разному, но по идее очень близки. У вампиров хочется чуть больше гражданских технологий. В обоих кампаниях важен старт, дальше само пойдет.

Гномы - отличная сбалансированная раса. Дерево развития прекрасно. Отсутствие кавалерии скорее фишка, чем недостаток. Вертолетики можно не строить. Очень эффективны, но не очень нужны. Стрелки отличные, пушки отличные.

Орки забавны, хотя копейшики гоблинов чересчур сильные для простейших воинов. Воинственность армии поддерживается достаточно просто, играется за них весело. Застройка городов очень и очень скучная. В паре ключевых городов строим что надо для армии, в остальных строим одно и то же.

Лесные эльфы в большой кампании, на мой взгляд, очень сложная и очень скучная раса одновременно.  Пустое дерево исследований. Скудная экономическая модель. Очень много времени тратиться на ожидание и восстановление армии, иметь много армий не получится из-за недостатка денег. Т.е. повоевать всласть не получится. Это особенно обидно, потому что юниты, особенно стрелковые, отличные. Сражения сами по себе за них интересные. Вся игра сводится к тому чтобы ни во что не лезть и ни с кем не конфликтовать.

Цари гробниц - очень забавная во всех отношениях раса. Количество армий расширяется через исследование. Это немного мешает на старте. Но отсутствие платы на содержание армий и их количество очень упрощает жизнь в финальной части кампании. Там где остальные расы ищут баланс между содержанием армий и доходом Цари могут пройти "зергом". Берем быстро воспроизводимые юниты, формируем максимальное количество армий, сливаем их и повторяем до победы. Дерево исследований на троечку. Много исследований делается за деньги. Количество героев также регулируется исследованиями. В целом играбельно, но возвращаться к ним не хочется.

İlk oyunu alıp hayran kalarak bitirmemin ardından 3 gün sonra bu ikinci oyunun çıkması ve an itibari ile tüm yan görevleriyle bitirmem... Her zaman görürdüm bu geri bildirim yapanların yazdığı "ilk kez bi' oyuna/filme/ürüne yorum yapıyorum" diye geri bildirim yapanları ve kesin bot falan diyerek okumazdım lakin bu oyun ve tabi ilki de olmak üzere mükemmel yani tanımlayacak kelime bulmak zor. Oldukça iyi iş çıkarmışlar. Bir üst seviyesi ne olur tahmin yürütemiyorum.

Her şeyden önce oyunda üstüne katarak ilerleme mantığının çevre tasarımına yayılması harika bir düşünce, tebrik ederim. Çevre tasarımı ve ışıklandırma kısacası ortam muazzam. Hele ki oyun bitiminde Kaynak Düzlüklerinin aldığı biçim, otur izle o derece ve tabi müzikler aslında ilk değinmem gereken buydu. Müzikler aşırı iyi oyun ile bütünleşmenizi sağlayan yegane etmen zaten bu müzikler. Uzatmak istemiyorum oyun neredeyse A'dan Z'ye mükemmel. 

Neredeyse kusursuz diyorum çünkü kusur olarak gördüğüm tek şey yeteneklerin kontrol mekanizması. İlk oyunda ki yetenekler bu oyuna kıyasla daha az olsa da karakteri kontrol ederken tüm yeteneklere tam hakimiyet sağlayabiliyorsunuz. Lakin bu oyunda yetenek ağacı dolayısıyla elde ettiğiniz yetenekleri 3 tuşa atayabiliyorsunuz ve ihtiyacınız olan yeteneği kullanmak için sürekli oyunda "Q" tuşu ile tuşlara yetenekleri atamanız gerekiyor. Bu durumdan dolayı oyun ilerledikçe elde ettiğiniz yetenek fazlalığından dolayı çok fazla dur kalk yapmak zorunda kalınıyor. Bu konu da nasıl bir çözüme gidilir bilmiyorum ama kesinlikle elden geçirilmesi şart.

Devam oyunu yapılırsa umarım aynı çizgi doğrultusunda bozmadan devam ederler. Oyun resmen bir sanat eseri.

[h1] To The Moon [/h1]
[i] "I never told anyone, but... I've always thought they were lighthouses." [/i]

Judgement: [u] Worth Full Price[/u]

Edit: Nominated for the “I'm Not Crying, There's Something In My Eye” Award, since it did make me cry, but surprisingly not till the day after. Everything's Alright is just a beautiful song, what can I say.

TL;DR
To The Moon is a short piece of interactive entertainment, that while not entirely a game, still manages to really get under your skin. It continues the trend (or supersedes the trend really, since this came out in 2011) of 2D, top-down, pixel-art games that focus more on story than interactivity.
And by God is the story worth it. Chances are you'll only get 4ish hours out of a straight run through it, and then maybe another hour with the mini-sodes that come as free DLC, but those 4 hours manage to pack quite the punch. 
If you can stand the art style, and are willing to overlook the lack of traditional game mechanics, you'll find yourself engrossed in one of the most human stories I've ever seen. If it's your first foray into more story focused stuff, it's a fantastic way to start, and even 5 years after its initial release, both the game and its soundtracks are absolutely worth buying at full price.

Soundtrack: [u] Worth Buying[/u]
Link to Purchase: https://freebirdgames.bandcamp.com/album/to-the-moon-ost

A 33-song soundtrack with a hefty focus on piano and chimes, it manages to be upbeat and heartfelt at times, and morose and foreboding at others. Clear standouts are all of the renditions of For River, and Everything's Alright, but [u] I highly advise not listening to any of the soundtrack before playing the game[/u]. The music manages to punctuate some of the moments you experience so well that you should let them be new to you when you first play the game.
Plus, the soundtrack is only $2.50 when you couple it with the game, and that's when it's not on sale. It's available for $5 on the creator's Bandcamp page, and 50% of the profits from that get donated directly to charity, so it's worth picking up no matter the avenue of purchase you choose.

Full Review:
I don't try to make it any secret that I appreciate stories about people more so than any other kind. Stories with far reaching implications or analogies to all sorts of things are great and all, but at the end of the day I can relate and engage most of all with stories about the struggles of individuals.
This can be made even stronger with good world building to go on top of that story, though. Some of my favorite games to be released in the past decade have had phenomenal worlds built inside them, with far reaching consequences, but which narrow their focus down to the people within them. Like how The Last of Us manages to create this incredibly beautiful and vivid vision of the end of the world, but at the end of the day is the story of a guy incapable of coping with loss. Or Bioshock Infinite, which manages to tie in multi-verse theory to create an incredibly complex narrative, but also shifts its focus away from the extra-dimensional and instead reflects on one self destructive guy who saw and did some really messed up stuff.
To The Moon does the same thing, to an extent. It gives itself this great setup that could be used for all sorts of things, and then just tells us the story of one guy on his deathbed.

If you haven't read the description for the game, then here's a little setup: Drs. Watts and Rosalene are professionals who specialize in fulfilling peoples dying wishes. They manage to achieve these things by going into the memories of their patients, and altering them so that they fulfill their wishes themselves, if only in their heads. So for our dear Johnny in To The Moon, the Doctors goal is to make him an astronaut. This is where we get our core gameplay loop, as they must start digging from the most recent memories available, and then skip backwards in time until they make it to the patient’s childhood. Then, like Inception in some ways, they will convince or push the patient towards achieving their dying wish themselves, and train to become an astronaut for instance.

That's all the setup you should need, and if you wanted more information on the games plot, I just encourage you to go play it, since it's only a 4-hour experience anyway.
To get back to the critique at hand, what To The Moon manages to do that impresses me more than anything else is how absolutely sincere it is in pretty much everything it does. A lot of Game Maker style things like this get churned out over time, and some of them end up being utter tripe because the developer didn't earnestly care about the story or game they were presenting, but you can tell that they really cared here. Every character feels like a person in their own right, and getting to know Johnny in this Benjamin Button esque journey through his memories manages to flesh out who exactly he is and how he thinks over time. Rather than exposition dumping anything on us, the game treats the player as an extension of our dear Doctors, whom would be getting to understand Johnny in the exact same way we are, as the reverse-time'd fly on the wall.
Really, I can't explain much of what this game does to really hit you without lessening the impact it will have. I guess that happens to be true with a lot of the things I end up reviewing, or it just happens that I end up reviewing things because they managed to surprise me so.
Look, this review is out about 5 years too late to the party, so the odds of anyone reading the TL;DR, let alone this part way down here are exceedingly low, so if you are still here, then good job and thanks, and also just go buy the game. There's around 23,000 reviews for it, and 97% of them agree with me that it is worth your time and money to experience.
Whether they believe it's as great as I do is uncertain, but if this many people think something is worth your time, it just might be.

To surmise, To The Moon is a beautiful piece of heartfelt art that manages to engross and entertain, and above all manages to connect to you. You'll laugh, you'll cry, and you'll probably finish it wanting more. Which you would happen to be in luck with since Finding Paradise, the sequel, is set to come out in the Summer of 2017, and follows Drs. Rosalene and Watts once more into the memories of another patient.

Link to Finding Paradise: http://store.steampowered.com/app/337340/?snr=1_5_1100__1100

Worth your $10, and absolutely worth your time, To The Moon is truly a special little gem, and you should probably just go buy and play it now.

Даже со старой видеокартой GeForce GTX 660 я играл с удовольствием, без каких-либо тормозов. Звуки и музыка в игре - отдельная тема для разговора, ибо это прекрасно! В процессе игры (выживания) можно и не понять, что на самом деле здесь есть сюжет. И причём какой! Достойный книги! Примерно в середине игры я было разочаровался, т.к. просто не знал что делать. Вроде всё исследовал (как мне казалось). Пришлось (да, каюсь) посмотреть в сети кто где какие места нашёл. И тут вот что выяснилось (у меня всегда с этим беда) - нужно ОЧЕНЬ ВНИМАТЕЛЬНО рассматривать не только всякого рода обломки, но и ВСЕ скалы и дыры. Ибо даже в огромном подземелье может находиться небольшой (но всё же заметный при нужной внимательности) вход в пещеру, где будет лежать "ключ" для дальнейшего прохождения. Ну и отдельное "ого!" для концовки игры! Эпично! Красиво! Музыкально! Захватывает! Я даже будто сам на себе почувствовал облегчение героя от того, что наконец удалось свалить с этой планеты! Но, в то же время, было жалко всё оставлять, ведь столько трудов было вложено, столько часов было потрачено на изучение подводного мира и эти все рыбки....ставшие друзьями....в общем, игра отличная!!! Я давно такого не встречал! Не то что советую, а настаиваю!!!!

Tales of Berseria is, at the moment, the best JRPG I've played. The combat is fluid and while it does seem like a button masher at first it does have some depth to it. You get several moves you can assign to your skillset in order to perform them, each enemy has aweakness so this makes it flexible to always be geared up in order to exploit enemy weaknesses to your hearts content. You can also change how your teammate AI works so they can perform as well as you desire.

On top of that you have Mystic Artes (special moves) which, unlike previous Tales games which required certain conditions to be met, are activated by pressing a button during a combo chain which makes them flow much better. The best part is that you can even chain all the Mystic Artes of your party members in one move. If you have a controller then activate your Mystic Arte by pressing L2 during a combo then hold L2 and press right on your D-Pad, press right again till your fourth character does it then while holding L2 press up on your D-Pad then down. Note that this switches out the last character with whoever you had in reserve.

The characters are one of the main highlights as well. It's refreshing to play as a group of anti-heroes, at best, or villans, at worst, who are all in it for themselves rather than your normal JRPG heroes who do it because they're either chosen or want to save the world. For Velvet, the main protagonist, revenge always comes first before anything else. The rest of the characters are pretty great too, plus the character development really gets you to root for them.

The story is based around revenge, it's not very complicated and doesn't try to derail itself either. My only complaint is that the final dungeon has a bit of needless padding. The design is a bit tricky at first however the main problem is that the dungeon also contains each characters most powerful Mystic Arte as well and to get them you have to find a key for each of them and use them on the correct entrance in the dungeon which leads to a bossfight after which you get a Mystic Arte for one of your characters. That feels like needless padding since it feels like they could have been given any other way as well.

All in all I'd recommend this if you like good characters and good combat and just JRPGs in general.

review: Щикарно,мазохиста мне в вагину

As background, i have played a lot of Total War and other strategy games, but this has definitely took my top place. Whilst it has it's little flaws, as any game will, it's just so beautiful and well executed.

The combat is a big draw to me too and i greatly enjoy creating strategies for different battles. Though sometimes nearer end game it can seem unfair and be a little frustrating having to micro manage multiple people against an army of AI that can simultaneously manage as many as they want. Though so long as you are careful (and sometimes with the aid of the pause), it doesn't dampen the experience at all.

The diplomacy is, of course, very heavily focused in this game and personally i think they pulled it off brilliantly. Nicely streamlined with simpler commands for quick deals and then more in depth options (such as Cao Cao's proxy war ability), which require slightly more finesse to pull off to your advantage..

I'm also a massive fan of the period and historical relevance; so having a game set like this really made me happy.

There are a few little issues that bug me, such as the auto-delegation (which usually means auto-defeat) boat battles. I wish they would either take the battle to the nearest land or input a boat battle system. Also little things like locks on certain kinds of weapons that can be equipped to generals. I would also like more uniques, but with time i am happy to see they are adding more and more.

Overall, even with it's little irritations, i think this is a fantastic game and would highly recommend. I am eager to see what else is put into this game and sink more hours into it.

Opera d'arte. Avviato per la prima volta il gioco mi sono venute in mente queste due parole. Non si può pensare ad altro di fronte ad un lavoro artistico del genere. Columbia è sbalorditiva, colorata e sopratutto piena di vita.
Come sempre, uno dei tratti distintivi di questa serie (oltre l'ambientazione), è la storia. Anche questa è curata nei minimi particolari, coinvolgente ed emotiva.
Dove secondo me il team di sviluppo si è superato, sono i personaggi secondari. Caratterizzati a dovere, sono convincenti e umani quanto basta, sopratutto nella loro crudeltà. Discorso a parte per Elizabeth: se non è il personaggio più bello da anni a questa parte, poco ci manca. Riesce a trasmetterti emozioni anche grazie a uno sguardo.
I combattimenti sono praticamente gli stessi dei primi due, con l'unica differenza che stavolta non ci sono i plasmidi ma i vigor come poteri speciali. L'IA è decente. Giocando a difficoltà massima si nota che principalmente più sono, più tendono ad aggirarti, ma niente di che.
La storia si conclude con uno dei finali più belli nella storia dei videogiochi a mio avviso.
Pro: storia, ambientazione fantastica, Elizabeth.
Contro: IA deficitaria, ripetitivo alla lunga, salvataggio manuale assente.

Mein Senf zu Dirt 4.
Dirt Rally war für mich ein Überraschungshit. Ich bin eigentlich mehr der Racer und weniger ein Rally-Fan, aber Dirt Rally hat das geändert. Eine so schöne und tolle Fahrphysik hatte ich vorher noch nicht erlebt (Thrustmaster T500RS + Gearshifter). Ich spiele sonst vor allem die Formel 1 Serie, aber Dirt hat wirklich gezeigt, wie unterschiedlich und trotzdem extrem fordernd der Motorsport auf seinem jeweiligen Gebiet sein kann.

Und nun kam Dirt 4. 9Gag zum Trotz habe ich es dennoch vorbestellt. Alle Fahrhilfen ausgeschaltet, Lenkrad aufgebaut und los geht´s. Wie es sich anfühlt? Genau wie Dirt Rally. Und das mochte ich sehr. "Never change a running system". Und während an der grundsätzlichen Struktur wenig verändert wurde, kamen kleine neue Extras hinzu, die mir sehr gut gefallen. Die erweiterten Rennserien, die neuen Fahrzeuge, die Fahrschule und der neue Karrieremodus mit seinem eigenen Team. I really love it. Es macht einfach nur Spaß. Die Grafik? Gefällt mir. Wem die Grafik hier nicht gefällt, dem gefiel auch Dirt Rally nicht. Und dann macht Dirt 4 irgendwie auch keinen Sinn. Den Casual Modus mit Controller oder sowas habe ich nicht getestet. Keine Ahnung ob es Einsteiger leichter fällt ins Spiel zu finden. Würde mich aber auch interessieren. Jedem das seine. 

Aber für jeden der aus ist auf eine knallharte und anspruchsvolle Rally-Simulation, die mehr bietet als sie vom Titel her verspricht, sollte hier zuschlagen. Und wer weiß, vielleicht sehen wir uns ja mal in der Bestenliste. Aber nur wenn ihr es nach oben schafft ;)

Après avoir passé plus de 250 heures sur Subnautica, je peux vous en parler en toute connaissance de cause…

Vous l’aurez compris, j’adore Subnautica qui nous donne un univers différent de ce que l’on connait en matière de survie. Au début, j’étais assez réticent à l’idée d’évoluer dans un univers sous-marin et finalement je suis agréablement surpris par les possibilités offertes par un tel espace !

Il est très intéressant d’évoluer dans les trois dimensions de l’espace et de trouver des choses à découvrir à des profondeurs différentes. À la gestion de la nourriture et de l’eau commune à tous les jeux de survie ou presque s’ajoute la gestion de l’oxygène.

On est un peu perdu dans les premières heures de mouvement tant il demeure vaste, mais très vite on retrouve ses marques. Nous détenons une petite capsule de survie très rudimentaire, mais très vite, on peut se construire une base impressionnante avec tout ce que l’on désire pour manger, boire, respirer, dormir, s’amuser, etc.

C’est un jeu d’exploration et vous devrez parfois passer quelques heures à trouver des éléments qui vous apparaitront nécessaires. Les crafts, mis à part les premiers déjà accessible devront être découvert en étudiant différentes pièces détachées des objets les composants pour les plus gros.

Tout cela oblige à la recherche et à la curiosité pour découvrir à la fois les différents plans, mais aussi les éléments vous qui vous permettront plus tard de construire selon vos besoins.

En évoluant dans le jeu, vous aurez la possibilité de produire vous-même votre nourriture, eau et même différents produits de base utiles pour le craft.

Subnautica est à mettre vraiment entre toutes les mains !

Vous pouvez y aller les yeux fermés, vous ne regretterez pas votre argent et je vous promets de longues heures de détente…

Each location in the town offers various things to unlock to increase the length of your runs. This is a game that will definitely give you the best bang for your buck in terms of value. You can also get some friends together and climb the tower together. Beating sections of the tower even give you shortcut bac, but even those aren't free. You still have to defeat waves of enemies while destroying a central cube to teleport to the next section. 

There's so much to praise about this game but I'll just wrap up and say I definitely would recommend this game to anyone who wants a little dungeon crawler.

The sheer amount of love, dedication and effort put in this game through the years should be more than enough to convince almost anyone interested to buy it. Luckily for those who remain doubtful, there's still much more to strengthen the case.

In essence, you are thrown into a beautifully crafted 2D world with nothing but your clothes and some basic equipment. From there onwards it's a riveting and ever expanding journey of discovery and growth. A huge randomly generated world awaits you, filled with different biomes, ever-changing weather, countless and diverse monsters to fight and a bunch of secrets for you to uncover. The possibilities are really astounding, both in the amount of things you can craft and build as in the extensions available for you to explore. There's also a nice storyline, materialized in a series of simple events to be performed and bosses to be defeated to push the game forward. But the really mesmerizing part is the whole universe that surround and enriches that fairly basic premise.

Everything you see in the screen at anytime can by the end of the game be literally destroyed and rebuilt at will. The world is yours to craft and terraform at your heart's content, and in this aspect Terraria offers limitless hours of amusement for those creative enough to enjoy its possibilities. Want a basic not at all fancy house? Well, even for the simplest one you can indulge in multiple styles of furniture and building blocks with different crafting requirements. And not even to mention if you want to go all architectural and pompous in your designs and level of detail. The amount of tools and elements put at your disposal, whether you wanna use them or not, is simply astounding, but you never get it forcefully shoved down your throat if it's not your cup of tea and you'll rather keep it simple. To top it all off, there's a nice cast of NPC characters to meet and special events that can be triggered to add some extra flavor. And, yes, a fishing minigame built in. For when you just wanna sit back and relax.

Rounding things up, the game also looks and sounds really great. The soundtrack, even at close to 300 hours of gametime, hasn't got the least tiring, being of great quality and with an astounding variety of themes. It complements the world perfectly, changing according to biome, event or boss fight to make sure it never gets even near to boring you. Combat is also nicely done, with great diversity of weapons and different styles to master, each with favored equipment for optimal results.

Overall, I honestly think Terraria is a must have in any gamer's library. And for the amount of content you get, it's even cheap as hell.

In recent time, just like with Skyrim, I've seen quite a lot of people bashing this game as if it's not good in any aspect. This mostly came to a head thanks to Fallout 76, which quite frankly isn't/wasn't good, so I get it. Every once and a while you've just got to lash out at something. But my history with this game since its launch can be best described as a bumpy road of emotions, and after seeing people very recently still bashing the game like they did when 76 came out, and seeing that Skyrim review I wrote out just a bit ago, I decided I should write one out for this game too. I mean, it's only fair. And I think it's best to begin with my history with the game.

I got this game a couple days after it came out, and I originally bought it on Xbox One as my computer at the time had absolutely no hope of running the game. I had a completely vanilla experience, and did a couple different playthroughs before moving on to PC. That "bumpy road of emotions" I mentioned earlier is essentially how I came to enjoy this game the way I do today, and I think it's and important part of this review. The first two times I played the game I did two different endings as well as Automatron and Far Harbor. I still enjoyed the game very much by this point, but was sort of losing steam as the hype train usually does. But it was when Bethesda announced and later released Nuka World that I became, well, to put it bluntly, pretty pissed off. I was very unhappy with the fact that every DLC in the game's history was released before the game itself was even a full year old. It was incredibly disappointing to me, but ultimately I got over it. I later came to believe that it wasn't as good as Fallout 3, but I've since changed that stance. There's a reason why I didn't call it a roller coaster of emotions, because it's not quite as crazy and full of twists and turns or anything, but it brings me to my next point. I genuinely believe that Fallout 4 is better than Fallout 3 now. You're free to disagree with me, of course, but honestly I don't even intend on going into much detail with that point due to my limited memory of the latter. Instead, I will tell you of the reason why Fallout 4's story is not nearly as a bad as people make it out to be.

After having played the game enough times and experienced each faction pretty thoroughly, at least I'd say so, I've come to realize something about the game. It strikes me very much as a story about personal morals more than anything else. Let me explain. When you play through the game you have four different factions to choose from for your ultimate ending choice. The Minutemen (which are around no matter what so I don't really count them), the Brotherhood of Steel, the Railroad, and the Institute. As you play through the quests and finish the game with the latter three you come to learn more and more about them, their ideals, the opinions and beliefs of its members, the good and bad things they've done, many things like that. But no matter what it is, everyone has a favorite out of these factions, the one they identify or agree with the most. Mine is personally the Brotherhood of Steel, because I have personally decided that Synths really are just perversions of technology and shouldn't exist for the most part. However, there are plenty who would disagree with my viewpoint and call the Brotherhood evil, which brings me to what exactly I'm getting at here. No matter which faction you choose (save for the Minutemen) it will always be your choice based on your own chosen set of morals. It will be what you perceive to be the best, and you've decided that for yourself. 

A pet peeve of mine when it comes to everyone's favorite Fallout game, New Vegas, is that the karma system is there to tell you whether something you did was good or bad. I've always thought this was a weird system because often times I would do something in the game that wouldn't seem like it was really bad, but the game would tell me I lost some karma for doing it. Or as a more broad example, by siding with Caesar's Legion you essentially gain the animosity of every other faction and various character in the game such as Arcade Gannon. The game flat out tells you that you're siding with the bad guys by making you the enemy of literally every faction that can be perceived more as the good guys. That's not to say the Legion or the NCR aren't complex or nuanced or anything, I've just never understood the need for the game to tell you through the karma system that what you're doing is good or bad. That should be something you have to figure out and decide on for yourself. And that's very much why I love the factions of Fallout 4. Without the karma system in place, the closest thing you have is the opinions of the various companions you can travel with. My first time playing through the game I chose to side with the Brotherhood of Steel, and by the end of the main story I wasn't quite sure if I had made the right choice. I doubted that I went with the right side. This was supported when I found out the opinions of some of my favorite companions in the game. Over time, after playing all of the other factions, I've decided that I agree with and believe in the Brotherhood the most out of any of the available choices, but the fact alone that I felt doubt the first time I finished the main story of the game speaks a lot about how the game can mess with your morals and beliefs, at least I think that's the case.

When you look beneath the surface of each faction you come to find good and bad things about them. The Brotherhood isn't exactly the nicest, and the Institute isn't exactly the worst. But that's what makes it interesting to choose a side. You are unsure which would be the best choice, which you, yourself, think is right or wrong, good or bad. There's a reason why the actual nature of each faction is still talked about today. And I feel like Far Harbor plays on this concept of personal morality as well. Should the Synths of Acadia be wiped out? Should DiMA answer for the things he's done? If he does, the factions of the Island will never find a mutual peace. You are ultimately the one to decide which of these three factions are more deserving of existence or are simply more right than the other, and the only option that results in all three finding peace occurs only after DiMA does something he is so against that the last time he did it he literally pulled that memory from his head. Morals really push the story forward, and without a karma system present it's completely up to you to decide which you identify with more than the others. This concept of morality to me is what adds complexity and nuance to the main story, and the Far Harbor story. And ultimately that's my biggest reason for why Fallout 4 is a good game with a good story.

As always, you are free to agree or disagree, I cannot tell you what to think. But I would ask one thing of the people who may be reading this. Please don't act as if ANY of these games are bad if you like even one of them. Fallout 3 and Fallout 4 both have amazing things about them, some of which can't be seen on the surface. Rather than focusing on the things you don't like about them, focus on the things you do like. That doesn't mean ignore what you dislike as if it isn't there, but simply enjoy what you like rather than set your mind towards what you consider negatives. Every game is enjoyed more that way.

Is it fun? Depends on how you're playing. Official servers probably aren't worth your time, unless you have unlimited time and a mega tribe. It's best with a group of friends on a private or public unofficial server, IMO. There are plenty of great mods out there, too.

PvP on official servers probably isn't worth your time unless you have a mega tribe. Just buy Mordhau - It's half the price, and the PvP is infinitely more accessible.

Is the combat good? Not really. Out of any $60 game, this one has the worst combat I've experienced. The combat is pretty much just getting hit and knocked back. Feels pretty lazy, at least for a $60 title. If the game was $15 and in beta, this would be closer to acceptable.

There are dinos that can steal thousands of pounds of resources from you and run away, and they're the size of a small dog. Finally got that perfect level 150 wyvern egg that weighs 120 pounds? Too bad, a seagull stole it from you and ate it in 1 second. The devs cannot differentiate between fun, challenging, and purely annoying.

Dino pathing is pathetic. Out of any $60 game, this game has the worst AI pathing that I have witnessed. Dinosaurs do not behave like dinosaurs. They will easily become stuck on trees, rocks, and other small objects. Oh, are you trying to tame this horse? Well too bad, it ran away from you and jumped off a cliff that's 150 feet high because it was just cool with that fall. Oh, are you trying to tame this horse on the beach? Well too bad, it ran away from you and straight into the ocean and got eaten by sharks, because we've all seen horses do that before in real life, right? This has been a glaring problem since early access, and was not (and probably won't ever be) fixed when the game "left early access" and doubled its price to $60. It's probably above the dev's skill level to fix.

You can't walk over small ledges. You cannot lift yourself over a small ledge; you need a climbing pick to climb at all. You cannot slow your fall using vertical walls like in Conan Exiles. If sprinting, the terrain is pretty unforgiving. The game tends to just... fling you. It's not overwhelmingly common, but it's enough to be annoying. It's probably above the dev's skill level to fix.

I don't know how this game left early access and its $30 price tag. There are plenty of moments for fun, but the onslaught of bullshit you have to deal with brings this game down, big time - and unfortunately the devs have only made it worse by adding annoying dinos and not fixing bugs or pathing.

Don't get me wrong, ARK can be lots of fun - if you can find a way to play it that suits you. Don't plan on the devs fixing the parts of the game that obviously need to be fixed, though. They'd rather make money than a good game.
