To start, I wanna say that I played every single Fallout Game there is. All of them. And I completely agree, that Fallout 4 is more or less a failure if you compare it with previous titles. If you take a look at the game alone, it is okay.

Though I do not recommend buying the Workshop DLCs. They don't offer any noteworthy content except maybe for Vault-Tec (But only if you like building a Vault. I didn't.). The Workshop stuff is just a sick joke. Moneymilking, nothing more. Grab the Main Game and maybe the three "Story"-DLCs. Far Harbor, Nuka-World and Automatron. Only reason to buy them is because some Mods require them. For everything else see to your modding needs on the Nexus. Not only are there many fixes (for example new textures, that are ten times better than Bethesdas. They look good AND they also increase performance), but also good standalones (new Power Armors and Sounds).

Another tip, don't waste your money on the creation club. Most of the stuff in their is again just a Joke compared to the money you pay for it. Free mods have done it all better again.

Now. One thing I do want to add. I was really hyped for the Settlement-building at first, but it quickly gets very tedious. Radiant quests don't help making your life any easier. Go to the Nexus to find a fix for that. There are a ton of Settlement Mods. This way you can, for example choose one Settlement where you personally build, and the rest can be built automatically or after a prefab. You can also find a Mod to get rid of many of the Radiant quests.

As you can probably see already from my review, FO4 is quite a bit of work. Usually Bethesda Games get modded to fix a few things and add new stuff. This time it is all about making the game enjoyable. Like fixing the dialogue so I know what my char is really gonna say. In the end, I think the Game is okay. But not any better. My Recommendation is to only buy the game on a Sale with at least 50% off.

TL:DR
Game is okay. Needs a lot of Mods to be really enjoyable. Don't waste money on Workshop-DLCs. Only buy the three main DLCs. Ignore Creation-Club, instead use Nexus (Also has a handy Mod Manager). Best to buy game on a Sale with at least 50% off.

This is easily the best title on steam under $10.  

If you enjoy fast paced boss battles, building, farming and fishing, engaging combat with 4 different styles that feel significantly different, or taking your time to explore every nook and cranny of a procedurally generated world, you will like Terraria.  It starts out slow for anyone who is inexperienced in this type of game to get a hold of it and builds on difficulty in a great curve.  More experienced players can even skip bosses to take on more challenging content to progress faster.  The most experienced players will even still find challenge in Expert mode in vanilla and harder difficulties employed by mods.

The game never feels unfair in it's difficulty, so long as you're geared properly for the area you are in, the game gives you ample leeway in normal difficulty. Optionally potions are available to make the game even easier, albeit requiring more time investment in the passive gameplay aspects of farming herbs and fishing.  In expert difficulty the game is ramped up significantly, but also includes exclusive rewards to people who are good enough at the game.

Along with the procedural generation the game also includes a few world exclusive randomization.  The evil biome may pick between two different forms in the corruption or crimson, each with their own obstacles and rewards.  Each basic and moderate ore type may select between two variants, with each being similar in strength but slightly different in stats and effects.

One of the most interesting features of this game is that player characters are saved separate from generated worlds.  Allowing you to use a single character on multiple different worlds allowing the transportation of items between these worlds.  This includes being able to join in your friend's worlds with your own character from single player, keeping your inventory(and any player exclusive inventories such as piggybank, safe, and forge.) 

This game easily has hundreds of hours of content and after a few hiatuses it's still being updated.  Not to mention a thriving modding community.

对不起我只是点个好评而已，以下的部分没有评测看游戏好不好玩的请转其他评论。

看了很多差评气得想怼人。
这游戏数值已经够谨慎了而且很好理解，不知道为啥还会有很多“从出门起难得一比”“感觉敌人每高一级都强很多而玩家根本没没变强”之类的奇妙言论。如果玩一个满级几乎只有10级的游戏还要求可以像其他rpg游戏一样可以出门练级属性爆炸然后一刀一只怪体验爽快感打怪靠撵主要看剧情的话建议您换个游戏呢，这款游戏本来就是不是为您准备的。
换言之我承认了上述言论（指敌人疯狂变强玩家没变化这种说法）确实描述了事实，但是这款游戏正是基于如此需要玩家自行寻找解决方法，而一部分人就“什么？我升级了莽不过同级怪？垃圾游戏。”我不知道该怎么喷=x=您走吧，别留言了好吗。

如果真的有人看到这里了请允许我为您道歉。
简单来讲这款游戏是一款比较偏回合制RPG精髓的游戏，游戏性很高数值也很精巧，当然了。随机性也很令人蛋疼，毕竟有命中率的RPG游戏都是玩家与数值的博弈。这款游戏的剧情毫无亮点，画风有特点但不算精巧，一切的好玩之处都是与游戏中数值的博弈，当然，在此之上加入了朋友之间的互动。一帮热衷于此的朋友玩起来可以很开心，如果并不热衷于此，请安心选择简单模式，可以给你更大的容错范围。以上，感谢，以及道歉。

追加说一些东西的话，这款游戏依旧是一款互动＞游戏性的游戏。其游戏性如我上述所说集中的地方非常偏颇而且考验运气，而且重复游玩性往往体现在“和不同的人一起玩”而不是“这个游戏值得再玩一遍”。因此其反复游玩部分的学识商店内容也是令人难以满意，你无法通关时无法获得多少学识去购买东西，你通关一次了它反复通关时为你新增的东西不足以提供全新的体验……可以说是很神秘的恶性循环，但又不那么致命。毕竟重点在玩家与玩家的交流互动上嘛？

Although clunky in places, hard to figure out in others; Avorion is easily one of the best blends of 4X and ship building games *ever* made.

You will find yourself either mining away, killing pirates or trading early on, then eventually (if you choose to do so) Destroy entire factions or build an empire of sprawling stations and supply chains, in order to reach the core (the main objective of story) you will likely be in an arms race to find better turrets and components in order to beef up one or several large capital ships to take on the most powerful enemies in the galaxy!

The ability to make ships and download more from the workshops to customize; you ship, your fighters, your turrets and even your stations makes this an amazing immersive sandbox to build the sci-fi faction of your dreams. 

Play online with a few friends and really share the challenges of rewards by forming an alliance, more easily attain goals as a group than as an individual.

While the game have some scuffs and flaws, to me are namely UI inconsistencies, predictable AI and events, even understanding them does not take away too much from the game if you look past them. But there definitely are some moments that I find frustrating and grueling when moving AI ships around and navigating the galaxy map where the fix for these problems would simply to add one more contextual button here or shortcut key there.

As for the ship editor, it's easy to make ships, harder to make beautiful ships, but definitely accessible to anyone with enough patience to learn the tools. It is certainly not as intuitive as other first person crafting game but much MUCH more powerful. You can make great looking design in a few hours each that you'll be proud of. Just need to take the time to learn things like scaling/grid size/mirroring selection/copy/paste features. Watch videos on the subject or start toying around, its quite fun to master!

As far as overall assessment:
Is it perfect? No
Is it pretty? Yes
Is it fun? Yes
Is it addicting? Yes, Yes, Yes!

I found myself player over 100h within the first few weeks of buying the game, well worth the investment and I still haven't reached any plateau where I can't progress in some direction, I have yet to even mine the 2 rarest resources, have only a few legendary modules/turrets to my name and barely starting building my own stations, and I can't wait to get back to it.

The game deserves an easy 8/10 --- Fully recommend! Would give it 9/10 in the future is there are some UI and control improvements applied to fix some of these less fun problems.

Certe le gameplay change, cela ma perturbé aux début , mais on s'y fait vite et j'y ai pris goûts.
Je vais commencer par les points négatifs de ce FF XV
-Les magies d'élément tel que Brasier , Glacier , Foudre sont présente avec une association d'altération d'état ou de boost possible.
Donc finis les Ultimas , Meltdown , Boomrang etc...
-Les invocations : Sans Spoils , vous ne pourrez pas choisir quand vous voudrez invoquer votre G-force / Dieu , et qui invoquer , je n'en dis pas plus.
-Quelque quêtes relou , mais franchement il y en a dans tout les jeux...
-La Regalia , la voiture , putain c'est un veau , elle dépasse pas les 40km/h non modifier.
-L'histoire se finis rapidement malheureusement malgrès les DLCs qui se finissent eux aussi très rapidement.
-Même en ayant une bête de course, j'ai des grosses chute d'FPS à certains endroits.
-Le mode Online DEAD , dommage car il est vachement cool , je l'ai soloter et c'est largement faisable

Et les points positifs:
-Les persos : je m'y suis attaché de suite , chacun a son histoire , son passé , sa fonction , son caractère bref , c'est une très bonne bande de pote avec chacun leurs charismes allant de la joie à la tristesse ils sont justes , waw.
-Pouvoir controler plusieurs des protagonistes
-Le monde
-L'histoire bien que courte
-La bande son qui nous régale , j'ai les OST dans ma biblio hehe
-Les plats !!!! (je suis un gros porc)
-La gueule de certains perso / Daemons
-Nouveau système de combat plus énergique , un peu de renouveau n'a jamais tué, je trouve que c'est une bonne chose.
et certainement d'autre point que j'ai oubliés mais franchement vu le prix qu'il vaut , n'hésitez surtout pas.
J'ai vu des personnes dire qu'ils étaient répétitif niveau combat / quêtes mais en soit c'est exactement la même que dans certains  FF.

Bref si vous n'avez pas peur foncez !

Fallout 4 is a game that took me some time to come to terms with, after being a fan of the series for some time I had certain expectations for this new shiny sequel, these expectations were not met. Modernisation and streamlining for profits and appeasal of a larger mainstream audience has killed a lot of what makes Fallout so special, although it still gets my wholehearted recommendation as the big beautiful mess that it is.
 
The largest problem I had with FO4 is it's new dialogue system, you are now limited to four options because there are four buttons on a standard gamepad, seriously, Bethesda, I see what you were trying to do there but it is just wrong, you could have at least had them change based on the characters S.P.E.C.I.A.L.'s, which don't seem to matter at all apart from charisma. On top of this the dialogue options are summarised as a few words, which doesn't seem like a problem until you choose that option and your avatar says something along those lines but with completely different implications, this is just sloppy game design.

Number 2 on the list is the way in which S.P.E.C.I.A.L. is implemented, for a start where have skills went to? Across the Fallout series individual skills have been subject to change but never has it been streamlined until the point it no longer exists. Your more integral skills like hacking and picklocking have been shoved into a perk tree, this I suppose makes it more user friendly but in a way that kind of insults the target audiences intelligence, yeah skills is gonna be too many numbers for those idiots lets just give them an animated vault boy doing a dance on a chart and call it a day, yeah, that's much better. To be fair this is probably preferable to the average gamer, and the new system isn't at all terrible and does a pretty good job at maintaining a sense of development throughout the game, but it just doesn't hold up to it's predecessors for there ability at actually making your character special.

Something I actually liked about FO4 was it's settlements, although your settlers could easily be beaten in chess by a tamagotchi  and have as much personality as cardboard flavoured toothpaste, the settlements still give you a way to change something in the world. On my main character I've been building up each settlement to be well fortified and comfortable to live in for my settlers, who have also been supplied with combat armor and rifles. Although they are flat characters that don't even get dialogue options the way in which I have been allowed to invest my time and interact with them has allowed me to create the illusion that they are more. This is good game design.

Lastly, I want to talk about what makes Fallout what it is, and that is it's very unique and quirky setting. Luckily this has been left mostly intact in FO4, although in some areas the world felt lacking of detail, but in others there are some genuine surprises. Normally I don't bother with companions but the additional perks gainable by maxing out relationships had the inner completionist in me cycle through them all, each have their own relatively deep backstories and quests, I highly recommend trying a few of them out, my personal favourite ended up being Cait, my main and her are now the celebrity couple of the Commonwealth.

Okay so great, I got into a bit of a rant there but that's where I'm going to leave it. Overall Fallout 4 is still at it's heart a Fallout game but the gameplay has changed quite significantly with this iteration, it is sad to see something so special change the way it has but we must accept it the best we can and move on, this is in my opinion not game of the year material but it is a very enjoyable experience.

I had high hopes for this game but so far, it's letting me down. Over the course of time that i have played this game, i've ran into several problems that just don't seem to be getting adressed. i understand, that the community wants more guns, skins and other goodies in game. but i do feel the dev team should focus more on creating a stable enviornment for ALL players, rather than content at the moment. Here's what i think needs work the most:

Hit Registration- This is something that has frustrated me since i first started playing the game. it's absolutely ridiculous that any player should die due to shots not being registered. it ruins the fun, and kills immersion. I've ran into several occasions where i had the drop on enemy players, riddle them with bullets only for them to turn around, completely fine, and one shot me with a shotgun. it was kinda funny at first, but now it's just gotten old. 

Poor Match Making- i know i'm not the only one to experience this problem, and i believe it to be an issue because it unbalances the game. I've joined many matches only to find that when it's time to drop, i'm paired with only 1 or 2 guys during a 4 man squad match. Hell, sometimes i even end up completely alone. It happens even more so if you play with your friends and not strangers. That's now how a matchmaking system should be designed. if you are already at a dis-advantage as soon as you join the lobby, then what's the point of even continuing?

Poor Optimization- this is pretty self explanatory, but a problem none the less. i understand the game will not run the same across all platforms, but there is clearly a problem when my PC can run most games faster than a raped ape on bath salts, yet, even at the lowest settings, this game still runs slower than a one legged turtle on sedatives.

Crashes, Crashes, Crashes- the game is in alapha, i get it. but this game crashes more than i do driving cars in game. Not to mention, they are completely random. I'll crash at the home screen, in the plane, as soon as i touch the ground, as soon as i start the game, when i get into fire-fights, when i drive cars and the list goes on and on. 

PC locking freezes- i'm not sure how many people experience this, but it's a problem that i face sometimes. on occasion, the game will completely freeze. and it's not just the game, it's EVERYTHING. i am unable to alt tab out, or even use task manager to close the game. usually, i have to force restart my PC just so i can use it again. it's pretty frustrating.

Certain Commands Not Working- i'm not sure how many people experience this either, but on occasion ill find that certain keys don't work anymore. Sometimes i cant get into cars, sometimes i cant reload, sometimes i can crouch or go prone, sometimes i can't peek left or right. Mind you, i haven't remapped my keyboard at all. the charcter simply won't perform any of the animations it's supposed to. it's like i'm not pressing the keys at all. It's super annoying and has gotten me killed several times.

There's a lot more i could probably add to this list. but these are the biggest issues i could think of. i understand completely that the game is still in alpha. I understand that these are all things that could change over the course of time. i understand that these are all my opinions and that not everyone will experience the game the way i have. That being said. is PUBG a bad game? No, it certainly isn't. it's good fun and it's a game that i enjoy most of the time. However, when i'm having a bad time is usually because of the issues mentioned above.

i still look forward to the development of the game, there are a lot of good things about the game. but right now, i think the bad is what the devs should be focusing on.

Nach über 300 Stunden gibt es immer noch neue Herausforderungen! Terraria ist ein unglaublich liebevolles und in sich stimmiges Spiel, die Pixelgrafik stimmt einfach und schafft eine schöne Retro-Ästhetik in der man sich sofort zu Hause fühlt. 
Dazu kommt aber ein modernes Gameplay welchem es an Bossen nicht fehlt. Diese haben einen guten Schwierigkeitsverlauf und werden auch in ihren Phasen komplexer.
Der Spielverlauf wird generell für ein Open-World Spiel gut erklärt bzw. forciert. Man fängt mit wenigen Möglichkeiten an und orientiert sich an den NPCs, von denen immer mehr auftauchen je mehr man im Spiel geschafft hat. Dadruch ergeben sich wieder neue Möglichkeiten und Herausforderungen, denn Bosse werden freigeschaltet etc.
Das eigentlich Spiel beginnt erst im "Hardmode", der keinen seperaten Modus darstellt sondern die Welt härter und unwirklicher macht. Neue Monster und Bosse erscheinen und dazu verändert sich die Welt massiv durch neu-spawnende Biome. 
Im Gegensatz zu z.B. Minecraft, wo der Fokus eher auf Überleben und Aufbauen liegt, setzt Terraria mehr auf Content über Zeit. Es gibt tausende detailiert gestaltete Objekte im Spiel, hunderte Waffen und dutzende Armor-Sets. Dennoch kommt der Kreative Teil nicht zu kurz. Durch einige Tricks schaffen es die Entwickler dass die zwei Ebenen beim Bauen nicht stören, es ist vielmehr 2.5D denn es gibt eine Hintergrundebene und Layer für Verkabelung.

Der Multiplayer funktioniert immer flüssig und macht Spaß, teilweise sind Bosse auch erst dann schaffbar ohne sich einen Tag lang alleine vorzubereiten. Schwerer wird das Spiel übrigens nicht mit wachsender Spieleranzahl.

Terraria ist für mich DAS ultimative und einzige 2D Open-World Spiel denn mittlerweile ist es der Perfektion sehr nahe. Jedes Pixel ist bedacht platziert und wird auch einem OCD-ler Freude machen. Liebevolle Gestaltung, Content für hunderte Stunden und durchdachte Bedienkonzepte machen Terraria einfach zu einem Must-Have auf dem PC/Mac, den man sich auch außerhalb eines Sales kaufen kann.

The single player campaign is good, but without modding doesn't offer much replayability (without completing slightly repetitive side-missions).  The bulk of this game's content updates and support comes to GTA Online.  This is a complete mess: from long queue times to join others for a mission, to finding stable connections in freemode.  Online lobbies are peer-to-peer and full of hackers/cheaters.  The economy is so out of whack that it will take a new player (with no access to offices, buy/sell missions, heists, etc) 20 hours to unlock a single car.  Upgrades can cost just as much (if not more than) the starting price of the vehicle itself.  The expectation from Rockstar here is for you to grind repetitive content for hours like an MMO, without offering the depth or progression of an MMO.  Content is very widespread, which seems like a positive at first.  But each chunk of missions and unlocks ends up disappointingly shallow.  I only recommend this title for its single player, and even then only to players who have not yet played this game.  Otherwise, you're not missing out on much if you're looking to play online with others.

Well, I've had this now for a couple months, and, I have to say, that some of the great things that were in HOI3, are no longer present.  The echlon system that was as true to any command system in a game -that I've ever seen, has been replaced with a "pick a commander-and his rank/skill determines how many divisions he can control" system.  No More Theater, Group on down to Corps commanders.  Instead of refining that, they removed it.  Now you just have x amount of divisions and call it an army.  What is more frustrating is that the updated core productivity systems and unit building has been improved and really is on the edge of greatness, and if, that had been combined with an improved echleon system from HOI3, you would've had a knock-out fantastic game.  Unfortunately what you really have here now, is spagetti at times, spagetti that is hard to get your fork to keep on it, I start playing game after game, only to be bored by the new unit-commander system, that is more like loading men into the units of EUIV or CK2.  And, the production and historic choices are fun, but then, finally when it's time for battle, you find out just how flawed the battle AI is.  It just makes no sense.  They seemed to want to dumb this game down in the unit area, and smart it up in the productivity, so what you get is an ironic up and down...yes, the productivity and research has been improved.  The front and offensive, defensive lines seem alright IF you play a major power.  After you get into it, it is fun and interesting.  But, what I'm saying is they took out a major pluses of HOI III, and hopefully, will bring an option in a patch or mod somewhere to bring it back, and also improve the AI.  Please don't make me wait for HOI V.  The time in between III and IV was unbearable!

Hunt Showdown is really unique and one of the most intense and atmospheric multiplayer games I've ever played. It contains both PVE and PVP and while I'm usually not a big fan of those kind of games, it does work really good in this one.

The sound design is truly tremendous and one of my favourtite things about it. You can hear how animals and monsters react to your own and other players movements and actions in the environment. Also there are some kind of cans, shards and other stuff that can reveal your presence.

In every match there are ten players on the map, looking to find one of the boss monsters. If you beat the monster you have to banish it and extract the dropped bounty tokens to one of the three random exit points. The main concept of the game sounds quite simple and I was worried that it would get boring quite fast, but I was so wrong. It enables you to play a lot of different tactics, and also it doesn't force you to do anything, you can leave via one of the exit points anytime. 

Player engagements in Hunt are really intense and often keep my heart beating faster because if you die, you loose your hunter with all the gained perks and weapons. It can easily take up to five minutes or even more from the first visual contact to one teams dead. In rare cases one team also might just disengage and try to escape to not lose their progress.

You can play with one friend or solo, but you'll always be matched together as there are no different playlists for different amounts of players, so you shouldn't play alone as you will have a huge disantvantage.

I really didn't expect me to like this game as much as I do now, but I fucking love playing it and it turned out to be my best purchase in 2018.

This is an amazing "medieval simulator" which im REALLY surprise by how well it runs. The realistic approach to gameplay make for one of the most immersive RPG i've played to date. The story is fantastic, as are the characters.

BE READY THOUGH. This is now Skyrim. This is its own thing. You'll need time to learn the mechanics, master them, and that will take a lot of time. Not only is the story long (I've heard some people take upward to 100h), but also you'll spend a lot of time just roaming around, figuring stuff out, practice sword fighting, bow, upping your skills, playing dice... Man there's a lot to this game.

This is almost a sandbox, where you're left alone in an unforgiving medieval world. Your actions matters, what you wear matters, what you says matters. Heck, how long you take to do something ALSO matters (only sometimes, don't feel rushed) This is an amazing experience i recommand to anybody looking for a good RPG unlike any other.

Now i will say that the combat is absolutely frustrating at times, especially in 1v2+. Mainly because the locking mechanism is garbage. Luckily you can "switch target" by pressing TAB, which does help a bit, but still. I'd rather just flick my mouse on the side to select the target i want.

In any case, the positive outshine the negative by FAR. Get ready for an amazing experience.

Ainsi s'achève Assassin's Creed Origins après 70h de jeu (Ne comptait pas plus de 100h contrairement à ce que disent la plupart des gens pour le finir à 100% sans speedrunner...).

 J'ai été très agréablement surpris par ce jeu, autant que lorsque j'avais découvert le tout premier 10 ans avant. 

 Ce jeu est magnifique à en chialer, malgré ma petite GTX 660 (60fps mais en moche), le jeu est sublime! J'ai passé énormément de temps à contempler les étendues de sable ainsi que le Nil, les villes, les forêts etc...

 La map est très grande aussi, ce qui vient amplifier la force des graphismes et du réalisme apportée à ceux-ci. Si je prends l'exemple d'une région, le désert blanc: à l'aube le sable est jaune pour devenir orange au crépuscule et enfin devenir légérement bleuté la nuit. C'est juste époustouflant, et ça s'applique à toutes les régions. Il m'arrive aussi d'être époustouflé lorsque du phare d'Alexandrie, j'aperçois au loin les pyramides et que du haut d'une montagne je vois le Nil. Franchement, Ubisoft a fourni un travail exemplaire de ce côté-la.

 Au niveau de l'histoire et du scénario ainsi que des quêtes (tout le monde dit qu'elles sont scénarisées...), c'est... Mouaif. Disons que le début est lent et que l'histoire n'avance pas vite, en plus d'être un poil répétitive... Heuresement, les choses deviennent VRAIMENT intéressantes à partir de l'acte 3-4. Concernant les quêtes secondaires, certes la GRANDE MAJORITE des quêtes (et pas toutes) sont scénarisées, et parfois on recroisera des personnages. Mais par contre, au bout de la 100 éme quête, ça se répéte un peu et les dialogues se répétent tous, mais c'est normal vu la quantité de quêtes différentes qu'il y a; sur ce point c'est tout bénéf (SAUF LES QUETES AVEC LES ENFANTS ELLES SONT ATROCES).

 D'ailleurs en parlant des dialogues, la VF est excellente, et celle de Bayek est INCROYABLE! C'est un vrai plaisir pour les oreilles d'entendre un acteur qui se donne à fond dans son rôle. Lorsqu'il est énervé, on le sent, et c'est que du bonheur. De plus, la majorité des dialogues  sont plaisants car ils ont l'air naturels, et pas de simples textes récités par les acteurs. Couplés aux bruits environnants, c'est parfait.

 Ce qui nous amène à la musique: elle est bien mais sans plus, on reconnaît le thème de l'antiquité, et on ressent le lien entre ces musiques et les musiques d'autres AC (principalement par le thème). Par contre, y'en a pas beaucoup, et lors des scénes un peu dramatiques, ben c'est dommage qu'il y en ait pas (la plupart du temps...).

 Enfin, AC Origins se démarque par sa refonte de combat et son côté RPG plus assumé. Concernant le combat, il est plutôt bien réussi, et quand on donne un coup, on a VRAIMENT l'impression de frapper quelqu'un, on a un bon ressenti. Je crois qu'il y a environ 5 modes de combat, chacuns avec leurs éxécutions et leurs combos, ce qui varie le tout, mais vous allez sans doute en préférer 1 ou 2 et souvent les utiliser, et ça devient un peu répétitif à force, mais c'est assez plaisant tout de même.
 Les arcs sont eux aussi diversifiés, et ça part un peu en couille à ce niveau là (l'arc normal, l'arc sniper, l'arc mitraillette, l'arc fusil à pompe...).

 Concernant le côté RPG, on a l'inventaire qui est bien organisé et facile à utiliser (en plus d'être beau) qui permet vraiment de personnaliser Bayek. De plus on a les compétences, divisées en 3 parties.
 Ya pas mal de compétences, mais une bonne moitié ne sert à rien (gagne 5XP par headshot, sachant qu'il faut des milliers d'XP pour up c'est inutile), d'autres sont utiles (Sauter et tirer à l'arc, méditer pour passer jour/nuit) et d'autres sont cheatées as fuck (pouvoir contrôler la flèche de l'arc sniper et ainsi one shot n'importe quel ennemi dans un rayon de 70 mètres, même si il est super protégé...).
 Mais dans l'ensemble c'est correct, on sent une vraie progression (d'ailleurs la difficulté ils se sont pas fait chié Ubisoft, si l'ennemi a plus de 4 niveaux que toi il est quasi immortel, impossible de le tuer et lui il te souffle dessus c'est la fin...).

(Ubisoft a aussi sorti une mise à jour intéressante pouvant augmenter la difficulté du jeu (qui était trop simple), a rajouté un mode dans l'aréne et on peut maintenant rajouter de la barbe et des cheveux à Bayek!)

Points noirs:
-il y a de nombreux bugs quand même (Hitbox, ennemis dans les murs, problémes avec l'IA) mais vu le contenu à disposition, c'est largement acceptable,
-Bayek de Siwa: pour améliorer son équipement tue des centaines d'animaux, mais il est contre la violence animale et défend les animaux... Enfin bref...

Analise Outlast / Outlast Whistblower

''Outlast é um daqueles jogos de baixo orçamento, com poucas pessoas e uma ideia.'' 

História 7/10 
Gráficos 9/10
Jogabilidade 8/10
Puzzles 0/0

História principal - Outlast - Você recebe um Email de um desconhecido que te leva a um hospicio onde é relatado abusos com os pacientes de uma compania que quer lucrar em cima disso. Você como um bom reporter quer delatar isso para que essa seja a grande matéria de sua vida e acaba sendo o maior inferno onde você poderia se enfiar.

Gráficos : Escuridão sinistra e bem desenhada dão um "crima" muito bom ao jogo todo, detalhes são incriveis.

Jogabilidade : O jogo tem uma movimentação e camera fáceis de controlar, o mais complicado fica com a corrida/salto onde há necessidade de soltar o botão de corrida para que se consiga saltar, dificultando muitas vezes na hora da fuga.

Puzzles : Como em bons titulos que temos como Resident Evil e Silent Hill os Puzzles te dão agonia e satisfação sem falar na adicão com a história, porém em Outlast não há puzzle algum, o que me decpcionou muito.

Conclusão :

(Peguei boa parte dos documentos e notas, mas ainda assim, a história não me impressionou)

Não consegui me emocionar ou me aprofundar em ninguém no jogo, nem mesmo pelo personagem principal a onde eu deveria ter algum tipo de vinculo, mas na real, eu só queria terminar o jogo repetitivo que estava se tornando. O meu nivél de medo diminuiu drasticamente ao decorrer do jogo  pela monotomia que estava se tornando, era tão previsivél que eu apenas corria até achar documentos e depois a saída (muitas vezes pego no processo, mas uma vez que sabia onde ir tudo se tornava fácil e sem proposito). Quando cheguei na DLC eu já sabia o que esperar com uma história diferente que não vou mencionar aqui pois acho que seria spolier grande.

Por fim, eu aconselho a comprar e jogar, apesar de eu ser um pouco *dificil de se assustar* o jogo é bem interessante e da para tomar muitos sustos ali ou aqui caso você não curta terror como eu curto. Onde boa parte dos sustos que levei foram dos pacientes que não estavam me perseguindo, o terror psicologico de gato e rato me deixou um pouco cansado e eu muitas vezes me fazendo encarrar os perseguidores a ponto de parar de me esconder e enfrenta-los logo de cara.

■突き放した作りで難易度は高い
公式鯖の設定が激マゾだったりゲーム内でのチュートリアル的な要素が皆無だったりと
予備知識ゼロな初心者がなんとなくやったのでは
大型恐竜のテイムまでとてもたどり着けないであろう不親切なゲームです。
ローカルで設定を緩和して遊んでみたり、自分にあった難易度の非公式鯖を見つけたりと
最初は遊び方自体を自身で模索する必要があるでしょう。

広大なMAPに多種多様な生物がいてそのほとんどをテイムできますし
建築や装備品作成テイムしたペット同士でのブリーディングなどもあり
ゲームとしての奥行はしっかり存在しています。
エンドコンテンツにあたるボス戦などはかなりの戦力を要求されるので
育成した恐竜を持て余すこともありません。

2020年8月時点でも複数の個性的なMAPがあり大ボリュームのゲームですが
今後もジェネシスpart2などの拡張予定が発表されています。

app_name: South Park™: The Stick of Truth™
review:
Многостадальный проект Obsidian Ent. наконец-то увидел свет. За период разработки игра успела увидеть двух издателей, благодаря чему ее релиз откладывался в течение 6-8 месяцев.  

Феерия сортирного, и не очень, юмора, встречи со знакомыми персонажами, неожиданные повороты - эта игра дает возможность не только понаблюдать за происходящим со стороны, как при просмотре очередной серии, но и принять в событиях непосредственное участие. 

Игра позиционирует себя как ролевая, хотя развитие персонажа больше похоже на рогалик. Система проста. Здесь нет списка параметров, есть только одно очко умений за полученный уровень + очко спец. пассивного умения, получаемое за добавление друзей в соц. сети игры. Все. Игре от вас больше ничего не надо.

Боевая система так же проста как 2 пальца: нажми вовремя соотв. клавишу и наблюдай за происходящим. Благодаря количеству разномастных, хоть и схожих, супостатов, данный процесс не вызовет у вас скуку до самого финала, что было со мной при прохождении схожей по построению игры от студии Double Fine - Costume Quest. С данным продуктом, кстати говоря, можно провести много параллелей (ровно как и с множеством игр поджанра jrpg), но именно боевая система дает сто очков ЮП. 

Данный продукт настоятельно рекомендуется любому человеку, знакомому с сериалом. Многих охватит ностальгия по старым сезонам: музыкальные сопровождения, находимые предметы, безумие, творящееся на экране.
В отличие от всех остальных игр по лицензии (Гриффины, старые игры по ЮП), эта выгодно отличается качеством. Сделано на отлично абсолютно все: бои, диалоги, исследование городка, сюжет. 

За счет простоты игрового процесса и популярности франшизы South Park™: The Stick of Truth™ будет наиболее популярным проектом от студии, подарившей нам игры с серьезным филосовским поддекстом - Star Wars KotOR 2 и Neverwinter Nights 2: Mask of the Betrayer; вернувшей дух приключений и безумия в очередной части серии  Fallout - New Vegas; и готовящейся показать миру мейнстримовых RPG то, что в этих самых играх и важно, в продукте под названием Pillars of Eternity. 

Плюсы:
- Простота освоения
- Производительность
- Музыка
- Исследование мира
- Кат-сцены.

Минусы:
- Простота боев. Если вы выполняете все задания, не торопясь проходить сюжетную ветку, то с ними у вас не будет абсолютно никаких проблем. Особенно при игре за мага.

Portal 2 is a puzzle-based video game made by Valve in 2011 and is a sequel to the puzzle game with the same name in 2007. In the game, a player must use a tool that creates ‘portals’ to clear several chambers in a testing facility. Each level has the player also make use of physics-based objects like storage cubes, repulsion, propulsion and conversion gels. The story is about a test subject at a facility called ‘Aperture Laboratories’ named Chell who meets a robot that helps her try to escape the facility after being asleep for a long time and destroy an evil robot who controls the entire facility, GLaDOS.

The puzzles in the game were quite difficult but felt rewarding to complete. The difficulty comes from the fact that portals cannot be placed anywhere on the level and can only be placed on ‘portal-able’ white surfaces that the game designers carefully placed.   There is even an achievement for the game for completing one of the levels in seventy seconds. The puzzles will escalate in complexity as you continue playing the game, from using pressured buttons to utilising momentum, to using ‘Faith Plates’, high powered launch pads, to using gels that can increase surfaces’ velocity, make surfaces bouncy or ‘convert’ the surface to place portals. The Co-op mode requires you and your friend to work together to complete several puzzles of the same nature as the single-player puzzles except for the fact that you need to work together to complete them. 

Portal 2 has great replay value because of features like the challenge mode in the game, which encourages you to complete levels faster, the Co-op mode, where you complete levels with your friends and the Workshop, which has new levels created by the community daily even years after the game is released! When you complete the game, you can choose and download from over 600,000 single-player and 120,000 multi-player (co-op) levels on the workshop that are created by others.                                                                                                        

Another thing about Portal 2 I liked was the soundtrack in the game. I thought that the soundtrack was excellent because of the setting in the game being an abandoned test facility. The soundtrack sounds very glitchy and occasionally has some orchestral pieces in songs like Haunted Panels and '(defun botsbuildbots () (botsbuildbots))'. My favourite song in this soundtrack was 'The Friendly Faith Plate'.

Overall, Portal 2 is an excellent puzzle game with balanced difficulty with it’s puzzles which makes you feel clever when you complete a level rather than frustrated when you struggle with it. The atmosphere of the game is achieved with the glitchy, orchestral soundtrack and the overgrown look of the environment. The replay value is fantastic because of the features like the Steam Workshop, which allows people to create and upload their own creations for other people to play. In my opinion: worth your £7! If you also want to know about the developers’ progress and creative process, the e-book “Portal 2 - The Final Hours” is worth buying too (only £1.59).

Grand Theft Auto V is THE fucking-around simulator of 2013. There's a lot of fucking-around simulators set in sandboxes, but there's none quite with the same hallowed recognition and flair that Grand Theft Auto possesses. It's unevenly designed (see: the fucking UI re: it being garbage beyond figuring out waypoints), padded as shit to fill out a 40-hour game time (that's only if you do the main missions and little else in between), and the game itself feels well-detailed and alive and somehow at the same time feeling like computer people existing in a computer environment. Now that it's 2015, it's finally out on the PC and it has new content for its multiplayer platform! Unfortunately for Rockstar, I don't give a shit about Grand Theft Auto's multiplayer mode. If I wanted to play a multiplayer Grand Theft Auto, I'd just buy a box of surplus grenades from my local Neo-Nazi and huck them at passing cars during rush hour.

Despite the tongue-lashing I gave the game, I like Grand Theft Auto 5. I like it a fuck of a lot more than I liked Grand Theft Auto 4, which managed to tap me out through a combination of awful writing, ancillary bullshit, and not being able to shoot Roman in the face when he begs me to take him bowling. Oh, don't worry - there is so much fucking around you can do here, from golf to taxi driving to underwater deep sea diving to fighting with other shitlords on the Steam Discussion forums on whether Claude Speed is still canon in GTA or not. But if you want to just dig deep into the miserable lives of three shitlords looking for scratch so you can get into all the awesome multi-stage heists to pull off for sweet dollars and sweeter gamer cred, you can do that too and ignore everything else.

Now that I've validated your opinion on this video game, I am going to say mean things about the writing. If you don't care about the writing of Grand Theft Auto, please do not reveal the spoiler tag. Pretend I'm talking about cheeseburgers or something.

[spoiler]I think the writing of GTA 5 is highly uneven. Sure, Rockstar are taking bold leaps forward by having three main characters with wildly different lifestyles and circles of friends, and that is something to applaud. I want to see Rockstar do some Wire-type shit with many main characters, but they have to overcome their hurdles first.

I think largely I was tired of GTA 5's satirization because I know what they're getting at, I just don't find it funny anymore, and it think it has more to do with 'haha lol political satire rofl topical humor, titties and dicks, rofl' than it has to do with the lack of attempt of actual satirization. The game is kind of really misogynist, and I don't know whether that's an intentional choice or whether it escaped the glaucoma-ridden panopticon of SATIRE that the writers tried to create. (I'm betting on the latter). The torture mission sucked and I told the game to go fuck itself when it was over. The main characters are fun and occasionally have actual human emotional moments, but their characters kind of fall apart towards the middle part of the game and are driven by the overwritten 80's action movie plot that you can either wrap up neatly or not. It's all shoddy writing masked by excellent world detail and voice acting performances, and I hope Rockstar ups their writing game for the next time around.

This was my first experience with Yakuza series and I wouldn't have thought I would sink so many hours into this game.

It's way different then anything recent lately from AAA companies in fact you can't even compare the value here.

Yakuza 0 is an excellent game. It is the experience every gamer dreams of - great story, content and gameplay, that's barely the surface. 

[ + ] PROS
* story - it was certainly well executed
* protagonists - I grown attached to them quite easily
* cast - were simply amazing, the dialogs felt real with lot of effort into animating them
* gameplay - both protagonists have their own styles of figthing and you can improve them and get new moves if you put effort into it
* the music - the music gets you pumped so much you enjoy every fight, it's Japanese rock at it's finest
* content - the story was long, side missions were a lot and even a side business for both main characters
* minigames - you have it all and the best part is how over the top serious both playable characters do all of them. There were also missions and extra money you could earn from them
* endgame - the game awards you for good effort (rarely seen in other games)
* all the boss battle intros were so much hype and got imediatelly pumped up for battle

Unfortunately there were a few things that bugged me, I can understand why it was not done properly but keeping in mind the price of game, it's no wonder why it was done this way.
[ - ] CONS
* regular animations - many enemy characters have goofy animation where their heads point towards you always no matter which direction they go, also their running and walking was always akwardly in sync.
* no voiced substories - this is by far the biggest gripe with this game I had, there was such an amazing potention here because those substories were mostly funny.
* keyboard/mouse setup is impossible due to how mouse movement 'works'. You definetely need a controller.


I do recommend this game for those who want something cool, different, decent and with good story/characters.

In X-Com 2, a pretty good squad tactics game and a pretty good management sim combine to form a pretty great game with a surprising strength

XCom 2’s premise is quickly told: In the first game aliens have conquered the earth, the international defense force X-Com has failed to repulse them and is now forced to continue the fight guerilla style. As the commander of this new and quite diminished force, you’ll have to wear two hats: Manager of an ever growing force of increasingly heavily armed people, and commander of a squad of 4-6 of these heavily armed people out on deployment.

Management duties take place within the Avenger, an alien spacecraft that X-Com found parked somewhere and now uses as a local base. There is space on board you can fill with helpful facilities, your scientists live here and amuse themselves with dissecting aliens and decrypting their social media profiles, while your engineers turn your hard-earned cash into weapons, armor and gadgets for your troops to play with. Your job consists of worker placement, deciding what this month’s budget will be spent on, what missions the Avenger will undertake and what to research next, and, when the shit hits the fan, who is going to go on mission and what they’ll take with them.

That’s when the hat changes: Out in the field, your troops have two actions per turn and pretty much two skills: moving and damaging stuff, mostly by shooting it. The primary game-play loop is this: Move until you hit a troop of aliens, and then use all the actions still left this turn to wipe them out before they even take their first turn, because in this game, you do not want the enemy shooting back at you. That might sound quite limiting, but it isn’t: Positioning is an art, and your soldiers earn levels that bring with them a bunch of new variants to move and damage stuff, all with interesting trade-offs between chance to hit and potential damage. Your people can belong to nine different classes, and they all have their situational strengths and weaknesses. Just hope that you never trigger more than one alien patrol, because if you do, the second party will almost certainly get their turn, and they will almost certainly use it to kill people. And losing people is something X-Com can ill afford.

Both game-play modes aren’t especially deep: Management just means deciding which number you spend your time increasing, and the optimal route through the tech procession is pretty easy to suss out. Battling it out in the field is a bit more demanding, but after a while, you know how to deal with the specific alien types, and the tech progression will at some point supply you with one turn kill answers to even the beefiest mobs the aliens have in their arsenal. You won’t be overpowered enough to rescue your people from stupid moves, but you’ll hit on a strategy that will just work if executed right.

So, while it isn’t exactly challenging to climb the tech ladder and accomplish missions (at least not on default difficulty), it’s plenty engaging, especially because the game has a hidden strength: It’s an awesome story generator.

Every mission has at least one memorable moment: Your sniper put down that Berserker just before it curbstomped your precious ranger, or your inept but unbelievably lucky specialist fails to hit a chryssalid standing less than a meter away but still manages to avoid the snapping claws of death. A lot of this goes on in the players head, of course, but the game tries its damnedest to help out: Every mission can end with a propaganda shot of the victorious troops. Soldiers can form bonds that have mechanical benefits but are steroids for your very own head canon. They get tired, wounded or psychologically scarred. It’s really amazing how attached you can get to your soldiers, and I at least never got tired watching my favorite squads in the field.

This is where the main fun for me springs: Watching a group of people struggle and succeed against what is described as overwhelming odds. Feeling like a tactical genius when things work out is a nice side dish to that.

A few minor issues mar the experience: The colorful palette of the game clashes a bit with the grim tone of cosmic horror the plot tries to tell. Also, said plot is very front-loaded. The introducing missions and the introduction of the chosen is done very well, but during the second act of a given campaign, your enjoyment is mostly left to the random mission generator, and the final act is very satisfying as a tactical challenge, but I would have wished for a bit more resolution of the actual plot line.

But I cared only a little bit about that when Jane Kelly, the ranger I got in the very first introduction mission, used her katana to cut the last avatar of the Ancients to ribbons, under an unknown sea shone upon by strange stars.

TLDR: Pretty good management sim, great turn-based squad strategy game, excellent story generator, absolutely worth playing.

Einen gewissen Reiz wird EU IV natürlich immer haben. Das kann keiner bestreiten. Doch die letzten Updates waren/sind einfach eine mittlere Katastrophe. Die Paradox Entwicklerstudios denken sich offenbar; da die AI zu dämlich ist, 'nen vernünftigen Krieg zu führen, geben wir ihr einfach unbegrenzt Geld, unbegrenzt Machtpunkte, automatisch die nächste Institution, alle kolonialistischen Freiheiten und Boni und der Spieler darf schön bis zum Spielende der Entwicklung hinterher hinken, ganz gleich wie günstig das Terrain in ökonomischer und institutioneller Hinsicht ist. Es gibt neue Provinzverbesserungen - tataa! - die AI baut sie instant aus und finanziert nebenbei noch problemlos Rebellenarmeen. Das besondere Feature ist dann: erobert man dann kriegerisch diese Provinzen, ist alles wieder fort.
Dabei gilt; je härter man expandiert, desto krassere Gegenfraktionen entwickeln sich - konsequenzenlos - und das ausgerechnet im Herzen eines diplomatisch zutiefst verworrenen und gespaltenen Europas.
Ist ein Staat dann doch mal bankrott bspw. weil er 120 K Söldner aushebelt, um seine Kriege zu gewinnen, saniert er sich vollständig binnen kürzester Zeit.
Die eigenen Untertanen geben, speziell wenn es dann in den Kolonialkriegen heiß hergeht, aber auch in Friedenszeiten, wenn sie bspw. ihre Umschlagplätze nicht schützen, nochmal zusätzliches Momentum - natürlich gegen den Spieler selbst.
Die AI verliert Kriege, Geld, Handelseinfluss, Schiffe, man verhängt Embargos, man sabotiert ihren Ruf, verleumdet ihre Kaufleute, unterstützt in der Breite Rebellen - macht alles nichts - die AI ist mit ihren unendlichen Ressourcen über jede Form äußerer Destabilisierung erhaben und selbst über 100% Warscores im Stakkato-Takt lacht sie nur, wenn der Matchplan für sie einen Störer im Endgame vorsieht.
Paradox sollte m.E. allmählich mal anfangen, zu hinterfragen, wozu sie die Diplo-Aktionen aufstellen, wenn spielerische Aktionen stets an einer Invincible AI abprallen. Das sei nur der Gipfel des Eisbergs. Es ist noch nicht so, dass EU IV unspielbar wäre, aber Paradox Entertainment stellt immer mehr die Weichen in diese Richtung, was EU IV zu einem mittlerweile äußerst zähen Spielerlebnis macht.

It's a game about playing a puzzle game to get laid.  Sounds simple enough, right?
Yeah no. Here we go.

HuniePop is a dating sim/puzzle game based around your character talking to, dating, and ultimately making love to one of 8 regular humans and 4... not... humans. Specifically, a fairy who's coaching you on how to get laid, a catgirl (you get an achievement called Bestiality for getting the option to date her. Have fun having THAT on your record forever. It's literally the worst achievement I have.), a space alien, and THE GODDESS OF LOVE HERSELF. These 12 characters have different likes and dislikes, with that affecting what foods you can give them to keep talking to them (as they all have what I'd hesitate to call a "stamina" meter that drains with each conversation), what gifts you can give them (to increase your Hunie, which is basically your "stat points" you use to increase your traits), and what Joy Tokens (the things you match in the puzzle side of the game) give you the most affection. Your goal? Have sex with all 12 women.
Don't worry, it's not sexist. You can play as a girl, too. See, men aren't the only pervs out there. Plus, the game's censored on this version, so dooooooon't woooooooorry.
The talking aspect, probably what you'll be doing for half the game to build up your Hunie and increase your traits, consists of three different possibilities. Asking the girls questions to learn their traits, answering random questions, or answering questions about the traits that you already know. Answering them correctly earns you Hunie, and if you give each character a specific kind of gift, you'll get 50% more Hunie. AND if you buy them alcohols, which you can only do at night I think, you'll get even MORE Hunie.
Gifts, however, cost money. Or Munie, I suppose. How do you get Munie? By successfully dating the girls. This is the part of the game that most people know about, the Bejeweled-style match puzzle... thing. You match Joy Tokens, of which there are 8, to gain affection. Only four of the tokens give affection, though. These are "Romance", "Talent", "Sexuality", and "Flirtation". Each girl has a favorite and a least favorite of these tokens, with the favorite giving more affection than the others and the least favorite giving... the least. Obviously.
The other four tokens are Bells, which if you match them give you extra moves, Hearts, which give you Passion (which I'll explain in a second), Teardrops, which gives you Sentiment, which lets you use date gifts to improve your chances of succeeding, and Broken Hearts that are basically poison mushrooms and decrease your affection and will SCREW YOU OVER AT EVERY TURN.
Ahem. Passion is basically a score multiplier. The higher your Passion level, the more affection you get per match. The puzzle parts aren't too tricky on the surface, but on higher difficulties, if you suck at them, prepare to never get laid in the game.
and if you're playing this game on hard, prepare to never get laid in real life because you're a f***ing try-hard.
The goal is to date a girl 4 times, with the last date at evening or night, so she'll sleep with you. So yeah. Not too hard to figure out. The sex minigame is basically "match as fast as humanly possible", with the only strategy you can use being "GO FAST".
Overall, the gameplay is pretty solid. What about everything else?
The art style is reminiscent of the style of anime and manga, and it works well to highlight the various characters features. Hairs and eyes are colorful as hell, and outfits are usually pretty... out there (no teacher dresses like that, Aiko, jesus christ) with the exception of Kyanna and Nikki. Everyone besides them dresses like they live in a fantasy world where their traits are exaggerated to hell and back. (which they DO live in, but that's beside the point) So yeah, art's good, what about the characters?
The 8 human characters have varied personalities and suprisingly good voice acting. They're all very interesting in their own way, from megab*tch party girl Audrey to friendly university student Tiffany, each character has a unique personality and they all feel like complex characters. Aside from the four secret characters, of course, who are all meant to be silly completely intentionally.
So yeah. Gameplay's pretty fun, characters are interesting, art's good... Writing?
The writing is some of the funniest s*** I've ever heard ever. Just... Here's two highlights. 
"F*ck these birds, am I right?"
"Thanks for the sex, homie!"

just... goddammit.
So yeah. This is a pretty good game. Even if you don't like the idea of f***ing random women, the dating aspect is pretty interesting, the gameplay is solid and fun, the characters are varied and interesting, the writing's hilarious. I definitely recommend this game, even if you don't wanna bang random women.

Having said that, it can get a bit repetitive once you have achieved everything in-game. I found that in the pursuit of money, I settle into a routine of tending farm - I don't visit mine or socialise with the villagers anymore. I suppose it sort of mirrors what happens in real life for some people. So I reckon you definitely want to limit the amount of things you farm, if you are playing the game, be it crops or animals. 

Another thing to consider / remember is that ConcernedApe does bring update overtime, so be prepared to evolve your farm, or design your farm in a way so it is upgradeable over time.

Jouant à Skyrim depuis sa sortie en 2011 et ayant plus de 400h de jeu dessus je pense pouvoir fournir un avis complet.
J'avais déjà fait une évaluation de Skyrim il y a quelques années mais elle était loin d'être complète et très subjective (je ne prétends pas être complètement objectif aujourd'hui mais au moins mon avis sera mieux construit).

Aujourd'hui ce jeu est considéré par beaucoup (dont moi) comme un classique et comme un RPG incontournable. Il est considéré comme tel pour deux raisons principales. 
Tout d'abord Bethesda aime le sortir sur toutes les plateformes, il est sorti sur la génération PS3/X360 et aujourd'hui on entend des rumeurs de Skyrim sur PS5 et Xbox Serie X. C'est sûr qu'en appliquant une telle stratégie le jeu reste dans les esprits. Mais si le jeu sort encore aujourd'hui c'est parce qu'il se vent toujours de façon satisfaisante pour Bethesda, et cela est dû à sa qualité.
L'autre raison qui fait que Skyrim est considéré comme un classique c'est, comme dit précédemment, sa qualité. Le jeu est bon, mais il n'est pas exempt de défaut.

Commençons enfin "mon évaluation".

[u] Histoire et quêtes [/u] :

L'histoire principale prend place 200 ans après les événements de The Elder Scrolls IV : Oblivion dans la région de Bordeciel, région au nord du continent de Tamriel. Cette région est peuplée par les Nordiques.

Le jeu raconte le retour des Dragons en Bordeciel menés par le terrible Alduin, Le Dévoreur des Mondes et premier Dragon. Pour faire très court, la quête principale consiste à trouver un moyen d'arrêter ce Dragon de l'apocalypse. Elle ne se démarque pas par son originalité, elle est satisfaisante sans non plus casser trois pattes à un canard.
Selon moi, le plus décevant c'est le combat final contre Alduin. On s'attend à un combat épique, grandiose et se démarquant du reste de nos combats mais hélas ce combat n'est pas vraiment différent d'un combat avec n'importe quel dragon que l'on peut rencontrer au cours de nos aventures.

Le jeu est riche en ce qui concerne les quêtes secondaires : 
- On a l'occasion de pouvoir participer à une guerre entre l'Empire de Tamriel et les Sombrages (des indépendantistes Nordique). Le choix du camp est libre et n'apporte au final que peu de différences. Néanmoins ne vous attendez pas à de grandes batailles dignes du Seigneur des Anneaux avec des milliers de combattants. Ici vous aurez le droit à des batailles en 20 vs 20.
- Il y a ensuite les quêtes de guildes. Il y a 4 guildes dans le jeu (je ne compte pas la guilde des bardes) : Les compagnons (guilde de guerriers), La Guilde des voleurs, La Confrérie Noire (guilde d'assassins) et L'Académie de Fortdhiver (guilde de mages). Le joueur peut faire partie des 4 guildes. La qualité des quêtes est en deçà de ce qu'on pouvait avoir pour les guildes équivalentes dans Oblivion à l'exception de La Confrérie Noire qui égale La Confrérie Noire d'Oblivion.
- Pour le reste des quêtes secondaires, là c'est très inégal, il y a des quêtes très intéressantes et plutôt bien écrites et d'autres qui sont vraiment nulles.

Skyrim possède également 2 extensions : Dawnguard et Dragonborn.
Ces deux extensions ont un scénario plus intéressant et plus original que la quête principale. Elles nous offrent également des combats finaux plus épique que contre Alduin.
Elles peuvent être faites à n'importe quel moment mais je conseille de faire Dragonborn une fois la quête principale et Dawnguard terminées.

Le jeu invite le joueur à explorer par lui-même les contrés sauvages de Bordeciel. C'est pendant ces explorations qu'il pourra créer ses meilleurs souvenirs du jeu.

[u] Graphismes et design [/u] :

Les graphismes du jeu sont bons pour du 2011, il faut cependant noté qu'en 2011 il y avait des jeux qui surclassaient Skyrim en terme de graphisme. Aujourd'hui on remarque que sur ce point le jeu à vieilli et c'est un peu normal.

L'ambiance est toujours aussi charmante, immersive et cohérente. Le jeu arrive à bien nous représenter les paysages froids de Bordeciel.

Le design des villes est bien réalisé et il en va de même pour les PNJ. En ce qui les concerne c'est une vraie avancée par rapport à Oblivion où les personnages étaient hideux.

[u] Bande-son [/u] :

Alors là, rien à redire, elle est parfaite. Les musiques de Jeremy Soule sont absolument magnifiques. Elles savent être calmes quand il le faut et elles deviennent épiques lors des combats contre les Dragons.

La VF est également de qualité. Les doublages sont vivants et ne nous sortent pas du jeu.

[u] Durée de vie [/u] :

Pour faire la quête principale, les extensions, les guildes, la guerre et les meilleures quêtes secondaires il faudra compter pas loin de 100h de jeu.

[u] Mods [/u] :

Comment parler de Skyrim sans parler des mods. Sur le Nexus Mod (site regroupant beaucoup de mods) c'est le jeu avec le plus de mods et ils sont très nombreux sur le Steam Workshop.

Pour moi, les mods sont un plus, un bonus mais ils ne définissent pas la qualité du jeu.
On entend certaines personnes dire "Skyrim c'est trop bien, il y a plein de mods" ou bien "Skyrim sans les mods c'est naze".
Les mods sont effectivement une bonne chose pour Skyrim mais Skyrim sans mods est déjà excellent.

Les mods sont nombreux, on peut trouver de tous : des mods graphiques, des mods de quêtes, d'armures, d'armes...
Certains mods rendent le jeu absolument magnifique.

Il faut cependant faire extrêmement attention avec les mods, surtout ceux apportant le plus de modification au jeu de base, ils peuvent complètement corrompre vos sauvegardes (pas au sens littéral mais le jeu aura tendance à cracher toutes les minutes), vous obligeant à désinstaller le(s) mod(s) en question et à recommencer une nouvelle partie.

[u] Bugs, le gros point noir de Skyrim [/u] :

Les bugs sont fréquents dans Skyrim, même sans mods. Ils peuvent être drôle ou bien très handicapant, vous empêchant par exemple d'avancer dans une quête et vous bloquant. 
Heureusement, après bientôt 9 ans, beaucoup de gros bugs peuvent être réparés ou éviter grâce à des mods correctifs, des commandes pour la console de commandes ou bien des petites astuces.

Mais si Bethesda à obtenu le surnom de Bugthesda ce n'est pas pour rien.

[u] Conclusion [/u] :

Pour conclure (enfin), Skyrim est un "must have", c'est un incontournable. Il a des défauts mais il a aussi énormément de qualités.
Pour les personnes intéressées je conseille la version Legendary plutôt que la Remastered pour la simple raison qu'il y a beaucoup plus de mod sur le jeu de base que son édition remasterisée (même si cette édition est plus belle graphiquement). Autre avantage de la Legendary : elle est moins chère (environ deux fois moins chère).

La version Legendary ne semble plus être disponible à l'achat sur Steam mais il est toujours possible de l'acheter en version physique et d'activer la clé d'activation sur Steam. Une simple recherche Google vous permettra de trouver votre bonheur.

And now the monst disapointing downsites.
First and foremost, every Fallout (from Bethesda.) had a great storyline. And by that i mean the number of outcomes you can get mostly dependend from the choice of the faction. Then you had side quest. Some funny, some hard. Most of them impacted the outcome too. And the paths you could take on these quests? Amazing. But here? first thing we might notice is the dialogue "window". We only have 4 dialoge options: Good, Bad, Neutral and Curious. And nothing more. There is nothing you can change about the main quest. Then we have the massive DLC fail. 1st DLC adds bassicly customizeable robots, 2nd accualy have prety good story line, the 3rd lets you be a raider leader but you have to do evrything. If you have the time of course.

Poorly thought out game mechanics and balance. I think the creators didn't know how to make it difficult enough to keep ppl playing without resorting to relying heavily on luck.

Another stupid thing that the developers came up with to try and keep ppl playing and wasting their time is the unlock system. Basically it unlocks the "chance" of getting better cards on your next run the longer you play. Again you will have to be very lucky to find those abilities or cards. And why not unlock all those cards and let the players utilize them instead of forcing them to spend hours dying?

買おうかどうか迷ってる人向けのムービーだけ見てもよくわからない部分を補足。


■ 共通

エピックスキルは、1LVづつで良いので、そのグループ内の全てのスキルを覚えればOK。

ほとんどのスキルは一定数づつ効果が上昇するが、スタミナは最大まで上げれば無限ダッシュになる。

ドローンは回収の必要が無く、仮に撃ち落とされても40秒程度で復活する。
スキルを上げれば、復活も早くなる。

マップ画面で右クリックすると、終わったメインミッションをやり直せる。
例えば、マルチで勝手に終わってしまったミッションとかもやり直せる。

チームコマンドの偵察は、狙った場所を中心に偵察する。範囲はあまり大きくないのでしっかり狙うと良い。

資源を運んでるトラックは、完全破壊してもある程度回収できるので、逃げられるぐらいなら破壊した方が良い。
（燃え尽きて真っ黒になっても。ドライバーを倒してしまうのがベスト）


■ ソロ

仲間を連れて歩くゲームにゲームでありがちな面倒な「待ち」や「勝手に戦闘始めた！」がない。
これだけでも、ソロで快適に遊べる。

・乗り物には一人で乗って発信しても問題ない。
（ヘリに一人で乗り込んで発進しても、例え上空でも乗り込んでくる）
・倒れて放置して逃げても問題ない。
・自分との当たり判定がないため、すり抜ける（階段で邪魔になったりすることが無い）
・射線に入って来て目標が見えない。ということがほぼ無い（数時間遊んで1回あるかどうかぐらい）
・仲間のステルス能力が異常に高い…敵の前を走り抜けても見つからないレベル。
・勝手に戦闘を始めたりはしない。
・乱戦状態になると指示が無くても戦ってくれる。
・自分が倒れると助けてくれる（１戦闘に１回のみ。スキルで２回になる）
・適当にマークして「戦闘開始」とやると、結構遠くの敵でも倒しに行くので、どうにもならなくなってから実行した方が良い…と思う。


■ マルチ

・マップ画面で「仲間」にファストトラベル出来る。
・Syncショットのルールがソロと違うので注意が必要。
（エイムすると、対応する番号のグルグルが止まる。
　エイムを外すとグルグルし始める。誰がどれを狙っているかはメンバー一覧でわかる）
・人数が少ないくても補充はされない。
・人数が少なくて防衛などがキツイ時は、「傭兵」を召喚するとかなり楽になる。
・仲間との衝突判定があるので、階段などで立ち止まると邪魔になるので注意。（ソロの時とは違う）

Ziel des Spiels ist es, mit dem Raumschiff seiner Wahl eine Sternenkarte System für System zu passieren und im letzten Sektor einen Endgegner zu besiegen. In jedem System gibt es zufällig generierte Ereignisse zu bestehen. Das können gegnerische Schiffe sein, die es zu bekämpfen gilt, man findet einen Händler, oder man trifft textbasierte Entscheidungen. Das gemeine: Im selben Ereignis die selbe Entscheidung zu treffen garantiert nicht, die selbe Konsequenz zu erwirken. So gestaltet sich jeder Spieldurchlauf anders. In jedem System bekommt man Rohstoffe oder Gegenstände (Waffen, Besatzungsmitglieder, Perks, Munition, ...), mit denen das eigene Schiff ausgebaut wird, hoffend, dass man am Ende stark genug ist, den Endgegner zu besiegen.

Extrem kurzweiliges, rogue like game, mit sowohl strategischer Tiefe (jedes Schiff spielt sich anders), als auch taktischem Anspruch in den Kämpfen. Ein Spieldurchlauf dauert etwa 3h, der Tod ist permanent. Damit sind Spannung und Ärger gleichermaßen garantiert. ;) Es gibt rund 20 Schiffe durch das Erreichen von Erungenschaften freizuschalten. Ich habe nach 90h erst etwa die Hälfte freigespielt.

This game sucks, and not in a "well you overhyped it" way. Sean Murray is Peter Molynieux 2.0, marketing a title on promises he ultimately couldn't keep. Worse though, all of the trailers contain important features that were stripped from the final release. If I had to do a word association with No Man's Sky, the word that would come to mind is "con." I know it sounds like I'm just some butthurt troll, but this is a really sad case of a "bait and switch." 

To say you can't get some form of enjoyment would be a complete lie. While the title is extremely repetitive and relies on "dice-rolling" for everything single thing, there's always some hope that your efforts won't be in vain. But then you start to notice how poorly designed everything is, and then it hits you - it was intentionally designed this way to artificially extend the game time. And when you reach "the end," it's a huge slap in the face.

It's sad to say, but this game needed another year or two of development. Sean's teased the addition of features, but it'll take months and months to even fix some of the broken basic mechanics - in other words, the foundation itself isn't great. If two years down the line a bunch of stuff is added and it goes on sale for $15, then MAYBE think about it. Right now, there are much better games that are a third of the price.

Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair is a story about Hope and Despair, but one with a far different take. Instead of a hero that is relentlessly optimistic, we have a protagonist who is grounded in reality, virtually normal in all ways, but still intelligent and sharp, and his way of solving murders and talking to friends is different than Makoto Naegi.

The gameplay is more refined, although some minigames could stand to be a little more polished. The non-stop debates are back, and they're as fun as ever. Like usual, you have to use the evidence to find holes and twists, and this time, you don't just say people are wrong. You agree with them, back up their statements, reinforce points.

The cast of characters is just wonderfully entertaining. There are bound to be favorites. I know I've chosen my favorite waifu(s), and it makes it all the more painful when you see them become a victim or become a blackened.

The story kept me heavily invested and I was on the edge of my seat wondering what evidence and whose testimony would change the course of the trials. The many moral dilemmas that each characters face made me consider what I would do in a similar situation.

There is also a good chunk of post-story content that'll keep you coming back for more. Minigames are fun, but the main attraction here is the dating sim. Now you can date your favorite character! What's not to like?

Danganronpa 2: Goodbye Despair is a story that invests a lot into its story, its characters, and its presentation. It takes what made the first game good and makes it better, exceeding the first game in almost every way. I give this game a 9/10.

The game is way more complex then it looks. You will need to micro your pawns at times unless you want to watch things fall apart. It is brutal and unforgiving in ways you won't expect, pawns will die unless you save scum and even save scumming might not save you. 1 big mistake can cause long term damage that might prevent you from ever recovering.

Play on easier setting and in normal environments if the above sounds too brutal. Avoid Desert/Tundra/Ice caps environments unless you are looking for more complexity.

The easier settings are the best way to learn the game, slowly work your way up if you want harder gameplay. 

Or just play on the lower settings and enjoy building a beautiful/rich colony.

Hm, now, what to say about this game? This game is just absolutely adorable, and definitely worth your money. It is by no means complete, but what they got so far is perfect for those that love management-type games. The basics of the gameplay is that you are a Rancher on a far-off planet. The things you ranch are Slimes, which are adorable blobs, and to make the muns you need, you need to collect their plorps, which is their poops. There isn't too much story, but trying to find what your Slimes like, fulfilling orders, and following the poop market makes this game so much fun. For some basic tips, you cannot suck up Largo's (When a slime eats another slime's plorts, it becomes a combo of the two), the Tarr's are bad, and the super-big slimes, you basically feed until they explode.

0.5.1 edit: Alright, after returning to the game, and playing it for a bit longer, they have added a LOT. There are 4 new kinds of slimes, Slime Science­™, and all new area's to explore. There are small story signposts dotted along the world, so I still recommend Pooper Scooper Simulator!

Just picked up Battletech in the Humble Bundle monthly pack.  I've been strangely obsessed with it lately.  I very vaguely remember playing the pen & paper version of this way back when I played D&D.  Basically giant robots with various weapons strapped on them fighting it out.  It's turn based combat, so you're able to plot out your moves in detail before executing them.  3 basic weapon types: lasers, missiles and guns.  Hits are localized, arms, legs, torso, head.  You can blow off a leg and knock an enemy down, take off an arm and all the weapons mounted on it, hit an ammo store and cause extra damage, or go for a headshot.  The maps and landscapes are varied, you can take cover in forests or behind buildings, stand in a lake or river to keep from overheating, or use jumpjets to fly up atop a cliff for a bird's eye view of the battlefield.  Each mission pays credits and allows you to take salvage from the enemies to piece together new weapons or new robots.  You must pay your warriors each month, and pay to repair or replace your robots.  There's also a starmap where you can plot a course to new star systems with new missions and different planet types.

I didn't expect much, but was pleasantly surprised with the depth of this one!

Después de 100 horas de juego, puedo sin ninguna duda afirmar que este juego no es para todos. No te vas a encontrar enemigos, no es un simulador de negocios (no uno muy completo por lo menos...), no hay historia profunda ni existen personajes memorables. Sólo eres tú, el camino y tu camión navegando por todos los rincones de Europa, empezando por Europa central y Reino Unido. Es un juego en el que tu único objetivo es llevar tu mercancía dentro de un generoso límite de tiempo.

Como dice el dicho: no se trata del destino, sino del trayecto, y este juego tiene mucho trayecto por ofrecerte. Desde las calles de Amsterdam, las costas de Inglaterra y los túneles y montañas que separan diversos países como Francia, Inglaterra, Suecia, Bélgica, Alemania, puedes perderte por horas entre los majestuosos paisajes del juego.

Nota: este juego no es para impacientes. No existen atajos que puedas tomar, pasarás muchas horas de juego conduciendo por toda la red de carreteras de Europa. Sin embargo, si te gustan los ritmos calmados, explorar, los paisajes y la conducción, tienes que probarlo.

Pros:
- Múltiples caminos por explorar con hermosos paisajes
- Puedes costumizar tu propio camión y elegir de una amplia gama de estos (7 diferentes marcas, múltiples modelos por marca)
- Eventos inesperados en carreteras te pide que prestes atención y te pone variación a tus rutas
- Una lista de posibles entregas te permite elegir tu destino, el cual se expande con tu nivel de juego y tu distribución de "habilidades"
- No es muy exigente con una PC y puedes disfrutarlo en baja o máxima definición
- Puedes colocar tu propia música...

Cons:
- ...porque la música del juego es escasa por decirlo de buena manera
- A veces parece que los accidentes más grandes ocurren cuando se te está acabando el tiempo o tienes entregas de corta duración y larga distancia
- Repito: no es un juego para el impaciente, es una mecánica repetitiva donde tu única variación es en el tipo de mercancía que llevas, las rutas que sigues y las ciudades que decides visitar
- Al principio no podrás elegir ciudades de largas distancias o las mercancías que te piden surtir no son para las ciudades que desearías tener

Recomendaciones: cuando menos un Joystick (pero nada te impide jugar con el teclado...), tu selección de música y mucho tiempo libre

Alright, decided to write a review after about 25 hours of gameplay.

First: my initial experience was pretty bad, constant crashes and problems on the first island. What i played was wonderful, but a crash always happened after maby 30 minutes, which was kinda okay, since new release and constant auto-saves usually meant it was fine.

Second island was problematic due to the crashes, they happened a lot more and with shorter time in-between. The gameplay was harsh, now with less space to use for enclosures and more buildings and dinosaurs to fit in.

My experience was hell on the third, a new mechanic, as well  as crashes every 5 minutes meant i could not make progress. After hours of searching online for a solution, i found none. I contacted support which responded after a bit less than 12 hours.. And they found the solution. After that, i have played for maby 7 hours straight without a single crash.

Now, my experience has, as you might imagine, become a LOT better without the damned crashes. So here is my final opinion:

The game is very, very good for what it is: a Dinosaur Park Tycoon. It has a very big variety of creatures, some i even had to google. The missions are fun, if sometimes slightly stressful (here you got a sick dino you got no clue what is, have fun!). 
Alongside the dinosaurs, you got a LOT of buildings, and options, for how to run your park. You can make small, medium or large enclosures, keep them seperated or have many species together, some carnivores are actually fine being together with other carnivores or even herbivores.

On top of trying to keep your prehistoric attractions in a pen, you also got pretty good park management. There is a lot which factor into how happy your guests are: quality of food and drinks, access to fun things to do such as bowling or arcades. Hotels increase potential guest count as well as buildings dedicated to science, security or entertainment branches. With all of this, you have to make certain decisions on what to include, cause it is not all islands you got space for all of it.

All in all, it is a solid game, some things could always be improved upon, but as is, it is a very good dinosaur park tycoon, and i would highly recommend it for anyone who is a jurassic world or park fan.

Based on my experience, I am actually incredibly surprised about the negative reaction. Maybe people just don't know about optimizing their systems, or maybe I just got lucky. This game had a tiny amount of stutter in the first minute, and I have had LITERALLY no problems since.

Seeing the initial negative Knee-Jerk of the collective internet, I expected the worst.

I loaded the game up, expecting a buggy pile of garbage that didn't deliver on any of its promises. But, just for fun, I hit record on OBS to capture whatever happened (good or bad). Sure, I'll take a performance hit when I capture, but whatever. It booted up just fine. I came to on a barren desert planet. First thing I did was set my framerate cap to 60, expand the FOV, then restart to apply. "That's a bit annoying," I thought, "having to restart to apply video settings." 

And then I started playing. And an hour went by, and another, and another, and so on, and played until the wee hours of the morning. No lag, no bugs or issues at all, several hours of 1080p 60fps footage, and the game's exactly how I imagined it. I'm completely captivated by the aesthetic and exploration. The only minor annoyance, so far, is not being able to click immediately. I won't say this is the most amazing game ever made, but it delivered exactly what was promised on the store page, and exactly what I wanted, anything added in later patches will just be icing.

Granted, this isn't for everyone. This is a niche game. If you read the description and thought (I'm not sure about that), then you won't like it. But if you're into just wandering for hours in Minecraft, or exploring new worlds in Starbound, or you've poked around SpaceEngine and wished for gameplay features; then this game is for you.

For reference: i7-4770k, 16GB RAM, GTX 770, SSD.
