Мечтали ли вы когда нибудь оказаться в шкуре космического путешественника попавшего на неизвестную планету? А задумывались ли вы о том с чем такие путешествиники могут столкнуться? Вот разработчики Rimworld явно задумывались, потому что в игре продумано на столько много ситуаций и ньюансов что порой это просто поражает воображение!

Только представьте сколько разных и неповторимых ситуаций может произойти когда у вас по каждому параметру существует более 100 возможных вариантов развития событий и с добавлением любого параметра разнообразие растет в геометрической прогрессии... Здесь учтено практически все. Статус ваших поселенцев, душевное и физическое здоровье, все от старых шрамов до размеров комнаты персонажа имеет свое значение. Но практически на все это вы так же можете повлиять, если с размерами комнаты все достаточно очевидно, просто отсроить побольше (или поменьше, в зависимости от предпочтений поселенца) и поселить его там, то с разного рода травмами дела обстоят не так просто, но от этого не менее интересно, дело в том что вы можете заменить практически любую часть тела любого из поселенцев, на этом построена целая отдельная механика, и опять же вашему подопечному может понравится это, либо наоборот повлиять на него негативно от чего он будет получать постоянный дебаф настроения.

Помимо персонажей и их состояний есть разного рода события, постоянно падающие с неба корабли, враждебные по отношению ко всем рейдеры и пираты, переодически устраивающие набеги на ваши колонии. Погодные условия, дикие животные, не до конца понятно откуда берущиеся механойды которые могут испортить вам жизнь на долго, потому что драться с ними в открытом бою очень сложно, а оставлять на карте не тронутыми может привести к тому что вам негде будет засеивать поля, охотиться и добывать древесину, либо вообще их корабль будет являться источником странного шума который будут слышать только поселенцы мужского пола, и от этого плохо себя чувствовать. Разнообразие возможных сценариев развития событий поражает вооброжение. А если добавить к этому еще и пользовательские модификации которые расширяют пул возможных событий на столько на сколько вы сами захотите. Да вообще сама по себе оригинальная игра без каких либо модов способна затянуть на десятки и сотки часов, но как известно, качественная реализация поддержки пользовательских модификаций позволяют охватить гораздо большую аудиторию.

По сути игра представляет собой любопытный симулятор поселенца на случайно сгенерированной карте, но как только вы начнете понимать механику игры, вы заметите что просто строительством базы и менеджментом поселенцев игра не ограничевается, и чем дальше - тем больше! При достаточно простенькой графической составляющей игра предлагает вам неповторимый игровой опыт и совершенно не дает вам скучать.

Кроме всего перечисленного игра предоставляет вам полную свободу в плане геймплея, здесь нет такого понятия как "сложность игры", вы просто задаете начальные параметры такие как, например, кол-во поселенцев, стартовые технологии, баффы или дебаффы которые с разной долей вероятности будут действовать на ваших колонистов во время старта, и все это вы можете тщательно настроить лично подстраивая под ваши нужды. Таким образом можно начать игру с племенем дикарей в одеждах из шкур, которые выживают забивая разного рода местную живность палками для пропитания, а закончить высокотехнологичным городом государством которому не страшны даже сотня вражеских тяжело вооруженных солдат. Либо вы можете с самого начала выдать всем своим поселенцам лазерные винтовки и уже вы готовы отправиться в рейд на первое попавшееся поселение на планете, и там, на захваченной территории, начать обживаться. Но никто не будет держать вас на месте, и если вас не устроит та или иная карта вы можете в любой момент отправить поселенцев на поиск более подходящего места жительства, либо опять же захватить уже существующий городок или лагерь. Что стоит отметить - игра дает вам возможность развивать более чем одно поселение на планете, вы можете занять 5-10 и в теории даже больше локаций постоянно переключаясь с одной на другую и гонять караваны между собой и союзниками, но в данный момент эта функция может приводить к нестабильности игры, лично мне удавалось вполне свободно содержать 2-3 поселения, одно в качестве центрального и два других в качестве фермы ресурсов, но при большом кол-ве локаций пропорционально растет кол-во предметов, персонажей, и случайных событий, что влияет на производительность и может приводить к ошибкам, о чем вам и сообщает игра если при выборе в настройках пункта "Более 1 поселения". Но будем надеяться что разработчики исправят это и дадут нам возможность захватить всю планету целиком.

В общем рассказывать обо всех ньюансах и возможностях игры просто бессмысленно, такого невероятного колличества уникальных игровых ситуацийсейчас, наверное, не встретить ни в одной игре. Да это не AAA проект, и игра находится в раннем доступе. Но уже сейчас видно что разработчики вкладывают в игру все свои силы, и от обновления к обновлению добавляется просто огромнейшее количество контента. Что кстати не мешает вам в ожидании очередного обновления поискать интересные пользовательские моды, которые тоже очень качественные и часто добавляют очень интересные геймплейные возможности не предусмотренные в оригинальной игре.

Как итог можно сказать что подобных проектов практически нет на рынке, за свои деньги игра дает вам гораздо больше впечатлений и эмоций чем большинство именитых игровых тайтлов. Но как и у всего, у этой есть свои особенности которые могут понравиться не всем. Я хочу сказать что если вы предпочитаете сессионные игры на 20-30 минут, то я удивлен что вы дочитали этот обзор до этих строк. Дело в том что эта игра скорее для вдумчивого и длительного геймплея где одно поселение вы будете отстраивать несколько вечеров, переодически загружая автосейвы потому что генератор рандомных событий работает отлично, и вы с равной степенью можете получить груз ценных ресурсов которые позволят вам резко повысить технологический уровень вашего поселения в разы, или с тем же успехом вы получите короткое замыкание посреди зимы которое опустошит все ваши аккумуляторы, и вам придется выбирать чем жертвовать:
[list]
 [*] Здоровьем поселенцев, отключив центральное отопление что приведет к болезням, обморожениям и возможно смерти одного или даже группы, если у вас нет теплой одежды.
 [*] Либо вы можете отключить питание вашей фермы гидропоники, что осложнит проблемы с питанием и опять же поселенцы без продовольствия долго не проживут.
 [*] А может быть вы не боитесь рисковать и готовы отключить оборонительные сооружения? Стоит ли говорить о последствиях если на вас внезапно нападут когда вы будете к этому не готовы?
[/list]
 В общем в этой игре все зависит от вас, и решения которые вы принимаете могут повлиять самым неожиданным образом, когда вы уже забудете о том что произошло 10 игровых часов назад. 

Если собрать и обобщить все что написано выше - [b]игра великолепна.[/b] Я рекомендую всем кто любит спокойный размеренный геймплей хотя бы попробовать, сразу предупрежу - это займет у вас много времени, игра на столько затягивает что я невольно как будто бы вернувшись в детство могу провести за ней целые выходные, и ни разу об этом не пожалеть. Так же рекомендую после ознакомления с игрой обратить свое внимание на пользовательские модификации, игра предоставляет столько возможностей для модификаций что вы можете не узнать игру после нескольких установленных модов, и вам это понравится - гарантирую!

Para comenzar, debo de decir que lo que me llamó la atención de Hollow Knight, fue su increible arte. Lo compré con la ídea de que, apesar de las opiniones y sus puntuaciones, podría no gustarme, pero al menos disfrutaría de su acabado artistico o su banda sonora (ya que lo adquirí junto con su Soudtrack). Pero me llevé una increible sorpresa al jugarlo y sentirme inmerso en su increible mundo.

Sabía que me enfrentaría a un mundo hermoso y banda sonora envolvente, pero no esperaba una jugabilidad que haría sentir en mi, sensaciones que titulos como Dark Souls y Salt and Sanctuary provocaron. Let me tell you a story about a little game called "Streets of Sim City".  One day, while viewing the wall of new Best Buy computer games like a wall of new releases at Blockbuster, I noticed a game with cars and explosions under the title of "Sim City".  Could it be?  A game where I can achieve my dream of being able to drive around in my Sim City cities?!  Goodness, it was!  The back had a few images of seemingly stellar gameplay along with a whole mess of possible game modes and options.  As I read I became more and more excited about the chance to not only drive through my cities, but to fire missles, enjoy crazy deathmatches and fight aliens from space as a crazy old lady.  Suddenly, the game that was all I ever wanted became much more than that, it was the epitome of what an amazing game should be.  I rushed home and installed the game, thinking of all the crazy things I would see in my cities and all the wacky adventures I was about to undertake.  And then, I played...the game, was terrible.  Gone were the wacky adventures and crazy things to see.  In their places were poor graphics, poor gameplay and plenty of crashes.  I was angry, but I couldn't stop playing.  Each time I loaded a new city I kept driving, even though it was infuriating.  "Why am I doing this to myself," I would ask.  Then I realized, I was enjoying myself because I was doing the thing that drew me to the game in the first place.  I was driving through my cities.  That was what I wanted before I was lead down the road of what could have been.  I had forgotten my dreams and inserted new ones based ficticious hype I had created in my own mind.  In the end, I played Streets of Sim City way more than I should have.

This is my feeling with No Man's Sky.

First of all, I have to point out that if your framerate is bad, be sure to go into the options tab and increase the framerate cap.  As for crashes; mine crashed the first time I ran it, but I also had alt-tabbed, which doesn't work correctly.  This is a big problem that they need to fix, but the game didn't crash on it's own.  Alt-tab issues plague many newer games, even those from large studios, so I can't be upset about that.

The biggest thing causing most people anger is the multiplayer aspect of the game, or lack-there-of.  I never thought this was going to be multiplayer, even when Sean Murray was talking about it, so I'm not too put off by that either.  

So, where did my own disappointment lie?  It was with the worlds themselves.  As with most people, I foolishly thought that the procedural generation that went into No Man's Sky would be a bit beyond the type we saw in games like Spore.  Even those of us that deal with procedural generation expected that maybe the crew at No Man's Sky knew something we didn't.  Perhaps, they had figured out something new and that was going to create this amazingly diverse universe.  However, no, it was not anything new at all.  It was the same system built upon the same general rules and played out in the same random order, just on a much grander scale.  I expected that I would see world's that varied so much from one another that there would be no end to the crazy things I would see and the wacky adventures I would take.  This, sadly, did not happen.

In No Man's Sky, the worlds are indeed varied and there are some crazy things to see, but it's not the holy grail many, including myself, really wanted.  Instead, it's a game.  A fine game, but just a game.  

I really do enjoy No Man's Sky and I plan to keep playing it for a long while.  Even if it's not what the multitude of YouTube videos, only outmatched by the planets in this game, had led us all to believe with speculation and hype, it is still the same game that I got excited about in the beginning 3 years ago.  I never planned to meet anyone.  I never planned to build bases.  I never planned to find a whole different set of flowers on every single planet.  I did plan to fly from one planet to another, wandering around collecting samples and resources so that I could improve the ship I was flying to all these planets in.  I got what I wanted that first day when I saw the title and the picture on the box, and that still outweighs my disappointment in all the stuff I made up while reading the hype on the back.

Generally a very well done and faithful recreation of the original game. The developers did a great job maintaining the asthetic and level design while also expanding and altering some areas to seem more realistic and well laid out. That being said, a few areas feel somewhat simplified in a bad way. I am fairly sure they cut a few engangements and areas from a specific earlier level, and a few other areas have been negatively streamlined for ease of access. The game also suffers from some optimization issues. Runs pretty well all things considered, but does get INCREDIBLE frame drops in a few areas. These are relatively rare mind you, and don't overall distract from the enjoyment. 

All in all, well worth the purchase if you are a fan of the original. Honestly, I truly felt like I was replaying that classic game I loved so much when I was younger, but it was just better looking with a modern engine. Even if you never played the original, this may be a good way to enjoy it in the here and now. Plus or minus a few things, it is undeniably Half Life.

(Also, the Surface Tension level in this is amazing. They added several AWESOME encounters and set pieces that really capture the desperate feel of the soldiers struggling to survive, let alone control the base. 10/10 would Xen again.)

Edit: It is worth noting that the game is still unfinished. The page of course says this, but on that point it has been unfinished for sometime now. I remember playing an earlier build of the game perhaps 2 or so years ago? Said build was as finished as the current steam version is now. Granted that I think it was not nearly as well constructed (enemy A.I, graphic fidelity, optimization etc...) but that the Xen levels have still not been added after all that time is definitely a mark against it, and may be worth considering when looking to purchase. Also, the price tag of 20 dollars feels a bit steep, but that may just be me. I still highly recommend the game though. Considering the effort they have put into this I doubt they would just abandon development at this point. I have confidence the Xen levels will be released eventually. But even so, potential buyers should keep these things in mind.

Pros: One of the most authentic competitive experiences, whereby you and your team are 100% responsible for winning or losing; there is nothing random or luck based. In this regard, this game really feels like you are playing a sport, which brings all the feelings of pressure, adrenaline, and aggression, as well as the highest of highs from winning, and lowest of lows from losing. This game is at its best when you play with a pre-made team, so you can experience the joys of competitive team sports - a unique experience which I have yet find a game which replicates as well as rocket league. Controls are easy to understand, but unbelievably difficult to master, making this game accessible to nearly everyone. Control design and responsiveness is seamless and fluid. Style is lovely, and music adds to the feel of the game. 

Cons: This is a debatable con, but the game is incredibly unforgiving, meaning poor decision making or technical errors will likely result in the opposing team scoring on you, especially as you move up the ranks.  This not a con of the game design, but rather a caution for people who want a feel good team game. On a similar note, as one might predict, competitive game modes are VERY competitive, and not for the faint of heart. You will undoubtedly experience rage quitting, criticism, and occasionally smurfing/trolling. The learning curve for this game is so so steep, and be prepared to put in hundreds of hours to get to a fraction of the technical level that you might see pros playing at. 

Overall, I love this game, but its a lot like golf: you love when you're doing well, you're miserable when you're playing poorly, you never have anyone to blame but yourself for screwing up, and you probably won't get good until you've played for years. I would absolutely recommend this game, but be aware of what you're getting into, or else you might end up letting this game collect dust

Honestly I was rather nervous and almost didn't buy it despite being a Kojima fan over the ages. Some of the reviews I'd read prior to the steam launch left me wondering if we even played the same game. Or rather, it felt like they barely even finished the tutorial before writing about it. The game is kinda long, either that or I just took the scenic route every trip I made. Just doing the primary missions with 0 cutscene skips outside of run of the mill tasks was nearly 40+ hours of content. 

Before we continue, I'll just stop and say that yes: You deliver. That's your job, that's the premise of the game, if you're expecting to not be apocalypse amazon prime I'd imagine you didn't look into Death Stranding very much prior to reading this. It has atmosphere and story, the quests are not the meat of the world but rather the world itself. Funnily enough, just getting from A to B has more substance than most things on market these days though; So quit whining, pick up your shit and get moving.

Controlling the character and the mechanics take some getting used to, but the balance mechanic has both boons and banes to it in terms of use vs risk. Once you get the hang of it you'll be scaling cliffs like a goat and doing things with the vehicles your beginner self would have thought impossible.

Combat is interesting and feels rather responsive, often times I was able to switch up strategies and weapon types without feeling too outgunned. {Besides, Sam has fists of iron.} Weapons have enough variety to cover every situation I encountered and left me satisfied, expecially in the mix of all the useful terrain gear and fun gadgets.

I liked the story, had great fun with the gameplay and wonderful scenery, loved the characters and actors, and genuinely will be revisiting it often over the years I'm sure.

Наверное, это не самый простой обзор. Сложно вот так вот давать хорошую оценку продукту, столь неприветливо встреченному подавляющим большинством аудитории. 

Я сразу сделаю ремарку, что мультиплеер и зомби режим я не трогал, потому как мне они не интересны. Поэтому мой обзор касается только КАМПАНИИ. 

И тут игра мне в целом понравилась. Были огрехи с технической стороны при запуске, но на момент написания обзора игра даёт приличную картинку на моей средненькой машине и всё при 60 кадрах. Это с гигабайтом-то видеопамяти.
Текстуры, правда, временами размазываются по непонятным мне причинам.

Касательно сюжета сразу скажу - это очень необычно со стороны серии. Я бы даже сказал, по своему это злая сатира (если утрировать) на жанр компьютерных боевиков в целом.
Ролики сняты крайне хорошо, персонажи неплохие, каждый со своим мнением и реакцией на ту или иную ситуацию. И самое главное, что линия сюжета чётко прослеживается в диалогах и событиях, как слова главного антагониста плавно оказываются единственным выходом победить в войне. Войны выигрывает лишь тот, кто готов положить свою жизнь на победу. Ибо смерть - не бесчестье. И если простой пилот может себе позволить ратовать за важность человеческой жизни, то капитан военного корабля - уже нет.
Тут лишь надо внимательно читать диалоги В ОРИГИНАЛЕ и забыть о существовании русской локализации. Вас 9 лет минимум в школе английскому учат, так что его незнание не является оправданием.

Сама кампания даёт нам возможность полетать по солнечной системе и пострелять врагов, как на своих двоих, так и в кабине "Шакала" - аэрокосмического истребителя. Бои на "Шакале" аркадны до невозможности, но вносят приятное разнообразие в геймплей. Большинство заданий имеют небольшую протяжённость, потому геймплей истребителя не успевает приесться. 

Наземные операции же куда разнообразнее в геймплейных подходах. Да, стелс миссии далеко не сплинтер селл, но сделаны не спустя рукава. Перед каждой миссией есть возможность выбрать из богатого арсенала оружия и снаряжения, а враги достаточно разнообразны.

Сами миссии тоже не страдают самоповторами. Мы можем как и исследовать заброшенный комплекс на астероиде, так и мчаться сквозь вражеский флот на последний суицидальный таран вражеской верфи.

При этом игра в каком-то смысле приобрела реализма - штурмовой мех на открытой местности за секунду сделает из вас дуршлаг, а ракета в лицо сразу отправляет на чекпоинт. 

Достаточно обидно глядеть на то, как крепко сделанный аттракцион с неплохим и реалистичным сюжетом, с хорошим визуалом и парой неплохих находок имеет такое множество негативных отзывов. Я бы скинул это на предвзятое отношение, русскую локализацию (которая просто делает персонажей безликими и переводит всё через жопу) и проблемы с мультиплеером, которые безусловно есть.

Muito foda!Dying Light consegue te prender muito bem durante todo o jogo, seja pela jogabilidade excelente ou pela história que embora seja um pouco previsível, sem autenticidade e tenha personagens um pouco estereotipados demais, consegue nos entregar uma boa experiência e uma convincente história com reviravoltas no enredo muito perspicazes. Bom, mas agora vamos analisar cada aspecto do game.(Análise do jogo Offline)

GRÁFICOS: Os gráficos são espetaculares mesmo, os efeitos de iluminação são impecáveis, as modelagens dos npcs e inimigos estão muito realistas, os cenários muito vivos, com cores e harmonização que reforçam muito a imersão do jogador, os detalhes dos efeitos como poeira, coisas voando com o vento, o passar do tempo e a mudança da posição do sol e os efeitos de sombra causados por isso estão impecáveis e você consegue perceber muito bem quando o sol está se movendo e o tempo passa no jogo, apenas quando você entra no jogo ocorre um delay de renderização de alguns segundos, mas nada que atrapalhe significativamente o game em si. 

ÁUDIO: O áudio também é um bom ponto forte no jogo, você se verá muitas vezes com um calafrio só de escutar um volátil gritando no escuro. A dublagem em PT-BR está muito boa também, mas ainda prefiro a original. A trilha sonora é bem discreta mas é executada de uma forma muito boa e faz com que ela realmente tenha diferença enquanto você joga, os efeitos normais do jogo como passos, tiros, gemidos do zumbis e etc estão muito realistas e são muito bem executados também.

FÍSICA E AI: A física do jogo é muito boa, com efeitos de danos muito realistas e bem feitos, você consegue ter noção do impacto de cada arma branca no corpo dos zumbis e isso é uma delícia, o jeito que os inimigos reagem aos variados golpes é muito realista e satisfatório também. O senso de altura das quedas também, o jogo não faz de você um super humano que suporta cair de um lugar muito alto, dando mais realismo ao jogo. A AI dos inimigos varia, a dos zumbis não tem muito o que descrever, são burros e são ligados no modo kill, já o de alguns voláteis varia, alguns fogem, outros chamam reforços, outros te perseguem e em geral é boa, dos humanos é boa também, te emboscam, lançam coisas em você, bloqueiam e assim trazem assim um bom desafio pro jogo. Uma coisa que notei foi que alguns inimigos humanos tem visão de águia e te conseguem ver de muito longe você se aproximando ás vezes, mesmo você sendo cauteloso.

JOGABILIDADE: A jogabilidade certamente é o ponto mais forte do game, o parkour está muito fluído e é muito fácil de executar cada controle, os quais respondem muito bem também, os combates são divertidos e realistas não deixando nada a desejar, com muitos golpes, habilidades e jeitos diferentes de você matar seus inimigos, sem falar que as modificações nas armas ajudam muito na variedade delas e na diversão do jogo também. Quando a noite chega no jogo ele se torna "outro" digamos assim, afinal os voláteis saem de seus ninhos e começam sua caçada e onde antes você caçava, você se torna a presa, e o stealth é algo essencial durante as noites do jogo.

DURAÇÃO: A duração do jogo varia de acordo com o que você quer do jogo, por exemplo, se você for apenas pela história ele se torna um pouco curto, mas se você fizer as missões secundárias o jogo irá garantir muito mais horas pra você e isso sem falar nos secrets e desafios extras pra cumprir.

Resumindo, é um ótimo jogo mesmo, recomendo a todos e garanto que não vão se arrepender da compra! O começo pode ser um pouco estranho e difícil mas quando se pega o jeito, o jogo se torna muito viciante e divertido! 9/10

A definite step up from CK2, an already fantastic game. CK3 is much easier to get into while retaining all of CK2's intricacies. 

There's genuinely nothing quite like causing forcing your extra sons to be knights and praying they all get horribly slaughtered. Or, if that's too gruesome a way to ensure your heir gets all your titles, just disinherit them. There's nothing quite like disowning a child and banishing them from the kingdom to secure the throne. 

The majority of the complaints I have are more quality of life, I.E there should be a way to select a group of your prisoners and being able to ransom them as a group rather than individually, Ironman is automatically off and it isn't apparent it's off when you start the game, which means you can go a long time without realizing you haven't been earning achievements. 

My only real big complaint is that alliances need some work. There's been plenty of times where I've called an ally into a war but they just... Dance around their kingdom, or don't do anything helpful at all, even if they're fighting no war on their own turf. Hopefully they'll add in some way to direct your allies on where they should go or something like that. 

Overall though, the game's absolutely fantastic. Much of CK2's DLC exclusive content is automatically in this game, and it feels like a much fuller game than CK2 was at the beginning.

Civilization VI is worth playing. TLDR is that it's better to play casually and not competitively. That is what I find most people don't see from these games, and why it generally has mixed reviews. People just expect a certain mechanic that was originally in the predecessor games to be in this game or outright hate new mechanics presented. I would say the design concept for the game was understandable and actually fun. Disregard their DLC policy for a sec, Firaxis has come up with an innovative way to replay the game for Civ VI.

I think the most influential mechanic is the new districts systems. It is a huge stepaway from older game titles. As most of the harbors, workshops, libraries or markets used to be city center buildings. Now they take up one tile district and have "adjacency bonuses" based on the geography of your land. Which points out that geography is really really important for adjacency bonuses. A negative is that you can never remove a district and that you have a district limit based on your population within the city. My only problem with this is that wonder buildings take up a tile too, and when you're short on land, it can be a real headache to place tiles for food or production. And you can be limited on the amount of wonders you can build. (Therefore you cant spam wonders with alot of production)

Another huge change is the diplomatic aspect of the game. Each civ will like you depending on if you complete certain objectives. Vice versa, they will hate you for certain objectives. Their is also border frictions, coveted land, city state squabbles, and more. The only problem is that you can recieve a war declaration from a civ across the otherside of the world (If you play on huge or large map modes). It can become laborious to move your troops around the world because of this. Especially if you play on higher speed games. Also alliances are possible now too. If you meet the threshold for a possible civ alliance, it will automatically be a defensive alliance unless you persuade or are asked to do a joint war. Note that you do not recieve shared vision, that only happens on alliances level 2 or above. A huge dumb thing I hate with alliances is that they can attack a city state that you are a suzerain of. And, then you won't ever get a casus belli for protecting a city state. Which this is also a new thing too. Casus belli's have finally appeared and give reduced or increased warmongering depending on the outcome of war. These range from holy wars, liberation wars, city state wars, suprise wars, and more. I've always thought this was very dynamic, yet the warmongering penalities are unclear.

I think these two new mechanics influence a lot of people's opinion of the game. Districts, and diplomacy can be a real pain. But I think they provide a unique experience. Why else would firaxis want to remake a civ game with the same mechanics?

+ Good Graphics
+ Memorable and interesting characters
+ Huge world to explore
+ Very active world 
+ 4 equally fun ending paths
+ Healthy mod community
+ Always something to do
+ Companions that are actually characters and not just stereotypes or bullet sponges
+ Really fun and intuitive combat system

Cons: 
- Voiced protagonist
- Dumbed down BioWare diologue system
- Companion ai can be really stupid at times
- UI is not as PC friendly as it should be, mods help
- Main Story is laughably predicatable
- Side quests can get pretty repetitive and monotonous

- Shit optimization

I don't think the game is as awesome as I thought it was at launch, but I still think the game is great fun and one of those games I can play in between other games whenever I need to take a break.

This game is absolutely killer. 8/10. 

I have an i7-8750H, GTX 1060 6gb, 32gb DDR4 and an m.2 drive, and yet even on some slightly reduced settings, I notice the framerate stays below 80 fps in-game, which is irritating to say the least, however I experience no other problems or bugs and the game looks gorgeous.

Compared to previous, the multiplayer is less like Unreal and more unique despite being somewhat less like normal PvP combat. On the other hand, unfortunately, compared to 2016's 54 possible achievements, this game has a paltry 33, which I personally find very disappointing.

In-game, so many of my complaints about DOOM 2016 have been rectified, and many things I didn't even know I wanted have been added. I LOVE the campaign (except that effing Marauder). My chief complaint about the extra lives system actually has more to do with the terrain than the lives. For example, it is VERY easy to get stuck, crammed in a corner or stuck against a wall surrounded by enemies even when you keep moving. You'll find yourself sometimes getting stuck on nothing but a terrain oddity. I lost 3 lives to Cacodemons in just a few seconds this way. Also there are several no-no areas where even if you're clever enough to reach certain spots, the game will count you as out of bounds and bounce you back to the main level, though this is mostly an annoyance. 

Traversal, one of my biggest game gripes, is so awesome now I don't know if I can go back to 2016. Graphically this is a delight, the world is SO MUCH more amazing than previous with so many things going on in the background. The environment itself is alive where 2016's entry was frequently bland and stagnant. Color-wise too this game manages to maintain the same and better dreary, creepy, dark environments while being magnitudes more visually pleasing. 

I think I've put more time in just in the few days since it came out than I did for the first year of 2016's release. But to be truthful, this isn't even the same game as that was now. It's a whole other level, and the Doom Slayer of 2016 is back to full form as opposed to the fresh-from-the-coffin figuring things out mode. It plays and feels very different.

In the 2016 entry, it was too easy to settle into your favorite weapons and mods, and never use any others. Some were clearly better. In Eternal, you will HAVE to change up your weapons, swap mods, and adopt different strategies immediately while getting health, armor, and ammo directly from your enemies' corpses. It's so much more interactive this way and I love it.

Aside from occasional environmental failures mentioned before, the only thing I really felt bothered by was how unserious lots of components of this entry feel, from goofy sound effects to general silliness of the overabundant references throughout the game, which makes it kind of hard to take the Slayer or the story as seriously as I'd like and I feel this contributes to why it doesn't exactly feel like a perfect sequel. But these things have managed to grow on me and I love to visit the Slayer's room in the campaign to check things out. I highly recommend this game with praise.

I've played Fallout 4 for a while, and mostly enjoyed my time with it. The game is, for lack of a better term, a simple experience. Its entertaining, but there's really not much there. Despite my "No" recommendation I actually would recommend it if you're just looking for some brainless fun. The game could most easily be described as functional and entertaining, though not great in any regard. 

Where this game falls apart is in the story department. Though the game gives you choices it is very heavy-handed in what it considers to be the "correct" choice. This is made overtly clear to you through dialogue during an event, and well after. It can be frustrating when you make a choice the game isn't made to appreciate and have to sit through characters berating you constantly. In spite of the game being an open-world adventure, your main story is very forcibly "railroaded" into a single path. 

The most grating example is in the Far Harbor DLC, in which a choice you can make in the story will lead to everyone on the island admonishing your for your decision. This will happen regardless of whether or not they were even aware of your involvement at all.

Personally, I would recommend that anyone considering this game pick up Fallout: New Vegas instead. It's graphically inferior, being an older game, but the game play and design are leages above Fallout 4.

It's a real shame though, because it does a fantastic job with atmosphere, sound, killer design and tension. It has a massive carrot on a stick sort of progression which gets you coming back on. If you're in lower population countries like Australia, lobby times average between 5 - 10 minutes before finding a game.

Despite its good points, this game isn't worth the frustration and toxicity you will experience.

I LOVE this game. Brilliant idea, and executed expertly. Dead by Daylight allows one of two options: you play as a victim or as a deranged killer. The match begins with four victims who must go about repairing a number of generators and finding and opening an exit from the arena, all the while running and hiding from a psychopath killer, who's job is, you guessed it: kill the other players before they can escape.

Everything the victim players do sooner or later involves a series of skill checks, which exactly like the reload in Gears of War is a wheel with a small area marked, and a dial the player must successfully hit to pass the check. Hitting the check too soon or missing the marked area will cause the check to fail, making a generator blow up in your face or you to stab the teammate you're trying to heal. All of these creates a noise that the killer will hear and be able to locate your area, so passing skill checks is a must.

The killer player wanders around the map searching for the victims, attempting to stop their attempts to activate the generators and run to safety. After hitting a victim player twice, the victim goes into a "dying" state, where they can be picked up by the killer and carried off to one of many hooks around the map, and will be sacrificed to the Entity if left on the hook too long. They can also bleed out if left too long in this state, or a teammate can find them and help them back onto their feet.

The game becomes a wicked rush of adrenaline and fear no matter which side you play. You're either terrified as the heartbeat warning the killer is nearby grows louder and faster, or rushing after a fleeing prey as the killer, attempting to catch and murder the four other players and stop them from escaping your wrath. To anyone who enjoys the feeling of both fear and excitement, I VERY strongly recommend this game. 9/10, only because of camping killers. You know who you are, and should be ashamed. Плюсы

- Система баффов и дебаффов, вписанная в сеттинг: бзики и болезни героев, приобретаемые в походах (и излечиваемые в психушке)
- Удобный интерфейс с подсказками и справочной информацией там, где она нужна

Минусы [i](на момент прохождения / билд 14545)[/i]

- Игра безжалостна к казуальным и неподготовленным чтением гайдов игрокам [i](да и ко всем остальным тоже)[/i]

- Баланс в игре таков, что ваших героев убивают. Часто, и несмотря на ваши старания. Это соответствует атмосфере и сеттингу, но, в целом, игра дает больше негативных эмоций, чем позитивных

- Тактические возможности игрока и защитные способности героев намеренно ограничены, в результате основное влияние на результат оказывает не тактическое планирование, а рандомайзер

- Много однообразного геймплея из-за необходимости прокачивать большое кол-во героев (для финальных уровней нужно минимум 4 по 4 - т.е. 16 героев, прокачанных до 5-6 уровня)
 
- Несмотря на кажущееся разнообразие, есть практически бесполезные классы (большинство лекарей, например), предметы и скиллы

- Некоторые боссы и мини-боссы сильно перекачаны для подземелий своего уровня. Например, неожиданно много героев может потратиться на (необязательного) Пророка и на второй уровень финального подземелья (Darkest Dungeon)
  
Заключение

Игра сделана качественно, но не советую брать, если рассчитываете пройти ее до конца:   тактические возможности не так широки, как кажется в начале,  борьба с рандомом быстро надоедает

Upon release, I believe No Man's Sky was one of the most outrageous games for sale - multiple promises broken by developers, the game-state being buggy, full of graphical and loading issues for those even with monstrous rigs, and a vast universe that was simply, well, barren. I myself did not experience this, instead I heard it from my friends that spent the full price of their hard-earned (or maybe not, some of them are pretty shady) money for a game promising untold experiences, limitless exploration and the ability to do it all with your friends; it sounded like what every space-faring hungry adventurer would want! 

Instead there were outcries - outcries of betrayal, of deceit, of hurt. The game that was promised and the game they received were polar opposites. For months, Hello Games endured negative reviews and backlash, the player base noting their disappointment and disposition for the product they had received. 

And then, Hello Games did something not many companies would do (which I envision is just quitting, scrapping the project) - they listened, and they rebuilt their game, and made good on the promises that were once told. Through constant updates, through thousands of hours of hard work on their part, and an observant eye and ever-listening ear, the community continued to point out the wrongs, so Hello Games could make them right. 

Will I say that the game is worth your time, worth your money? Well, I would venture to say that with a space-faring crew of friends (if not, strangers!) in a vast universe that has been tuned and tweaked to deliver hundreds of hours of fresh gameplay, of exploration and discovery and base-building and adventure - well I would say yes. The developers are constantly learning and improving their game; no longer do players have issues with their titans of PCs handling this game, no longer is the universe barren and void of activity, no longer do players lull away in their misery of a game that could have been. 

It is a resurrected game of unlimited possibilities. It is No Man's Sky.

Enfin un Soulcalibur qui renoue avec les premiers !!!
Même si l'ont vois que malheureusement, le budget à été diminué pour l'équipe de développement, ils ont fait de leur mieux et un bon compromis.
Donc, oui, il n'y a plus de cinématiques à couper le souffle. Oui les graphismes n'ont pas évolués depuis le V. Oui, certains décors semblent fades et peu détaillés (d'où la présence du floue pour "masquer" ce manque de détails). Oui le mode histoire avec les quêtes à une narration simplifiée avec juste des dessins (certains très beaux) qui se répétent et des lignes de textes.
Mais en contre-partis, on gagne un jeu avec un gros contenu solo avec la possibilité de créer entièrement des personnages personalisés de A à Z (sauf pour les modes de combats) jouable dans tous les modes (sauf quêtes) et un gameplay énorme.
Comme dans les premiers Soulcaliburs, les mouvements et attaques sont naturels, instinctifs, fluides et précis. Ici, pas de combos faits de façons identiques avec tous les persos ou prédifinis comme dans Tekken ou interminables comme dans Killer Instinct. Il y a bien des petits combos de 3 ou 4 coups propres et différents à chaques personnages, mais les vrais enchainements se font en enchainant les coups "ordinaires" celon la situation et les circonstances, ainsi que la position de chaques joueurs. Sachant qu'il es toujours possible de contrer, bloquer ou éviter quasiment toutes les attaques en s'y prenant bien. Les bons joueurs se prennent rarement plus de 2 attaques d'affilés lol.
Ici, c'est pas celui qui tape le plus vite ou le plus fort qui gagne, mais celui qui sait le mieux gérer les très nombreux coups "ordinaires" différents et blocages / contres / esquives aux bons moments et dans les bonnes situations qui gagne.
Et même là, le Soule Breaker peut renverser la tendance en donnant une chance de renverser la situation alors même que vous alliez mourrir en apportant une touche de aléatoire qui, même si certains joueurs s'en plaignent, existe réelement dans les vrais combats (ceux qui ont fait du Bushido ou Kendo le savent que souvent, on ne peut pas voir venir ou anticiper certains coups, et si on arrivent à les parere c'est par chance).
Là, un combat peu durer que 10 secondes, ou plusieures minutes celon les joueurs juste pour 1 manche.
Et pour les joueurs qui restent constamment en garde, là aussi c'est prévu : la jauge de fatigue (couleure autour de la barre de vie). Lorsqu'elle passe au rouge, n'importe quelle coup suivant passe à travers la garde.
La soule charge es aussi très bien pensée : utilisée soit pour placer un enchainement qui fait très mal (mais pas excessif non plus), soit pour avoir un gains de puissance pendant plusieurs secondes avec l'ajout de nouvelles attaques puissantes propres à chaques personnages. Sachant aussi que l'attaque soule charge peut être contrée ou évitée (le 1er coup uniquement).
Bref, tous les coups (et ils sont très nombreux et différents) sont évitables d'une façon ou d'une autre, même les plus puissantes, et tous les coups ont leur utilité, même les plus basics et banales.
Tout ça dans une fluidité et visibilité exemplaire.
Au final : ce soulcalibure n'a peut être pas un superbe écrin comme d'autres jeux de combats, mais son coeur (qui sont les combats) es pour moi le meilleur gameplay qu'il y a en jeux de bastons.
J'èspére que les développeurs auront plus de budget pour le prochain.

EDIT : après plusieurs heures du mode "Balance de l'âme", il es truqué.... certains combats (beaucoup trops) sont impossible  à gagner sans faire des missions secondaires répetitives pour monter de plusieurs niveau.
Mais ce qui es extrêmement énervant, c'est que dans ces combats truqués, l'IA es INVINCIBLE ! Même en utilisant les 3 modes de combats que je maitrise le mieux (que je joue depuis Souleblade), impossible de placer plus d'un ou 2 coups... L'IA nous massacre en quelques secondes dans un déluge d'attaques impossibles à parer ou contrer, des anchainements anormalement rapides (quand c'est nous qui jouont ces modes de combats identiques, ils sont nettement moins rapides). Sans compter que l'IA réagis celon les boutons sur lesquels vous appuyez... Ce qui fait qu'il fait TOUJOURS les bonnes attaques ou parades pour contrer quasiment toutes les votres. Et en prime : la barre de vie des ennemis descend très très lentement (même avec un soule charge) contrairement à la votre qui chute de 50% en 2 attaques...
Et quand vous arrivez à être à 1 ou 2 coups de gagner le combat... il s'arrange pour vous tuer quand même en 1er...
Je ne suis pas un pro, mais je suis assez doué dans plusieurs modes de combats , et voir avec quelle facilité il me massacre sans que j'arrive à bloquer ou éviter quoi que ce soit et que je peine comme un fou pour réussir à placer que 1 ou 2 coups c'est abusé...
Sur chaquuns de ces combats truqués, j'ai réessayer une dizaine de fois, avec différentes armes /mode de combats... rien à faire. C'est toujours pareil.
Bref, régulièrement vous tomberez sur ces combats truqués et dans ce cas, si vous ne voulez pas balancer votre manette per terre (ce que j'ai fait à la 10éme tentative ce soir sur une de ces missions), abandonnez et revenez la faire quand vous aurez plusieurs niveaux de de personnage et de votre arme de plus (au moins 5).
C'est devenu une mode maintenant de truqué des jeux (que ce soit des jeux de combats, courses ou aventures) pour augmenter artificiellement la durée de vie... c'est pitoyable

DOOM je hra z pohledu první osoby (First-person shooter) z roku 2016, od amerického vývojářského studia ID Software, publikována společností Bethesda Softworks. Jedná se o reboot a pokračování hry "DOOM" z 90. let. DOOM je první hra, která využívá engine "id Tech 6". (Engine je specifický tím, že hry podporuje 60 FPS na 1080p). [spoiler]Příběh se odehrává na Marsu, kde se vžijete do role vesmírného mariňáka "Doom Slayera". Probouzíte se během rituálu, během kterého z vás démoni chtějí vytvořit svého poskoka. Následně zjišťujete, že jste se ocitli ve středu démonické invaze v zařízení UAC. Zde se snažíte najít zdroj této invaze a zastavit jí, a to s pomocí předsedy UAC "Samuela Haydena" a jeho vytvořené umělé inteligence zvané "VEGA". Zjistíte, že jedna z hlavních výzkumníků, Olivia Pierce provádí kult na poštvání ďábelské armády z portálu a následuje ji na vrchol Argent Energy Tower. Poté, co Piercovou dostihnete, tak následně aktivuje akumulátor, který vytvoří portál a za velkého výbuchu Argent Energy Tower, jste teleportováni do pekla. Zde máte za úkol najít portál na návrat zpět na Mars za použití značek zanechaných předchozími Haydenovými expedicemi. [/spoiler]
Hra si bere od svých předchůdců dobrý příklad a hned od začátku vás bez nějakého velkého vysvětlování vrhá přímo do akce, hra si absolutně na nic nehraje takže na regeneraci životů jako např. z Call of Duty zapomeňte a hrdě se hlásí k odkazu originálu (DOOM, 1993). Samotný příběh tu nehraje zase takovou roli, pokud se u hry nebudete moc soustředit, lehce děj přehlédnete a odsunete na 2. místo. Novinkou tohoto dílu je boj z blízka, který vám dává možnost využít (tzv. Glory kill), který nabídne zajímavé zničení daného nepřítele. Drobnou novinkou je také vylepšování zbraní a obleku, pro které ale budete potřebovat najít speciální objekty ("Argent cells" a "Elite Guards") různě rozmístěné na mapě. Na konci této hry navazuje pokračování dalšího dílu této herní série "DOOM Eternal".

通过一个月断断续续的不懈努力，我终于通关了Dying Light，首先简单对这个游戏进行一下总结吧，游戏的背景设定是一座叫做哈兰的城市爆发了丧尸病毒，主角作为政府防卫军GRE的特工被派到到这里来寻找一份被GRE背叛特工偷走的重要文件。这条主线贯穿了游戏始终。我认为这款游戏设计的最大亮点：一是游戏拥有自主的昼夜更替系统，二是新颖的跑酷元素。到了夜晚，会出现行动极快战斗力极强的夜魔，丧尸也会开始入侵，活动更为频繁，能力也会强化。它跟丧尸围城一样都是开放世界，但是却跟丧丧尸围城的割草风格完全不同，前期几乎完全靠近战武器的搏杀，一个人根本无法面对成群的丧尸，到了夜晚更是只能依靠各式各样的跑酷技巧躲避敌人，在面对敌对幸存者更难处理，他们都可以格挡你的攻击，这就更需要你把握好攻击方式和自己的体力条，一但体力条见底，主角的动作将即为缓慢，战斗力将变得极低。哈兰市共有三大区域，随着主线的推进，这三大区域将会依此解锁。游戏是无缝的开放世界，里面有各式各样可供玩家收集的元素，前期感觉自己武器都没有。。。疯狂的搜刮各个角落找材料，那种感觉一度以为自己好像在玩吃鸡...直到后期有了步枪，散弹枪各种枪械才觉得有了一战之力。
还记得最后一关去楼顶找塞斯，在去的路上看了一眼黄昏下的哈兰市，残破的废墟反而有一种颓败的美，那一瞬间我好像明白为什么主角选择留下了，毕竟这里埋葬着他的杰德啊。
游戏的恐怖氛围做的一般，也可能是因为我都是和舍友一起玩的所以没感觉？血腥程度倒是不低，也几乎没有那种突然出现给你“惊喜”的surprise,我还是要吐槽一下剧情，基本所有的转折我都猜到了....也觉得反派...有点蠢，各个人物并不是非常立体，感觉大部分时间在塑造主角的人格，其他NPC只是一个衬托的作用。不过毕竟这是一个主打跑酷和沙盒的丧尸游戏，不能对他要求太高。
游戏的打击感我觉得也还不错，水管桌腿那些武器敲在丧尸脑袋上还是很有质感的，玩家自己根据图纸合成的武器带有的特殊效果也很带感。
接下来说说比较大的缺点吧，首先我感觉进入游戏后我的鼠标晃动有点奇怪，其次游戏的整体色调怎么说呢，有些过于明亮油腻，每次玩完眼睛疼。而且游戏的可玩性较差，我一度觉得没有基友一起我都玩不下去，通完主线更是没有再次打开游戏的欲望，模式是在有些太重复单一。不过匹配模式还是很赞的，我看了不少大佬提携萌新的事例，对，这点很棒，就是你在别的玩家的存档获得的技能点和装备也会保留到自己的存档，人间处处有真情。
最后，最大的缺点：我WIN10系统，为什么总玩着玩着就闪退！就闪退！

Not worth $60.

Not worth $30.

The things that I had problems with:

The community circumventing griefing by making their Steam profiles private, naming themselves 123, and removing their profile pictures to proceed to run rampant on servers that are PVP.

The game borderlines on mobile phone gaming level with the inane amount of waiting this game has in its multiple systems, and this is putting the crafting system to the side.

The Tribe Log needs revamped, as people can use explosives to destroy your base, and the log will only say "...has been destroyed," and not by whom, defeating the purpose of letting you know in said log, because you can visually see the absence of said base.

A lot of graphical errors on a healthy mid to high end system on highest settings, not including random dips in framerate when nothing on screen is happening that would cause this.

The leveling curve is very quick up to 60, then skyrockets (meaing taking forever) toward 100, instead of being progressive. 

In order to get the most out of this game, you have to invest thousands of hours, and I find this argument is backed by the community, being most players are either under 100 hours, or over 1000. 

Explosives on a pvp server allow NEETs to wipe you every time you go to work or take a nap, which means this isn't a balanced mechanic, being the materials are either too easy to get, or explosives do too much damage. A lot of people, probably being NEET themselves, would just say I'm being salty for not living on assistance or under someone else's employment. I'm going to ignore these arguments posted below, so don't bother.

They released DLC for cost on an Early Access game before it was released, and before it's been fixed.

I know I'm late to the game with this, but I don't mind waiting for the sales (with a few exceptions), and I think I picked Tomb Raider up for about $5.  I wasn't all that thrilled to, because the last time I played a TR game was TR2 when it was released on the old PS1 console.  TR has the stigma that comes with it that it's basically a game about boobs with legs that had to solve some puzzles that were only frustrating because of how unweildy the controls were, but I heard good things, so I figured I'd give it a try.  I mean, I'm a fan of both boobs and legs, but I was never into cheesecake when it comes to games.

The first thing I enjoyed when starting out was the new model for Lara.  I saw some people complaining that once again gaming delivered an unrealistic body-type, but the fact is, Lara is built pretty much exactly like someone who does a lot of cardio and rock-climbing.  The body type can't be unrealistic, since she's pretty much a spitting image for the model she's based on.   Naturally, she's easy on the eyes (I'm not complaining here), and the camera only forces you to look directly at her butt a few times (again, not that I'm complaining), but not so much that I ever felt the need to invoke the spirit of Benny Hill.  Besides, she spends so much time covered in grime and gore, you barely get to notice it.  I don't see what people were complaining about.

On to the game itself:  I liked it.  I thought the story was engrossing, and the gameplay was good.  I'm not an avid gamer (job, family, responsibilities and all that), but I was able to beat it over a weekend.  It's pretty hard to keep my attention on one game for too long, but this one was entertaining enough to make me forget everything else in my library until I got to the end.   I'm also probably going to go back and try to 100% it, or maybe even try playing through the story again on a harder mode.  Possibilities are endless ... in a way that's pretty linear.  Not very open world, is what I'm trying to say here.  

So ... Hot, badass chick?  Check.  Island inexplicably full of American henchmen completely willing to follow and kill for a madman bent on raising a hellish ghoul from the dead even though they somehow seem aware of what a bad idea that is?  Double check. And is that island full of rusting metal to a degree that you will feel compelled to get a tetanus shot after about 5 minutes of gameplay?  You can bet your unpoisoned bloodstream it has all that and more.

To put it another way ... I'll probably get the sequel at full price.

Despite my attempts to remain stoic, I'm now a RIP AND TEAR fanboy. Wow, what a blast to play. While not the physics masterpiece of the original Halo, they share an emphasis on freedom of movement, fluidity, effortless experimentation, and plenty of things to smash and blow up. It even has a decent story!

GOOD
+ Fun: Run'n'gun fun! Easy to pick up, difficult to master. Light enough to get into quickly, substantial enough to provide plenty of depth and experimentation.
+ Story: It's a good one. There isn't a lot of it, but what's there is intriguing and well told. Hayden is particularly interesting. The Doom Marine's infinite hatred and disdain is SHOWN, not told.
+ Sound: Incredible sound design -- hope you've got bass!
+ Voice Actors: There are only two characters who really speak, but they're both interesting and superbly voice acted.
+ Length: Probably perfect. It doesn't outstay its welcome nor does it leave one unsatisfied.
+ Replayability: If you're really hungry for more at game's end, the arcade mode is a BLAST (often literally). The community maps/games/challenges can also be interesting to explore (although they didn't do it for me). Also, you can gear up your weapons, and while you'll get most unlocks with a thorough playthrough, you'd want to go through again or do arcade mode to try them all.
+ Weapons: They are beautifully animated, acoustically perfected, and SO satisfying to use. The game won't waste time giving you big, awesome ones very early. Gearing them up according to one's own playstyle/preference is also 
+ Art: Frankly, many of my screenshots in this game could be paintings. The lighting and landscapes are lovely, but even the interiors are gorgeous and interesting (assuming you've got the graphics power). The armour, power ups, character design, etc., all solid! There are also little bits of flavour here and there on computer terminals, in detailed environments, and so on that all add a lot of character.
+ Exploration: NAILED IT. It's not a huge open world, but exploration is not just rewarding -- it's actually FUN to do. It doesn't feel like a chore. I typically skip additional content, but I couldn't help seeking it out this time.

BAD
- I wonder if it was a bit poorly optimised. Seems overly demanding, graphics-wise.

NEUTRAL
= The player-made content seemed uninteresting to me, but that's not why I got the game.

Like many of the other reviews, I trully feel conflicted. Do I like the game? Yes, is the short answer, but with some serious conditions. This holds it back from a definite "YES", but a "yes while its on sale".

[b]The game's biggest selling point is the nemesis system[/b] which adds some serious replayability to the game. I completed the story once, so I haven't had that much experience with how the game diverges on different playthroughs but it was honestly very pleasing when my army of orcs ganged up on the local warlord and took his head off. Of course, it also felt pretty nasty when I would get stabbed in the back by one of my trusted warchiefs. But the Nemesis system is what really sets this game apart. If you like building an army, seeing your recuits grow, see them interact with other orcs/enemies, and taking over land, you will love the nemesis system.

[b]Let's talk about the open-world: It's kind of dissapointing.[/b] It is mostly static with some activities for leveling and recuiting orcs, along with exploration sites. The world map is actually quite small in experience and you will quickly get to the endgame before you know it, having dominated most of the land.

[b]Combat is fluid.[/b] The hits feel satisfying and the executions are beautiful (and conversely, when an orc captain executes you, you can definitely feel the brutality). You have a wide variety of tools at your disposal when approaching combat i.e. stealth, hit and run, magic, ranged, etc. The magical options are slightly lacking (really just an ice blast as your 'E' stun, the rest consume might). Speaking of which, the resources for your "god mode" aka elven rage builds as you kill orcs whilst your might increases as you damage enemies and avoid attacks to pull off a variety of special attacks. The game rewards you for doing well in combat and punishes you for being bad (a system that takes some getting used to). Overall it feels fair and enemies get harder as the game progresses. 

[b]RPG elements do exist in this game[/b] in form of lootable weapons and armor with better stats as the game progresses. Lootables have skills that can help you and you can form strategies for how you will approach taking a fort. Honestly you can kill stuff that's above your level if you dont spam your strategy and have the combat skill. Leveling also gives you access to ability points that you invest in abilities (duh). These range fropm poisoning barrels, pinning enemies to the ground, teleportation to enemies, mounts (you can ride a dragon), and more. I had alot of fun customizing Talion.

[b]The story is what failed to grab me.[/b] Continuing from the previous game 'Shadow or Mordor', the game follows Talion, a ranger from the black gate seeking revenge for the murder of his family and bonded with a wraith of the elf Celebrimbor. The ring of power is taken from you in act 1 but you get it back later to build your orc army. But the events after the first act started to feel pretty boring and I felt a lack of progression with our main characters (you do see how their goals and ideals differ and how that affects their relationship towards the end of the game). If you played the game with just the story missions in mind it would be a pretty short ride (around 10 or 15 hours?). I have almost 40 hours played and feel bored from the lack content. The content that exist isnt anything to write home about either. It standard and what you would expect. The side missions add onto and build on the existing lore from the books but I hear from LotR fanatics that the game kind of ignores parts of the lore altogether. This is my biggest issue about the game.

Some final thoughts:
-It sounds great
-Game is challenging and rewarding (YOU WILL DIE)
-I love the mounts/monsters (eating orcs with graugs is really satisfying)


[b] tldr; If you like the idea of the nemesis system, have played the previous game, or love LotR, then buy this game on SALE. [/b]

The difficulty is up there and not for those who cower in the face of a challenge.  Everything is well thought out from the estate, to the heroes, to the battles and bosses themselves.

The only con I can say about this game is the difficulty.  This is an unforgiving game and can be unfair (just slightly unfair).  I have a few friends who loved watching me play, but when they played, it proved to be too difficult for them.  I personally take this a pro and not a con.  Mistakes and bad planning should be punished and good plans with calculated risks are rewarded.

In the few times I've had to contact the Dev's, my experience has been pleasant and helpful.

在打折期间入了普通的传奇版，评论里主要都是讨论缺点的，大家对这些也都心知肚明，我就不多说这些了，本人主玩mt模式，多介绍一下争霸赛，希望给大家一些有帮助的经验

因为这几个版本的游戏都有很多不太合理的地方，所以玩起来其实每个模式应该都比较吃力，那我举例来说，个人非常喜欢传导球，但是这几个版本感觉非常不鼓励传球，特别是这个版本的黄油手，我是真的想骂街，下面进入正题

1.争霸赛是个人感觉在mt模式里比较有意思也非常超值的模式，在99星通过普通的争霸赛之后，会有三选一紫卡球员，其中阿泰斯特非常推荐，防守很强，三分也比较稳，对阵游戏中数值超高的流氓球员，可以进行很有效的防守干扰；在通关历史争霸赛之后，会有4个红宝石球员，两个紫水晶和一个钻石球员，可以极大的增强球队实力。全通之后还可以再从之前剩下的两个紫卡球员中再选择一个，个人认为通关争霸赛十分必要；另外今年加入了全时争霸赛，99通关之后，还会有钻石三选一，个人非常推荐昂塞尔德。

2.氪金玩家忽略这条，大家初始阵容需要一些很好的金银绿宝石卡球员，在这里推荐一下，金卡波神，绿色的贾巴里帕克，金卡西蒙斯，雄鹿的银卡中锋。。应该是叫梅克，这个b当时在我不会打时，在每周挑战里给我打尿了，我就记住他了，当自己的资金上来之后，入红卡詹姆斯和哈登，说实话pc端球员比ps4那边便宜很多，大家别多花没用的钱，要善用拍卖行

3.讲一下最基本的打法，具体的不在这里多说，个人认为在争霸赛里对抗电脑，打最简单的突分最为有效，当有比较强的突破和终结能力球员之后杀进去造犯规，在空中多做一些骚动作，增加对抗，裁判很容易响哨给罚球，找机会分出去三分，当你造成比较大的突破杀伤时，电脑会开始包夹，这时候不要硬打，找机会分球，会很容易得分，在防守端尽力防守，别被人一步过，电脑设置的很不合理，像蜜汁漏人，被人射三分，或者被人各种不讲理进球，随它去吧，保证好心态，这样一来二去，分差就拉开了

4.历史争霸赛有一点很讨厌，你如果mt币挣得不够，拿不到三星，非常恶心，最好入手一个火箭的教练德安东尼，非常便宜，炮轰战术可以加快节奏，钱会比较多，另一个就是背身单打，这是钱最多的打法，可惜感觉这个版本背身不是很强，不是特别推荐

5.我打的pc端今年，感觉比ps4球员便宜很多，阵容比较好，我哥们还是ps4，用零碎的时间打2k，现在全时应该只剩一关了，出去浪了没打，他的阵容到后期才有红色球员，主要就是绿卡蓝卡也都打过去了，所以事实证明还是可以打的，就是有些恶心，我这几天刷夜过了普通和历史，全时有些打不动了，稍微缓缓。。

今年的2k确实还有很多不好的地方，可这还是一个非常不错的游戏，建议打折入手，光是和同学打打快速吹吹牛逼，也挺好的，网的问题没法评价，我和朋友在欧洲念书，连服务器没啥问题，线上还是不太流畅，所以也不咋玩线上
PS：说实话我刚开始也是想在这里臭骂一顿的，但是发现好像能骂的都被人骂完了哈哈，就希望在这里给大家介绍一下有用的小经验，希望能给新人玩家一些帮助，也希望2k自己心里多点B数，让我们能玩的开心点

[h1]Tomb Raider é um excelente jogo de aventura[/h1]

       Tomb Raider, em português, assaltante de túmulos, é um jogo de aventura com elementos de fantasia e puzzle, em terceira pessoa, se tratando de um Reboot de toda a saga Tomb Raider (infelizmente nem todos sabe disso) antecessor do Rise of the Tomb Raider. 

        A saga Tomb Raider  já sofreu vários reboots e alterações individuais ao longo da história, e quem conhece Lara Croft, sabe que ela é uma anti-heroína, fria, calculista e mortal ( porém acredito que com este reboot, eles vão aliviar estas características) [spoiler] além de ser muito gostosa[/spoiler] . Se ela ta caminhando na rua, e um cara da um oi pra ela, ela mete bala. Se aparecer um mendigo pedindo esmola, ela mete bala. Se aparecer um carinha querendo limpar o para-brisa, ela mete bala. Se aparecer um pinguim perguntando as horas, ela mete bala. 

        Tomb Raider, é um jogo que foca nos acontecimentos que levam a protagonista, Lara Croft, a ser o descrito acima. Apesar de alguns jogos da franquia, já retratarem ou mencionarem estes acontecimentos, nenhum deles, foca SOMENTE nisso. Por exemplo, ela pede desculpa, depois de matar um cervo para se alimentar. Por questões como esta, ocasionalmente vejo alguns jogadores reclamarem do jogo, dizendo que Lara é muito chorona e tals, porém são estes que nem se quer sabem do que se trata o jogo.

       Enfim, o enredo começa com Lara realizando sua primeira expedição a fim de encontrar o reino perdido de Yamatai. Yamatai é um reino MUITO ANTIGO numa ilha localizada no triangulo do dragão, oceano pacifico, historicamente, protegido por poderes e guardiões sobrenaturais. Yamatai, foi governada pela primeira e ultima rainha Himiko (lembre-se deste trecho). Quando o navio chega as proximidades da ilha, ele é atingido por uma fortíssima tempestade e é destruído em pedaços. Lara acaba se separando dos outros sobreviventes e é nocauteada por alguem desconhecido. O jogo ai segue tendo como objetivo principal, reagrupar com os outros sobreviventes de sua embarcação. Os detalhas da história da ilha, assim como os diarios de outros tripulantes e sobreviventes de outras embarcações, podem ser descobertos através de secrets espalhados pela ilha (eu acho extremamente recomendável encontra-los). Os personagens secundários não são muito bem desenvolvidos, pois você passa apenas poucos e breves momentos com eles e também encontrar alguns vídeos e diários, mas mesmo assim, você acaba se simpatizando com alguns deles.
         Em relação ao gameplay, você irá encontrar vários quick time events( se você gostar ou não, vai depender do seu gosto), a parte de tiro é totalmente Arcade, sendo que a Inteligência Artificial dos inimigos é boa, eles dão cover, tentam de flanquear, pegar por trás, rusham na hora certa, etc.  O jogo tem um modo de visão que destaca objetos-chave para seguir em frente, nesta visão, todos os objetos não importantes são mantidos em tons de cinza e importantes em amarelo. Ela realmente facilitou MUITO os puzzles (eu achei nenhum deles difícil). 
         A ambientação em considero o melhor aspecto do jogo. Paisagens lindas e ambientes horrendos, muito bem detalhados.
         Os gráficos são legais (não me importo muito com isso).
         As animações são muito bem feitas.
         Infelizmente não posso avaliar o mulitiplayer devido a que sempre estão sozinho numa partida.
         Como um comentário final, infelizmenete, eu achei o jogo curto. Na primeira jogatina, somei 10 horas de gameplay no modo difícil e explorando em torno de 78%, provavelmente 13 horas com 100%.

        
	Nota final 9.1/10

Darksiders 3 ist anders als die anderen Teile. Es deutlich schwerer. Gerade vom Anfang bis gegen Mitte des Spiel, stirbt man sehr oft und das auf einen normalen Schwierigkeitsgrad. Wodurch es Dark Souls Ähnlichkeiten hat. Aber dieses ausgelieferte Gefühl hatte ich gegen Ende nicht mehr. Was neu ist, das man eingesammelte/verdiente Seelen bei Vulgrim gegen Level Erfahrung abgeben kann. Hat man eine bestimmte Anzahl erreicht steigt der Charakter ein Level auf und man kann z.B seine Gesundheit verbessern. Waffen können bei ihm nicht mehr verbessert werden, dafür brauch man bestimmte Dinge, die man aber erst kaufen oder finden muss. Die Story kam insgesamt nicht richtig in fahrt, liegt aber auch daran, das fast alles von Anfang an klar war, was zu tun ist. Technisch hatte ich keine Probleme, bei maximalen Einstellungen (9900K, RTX 2070), keine Drops, Abstürze oder Bugs. Steuerung ist auch ein Tick anders, aber den Dreh hat man schnell raus. Mit einem Controller wunderbar spielbar. Es gibt in Darksiders III viel einzusammeln bzw. zu suchen. Wie z.B Items zum heilen oder Seelenpacks. Natürlich gibt es hier auch wieder einige Boss Gegner, die gut gemacht worden sind. 

Was nicht so schön ist, das Speichern/die Checkpoints. Nach dem Tod startet man immer bei dem letzten Vulgrim Spot. Und muss z.B wieder zum Boss laufen. Der mal näher oder mal weiter weg ist. Andere Spiele starten nach dem Tod direkt den Boss Kampf neu und nehmen nicht das Action Gefühl raus. Gerade wenn man erst im Spiel klar kommen muss, denn im richtigen Moment ausweichen ist hier lebenswichtig. Und man seinen besten Schwierigkeitsgrad herausfinden muss. Letztendlich bin ich auf dem leichtesten hängen geblieben. Ab Mitte bis Ende war er letztendlich zu leicht, da ich auch schon fast Level 60 war. Weil ich einen Sammeltrieb habe und gerne alles mögliche finden möchte. Man kann zwar jederzeit den Schwierigkeitsgrad ändern, dennoch shit, da man für "normalen Schwierigkeitsgrad Errungenschaft" das ganze Spiel damit gespielt haben muss. Also dabei gelassen und keine Nerven verloren :)  

Rätsel sind auch vorhanden, aber sie sind nicht herausfordernd. Aber das fand ich ok, denn mit Darksiders verbinde ich persönlich mit Hack and Slash Kämpfen.

Insgesamt sollte man das Spiel im Angebot kaufen. Denn 60 € für ein Spiel das November 2018 raus gekommen ist, ist viel zu hoch. Bis 20 € alles wunderbar. Darksiders 1 und 2  haben ein besseres harmonischeres Gesamtverhältnis. Dennoch ist der dritte Teil nicht schlecht und macht, wenn man weiß wie alles funktioniert Spaß.

PD2 is mainly one of these first person shooters with hordes of enemies to shoot and that you play in COOP, if you're looking for a heist game with a little more subtle approach, look elsewhere.

The premise of having a stealth system and doing heists is nice on the paper, until you realize that doing heists is basically doing a perfect stealth run that requires a perfect organization to be successful, something you'll not be able to do after a few hours unless you are lucky as I was and had a friend to tutor me through. However, the exercise remains quite frustrating because the bugs, the fact that the AI can bullshit-spot you a and the fact that the developers do not seem to care a lot about it, nor have made any improvements.

Instead, what you are going to do most of the time, is playing a left for dead clone, with perks and levels to keep you doing the same missions over and over and shoot the same hordes of zombies... I mean cops over and over to get unlocks and that's where it gets pretty bad as the game is plagued with DLCs and micro transactions. Be aware, that once you've paid for the base game, you've only paid for the right to stare at all the content you need to buy through DLCs, which you're eventually going to do, because humans don't like to be left behind or reminded they've less than others. Aren't games supposed to be a space where you want to forget about the harsh things of life ? Oh, never mind. This game is gateway, a service, not a product and it is the worse kind of service you could get because micro-transactions allow you to unlock random weapons skins that improve stats of weapons you may not own because they're in the DLC you do not have (yet). At this point, going to the casino is probably less exploitative than this because you may eventually get some money, here its just some virtual shit. While I can understand the developers need to make a living out of their game and constantly produce content for it, there was a time where they didn't use exploitative means such as these and created expansion packs and sequels when they wanted to add new content.

Its a shame game design has become that exploitative of people's impulses and here we are talking about an "indie" developer who's playing the same card as Activision, Ubisoft or EA. However, they seem to have seen realized it since the community was pretty vocal about what I mentioned (even if some flaws will remain forever) as they have recently apologized and promised to improve the situation here : http://steamcommunity.com/games/218620/announcements/detail/85928399508949511. Apologizing for making people angry because they realized how exploitative the design of your game could be doesn’t change the core of the issue, only a new game could.

TL-DR : Its a coop shooter with a flawed stealth system that has a lot of content to buy and unlock to make sure they exploit your ego and desires to get more stuff in order to get stuff and then buy more stuff because your friends have it. Once you stop playing, you'll feel like you could have played something else and had the same fun with your friends and probably paid less.

I hated this game when I started playing this a year back. The reason being, I was all into Tom Clancy's The Division at that time which is a nearly perfect third person shooter, and same I was expecting from Fallout 4. (Just to let you know this was my first Fallout). 

However, there was something in the game which always kept calling me back and now I am at 549 hours with it.

This game is absolutely amazing. The environment is growing with you, and not just some part of it,, the whole of it. That is why it's shooting initially sucked as later I realized my protagonist did not have enough skills to shoot properly. The personality of your character grows as you play along which are divided in various aspects such as persuasion, strength, ability to take rads, scavenging, talking, etc etc etc.. I would say,, this is the best RPG I have ever played. Immersion of the character is just huge, much more than GTA or Mass Effect. You can build house, settlements, recruit people, assign them to tasks, create new weapons, have a girlfriend or BF, take side with any faction.. and I am not even touching the mods yet. You can not play this game in COD style, that's like eating pizza like a soup noodle. This game has its world and you need to go along with it. So far this game has been incredible. All of the new mechanics added to this game has really made it that more engaging and challenging. 

What I wish to put forward are aspects of the game that could/need to be improved. 
Natural Disasters:
- Natural Disasters are too helpful most of the time. The yields from many of them outweigh the initial damage. There needs to be more of a downside. Greater damage output from these. Volcanoes should have ash clouds that cover a certain radius and damages food and other yields. Hurricanes should cause lasting flood damage. etc. 
- New disasters such as earthquakes and tsunami's should be added. 
- New higher levels of disaster intensity. 
- Don't shy away from having districts outright destroyed 

AI:
- Stop having AI kill every city state in sight! Especially if that city state is your's and the AI is a declared friend. 
- Stop AI form accusing  and denouncing the player of warmonger penalties if they are regularly going to war was well. 
- AI still cannot go to war against the player very well. 

Civs: 
- All the new civs are great, but this leaves many of the vanilla civs very lacking. Please consider boosting some of the vanilla civs to keep pace with the new civs just added. I would not recommend nerfing the new ones. 

Resources:
- There needs to be more resource diversity in the game. Many of the resources are too generic and don't go far enough. Such as fish. This resource could be broken into various fish, each having a slightly different yield. I would definitely recommend looking at the Resourceful 2 mod for some ideas. 
- Make all strategic resources relevant in the late game. Combine coal and iron to make steel for late game warships and tanks. Use horse and niter for the calvary unit, horse and iron for knights, etc. Make all resources relevant throughout the game. 
- Create finished products that can be sold through the various types of resources (bonus, luxury, strategic). Right now resources are just had in a raw form that we work with a tile improvement. Take it a step further and use it to create items that can be sold. 

Spies:
- Expand on their range to sabotage any district. But allow them to specialize on which district when given a promotion. If the sabotage option is available, have a second list show which district. This could help focus damage depending on which victory type the enemy is going for. 
- Relics should be stolen. 
- Please make it a bit easier to fabricate scandals, I can almost never get this done. 

Wonders:
- Many of the religious wonders should have a relic slot or two. 
- Bring back the ability to theme wonders 
- Please return national wonders. Have 2-3 for each district with various requirements. They could be built in the district or on a tile next to it. Permit only one to be build per city. 

Other:
- Have a fission power plant available after the nuclear power plant that creates no CO2 emmissions in the last era. 
- Please have a tile improvement for rainforest 
- Natural wonders are still difficult to create because of the mandatory up-right diamond shape. Please get rid of that. It should be able to be created for any 4 connecting tiles of the right appeal. 
         - This should also include coastline and lakes for having appeal 
- Rock Bands need some kind of counter.
- Keep unique tile improvements, districts, and buildings of cities you take from others. Let there more of a boost/reward for taking cities. 
- Have a means of removing a district from a tile!

완벽한 그래픽이 더 완벽해져서 돌아왔고, 쩔었던 BGM이 더 쩔어져서 돌아왔지만 스토리와 번역만큼은 그렇지 못했다. 액션성은 훌륭하고 서브퀘스트 또한 분위기와 스토리에 잘 녹아든다. 전작인 오리와 가시 존나 많은 숲이 그러했듯, 이번에도 자비없는 가시들이 맵마다 깔려있고, 이가 부족했다고 생각했는지 레이스 기능까지 추가하여 오리에게 다시 한 번 가시밭길을 선사했다. 

그러나 이전작의 메인 빌런이었던 쿠로와 오리의 관계를 생각해볼 때, 이번 작의 메인 빌런 칼날소리는 쿠로와 달리 오리와 사생결단을 낼 이유가 없고, 이는 오리의 입장에서도 마찬가지이다. 이번 작의 오리가 구르는 이유가 와닿지 않고, 어디까지나 '남의 일'이라고 생각되는 이유는 어째서일까. 

게다가 성우와 맞지 않는 번역 상태는 몰입을 방해하다 못해 짜증마저 불러일으킨다. 높임말과 예삿말을 섞어서 번역한 놈이 누군진 모르겠지만 광화문 광장의 세종대왕 상 앞을 지나간다면 누군가 뱉어놓은 싱싱한 껌을 밟길 간절히 기도하겠다.

다만 이 모든 단점들을 덮어둘 정도로 게임성과 그래픽, 오케스트라는 완벽했다. 오리와 도깨비불은 전작의 명성을 잇기에 충분한 작품이고, 게임을 예술이라 칭할 때 빠져선 안 되는 작품임에는 분명하다.

- level design, de jolis paysages / points de vue
- il tourne bien... (en même temps il ya pas grand chose à afficher)

Les - :

Ark foisonne de vie, la faune et la flore sont abondantes et diversifiées, les biomes sont vraiment différents.
Grosse déception, je cherchais un nouveau survival pour remplacer Ark, mais ce jeu m'a juste  donner envie d'y rejouer.

Avec les attaques de camps de PNJs qui repop rapidement, et le mode de combat Conan ressemble plus à Guild Wars 2 qu'à Ark. Mais ça serait insulter Guild Wars 2 qui est excellent.

Having Jeff Goldblum narrate a game is basically like pouring warm caramel in your ears. Hot, smooth and just a little bit sticky. But in reality, it’s all just part of the immersion for Jurassic World Evolution. First, the dinos, because with over 40 species to unlock, there are plenty of them, just as you’d hope. From the ostrich-like Struthiomimus, to Triceratops and Brachiosaurus. 

Regardless of the species, it feels like each dinosaur has a distinct personality, and that doesn’t just come from not the way they behave or misbehave in the park. Each dino has a status panel that you can view to check up on how happy they are, although, trust me, you’ll know when they’re not.

It’s just a shame that at certain points you’ll be furiously leafing through the game’s fairly awful help menus for a way to figure out exactly how to do that thing the Security Guy just asked you to do.

None of that detracts from the fact that Jurassic World Evolution is a smart, expertly crafted dinosaur theme park sim, balancing immense joy with a constant low key nausea for the inevitable perils that come with running a dinosaur theme park. It’s full of the kinds of intricacies you’d hope for in a Jurassic Park game, the fantastic management sim mechanics that Frontier is famed for, lovely little nods and references to the movie series and, honestly, why wouldn’t you want to play a game that lets you drive your own gyrosphere through the legs of a T-Rex? It’s true, life always finds a way, but in Jurassic World Evolution it’s all in your hands.

I started out as a really tall and breasty wanderer. 
In the middle of what looked like an abandoned bar during a menacing sand storm. 
I roam around wrecked houses and loot anything that fits my small inventory.
I find the local bar where I sell my stuff and buy some food for my empty stomach and immediately devour the dry meat. 
Someone sitting at a table asks to have a drink with me, being poor as shit I oblige and go listen to the old man's tales. 
Some insane mumbling but! I see a nice opportunity. I recruit him into my awesome nameless_0 squad and take off his clothes to use them for myself, leaving him with rag pants.
Then I use him to work the mines in order to get some quick cash. 

Foolish me decided that it's too slow and I wanted a quick boost so I decide to steal, I move to a bigger city and go steal from the best place (training camp, prison) I thought that by sneaking and stealing stuff when no one is on the floor with you - you get away unscathed. Foolish. As soon as I leave the town a guard chases me asking to check my bag, I decline and decide to fight for my life - my intent being: run as fast as you can.
Sadly, the guard is faster and he one shot K.Od me. I end up with a critical chest injury and caged. 
After a while I regain conscious and I almost starve - few days pass and I end up a slave.
I break away thanks to the tools I stole from the guards and return to my mine now forever branded a slave...
And here is my adventure stands (for now) after 1.7hours in game and 2 attempts.
