THE GOOD:
-Game is graphically great, everything looks as good or better than ETS2. You should be able to run this at the same settings as ETS2. You can also copy over your configs from ETS2. Just go to *\Documents\Euro Truck Simulator 2\profiles\###### and copy all the .sii files then go to *\Documents\American Truck Simulator\profiles\(same #### as ETS2) and paste them in there.
-Gameplay is just as fun as ETS2
-Trailer dropoffs are more varied. You can have them do it for you for no bonus XP, "do it safely" which is an easy dropoff and gives you some bonus XP or you can do it for real which is usually difficult for 40-90XP. There's an option in the menu to just choose one but you can always have them park it for you or change the dropoff point if it turns out to be too hard.
-There's a huge amount of environmental pieces and NPCs. Driving through the desert you'll see tumbleweeds rolling across the road, helicopters flying by, airplanes and even military jets zooming over, parasailers, blimps and just so many little details that keep things interesting and keep you looking around for the next little detail.
-Devs are dedicated to it and have promised support for a long time. They did the same for ETS2 so I have no doubts they'll continue working on this.

THE BAD
-Game is limited right now. There's only California and Nevada along with 2 trucks. SCS has promised to continue adding states and they're working on Arizona right now. There's licensing problems with the trucks but they'll add in more as they get that sorted out. This will no longer be a problem in the future but at least both states have a lot of road and detail it still feels small.
-Traffic AI is really bad. Lots of cars/trucks driving straight into you without braking or caring. While it is a realistic depiction of American drivers, it makes for very frustrating gameplay.
-Police are harsh. America doesn't have a bunch of speed cameras so instead they added in random police cars that will ding you for going a few over the speed limit. Some people have said that it seems like the police are more lenient on highways and stricter with backroads which might be true but I haven't verified this. It's a good new system but extremely rough on new players.
-Fines are huge. $900 for speeding. $800 for running a red light, even if you stop a bit late but aren't blocking traffic. Once you get some money flow coming in it isn't a big deal but it's hard on new players. It was the same thing in ETS2 however with the new police system it's a lot easier to get ticketed for speeding so it racks up fast.

Overall, it's a fantastic game and to put it simply it's an improved version of ETS2 but set in America. There's only 2 states and trucks at the moment but there will be more in the future. It's well worth the $20 asking price and will provide just as much entertainment and fun as ETS2 does.

This game is fun, as long as you don't care about actually winning a campaign.  I've played both the 1984 and 2000 campaigns, while accomplishing most missions with the occassional damage from enemy weapons fire (maybe 1 out of 15 engagements resulted in me actually taking damage).  In most cases, your submarine could survive one hit from an enemy torpedo, maybe even a second if you were quick to respond to damage and flooding from the first.  Enjoy that confidence in your sub and crew, because it will come to a screeching halt in the final mission of the campaign.

When you get to undoubtedly the final mission of either campaign, when Russia or China sorties their ballistic missile subs; all your previous expectations will fly right out the window.  Prepare to have a swarm of torpedos fired at you from enemy crews that apparently have a sudden boost in training, intelligence, reaction time (like 1 second), and just a single torpedo strike will take you out of the fight.  And don't worry about doing an emergency ballast blow or abandoning ship.  Your crew will be dead, campaign over, thanks for playing, now start all over at the beginning!

I'm sure reality is far less forgiving than this game, but it's particularly frustrating to have this final mission thrown at you with the deck stacked against you to this degree.  It's one thing for a game to get progressively harder as you play it, but this game is so blatantly making the final campaign mission deliberately impossible to accomplish, makes me want to throw my moniter through the window.  I rarely feel this much frustration with a video game, but the fact I'm writing my first player review of a video game ever (been gaming since the early 90's) should speak to how angry I am at how the devs have made the final campaign mission.

日本語化すると「Half-Life Japanese Caption Ver」というものができ、そちらからゲームを起動することになります。
なのでHalf-Lifeにプレイ時間は記録されません。自分も日本語化したのでプレイ時間が極端に短くなっていますが、難易度普通で一度クリアしました。
チートコマンドで無敵になったりすることも可能ですが、それだとゲームを始めからやり直す必要があります。
途中から「敵が強いからここからはチートを使おう・・・」ということはできません。

ゲームの中身についてです
なかなか面白いゲームでした、当時名作と言われただけはあると思います。
しかし当然目新しいわけではないので今の時代の人がやると「どこが名作？」となってしまうかもしれません。
ランボースタイルで無双するようなゲームではなく敵に囲まれたりどこに位置取りをすれば一度に複数の敵を相手にせずに済むかを考えながら、あるいは死にながら進んでいくゲームです。このゲームの面白さはそこにあると感じました。

自分は難易度は普通でやりましたが難しく感じました、昔の海外のゲームは難易度ノーマルやミディアムでもなかなか手ごたえのある難しさだという話を聞いたことがありますがこのゲームもそれに洩れずといった感じです。

ゲームを始めた時に最初に戸惑う点としては床が凍っているのか？といわんばかりにツルツル滑るような感触があることです。初代カウンターストライクをやったことがある人ならその感覚に経験があると思います。現在のFPSならシフトを押しながら移動ですがこのゲームの場合シフトを押さないとそれが走るになります。
走っている人間は急には止まれないということでしょうかね。

Duck game es un juego de accion, plataformas, battle royal, en el que controlamos patos. Consiste en eliminar a nuestros oponentes con el uso de diversas armas distribuidas por el nivel. Duck game nos presenta un gran numero de armas para acabar con nuestros enemigos, de las cuales, todas matan de un golpe (disparo). 
El juego es muy facil de entender, con batallas rapidas y dinamicas. Cuando quede un ganador en pantalla cambiara al instante el ecenario y reapareceran todos los patos. EL primer pato en hacer 10 puntos gana.
Con duck game tienes risas aseguradas, las mecanicas del juego lo hacen muy gracioso y divertido, sobretodo si juegas con mas personas. Es mas recomendable jugar con amigos, esto hace la experiencia mucho mas valiosa.
Las batallas las hay desde simples hasta totalmente freneticas y caoticas, cargadas de adrenalina, gracias al buen diseño de los niveles en que se desarrollan los combates y el gameplay rapido de este. Puedes jugar con una persona en un 1 vs 1 o con tres en un todos contra todos, con la opcion de 2 vs 2.
El juego tambien cuenta con un modo para un jugador que consiste en challenges que debes completar. Este modo se siente mas para introducir al jugador a las mecanicas de juego, pero, deja mucho que desear como la implementacion de un modo de juego para un jugador igual al online (no puedes luchar contra bots en modo un jugador, solo esta el modo arcade que tiene los challenges).
Graficamente el juego tiene un estilo retro el cual queda muy bien con todo lo que ocurre en pantalla. nada se siente fuera de lugar y tiene algunos detalles visuales que resultan muy divertidos.
Duck game tiene una comunidad que constantemente crea mapas y mods para el juego puesto que tiene un editor de niveles. Puedes jugar los niveles creados por otros jugadores y crear mapas propios, el editor es facil de entender y con una gran variedad de opciones.
El soundtrack: Duck game tiene canciones que son energeticas y muy acorde a lo que ocurre en pantalla, canciones que son disfrutables y aportan a la experiencia de juego al igual que tiene unas que, si no estan tan fuera de lugar, dejan mucho que desear y a veces llega a molestar.
Duck game posee muchas mas cosas interesantes. es un juego muy divertido que vale completamente la pena jugarlo. Lo recomiendo completamente para todos.

After seeing THEY ARE BILLIONS for just a few moments on Twitch, I decided that this is a game for me. A Base-building system that strongly reminded me of my late 90es RTS, when Unit-Spamming and One-Unit-Rushes were still a thing of the future and you could do all kinds of weird things to just make your opponents game harder. Then the first wave hits, and suddenly it becomes more of a Tower-Defense Strategy game, a genre that, for me, took over from RTS as the strategy game where you had to plan, think and take it slow, no matter how intense the action got. Overall, the game combined all that I loved about Strategy Games.

Let casual players be warned: While this game can absolutely be learned, it will take a few tries and actually seeing what you did wrong at what point and learning from those mistakes. It took me several attempts before I won my first game. Also, this game may be extremely intense, but each session takes hours. Again, something I love, in a time of 20-Minute Sessions, I want to take my time on each map, and I probably spent more time figuring out my base layout that most RTS these days take per session. 

However, once you realize the workings of THEY ARE BILLIONS, it isn't that hard anymore, it is fair, requiring you to do things right of course, but as impossible as even a 10% map may feel during your first few attempts, when a rogue Zombie infects your whole colony, you can quickly get the hang of it and then work on your strategy.

Which is something you need to adjust every session. The maps layout, your progress in clearing and expanding, the amount of military units you command, it is all very situational. Watch any game anyone has ever played, after a few ingame days, they will have to adjust to their situation and no map will play out the same. It's challenging and a lot of fun, even if you end up losing, because even that may feel like a success. 

The first time I made it to the end of a game, and got the notice that the entire horde is apporaching from literally everywhere, I knew right away that I lost, but I was smiling the entire time that they tore my puny excuse for a defense to shreds. The lessons from the map were quickly drawn and clear as day: I lacked ressources, which had me lack workers, which had me lack military might, and the final wave includes every Zombie left on the map. The solution: Expand more agressively, kill whatever you can find before the final wave and conserve ressources whenever possible. Sure enough, the next Map I played, I scored my first win at measly 55%, but it was a win. 

But the most positive thing I can say about the game: Time flies when playing it. I tend to play games for maybe an hour at a time, leave it on idle and then play again when I feel like it. At least a third of my huge amount of hours playing Skyrim was the game just idling with me doing other things, my 48 Hour Playthrough of Elex took me 72 hours runtime. But when I sit down at 6 pm to play a bit of THEY ARE BILLIONS, I check my watch after what feels like minutes and realize that three hours have flown by as if they were nothing. Those 17.6 hours I currently have on record are all playtime, no idling. The game is addictive, captivating and immensely fun to play for longer sessions. Add to that the natural but fair difficulty level, a superb mix of high intensity combat and long, thought through planning when building your base, and I've got myself probably my favourite RTS this decade!

I cannot praise it enough, if this wall of words don't state that already. From seeing it on Twitch and thinking "This seems like Steampunk Age of Empires with Zombies with charming graphics" through having an army of Archers wiping the entire map clean to anxiously waiting for the final horde to step in front of my Titans' Cannons, THEY ARE BILLIONS is a superb RTS that combines everything I love about this game genre. I can't wait for the campaign and can say with confidence that this game is a masterpiece for Strategy Game Fans!

The story is well written. Even though it ends the same (same ending place and mechanic), you can change some little bits to make the main character more cruel, nice, or just friendly. The story doesn't seem out of place and it fits well with the game mechanic. The characters of the game have personalities that are not "average", possibly explaining why they have survived so long.

The game itself is easy to play and to understand. It does a good job of explaining itself, but still has lightly hidden things that can only be found if you decide to take a closer look. These hidden things can get you a better score, make activities easier, reveal more of the story.

The game itself can be difficult at times, especially on your first playthrough. You will probably find yourself cycling through your saves, trying to get a better result for a night. This might sound bad, but it makes the game more fun (though maybe a little more repetetive).

Because of the multiple scenario combinations, the game has replay value. [spoiler] If you use one of the disks in the ending, you also get NG+, leading to the true ending.  After this, you also unlock the custom game mode. [/spoiler] There are the achievements too. Combine all this, and you can get more than those 2-5 hours on your first playthrough.

I recommend this game. It is worth the money. Buy it. Trust me, I have almost 50 hours of play time and every achievement.

This game is pretty mediocre, honestly. Usually I would say "try this game" but its flaws were too much for me.

The definite highlights for me were the exploration and the combat. If you take the time to explore, you'll gain unlocks to upgrade your skills and weapons and get "extras" that you can see from the main menu. The combat is pretty good as well which was surprising to me. I kinda expected it to be just "functional", as in not terrible but not exceptional either, but the weapon customization options really added depth to it. Plus the enemy AI is surprisingly competent, throwing grenades to force you out of cover and constantly flanking you. But sadly these two nice mechanics are held back by the game's flaws.

Let's talk about the thing I disliked the most which was the movement. For a game with a large emphasis on exploration, the movement system is absolutely atrocious because of how slow and unresponsive it is. For some reason you cannot sprint, which combined with large maps it can slow everything down to a halt, especially when you're looking for that one last task to do to finish a challenge. And the platforming seems to be functional about 50% of the time. I lost count of the amount of times I've failed ledge grabs for no reason at all. Sometimes you grab it from a mile away, sometimes you just... don't. It can really ruin the exploration experience.

Notice how I specifically praised the combat and not the gameplay in general, because honestly it's all over the place. The game goes from a mediocre platformer to a great cover based third-person shooter to bad "on rails" segments to terrible, frustrating QTEs. It really sucks that these bad parts are not exclusive to one section or level of the game, they're present from start to finish. I don't think I will replay the game because of these issues.

Some cutscenes are really sexualizing. There's a particularly egregious cutscene where the camera has this top down view that was very obviously done in a way to make you see down Lara's cleavage. Strangely, these cutscenes are only at the beginning of the game, so it's not that bad. But still, I really wish developers didn't do this because it undermines the tone of the game.

Now let's talk about some smaller details:

I've avoided mentioning the story because I found it pretty forgettable, but that probably has to do with the fact that I skimmed through the lore.
The graphics are pretty alright (everything maxed out). It's not the best looking game ever, or even the best looking game from 2013 in my opinion, but it has some really nice vistas and effects. Lara's hair is pretty glitchy if you're using the TressFX option. And some animations look really strange.
The game has some difficulty spikes (I played on hard). Sometimes you breeze through parts like it's nothing, sometimes you get stuck for several minutes.
I did not play the multiplayer and have no plans to, so it does not affect this review in any way.
There's one character that doesn't fit into the story and feels like a self-insert from a developer. I won't go into details to avoid spoilers but you'll notice when you play the game.
The game crashed several times during my playthrough.
The camera shakes a lot so if you get motion sickness easily avoid this game.
There's not a lot of actual tomb raiding. In fact, the tombs are entirely optional. It's really just Tomb Raider in the title only.


TL;DR: The game is meh.

Ну, думаю, заполучив все ачивки, я имею право написать обзор.
Если коротко, то берите игру в любом случае (Если вы не любитель ферм и прочего казуального дерьма). Игра КАК МИНИМУМ 9/10. Я более чем уверен, что ганжн понравится любому любителю сложноватых игр. Если же вы не особо любите учиться играть, набирать скилл, и вам нужно всё и сразу, то эту игру вы вряд ли полюбите, здесь скилл приходит постепенно.
Для начала хотелось бы сказать, что разрабы этой игры невероятно щедрые. Они постоянно добавляют в игру кучу контента за просто так, не в качестве длс. Похвально.
Перейдем к самой игре.
Геймплей нереально затягивающий, мало того, что сам процесс игры приносит удовольствие, так ещё и контента, который надо разблокировать и опробовать, здесь тонны. В игре изначально 4 персонажа +2, которых нужно открыть. Игр, где есть несколько персонажей, довольно много, но игр, где принуждают проходить игру за каждого пеpсонажа можно пересчитать по пальцам. В том же айзеке прохождение за разных персонажей открывает разные предметы, здесь же, помимо предметов, у каждого персонажа своя концовка.
Графика может и не понравится некоторым, но лично мне она показалась приятной, хоть пиксели я не особо люблю. Всё здесь прорисовано довольно мило, анимировано тоже приятно.
К сожалению о музыке мало чего могу сказать, она не плохая, но чет не зацепила. Из 150 часов, около сотни я играл со своей музыкой. А вот звуки оружия, врагов и прочего подходят идеально.
Сеттинг оружия, пуль и всего подобного выбран и исполнен на высочайшем уровне, на каждом углу есть шутки, отсылки и т.д. и т.п. В ганжене ещё куева хуча всяких приятных мелочей и моментов, которые вы откроете для себя, советую купить его как можно быстрее.

Subnautica isn't so much a survival game as it is an exploration game, and a very well paced one at that. 

You will need to build a base, but in order to make it truly sustainable, you need to branch out. Each biome has new things to discover, which will help you to explore further and deeper. The system makes the gameplay extremely well paced. The progression isn't about becoming more powerful than your environment, but rather better able to reach out further, and discovery more of what the world has in store.

The greatest value in the game isn't the base-building, however. It is the very real sense of discovery you will feel as you encounter new fauna and flora which are truly breathtaking. 

That said, the gameplay itself is not challenging at all. The game is not about skill or tactics; just calm exploration.

I've seen a lot of complaints about this game, so let's try and iron a few out.

1: "The characters have little depth/backstory/are forgettable". To some extent this is true, however if you paid attention in the first 5 mniutes of the campaign Daniels says something along the lines of "Zussman was the only one i knew after basic". This is really important for the context of the setting. Often in WW2 soldiers barely knew anyone after signing up or leaving training. Zussman is a main character along with Piersen, the rest are arguably supporting characters and excel at that role, providing a middle ground for dialogue between Daniels and Zussman as not to draw out a back and forth between 2 characters. The problem is everyone is so used to being forced to be attatched to a character for the cliche moment they eventually die and I think the devs were effective in avoiding this

2: "The campaign is too short": This is the most true of the criticisms. They had a long time to get this sorted and a 6 hour campaign to cover the epic of World War Two is frankly not good enough. A lot of people called for a Russian campaign (i dont agree at all, its a very well covered front) and I personally would have liked to see a British story in Africa and Italy. I forgave them though because i spread playing the game out over a week (I played missions in Normandy one day, Paris the next and so forth" and was ultilmately satisfied with how long it took me. At least how long it seemed to take me. But again, if this game is Call of Duty "And this is World War Two", it failed. 

3: Political Correctness/Historical innacuracies: In campaign they got a lot right, even taught me a few things. Swastikas present for all you skinheads to gawp at. If you are so fragile that the occasional female yelling in multiplayer is enough to put you off how good the game is you may have to take a good look at yourself. 

Now to some of my own opinions, good and bad.

Zombies: If you like very little team coordination, character personality and repetitive fetch quests, this is for you. It's a refresher of the zombies experience but I don't think it was entirely necessary to re-work some good parts of the gameplay (the pace of the game is so much faster than any other zombies experience, making it hard for you to focus on an objective or a particular area, also the current map is complicated and too compact for the behaviour of the zombies. If boarded windows were still a thing the game would be much better just to slow things down a bit)

Graphics: It's a cinematic masterpiece but I think Modern Warfare Remastered looked better and the animations can sometimes be pure ass. A small step down from Infinite Warfare. 

Music: Wrong style. Some more instrumental to help emotion would be good. Also a step down from Infinite Warfare.

Multiplayer/hackers/performance: Solid multiplayer. Good playerbase and (for better or worse) it isnt region locked. What i mean is (As an Australian) I can be in a lobby in Australia and have empty spots filled by Americans and vice versa. A problem with Infinite Warfare was if there was a hacker in my region i'd almost alwasy get a game with them but with this that chance is lessened and it means the community will survive longer. The bad is if you connect to a 300 ping server. I can't say the lag was that bad but it's definetly there. Also hackers are there but Infinite Warfare did very reliable ban wave support. 

Price: Don't buy it on steam, alwasy buy in store and try to get the season pass.

Summary: 7/10. They delivered a solid PC game but the ever present hackers and lag will always cause frustration but i'm confident they will be sorted out.

To keep it short and sweet, Civ 5 is a deeply layered turn-based strategy game with a fairly self-explanatory premise - create a civilization that can stand the test of time. Seems simple enough, but the absolute fun and hilarity to be had playing with friends over multiplayer is where the game really takes off. That being said, if you fancy some alone time, Civ 5 is perfectly playable in singleplayer. Just be sure to adjust the AI difficulty suitably - they can be easy to cheese or unreasonably aggressive at times.

Circling back to the multiplayer with friends point, this brings me to the memory of how I lost over a dozen unspotted Japanese submarines to my friend roleplaying North Korea, because he decided to launch several nukes from Pyongyang to bomb random spots in the Pacific Ocean in a spectacularly unnecessary show of force. For no reason other than because he liked the animations. In that same playthrough I found my military riddled by such classic units as the Byzantine Gatling Gun, Aztec Musketman, and Austrian Catapult. And some Korean with a spear way off in isolation. All the meanwhile Ghandi was building a nuclear arsenal of his own.

Grab Civ 5 with the complete edition (all DLC) during a sale and encourage friends to do the same. You'll have fun with absurd situations.

Oh boy
Rockstar did it again. Every new GTA game makes new unachievable standard for other game developers. This standard can be beaten only by Rockstar themselves. Whole illusion of living city that includes radio stations, tv programs, web, different districts with different environment (different cloths that people wear, different cars, buildings) and many other details make you feel like it’s something more than just a video game. 

Single-player mode:
Missions in GTA include tons of action. It’s something Rockstar did incredibly well. It’s hard to make a game where you don’t do the same thing every single time you start new mission. Go there>kill someone/take something>go to the finish line. Missions include variety of thing you have to do. BUT whole storyline is kinda schematic for me. I have a feeling it’s based on the same scheme:
-we have a problem boys
-I have a plan, we can rob a bank
-it’s stupid we can’t rob bank whenever we are in trouble
-then give us better solution
-ok, but we have to do 4 preparation missions
It’s a first time we have a opportunity to play with 3 massively different characters (they are exaggerated too much in my opinion.). It allows us to dig into different subcultures. 
-problems of person that try to escape from “hood”
-middle-aged rich ex-gangster with spoiled family 
- redneck 
Thanks to that we can see this parody of California from three totally different perspectives.
Nevertheless I had great time playing storyline. Despite all those flaws it’s still good and worth playing. 

Online mode:
Concept of creating online mode where you can do similar things to the ones from single-player with your friends is absolutely delightful. Sadly this is the only positive thing I can say about this mode. It forces you to grind for everything. Do you want to try new activities from latest update? Firstly you are forced to spend tons of money on new “toy” (building, vehicle) which is required for starting mission (it’s useless after that). This investment will eventually pay off, after like 100h. Releasing new massively overpowered vehicles doesn’t help either.  I wouldn’t call it fun when you are killed multiple times by the same person just because that person bought new overpriced “Master Destroyer 2000”. Moreover you can actually see path of updates because Rockstar was getting greedier with new update. BUT THERE IS a SOLUTION FOR THIS. You can buy shark card with real money and skip that painful grind. Another problem is balance in some game modes. Rockstar doesn’t even bother to look into it. I would call online mode “give us your money and **** off”.

I can recommend you GTA V if you want to play single-player. Get it on sale and enjoy it. On the other hand online is reason I give this game a negative review. It’s almost everything that is wrong with game industry right now.

This game is amazing. I couldn't stop playing until I finished the storyline. The different biomes, all the different creatures, the story, the music, it's just beautiful. 
There are moments that you actually believe you are there, underwater, in danger, fighting to stay alive. Having said all this, there are a few things that still need a bit of work imo.
Getting resources is a crucial part of the game, the only problem is managing these resources, mostly mid to late game. 
At the start its all fun and games when you only have like 10 resources in your bags and 5-6 lockers, but it gets to a point when its just out right frustrating, having to do 10 trips from your Seamoth/Prawn, to your lockers just to store them. The disaster is even worse if you decide you want to start another base, and move all your inventory. Good luck and have fun. With all the technology available, submarines, nuclear reactors, I would say that having some kind of intelligent Inventory system isn't too much of a stretch. 
I'm glad there are mods that actually make this game alot more enjoyable. 
Inventory management (or the lack of it), is a game breaker to me, as you will spend half of your time looking at inventory and it's just not fun. You want to be out there exploring or maybe freely constructing your base ! :D
All in all a must buy, especialy if you like the survival genre. 9/10

第一周目自己玩，没怎么看攻略
第二周目看攻略，地毯式趟地图

有太多的瞬间让我难以忘怀

关于boss
卡了一星期的古达老师
每天晚上的1h都在第一个篝火与古达老师之间奔走
当时可能是心态放的比较平，不着不燥，因为深知自己的手残，略晓这款游戏的难度。
而且每次失败，我心里都会有一种感觉：我能打败他。
所以，打游戏不爱动脑子的我，强迫自己记招式，强迫自己思考战术，强迫自己不贪刀。
终于，最后一刀下去，一声清脆的声响传进耳朵，后又直接从天灵盖冲出。
顷刻间，所有压抑的东西，在那一瞬间释放，一个字：爽！翻！天。
在之后，推开后面那扇门
明亮的天际映入眼帘，心情豁然开朗，瞬间对接下来的路充满好奇与信心。
直到，被专家没收了所有的魂，然后发现传火祭祀场可以用魂升级！一口老血差点喷出，现在想想都还心疼。
此外，还有好多boss，都曾卡了我好久，因为我几乎没有举盾的意识，纯靠翻滚。
还是猎龙铠甲让我有了举盾的习惯，因为自己太菜了，一个翻滚不好，后边几招都要吃到，瞬间gg。沙立万都过来了，这个真顶不住了。在加上心态问题，就搁置了一段时间，
因为一些现实原因，环境的改变以及心态的变化，再后来，我学会了逃课，逃了无名和化身。
想到这里还是有些遗憾的，逃课一时爽，举盾降低难度。但是在沙立万之后，似乎再没有当初击败古达时的那种感觉。
奥，对，还有一个，就是dlc里的修女。

关于地图的捷径
探索地图大半天，在打开一扇门或者开启一个升降梯后，又回到原点，那种惊喜，只能用 卧槽 来形容。
但是后来才发现，奥，这有的捷径是用来给我打boss用的啊。这捷径设计的挺好，我死的也很快。。

关于恐怖元素
在地下监牢的时候，我一度怀疑自己在玩恐怖游戏。
霸王沃尼尔那张大脸，嗯，出现的。。。恰到好处。

关于剧情
对于玩游戏不怎么看喜欢看剧情的我，到现在还是有点懵。
只能说，这个游戏，有很多的故事，需要耐心地去探寻与发现。

玩到最后，有一种落寞的感觉。
脑子里不禁冒出这八个字：完成使命，结束生命。
所以
第三周目，这火，就灭了吧。

Incredibly promising game that, even at this point, is feeling very cohesive indeed.  They have the core gameplay - forgive this, you know it's coming - rock solid.  Anyone with any interest in co-op wave games (L4D, Payday, etc.) will find a lot to love here, and if you ever found yourself digging in random directions on Minecraft to just see what you find will love this game.  Like both of those?  You'll love this to death as my friends and I have.  Already bought it for my wife as well...

Although I had a couple of crashes, technically this is already better optimised and more beautifully rendered than many PC games are today, after shipping and late patching.  Gorgeous stuff and refreshing to see the core game already so gleaming.  They take advantage of the processing headroom they gain with low-poly graphics by cranking the texture shaders and reflections to 11.  Play this on all-Epic settings and you see real-time reflections that embarass AAA games - all without slowdown.

I have full confidence that they'll add more cruft and late-game material to cement this one as a defining example of the co-op wave-fighter genre done stunningly right.

Update: since the review they've lost most of that processing headroom by cranking up environmental effects and room sizes to levels that were absolutely impossible to see years ago, and that's honestly not a bad thing, lol

Skyrim is a lot more awesome than the game I expected it to be.

If you played Oblivion, Skyrim takes quite a bit more time to get used to, but it pays off in the long run. This is because it's more like a hybrid of Morrowind and Fallout 3/New Vegas. To egregiously over-simplify it, you gotta work harder to get the same results as in Oblivion. But that just makes the rewards all the sweeter.

Obviously, the main draw of Skyrim is becoming a one-man dragon genocide machine! But the real beauty of this game is that there's so much more to do besides that. For example, you can craft your own weapons and armor, stick fancy enchantments on your gear, buy and decorate a house, ride a horse through the beautiful snowy countryside, or rob entire cities blind - whatever your heart desires, really.

Is it a perfect game? No. There are bugs here and there, and spikes in the difficulty curve will make you scream at the unfairness sometimes. But it's still a game well worth sinking your teeth into.

I have no words to describe how much I love this game, but I'll try.

Your choices matter. There are secrets and layers everywhere. Battles are fun, both when you are aggressive and when you are pacifistic. The characters are incredibly lovable. The jokes are just plain funny, which on its own is an achievement nowadays.

I just can't do it justice without explaining exactly what I mean, and by doing that I spoil you and rob you from the thing the game does best: surprise you at every turn. Please please please play it before you get spoiled.

EDIT: An amendment is necessary now I've actually played the No Mercy route too. Well, I should add "tried to play", because it was the most emotionally taxing thing I've ever done. I have never felt so guilty over killing fictional characters. In the end I quit halfway the final battle because there's this one moment that was just too perfect not to quit over, and watched the ending and the effects it has on your future playthroughs on youtube.

Once you contrast Pacifist to No Mercy the many faces of the game become extra noticeable. The average playthrough takes you maybe six hours, but the tone over those six hours can shift from goofy frolicking about with skeletons and fish warriors, to darker-than-black comedy and psychological horror. All depending on your choices.

Undertale is a game with a colorful cast of characters, great music, and good story. However with shallow Gameplay and for only being 8-12 hours a game it's really really hard to play certain routes. Anyone who walks the middle path or does a neutral run will be frankly upset with the lack of a real ending. Unless you're going for a time consuming ending where you kill character A and spare character B then kill C,D, and F then a neutral run is kinda bland. I want to say the No Mercy and Pacifist runs are both good but they suffer from a gameplay perspective too. No Mercy is grinding as Frisk decides to spin like a top in one place for 20 minutes and the other is backtracking:The game. 如果要排出名不副实的游戏排行榜，尼尔机械纪元这款游戏绝对名列前茅。
白金工作室作为动作游戏的大头，在开发这款游戏时，对这款游戏的定位显然有着巨大的失败。就是他们将一个靠剧情和人设为核心的RPG游戏，按照动作游戏的设计思路来设计了。这样就会产生很大的几个问题。
一是极其糟糕的地图设计，本作采用了半开放式地图，但是地图中的互动元素少得可怜；而且地图中到处都是的空气墙加上动辄十几层高且大部分楼层空无一物的高楼，都让探索地图的体验十分糟糕。这对于动作游戏可能没那么重要，但在更注重探索的RPG里，尼尔所表现出来的问题就十分明显了。
二是极其无聊的支线任务，RPG游戏里通常都有支线任务来丰富世界观，增加游戏内容。但白金的支线任务设计太过于动作游戏化，毫无带入感地刷刷刷，找找找，再加上这款游戏的敌人设计太过于单一以及上面提到的地图设计的问题，玩家很快就会失去兴趣。
其他一些问题如故意设置画面数值导致游戏的优化在画面并不好的情况下显得优化也很差，在特殊视角下人物的剪影设计太过相似，都让这款游戏实在难以叫人满意。
总之，这是一款以剧情和人设为卖点，以动作游戏思路做出来的畸形游戏，不推荐购买。

总体来说物有所值，单人模式其实是有的，汉化也有，在创意工坊，也可以搜索贴吧，工坊里的汉化有点机翻，凑合用吧，总体玩下来感觉就是insurgency2 MOD day of infamy的加强版，目前还有部分闪退。

[h1]Опять за старое[/h1]

За свою почти тридцатилетнюю (!) историю существования, серия [b]DOOM[/b] претерпела не так уж много итераций. Были, конечно, всякие java-поделки, с, прости боже, rpg-элементами, но, в общем и целом, единственным существенным отступлением во франшизе стал [b]DOOM 3[/b]. Споры о котором, кстати говоря, не утихают по сей день. В остальном же DOOM был, есть, и, судя по всему, будет забористой стрелялкой для сильных желудком. Хорошо ли это? Ответ однозначный: да, хорошо. Но даже от неплохого произведения не всегда можно получить удовольствие. И в моём случае таким произведением стал [b]DOOM: Eternal[/b].

Пройдя в своё время [b]DOOM 2016[/b], я ожидал от сиквела, в первую очередь, исправления геймдизайнерских ошибок. То бишь: ликвидация арен и внедрение вместо них более типичных по своей структуре уровней аля [b]DOOM 1 & 2[/b]. Наивный. Аренные шутеры - главный тренд последних лет. Запутанные, витиеватые коридоры гигантских локаций, как это было в девяностых, нынче не в чести. Сейчас, гуляя по виртуальным коридорам различных баз и готических дворцов, собираешь в основном различные записки, да смотришь видеоролики. Экшен - прерогатива арен. Изредка, конечно, дают пострелять и в коридорчиках, но мало. Не понимаю подобного решения.

Правда, в перерывах между экшеном (который в Eternal'е стал ещё более лютым, нежели в предыдущей части) мы теперь ещё участвуем в испытаниях с элементами платформинга. Да, примерно как в [b]Марио[/b]. Выглядит всё это, на мой взгляд, крайне нелепо, когда весь из себя крутой [b]Думгай[/b] прыгает по парапетам да по выступам, и "паркурит" от одной стены до другой. Когда подобные акробатические кульбиты используются во время напряжённых сражений, это ещё куда ни шло. Но когда нам приходится добираться от одной арены до другой, прыгая при этом по парящим в воздухе платформам, да минуя ещё различные препятствия в виде огненных цепей и прочего, то меньше всего мне кажется, что передо мной брутальный шутер.

Также вызывают у меня некоторые вопросы попытки разработчиков выстроить на базе бессюжетного по сути боевика вселенную с проработанным лором и запоминающимися персонажами. Необходимо ли ДУМу такое? Едва ли. Подбирая по ходу сюжета [b]свитки с информацией[/b], вы, при условии, что читаете их, претерпеваете изменение общего темпа игры. Выйдя из очередной битвы победителем, утирая пот со лба, читаете витиевато составленные письмена, рассказывающие о мире игры. Тут бы отдышаться, но нет, приходится читать [b]околорелигиозную беллетристику[/b], разбираясь, кто есть кто. Можно, конечно, ничего не читать, но тогда вы упускаете львиную долю контента, да и просто рискуете не понять, кто "тот чел слева".

В остальном же DOOM: Eternal весёлый (насколько может быть весёлой игра про оторванные конечности и выпущенные на свободу кишки), [b]яркий, разнообразный шутан[/b], за которым приятно скоротать пару-тройку вечеров. Хотелось бы, чтобы разработчики в дальнейшем всё-таки [b]отошли от концепции арен[/b], и сделали уровни в игре более коридорными, но при этом по-хорошему запутанными. И совсем было бы круто, если бы разработчики [b]сократили количество записок в игре[/b]. Совсем отказываться от них необязательно, но вот подсократить их - точно не повредит. Ни сюжету, ни самим игрокам.

Overall, JC3 has a more feel-good vibe and I enjoyed the scenery more as well.

TL;DR: I enjoyed Just Cause 4 and would definitely Recommend it, but I would recommend JC3 even more.

I really like this game but there are two MASSIVE issues I have with it that you should know about before you buy it. 

ONE: 

This game is really good once you get the hang of it but actually getting a hang of it is a pretty terrible experience. Beginner Guides on Youtube are hours long. I thought that was crazy at first but after playing the game it makes sense and is not a great sign for how well the game communicates with you, the player. 

Total War has always had big flaws in communication of mechanics, especially campaign mechanics. For example, in Total War Rome "Squalor" is a huge issue in city management but until I played in hard mode and actually had to do research online I never actually knew what "squalor" meant and how to combat it. The AI that gives you tips never says and I just assumed Squalor meant poverty so build more financial opportunities for the people like Markets, Farms, and Entertainment. "Squalor" in the game actually means overpopulation and eventually there's seems to be nothing you can do about it aside from mass peasant recruitment and sacrifice or letting the city rebel and slaughtering people. 

That's just one example of a common issue in Total War games that hasn't been that huge a deal for me until this game. I've played Total Wars Rome 1 and Shogun 2 before playing Warhammer 2. They were both bad at communicating and tutorials but Warhammer 2 is about 10 times worse ESPECIALLY if you pick a race other than the High Elves. I wanted to play as the Skaven at first but after two miserable failed campaigns with just zero feeling of progress or understanding I almost quit playing entirely. My empire was terrible and I was struggling in every fight. 

After doing my own independant research and playing a High Elves campaign the game is starting to make more sense but this game SUCKS at communicating how things work. Expect to either slog through figuring things out in campaign after campaign that each takes a long time or be ready to watch youtube videos.

TWO: This game is WAY overpriced for what you get. I know this is at least a little subjective but Warhammer 2 only comes with 4 playable races and that, to me, is NOT WORTH $60. The four races you get are High Elves, Skaven, Lizardmen, and Dark Elves. I did research before buying but couldn't get a clear idea of if this game only came with 4 races or if it added four. Race guides titles for Warhammer 2 included all the Warhammer 1 races as well so I figured I got everyone but the Tomb Kings and the zombie pirates but Total War Warhammer 2 is, in reality a $60 DLC for a $60 game. If you want to play as humans or dwarves or anyone else, you need to buy Warhammer 1 which is still $60. Actual DLC is also very expensive. Buying a single DLC faction costs $20.

I could look past this but you are actually punished in game for not owning the DLC. As the High Elves you are not allowed to confederate Averlorn and Yvresse because their legendary lords are DLC and instead of just replacing them with a non-DLC lord when you confederate Creative Assembly instead chose to lock you out of confederating them. I realize this is not a huge deal since you can just attack them but from my own perspective and my own opinion this was made worse by the other cost issues I had with the game.

OTHER: Aside from those two issues the other problems I had was not being able to trade settlements and how fast the battles are. The battles on regular speed are very fast for a slow person like me especially coming from Rome Total war. Shogun 2 was fast but not nearly as complex since Warhammer has all sorts of magic spells and abilities to manage as well as units constantly routing and coming back. I'm not a the kind of guy that enjoys working on Micro control. I don't play starcraft because I don't have that tech skill. The game has difficulty setting that help but so this is only a minor issue but I pause ALOT and basically only play battles on slowmotion. 

THE GOOD: In other Total War games I've played most of the factions play very similar to each other, especially on the campaign map but Warhammer does not suffer from that issue. How different each faction is is the only reason having so few for $60 dollars isn't just entirely unacceptable. They each have unique campaign mechanics so variety is there and there is PLENTY of depth. Youtube tutorials just on Settlement mechanics are 45 minutes long not only because of how little the game explains itself but also because there's ALOT of depth in this game.

OVERALL:

The game is pretty good once you get the hang of it and provides much more variety in depth and replayability than other Total War games but be aware of the games issues before you spend the $60 or the $120 to get the full game.

I want to start off and say that I have no affiliation with the god-awful fanbase and that is no excuse to immediately judge this game, along with this positive review I'm about to give. 

Undertale is an RPG, created by the indie game developer & musician, Toby Fox. For the record, Undertale’s writing, characters, graphics, engine and soundtrack was created by a one man team, with only a few hand-picked artists that supplied additional art. The game was inspired heavily by the Mother, Shin Megami Tensei and the Touhou series. Originally, the game was roughly going to be 2 hours in length and published three years earlier, but development was continued over the course of three years. A delayed game is often than not a good thing.

The story follows previous chronicles where humans and monsters lived together in harmony on Earth. War breaks out between the two warring races with the humans victorious in winning the war and sealing the monsters beneath the Earth’s crust. Many years later, a child climbs Mt. Ebott; a towering mountain in the midst of what appears to be a hike. Clumsy as a young one would be, the ditzy child discovers a small cavern and seconds later, trips over an unexpecting vine, ending up plummeting down to an almost endless hole in the ground. This is where the game gives you your own in-print by naming the fallen child whatever your heart desires.  

After being saved from your long fall by a bed of golden flowers and being saved yet again by a motherly monster, presented as an anthropomorphic, white-furred goat from a psychotic killing flower, this is where the adventure takes off. You will find yourself lost by traversing the weird and eccentric places Undertale has to offer such as maze-like catacombs, a charming snow-covered town inhabited by jolly kind-hearted monsters, gloomy pathways with illuminating mushrooms and a huge laboratory, blanketed among the foreground of magma and craters, just to name a few. Everything that you wouldn’t think would fit the setting of an underground realm is present, defying all expectations in the process. Your ultimate goal in Undertale, you ask? To reach back up to the surface of the Earth, which is protected by a magical barrier, guarded by a notorious king of monsters. 

The humour of Undertale is also a diverse topic. It incorporates comedic elements of all styles; toilet humour, random humour, breaking the fourth wall humour and to some vague extent, British humour. Best described in total as quirky and corny to the point that you will be laughing along with some of the funniest dialogue ever conceived within an RPG. It's up there with similar games such as Earthbound and Borderlands where you would want to hunt down every last NPC just to listen to what sort of crazy, erratic yet witty things they have to say. On that note, Undertale has replay value written all over it and what enhances this is the fact that the character’s dialogue changes after completing your first run, so it’s a different experience each time.

Undertale is a silly game that doesn't take itself seriously and when it does, it seldom follows through. Often as ever, characters seem to have a change of heart depending on how you interact with them. The battle system is unique as it incorporates various styles of game mechanics found across different video game genres, such as JRPG's and bullet hell games. For example, you have your typical turn-based commands where you can attack an enemy until their HP falls to zero, or you can find out more information about the monsters you confront, giving you an easy way out of not doing any harm, but understanding how their pattern works ultimately allowing you to spare them. Sure, you won't get rich out of the experience points, but you will get definitely get rich out of gold and best of all, friendship. All of this, not before delivering a random quote with a touch of humour. 

When analysing the overall artistic effort put into the game, at first glance it looks as if an elementary student did most of the work in MS paint and it wouldn't surprise me if that was the case. Graphics don't make a good game and this is what Toby Fox had in mind; to compensate, the soundtrack is simply outstanding. I personally couldn't stop humming certain tunes, eventually becoming stuck in my head during many sleepless nights. Much like how Undertale contains various types of humour, this game includes a wide plethora of different musical styles; ranging from vintage chiptune, to heavy pop, all the way to relaxing guitar and soothing piano pieces. There’s at least one music piece out there for everyone and it truly captures your expression from emotion, whether a happy-go-lucky song gives you smiles or a soft touching, tranquil song gives you tears.

As you progress towards the final stretch of Undertale, take my previous point where I said it rarely follows through with sentimental value and throw that out the window. It changes into some kind of emotional rollercoaster; a major juxtaposition to the charming, harmless nature. It's a bitter-sweet tragedy, continuing to boggle the minds of fans and gamers alike. It’s something to remember for generations to come and it all boils down to how contrasting this game is in comparison to future video games and the classics we grew up playing. 

Undertale gives you determination and I was determined to write this review from the very beginning. I hope this brief review gave you some insight without shoving the whole nuisance of a fanbase into your face. As anyone who would give a good ending note for a review, if this is your first time playing Undertale, don’t take the game for granted and play it at a steady pace not to miss out the most iconic and rather amusing content that’s packed to the brim.  Thank you for reading and remember to stay determined, good luck.

DOOM Eternal evolves the formula of its 2016 predecessor by adding layers of complexity to the tried-and-true formula of speed and slaughter. Enemies are generally tougher, but many now have strategic weakpoints on their bodies, and the player is equipped with a variety of new tools to immolate, eviscerate, or dismember the demons in their way. The result is a game with both brains and brawn.

These changes encourage - and on higher difficulties, necessitate - the player to not only run and gun, but to strategize while doing so. Enemy priorities are important, as is the rotation of equipment and weapons based on the fight you find yourself in. Low on ammo? Find an imp to chainsaw. Low on armor? Group up some demons and set them aflame. Resource management is key in Eternal, and the smart player is rewarded for getting down the gameplay loop that keeps them in the fight.

That being said, returning players might find themselves somewhat out of their depth in the early stages of the game. Going from Nightmare in 2016 to Nightmare in Eternal is quite the leap. The Darkest Dungeon ist zu Beginn ein eher verwirrendes und schwieriges Spiel. So sterben einem etliche Helden beim Versuch das Spiel kennen zu lernen. Nach einer gewissen Spielzeit stellt sich beim Spieler eine trügerische Sicherheit ein, da man ja nun zu wissen glaubt das Risiko einschätzen zukönnen. Diesen Fehler macht einem das Spiel meist umgehend und eben so häufig nicht gerade fair klar.
Positives:
- Sehr schöne individuelle Grafik
- Spannende Klassen und Kombinationen
- Super Synchronstimme
- Spannende Dorfinvents
- Allgemein eine Hammer Atmosphäre
Negatives:
- Unverständliche Zugreihenfolge im Kampf (trotz hohen GES-Werten)
- Teilweise absurd unfaire RNG
- in den höchsten Levels unangemessen hoher Schwierigkeitsgrad
- Höherstufige Helden fühlen sich schwächer an da die Gegner extremer leveln
EXTREM NEGATIVES:
- SPOILER: Im Verlauf des Spiels wird das Dorf von Briganten Angegriffen dieser Angriff ähnelt von der Schwierigkeit dem Darkest Dungeon, tötet also einen Helden bei Rückzug und ZERSTÖRT VERBESSERUNGEN IM DORF, zur Krönung des Ganzen muss diese Quest beim Auftauchen umgehend gelöst werden, als wäre sie gut vorbereitet nicht schon schwierig genug. Sollte meiner Meinung nach entweder komplet gestrichen werden oder zumindest im Schwierigkeitsgard angemessen gesenkt werden.

Somit ist The Darkest Dungeon ein Spiel für jeden der eine Herausforderung und eine hammer Atmosphäre mag. Denoch kann ich es nicht wirklich weiter empfehlen, da es gegen Ende einfach nur noch absurd und Nervenzehrend ist.

Первую треть игры персонаж вынужден бегать с водопроводной трубой/монтировкой. И тогда, чтоб с этого вышел какой-то толк и тупая бошка пала на землю, бедного кусаку придётся долбить пол часа. А тут их тысячи! И по одному они, как правило, не ходят. [i] - Зомби и люди, люди и зомби. [/i]

В игре представленно несколько типов зомби: [list]
[*] обычные кусаки - их много, они медлительны и опасны только количеством;
[*] прыгуны - шустрые и очень манёвренные зомби, увидят издалека, умеют лазать, прыгать и цепляться;
[*] бегуны - встречаются ночью, очень опасны, заметил один - долго не проживёшь.
[*] все-возможные разрушитель и прочие великаны, которые очень медлительны, но ОГРОМНЫЕ И КИДАЮТ МАШИНЫ;
[*] кислотные блевуны;
[*] прочие. 
 [/list]
Но зомби не главная опасность. Страшнее зомби только [strike] неудачный прыжок с водонапорной башни [/strike] люди. Бороться с ними сложнее они хорошо вооружены, не стоят столбом пока ты их унижаешь и, как и зомби, не ходят в одиночку. Драться с ними на ножах хоть и сложно, но всё же интересно. Они умеют вовремя приседать, отбивать удары, бить ногой и в целом вести себя как хорошо натренерованные орангутанги. И по традиции, всю эту компанию разбавляет один человек с винтовкой. Он сразу придаёт сражению больше энегрии и подвижность.

В игре присутствует много геймплейных механик, такие как забеги на время, гонки, зачистка карантинных зон и т.п., но их я всё же пропущу.

Привлекло меня это детище... своей атмосферой. Пожалуй, так это назову.

Немаленький остров, эдакий аналог Зоны. Фауна и флора изменились из-за некого катаклизма, случившегося на этом острове, где ранее располагался комплекс лабораторий и их обитатели теперь гуляют на свободе. Локации поначалу впечатляют, но толку от них нет. Они просто существуют, по ним бродят всё те же боты.

Также по острову раскиданы многочисленные жуткие местечки - мёртвые города, подземные комплексы, аномалии, духи-скримеры, которые, сперва пугают, но потом повторяются из раза в раз на тех же местах и с тем же музыкальным сопровождением - можно предугадать и не дёрнуться во время боя с врагами. 

Бои, в основном, сконцентрированы на ближней дистанции - ножи, лопаты, мечи, топоры, катаны (казалось бы, откуда там катана, но... НАДО). Огнестрельное тут тоже есть, но оружия полно, а вот патронов... даже если создавать самим, мало да и не особо интересно пользоваться - пара попаданий уничтожит любого рядового противника. А вот "бои" с боссами проходят иначе - их надо заманивать в щедро раскиданные по арене ловушки, которые и наносят им основной урон - то заморозить, то заставить влететь в стену или край арены, сделать это очень просто. Все противники безобразно тупы, пускай и пытаются пользоваться своими преимуществами. Убить их особого труда не составляет.

В эту игру понапихали много отличительных черт, будто переиграли в Сталкера или ещё во что, желая сделать "как они", но удовольствия остальным игрокам мало. Атмосфера Зоны есть, но на кой чёрт там живут "дружелюбные" боты не понятно - возможность добычи артефактов есть только у главного героя, доступ на остров есть только у "добровольцев" и силовиков...

Здесь вообще многое, если не всё, нелогично. Лора нет, разбираться со всем происходящим никак не позволяют, побочные задания заставляют носится по всему острову туда-сюда-обратно и убивать одних и тех же противников в тех же локациях. А сюжет, это просто очень грустно. 

Подводя итоги, из хорошего: недолгая атмосфера а-ля Сталкер, сюжетная завязка, пожалуй, ещё и музыку можно упомянуть. Из плохого - всё остальное.

I wouldn't say this game is badly optimized, but sometimes it does dip in performace here and there (and it crashed once).

Still definitely worth buying full price, but if you catch this game on one of it's many sales then consider yourself lucky, because you're in for far more hours of fun than you've payed for. Este jogo realmente mudou muito em todos esses anos antes de finalmente ser lançado, mas essas mudanças na minha opinião em grande maioria não foram boas, a maioria foi ruim.

-Para começar, a mudança mais gritante de todas, itens por região, Por quê? Por que foi adicionado isso no jogo? Foi uma tentativa de aumentar o tempo de gameplay do jogo? Não sei, mas sei que tudo que isso fez foi deixar o jogo mais maçante e frustrante, considerando que você fica um tempo considerável pra juntar os itens (que agora são basicamente a única forma de up no jogo) pra dar 2 passos pro lado, mudar de região e ser destruído por qualquer coisa que se mexe. Os únicos itens que permaneces da mesma forma ao passar de região, são uns com um "+" marcado, mas eles são mais raros e pelo o que eu encontrei bem mais fracos que os sem o "+". Isso faz você perder a sensação de liberdade que o jogo antigamente proporcionava.

-Aproveitando o gancho da evolução no jogo ser apenas feita por itens, você se sente ainda mais frustrado ao ver que agora não tem árvore de habilidades, você começa o jogo já com todas inclusas, para upar de level a úncia maneira é encontrando artefatos pelo mapa, que em sua maioria têm buffs completamente inúteis.

-Eu queria muito saber o que aconteceu com as vilas de antigamente, elas eram bem mais bem feitas e mais legais, agora todas elas são só um punhado de casas jogadas num canto, sem falar que pra achar elas agora está bem mais difícil, antes era só abrir o mapa que ficava bem sinalizado, agora não, tem que ficar duas horas olhando pro mapa procurando um amontoado de cubinhos marrons pra quando você achar ter a chance de ser uma vila ou não.

-Por que o sistema de crafting é tão inútil? Ainda é importante fazer comida e poções pra regenerar a vida, mas outras coisas como armas e armaduras são completamente desnecessárias de serem craftadas, além de terem a dificuldade de serem desbloqueadas separadamente em cada região fazendo uma missão que libera o crafting em cada tier, ainda tem que ficar um tempão grindando pra conseguir os materiais que precisa -maldita teia de aranha que é muito chata de pegar e diamante que é absurdamente caro-, mas além da dificuldade em fazer seu itens, se torna muito mais vantajoso simplesmente resgatar os npcs que liberam itens melhores na loja e comprar direto nela, os itens de melhor tier ficam em torno de 800 moedas, o mesmo preço dos diamantes quando comprados com o vendedor, isso que pra craftar cada armadura precisa de em média 2 diamantes cada peça, e a armadura feita é pior que a comprada.

-Além desses detalhes que eu julguei serem problemas ainda há alguns bugs, que por mais que não atrapalham tanto é estranho se deparar com alguns deles, por exemplo, na classe mago, se você pular de um lugar alto e ficar apertando shift sem parar ao invés de só segurar, ele vai flutuar muito melhor do que se tivesses com a asa-delta, numa das dungeons do jogo, o castelo, é muito fácil encontrar na região onde tem um grade pra impedir você de passar pra ir pro boss um banco, se você sentar nesse banco e sair pulando, dá pra simplesmente atravessar a grade, daí dá pra atrair o boss e qualquer outro mob do lado de dentro pra perto da grade e fazer o mesmo processo pra voltar e ficar simplesmente atacando os bichos depois da grade. Sem falar ainda do bug que muito dos mobs têm de simplesmente ficar correndo com a cara na parede enquanto são atacados, o pior é que parece que esse bug era conhecido mas simplesmente não foi consertado, já que quando os mobs ficam assim, eles ficam impedidos de receber qualquer tipo de dano.

Questo gioco è assolutamente fantastico per me.
Era tanto, anni, che non mi divertivo così tanto con un gioco per pc.
Devo dire che l'ho trovato assolutamente privo di bug, l'ho preso a novembre; ho smesso di prendere giochi appena usciti e di fare da cavia agli sviluppatori.... e i fatti mi danno ragione. Apparte questa piccola premessa, veniamo al gioco.
Mi ha appassionato da subito, ma ho aspettato a recensire..... ormai sono quasi a 200 ore di gioco e dovrei quasi essere alla fine della Quest principale e fatto penso il 90% delle secondarie.
Le meccaniche di gioco sono abbastanza complesse, lo scassinare serrature, tirare con l'arco, i combattimenti..... perfino il gioco con i dadi nelle taverne.... ci vuole un pò ad entrarci, ma quando hai appreso la tecnica è veramente appagante; anche i combattimenti, mai uguali! Difficile in un gioco single player che non ti vengano mai a noia i combattimenti. Non è il classico gioco da bimbetto.... due sciabolate e il nemico è morto... no... se non ti muovi bene sarai tu a morire, anche a livello normale. Ma niente di preoccupante, il gioco è longevo anche senza mai salvare, o quasi mai.
Passo intere giornate a caccia (è bellissimo cavalcare in prima persona... non in terza come altri giochi), per poi rivendere pelli e carne...... oppure a dare la caccia ai banditi disseminati nei boschi, e vi assicuro che non è mai banale, anche quando si è raggiunto un certo livello tecnico di battaglia e siamo equippaggiati di tutto punto. Anche la meccanica di progressione delle abilità è abbastanza complesso, mai scontato.
Un'altra cosa che mi ha colpito positivamente di questo gioco è che è "reale", "vero"... nel senso che se sono nel bosco a caccia, posso vedere cinghiali, caprioli, cervi, a volte banditi o guardiacaccia ma mai draghi volanti... alberi parlanti, mostri enormi alti 10 metri o minchiate varie.
Le quest secondarie poi, sembrano principali, con un livello di profondità mai vista. A dir la verità la sensazione è come guardare una serie tv con tantissimi colpi di scena e tantissima libertà di scelta; si possono affrontare quest in Stealt senza menare un colpo o combattere da subito.
Son dovuto entrare perfino in un monastero, farmi frate, restare lì diversi giorni.... vita monastica.... e la notte a giro per il convento, scassinare, cercare prove...... ma non dico altro per non sciupare il game a nessuno.
A volte mi ci è voluto giorni a portare a termine una quest.... lungo la strada capitano eventi (mai uguali e non sempre) che ti fanno cambiare obbiettivo per un pò, con altre quest da raggiungere. Se mi si passa il paragone è un pò come navigare in internet, apri una scheda... poi un'altra.... un'altra..... e dopo 3 ore non ti ricordi più cosa stavi guardando all'inizio!
E' così il gioco, un mondo vasto, puoi cacciare, commerciare, assaltare, fare la quest principale o le secondarie, apprendere l'alchimia (una goduria) e realizzare pozioni di ogni tipo, avvelenare le frecce, le armi.... avvelenare il cibo dei nemici.... e tante altre cose.
Il tempo non vi basterà mai, e macinerete ore di diverimento su ore. 
Ma mai il gioco mette fretta, questa per me una gran cosa, si può abbandoare la quest o le quest (non c'è un limite) che si stava seguendo  per fare ciò che si vuole.... appunto come ho detto cacciare, farsi un bagno nei bagni pubblici, commerciare, passare ore a giocare a dadi in taverna; oppure facendo un bel torneo. I tornei sono bellissimi, si combatte realmente nell'arena come nel medioevo...e vincere non è facilissimo. Poi sfide con l'arco in ogni città... ecc.
Complimenti agli sviluppatori.
Se posso fare un paragone è una specie di Fallout del medioevo. Certo qualcosa la cambierei, ad esempio avrei gradito più profondità nel dlc From the Ashes (l'ho fatto a metà gioco consigliato da altri giocatori ed ho fatto bene); non si può costruire infatti dove si vuole, non si può interagire molto con il proprio villaggio costruito (sto parlando del Dlc From the Ashes)... ma sono peccati veniali.
Mi sto davvero divertendo molto, la trama è ben fatta, le musiche.... sembra davvero di stare in un film a volte... di essere li davvero con i tuoi compagni ad assaltare un castello!
In genere non scrivo recensioni, per pigrizia più che altro, ma con questo gioco volevo dare il mio contributo, sto passando tante ore serene, divertendomi molto!
Con le tante Mod poi, sarà bello rigiocarci.

It is set in a cliche environment but there are a few twists that set this atmosphere appart from being just cliche. I do like horror games but there have been very few that have constantly kept me afraid of what might be lurking around the corner. This game feels like one of the better horror games of our time, but doesn't place first for me. The environments and enemies are disturbing, but because of the lack of options, you will spend most of the game hiding, running if caught, and then right back to hiding again. I understand, they want you to feel powerless, but doing so has kind of killed the variety of most encounters. You either get caught then die, or get caught then run and hide again. My favorite horror game Alien Isolation, is does the "underpowered scenerio" better in my opinion. These two games are very similar in terms of hiding/surviving, but where Alien differs, is that you have lots of tools to help you do different things. If you're cornered by the enemy, you have more options other then die or run. You can distract, hurt (and sometimes kill depending on the enemy), and get other enemies to fight each other, in order to make your life easier. In Outlast, the absence of tools leaves you with only the die, or run and hide again options. 

TLDR: Very good survival horror game that leaves you feeling helpless, but you are so underpowered that many encounters will be too similar and lacking in variety to keep the horror experience fresh.

CTD and Repetitive

FIRST THE CRASH TO DESKTOP ISSUE:  My first play session worked fine, except the menu was too small for my resolution (1920 x 1080).  A few adjustments in the settings fixed that.  However, during my second play session the game would crash after about 5 minutes of play time.  (For reference, I’m running this on Windows 8.1, 64 bit)  After some research, I finally discovered a fix which involved going into the registry and deleting some entries.  And I discovered this fix only worked as long as you didn’t start a new game.  If you did, you’d have to edit the registry again.  This is certainly something a player should not have to do in order to get a working game.

ON TO THE PLAYING:  So I bought the game because it seemed fun.  I generally like resource management and time management games.  I've played Sims, SimCity, Diner Dash, Cooking Dash, etc. just to give you an idea.

At first it was fun.  I could place buildings where I wanted.  A few like the houses even had different styles to choose from by typing the "F" key before placing it on the ground.  I liked watching my little worker ants hurry around.  I quickly got a handle on my food supply, and this was despite some of the workers hoarding a disproportionate amount of food in their houses which meant less for others.  It’s not that hard really.  Just have some farm fields during the growing season, and you also have a few hunters, fishermen, and/or gatherers.  I also got control of wood, stone, etc.

In the end, it seemed all I needed to do was sit with the workers pane open and subtract or add workers to different positions as I needed.  For example: “Subtract 3 workers from Gathering, and add those 3 to Building because I have a wave of construction projects going on.”  It’s just a matter of clicking up or down on the arrows next to the jobs in the list.  I just needed to do that and keep an eye on the resource panes.  That’s why it got repetitive, and I played less than 10 hours.  Maybe that’s all the game is really meant for.

If I had to describe Among Us in one word, it would be "addicting". The basic premise of the game is that you are part of a space ship crew, with a maximum of 10 players, and up to 3 of you are impostors. The crewmates' goal is to complete their tasks as quickly as possible and the impostors' goal is the prevent the crewmates from doing so, either via sabotage or by killing. It takes a bit of getting used to, but once you become familiar with the maps and where to do which tasks, you can start developing your strategies and that is where the game becomes really fun. Playing on public servers is quite entertaining, but if possible, host a private server, gather a couple of friends and have fun. That's where the game really shines. Additionally, if any of your friends is worried about not being able to play because they can't afford the 3,99€, then fret not: there is a free version of Among Us on the Play Store which they can download and it works a treat. For the price and the replayability value, I can't not recommend buying this game.

発売からだいぶ経ちましたので再評価します。

グラフィック、BGM、物語。
三つともが奇跡のように高品質です。
自分は、主人公エディットできるゲーム大好きですが、このゲームのゲラルトさんには一切の不満もありません。
渋い中年で髭面。何事にも大きく動揺する事もなく、台詞は知的で時にユーモラスさえ含みます。
分厚い人生経験が言動から滲み出ていて、単純に大人の男としても魅力的で、さらには歴戦の戦士とはかくあるべしを貫いています。満点です。

物語の途中で起こるイベントには、複数の解決手段が用意されており、どのように解決するかプレイヤーが決められます。また解決方法や、解決後の対応によって分岐が生まれるイベントもたくさん用意されています。
コンピューターゲームのくせに、ある種、TRPGが持つ、「イベント解決するためにはどうすればいいのか、その手段を思考する楽しさ」が盛り込まれているのです。
物語の展開もイベントの解決策も一つしか存在しない、線路の上を進むだけのRPGしかやったことのない人にこそ、一度はプレイして欲しい作品です。

惜しく感じたのは、戦闘アクション（システム）が少々雑なところのみです。
ぶっちゃけカウンターと魔法を使うタイミングさえ覚えれば、あとは（よほどのレベル差がない限り）作業になって、完封するのも容易です。

とはいえ、戦闘アクションも他の盆百なゲームと比べればそう悪くありません。
GTAなどに代表されるオープンワールドゲームの中でも、よくできている位置にあります。
他の要素があまりに高レベルでまとまっているため、相対的に見て、アクション性・アクションシステムの完成度が低く感じてしまい、満足できない・不満を持ってしまう人もいると思います。

実に贅沢な不満（ｗ）ですが、ここまで他の要素が完璧なので、戦闘ももう少し力入れて他の要素に近いレベルまでもっていって欲しかった、と、そう惜しむのも仕方ないでしょう。それだけ戦闘以外のレベルが高すぎるのですから。


もう一つの惜しい点として、ぶっちゃけストーリーが長すぎる事です。
これは贅沢な文句になるのですが、いくつもの分岐があり、複数のエンディングが用意されているゲームなのに、メインストーリーを終わらせるだけでもかなりの時間がかかります。
周回する気力どころか、人によってはクリアするのも諦めるほど長いと思われます。
正直、自分も物語後半から「もういい加減に終わってくれ・・・エンディングを見せてくれ・・・」と思いながらプレイしていました。

とはいえ、全体的にみて、最高のRPGのひとつに挙げられることは間違いありません。
ゲームが好きな方なら、ぜひ一度プレイして欲しい作品です。
圧倒的すぎるほどに作りこまれた世界を感じてください。

For example different weapon rounds like light sword or nunchuk , boss rounds, time-challenge rounds and so forth. In the most basic round your kung-fu styles change from crane to tiger, eagle and what have you. In those same basic rounds enemies drop melee & ranged weapons, ranging from different swords & staffs to bows & throwing knives.
There are three different difficulties for the level mode to unlock, with over 25 passives. Three survival based modes.
They overhauled music, soundeffects and animation for the steam version. There are also achievements for those of you that just need to have them all.
Any of you that are still on the fence when it comes to "One Finger Death Punch", take a look at "WTF is...One Finger Death Punch" on youtube.

My Time at Portia is a charming game with a relaxed and positive vibe. There is plenty to do and you may find yourself struggling to fit it all in. Luckily there is a handy slider in the settings which you can use to increase the length of your days, giving you more time to gather resources, explore dangerous ruins or romance the townsfolk. Other innovations include having the storage boxes linked to the crafting stations and being able to sort all of your inventory with the press of a single button. Good stuff.
Unfortunately the copious language and grammar errors that litter the written dialogue are not so great. Even if you choose to view them as an endearing quirk it is still hard to ignore the discrepancies between what is written and what is actually being said (if indeed there is any spoken dialogue at all). This is a shame as it makes the whole game seem unpolished and amateurish. I appreciate that the developers do not speak English as a first language, but I can't believe it would be that expensive to hire a proof reader before publishing.  
On the whole though, I enjoyed my time IN Portia and would recommend it to casual players looking for a few hours of escapism in a charming and beautifully rendered world.

I purchased this game 6 years ago when it was originally a decent RPG game. Since the alpha release the following features where removed:
-Skill Trees
-A experience based leveling system
-Permanent equipment and items

If you are confused about that last one, allow me to explain the region locking system the game has. For starters you do not have levels that will increase your stats. When you find any new piece of equipment it will contribute to your overall strength. So your goal is to get equipment, however if you decide to leave a boime early, the moment you cross into a new biome all your equipment becomes useless and your glider, boat, every helpful item, gets deleted. 

When I bought this game 6 years ago I bought it to play a traditional RPG with exploration, not a makeshift attempt at a bad rougelike game. 

If you're looking for a RPG game with progression and a basic leveling experience, then this isn't the game for you.

전작과 마찬가지로 스토리 중심의 추리 어드벤처 게임이다. 많은 시리즈 게임이 그렇지만 이 게임은 특히나 전편의 중요성이 높다. 2부터 시작하면 스토리를 상당부분 이해하기 어렵기 때문이다. 제작진도 1을 플레이한 후 하는 것을 전제하고 있는 듯, 1의 주요 요소에 대한 설명이 없다. 사실 1의 요소를 설명하는 것 자체가 2의 스포일러가 되기 때문이기도 하다. 전편과의 연결, 세계관 확장 등을 훌륭하게 해낸 수작이다.

1과의 차이점을 보면, 우선 무대가 넓어졌다. 학교->섬이라는 설정상 확장뿐 아니라 게임상에서 돌아다닐 넓이도 넓어졌다. 

1이 비교적 상황의 리얼함이 있었는데 반해 2는 꽤나 황당한 상황이 많다. (물론 결말에서 다 설명되긴 한다.)

1에 비해 등장인물들의 개성이 더 뚜렷하다. 1은 몇몇 캐릭터의 존재감이 상당히 약한데 2는 전체적으로 개성이 넘쳐서 인상에 강하게 남는 캐릭터가 많다.

1은 학급재판 시작 전에 단서들을 추론해서 대충 범인이나 방법을 알 수 있는데, 2는 재판 도중에 동료의 힌트를 통해 밝혀지는 게 많은 편이다. (1도 동료들과의 협력을 이야기하지만 2는 특히나 그 부분을 강조하기 때문인 것 같다.) 사건들도 1보다 더 꼬아놓은 게 많아 이런 점이 두드러진다.

Не думал что настанет день когда я захочу написать обзор так еще и негативный так еще и на скайрим, одну из лучших рпг современости. Беседка молодцы наконец то консольщики получат моды и приличный уровень графики тем более что всем поклоникам скайрима этот ремастер дали бесплатно. Вот только есть одна проблема которую я надеюсь исправят где то через неделю с выходом редактора для 64 битной версии,  а именно отсутсвие модов. Я вообще мало понимаю людей что играют  без них ибо это просто невозможно без 4 неофицальных патчей скайрим лагает и багает где только можно. Вот вам реальный пример как я поиграл в ремастер. Я прошел начало порадовался что огонь драконов даже в ванильной версии выглядит прилично поплакал с мыльного оружия и лиц, полюбовался пейзажими (они очень хорошо выглядят) и тут я пришел в ривервуд пошел в кузницу и услышал реплику от маленькой девочки "тут дохляк".  Какого же было мое удивление когда я обнаружил что это Фотис что просто помер на улице рядом с кузницей само собой пришлось начинать заного и хорошо что это было только начало ибо потом бубны с консолью и респауном НПС были бы мне обеспечены. If you have any taste at all in the horror genre, any interest in finding a unique competitive game, any interest in a fair grind, then this could be your game. 

If you're looking to get immersed, then i can tell you that the developers have masterfully crafted a game that instills fear and suspense into its players regardless of the rank or hours played. This game has done what all the other attempted copy cats have failed to do. They have made the game extremely engaging. The chases are always intense. Every second counts. Every decision you make and every trick you try to pull has an impactful risk and reward. The visuals are perfect. The display of horror from the survivors perspective feels incredibly real. As for playing the killer, you can feel the strength of your hit and the hate behind your attacks. If you want to feel your actions on either role. you can and you will.

On the competitive standpoint, This is the best balanced 4vs1 game of it's kinda that you could come across. I've been playing this game hardcore ever since the 1st day of it's beta. No matter how long i play, i still find something i could improve on after every match. In terms of the meta builds, there are some clear top tier perks, but with enough skill, you can find success in almost any build and have plenty of fun running those builds. There are of course some questionable balance decisions on the devs end, but it's undeniable that the game is in an excellent state. 

One great aspect that makes this game so replayable is the grind system. No matter the outcome of the match, you are constantly progressing towards a better loadout and better equiptment. It's always satisfying to bring in the tools you've worked towards and watch those hard earned rewards give you that extra advantage. At this point, I have 26 characters at maximum level and prestige along with 7 characters with all perks which is entirely unnecessary but is something that has kept me enjoying the game and challenging me even up to this point.

Above all, this game is immensely fun and I am glad to have played this game so much for so long. I've convinced about 10-12 people to purchase this game and I hope this review can convince even more people because I want this community to grow and I want the devs to be rewarded for their amazing work.
