I didn't realize I had written a review for this game. I was going to wait until I finished the game to give an overall review, but I want to rewrite the nondescriptive review I wrote apparently back when I only had an hour clocked in on the game.

So here is my experience: I like the game a lot. As of the writing of this review I have 12.3 hours played. The storyline is really cool and feels like one that you'd read in the comics, and Joker's antics are darkly humorous. Harley Quinn is a babe. I mean, she's a total psychopath... The game looks really nice, and even though it's about 5 years old, the graphics are still pretty neat. Unforunately, I don't know if it's the graphics or just its general optimization, but this game seems to take a fair amount to run. This computer can run Killing Floor 2 on almost all max settings and run well over 30 fps, but this game seems to vary between 20 to 30 fps. And I feel Killing Floor 2 always has so much more going on at one time (plus much higher graphics). The game loves its slow motion effects and while a lot of times its satisfying, like when you land the knockout blow on an opponent, sometimes it's a little overdone IMO. (Like the Bane fight and every time he charges past you there's slow motion and all I want to do is hurry up with the evasive maneuver). Nothing that distracts too much from the game though. Combat feels good and makes you feel like the Batman himself, and the gadgets are handy. Finding the Riddler's hidden items and stuff is fun too. Overall it's a pretty immersive game with beat 'em up and exploration elements. You also get to upgrade weapons, armor, gadgets, etc.

Now let me talk about some of my lesser experiences with the game. There are levels where you're up on ledges high up above bad guys with guns and you need to take them out without getting detected or else they'll drain your life with few bullets and perfect aim that can follow you as you move because you know, asylum inmates get sniper training apperently. But if you just grappel to a ledge like one foot away from you they lose sight of you (gotta love how enemies can go from stupid AI to perfect intelligent AI and regress back again). The first couple times this mechanic is done it's cool. It's definitely a Batman sort of thing. But then every few levels there's another room where you do the same ledge stealth thing. Then a few more levels there's another one. Then after you beat it this last time you go to the next room, do a thing or two that leads you to the next mission, backtrack to the same room you just had a ledge stealth level and yes you guessed it, suddenly there's more bad guys with guns in the same room so it's right back to the ledges with you. These levels aren't hard. It's just all about patience and if you don't blatantly screw up. But it's annoying that these levels keep getting copied and pasted every few levels. It would be one thing if it felt like the natural progression of the game and couldn't be avoided, but when you back track to the same place you were just at two seconds ago and suddenly there's more guys and you have to do it all over again, then to me it feels like they were a bit lazy and wanted to keep reusing that mechanic to try to make filler in between the other parts of the game, make it feel like there's more to the game than what there is. It's just so much waiting. And I admit, I'm kind of an impatient guy, but I didn't mind these parts the first couple times I was introduced. It just feels like "I've already done this let me continue the *story*." I feel like games follow a simple formula: Each level presents a challenge, and if you beat the level you've proved you can overcome that challenge, so the challenge doesn't repeat later because it doesn't have to and there would be no point. Imagine if in COD 4: Modern Warfare, after you beat the ghille suit level, snuck past the entire enemy army and everything, and two levels later, you had to backtrack through the same way. Then two levels later you had to sneak past another army that had a similar environment, so forth and so forth. Nobody would like the ghillie suit levels anymore because we already showed our stealth skills, overcame the challenge, and the mechanic was appealing because it differed from the norm of the game and stuck out as a stand alone level. That's what I kind of feel about these ledge stealth levels. They could have easily switched it up by having you sneak in different environment styles at least. So if you don't mind slightly repetitive gameplay and are a patient person, then this probably won't bother you too much in the game.

Another thing that was annoying is that this game can be inconsistent at times. Aside from the dumb AI switching to super intelligent AI in a split second sort of deal, there are times the game will tell you everything to do in a step by step kind of way and you're just like "yes, that's obvious I'm not dumb." But then they'll introduce some foreign mechanic or strategy or something and not tell you a thing, leaving you to run around blindly before finding this hidden thing or figuring out that you're supposed to use this control to do this. Similarly, sometimes it'll tell you where your destination is on the map clearly and other times, you can only see your destination on the whole island map rather than on your specific region too even when it's close by. It's those little things that can nag at you and make you wonder why it's not staying consistent. There have also been plenty of times where the game tells me to do this strategy and I'll follow it, the AI does the pattern they're meant to for the said strategy, then I'll screw up like a moron and when I retry, I do the same strategy as the game is reminding me, and suddenly the AI is acting in a totally different, disorganized manner (example, once when on a ledge stealth level I was supposed to throw batarangs until the bad guys claimed they would guard the door and then while they were in front of the door close together I could wipe them out quickly. But I messed up the first time around and the second time around, two the the bad guys went to the door when they said they were going to, but one of them stayed far away and I spent a half an hour trying to get him to do the pattern that he was claiming he was going to do but he wouldn't do it.)

It's a great game, though, and I do recommend it, just have some patience with it on some of the levels. It's one of those games where the good parts are amazing and you can't get enough of but the lesser parts are soooooooo frustrating and make you want to shut off the game for a while.

A bit disappointing.  As a big fan of the first two games, I had high hopes for this one.  I feel like I should enjoy it too, but ultimately I found the game kind of boring.  I finished the game with one character, got 2/3 with two others before I got bored and quit, and only did two-and-a-half of the DLCs with the max-level character before I was bored out of my brain and uninstalled.

Visually the game is very similar to BL2, with some enhancements along the way.  The usual iterative improvements you would expect.  Similarly, the gameplay is improved over BL2.  In this area I feel the improvements were more significant.  The enemies, locations, gun-generation, drop-rates, fundamental combat gameplay, etc, are all significantly improved.  In terms of pure gameplay, I would consider this the best game in the series.  All the more reason why I find it bewildering that I ultimately got bored.

The writing is perhaps the game's weakest area.  Many of the characters are badly written, and many returning characters feel like the writer did not understand them.  The jokes often fall flat, which is bad in a game that lays them on pretty thick.  The main villains are terrible, as is the Mary Sue in the supporting cast, but both of these complaints are well-documented all over the internet.

The quest writing is also quite frustrating, with most quests taking the "Haha, you thought that was the end?  No, we just changed the rules!" approach.  I think this was one of the things that most impacted my enjoyment of the game, as quests tended to drag-out and get boring/frustrating long before I finished them.  I was bored and wanted to do something else, but the conditions just got changed again.  Level design also conflated this.  While the levels were interesting, they tended to feel too long.  That size with lots of alternate paths for different side-quests would not have been so bad, but instead they tended to be one main path and if you did not do the side-quest on the first pass... well, you just added an extra 30 minutes travel-time when you go back for it.

Best City Building Game Ever.  

If you don't like paying for DLCs, don't buy them.  With all the mods and assets (for free, by the way) on Workshop for this game, the DLC's are not at all necessary.  I've been playing this game for years now (2,496 hours at the time of this review) and have never been bored once.  And the only DLC I ever bought was AFTER DARK …. only because it gave me bicycle lanes.  I've felt no desire to purchase the Disasters or the Mass Transit DLCs, even if they were dropped to $1.00 each ….. okay, maybe the Mass Transit one if only $1.00.
  
But I've gotten off-track of my point, which is that with all the mods and assets that are free for this game, you don't really need the DLCs.

If you just subscribe (it's free) to the First Person Mod by Tony56a, you can have days and weeks of fun just traveling around in your city.  As a Cim yourself or just riding along in a vehicle or a Cim wherever they go.  The game is COMPLETEY DIFFERENT – and sooo much fun – once you jump down into it and actually look at it from ground level.

Frustrated with creating a city?  Don't bother to create one --- on the Workshop, you can subscribe to a city of your choice (again, for free) that is already all set up for you, mods and assets, roads, city services, and all, and immediately start playing about down in the city as a CIM yourself.  Or you can start from there (with all the frustrating work of setting things up) already done for you.  From that point you can play with what you subscribed to or start adding in or removing anything you like from the city.

Anyone who hasn't tried this game is cheating himself/herself of one of the most fascinating experiences ever …. and I gotta tell ya, NO ONE could get me to play ANY computer games before I was forced by a family member to sit down in front of this one for one hour and play it.  Now I'm hooked and spend almost all my spare winter season hours on it  …  and, to my shame, some of my summer gardening hours as well.

And, honestly, for a vacation into a world you can make into your very own, the initial price is more than worth it.  If I lost it and had to start over and buy it again, I'd actually be willing to save up till I had $60.00 US and buy it again, if that was what it cost then.  And really, all anyone ever really has to pay for is the initial game, regardless of what the naysayers are whining about.

This is my first Civilization game, but I'm familiar with turn based strategy.

I think this game is simply great. It's fun to try to win the game in different ways, on different difficulty levels, with different leaders and explore the map. This game has very well guided tutorial, but you have to try things by yourself to get familiar with deeper strategies. You can start off with easier AIs and then go gradually further.

Really fun game for fans of turn based strategy and sandbox gamers alike. The game may be sometimes a bit silly and there are stronger tactics than others (which the game acknowledges), but you have to play this game with a little of tongue-in-cheek attitude, because if you desire absolutely realistic empire building simulator, this won't be it. This game leans more on the fun factor.

For example my latest game is with China and I'm trying to reach a culture victory on a small map with enemies very close to me. The idea was to build many little settlements around the capital and then wall them off with China's great wall for defence purposes, like in the history, but usually plans change when the AIs declare wars and build their own cities. You never know what they are going to do next.

Highly recommended!

This review is mostly aimed at those that played the game on launch.
The Short: The game is better now, still not very good... but better.

The Long: If you are looking for a pure gathering tech-demo. Then this is the game for you. The addition of 3rd person helps ground you in the universe. Shame about the poor implementation of the feature. This summs up the game. Good progress, shame about the implementation.

Gathering is now far deeper, shame that it is still harsh on your finger-ligands; you will be holding down whatever button you have bound to "fire" for hours on end.

The menu's are now deeper, but also un-intuitive and each menu have sub-menu upon sub-menu with different keybinds for each layer of frustration.

The combat is better now, but still poor and clunky.

The graphics are better now, but still rather bland and uninteresting.

And so on...

In the end, this would have been a fine addition to the pre-release promise of Mass Effect Andromeda. But as a stand-alone game, do not buy it unless you, like me, feel the cost is worth it just to check out the tech. As a game, it is very nisch indeed.

OLD REVIEW FOR THE RELEASE VERSION

Yes, the game is repetetive.
Yes, the game is nowhere near as good-looking and immersive as the pre-launch game-play
Yes, Shaun from Hello games promised things that were not delivered.

But. Is No man's sky secretly genious?

I have reached the center of the galaxy, so I know what happens. However, that is not why it is secretly genious. Well, not the MAIN reason of the under-cover savant-status I will try to argue for.

In this game, the goal is just something to aim for. The true game is maintenance of your systems and figuring out how to reach the center as fast as possible. I recently read a review were someone said: Wide as an ocean, deep as a puddle. Well. Kind of. However, the shallow game is the smoke-screen. In reality it is so wide, and so shallow that it eclipses the very concept of our lives and circles back around to become the most deep game that has ever, and can ever be produced by humans on a transistor based computer system. To understand the game you must consider "what is a game". For the past decade and a half we have moved away from the roots of gaming, from epic classics like populus and qubit. Todays games have hand-holding, constant rewards, and a pat on the back even if you do poorly. Todays game has exposition of how important your actions in the game are. They have action and insane experiences that take the post-real narrative found in movies and turn them up to 11.

Take a game like CS:GO. In reality it is not about skills, it is not about getting ranks. It is about playing, finnishing, and, win or loose, start queing again.

No manssky does away with all that and return to the foundation of what a game is. Sure, the game has a samey-feel to it. Sure, the animations are very stilted and immersion-breaking. Sure, the AI is JUST passing the nightmare found in Alien: Colonian Marines. And yea, sure, whoever coded space-combat and its companion systems; should be shot, quartered, and forced to grow potatoes in Greenland. But, as you play, you realize that were there is need for after-thought and a deft hand in design, nomanssky has you covered.

Different upgrades to your warp-drive allowes you to go from mostly dreary and booring systems, to dreary and booring planets with more grass. At the highest tier you get to go to blue systems, and by then, you will be longing for a grass-less and foilage-less planet. If only as a change of pace. Different colored back-drops indicate what type of resources you are most likely to find in the system space, and perhaps even on the planets. Different systems are not explained to you, you learn them by spending hours in game and slowly seeing patterns.

Industry standards are turned on their head all through the game. As an example:

Money does not matter, since you simply will have no chance to pass the ever rising cost of new ships. Once you finally grind to max itemization, money is used for buying items so you can get back on the road rather than spend hours looking for that one shitfuckingasshole resource you are missing to repair your hyper-drive..

Because that is what the game is about. It is about staying on the road.

The end goal does not matter, it is the journey that gives life meaning. 

Noamnsky is fucking philosophy!

So, awards time. Do I reccomend it to the gamers of today? Hell No. I'd be hardpressed to reccommend this game to ANYONE. Still: Do I think you should all buy it and play it, fuck yes.

/Noam Chomsky.

It pains me to leave this negative review. After almost 300 hours im giving up. There are alot of reason For Honor is not a good game right now. Somehow the developers managed to bring back to life a dead game and ruin it again in less than a year.

So where do i beging:

-The latest expasion "Marching Fire" is a miracle on its own. First of all i bought the Gold Edition a few months back and was told that every future expansion would be free. For some unknown reason this one wasnt. I am not going to give a greedy company 30 euros for a gamemode, 4 new heroes i can buy after 2 weeks and 4 skins. Nevertheless this is the smallest problem.

-Marching Fire introduced the "Wu Lin", 4 chinese heroes. They are the most broken pieces of heroes you can ever imagine. Extreme fast attacks and they introduced new features. One of them even has teleportation. Yes you read that right. In a fantasy game where you try to have some kind of realism and balance, along comes a hero who has 2 teleport skills all over the map which have 100% hit success and can ignore physical obstacles. They can all hit with 400ms lights (which is the fastest attack speed), even the TANK. Yes the tank with monster HP, Attack and Hyper Armor has assassin like speed. Go figure. Playing against the Wu Lin is a guessing game where the the attack will come from. Perfectly balanced.

-What adds more to the insult? The Wu Lin screech like they have some sort of disfuction on every single move! Try to keep calm playing against a demigod who screams chinese on the top of their lungs every 2 seconds.

-90% of the old roster is totaly obsolete. With the exception of a couple of heroes who got reworked lately, the rest are trash and can get stomped by a half decent Wu Lin player.

-They changed how gear works. They replaced stats with some useless features like "5 hp more when you revive" For comparison JJ (a Wu Lin hero) can do 50hp dmg with a light strike or something. A lot of us players had spent a huge ammount of money and gear chests to define our playstyle. What did they do? They replaced all that epic gear with 1 single perk and gave us 5 more chests of something. What an absolute "fuck you" from ubisoft.

-I dont understand what they ruined on this last patch but the parry function has been messed up. You miss alot of parries.

-Speaking of the last patch, the graphics now are washed up. They twinked the saturation or something and its pretty ugly.

-They still havent got rid of useless missions like "revive 5 allies" or crap like this. Noone likes those and they are a chore to do.

Finally dont listen to players who have bought the expasion and defend this piece of crap update. They have buyers regrets or they are plain stupid. The devopers fucked us up on waiting months for a new update with changes and heroes no one asked about.

For the time being i will take a break and maybe return in the future to see if they have changed anything. 

P.S. I know people say FH community is toxic but no, compared to esports out there the community is pretty nice. You might encounter a douchebag once every 20 games.

There are issues with this game, issues with inventory, combat and controls. In another game these issues would be somewhat painful to live with but with Divinity: Original Sin 2 I am more than happy to look past them. The world is so deep and interesting I have the urge to know what's around the corner. I have the desire to see what interesting fight mechanics are coming up. I want more and the game offers more. I can see me playing at least another thirty hours to finish it and I can see me immediately starting again with the other characters.

If you're unsure amout this, if you don't mind slower strategic game play, if you're happy to sit through hours of conversation and character development then don't think twice. You'll get your money's worth out of this game and then some.

You don't need to play Divinity: Original Sin to enjoy this game, but the enhanced edition of that is equally as good.

I'd like to add too, that the developer will likely long be supportive with updates and fixes, I'd imagine in a few months most, if not all, the little quality of life issues I have with this game will be fixed up and patched out.

Plus de 400h de jeux en trois mois et je ne suis pas lassé. Civilization V est un très bon jeu. Mais il faut prendre le temps de l'apprivoiser.

Pour ma part j'ai entrepris d'essayer trois fois chaque civilisation, une fois au hasard, une fois sur une carte donnée, et une fois avec une difficulté élevée. Je n'ai pas encore fini ... J'en ressors que la plupart des 43 civilisations (DLC comprises) sont intéressantes.

Difficile voire impossible de comparer le jeu avec Civilization 4. Mais voici déjà quelques points utiles à connaître, si vous avez Civilisation 4 (et le reste de ma critique va tourner autour de ça) :

- les parties durent beaucoup plus longtemps. une partie en taille normale dure 8h, une partie en taille minuscule dure 3h. Et ce même si l'arbre des technologies semble plus petit que celui de Civ 4.

- on est bien sûr libre de jouer comme on veut mais la mécanique de jeu nous encourage à gérer un petit nombre de ville (ce qui ne rend pas la partie moins longue, si vous avez suivi). Quand vous prenez des villes, vous avez le choix de les annexer ou de les rendre fantôche (ça vous donne des sous et des bonus, mais vous ne gérez plus la production). Bien sûr si vous prenez un bourrin, vous êtes libre de bourrer, mais il faut impérativement désactiver les autres types de victoire pour gagner en conquête, et prendre des villes jouera négativement sur votre taux de culture (qui vous permet de gagner des doctrines, des avantages de jeu).

- Niveau gameplay, à noter la présence des cités états (villes qui ne cherchent pas la victoire, qui vous donnent des bonus quand elles sont contentes. Vous pouvez faire du commerce avec elles). 

- La partie militaire est également très différente (les unités ne s'empilent plus, à l'exception des avions), la partie espionnage aussi (les espions volent des technologies. C'est pas terrible mais si vous désactivez l'espionnage, ça enlève aussi la diplomatie, un des points les plus intéressants du jeu).

- Les merveilles ont des propriétés différentes que dans Civ 4, il faudra donc jouer un certain temps pour ne pas forcément se précipiter sur la pyramide, le mausolée ou chichen itza. Aussi, il n'y a plus deux caractéristiques par personnages / civilisations (impérialiste, organisé, etc). A la place, il y a un avantage unique qui, si bien employé, peut tout déchirrer dans une partie. Et bien sûr un bâtiment unique et une unité unique.

Par exemple, le Brésil double son taux de tourisme (pour la victoire culturelle) pendant les âges d'or, on cherche donc à avoir un max d'âges d'or (qui n'est plus limité par le nombre de personnages illustres. Un personnage suffit). A côté, les Ottomans paient moitié moins en entretien pour leur flotte navale, on privilégie donc les villes côtières et les attaques par voie navale (et les bâteaux font très mal dans civ 5). De son côté, l'Indonésie gagne une ressource unique (qu'on ne trouve nulle part ailleurs : cannelle, poivre ...) pour ses trois premières villes posées sur des îles ou continents différents. Très utile pour le commerce. Etc.

- Enfin, il n'y a plus d'états vassaux (et donc pas de capitulation), mais un ennemi vaincu peut revenir dans le jeu, si un adversaire libère sa ville.

Bref, avec 43 civilisations il y a des tas de stratégies à essayer et adopter. Ce qui fait d'ailleurs qu'il y a des civilisations plus faciles que d'autres à jouer, mais pas un grand préféré parmi les fans (j'en ai moi-même cinq ou six).

Le graphisme du jeu est très beau, la bande son aussi de manière générale, les civilisations font des remarques amusantes et assez variées. 

Pour conclure c'est donc un jeu très différent de Civ 4, qui vous fera probablement penser différemment et jouer différemment (je pense que j'attaque davantage dans le 5). Si vous avez du temps pour jouer, parce qu'une partie c'est très long (et c'est quand même le gros gros bémol de cet opus. Je ne vous parle même pas du multijoueur !), je vous le recommande vivement.

Don’t Starve (с англ. — «Не голодай») — компьютерная игра в жанре action-adventure, со случайно генерируемым открытым миром, с элементами roguelike и выживания, разработанная канадской инди-студией Klei Entertainment. Игра вышла 23 апреля 2013 года в Steam.
Игрa имеет два режима игры: выживание и приключение, однако прямой доступ к игре имеет только режим выживания. Выбрав персонажа, который имеет свои уникальные способности и скины, а также настроив мир, игрок может начать выживать. Персонаж появляется в определенном месте, где его встречает Максвелл, который советует поискать вещи для ночлега. Сама цель игры — продержаться в случайно собранном мире как можно дольше. При этом у игрока есть две концовки: смерть и портал Максвелла. Первая наступает, когда у игрока количество очков жизни становится равным нулю. Для второй требуется пять частей портала, который введет в другой мир, объявляя конец предыдущему. Следствием долгого выживания является разблокировка персонажей, для которой требуется очки опыта. Чем больше прожито дней, тем больше очков. (Материал из Википедии — свободной энциклопедии)

"The Forest" is an open world, first-person, crafting & building adventure. The graphics are first rate. The gampelay is smooth, varied, and thoroughly enjoyable. The AI is complex and savage with no apologies-- giving us genuine jump-scares that leave us rattled. But wanting more!

It's super easy to love this game.

My two biggest worries when loading "The Forest" for the first time were the tedium of crafting, which I do not enjoy, and the directionlessness of another open world. To put to rest these concerns for others, the crafting can be as much or as little as you want in order to survive and never has to be overwhelming in any way at all. There is more to the game than that. Yes building a cabin out of logs is too much for me -- so I don't do it. But later when I realize I can stitch together a wetsuit with a couple days of heavy hunting... well... suddenly crafting becomes a whole lot of fun again! 

Open world? Rest assured there is a plot here. No, it's not the usual side-quest driven narrative we're used to, this one's more about the thrill and it's unbelievably scary, while never failing to remind us just how horrible this paradise island really is and why we want to get out!  I love that sometimes failing the game will help reveal the story, so let yourself fail once or twice if the point of your adventure is out of sight and mind. 

Top to bottom "The Forest" is built right and continues to receive loving free updates from its creators.  There is a lot to discover and a lot to learn, and it always proves  to be massively rewarding.

"The Forest" does some key things differently to make it stand out in a busy gaming market.

你战战兢兢的打开了那个避难所小子的图标，惊讶的发现游戏还能凑合的运行，虽然整个电脑发出了杀猪一样的咆哮，但是游戏还是凑合能玩下去。
于是，你看到了光亮的战前世界，呃，很亮，很美，很.....卡通？确实为什么会有一种50年代的塑料玩具的气息呢？
现在你正对着自家的梳妆镜，然后看到自己的脸....在快速的，魔性的变化..........仰赖于这次神奇的捏脸引擎，我们再也不会捏出猪腰子脸和面瘫了，男性很帅气，女性........呃，还是不要说了吧。
你和你的妻子/丈夫在进行了一段“战前美国人的日常”之后，避难所科技那个无聊的推销员又带着“你知道安利	避难所科技吗”的垃圾陈词滥调来推销了，虽然你觉得核战似乎一直很扯淡，然而这次.....BOOM........
好吧，你现在必须要到避难所去了，你的妻子/丈夫和你一起共赴冰箱......没错，是冰箱。
当你觉得可以在战后来一个雌雄双煞带着个孩子横扫废土的时候.........
”达令我会永远记着你的，我去找儿子，你还是在这做一团人肉棒冰吧“(此处就不剧透了）
500年.....啊不对，200年过去了，现在，是时候到达废土了。
苍凉的战后世界
到达废土之后你看到的是自己一直以来忠诚的巧手先生，当巧手先生带着哭腔的说道”乔瑟夫(joseph）先生（人工识别姓氏，可以读出来！）我在这孤独的守了200年“的时候，你的眼泪哗地就流下来了。Well，现在只能是JOJO的奇妙废土冒险了
这是一个苍凉的战后世界，唯一一点让人感到舒服的就是，天似乎还是那么蓝，就和200年前一样，景色也还是凑合，比起华盛顿的那帮天天只能看到屎黄色的天屎黄色的景色的倒霉鬼来说，波士顿的天气似乎并未因为核战变得那么恶心。
你往战前的加油站走去，途中发现了几具尸体，找到了一些衣服，然而你发现原来护甲都是模块化的了，虽然也有一体化的一副，但是大部分废土找来的护甲都不再是那个无语的一体成衣，你可以左臂穿个牛X的大盾，右臂来个废土客的皮甲，穿的十分魔性。
到达加油站后，这里应有尽有，起吊机，修理装备，这里就是你以后的魔改天堂了，最主要的是，你的忠实伙伴狗肉也在这里。
冥冥之中你似乎记得在别的地方看到过好几个带着狗的流浪汉的身影，这些人就是废土之神，你突然觉得现在自己也是了（笑），而且似乎你的狗肉更加的智能，他居然能捡东西.......还是不死狗（又笑）
突然之间地底钻出了几个带着土的肉蛋——居然是巨大的老鼠，他们居然身上还带着土！就在你还在思考”华盛顿的老鼠不是不会钻地么“的时候，你二话不说拔枪按下了Q键进入了VATS模式，然而突然你又纳闷了”V模式不是THE WORLD时间暂停么，怎么变成了慢动作了？“，可能是哔哔小子的机能不一样吧，V模式的的慢动作虽然慢的出奇足够你去思考，然而时间依然是流逝的，不过比起那个时间冻结的VATS模式来说，显得动感了很多。
三下两下干掉了这几个粉耗子之后，你终于发现所有的道具栏都是浮动在物件之上的，不再需要打开那个烦人的道具烂了。

一阵摸爬滚打之后，你找到了独立战争纪念馆，而义勇兵居然迫不及待的让你穿上了....动力甲？！？！天呐，这刚几分钟啊，就能穿上动力甲了么？

穿上这套长满铁锈的动力甲之后，你发现菜单变得如此霸气，各种仪表历历在目，然而，事情没那么简单，这次的动力甲也是模块化的，而且还需要能源，现在仅靠着一颗快没电的核融电芯，驱动这个七零八落的废铁，顶多在匪徒面前成逞威风就只能嘎支支响了

此时更为恶心的情况来临，死亡爪？这等杀人于无形怪物为何在游戏初期就出来溜达了？

用动力甲顶着死亡爪，费尽心思的干掉了他，这套动力甲也不堪重负，虽然还有能源，但是暂时也只有放在魔改加油站的份儿了。

现在，义勇兵和你一起展开了寻子和重建社区的工作。

而在另一个宇宙的你，此时稍息片刻，望着窗外的车水马龙。

你庆幸于这个宇宙的世界依然是平静的，自己可以坐在这里，驰骋在另一个宇宙的废土之中。

Tl;dr Bomber crew is a fun game that doesn't explain things very well but is a good purchase on sale

I picked this game up when it was on sale and had a blast. The most fun I had with it was learning how to play and figure out how stuff works because the game doesn't actually do a good job of explaining everything. The main appeal for me was the micromanagement aspect of the game as you control 7 members of a lancaster bomber crew to conduct operations over Europe. You equip them and modify your plane before each mission begins so there is a bit of funds management too in deciding where to allocate your money. Many of the reviews I've read say how hard this game is and yes I can see it being difficult to pick up but once you figure out how to play the game...

[spoiler] Put max armour on everything (including the crew) except 2 engines which should be light. Equip the hardest hitting guns with an ammo feed at the back and front of your plane. Have the best radio, hydraulics and oxygen systems. Fly at medium altitude for the most of the campaign. Don't even bother with equipping parachutes because everyone should survive. Only move your engineer and navigator to do stuff.[/spoiler]

... the micromanagement for the most part is reduced to pressing reload for two gunners every couple of minutes, pressing auto tag enemy fighters every few minutes and maybe changing altitude to make your bombing run. What I'm trying to say is I feel that as you progress through the game the main appeal of the game which is micromangement becomes too easy.

Other criticisms are that the fast forward button appears only when you're flying over Britain so there may be several minutes of flying and doing nothing which sucks and is boring. The game doesn't stress the importance of protecting your landing gear but you'll figure that out quickly. To save you frustration you could read this ([spoiler] on the bottom right hand corner of the screen there's a diagram that shows you the status of the plane. Make sure the wheels aren't black when you lower them to land or you may explode. If they are black and you have to land then make sure everyone is healed and the plane isn't too badly damage as in everything is red.[/spoiler]). Controls seem fiddly such as if I order a crew member to pick up a fire extinguisher or health pack they don't respond. The game doesn't stress that your plane should be level when bombing so do that to avoid frustration. You know what? The game doesn't explain a lot of things but it does have a guide section somewhere in game if you want a read which kind of helps.

Overall Bomber crew is a fun game.

Ein umwerfend gutes Spiel, besonders die Story ist spannend bis hinten gegen und steht dem Vorbild der Fernsehserie in keinster Weise nach.
Zuallererst sollte man definitiv sagen, dass The Walking Dead in erster Linie eine Erzählung ist und das Gameplay sich auf herumlaufen und gelegentliche Quicktime-Events beschränkt. Wer mit so etwas gar nichts anfangen kann, sollte The Walking Dead meiden.

In der Rolle von Lee Everett erlebt der Spieler den Kampf ums tägliche Überleben in einer postapokalyptischen Welt, in der jeder Mensch sich in ein Frischfleischfressendes Monster verwandelt hat. Aber auch den anderen Überlebenden ist schwer zu trauen und Verrat und Haß drohen die kleine Gruppe von Überlebenden auseinanderzureißen.
Die Grafik hat einen Comic-ähnlichen Stil und auch wenn sie teilweise nicht sehr hochwertig ist nach heutigen Standards, so ist sie doch exzellent umgesetzt und die Level sind schön gestaltet.
Die einzig wirklich hässlichen Texturen findet man bei den "Walkern" (die Untoten, also Zombies). So sehen die Haare zum Teil extrem schäbig aus.

Ein wichtiger Aspekt sind die Gepräche zwischen den Protagonisten, in denen man als Spieler auf verschiedene Weise entscheiden kann. Das spiegelt sich zum Teil auch später in der Story wieder.
In einigen Aspekten hätte dieses Feature aber noch mehr zur Geltung kommen können und einige Entscheidungen hätten noch folgenschwerer sein können.

[h1][b]Fazit[/b][/h1]

Alles in allem ist The Walking Dead ein großartiges Spiel und für mich die größte positive Überraschung des Jahres 2012 gewesen.
Ich wäre gewillt dem Spiel volle Punktzahl zu geben, allerdings stört mich, dass am Ende des Spiels und auch mittendrin viele allgemeine Dinge offen gelassen werden. So z.B. erfährt man nie, woher der Virus eigentlich kommt und wie es in anderen Teilen der Welt zu sich geht. Das wird zum Teil in der Fernsehserie erläutert, die man sich auch auf jeden Fall anschauen sollte. Allerdings passt das natürlich auch sehr gut ins Szenario, da Lee von jetzt auf gleich aus seinem alten Leben katapultiert wird.

Ein weiterer Aspekt ist, dass das Spiel einen nicht allzu hohen Wiederspielcharakter hat, was Wendungen in der Geschichte angeht. Im Detail kommen bei anderen Entscheidungen zwar in der Tat andere Sachen zum Vorschein, im großen und ganzen bleibt da aber nicht viel Neues zurück. Die Story an sich ist aber auch beim 2.ten Mal noch umwerfend gut.
Trotzdem eine klare Empfehlung!

For all the one´s who actually want to know why it is good, and question my opinion (with good reason, i´m just some guy on the internet in the end) here´s the long story.
DISCLAIMER: i´ve spent close to all my game time with this one my MOBILE PHONE so don´t judge by my play time

Super Hexagon is a fast paced game thad i´d under no circumstance call easy. The goal is to endure 60 seconds of the game basicly hating you, dodging walls with you triangle. Sounds simple, is simple.
The majority of the time you´ll spend here will have you dying. That may sound annoying, but it really isn´t, and there´s a good reason for that. That reason is the ovewhelmingly good feeling you´ll get after completing a level the first time. Even if not finishing levels (which there are 6 of) you´ll feel accomplished and FEEL how you improve in performance. This is a feeling that you may know if you´ve played any game of the Souls series or even Monster Hunter.

The Graphics are really quite simple yet immensely effective. It´s easy to describe the visuals, just look at steams screenshots,  but the feeling you get is a bit harder to describe. I´d describe it as something between tunnel vision and immersion. The pulses going in the rhytm of the beat, the changing of direction and colour.... it just is a beautiful composition.
Also: Epileptics beware, obviously.

Then there´s sound too, i don´t have much more to say than that it´s perfect. I´ve gotta admit, i´ve played with it turned off most of the time (mobile phone reasons), but when i turned it on from time to time i was just amazed by the blend of Fast paced beats and relaxing passages beating in your ears in best electro fashion.
As with the graphics: Simple yet effective and sooo sooo good.

The controls are good too, yet again, i´ve played mobile for the most part, but even the PC controls feel natural.
Nothing special to say here though.

There you have it, my opinion on this master piece of this "pick up ´n play" title!

Before we start: I don't like Doom 3. And I think, this DOOM (Doom 4) is a better installment than the last one.

I'm sorry, because maybe I've offended you, because you maybe played Doom 3 and maybe liked it.
And I can understand why you like it. A lot of people told me, why they liked Doom 3 and I can totally understand them all. 

But hear me out, because maybe I can warn you: Since I've played Doom 1 and 2, I was disappointed from Doom 3. It was slow, the levels were small, the sound was bad. It didn't felt like an successor of Doom. 

Doom 4 on the other hand, brought everything I wanted back: fast movement, no reloading, good sound, more open levels, visuals you can recognize from Doom 1 and 2 and the story stands more in the background, like in the old Dooms. 
The Campaign is great, if you liked the classic Dooms. The only problem for you could be the upgrade system for weapon mods, armor and ammunition. 
Also to get back more health, you have to perform glorykills ( a fast close combat animation) to get health and amnunition back. This'll stop you for 2 seconds or so.

Be warned, if you're more a fan of Doom 3: This game isn't scary or dark like Doom 3, you feel more like a badass than a marine who tries to survive.

I just finished the game, and it is far and away the best Assassin's Creed Game I have played.  As a few of the major review outlets have already pointed out, there is much greater depth to the gameplay than in previous entries, and I'm fairly certain that a significant chunk of that extra year of development time was spent by the devs playing The Witcher 3 to see how an action RPG is done.  I'm not saying that ACO is an RPG, but it certainly feels more like one than any of the previous games.  

Egypt is gorgeous, Bayek is relatable, and the world is full of lore-enriching secrets that made me excited every time I saw a question mark on the map with a distinct golden tint.  The side quests were typically well-designed multi-stage endeavors that made playing the role of Egypt's Medjay feel meaningful, as well as making the world feel very much alive.  The main campaign is good, even great at times.  Without giving anything away, the ending didn't have the positively hollow feeling that Syndicate's did, and more importantly, it felt earned.  

The new gear system was appreciated in that it was fun and balanced, as opposed to the needlessly convoluted system of Unity and the overly-streamlined (but by no means bad) gear system of Syndicate.  I actually liked that outfits were purely cosmetic with outfit upgrades existing as a separate crafting system applied to Bayek rather than to individual outfits.  My only real gripe about the leveling system is that given the sheer amount of content in the game, the cap should have been higher.  That said, you can keep unlocking ability points even after reaching the max level, and based on the number of abilities I never wound up unlocking, it seems like the ability tree was meant to be crafted based on preferred play style instead of being maxed out to the point where Bayek just becomes OP.  

Performance-wise, the game runs just fine at high settings on a GTX 1060 with an i7 6700HQ and 16GB of DDR4.  By "just fine," I mean that it never quite gets to a stable 60 fps, so I just locked it to 45 and enjoyed the game.  I'll note that while 60 is always preferred, I'll take 45 FPS on a 4K screen at 60% resolution scaling.  It still looked great, and all frame rates above 30 fps are above the "floor" of remotely enjoyable frame rates in video games as far as I'm concerned.  But that's just me.  

Might as well just add that this game did not murder my CPU.  Optimization could have been a bit better, but I'll wait and see how things are several patches from now before giving a final verdict on that front.

When you put into perspective that this game is a Kickstarter project which had only a budget of 50k+ $ you appreciate this game even more. The attention to detail and level of commitment put into this game shows from the very start until the very end of your play through. The art style and overall presentation of this game is beautiful. I also have to say the font chosen for the text is so subtle yet so elegant and satisfying to read. Every song in this game lets you feel some kind of emotion, from excitement to peace, from happiness to sadness, from fulfillment to emptiness... The core gameplay mechanics are simple and straightforward, while in combat you attack and dodge, patience is key and rewarding. Every successful hit and dodge is satisfying even though you do it a 1000 times over the course of your play through. The enemies can be challenging but with some practice every obstacle you face in this game is possible to overcome. Your main goal is to explore, interact with the NPCs and find your next task. Even though you don't have to really understand the lore of this game you can try and interpret it in your own way, it gives additional flavor to your experience and connects you with the game on an emotional basis. There are also many secrets in this game, which can be easily skipped if you don't pay attention to them. My advice is to be curious and not rush through this game as a lot of wonderful content is waiting for you in those hidden areas. I could go on and on, on the satisfaction that I had while playing this game, and I am not even finished playing it. This is truly a hidden gem for everyone that hasn't played it yet. It doesn't surprise me why so many people rated this game positively, as it deserves every praise it can get. I am looking forward to Team Cherry's next project, Silksong, where I have no doubt they will once again deliver big time.

I have been a long-time fan of the Tomb Raider games, ever since the first one game was released in 1996 on PS1. Once I was old enough to start playing it, I remember all the times I was flattened by boulders, accidently jumped off something too soon or too late, and used my limited save crystals at the wrong times either before I was going to die, or when I had almost no health left. (These were tough times and I was still too young to understand the concept of “strategy”. I was 8, oh well.)

But fast forward to when the first of the rebooted Tomb Raider series was released, and every time I made a mistake, I felt like a monster for each gruesome death and horrible injury Lara suffered. When Rise of the Tomb Raider was released I knew what I was getting into, and began to appreciate the adventure a whole lot more.  

The story

Rise of the Tomb Raider continues the story of Lara Croft, only a few years after the events that took place on the island in the first game. With her newly-found survival experience and training, she has spent the last few years following the clues left on here fathers’ last expedition before his death. It was this expedition that led to everyone believing the that the Croft family name was synonyms with mad men and fools searching for answers that aren’t there; but Lara hopes to change that in locating the Divine Source, a mysterious power that can grant immortality. But with all great power comes greed, and a tyrannic organization named ‘Trinity’ intends to harness the power for themselves. Your mission: Find the Divine source, take down an entire army, and re-instate the Croft name as the great explorers to have ever lived. 

Gameplay

The game runs on a 3rd person shooter mechanics, but a lot of the game is based on the exploration aspects. Scaling mountains, hunting for supplies, solving intricate puzzles are only a fraction of things to do in this game. The game feels and runs as smoothly and the graphics are crystal clear, from the reflections off the water, to way sunlight diffuses to the trees. Very close detail has been given to make each and every location feel unique and as spectacular as the previous level.

Music

The music adds to the ambience of the game, and makes every location seem even bigger that what you first anticipated. And as always there are lots of moments that hail back to the violin-jump scares of the original Tomb Raider games to make sure that you are awake and constantly trick you into stuffing up. (I hate boulders! They are the stuff of nightmares!)

Overall 8/10

Pros-
A solid 10/10 game. Fun and engaging combat. Tons of customization with your weapon and upgrade loadout. The story is amazing, and it gets even better once you start doing side missions. Even when you beat the game there's tons more of stuff left to do like upgrading and collecting the weapons, and completing side missions.
The music is also outstanding for a game. The music doesn't have 1 or 2 good songs, but instead all 40 of them are good enough to listen to on their own. The game also has a nice balance between being super easy, and insanely hard. You can make the game so easy it automatically fights for you, (basically story mode), or you could make it so hard that enemies one shot you no matter what. 

Cons-
Sadly there's not a whole lot of variety in difficulty settings as its just 4 main difficulties, and some special upgrades for easy mode. A lot of the shooter sections also become stale after a while as there's not many upgrades to the shooter sections if you include missiles, not including those there's none. There's also not much of a replayability factor so once you 100% beat the game there's not a whole lot you can do. 

Final Notes-
This game can easily provide over 60 hours of content though if you speed through it, and you will definitely get your moneys worth on this game. I would recommend this to anybody if you're willing to spend the $40 full price, or the $20 on sale.

Bis jetzt knappe 80 Stunden Spielzeit. Und ich muss sagen, das Spiel fühlt sich runder als ARK an und spielt sich auch wesentlich leichter.  Denn während ich ARK nur mit über einem Dutzend Mods als Spielbar empfinde, reichen mit bei Atlas ein paar INI Anpassungen. Zudem hat es auch wie ich finde, mehr PvE Elemente, als ARK.
Updates kommen recht häufig und mit merklichem Inhalt. Es wurden auch viele Schwächen, die ARK hatte ausgebessert, auch wenn noch nicht alle. Ist aber auch noch EARLY ACCESS und kein fertiges Spiel (was einige zu vergessen scheinen, wenn man sich mal die Kommentare durchliest). Wäre das Spiel bereits abgeschlossen, würde ich eine Kaufempfehlung aussprechen. Zumindest für all diejenigen, die mit diese Art Spiel Freude haben. Da es jedoch noch nicht fertig ist, muss auch ich abwarten und sehen, in welche Richtung es weiter geht. Denn der Schwerpunkt des Spiels soll eher bei PvP liegen.  Und da ich nur an PvE Interesse habe, besteht meine Sorge darin, dass es schlussendlich nur auf PvP ausbalanziert und dadurch genauso ein vermurktes Balancing wie ARK haben wird. Das lässt sich zwar alles korrigieren, macht aber sehr viel Arbeit. Deswegen noch keine bzw. wenn dann nur eine bedingte Kaufempfehlung.

*Meine Erfahrungen basieren ausschließlich auf eigenem privaten Server mit paar Freunden. Wie es auf öffentlichen Servern zugeht, kenne ich nur aus Videos. Da ich jedoch aus paar anderen Spielen weiß, wie unausgereift einige Spieler sind und wie gerne die einem den Spaß verderben, werde ich es vermeiden, bei Atlas je einen Fuß auf einen öffentlichen Server zu setzen. Ich vermute auch, dass sehr viel Frust und Unmut durch eben noch fehlende Sicherheitsmechanismen auf öffentlichen Servern entstanden ist, da viele ihr schwer erspieltes Hab und Gut an andere Spieler verloren haben. Deswegen erwähne ich das extra, da meine Spielerfahrung eine andere ist, als die von (ich vermute mal) den Großteil der anderen Spieler, die auf öffentlichen Servern gespielt haben.
Und deswegen kann ich jedem, der mit dem Spiel was anfangen kann und eine ruhige Runde alleine oder mit Freunden spielen will, ans Herz legen, sich seinen eigenen Server einzurichten. Es gibt Wege auch auf schwacher Hardware, die große original Map zu spielen. Einfach googeln ;) Oder man bastelt sich selber eine kleinere Karte. Dafür ist jedoch etwas mehr Arbeit notwendig. Vor allem, wenn man die Powerstones, EndBoss, usw. richtig einbauen will. Es lohnt sich jedoch und man hat zudem die volle Kontrolle über die Einstellungen, Backup und Mods (die jetzt vermutlich wie Pilze nach dem Regen wachsen werden) ;)

I have a love\hate relationship with this game. I love the concept, love the gameplay, and love the customizability. I can feel the love from the Devs.  However, I'm extremely disappointed in how sluggish loading times are and also very frustrated with the file management system. My rig should be able to soundly handle this game.

File management lacks the following:
-Save overwriting (cut down on the volume of saves). Each time you "Save" it automatically creates a new save file.
-Due to volume of saves, it compounds the time it takes to bring up the "Load" menu.
-File deletion: You can't select multiple save files to delete simultaneously, leaving you to click OK and then wait for the list to refresh.
-Bug related to deleting files while accessing Load menu from Starting Screen: tried to delete an old save; it not only failed to do so, but also decided to load the save file (which feels like forever).

I'd love to play this game for hours but I don't want to dedicate most of that time to Load screens.

玩了十几个小时之后评价一下《死亡细胞（Dead Cells）》这款游戏。外面对这个游戏的定义是Metroidvania+Roguelite，但首先需要明确的是：死亡细胞不是一个Metroidvania游戏。它不像奥里与黑暗森林/空洞骑士那样有着严丝合缝、循序渐进、峰回路转的关卡设计，所谓的“银河城要素”仅仅在于你在特定关卡里打掉关底Boss后解锁的符文，也就是藤蔓、爬墙、传送、砸地这些功能，基本上属于“至少得有这些花样”的浓度。你要说这就代表它是个银河城，那差不多就像是说起点上的古武机甲文是硬科幻。死亡细胞的关卡是随机生成的，这在客观上也明示了你不用对它的关卡精巧度有什么期待，总之就是一路排头砍过去或者一路扔道具等怪被射死（当然还是要熟悉怪的特性），完全不存在水之逃生或白色宫殿那样的考验环节——苦痛之路就别提了，人作死，就会死！除了这一点之外，死亡细胞是一个挺棒的Roguelite刷刷刷游戏。过关的主要难点在于你是否合理搭配了两种武器和两种辅助道具的特性，以及是否选择了正确的加点。游戏中的武器和道具全部可以通过反复洗属性词条来获得更好的搭配效果，一个“夹住敌人后使其燃烧”的捕兽夹当然应该和“对燃烧的敌人造成100%额外伤害”的武器配合，而“如果附近有敌人流血/中毒/燃烧则你的DPS提高XX点”的突变（也就是本局游戏中可选的Perk）和“道具冷却时间缩短百分之XX”的突变到底该如何选择，就要看你自己的偏好了。由于你捡到什么装备全靠随机（以及之前的收集），这游戏的一大乐趣就在于因地制宜，搭配出各种各样幺蛾子的杀怪套路组合，然后在实战中检验它们的效率，并不是昏昏欲睡地一遍遍碰运气。作为Roguelite的部分，游戏中有大量武器图纸——杀怪捡到图纸后还要通过当前的这一小关才算收入囊中，死掉的话会爆出来，十分心疼！然后花费细胞去解锁图纸，最后这些已解锁的武器就会挂在起始区域的这堆瓶子里，看上去琳琅满目，很有成就感。而且各种武器的打击感区别很大，爽快度也很足，看得出来很是下了工夫！

I've been thoroughly enjoying this game, and there is still more that I'd like to do and see.  However, it's certainly not for everyone, and I feel that it's missing a few key additions that would make it far more enjoyable.

The short version/TL:DR:
This is a game about exploration and enjoying your unbridled freedom.  If you're looking for a game with a rich plot and interesting storyline, look elsewhere.  If you're looking for a game to just explore, take your time, and take in the scenery, give it a try.  To put this in perspective:  If you played Skyrim for several days or weeks before ever finding a greybeard, you'd likely enjoy this game, because I spent my first 10 hours or so on the starting planet.  On the other hand, if you were fighting Alduin on the first or second day in Skyrim, I wouldn't suggest trying the game, because if you rush it, you will run out of things to do very quickly.  If there is a sale or price drop to 20-30 dollars, then I would suggest that everyone should at least try it out for themselves, because I'm certainly glad that I did, even with its current price.


The long version/bugs/suggestions for improving the title:
The game is fairly well-designed, in my opinion, with the in-depth tutorial and how you progressively find bigger and better things.  You'll find slightly better multi-tools, ships, and upgrades the longer you play.  You eventually get so many exosuit storage spaces that you can trivialize things like space combat and exploring planets with extreme conditions by just stocking up on shielding sheets.  Finding planets with resources like the gravitino ball or sac venom makes turning a large profit fairly easy,  and the constant sentinel attacks keep you on your toes.  On one planet with sac venom, I was able to make around 10m Units per hour.  There is a lot of grinding in the game to get the resources you need, and some of the planets feel like previous planets with slight variation to color schemes and signs of life.  That being said, the game is very visually pleasing, and some of the plants and animals are fascinating and bizarre to look at and interact with.  The game isn't perfect, but if you're a fan of adventure and exploration, it's a very enjoyable experience.

The game does have its bugs though:  One outpost I came across was floating in the air because of the sudden terrain drop below it.  Landing the ship near steep terrain could cause you to get launched far into the air when you exit the ship, or send the ship into orbit when you try to start flying again from said landing position.  When trying to scan all the animals on a planet, I've had some spawn inside the ground and had to blow up the ground to get to them (not talking about cave systems, but literally inside the ground).  I've also experienced about 3-4 crashes, but with how frequently the game saves (every time you leave your ship) or has places to save available, this wasn't a huge issue as it amounts to about 1 crash per 10-12 hours of gameplay(for me at least).

As far as what I think the game could use, and what would make it a far more enjoyable experience:
1. The option to have more social exchanges would be great.  If you could join friends and experience things with them, it would greatly add to the overall experience.  If there was a separate market system just for players to buy or sell resources to eachother, it would make obtaining some things far less annoying.
2. Blueprint duplicates are kind of annoying, and you eventually stop grabbing them because it becomes a waste of time to do so.  If you instead got around 5k-10k units for each duplicate you found for "uploading it to the galactic trade network" or whatever, then you'd be more inclined to grab them for some extra money.
3. Traveling along the surface of planets is not always an enjoyable experience.  especially if its barren and you're gathering resources.  Flying the ship along the surface doesn't show all the resources or animal life below you.  If there was some sort of land vehicle, either deployed when you land your ship, or craftable, it would make scanning planets and gathering resources a more enjoyable experience.
4. Ship trading is an expensive and time-consuming process.  Waiting for ships to come into a trading post or space port, then manaully looking at each one to see if it's an upgrade or not can be tiresome.  It would be nice if your previous ship could be traded to help reduce the new ships cost, or if you could sell your own ship to npcs or possibly other players if you have multiple.  It would be helpful if there was a market setup for buying and selling ships to speed up the process, even if its just from npcs.
5. Another ship-related issue I've had is determining what ship class it is.  I'd like if either the npc told you what ship class it was (after learning the words) or if it had its own universal symbol when you look at the inventory (like a little gun icon for fighter, planet for exploration, and unit symbol for trade ships).  You can usually spot a transport ship because its so big and bulky, but explorers and fighters look pretty similar.  In my opinion, fighters are the only ones worth using so that you can deal with pirates.  On multiple occasions, I'd buy a new ship, go out and test it, find out its an explorer, and bring it back to the space station to be an expensive decoration just sitting there as I go back to my old ship.
6. The final point I'd like to make is that many of these would eventually be addressed with workshop/modding support for the game.

Overall, I'm still enjoying the game as I near 50 hours playtime, but I'd like to see what more can become of it.  Keep in mind, this is all my own personal opinion on the game from my own personal experiences with it.  I may come back to edit this if I feel there's more I should add.

Look, is this the spiritual successor to Chivalry? Yes. Does it feel way more polished? Yes. Was I good at Chivalry? No. Am I good at Mordhau? Also no. Do I love Mordhau? YES. Can I get a positive K/D in most games? No. Does it f**king matter? ALSO NO.

If the concept of this game is interesting to you, get in while the getting's good. It's stupidly fun charging into battle repeatedly even when the result is getting your skull splattered by a maul outside your FOV (oh yeah, max out your FOV right away, trust me). Sure, I almost smashed my Logitech g502 when a guy with a frying pan deflected my every axe swing and cut my legs off with a swing of the ol' cast-iron, but that's besides the point. This game is just stupidly good hack-and-slash fun, even when you're bad like me.

There's a stupid amount of depth to the combat system, and so far it feels surprisingly balanced across all the different weapon types, different grips, loadout customization, etc. I played on launch day, I fought through the server disconnects and ping issues, I didn't get any exp/gold for the first 7hrs of gameplay, and I DONT REALLY CARE because I had a ton of fun along the way.

This game has the opportunity for so many intense moments, like being rushed by 4 enemies and managing to time your parries just right to keep alive for a few extra seconds before firing off a riposte and splitting open one of their skulls, suddenly it's only 3v1 and wait what is that? More of my team is here now and I just took out another guy because he got distracted. Sure, most of the time it's just me getting steamrolled by that wave of enemies but every now and then I feel like the damn Hound out there.

I never got into Alpha but I had my eye on this game for a long time, and I can proudly say it's everything I hoped for so far. The ONLY real criticism I have of the game itself is they need more maps, and I feel like Chiv had certain maps that were more interesting in their design, but that is something I'm sure they can add to over time.

Отличный мясной шутер на легком и среднем уровнях сложности, на высоком – есть трудности, такие как мародёры и может быть гладиатор, но к концу игры мародеры становятся не такими опасными врагами, так как успеваешь научится их контрить и убивать. На кошмаре игра предоставляет полный набор испытаний, вы должны досконально пройти игру, собрать все секреты и открыть все предметы на базе, на этом уровне сложности – реально сложно, иногда в игре встречаются отдельные арены, которые представляют самые сложные испытания в игре – и это не боссы. Игра хорошо оптимизирована и идет стабильные 144 кадра в 2К и 135 кадров в 4К, но есть одно место – это добивание гладиатора, и там есть просадка, почему – непонятно, ибо это кат-сцена. Паркур – слабая сторона игры, есть секреты, при сборе которых вы будете ненавидеть эту игру и ее создателей. Если проходить игру на высоком уровне сложности и собирать все секреты она занимает около 22 часов, учитывая сколько сейчас стоят современные игры, то игра стоит своих денег, но не Deluxe издание, оно дает скин и звук из классической игры, и вроде бы два дополнения, но они еще не вышли и я думаю, что эта игра не стоит 2800 рублей, лучше купить RDR2. Эпичная музыка – есть. Примерно 40% способностей костюма и 60% способностей рун и оружия – мне показались бесполезными, но так чисто ради достижения можно прокачать и повозится с поиском секретов. Если просто пробегать игру на средней сложности и без заморочки с секретами - я думаю шутер часов на 10-12. В целом игру могу порекомендовать, но не всем, это не просто мясной шутер, игра требует того, чтобы вы были сосредоточены и внимательны, либо низкая сложность игры – для вас. За те деньги, что просят за нее это слишком слабо и скучновато поэтому не рекомендую, только для тех кто знает, что он покупает.

Hunt: Showdown...o per meglio dire Hunt: Horrors Of The Gilded Age il mai nato.

Hunt è un gioco perfetto per tutti coloro che si aspettano l'ennesimo Battle Royale ma SOPRATUTTO a tutti quei giocatori a cui piace camperare e lasciar fare il lavoro sporco ad altri.
Sia chiaro il gioco è ben fatto, il cryengine è sfruttato oserei dire perfettamente, l'ambientazione nel Bayou della Lousiana è da paura, le armi e la ricostruzione storica di fine west ci sta veramente benissimo ed anche le animazioni dei mostri sono qualcosa che sinceramente ci voleva, dopo tragedie storiche come Mass Effect Andromeda ed altro.
Crytek, ancora una volta (per quanto il gioco non sia ancora del tutto ottimizzato) ha saputo fare qualcosa di bello sfruttando ciò che era suo ormai da una vita.

Ora arrivano però le note dolenti.

Hunt è un gioco rivoluzionario o cmq innovativo? 
Come idea sicuramente SI...come sviluppo, obbiettivi e metagame ASSOLUTAMENTE NO.

Questo è un gioco PVE/PVP dove l'obbiettivo principale dovrebbe essere quello di uccidere il boss per fuggire con la bounty...cosa che non fa MAI e ribadisco MAI nessuno visto che è più facile ammazzare tutti i player presenti nella mappa e dopo, nel caso, farlo...manco fossimo su PUBG o FORTNITE.
In 20 ore di beta mi sarà capitato di vedere un banish una o due volte, mentre io ne ho fatti esattamente 32 (quasi uno a match).

Crytek ha ben pensato di annullare il progetto precedente per farne uno al passo coi tempi ma ha commesso un doppio errore.

E' verissimo che i giochi Battle Royale stanno andando da paura, ma il 2018 è l'anno del grande ritorno del genere coop pve (Vermintide 2, Deeprock Galactic, Sea Of Thieves, A Way Out, State Of Decay 2, GTFU e molto altro ancora) ed un gioco come Horror Of The Gilded Age avrebbe fatto faville a dire poco, diversificandosi dalla massa di prodotti tutti uguali.

Per come la vedo io se avessero mantenuto il vecchio progetto avrebbero venduto il triplo.

Sia chiaro (me lo dico da solo) Twitch e Youtube non sono dati attendibili ma cmq ci danno un'indicazione di cosa preferisce la maggior parte del pubblico attuale ed Hunt è già praticamente morto: quando non ci sono Sequisha o qualche streamer americano famoso, a malapena raggiunge i 1000 spettatori.

Il gioco è brutto?
NO ed anzi, devo dire che a tratti è anche divertente, ma non ha quel mordente che ti dovrebbe tenere incollato giorno e notte visto che è un Pubg fatto male, un Fortnite dei poveri e per quanto io sia stato duro sotto sotto sapete che è la verità.

Si entra nel match, si campera, si da la caccia agli altri player e DOPO, forse, se avanza tempo si fa il boss per la bounty.

Compratelo se volete qualcosa di alternativo, magari quando sarà in forte sconto.
EVITATELO COME LA PESTE se cercate qualcosa di differente ed innovativo.

This is my most-played game on Steam for a reason: it has near-endless replayability. The only similarities between Terraria and Minecraft is the fact that both are sandbox games, and both have mining and crafting.

The music is often overlooked in Terraria, and to be honest it's very good, even though it can become repetitive after a while. 

The graphics are not exactly setting the bar high, but it fits the game very well, and allows it to run comfortably on older systems.

Network play can be somewhat jarring due to ping delays if you are playing on international servers (similar to Minecraft) but works fine on a local networks and national servers.

There are numerous boss fights and events, and lots of looting and character progression, even some significant world progression as you enter "Hardmode".

Add all this to the fact that you can get this game for $2.49 during sales then there is really no reason not to give it a go. Be prepared to spend at least ~50 hours on it.

Если бы не 3 ценных металла, которые таки надо копать - я бы все исследование вообще сократил до посещения станций в системе, что отдает скукой.
В связи с этим мысль о том, что нужно куда-то полететь может даже вызвать приступ злобы.

В игре есть возможность соорудить базу, но я о ней ничего толком не узнал, потому что все ее обитатели имеют квесты, в рамках которых ты должен для них куда-то полететь и что-то найти... Но в связи с предыдущим пунктом - не хочется. Поэтому вся моя база - это компьютер в пещере и телепортер рядом.

Про примитивное взаимодействие с представителями рас тут уже не раз писали. Упомяну лишь, что в торговых отношениях с ними нет баланса. Вот просто нет. "Баланс" - это про торговые ресурсы, а про остальное - сливаешь ионизированный кобальт тысячами и становишься миллионером. Покупаешь экзотический корабль S класса и никуда на нем не летишь, потому что "там то-же самое".

В итоге, в моем случае, цель то для игры ставится, но мотивацию под нее мне лично найти очень сложно. Так что я считаю так... Если вы готовы окунуться в примитивный процедурно генерируемый космический мир, у вас богатая фантазия по этой тематике и вы не станете задавать вопроса "зачем" - добро пожаловать! 
К тому-же есть моды. На всякие раздражающие косяки (а их все еще много) люди уже сделали патчи, которые их исправляют или убирают вовсе. Есть еще и Rayrod's Overhaul, где чувак добавил около 13000 различных вариаций биомов руками. И, хоть сейчас он допиливается под новый патч, но с ним определенно будет другой экспириенс от исследования.

Несмотря на примитивность как игровых механик, так и планет - моего внутреннего аутиста игра порадовала. Насобирал белкового жемчуга на год вперед. А моды сделали процесс быстрее и приятнее.

Para quem gosta da Serie Warhammer 40,000 vai amar de jogar esse game sensacional, vale cada centavo, eu peguei na promoção, porque R$ 106,00 esta caro ele deveria estar por R$ 50,00 esta bem pago, segue analise detalhada.

A marca Warhammer cresceu muito ao longo dos anos e acabou por saltar das nossas mesas para os computadores com vários jogos. Dawn of War é uma das séries que se destacou pela sua qualidade e a capacidade de oferecer uma versão videojogável ao nível da escala que a série Warhammer 40K promete e prega nas suas histórias do jogo de tabuleiro. Para este jogo novo lançamento, o estúdio Relic Entertainment ficou novamente encarregue da sua produção.

Warhammer 40K: Dawn of War 3 dá o destaque a três facções com os seus respectivos líderes, os Space Marines liderado pelo já conhecido Gabriel Angelos, os Eldar por Farseer Macha e os Orks por Warboss Gorgutz. Neste jogo é nos contada a história de uma arma de larga escala de nome Spear of Khaine perdida no planeta Acheron, arma este que estas três facções tentarão conquistar para seu próprio benefício.
As missões do jogo irão colocar-nos faseadamente nas mãos de cada uma destas facções no qual iremos entender os motivos e conhecer o método de funcionamento de cada uma delas. Ao bom estilo de um jogo de estratégia, teremos um formato pedra/papel/tesoura entre estas três facções, no qual precisamos de aprender as nuances de cada uma para sermos bastante eficientes em combate. Apesar de ser bastante simples a início, o jogo começa na campanha a demonstrar um problema que vai sendo mais profundo ao longo do jogo, complexidade no que toca ao lore e ao conhecimento específico de cada uma das unidades.

Dentro de jogo, temos um sistema bastante simples onde um herói será acompanhado de várias unidades e teremos de efectuar as várias missões que nos são impostas, desde ataques em larga escala, até a invasão de fortes que requerem uma jogabilidade um pouco mais furtiva, irá depender da missão. Iremos recrutar essas unidades através da colheita de recursos para serem usados nas respectivas infraestruturas e fica ao nosso critério se queremos esperar um pouco mais de tempo por uma unidade maior, ou continuamente debitar soldados mais fracos para um exército mais avolumado.

Com o passar das missões vamos começando a descobrir novas habilidades não só para o nosso herói como também para as nossas unidades, sendo necessário prestar bastante atenção ao que estamos a fazer para conseguirmos tirar o maior partido delas sem nos perdermos com a enxurrada de informação que nos será atirada. Para os fãs de Warhammer, saber estes detalhes será um regalo.

Depois da campanha podemos ingressar no multiplayer e pôr à prova todo o nosso conhecimento. Como seria de esperar, aqui a nossa abordagem para com o jogo muda um pouco, sendo necessário agir e reagir de acordo com os acontecimentos do momento. No único modo do jogo teremos que enfrentar outra equipa de jogadores e destruir as suas infraestruturas adjacentes e depois a principal para conseguirmos a vitória, um pouco como os MOBA, mas nem tudo será tão simples.

A maneira como o jogo foi construído obriga o jogador a não se excitar com as pequenas vitórias que iremos conseguir nas várias batalhas que iremos conseguir ao longo do tempo. A manutenção das nossas unidades é bastante importante e os ataques suicidas ou sem nexo terão consequências graves como contra-golpes rápidos e que poderão deixar toda a nossa estratégia e equipa em desvantagem. É um modo bastante equilibrado e que criará momentos interessantes se tivermos bons jogadores em acção.

Respeitando um pouco a vertente de tabuleiro, podemos também personalizar as nossas unidades brincando com as paletes de cores e gravando posteriormente. São apenas simples modificações cosméticas que são bem vindas. Dawn of War 3 é um jogo com um detalhe gráfico simples e que não se torna demasiado exuberante. As grandes batalhas têm uma boa quantidade de efeitos e jogos de cores para encher a nossa vista. Toda a sonoplastia está muito bem trabalhada e as actuações de voz dos Ork são bastante hilariantes. Apesar de nunca ter experimentado um título desta série, gostei do que vi em Dawn of War 3, a história não é nada de inovadora mas serve para este tipo de jogo e os aspectos mais complexos poderão assustar os jogadores mais novos, mas no geral é uma experiência positiva.

Se gostam de jogos de estratégia com um forte foco no multiplayer, então Dawn of War 3 é para vocês. É rápido, interessante e tem muito conteúdo para os mais geeks explorarem.

Positivo:

Personalização das personagens interessante.
Um modo campanha consistente
Vertente multiplayer viciante
Actuações de voz

Negativa:

Um pouco simplista por vezes
Algumas missões básicas

[b]Phenomenal tactical FPS that improves upon it's previous entry in almost every way. [/b]

Pros:
-Tight tactical gameplay
-Amazing feeling gunplay 
-Sounds are just incredible
-Graphics are really good for an indie game
-Incredibly satisfying

Cons:
-Not the most polished game (but not that bad either)
-Third person player animations need some work
-Kinda short on content (plenty of guns but not that many maps and modes)
-Matchmaking and server browser can be better

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

This is the game you are looking for if you are tired of bullet sponges and too much casual hand holding in FPSes. In Insurgency you have to actually be aware of your surroundings and be very thoughtful of where you are and where enemies could be, since there's no minimap, 3D spotting and the HUD is minimal. So you're forced to play mindfully in order to do well since a single shot can kill you.
There's no way around it, this game is brutal and the learning curve is quite steep, but when you start to get the hang of it it becomes an extremely satisfying experience that can't be found in any other product atm.

[h1] Sound [/h1]

The sound effects and sound tech in this game are just brilliant, I have yet to play a FPS that does it so well and is this immersive. 

[h1] Graphics [/h1]

The first person models and animations for the weapons are excellent, on par (if not better) than most of AAA shooters coming out in 2018. This was already a strong point in Insurgency Source and they've managed to improve it even further on the UE4. 

Overall environment detail is very high and each map has a distinct look and feel to it. 

Third person player characters could be better, the textures are not that great and the actual models feel a bit off in scale. Also, although the third person player animations have improved since the beta, they are not up to standard and seem very stiff and unrealistic sometimes.

[h1] Optimization [/h1]

After playing the pre-order betas I was left a bit disappointed by the lack of optimization and polish that was present at the time.
But I'm glad to report that devs managed to fix most of the issues and the game runs really great now (GTX 1060 6gb, Ryzen 2700x, 8gb RAM). There's still room for improvement though, especially in textures loading in game looking blurry and some stuttering here and there.

[h1] Veredict [/h1]

As it stands on release the game is incredibly fun and satisfying and is definitely a must buy. And despite still not in the level of polish and content we should expect from a fully released product, given NWI's track record I have no doubt this game will receive many great updates and become the great product it deserves to be.

好久没写测评了，但这款游戏又让我有了写测评的欲望 。

游戏的画面和音乐那些就不介绍了，因为这些你们都可以从预览视频里看得到，而且也有不少专业的测评家评过分了，看看我玩的小时数，就知道我对于游戏的欣赏程度了，我玩了两遍，走了两条故事线，顺便拿了不少成就，我在这里想谈谈游戏人物给我的感觉，按照惯例，我的测评是会剧透的，请还没玩的各位慎重哈。

【剧透预警】

首先，我得说这个游戏在人物塑造方面花了功夫，游戏里的每一个人都是现实生活中的一个投影，他们就像是你的一个高中同学、小学玩伴，或邻居家的爷爷奶奶那样，在某个时刻突然让你产生一种亲切的熟悉感，对，没错，亲切，这种感觉是这个游戏给我的感觉之一，嘴里嚷着crime的Greg，让我想起曾经一起翻墙逃课的死党，温暖全能的大男孩August，更像是我高中时班里独当一面的班长，或大学中遇到的某个可靠的学长，而外表冷酷内心细腻的Bea，则是我的那个整天冷脸吐槽我的“哥们“或损友，游戏的背景和格调虽然很有美式风格，但里面的人物却始终看起来如此亲切，跟着Mae回到家乡，就仿佛自己回到了家乡一样，面临着各种怀旧，各种新鲜，和各种无奈。

Greg是我最喜欢的一个人物，在游戏未开始前我甚至以为他也是主角之一（毕竟在封面上），他调皮、活泼而热情，外表看起来坏坏的，随身还带着刀子，天天嚷着要做坏事，我前面说了，他就是那个曾经一起翻墙逃课的兄弟，但是，谁能想到这样的兄弟也有成长的一天呢？他与August真的是很有爱的一对，两个人性格互补，彼此照顾，并且相约要去更好的地方生活，多么美好的一对，当Greg站在湖边对Mae说出他对未来的困惑时，我相信这些困惑已经变成了他无言的解答，我并不担心他和August，因为他们总是能在互补的同时保留对方的天性，他们虽然会吵架，虽然会有很多很多的问题，但是相信他们会走下去的，就算走下去又怎样？人生得一人相知足矣。

Bea，则是一个非常非常好的朋友。她内心细腻、温柔，有着自己的梦想，自己的执着，当现实以剧烈的撞击摧毁了她的生活时，她果断的扛起了家庭的担子，成为了家中的支柱，每天见到她，她的第一句话都是“累”，我相信她真的很累，累到没时间去休息，没时间去做梦，她以不屑的眼神和嘴边的香烟来掩饰自己内心的无助，而这样的她，在遇到朋友任性而充满孩子气的冒犯后，仍然会选择原谅，选择理解，她在现实面前强装的理性，在面对Mea的那一刻完全崩溃了，因为Mae就是她心中的那个仍然做梦的孩子，现实固然无情，但是可否为之放弃游乐世界的勇气呢？我认为，答案是否。

而Mae，Mae，Mae，Mae，Mae，Mae在某种意义上，有点像我自己。她善良、风趣，充满孩子气，但有时候又很鲁莽，会得罪很多人，她有一套自己看世界的独到体系，在乌合之众中发问的往往是她，在树下为落叶而流泪的也往往是她，即便我不是百分之百的像她，我也想成为她，成为一个“怪胎”，一个质疑者，一个legends的创造者，关于她奇怪的梦境，我觉得可以从很多方面去解读，但又都差了点意思，希望有玩过的人来一起讨论哈。

其次，我来说说这个故事的主题，成长以及生活的荒谬。我觉得在这个世界上，每个人都或多或少的会有一些成长上的困惑，而每个人又都默默地承担了这份困惑，直到完全遗忘了它们。这个游戏将这些困惑全都摊开了，仿佛煎饼摊上的大饼，唰的一下就被全部展现了出来，为什么小镇要引入高速公路？为什么小镇要革新？为什么朋友都要离去？为什么父母变得更加苍老却更为忙碌了？上大学到底有多重要？辍学又有多糟糕？为什么像Bea这样的好人会陷入绝境？这到底是谁的错？这些全部都是Mae所追问而我们会开始思考的问题，一切都在变化，而这种变化在很多时候都是荒谬的、不合理的，甚至人类本来就是荒谬和不合理的，我们要如何看待这些问题？

当然，也不要指望一个游戏能给你全部的答案，这些问题本来就没有标准答案，更何况玩家们来自五湖四海，感受又怎么可能会相同，只是正如我一直说的，好的游戏会让你去思考，会给你一个审视自己的机会，这与好的书籍、电影和音乐无异。你可以从游戏中审视自己，也可以在游戏中感受亲切的氛围，更可以捉鬼、解密，从各种小细节中感受到开发者的用心，并且手机成就也是一件容易让人上瘾的事hhh

再说一句，我真的好喜欢Mae的涂鸦啊啊啊，不说了我去买马克笔了。

With a quirky artstyle, but a scientific approach to liquids and gasses simulation, Oxygen Not Included (ONI) is a game that challenges as much as it educates. 

A much more optimistic approach to an ant colony simulator than the likes of Rimworld and others, in ONI you are challenged primarily by the environment and your own want of expanding beyond what you're capable of.

If this sounds like something you'd enjoy, then I'd recommend it to you to try, and see if you like or even love it.

ONI is great playing it while on voice-chat with someone else playing an entirely different colony at about the same level of development as you, you're able to talk through your challenges and get help, and find greater humor in the funny moments that happen in a game like this. This is why I have nominated Oxygen Not Included for Steam's "Better with Friends" (2019) award. Though as a single player game I doubt it will win a category so dominated by multiplayer games.

Assassins Creed Odyssey brings the best parts of a lot of single player RPG's together into a single game.

The menu system seems inspired from DA Inquisition

Greek mythology reminds me of God of War 2

Crawling through the gaps in a cave entrance is straight out of Tomb Raider

AC Black Flag ship battles return, though admittedly not as fleshed out as in AC Black Flag.

Some perks such as Rush Assasination remind me of the Blitz perk in Fallout 4

Stealth mechanics well known from previous AC games

And of course the Spartan Kick from 300

If you care about decision making, choice and consequence, AC Odyssey definatley does not make it obvious which choice is right or wrong. I've tried doing the right thing but ended up screwing everything up lol. I recommend choosing the more aggressive/assertive choices to get better endings.

Also, this game is HUGE. 200hrs of gameplay and finished main quest, cultist questline, but still have not finished all side quests (about 25% of side quest left). Haven't even touched any DLC yet.

If you like single player RPG's such as those above games, you'll enjoy Odyssey.

What is DOOM? DOOM isn't just your ordinary shooter, no, DOOM is a fast-paced, action-packed shooter that is never calm. You will always be on the edge of your seat slashing through demons with the large arsenal of weapons you have. DOOM is for people that want to not only kill and shoot but completely annihilate their enemies. This game is the definition of gore but with the amazing soundtrack, it's impossible not to get pumped and enjoy your time. 

What doom gets right is the way the game is centered around YOU, the player. In other shooter games, you must take cover, plan your movements strategically and quickly shoot down your enemies before they shoot you down. With DOOM it's different, very different. Here you just rush in like a maniac with your preferred weapon of choice and just all out slaughter everything in sight. Cover is for girly girls, you don't need or want cover while playing DOOM. The healing mechanic allows you to focus solely on killing demons without even worrying about your health. If you like going all in like a madman and just destroying everything in front of you this is a game for you.  

There's not much to say about the story or level design. This isn't a game for that. This is a game made to appeal to your primal sense of rage and destruction, which it does perfectly. While the levels are cool and definitely do their best to keep it fresh, most of the time you won't be paying attention to the tiny details. The game also offers a bunch of different enemy types for you to literally slash through each one with its own unique look and attack. In essence, DOOM isn't a deep game, quite the opposite, but this is its strongest point. You just hop on and immediately start enjoying it, no matter if you're a hardcore fan or just a casual playing for an hour on the weekend. The developers did a great job by keeping it simple, yet entertaining for hours. 

Verdict: 8.5/10.If you like shooters and destruction give this game a try, you won't regret it.
