review:
Um dos melhores jogos da Série Total War. O único ponto negativo que deve ser mencionado é a prática abusiva de lançamentos de DLC's que liberam unidades de força exagerada e desbalanceiam o multiplayer em prol do lucro. Tirando isso, o jogo é fantástico: todas as campanhas do modo single player merecem ser jogadas e rejogadas. Já o modo multiplayer vale a pena caso você jogue apenas for fun. Jogar competitivamente não é uma opção, dado o problema mencionado acima.

UPDATE 1 (dois anos depois): Após alguns patches, o jogo começou a apresentar um grave problema que impede a jogabilidade - crashes randômicos que levam direto ao Desktop sem mensagem de erro. Isto acontece a qualquer momento: entre turnos, no carregamento de saves e batalhas, ou mesmo durante uma batalha ou no mapa de campanha, quando selecionando itens para generais ou efetuando ações com agentes. Este problema surpreendentemente não é exclusivo ao Rome II, estando presente também em outros títulos da série, como Empire e Medieval. Uma breve busca por "Crash to Desktop Total War" no google exibirá uma lista infindável de jogadores passando pelo mesmo problema, sem resolução.

NO MOMENTO, NÃO COMPRE O JOGO - ESTÁ INOPERANTE PELA QUANTIDADE DE BUGS E ERROS DE PROGRAMAÇÃO. Caso hajam correções, atualizo novamente.

Update 2 (algumas semanas depois): Algumas correções parecem ter sido feitas, e os crashes diminuíram, especialmente os que ocorriam em meio às batalhas. A campanha principal (romana) também parece protegida. As campanhas secundárias, todavia, seguem com problemas. A de Cartago em especial está cheia de bugs - que podem inclusive ser identificados: são erros de programação vinculados a itens e construções específicas, que quando acionados, crasham o jogo. Parece que alguém andou cagando a programação e metendo ponto ou vírgula onde não deveria.

NO GERAL, O JOGO VOLTOU A SER JOGÁVEL - MAS PREPARE-SE PARA ALGUMAS FRUSTRAÇÕES E SEMPRE SALVE O JOGO. SAVE GAME O TEMPO TODO!

tl;dr: frustratingly challenging but a decent rts. Its an RTS with a fluent economy. You need to balance everything to make it work. And if it's not enough to you make sure your own people do not consume more than you are producing, there is also an AI that tries to kill you. Don't expect easy wins. The singleplayer campaign will drive you nuts. 

The gameplay makes sure you balance your buildings/units so there is balance in there. So you need to have enough resources/economy to exists but it also forces you to expand. But in good pace of offcourse. Go too fast and you will run out of resources due to upkeep. Go too slow and the Ai will keep sending bigger waves of enemies. 

The levels are built in a way, that the challenge is different. Not all maps are about conquest. Later in the game you can even select different factions with their own speciality that fits your style of play. Also the maps can be won in different ways. The main thing about the gameplay: it is hard. So hard that you will actually lose or get to a point that you just want to quit yourself. 

You cannot turtle up too long because you will run out of time, or the waves of AI attacks will get so large it keeps ruining your defense. 

The maps are divided in different areas, each are has different resources you can exploit but in a decent way. Hunting areas allow 1 hunting lodge. The building mechanics of the game does not allow you to actually fully fortify certain chokepoints or go mad on resources. Are area has a limit to the amount of buildings you can place so you need to think what you want to place where. 

Resource economy is a different game in the game. You need people to harvest resources, get too much people you need more food/money/wood etc. Next to workers you need troops which also cost money/food and the amount of soldiers are limited by the buildings you can train them with. So also here, no massive armies to zerg the AI. Also here you need to think what kind of troops you need and how you are going to attack. 

It took me around 25hours to complete the campaign on hard more. (it chooses hard by default, the other options are normal and extreme. No easy mode here :P). The game feels a bit short with only 11 missions, but i think i restarted over 20 times because i got outplayed by the computer. After completing the mission you can see the bonus objectives. ... so you can replay it if you like. I didn't :)

Je le conseille fortement à tous ceux qui ne connaissent pas cette saga extraordinaire puisqu'une fois torché, en à peine 8h en express, vous aurez, comme pour une envie de pisser, le réflexe de courir au plus vite vers le soulagement : Half-Life 2.

Updated Review: 88/100

<rant>

The main reason I'm leaving this review at this moment without too much time spent in-game, is because someone left a review complaining that the game deletes your save file after you die, and how that's a bad mechanic. If you're someone that is complaining about that...I don't know what to tell you. You should have done your research before buying the game, I guess? But to say that it's a bad design decision is just ignorant. It "ruins the game"? It adds STAKES. Which MAKES THE GAME. If you could just wander around without fear of anything bad happening, what would be the drive to go forward? You may be okay with creative mode, but a lot of other players need something pushing them forward, whether it's a good story or the fear of starving to death. And the fact that your save is deleted, again, adds stakes to the game. Which is a conscious and GOOD design decision in a game like this. If you could just save whenever you wanted it would remove those stakes and make the game trivial.

I'm usually not one to say this, but it's getting ridiculous with people complaining about things in games that are CORE design decisions that the game is based and balanced on, saying they have a right to play it so they should cater to them. Accessibility is one thing, for example the Xbox Adaptive Controller is wonderful because it allows people with disabilities to play games. But, they play games the way the designers intended, they just use a different controller. There is a kid that plays FFXIV WITHOUT ARMS. He plays with his feet, and still does kick-ass and his DPS is awesome. If he can play a game, and play it well, without the designers catering to him (without the adaptive controller, mind you, just a regular DS4), then an able-bodied person can play anything. I know the cliché example is Dark Souls, but it's a cliché because it's the best example. There will never be an easy mode in Soulsborne games, and there never should be. It would unquestionably take away from the game. Just like removing the save deletion mechanic from Don't Starve would also take away one of the key components of the game.

Grow up, play more games, observe their design and mechanics, then play this game again and tell me it's bad design.

Oh, and allow comments on your reviews. Don't be a coward.

</rant>

Ever wondered what it would really be like to play the part of a hardened criminal on the verge of insanity, lining your pockets with bills earned from a hard-fought battle with the police?

Sometimes I wonder what that would be like too, so I picked up this title for myself. Unfortunately, it seems like the whole "hardened criminal" thing sort of got dropped by the wayside during Payday 2's development, as I was greeted with a different sight upon booting it up. Instead of a First-Person Shooter, it seems like the camera is more geared for a third-person perspective. Fair enough, I thought, the wider field of view will certainly be useful in a gunfight with the police; but it was then that I noticed I was not piloting a tough-as-nails gunfighter just trying to stick it to the man... I seemed to be in control of a small-waisted white woman with immaculate skin and sparkling blonde hair. Not only that, but it seemed to me like I was riding a horse rather than being on foot, as I had first expected!

That's right, I, like many other people (according to the Steam forums), was hit with the glitch that swaps out your copy of Payday 2 with that of Barbie Horse Adventures 5®... and to tell you the truth, I couldn't be happier! I never realized what a dour mess my life was before this game; I mean, come on! I was fantasizing about shooting at police in a video game for goodness' sake! These are the men and women who protect our streets and would never, ever do anything to breach the trust of American citizens!

I've now played almost 250 hours of Barbie fun-time, and I've had a blast every second I've spent in-game. The lasso mechanic is spot-on, and I especially enjoy the dress-up minigame that takes place in between story segments! At the end of the day, this game is a fun little way to pass the time... Now if you'll excuse me, I've gotta get back to it. Butterscotch isn't gonna recsue herself y'know! Woohoo! Ride 'em cowgirl!

Don't mind my play hour, I only bought the game yesterday, I've heard a lot about this game ever since last three years ago, at first I have no interest about the game mechanic, never played any of the SM Civilization games and have never even tried a turn-based game before. When I first decided to try out this game since I have extra change, having low expectation that it might interest me. I was wrong, I was very, very wrong. 

First, I start as the Native Americans, there happens to be a cool narration right before a game starts, which caught my attention. However, this game didn't work well for me for the first launch, it crashed right before I can even command my worker to do anything, there was no crash report or error messages, I was quite pissed and was going to refund it but then I rebooted my computer and gave it another chance.

The second time I played as the Germans, let me state a thing about this game, if you are not used to a slow-paced game like me, please keep playing until the Medieval Era (at least), because in the very beginning there is not much to do except a lot of researching and building and building and then exploring, however this game keeps you interested in every way by giving random global notifications or messages from every different civilization around the map, not to mention barbarian camps that spawns brutes every 4-5 turns to invade your city, that you'll have to destroy their camp if you want to stop them.

I discovered and met Warsaw first as the German civilization, which was quite ironic, and I have already thought about declaring a war against them just to see what happens (lol). There is so much to do after you have expanded your civilization into 2-3 cities, you can either connect the roads to other cities to earn more gold, or build tons of trading post. Then I met China and apparently they are not very friendly with me, because I settled one of my city near their borders, I trained many different types of troops and surrounding that specific area for the lulz and they started getting really pissed, then she declared a war. Another thing that I find very interesting is the combat system, it's not like most strategy game that when you attack a bigger type of army than you will lead to dealing almost no damage at all, I built a catapult thinking it is indestructable, just because I think it's big sized, but then I got rekt by infantry units in a few turns, there are many ways to counter your enemies by training your troops which is specialized in dealing with a certain type of an army. It also shows chances that how likely you're going to loose the battle and predicted approx. how many will get rekt after the battle.

Well in conclusion, I played for the whole night, and it was a really bad idea, from 12am to 5am and when every turn is over, you just can't stop playing, I would recommend this game to all people who is looking for strategy games, it might not look like a strategy game from the pictures but go and give it a try, it'll be the best decision you'll ever make.

GTA V oferuje przyjemny tryb dla jednego gracza który oczywiście ma swoje minusy np.
parę nudnych misji. Fabuła jest ok, nie jest super ciekawa, chociaż nie jest też super nudna. Zakończenie jest dość słabe w moim odczuciu (niektóre z nich niestety blokują też przejście gry na 100%). Misję z paroma wyjątkami są mega przyjemne, niestety po zrobieniu ich wszystkich wieje trochę nudą. Sam singleplayer 7.5/10. Skąd więc nie polecam tej gry? Ponieważ mamy 2020 rok i w większości przypadków jest ona kupowana ze względu na tryb online. I co jest z tym trybem nie tak? WIELE. GTA online nie przypomina tak naprawdę GTA a bardziej saint’s row. Początkujący gracz jest bezsilny w porównaniu do latających mioteł które strzelają rakietami. Sesje nawiedzają tony grieferów i hackerów pragnących zepsuć ci dzień. Zarabianie na początku to jeden wielki żart więc będziesz zapierdalał za najniższą krajową by zarobić na mieszkanie czy inną posiadłość pozwalającą zarobić więcej pieniędzy.
Nie chcesz by ktoś rozwalił twój ładunek więc będziesz używał glitchy na wyczyszczenie sesji. Apropos błędów to jest ich ogrom od takich które sprawiają zablokowanie postaci w miejscu gdzie jedynym wyjściem jest restart gry do takich który usuwają dorobek graczy.
Warto też wspomnieć o długawych loadingach (ok. 10 min), toksycznej społeczności i masie paywalli. Więc czy GTAO ma jakieś plusy? Fun grania z przyjaciółmi (chociaż też nie zawsze) Jeżeli masz zamiar kupić GTA V ze względu na tryb online a jesteś bardziej solo typem gracza to stanowczo odradzam.

[h1][b] Subnautica, une aventure subjugante[/b][/h1]

Je précise que je n'ai joué à l'heure actuelle qu'au mode histoire (survie), et pas en VR.
Pour ceux qui ont la flemme de lire mon test: subnautica n'est pas fait pour vous. Il faudra lire. Et pas qu'un peu !

Subnautica est un énorme coup de coeur.  A tout les amateurs de jeu d'aventure/survie avec un vrai lore (et pas juste : accident>>> débrouilles toi !) Vous pouvez le prendre les yeux fermés.

Les 4-5 premières heures sont plutôt laborieuses. Mais l'intrigue, le level design, l'univers et l'ambiance sonore font que ce jeu nous prend aux tripes. Il n'est pas rare de lancer des "WAOUH c'est quoi ?" et - quelques minutes après - provoquer une peur panique dans une grotte sombre. Jouissif.

Voici les points positifs mais aussi négatifs:

[h1] Les points positifs[/h1]
[list]
[*]L'ambiance
[*] gameplay bien pensé (et intuitif)
[*]L'univers
[*] graphisme et level design
[/list]

[h1] Les points négatifs (ou plutot à améliorer/rajouter)[/h1]
[list]
[*] carte non aléatoire (rejouabilité moindre)
[*] pas de coop (la carte aléatoire sera nécessaire)
[*] pas de système de convoyeur: si vous êtes plutot sédentaire ( 1 grosse base), rameneer tout votre minage armoire par armoire est long voir fastidieux. (on devrait pouvoir assigner des stockages à des minerais et quand on connecte un véhicule à notre station/base ils s'acheminent automatiquement vers lesdits rangements).
[*] survie vraiment facile: je suis loin d'être bon à ce genre de jeu mais je n'ai jamais rencontré de problème.
[*] le clipping (apparition d'objet) est omniprésent. (peu être distance d'affichage trop courte.)
[/list]

A regarder comme ça, on pourrait croire que je ne recommande pas le jeu mais c'est tout l'inverse !
On se sent tellement impliqé que l'on se laisse prendre dans la magie du paysage et de l'ambiance. Le gameplay corrobore tout ça avec finesse, intuitivité et quelques bonnes idées (ou idées reprises) que je vous laisserai découvrir par vous même.

The art-style and combat systems are very reminescent of old-school RPGs, especially from the Mother series. However, this game puts many fun twists on the expected RPG norm. For example, the player has the choice to end conflicts peacefully without killing his/her foes. In addition, dodging enemy attacks occurs in a top-down, bullet-dodger style. 

What makes this game most memorable, however, are the amazing story and the great characteres. These characters will keep you coming back to replay the game over and over again, which may yield differing stories. Lastly, I have to commend this game on its music. The songs are orchestrated wonderfully and always fit the mood of whatever you are doing, with a special mention to every single boss theme. 

This is a game I definitely recommend trying

Assassin's Creed: Odyssey is a truly massive game, befitting of the name 'Odyssey.' I have played several other Assassin's Creed games, but none of them have grabbed me in the same way that Odyssey did. I didn't want to play anything else for weeks after it was released, and I still don't. Unfortunately, having completed all the branches of the main quest and all the side quests I could find, I am left waiting for the DLC to follow, as well as some light achievement hunting and resource hoarding. But I still itch to get into the world, to explore the last few question marks on my map and to finish out all the locations, and to sail the waters, wreaking havoc on pirates (and, honestly, any ships with shiny epic sails and a chance of good loot!).

For me, this game was different from all the other Assassin's Creed titles. Some part of this was due to the newly-added roleplaying elements. Although not extensive -- the "branching dialogue" is inconsequential in many of the scenarios, so in some sense it's an illusion of choice -- they do give one a feeling of control and ownership of the story. I felt very invested in the story of Kassandra. No spoilers here, but I can say that I enjoyed the twists and turns of the story. There is still the perennial Assassin's Creed problem -- the shoehorning of historical figures into important narrative roles isn't any more charming here than it ever is, but it did help to provide a framework for the overarching story. 

The gameplay was phenomenal, with fluid and cinematic combat (on foot, at sea, and in conquest battles). I've read that a lot of people mentioned falling behind in levels, necessitating a kind of 'grind' to get to a level that allowed progression of one of the quest branches. I didn't have this problem until very late in the main story, but even then I didn't feel like I was being deprived of continuing with the story. There was so much to do in terms of different story arcs, side quests, bounties, exploration, etc. that it was just a matter of doing something else fun. Oftentimes I forgot about going back to what I needed leveling up for, becuase I was having too much fun sacking forts, sinking pirates, finding treasure, assassinating leaders, etc. to want to rush back to the story quest. It probably helps that I was obsessed in early stages with completing everything from an area before I moved on, so I was usually a few levels ahead. Your mileage may vary.

Over all this game is stunning if they make more like this they will not have to worry about anything in the future. This is the game that I have been waiting for, for a long time I have to play on weekend b/c if I play during the week I will not get anything done.

Hey there everyone. I've had many years of experience in all genres of games & gaming in general. So I figured I'll try to write the best, most accurate review I can without using the 'useless' details. I hope you guys enjoy. :)

So to start things off. A Realm Reborn is NOT a "different" Final Fantasy from the original XIV, but at the same time it is. Final Fantasy XIV was a very unsuccesful game. So it was redesigned by a new team from the ground up and A Realm Reborn was released. ALSO THERE IS AN ACTUAL STORY TO THE GAME FOR ALL YOU STORY BASED PEOPLE! :D

-------Graphics-------
The game is stunningly beautiful for graphics. Modern laptops / PC's should not have massive framerate issues at all unless you're in 2 of the 3 main cities & it's heavily crowded in them. Depending on your settings, you will notice downgrades (of course) within the water, and the shadows. They even went as far as to lessen the amount of animation in character movements. What stinks is that the PS3 cannot control these options so the game is a bit choppier on that system. I'm not entirely sure about the PS4 as I don't have one. I would imagine it's more of a modern - high end PC power. The dungeons look stunning as do the creatures & bosses. I did the first dungeon called Sastasha, and my whole group stopped just before the last boss because we were too "wow'd" by the fact there was a sunset over the horizon of the cave. It looked absolutely gorgeous.


-------Audio-------
As far as sound goes, the game will sometimes glitch with what sound(s) it produces. Randomly at times in combat you'll just stop hearing your characters skills / spells. However, with that said, the music is very nice to listen to. I'm not saying it doesn't get repetitive after mannnnnnnnnny game hours and eventually you'll use your own. But remember, this is a Final Fantasy game. They want their music to at least be somewhat tasteful. I'm not entirely sure why they did this either, but when you're on a mount, if you aren't moving the music for the mount softens. Upon moving again it kicks back up. This is a bummer because I'd like to just sit there and listen to the chocobo theme for hours. :D
All in all though you can tell they took their time and didn't just throw slop together knowing MMO'ers use their own music anyways eventually.

-------Characters & Character Customizing------- 
The characters look amazing to say the least. You have 5 races to choose from, both male & female unlike Final Fantasy XI which Miqo'te (female) and Rogeadyn (male) were gender restricted. Boring Humans (Hyur), Freakishly Tall Elves (Elezen), Little Cute People(Lalafell), No-Claw-Having Cat People (Miqo'te), and Chris Redfield's / She-Hulk's (Roegadyn). Within those races you first choose the gender, then you choose 1 of 2 options for a clan / tribe. These can have some differences, to many. Mostly being stat wise. One clan/tribe has melee/ranged based stats while the other has caster based. Then you go on to customize the look of your character. This ranges anywhere from the height and voice & changing the color of your hair / eyes, to the breast size on females & muscle tone on males. While there is A LOT to offer when it comes to customizing, there are some downsides. There are only 4-6 different base faces which may seem like enough but when you see the options you'll soon find yourself leaning toward the same one every time. While there are quite a few hairstyles / facial hair options, you'll soon take notice that they could have added in a lot more. Such as adding length for facial hair for guys, and more actual styles of hair for girls with a sub option of hair band colors and not 3-4 of the same hairstyles all just with a different color hair band. Some can have earrings which is actually a downer because it interferes & overlaps with earring based gear (yes earrings do show up when you equip them). 

-------Gear & Loot-------
Since gear was mentioned in the previous paragraph I figured it was fitting to put it next. Now don't get me wrong, I like the look of the gear in ARR. But if you've played games like World of Warcraft you'll be disappointed in the way this game is done. Most loot is earned simply by completeing quests & dungeons. You will NOT find an upgradable piece of gear on a creature. Remember, this is Final Fantasy. You find them via dungeon treasure boxes & raids. Also there is not a buttload of gear. They do have a wide selection of things because of how many classes / jobs there are but you'll not see outfits that you go, "Hmm, I wonder where they got that." The weapons don't look all that flashy until higher levels / endgame. But they still graphically look very well done. EVERYTHING EXCEPT YOUR BELT shows up on your character. They just introduced the new Glamour system which lets you change the physical look of your gear without altering the stats (Transmogging for you WoW readers). The loot table goes as follow;

White (Common) - Pretty useless stuff, but if it's better, wear it.

Pink (Aetherial) - Better or worse than greens as the actual stats on them can differ. So in short, they aren't fixed stats and are not tradable.

Green (Uncommon) - These are pretty much your dungeon leveling pieces of gear.

Blue (Rare) & Purple (Epic) - Towards your end game you'll get these. Of course these have better / best stats.


-------Classes & Jobs-------
Very basic description. Will list the classes / jobs beneath. You start out as a class, and at 15 once you've completed the required quests you'll be able to change into a different class at any point in time by visiting that class specific guild and joining them. Or choose to go further within the first class of choice to learn a job. A Job is an advancement in the class you already are. For example, Conjurer (healer) into White Mage (advanced healer). You need 30 in Conjurer, and 15 in Arcanist to advance to a White Mage. The game is typical in terms of tanks, heals, and dps'ers. It shows you that as well. You can be any & all classes / jobs in the game as long as you meet the requirements and you can change at any time. All you have to do is equip the proper weapon to change to that class or job. One thing I probably should mention as well. There IS crafting in the game. They're also classes. They're known as Disciples of the Hand. 
Here are the Classes & Jobs that go hand in hand with each other;

Disciple of War (Melee & Ranged):
Class: Gladiator (Melee Tank) - Job: Paladin 
Class: Marauder (Melee Tank) - Job: Warrior 
Class: Pugilist (Melee DPS) - Job: Monk
Class: Lancer (Melee DPS) - Job: Dragoon 
Class: Archer (Ranged DPS) - Job: Bard 

Disciple of Magic (Caster):
Class: Thaumaturge (Caster DPS) - Job: Black Mage
Class: Conjurer (Healer) - Job: White Mage
Class: Arcanist (Caster DPS W/Pet) - Job(s): Summoner (DPS) & Scholar (Healer) 

Disciple of the Hand (Crafting): ~NOTICE~ You ALSO level these up as a regular class. Unique. :)
Class: Alchemist
Class: Armorer
Class: Blacksmith
Class: Carpenter
Class: Culinarian
Class: Goldsmith
Class: Leatherworker
Class: Weaver




So that about sums up my most important / basic review. Sorry for thy length. This game does have A LOT to offer. I encourage anyone who's a fan of MMORPG's to give this a try. If you'd like to know anything else about the game, feel free to just ask me or look up what other reviewers have said. Take it from someone that's played a ton of World of Warcraft. This game is unique in a fun way and actually shows you so. I have a blast playing it and hopefully see more of you guys on it. ^-^

I'll be honest; this is probably my favorite game EVER. It's my go to game when I'm bored, and it's the reason I even joined steam in the first place; because this game is so cheap when it's on sale. It's amazing, the gameplay is great for the price (even when not on sale!) and I have sunk SO many hours. (It only looks small, because most of my gameplay time on this game is spent offline; and therefore not recorded)

People have been complaining of the bugs that this game brings; and they kinda have a point, because this game is very broken, UNMODDED. This game has a very active modding community, and they have almost patched in all of the holes that EA left in on release. It's honestly amazing, and if you have any problem, you can always go to the VERY active community for help.

Let's not even talk about the custom content scene. (similar to the modding scene, but it's for custom content like hairs, clothing, etc) I have spent LITERAL HOURS just fretting which texture to use, which default eyes looks better, mindlessly clicking "Download this" on any Sims CC website available. 

And the core of the gameplay. GODDAMN IT'S SO GOOD. There are those small, tiny, details, like the outcome of an opportunity that you forgot to fulfill, or the scary music when a burglar comes in, that make this game as awesome as it is, and also why many people are still playing this game, because the sequel to this game, The Sims 4, is VERY lacking in these EXACT details. 

People complain about the DLC a lot, but TBH it still has more content for the price than something like The Sims 4. (Can you notice I REALLY hate the sequel?!?!) Anyways, this game is worth playing, for any purpose you want: 3 hour fun with a weird looking green dude that woohooes everyone? 80 hour fun with a perfect white-picket fence family? Your choice!

Please buy this game, to show EA that they're doing the sequel wrong, and that they already did all of this right, if only they would fix all of the holes that they left on launch. What if they do fix it? Ah, a simmer can dream. :)

Оглядываясь на предыдущие две части, игре можно дать 6.5 из 10 за однотипный игровой процесс. Не рекомендую.

[u] synopsis [/u]
you play as rico rodriguez, a man working for a spy agency. in previous games, you have been sent to different places to take down evil dictators and crumple criminals. but now, you go back to your birth place of medici: a beautiful tropical island. there you meet with some old friends from before you left. you find the rebellion: a group of people working to overcome the evil dictator General Di Ravello. Di Ravello has taken over medici and see's global domination as his ultimate goal. In jc3, you must crumple Di Ravello's forces and tear down his empire. take back Medici and return it to the paradise it was before.

[u] on release [/u]
this game was not finished. well, sort of. it was poorly optimised for amd GPU's, a problem which avalanche should have adressed earlier. there would be problems like performance issues and (for me especially) the world would not load. there would be huge chunks missings out of the landscaspe. big, triangular holes in the ground which only appeared when going near to it. view my screenshots for a cheeky look at what im on about

[u] now [/u]
after about 3 weeks of being out, amd released a new graphics driver which fixed all the problems, there was no glitches or missing landscape, it was finally what it was designed to be: a beautiful landscape.

[u] pro's [/u]
+HUGE open world to explore
this world is 1000km squared in total (400 miles) which makes it bigger than gta V and even the witcher 3.

+colourful, beautiful landscape, sky and water (no 4k grass blades volvo plz fix)
the landscape is so vibrant and alive, the colours are bright and sharp

+even more destruction than last time
let's be honest, jc2 was not really that destructible. you could take down water tanks and whatnot but they all fell the same way. it was kinda repetitive. but on jc3, there is an all knew physics engine which makes it AWESOME. each destructible object is built up of many different smaller objects.if you crash a plane, it will fall apart and all the pieces won't sit there and disappear after 5 seconds, they will be proper physics objects that you can move around and tether to other things. when you bomb a radio tower, it will start to slowly tumble in any direction, every little bit, every little piece of metallic doom will fall apart when it hits the ground and the whole thing will result in another explosion. there are a lot of things you can blow up this time. walls, guard towers, giant masts, sunflowers, bus stops and A LOT more.

+the grapple hook
in jc2, it was not that good. you could take yourself over to another place with it or pull an enemy back a little but that was it. this one is new and improved. for one, it is stronger so if you attatch someone to a building they won't fall back down again after 4 seconds. there are up to six tethers (grapple attatchments) this time so you can attatch multiple things to multiple other things. you can make a conga line of civillians on the back of your car or under your helicopter. you can steal a plane by attatching it under your helicopter and flying off. you can steal people. it's glorious. my favourite grapple feature (of course) is the retract feature. when you have a tether, this tightens the it, forcing it to get smaller, forcing the two things on either end to come together. you can do amazing things with this. human catapults, crucifixions..... wait what? yeah, this does lead to very evil intentions. stretching an npc's limbs until he dies (luckily theres not dismemberment). with the retract feature, you can down structures and make them fall on people. also touching down on the destruction and physics category, you can pull down guard towers and, as said before, they are made up of pieces of metal so it will just completely fall into a pile of rubbish (before exploding). and also, if you grapple an npc or animal, you go flying towards them and drop kick them ("you can drop kick a cow GOTY 2025")

+wingsuit
this is new with jc3 and is a very nice feature indeed. yes, it is hard at first but once you use it for a while, you will get used to it and become some kind of epic global elite ninja (VOLVO PLZ NERF). if mastered, you can go very fast with this thing and makes travelling very nice and easy (EZ PZ). vehicles are so overrated.

+mario
this guy is pure banter

+unlimited c4
you don't have to worry about how many bomb you have (apart from grenades) because c4 is unlimited now! you start off being able to plant up to 3 bombs at a time but can go up to 5 (i think). once exploded, you can just plant another set BOOM........ done (pardon the pun)

+jc3 mp coming soon
that's right, they're back. the beasts who made jc2 multiplayer are working on it now and i reckon it won't be long. imagine being on a bridge when suddenly, it starts to fall down, and you die. i played jc2 mp for about 25 hours and i loved it. you could hundreds of players in one server which was amazing but there were no npc's. imagine there being npc's in jc3 mp and everyone using their tether to make the BIGGEST conga line ever to have existed.

+new liberation
in jc2, it was annoying to take over places but now, theres all new task to take over places like killing the base general, disabling the security or missile system etc. although towns are kinda all the same (more below), the army bases are all unique in design and are fun to destroy.

+challenges
there are various challenges whether it's driving, shooting, wingsuiting or flying a plane. most of them are just time trials where you go through checkpoints but other are where you must destroy as much as possible or whatever. they are quite fun to do. by doing challenges, you get gears. the better you do, the more you get (up to 5 available in a challenge). these gars unlock 'gear mods' which are modifications to things like cars, planes, boats, explosives, guns, wingsuit, grapple hook. modifications are little things like more grapple tethers, upping the max c4 in one plant, having nitro on vehicles, wider blast radius on grenades etc.

[u] con's [/u]

-some boring missions
a few of the missions kind of drag on a little bit. just the same old 'ride on a car and take out enemy's following'. you know the drill.

-repetitive takeovers
liberating a base or town gets repetitive because most of the time, it's just the same thing. blow up some statues, destroy a gas tank and whatever. of course, some places will have different things like not every town will have a gas station and now every town will have a statue but its all the same really. it is fun to blow up stuff thought as (as i said earlier), the physics make all explosions unpredictable. 

[u] all in all [/u]
all in all, i recommend this game to anyone who likes destruction, open worlds and unpredictable, random and funny physics. it's a good investment and will keep you entertained for hours on end. do not get if you have a low end pc or potato. i have a mid-range pc (specs on profile) that can run at the lowest settings (stupid websites said high). so of course, do not pre-order games and don't believe sites like can you run it. the hype overcame me and forced me to pre-order so take it from personal experience: don't do it.

Мой друг, пока я играл, подошёл к экрану и спросил -  "что за уродскую дичь ты гоняешь"? 
Но это не уродская дичь, и вот почему:
В игре ясный, четкий и понятный геймплей, основанный на большом наборе простых механик и от их комбинаций получающий нужную глубину. С точки зрения стратегии, радует система выбора способностей и их реализаций в зависимости от позиции в битве и сопряженная с ней механика перемещений. Генератор подземелий простой но крайне действенный и эффективный. 
Ну а самое главное - принцип, заложенный в игру - no pain, no gain. Если ты хочешь что-то получить, нужно что-то  отдать. Хочешь получить бонус - получай негативный эффект в другом аспекте. Хочешь найти награду в мусоре - будь готов наткнуться на болезнь, которая там обитает или получить дополнительный стресс. Регулярное получение болезней, срывов, ран и вредных привычек, вкупе с неожиданными временными исчезновениями персонажей должны свести с ума любителей легких прогулок и перфекционистов  Для многих, кому хочется просто отдохнуть перед экраном, эта игра не подходит, т.к. она постоянно изматывает выбором. Заставляет не просто рисковать, а порой целенаправленно жертвовать чем-то (а скорее кем-то). Из этих мучений и страданий и рождается победа с чувством облегчения. Игра постоянно ставит игрока в неудобное положение, располагая его между собственной жадностью приобретения и жадностью потерять накопленное. При этом это всё чрезвычайно увлекательно, так как наград всегда потенциально много.

Только этого достаточно, чтобы сказать, что как игра, durkest dungeon удалась. Но всё это подкреплено тем, что делает её не просто хорошей или отличной игрой, а игрой культовой. Это визуальный ряд, конкретно точность образов, которые подобраны под эту гнетущую атмосферу. Готика с элементами произведений лавкрафта воплощена с помощью мрачной цветовой палитры. Самым положительным эпитетом, которым можно наградить визуализацию персонажей данной игры - это угрюмый и суровый, т.к. в остальном это что-то отталкивающее, мерзкое и неприятное, что идеально подходит по сеттинг. 

Музыкальные мотивы города также наполнены беспробудной тяжестью и унынием, что однако не мешает её быть приятной а слух. Ну а в локациях, музыка хорошо передаёт ту атмосферу, что присутствует на экране, будь то пещера бухты или заброшенный заповедник. К слову декорации также достойны похвал, хотя на них очень редко отвлекаешься. Помимо музыки, не возможно не отметить голос рассказчика, который внедряется в твою голову и как бы за тебя описывает происходящее на экране. Особенную живость дают постоянные реплики персонажей, в зависимости от ситуации и контекста. В своё время именно это сделало dragon age origins такой уютной. Тут также появляется ощущение, что это не просто кукольные болванчики, а кто-то более живой.

This game has managed to hit the spot I've been looking for in a game for a long time. It has the historic events that really make the game feel very deep and complete (even if at times I wish it was even more so). The incremental advances and constant need to just get a little edge here or there over your opponents and rivals really pushes that "just one more" feeling to the max for me. 

Sure, the game is intimidating at first, but if you want a complete strategy game, what do you expect? After a couple rough starts (~30 hours of "Ok, remember that for next time" mistakes), I started to figure out the basics. The manual is decent, but one really needs to read the guides written by the wonderful steam community. They help a lot in understanding this expansive game. 

I am admittedly only beginning to feel like I have a handle on the game, and still I want keep playing because I know there is so much more to learn. The trade system: who the heck knows how that works, but I'm gonna figure it out. The battle mechanics are complex, but not beyond understanding. The diplomacy is probably the best part of the game, but I still struggle to understand how to consistently do well in the political sphere. This probably all sounds like bad things, but I promise it's good. If you like to really dive into a game, like I do, you'll love this. It's something you can chat with other players with and really appreciate amount of effort in the accomplishment of "I made Spain as Portugal and colonized Siberia" or "I held off the Europeans until 1750 as the Chickshaw." That's the beauty of the sandbox and of this game.

Eksilerini sayayım;

-Uçaklar, botlar, helikopterler hava alanlarında kolayca bulunabiliyor. Yani 1 milyona bi uçak almak çok mantıklı değil, kişiselleştirilebilseydi uçaklar, botlar, helikoterler mantıklı olurdu ama o da yok. Sonuçta koca bir eksiklik diyemesem de bu kısmı biraz eksik kalmış oyunun.

-Arkadaşlarınız yoksa bazen boş boş dolanıyor hissi verebiliyor, ama arkadaşlarınız varsa her türlü saçmalığı yapıyorsunuz çok eğlenceli oluyor :D

-Hileciler baya var, oyunda millete para dağıtıyolar. Şöyle diyeyim 15 dk lik bi görevden en fazla 20 bin dolar kazanabilirken bu adamlar 2 saniye içinde istedikleri yerde 20-30 para çuvalı spawnlıyorlar ve her çuval 40 bin dolar. Ben istemeden aldım bu paralardan (adamlar sizin çevrenizde spawnlıyabiliyorlar) ve oyun zevkimin içine etti. Eğer benim gibi düşünen biriyseniz, hileli paralarla aldığınız arabalar, uçaklar size aidiyet hissi vermiyor. Kendi paramla zaman içinde alıp modifiye ettiğim arabalara binerken büyük zevk alıyorum ama bu arabalara binince çok boş geliyor insana. Ama yine de hilecilerden kaçınabilirsiniz.

Neyse sözün özü ben şu ana kadar 250 saate yakın oynadım bu oyun insana kendini 700-800 saat oynattırır diyorum kitabına göre oynarsanız (hilesiz vs.), daha yeni ücretsiz update geldi. Adamlar 2-3 aya bir update getiriyorlarmış ve bedava hepsi bu da bir artı, dlc olayı yok.

孩子，不知道在这个时候，在这个泥泞的雨天里，你是否还记得。
今天是你的生日，我将要送你一份礼物。
在这颗行星周而复始的运动中，在漫长而繁琐的重复日历中，我不断期盼着你的生日的到来。我还记得过去给你准备的那些礼物。每年你的生日，都是我生活中为数不多的光点。
人生中有很多不期而遇的事情，比如我和你母亲的相识。那是在东欧大迁徙的路途中，我从波兰进入苏联时。
自从“大崩溃”之后，东欧平原就热闹了起来。我从德国出发，以游客身份乘火车到达波兰，再经由一位在华沙的联系人，坐汽车到达边境线不远处的一个村庄。
村子里就像当年的盟军部队一样，汇集着诺曼人、盎格鲁-撒克逊人、本地的斯拉夫人，甚至还有来自遥远东方转道而来的朝鲜人。人们坐车，骑马，甚至还有背着远足包从遥远的地方徒步来到这里。我看着这一张张满是疲惫的脸，发现在疲惫之下，是一种兴奋和憧憬。
我不由得想，在我的脸上，是否也有着这样一副表情。
联系人叮嘱我，到了村子，不要和人讲话，安静的呆着，等着第二天，会有人来把我接走，并告诉我接下来该怎么办。
独自等待命运是一件令人反感的事情，但对我而言不是，我曾经经历过这种时刻，坐上运兵卡车向西线征发的时候、在法国境内随着部队转移的时候、走出地堡向盟军投降的时候，我都曾感觉命运的丝线搅作一团，含混不清的指向未来的某个终点，我试图去看清在那些终点处自己的命运，却只能看见一团迷雾。
在村子中唯一的酒吧吃过晚饭后，我去往村边散步。村外是一片并不茂盛的树林，树冠的尖顶直指苍穹，黑漆漆的掩映着天空中为数不多的星星。出于一种难以描述的冲动，我决定去树林里走走。
我步履缓慢，远离村庄。
回头望去，这个庇护所一般的村庄，渐渐变成建筑和光点的混合物，人的生气渐渐弱了下去，只剩下波罗的海吹来的季风，轻声在我耳边诉说。
正在我享受这种独处的安静，放松心中因未来而产生的焦虑时，我远远地看见一个人影，从那片树林之中慢慢显现。她似乎也看见了我，慢慢地和我相对走来。
一边是村庄，一边是森林，头上是亘古不变的微弱星光。我和你的母亲就这样在一个夜里相遇了。
她走到我面前，停下了，对我点头示意。男性的审美，从中世纪到现在，都在不断的变化着，女性的美丽从曾经的雍容华贵变成了如今的简洁干练。在那个时间点，我的眼里，向我迎面走来的这个女人是美的，记忆这东西作风诡异，我无法记起那天她的穿着，甚至不能透过时光大海去还原她那时候的样貌，但她那时的美，足以撬动我紧闭的双唇。
我不顾联系人“别和陌生人说话”的叮嘱，用德语说了一句：“你好。”
她偏了一下头，表情有些犹豫和苦恼，一字一顿地用英语说着：“你会讲英语吗？”
我只会一些简单的英语，那是在西线作战的时候，帝国卫队的上尉教我的，不过都是一些劝降的语言。
“我的英语……不好。”我艰难地组织着语言。突然我灵机一动：“那不如我们用俄语交谈吧。”
人人都会讲俄语，至少来到边境的人们都会。
她笑了：“愿你在熔炉中得到锤炼，同志。”
“愿你在熔炉中得到锤炼。你是才从那片树林里过来吗？”
“是的，听你讲话，你是来自……“
“德国。”
她语气生硬了一下：“我是英国人。“
我理解她这种生硬，在二战中，德国和英国在西线展开了旷日持久的拉锯战。其惨烈程度已经不是“屠场“或者”绞肉机“这种词语能够描述得了得了。相信我，孩子，你所见过的所有冲突和战争加在一起，也比不上我当年在西线作战时每天看到的情景惨烈。
不过那场前无古人的世界大战已经结束了，德国战败了，人们和书本都已接受了这个事实。只是脑海中还残留着战争时期，本能似的，对敌国的憎恨。
就这样，苏珊，一位来自英国的战地护士，认识了我，一个曾经敌对国家的军人。
第二天，我和她乘同一班车，离开了那个村庄。
在联系人——就是偷渡头目——的帮助下，我们倾尽家财，到了苏联境内。
说是散尽家财，其实也只是在“大崩溃”带来的金融海啸吞没一切之前，将所有在未来一文不值的东西，换成了一艘逃离的舢板，去往这个世界上仍有希望的国家——苏联。
苏珊放弃了在英国一所医院的工作，变卖家产，在黑市上兑换卢布，加入了百万苏联偷渡客的队伍。
在去向苏联的车上，我曾经问过她是否有过不舍。
“我卖掉我爷爷的那块怀表时，是在离家不远处的一个街角。黑市贩子出现在我面前，伸手要过怀表查看了起来。我说这是战前的产品，瑞士货，做工优良，只要一百卢布就可以出手。黑市贩子摇摇头，说他只会出三十卢布，如果我不愿意，他会考虑直接下手抢。“苏珊如此说：”你根本不知道大崩溃之后短短的几年内，政府变得是如此的虚弱无力，对国家的控制变得空前松散，混乱在各处滋生，无政府主义者走上街头，遵纪守法的好人被受欺侮，而奸猾残忍的小人日益得势。我受够了，这是文明的倒退，这样的世界使人变得像动物。无论如何，我也要去苏联，因为那是世界上唯一还有秩序的地方。“
我当然知道，在德国，这些事情也一样地发生着。
自从冷战以苏联的全面胜利结束以后，整个资本主义阵营的经济都在与苏联的贸易战争中崩溃了。
书本上称之为“大崩溃“。大量人口失业，实业萎缩，资金流动减少，国家信用崩盘，货币贬值，物价飞涨，政府大量裁减公共开支，到后来，甚至连维护基本的警察和军队都显得困难。人们都在经历了工业时代的辉煌后有些惊讶，为什么我们的文明会如此脆弱，一场金融危机，就毁掉了大半个世界的经济体系。
我也在路上遇到过强盗，或者不按照规矩办事、半买半抢的商人，不过对方往往囿于我的军官身份，在巧取豪夺时有所收敛。
再后来，我们到了苏联后不久，在顿涅茨克城郊的一座东正教堂里，苏珊成了你的母亲。
婚礼很简陋，没有亲朋见证，教堂里只有我工厂班组的几个工友和我们的几户邻居。
干瘦的神父用不饱满的声音询问着我们是否愿意在未来的一生中，忠诚地陪伴着对方。
我在心中感谢上帝，在这个濒临崩溃的世界中，仍赐我一个家作为避风港。
你的母亲微微低头抹了一下眼泪，说“我愿意。”
我没想到，她会那么快就失约。
命运在我眼中是一个大毛线球，纷繁复杂，却也有着他的规则，我原以为你的母亲会是另一根和我混在一起的漫长线条，却没想到，那只是我的毛线球上一个小小的疙瘩。
在你出生那一天，她死于出血。
我不曾在你面前提起过这件事，但在今天我希望你能明白，你的生命，是你母亲给你的最好的礼物。
在这颗行星周而复始的运动中，在漫长而繁琐的重复日历中，我不断期盼着，你的生日的到来。每年的这一天，是我生活中为数不多的光点。这个日子对我来说如此重要，是你母亲和你支撑着我，让我每天在乌拉尔农机厂从事着毫无快乐与荣耀可言的繁重劳动——那些机械重复的劳动使我的手臂和后腰酸痛不堪。
我想把这个家支撑下去，这是我对你母亲的承诺，是我们在那座教堂中，用俄语认真许下的誓言。即使在困难的生活中，我仍然坚持每年为你准备礼物，从“超级伊万“人偶到篮球、乒乓球拍、国际象棋，虽然都是放在过去不值一提的东西，但我想这些物件能为你带来一丝不同于平日的惊喜，为这个家增添一些欢笑和希望。
这种努力慢慢有了成效，我也很高兴看到你一天天走出了没有母亲的阴霾。
你小时候问我，为什么别人都有妈妈而你没有的时候，我心碎得不知道怎么回答。只能一次次搪塞着说，你的母亲和我分开了，去了很远的地方，过着她自己的生活。
孩子，事实的真相就像这个世界一样，残忍得让人难以直面。

在你一天天长大的时候，无情的混乱，也从苏联的边境之外渗透进来，腐蚀着这个秩序的国度。苏联之外的世界变得越来越糟，国家分裂成各种自治领，时间好像退回了黑暗的中世纪。
苏联国内也对外界变化产生了应激反应，不过却是用一个极端来反对另一个极端。你看那些街上游行的少年们，那些打着“乌克兰少年团“旗帜的孩子们，他们狂热、争先恐后地效忠着伟大的苏维埃，想要为之献出一切。
出于对无序的恐惧，他们成为了秩序的奴仆。他们全心全意地融入并侍奉着集体，令我想起，小时候在法兰克福乡下念书的时候，老师布置给我们的暑期作业——观察蚂蚁，工蚁们无休地为蚁群搜集物资，不知疲倦，不问原因。
幸好你远离了这些孩子，当你瞪大眼睛，奇怪的问我，他们为什么会如此激动之时，我感到欣慰，你仍有着自己思考的习惯，而不是单纯的去跟随报纸、广播和礼堂集会中狂热的人群。
不知道在我离开的这些日子里，你过得怎么样。
彼得中尉向我承诺过，在我参加绝地求生之后，无论结果如何，我的配给，仍会按时按期发放到你的手中，你会有充足的食物、饮水、衣物、日用品，足以维持日常生活。
我曾以为彼得中尉就是一个典型的，融入了集体之中，把自己转变为一只工蚁的人。
那天我下班之后，在家门口的楼道里，遇到了彼得中尉。和他同行的，还有两个瘦高的穿警察制服的年轻人，这俩年轻人比你大不了多少，不过二十出头，但他们眼神空洞，只是平视前方，让人怀疑他们的瞳孔根本没有对焦在楼道的墙壁上。
中尉用一副公事公办的语气问我：“同志，自我介绍一下，我叫彼得，彼得中尉。请问你是叶甫盖尼•别尔谢廖夫吗？”
“是的长官。”
“可我听说你还有一个别的名字，是吗？克劳斯•施耐德？“
“我想你们找错了人，长官。”嘴上这么说，可我心里已经有一丝不安涌起。
“那么你能解释一下这份服役记录吗？”彼得中尉伸伸手，一个警察从他腰间的公文包里面拿出了一份文件。
彼得中尉对着那份文件念了起来：“克劳斯•施耐德，曾在帝国卫队第500伞兵营服役，无比忠诚与热忱，于法国境内有多次英勇表现……”他挑起眉头看了我一眼：“精锐战士啊。”
身份败露了，我本能地想逃，但这就是我们家门口，你不是正在家中，就是正在回家的路上，我这转头一逃，你可该怎么办。
除了束手就擒，我不知道还能怎样。
我对彼得中尉说：“我跟你们走，请不要为难瓦西里。”
彼得中尉点点头，使了个眼色，一个年轻人走上来，把我铐住，押上了停在楼外不远处的警车。彼得中尉坐在副驾驶的位置，两个年轻警察一左一右的坐在我身边，我们三个占满了整个后座。
中尉点了一支烟：“来苏维埃十九年了，你还习惯吗，克劳斯？”
我沉默的低头看着双手，脑子里想着你，不知如何作答他。
彼得中尉自顾自的继续说着：“应该是不习惯吧，曾经你住在乡间的大宅子里面，佣人每天为你洗衣做饭，冲好来自非洲的咖啡，把每天的报纸从邮箱中取回放在餐桌的角落上，真是天堂般的生活啊。在这里怎么会有那种日子，你一定过得很苦吧。”
我不知道他这是讽刺还是陈述，内心止不住的忐忑起来，在我四十年的人生中，即使在枪林弹雨中，也没有这么无助过。
他的到来，带来的不是潮汐和阳光，而是覆盖整个天空的乌云。
突然彼得中尉换了一个腔调，用一口德语说了起来：“我最初也不习惯，但我渐渐明白了这一切。”
太久没有听过有人说德语，我有一丝错愕，难以置信地，一字一顿地从脑海中拾起那熟悉的语言：“什么？我不明白？”
“这都是罪孽，还有债务。”彼得中尉一边抽烟，一边慢慢地说着：“不是宗教意义上的罪孽，而是现实上的。”
“你也是德国人吗？“我问道，心中的疑问已经压过了恐惧。
“是的，我以我自己的方式洗清了罪孽。“
“我不明白，什么是现实上的罪孽。”其实我心里明白，我在战争中夺走过许多人的生命，但我不认为那是一种罪孽，我只是奉命行事，去消灭那些奉命来夺走我的生命的人。他会是专门为这件事情而来？我不相信。
警车的车速慢了下来，因为前面有一队游行的人群，高举着“乌克兰少年团”的横幅，叫着“我们是您的手臂，苏维埃”，正在缓缓通过路口。
彼得中尉将烟头丢出车外，转过头来：“实话实说吧，在苏联的生活与我之前在德国的生活大不一样，每个人都把自己奉献给了集体，而不是如我们之前所追求的那样，去解放人的自由和意志。”
“这确实是，很大的不同。”我发现彼得中尉并不是那种蜂群思维的人，他对于这个世界有着自己的判断，但对于他的身份来说，这种判断过于危险了。
“初来苏联的时候，我也很惊讶并且难以理解，为什么这个国家会如此地践踏公民的个人意志，热衷于把他们都变成一个庞杂的社会机器上的零件。但后来我发现集体主义应当才是社会发展的正确方向，如果每个人不去尽力的为集体服务，那么我们作为一个社会，势必会放缓发展的脚步。试想，当你身体中的细胞、器官各自为战，肠道细胞想去环境更好的肝脏，肝脏细胞想做大脑的工作，你的身体还能健康吗？”
“可是我们奉行个人主义的时候，也取得了很多成就，你看看美国、英国、荷兰，还有……德国。”
彼得中尉摇了摇头：“那只是殖民时代的余晖罢了，曾经鼓吹个人意志的人，他们从大航海时代开始，就在世界各地掠夺资源与财富。你喝的咖啡，大多来自也门，那里的咖啡工人一个月的收入还不到五卢布，你可以想象吗？你们喝着剥削工人得来的咖啡，读着从东南亚砍下来的树木做成的报纸，享受着中国仆人的侍奉，一边大谈着自由民主与环境保护。就像强盗洗劫了你的家，然后告诉你，人和人之间应该自由与平等，你家不应该关闭门窗，你甚至不能教育的你儿子，只因为那是不尊重儿童自由发展的权利，你觉得这合理吗？你看，他们一旦失去了财富的支撑，很快就原形毕露，大崩溃以后，那些吹嘘人权与自由的国家，还存在吗？哪个不是沦为了无政府主义的渊薮，在时间的冲刷中，慢慢像沙滩上的城堡一样崩塌？”
虽然他的意思我不能全部认同。不过我逐渐明白他的言下之意。
“我不明白，这些话和我手上的这幅手铐有什么关系。”感受到彼得中尉是一个可以交谈的对象以后，我尝试性的向他发问。
“冷战过去了，是，那些和苏维埃对抗的国家都化为了灰烬。但我们并不是毫发无损。”
彼得，这个名字和俄罗斯铁血帝王一样的人，突然发出额一声轻轻的叹息。
他说：“苏维埃的经济也受到了重挫，对外贸易崩溃了，不止影响着资本主义国家。虽然执行委员会已经在努力发展农业与轻工业，但我们逐步增加的人口和生育率，正在渐渐吃掉我们得生活储备。简而言之，我们养不起这么多人口。我们需要一种公平的方式，帮我们遴选人口。”
警车停了，但我看向窗外，并不是警察局，而是机场。
彼得中尉从副驾驶上下来，为我拉开车门，拍拍我的肩膀：“我们曾经无情的掠夺世界，掏空了她的一切，还玩火自焚地毁掉了我们的文明，现如今这个世界需要我们用自己献祭了。我已经赎清了罪孽。该你了，祝你好运，兄弟。”

一架运输机在不远处等着我。

孩子，我从来没有因为自己参加过战争而感到羞耻或后悔，就算彼得中尉是因为我的战争罪行要逮捕我，我也只会如实交代我在战场上的所作所为，而不会去对战争的是非与正义做出评价。
我经历了那么多战斗，早已不需要正义的借口来欺骗自己开枪了。
但当我知道世界上还有绝地求生这种东西以后，我却感觉到，我在这个海岛上开的每一枪，都是不正义的。
我还记得我杀死的第一个人，甚至连枪都不会开。
他只是举起双手，走到我面前，哀求我保护他，声称自己家里还有妻子和孩子，希望能活着回去看看他们。
这场比赛只能有一个胜利者，如果他见到了他的孩子，就注定我不能见到你了。
我拒绝了他，他跪在我面前，大声地哭诉着，自己只是一个普通的报社职员，不应当卷入这场灾难中。
我用枪顶住了他的额头，如果他再这么闹下去，会暴露我的位置。
我想见到你，想完成对你母亲的承诺，将你抚养长大，给你一个虽然不完整却温馨的家，想保护你免受一切冲击，即使这冲击是来自充满恶意的世界，我也会不惜一切地挡在你身前。
前提是，我要在这场比赛中胜出，所以我开了枪，处决式地夺走了一个手无寸铁，无心反抗的生命。
这座曾是核弹试验场的无名岛上某处埋着若干台辐射抑制器，用以中和这座岛上的致命辐射。抑制器的功率会随着时间减小，用以引导人们聚集到一起去厮杀。
我趴在一处废墟旁的石堆里，看着远处将斜的夕阳，心想如果不是以生命为赌注，这也许是一项很好的竞技比赛。从太阳来看，这会应该是下午五点左右。
明天就是你的十八岁生日，我会赢得比赛，然后回到你身边，对你说着生日快乐，然后带你去你母亲的坟茔，告诉你，你的生命，是用你母亲的生命换来的。
第二天，天上下起了雨，安全区的范围已经缩的很小了，安全区外的辐射已经达到了致命的浓度，我已经不敢将盖格计数器当作手表戴在手上了，因为当它的指示灯闪起来的时候，我可能已经没办法跑进安全区了。我把计数器挂在我的kar98k栓动步枪上，像钓鱼竿上的鱼饵一样。
我一路摸在安全区的边沿，躲在树木或者石头后面守株待兔，又干掉了几个人。直到无线电耳机中传来“生存数量：2”的提示。
按照辐射抑制器的原理，安全区应该是一个球形。我在树后把盖格计数器往外探了一下，想通过辐射区的弧度推算一下安全区的大小。谁知道我刚把步枪伸出去没多远，盖格计数器不只是指示灯闪了起来，而且危险指示的蜂鸣器也嘀嘀嘀地响了起来。天知道安全区外的辐射浓度有多高。我赶紧把枪收了回来，警惕的观察四周，不知道自己有没有暴露，不过也许是雨声掩盖了蜂鸣器，附近并没有什么异动。
只剩一个对手了，我不想功亏一篑。
安全区应该就是前面这一小块草地了，草地上的草不深不足以藏下一个人，那就只有那一块石头后面可以藏下我唯一的对手了。
只要干掉他，我就能回去见到你了，瓦西里，我的孩子，我向你保证，这要不了多久……
不巧的是，我没有手雷了，只有一颗烟雾弹，于是我向左边的空地扔了烟雾弹，做出有人将从那边潜入的假象，同时我从右边快速接近那唯一一块可以藏人的石头。
随着我的快速逼近，我已经看见了那个石头后的家伙，戴着军用头盔，傻傻地用枪指着烟雾弹方向。
业余对手，我心里不屑的哼了一下。
孩子，我终于能见到你了。
但我却没想到，是在这块石头之后见到你。
我以为我们的相聚会在家里，在温暖的壁炉前，有着啤酒与面包。
那一瞬间我的脑子里闪过了太多的东西。最终一切念头都变成了你那孤零零的身影，靠在石头后面，拿着枪，对着远处的烟雾弹的瘦弱身影。
你被冻得很惨，在雨水中瑟瑟发抖，看样子你没有很好的利用身体的颤抖来给自己取暖。
我慢慢地走到你身前，摘下头盔，叫了你的名字，瓦西里。
你颤抖的回头，看向了我。
你的左手小臂被子弹擦伤了，业余的包扎让你血流不畅，我放下枪，为你解开了绷带，从背包中拿出一卷干净的绷带为你包扎了起来。你瑟瑟发抖地挤进我的怀里，我想你也和我一样，有很多话想说，却没法开口。
你是怎样来到这里的，你经历了什么，我不敢想象，我也不知该如何安慰你，只能紧紧地抱住你，我的瓦西里。
我轻轻的告诉你，你的母亲没有狠心地抛弃我们，她是为了赋予你生命而去世的。
孩子，不知道在这个时候，在这个泥泞的雨天里，你是否还记得。
今天是你的生日，我将要送你一份礼物。
这份礼物不仅是给你，也是给你母亲的，因为我曾经在她墓前不止一次发誓，我会好好守护着你。
我从大腿上的枪套里，取出了手枪，在你看不见的角度，把枪放进了嘴里。
我想，如果有生日蛋糕，请你别吹熄蜡烛，因为，那是这个崩溃的世界里，为数不多的光明。
生日快乐，瓦西里。

Some tips for newcomers: 
If you like stories, the story mode is deceptively good, in my opinion, considering the main focus of this game is Multiplayer. It'll also let you play most of the original characters, BUT they will be older versions with outdated moves from what I can remember.

Every day you get new orders with a focus on steel (game currency) and every couple of days you get orders with a focus on experience (to level your character).
Every time you hit lvl 20 and then level up again, you'll gain 1 "rep", a sort of reset, and either unlock better equipment or stop receiving worse equipment.
This behaviour stops at Rep 8, and the equipment does look progressively more complex as you level.
The equipment CAN influence things such as your damage, armor, chip damage, but it'll be marginal at best, and it does not have any effects in some game modes, so don't sweat it ─ someone who's worse than you but has been playing since launch won't win *just* because of their equipment.

All in all, a pretty cool game and definitely worth learning if you get it cheap.

I can't really describe how amazing this game is until you experience it yourself, but I can do my best. This game is one of my all-time favorites, by a long-shot (and that's coming from a dark souls fanboy; see pfp). The amount of content this game has to offer seems... endless, to say the least. For just $10 you get hours upon hours upon hours of amazing, rich, fulfilling game-play that just never seems to get stale. From fighting waves of goblins, to alien invasions, to fighting a pair of eyeballs that spit flames and shoot lasers, Terraria has A LOT of dip on it's chip. And that just goes for the enemies you're fighting, not counting the countless amounts of building blocks, weapons, tools, accessories, pets,(yes, PETS) armor sets, and many, MANY more items and materials you can craft and attain throughout your time in this game. For only having 2 dimensions, this game makes up for it by having immeasurable depth and a certain charm that is sure to have you thirsty for more every time you open it up. And, yes, some reviews (VERY little) will explain that this game may seem like an RNG/Item grinder, but can I just say that it never really FEELS that way. You sorta just dig and dig and dig and dig some more and then you look out the window and it's 1:43 AM on what was a Thursday. Terraria will drag you down and devour your time without you ever noticing, because the game is just that charismatic and, well, fun. If you buy this game I can promise you that if you put in the time and effort, it will reward you unlike any game you have played before with an amazing time and a level of satisfaction that is hard to attain through similar means coughminecraftcough. There is so much more I wish I could tell you, but I'd be sitting at my desk for at least another hour typing a small thesis. Please do yourself a favor and purchase this game so that you regret not buying it sooner. ;)

Initially, I was very sceptical about trying this game because of the reviews. But, there isn't a lot to be excited about in the PC world right now, so I gave this game a shot. I'm happy I did. There may have been some issues in early access, but this game is amazing! There are two game modes to play on, online or singleplay - co-op. There is a little bit of a learning curve, so it will take a little time to figuring things out. 

You can choose to play PvP or PvE, or PvP with Time restrctions (meaning that it isn't full on PvP all the time. I recommend playing single - co-op to learn the game.

The graphics are nice, but what I really enjoy is the huge world map you get to play in, and the ability to build your own house or castle (just use your imagination). Again, it will take a little bit of experimenting to learn how to use the building system. Every time I play I discover a new area or hidden cave, or some unexplored area. There is a lot to see and a lot to discover.

There is an option to pay monthly to host your own server if you wish, or play for free on official servers or other servers people are hosting. When you host a server, this gives you the option to be the admin, and to set the rules for the server (including how tough you want to make combat, lose items on death, PvP on or off, or set PvP to a specific time period, the amount of resources people can gather, and a lot more). This feature is always available for singleplay - co-op mode.

There is a lot of fan based moding going on too. You can add armor, weapons, or alter gameplay to your personal liking with the mods available. There are even mods to turn down the violence level if you wish (the game can be pretty gory), or to turn on or off nudity, etc.

I personally think the game is worth playing and I'm having a lot of fun. Conan Exiles brings some new things to the survival / mid-evil RPG genre. I personally like the idea of hosting my own server. This might be the wave of future MMO's, who knows, where you have the power to boot the weenies and help the cool people.

Anyways, this is all just my opinion. I'm having a blast playing this game. I'd put it on your play list and give it a try. Or, you could watch some Twitch feeds to get a feel for what the game has to offer.

I hope they continue to add new content and expand the game.

app_name: Total War: ROME II - Emperor Edition
review:
"Экономическая система упрощена до нуля...
Всё, что порадовало в серии - красочные сражения. Лучше уж поиграть в первый рим."
Прошло более полугода. На глаза попался Total war Rome II. Координально поменял свое мнение после 100 часов игры.
-Отличная графика, масштабные красивые сражения (замедленные с патчами до приемлемого уровня).
-Экономическая система непривычна после Рима первого, но имеет свои тонкости и хитрости, приводящие империю в упадок при необдуманной застройке.
-ИИ знатно подправлен как на карте компаний, так и в сражениях. Использует агентов по уму: однажды заблокировал мою армию у моста и делал так каждый ход 3мя агентами (я так понял, на случай провала двух первых) и не давал перейти в наступление второй армии, так как проход закрывала подвергшаяся атакам агентов армия.
На стратегической карте уже не выйдет "торговать со всеми до кого руки дотянутся, а если и сделаете так, то через 100-150 ходов будете в полной заднице из за системы "враг моего врага - мой друг". Приходиться выбирать партнеров, заключать/расторгать  договора в зависимости от действий других фракций. Простой пример: Вы - Понт, торгуете и имеет договор о ненападении себе с  Галатами, которые делят с вами регион, так же у вас неплохие отношения с Селевкидами. Вторые объявляют галатам войну и если вы ничего не предпримите, то по мере того, как Селевкиды будут "кушать" варворов, их отношения к вам будут становиться хуже. Но, стоит только разорвать с галатами договора и через 3-5 лет все нормализуется, однако сами Галаты, если выживут, этого вам не простят.
-Дипломатия играет новыми красками, не уровень EU конечно, но теперь союзник не нападет на вас после 50ти ходов хороших отношений, не имея веского повода, как к примеру, война с его вторым союзником, или постоянное ухудшение отношений провакациями и подрывной деятельностью.
-Полноценная сетевая компания на 2х человек, это вообще нечто. Если играть режим "1 на 1", возможно брать войска ИИ, при их битве с вашим оппонентом, под свой контроль. Захват и продвижение границ становится куда сложнее и интересней.
 Итог: субъективное мнение 8/10. отберет не один десяток часов, подарив в замен множество эмоций.

4.完成任务方式自由（可选暗杀、也可以突突，某些特定要求的除外）；
5.技能升级（随着技能解锁，可玩性越来越高，难度也越来越小，建议玩极限难度）；
6.任务不少（主线任务不少，也挺自由，可随意选择任务；支线任务较单一，主要就是偷资源、抢资源、反叛军技能）；

9.随从系统（没有基友不要紧的，有3个电脑AI，同步射击满足你的战术需求，还有一帮反抗军，满足你的人海战术）；

12.支持4人联机（喜欢和基友玩的，就联机呗）；
13.支持4pvs4p对战（喜欢PVP的，就玩吧。）；

Been playing Ark since Early Access. Probably one of the most versatile games I've ever played. Beyond it being a survival game with the ability to tame unique creatures all with a variety of unique abilities, craft weapons, tools, and utilizing cooking and farming mechanics, it is also a game where you can get creative and build epic bases either for form or function, or both. The maps are huge and are well-tended to by the devs. 

The natural surroundings on the maps are epic and serene. Sometimes I just like to fly around and take in the scenery. The Island has several major biomes that have unique weather patterns and sometimes unique creatures to that specific biome, making exploration fun and very interesting. 

Any game with resource acquisition and crafting is almost always going to have a bit of a "grind" involved, and Ark is no different. Creating large, extravagant bases, taming high level creatures or crafting powerful weapons do require some time investment ("some" is relative) but grouping up with your friends make this process much more palatable.

The game's lore is shrouded in mystery. There is no opening cutscene, no Star Wars-esque opening backstory, or anything of the sort. You wake up in an unusual place, and the rest of the story can be pieced together through clues or "explorer notes" found throughout the Ark. Through these notes (and for me, in all honesty, through YouTube) you can get a broader understanding of what's going on, as well as progressing through the game.

Combat is very versatile. Utilizing different tools, weapons and tames allows for a broad spectrum of tactical strategies to fit any given situation be it a cave dive or a base raid in PVP. 

Taming creatures is an adventure unto itself, especially at the beginning, and with a few exceptions, just about every creature in the game is tamable. Creatures do have their given purposes in certain familiar roles such as DPS-, support- or tank-style roles, but there are other creatures that are unique that simply cannot fall into any of those categories and are still a crucial component to your tribe (looking at you, Kairuku).

Overall I think the hours I've spent on this game say it all. I recommend it to everyone, but I've had a lot of trouble getting my own friends involved. The main complaint is that as a new player it's really a slow burn of a game -- it requires a lot of time investment and a little bit of grinding. For me, that in itself is enough of a sell simply because doing even the most mundane tasks in Ark (there are quite a few) provide another opportunity to explore, and like most of these types of games, Ark delivers almost to a frustrating degree with the small elements in the world that will capture your interest and draw you away from those tasks to pursue others -- going on a metal run you may uncover a high level creature you want to tame, or stumble across a cave, or grab that supply crate not too far from you. 

I suppose the common word in this review is Epic. Enough said!

Darkest Dungeon is a brutal turn-based, party-based dungeon crawler, where you not only need to manage your squad in combat, but also need to manage your roster as a whole. 

Pros:
[list]
[*] Great variety of classes, almost all of them have their place in your roster.
[*] Your characters will gain negative traits. The artifacts you gain have negative aspects. Mitigation abounds. Good stuff.
[*] Managing both stress and health in dungeons yields great decision making.
[*] Story telling is great. Narrator is great. Dark theme/art meshes well.
[*] Bosses are unique.
[*] Building up your town offers lots of strategic possibilities.
[*] Tactical fights are fun.
[/list]

YMMV:
[list]
[*] Permadeath. I don't typically like permadeath in games like this. However, combined with the no save system, you will be truly terrified going through these bleak locales. Here the permadeath adds real tension, as opposed to other games where you are likely to save scum your way out of it (well at least I am, don't judge me). It is painstaking work to level-up a toon, removing its negative traits and so forth; you definitely don't want them to die.
[/list]

Cons:
[list]
[*] Even when you know what to do, and who to bring in, the boss fights aren't easy. Frankly, life is too short to keep losing characters to bosses until you figure out their patterns. Unless you are hardcore, internet help is advised. 
[/list]

Overall: Well this game is awesome. You need to be in it for the long haul, thinking of yourself as the head coach of a team, carefully tending to your roster. That said, this game is very challenging.

It's simple. Playerunknown's Battlegrounds offers an exceptionally tense, yet fun, experience.

Right from the get go you jump from a plane, fighting for the best landing areas and hoping that nobody lands close to you.As soon as you land it's a mad scramble to get a gun and armour before anyone else can. Fail at this and you're deader than dead.

Once you've got yourself a gun and some armour, you've got 2 choices. Run further into the combat zone and try to find a good position to take everyone else out, or hide and hope nobody finds you. Running into the combat zone is a good idea if you're looking to get higher tier loot but others will have the same idea. This strategy is a high-risk, high-reward strategy if pulled off correctly. Fail to do so and you will be punished heavily by people with better guns.

Hiding works well but can be quite boring for the most part. You will occasionally get people skulking around and trying to scavenge left overs which can lead to a tense stand off. If you have a better gun and faster reflexes, you win. If not, you're getting shot to bits in a corner while crying. You can't hide for the whole game, however, as the dreaded blue (death zone) circle closes in and the white (combat zone) circle shrinks and relocates forcing you to move or die.

Red (explosion) zones can force you out of hiding spots unless you're in a building.As the game progresses the blue zone moves faster and gives you less time to get into the white zone, and the white zone shrinks in size forcing players into a smaller kill zone.

8/10

There's so much I can say about this game that I'm not sure where to start. I guess let's start with the good things about this game since it won't take me a long time to write.

Pros:
- Its price isn't too bad especially if you get it on sale 
- It can have some nice graphics but to run them and get decent fps you need a NASA pc (kinda like PUBG)
- Watching the professionals play is really entertaining plus they're nice people (well, almost all of them)
- The customization is good. You can go for many different designs for your car. However the cosmetic items can cost quite a bit (and I'll get into that later)
- Custom trainig maps are a thing and some of them could be a lot of fun, some of them could be extremely challenging if that's what you're looking for. You can also make ones yourself to fit the exact training you want to do.
- Finding matches is relatively fast (unless you have a super high rank) since there doesn't need to be that many people

Cons:
- Servers are a piece of shit. And instead of focusing on fixing the issue Psyonix concern themselves with pointless stuff that nobody gives a flying fuck about (like crates and new cars)
- Like I've already mentioned there are crates. I don't really have a problem with that but the issue is the odds of actually getting something decent - tbh I'd rather play the lottery than open crates
- The community is pretty toxic. Get ready for the "What a save!" or "Nice one!" quick chat spam. Or have the pleasure of seeing a 12-year-old tell you that he's gonna fuck your mother because you gave away the ball that one time in the game
- I talked about how it takes a short time to find a match - that's mainly because the game doesn't take enough time to find a good server with fitting opponents and teammates
- The outcome of a game is too often decided by sheer coincidences and it feels like Psyonix is just shoving their middle finger right into your face
- Mastering the game takes a long, but that's not the issue. A lot of times it will feel like all the effort and time you've put into getting better was for absolutely nothing and everything is against you, because again Psyonix whips out the middle fingers

I got Subnautica in a Humble Bundle and didn't even realize I had it for a few months.  I've put 26 hours into the game now and I can say that the game in its current state is probably a 7/10.  I would say that game play is 8/10, atmosphere/environment is 10/10, music is 7/10 (only because it can glitch and load in and out otherwise it's 9/10), story is only a 5/10 but it's early access so it's still being worked on.  That said, I would say that enjoyability factor is easily a 9/10... for the first 25 hours.  I have enjoyed the ever-living hell out of this game.  I've taken my sweet time so some of you might get to where I was (progression wise) much quicker.  Once you get to near end game, it starts to get... less fun.  The progression of tech and difficulty takes a drastic change near the end.  You are required to get far more and much harder to obtain materials to craft end game tech but it doesn’t' seem to scale nicely.  Once you have end game tech, you need to get to harder and harder areas.  These areas are harder to navigate, fraught with much more deadly creatures, and since they’re harder to get to, you must manage your h20/food to a much higher degree.  
The true end game hasn’t been implemented yet, but from what I’ve read it’s already on the experimental branch so it sounds like it’s nearing completion.   I think the game needs some serious reworking on the pacing.  It’s very slow to start but scales up a little too quickly at the end.  The game also needs better hooks.  That is, it doesn’t do a great job of telling you, “go here next, get this tech next” etc.  It does those things, but not always and not always at appropriate times.  This probably sounds like a critical review, and I guess it is, but understand, what the game is lacking it more than makes up for with enjoyment.  I have put 26 hours in, and only the last 60 to 90 minutes of that were frustrating.  Once they finish the game, if they figure out the pacing issues, if they add a few more hooks, this game will easily be a 10/10 for me.  I’m going to switch from survival to “creative” now.  So, I can get the true endgame stuff and play around with the base building (damn fun).  I’ll probably put another 5-10 hours in with its current state.  If/when they finish the game, I’ll come back for a fresh play through.

I've completed this game twice now. Once on PS4 and once here on PC. (Almost a 3rd time as I've been playing a bit in co-op with a friend). And I could maybe go for another playthrough someday. Rarely do I actually play a game twice. The last time I've ever done that was with Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV, GTA V, MGS Solid Snake and Red Dead Redemption 1. That’s out of hundreds and hundreds of games that I can even remember playing.

Everything about Dying Light is great and it's almost hard to believe that it's by the same people who made Dead Island. A prime example of a developer who knows how to improve and if you've played Dead Island, you'll remember that the atmosphere was what stood out the most.

It is a horror game that's scary enough to make your butt cheeks clench but just the right kind of scary that you can play freely without too much fear. The survival mechanics are light and by no means are they an inconvenience. Weapons will break if you use them too much so you'll either have to find new 1s or repair your current 1s but you can only repair them a limited number of times. You'll need to loot & scavenge for medical supplies but you can also buy weapons and items are stores, so your options aren't limited. You don't have to worry about eating or drinking though.

What makes Dying Light stand out from a lot of horror & zombie games and even open world games in general, is its atmosphere. It's by far the best atmosphere in any zombie game I've played and possibly even horror games. The way it's capable of making you feel uneasy & disturbed by the environment you’re in is astonishing.

The narrative is good, the concept of playing a double agent in a quarantined zone and the villain who is somewhat cliché is still interesting. You gradually grow to like Kyle, the character you play as. While also growing to like the other characters. Fairly early on you'll feel like you've chosen to side with the runners.

The gameplay is fun, it's nice being able to chop the limbs and heads off zombies while also being creative with traps & lures. The variety of zombie types also helps keep you on your toes. It does really well to give you the illusion that you're overpowered too but does even better at reminding you that it isn't always true.

I liked how it had RPG mechanics in the form of a skill system too and how exp was earned by doing specific things related to those skill sets. Like Parkouring over obstacles, climbing etc... would give exp to your agility skill set. Attacking, fighting, killing enemies etc... would give exp to your power skill set. Getting supply drops would give exp to your survival skill set. So you earn exp as you play pretty much.

Then when it comes to nightfall, it's like a whole different game. There’re a few missions you're forced to do at night during the base game and quite a few missions you're forced to do during the night in The Following expansion. I personally just avoid playing during the night because the Volatiles are damn scary.

The graphics are superb. They convey the disturbing atmosphere really well, from the abandoned buildings, cars & almost lifeless streets to the air itself. Unfortunately, they've recycled a lot of NPC & enemy skins, so it can ruin the immersion a bit.

The audio is probably what compliments the atmosphere the most. The zombie sounds are great, nice and scary and one thing I've noticed is that if you're one of those people who watch The Walking Dead and ask "how do they not hear the zombies sneaking up on them?" well you learn very quickly why in Dying Light. The most notable sound that evokes the most fear though is the screams from either Virals or Volatiles. The latter being the worse. The moment you hear those screams you know it’s time to keep an eye out or run.

There's a lot more I could say about it, but Dying Light is the perfect balance of an open world zombie survival horror game hitting nearly every nail on the head. I've clocked about 66 hours in the game and that's doing pretty much mainly the story & side missions. There's still a lot more to do on top of that.

THE GOOD
--------------------
This game is actually the 4th installment of the Arma series and I've been playing since the start.  The developers of this game have taken a rare approach to updating their game.  They keep the mechanics and feel of the game pretty much the same while making the graphics shine by just updating their custom Real Virtuality engine rather than replacing it, as well as adding new campaigns, missions, vehicles, weapons, and game modes.

The part where this game REALLY shines, however, is the community driven mods.  The game was built for modding and the developers have done everything in their power to make it easy for the community to make ANYTHING they want out of this game.  It may look like a hardcore military simulator from the store page, but I've seen games in this series turned into a civil war sims, "grand theft auto" like games (Arma Life), hardcore zombie games (DayZ), a StarGate tribute which had working, animated stargates and all your favorite characters from the show, ww2 sims (Invasion 1944), Jurassic Park tributes, and so much more.

These mods take a lot of work to create, sure, but there are also things you can do very easily without any knowledge of 3d editing or texturing.  Simply open the mission editor on the map that you like best and place a few soldiers down.  Now add some waypoints for them to attack a town.  Add some soldiers inside the town.  That's it!  If you make yourself a civilian character in the town you can watch a fantastic battle ensue between the two groups of soldiers, using proper flanking maneuvers and yelling back and forth to one another when they see an enemy.  This all would take at most about 2 minutes in the editor to have a full battle going on.  Want to do more?  Read the plethora of information out there on advanced editing and scripting in the game and before you know it you'll have the ability to make suicide bombers, "battle busses" (essentially a civilian bus with artillery and machine guns on top of it), nuclear bombs, and really ANYTHING you can imagine.  If you have any issues, someone will be willing to help you out either on reddit.com/r/armadev or on the official Bohemia Interactive forums.

I hope you'll choose to join me on my favorite game and play some cool missions together that you or I just freshly made in the editor!  Even if you don't like making your own content, there are fun mods already out there such as the popular Battle Royale mod where you're forced to parachute out of a crashing plane with 28 or so of your fellow players and fight to the death while scavenging for the best gear.  Just look around and you'll find endless entertainment in this game!


THE BAD
---------------
I mentioned that the engine is updated with each iteration instead of replaced.  This does sometimes mean that glitches that were in the first couple games reappear in later games, but with the increased popularity of the series lately the devs have been doing their best to squash all those nasty bugs.  Another warning I would give would-be buyers is that the game is very demanding for your PC.  People who have rigs that they THINK are powerful because they can play Battlefield 4 at full settings without much frame drop are in for a nasty surprise: Arma 3 truly stresses your hardware and the devs are still working on optimizations to take full advantage of your hardware.  At the moment it seems like most people are having a smooth experience but some peoples' hardware, even when pretty impressive, just doesn't get along with the game that well at the moment.

So I played for a lot of additional time and I have some further thoughts.
A lot of CK3 is made up of what I can only describe as 'things that happen'. They don't feel like part of any historical process or any strategy. They just come out of the blue apparently as some sort of RNG.
Take history as an example. Henry VIII founded the Church of England and split from Rome because of a series of factors that made him believe it was worth it.
In CK3, King Aethelred of Wessex just converted to Catharism and split from Rome for... some reason I guess? I went tag hopping to try to understand why, but I'm at a loss. It literally destroyed his realm and turned his allies against him, and there was nothing that he could gain from it. And yet the game did it. These don't feel like organic events, they feel like drawing a card from community chest.

The vassal wars/uprisings are also boring and don't seem to do much to limit you or the AI.

Great game so far, and remarkably limited in bugs for just having been launched. 

However, so far I have found the combat system incredibly frustrating and it is clear it has problems. Overall I really like the direction Paradox has taken this game and I will be happy to recommend it - when these issues are ironed out. This is because they have been so irritating that they're making me not enjoy the game.

 Some issues I have encountered;
-The (very helpful) icons that advise you if you are likely to win/lose a battle are frequently incorrect. One claimed that I would lose massively, and I had less troops than my enemy despite me having 5K and him having 2K. I won so decisively I ended the war.
-Wars still suffer from the characteristic Paradox issue of 'whack a mole' battles. I fought about six battles just chasing my enemy up and down the coast, each time butchering his troops and murdering his knights, only to gain just a handful of warscore and to find that his army reinforced (from WHERE!? he came from overseas!). The sorry episode only ended when I happened to capture him.
-Very strong allies with motivations to fight will just sit and do nothing (example: I allied with Lotharingia to fight France. Lotharingia did absolutely nothing despite France having open borders and no troops there.
-The AI will just immediately march on your capital all the time and it gets really irritating.

I should add however that CKIII features a greatly improved combat AI.

 I look forwards to the upcoming patches because I want to enjoy this game!
