Ich mag es trotz all seiner Schwächen, für die ich nicht blind bin und wo ich sogar mehr sehe als nur die, die alle herumsprechen.

Die Ästhetik der Spielwelt und ihre Hintergründe sind sehr detailiert und so ziemlich jeder Spielabschnitt ist visuell herausragend und erinnerungswert. Musik und soundeffekte und auch die Sprachausgabe sind von erstklassiker Qualität.

Die Geschichte ist raffiniert, aber nicht gerade logisch oder intelligent. Auch passiert im gesamten Mittelteil nichts von Relevanz, aber es hat immer noch mehr Handlung als die meisten Shooter. Bei einem erneuten Durchlauf merkt man, dass die Entscheidungen, die man gelegentlich trifft, keine Auswirkungen haben außer einer kosmetischen, was schade ist.

Innerhalb der Spielwelt gibt es einige Ungereimtheiten, die offensichtlich aufgrund mangelnder Differenzierung der Entwickler entstanden sind und andere aufgrund der anzunehmenden Vorgaben des Publishers Elemente des Franchises wiederzuverwenden. Das betrifft das Verhalten aller Figuren miteinander: NPCs mit dem Spieler, Gegner mit dem Spieler, Gegner mit deiner Gefährtin... es kommt zu einer Diskrepanz der Glaubwürdigkeit.

Die DLCs sind enttäuschend, weil sie Columbia nicht vertiefen sondern sich wieder auf Rapture berufen und nur Fanservice sind. Für sich genommen und spielerisch sind die wohl in Ordnung, nur versuchen die unvereinbare Dinge zu verbinden und es wird so getan als sei das von vornherein so geplant. Außerdem erfüllt Burial at sea nicht die angesetzten Erwartungen, so dass eine aufgeschlüsselte Geschichte daraus geworden wäre.

Dennoch habe ich für das Kernspiel viel Sympathie übrig, die teilweise irrational ist. Leider verbraucht sich der content recht schnell, aber es gibt mehr zum Nachdenken und zu entdecken als in vielen anderen Spielen und seien es auch kleine Eastereggs oder Makel. Es kommt sehr selten vor, dass ich gegenüber der Schlechtigkeit von etwas nicht zynisch reagiere, denn im Falle von Bioshock Infinite denke ich über alle pros und contras gerne nach.

Hat In Time, cos'è di preciso?
Per me è una piccola perla, una di quelle che sa come non prendersi sul serio, irriverente e adorabile, un'avventura platform che non solo soddisferà gli amanti della sfida ma anche chi semplicemente vuole passare qualche giornata ricordando i giochi semplici di una volta.

Impossibile non lasciarsi catturare dalle musiche spensierate e allegre, dal carattere della protagonista, dai colori e la vivacità del gioco ed è anche impossibile non lasciarsi scappare una risata in almeno un paio di grottesche e geniali occasioni  spacca quarta-parete.

Il gioco semplicemente parla di una bambina al comando della sua nave spaziale che per un guasto, si ferma vicino un pianeta e perde le sue clessidre temporali, che non sono altro che benzina per l'astronave. 
Da qui in poi la "Mafia" che abita questo pianeta pretende che sia tutto proprietà della Mafia e da qui in poi cominceremo la nostra raccolta, livello dopo livello.

Il gioco strizza l'occhio al caro vecchio Bugs Bunny Lost in Time per via della simil quest di raccolta, ma non lasciatevi ingannare, A Hat in Time è molto ma molto più ESAGERATAMENTE eccentrico, con boss no sense, livelli assurdi e personaggi di un certo spessore come ad esempio lo spettro e i suoi folli contratti ruba anime. 
Le musiche che spaziano da deliranti speed metal/pop/pixel/remix a rilassanti temi da Arcade di una volta ma in veste moderna.

Il gioco ha quella componente "Kawaii" generale che non stanca mai, la possibilità di sbloccare e personalizzare i vari cappelli della protagonista  dà una grande spinta per il completamento e ricerca di monete da inserire nella slot machine per sbloccare colori, musiche e skin, ogni cappello possiede poi abilità particolari e utili al fine del gameplay come rallentare il tempo, correre più veloci, vedere il mondo degli spiriti ecc.

Un gioco da non perdere, soprattutto per la possibilità di poter giocare con un amico in split-screen, opzione sempre più abbandonata e che fa decisamente piacere.
Il gioco risulta essere in inglese, ma esiste una patch tra le varie mod che aggiunge l'italiano ed installarla è semplicissimo e senza intoppi.

Il gioco tecnicamente è stabile, non ho incontrato bug e scorre tutto fluidamente, potreste aver bisogno di un attimo per adattarvi alla gestione della telecamera ma non impiegherete molto a familiarizzarci.

Consigliato a tutti gli amanti dei giochi platform e anche a chi non ne ha mai provati, un livello di sfida impegnativo e una protagonista dolcissima con una marea di livelli, colori e risate, sapranno farvi innamorare di questo piccolo grande videogame!

Dirt 4 sigue teniendo la misma sensación que Dirt 3 en modo Arcade, por lo que entiendo que sea su sucesor.

Dirt Rally tampoco era un simulador. Este es un juego producido para vender grandes cantidades. A aquellos que se quejan de etapas repetitivas:

El nivel de calidad alcanzado en el acabo de las etapas es estupendo, y muy dificil de conseguir con un generado procedural. Si es cierto que serían necesarias mas localizaciones, y mas elementos procedurales, que deberían ser una actualizacion o DLC, pero aún así es correcto el trato que se recibe.

A aquellos que se quejan del copiloto:

Para concluir, creo que es un muy buen juego, pero que todavía se podría mejorar aún más. El contenido procedural es el camino a seguir por Codemaster, y me parece que es la mejor opción. TL;DR: Game is nothing like what it could be, or what it was, items are locked to region in order to block any sort of interesting progression, the entire system exists to make the game not fun.

I played alpha, I didn't  expect the game to be the same, I expected both minor and major changes, and I wanted to be happy with whatever wollay put out, just because I used to legitimately enjoy cube world.

I mistakenly expected the game to be good.
This Cashgrab of a game is a LOT. of wasted potential. The old Cube World had fun and enjoyable exploration and combat, however in this version, almost all of that is gone.

Exploration Items are locked to regions, if you get the boat in one region and sail into another region, that boat is gone until you return to the region you originally got it in, and you'll have to get the boat in the region you're attempting to move to. This game's main feature was Exploration, and that's just been thrown out of the window in favor of a terrible Progression system reliable on a 'region lock'

Combat is Boring, and Power is dumb. If you have 1 star gear, you can't fight 3 star enemies. In Alpha, you'd be able to dodge enemy attacks and continuously throw out your own, until you inevitably killed your target. The ability to defeat enemies with skill has been completely removed. The combat relies on tanking hits or just not getting hit at all, some enemies will just soak up your damage until you SOMEHOW kill them, this makes the dungeons not very enjoyable.

Artifacts are just bad. Levels are locked behind artifacts, that's fine, but levels are litterally just the number of artifacts you own, and what do Artifacts even do in the first place? Make you use less stamina and move faster, that's all. No combat buffs to make the next region easier.

And some of you, who have played the game, might say "But what about + gear, that's not region locked"

God Eater 3 takes the core themes and mechanics from God Eater Resurrection and God Eater 2 Rage Burst and adds its own twists that makes the game incredibly fun and enjoyable all around. 

Gameplay: The core gameplay is still the same from the previous titles however, GE3 introduces new gameplay mechanics that allows better movement and more options to devour the gods that plague the world. 
-With the introduction of the Shield Dive that allows you to jump at great length, it opens up many options when it comes to dodging, traversing, and hunting. Since you use your shield to dive forward, you are also defending making this move safer than most. However, it will not protect you against strong and devouring attacks and it takes a good chunk of your stamina so its best to not abuse it as it will leave you open. It is worth mentioning that as long as you are locked onto an enemy, you will automatically dive into the enemy so if you're trying to get away from the enemy it is best to unlock first.
- Burst Arts are the new special moves that replace Blood arts from GE2RB. Unlike the Blood Arts, to use Burst Arts you must be in burst mode so devouring enemies is highly suggested. You will gain access to Bust Arts and other buffs as long as you are in level 1 burst. In GE2RB you could only equip one Blood Art and in GE3 you can equip 3 Burst Art. One for ground attacks, one for aerial attacks, and one for side-step attacks. Burst Arts give you far more options when it comes to attacks and encourages you to be stay in burst mode to access the arts and gain additional buffs.
-Devouring has been improved from GE2RB but it does not compare to the devouring system (Predator style) from GE Resurrection. GE3 allows you to perform devours in the air but that is the extent to what has been added to GE3. GE Resurrection gave you the ability to customize the way you can perform a devour and what kind of buffs you gain from it. In GE2RB you could only perform a quick and charged devour. At the very least, GE3 allows you to perform devour in the air which makes it the safest option when it comes to devouring. When performing a devour on a aragami in the previous titles, you would gain an enemy bullet which allowed you to shoot a special bullet based on the enemy you have performed devour on. GE3 no longer gives you an enemy bullet and only gives you the link bullet which allows you to give and raise burst levels to your teammates.
-Engage system links you with a party member both of you will automatically give each other buffs and share the burst meter. Sharing the burst meter is extremely beneficial since you can shoot link bullets to your linked party member and raise their burst level thus raising your own burst level. Engaging with a party member whenever is possible is highly recommended since you'll get additional buffs and the ability to enter to burst level 3.

Story: The story follows somewhat a similar format from the previous titles. Your created character is basically the chosen one of this story. Your character has a unique power that makes you stand out from the rest of the god eaters. You'll meet fellow god eaters that fill a specific character archetype but have their own unique characteristics to them. While you and your team face dangerous monster, you will also face government officials with their own agendas that threaten humanity's chances of survival. Along the way you'll encounter an anomaly or catalyst that the story will be centered around. While the formula isn't new, it is still enjoyable to go through. The characters are likable, the world is interesting, and the story is just anime fun.

Graphics and Music: I don't know enough to get all technical so I'll be simple with this section. The art style is still the same as the previous titles but with improved visuals and graphics. Music is great with some good remixes of previous tracks from the older games. However, in default settings, the music tends to get louder than it should be in some cutscenes so you might want to mess with the music and sound in the settings. Other than that, music and graphics are pretty good.

The game is a lot of fun and improves on a lot of things from the previous games. I highly recommend it to long time fans and for new comers, you don't need to play the previous games. While this is a sequel it does not rely heavily on story elements from the older titles. Every game you start with a new (created) character with their own story just set in the same world. It is game people shouldn't sleep on. Finally the game seems to have less content to the other titles but Bandia has announced they'll constantly update game adding new missions and stuff and it seems they'll be free updates/DLC. 

To newcomers and older fans, I recommend this game. Its a lot fun and you'll have a good time overall.

毫无疑问我是推荐的，游戏的好处有：游戏体验很沉浸，剧情其实挺深入人心，世界也很宏大，招募兽人什么的是相当令人兴奋的。
游戏细节尤其好，就我目前发现的，在进攻队长时如果骑着狂兽或者巨兽，他还会嘲讽你是个懦夫，不敢下来，的确如官方承诺的，你的做法会对游戏产生影响。其实也是刷刷刷，但是你不会觉得没意思，因为随时都有挑战自己的机会。
但是我觉得做的最不好的一点事是难度的划分。不推荐选择最高难度，就我游玩的这十个小时，如果你不是非常有耐心不会对不停重复产生烦躁，那你可以试试，但是烦人的是，高难度下兽人数量会增加，而且攻击频率，角度，精英兵种（盾，矛）都会变多，队长也总是围绕着一大群人，我是那种不太喜欢跟着主线一路走的人，刚进第二幕，我就去招募队长什么的了（当时是最高难度），我就发现，队长背叛或者死而复生这种情况非常之多，而且因为我等级很低，大部分时候只能羞辱然后再招募，每次进攻都非常的难，因为人实在是太多了，根本没有输出机会，其实最弱的反倒是队长了，内奸数量似乎也有显著减少。切回正常难度，才能正常体验游戏，一周目不推荐最高，很容易陷入复仇，被杀，招募，背叛，然后打不过的死循环。
[spoiler] 一定要挑战自己的话，先打主线，再去攻城，最简单的方法是去找一头巨兽，简直是战略核武器，谁也打不过[/spoiler]

但是不去选择宿敌（最高）难度的话，你会发现兽人们是真的没有脑子，潜行从他身体前边过只能让他感觉到有人，看不见你，警觉度削减也非常的快，等于是一点难度也没有，正面战斗的话，升级版qte吧，这点哪个难度都没区别。

别的不方便多说，能感觉到制作组想要我们沉浸进去的心思，但是因为主角很强，游戏也有一些bug，但都无伤大雅，我目前碰到的都是动作上面的，暗杀一刀插到地里面，抱着空气一顿猛捅，但一般这种游戏都差不多这样，队长们会在城里乱晃，你会被伏击，而且故事是真的不错，我是看过原著的，虽然感觉一些怪物没有那么强，（食人魔，戒灵等），[spoiler]但是看见尸罗莫名很开心[/spoiler]还没打到后面，但是我很期待接下来的表现，预购不亏！[spoiler]虽然发售当天就75折了。。。[/spoiler]

If I could describe this game in one word, it'd be: thrilling. Not in an action-packed or jump-out-at-you sort of way, but the in the sense that you truly get the thrill of adventure from this game. The story is great, the gameplay is exceptional, and the world is absolutely STUNNING. There are definitely quite a few bugs or glitches, but the otherwise great quality of the game is definitely enough to see past them. 

I stumbled into this game not knowing anything (really, it was an implulse buy), and I think you should too. This includes not looking up and reading everything online, because so much of the game's appeal is learning things on your own.

If you haven't gotten this game yet, do yourself a favor and get it. It's WELL worth it at it's full price, and I would have been happy paying more, even.
Nemá chybu.mulťák taky pohoda.S kámošema..... pecka gamesa

-- Matchmaking is non-existant, you will not be paired with players and killers of like skill or level, you simply will not. You will be paired with people who've been playing the game since release and have every item and perk (killers too) even if you just downloaded the game today. 

-- Completely imbalanced, killers get better perks quicker and are continuously buffed while survivors get nerfed.  The Shape should have been a temporary addition for Halloween, not permanent, his abilities make him the strongest killer easily able to eliminate all 4 survivors. Survivors however, get skills that stack so well with their items it means they can sabotage infinitely or actually outrun the killer (something that is not supposed to be able to happen) 

-- Terrible Servers, if you find yourself in a match with anyone outside your region (because there are no specific region servers) expect to be lagged into, through, and behind walls, sometimes even causing your character to freeze in an animation for the rest of the match (you can still move and interact though) 

--No real tutorial: One video a piece with "tips" on how to be a survivor and hunter is not a tutorial. It doesn't explain how to use any of the killers or what they do. The system such as the bloodweb or the items and what they're used for is not explained until you actually come across the item itself in game. 

-- Lots of poor sportsmanship among the playerbase, camping galore, once caught most players disconnect or simply give up and do not struggle so they die immediately because team mates will not save each other because the killer camps the place you are hung in. 

All in all the game has a great premise and really shines when all the pieces seem to line up on the rare occasion you get a good matchup. But unless server stability and gameplay imbalances are fixed I've got to give it a thumbs down.

Nad tímto seznamem jsem, jako věrný fanoušek knih, trávil celkem 249 hodin (čistý herní čas).

Pro případné vysvětlení, vyjádření se k daným bodům nebo vysvětlení zde vynechaných částí (kvůli spoilerům) mě prosím kontaktujte na mail: aenszguhelem@gmail.com 
Milerád odrážky rozepíšu a vysvětlím včetně všech detailů. 

Pro: 
- soubojový systém, který je příjemně dynamický 
- občas podařené narážky na knihy, seriál i minulé díly (slovní, místy i co se lokací a questů týče)

- nulová návaznost na minulé díly (načtení pozic změní pár kosmetických, pro questy nebo příběh nedůležitých bodů) 
- logiku popírající nesrovnalosti (kvůli spoilerům nebudu jmenovat)

- AI

When I was first informed of this game and I looked at it, I saw what I thought was just another indie RPG that had gotten positive reviews, and brushed it off. After some time though, people kept telling me to try it out . . . So I decided I would.

I have not even once regretted buying this game at full price, and as a matter of fact am proud that I supported it.
Undertale is a game that really does a good job at building up a character, and then letting YOU decide what you want to do with that character.
While the game does have many choices that affect your playthrough, they aren't always these guge game changing decisions. Often times they are subtle, or small. Which in my own opinion is still great, after all, I can't see myself making a better game.

The music in this game I wouldn't say is a masterpiece, but I will say I thoroughly enjoyed most all of it, and it fit so very well into the game. So all in all, I'd say that they did an excellent job with the music, and I'll be damned if there's any music that fits it better out there.

This game also brought something to mind for me. Normally I judge a game on how many hours I will put into it. Around 5$, I should have at least 10 hours. 10-15$ I'd best be putting in somewhere upwards of 25 hours, and so on so forth. With this game, it wouldn't matter if I only got 10 hours out of it, I enjoyed the experience so much that my previous rules didn't matter to me anymore.

So all in all, I won't go saying this is the best game ever made, but I will say it's a game I've probably enjoyed the most. Therefore, in my view, this game is worth the 10$ for the enjoyment I derived from it.

What made The Room so good in it's great formula of mystery and puzzle solving is back yet again for an outstanding sequel! If you're unfamiliar with the series, The Room firstly came out on mobile platforms, and was then fully remastered for PC. The original Room was released back in 2014 and The Room 2 released in 2016. The game's quite simplistic in it's concept. You have a safe, a box, or just a lock, and the player is supposed to open it. To do so you're gonna have to solve all of the sub-puzzles before cracking the big one.

While I do get frustrated a lot of times in puzzle games, I feel the difficulty for The Room games isn't too hard but also not too easy, it's perfectly balanced and is able to be satisfactory throughout the entirety of the game. It lasts about 3.5 hours total if you don't rush through it, just like the first one. While some people may not like the short length, I think a short game fits the genre better than a longer one. There are 6 chapters in this sequel, one of them lasts a minute and another one is a tutorial, so in the end we have 4 chapters with challenging rooms to crack.

I was quite surprised by the creepy atmosphere in The Room Two, it certainly felt darker than the first game while the main objective is pretty much the same between the two. However, there's a slight difference in this installment, instead of being focused on just one safe or table, now there are multiple places in the room to explore, so moving around with the mouse is possible now.

The port is really well made but I did have some slight annoyances. Sometimes I wanted to move a drawer and the game decided to move the camera instead. Also, it should be possible to type on the typewriter with the keyboard. It's nothing game breaking or too frustrating, just little details I'd like to point out.

The Room Three is already out on mobile, but I do hope it is ported to the PC just like the first two games have been. This is two of my favorite mystery/puzzle games of all time and having to pick between which one is the best is a tough call, they stand on equal ground in terms of quality, challenge and entertainment, two phenomenal games I'd recommend anyone to check them out, even if you're not into point & click / puzzle games. 9/10

[u] Gameplay [/u]
Portal 2 is a first-person perspective puzzle game. The player takes the role of Chell in the single-player campaign, as one of two robots—Atlas and P-Body—in the cooperative campaign, or as a simplistic humanoid icon in community-developed puzzles. These four characters can explore and interact with the environment. Characters can withstand limited damage but will die after sustained injury. There is no penalty for falling onto a solid surface, but falling into bottomless pits or toxic pools kills the player character immediately. When Chell dies in the single-player game, the game restarts from a recent checkpoint; in the cooperative game, the robot respawns shortly afterwards without restarting the puzzle. The goal of both campaigns is to explore the Aperture Science Laboratory—a complicated, malleable mechanized maze. While most of the game takes place in modular test chambers with clearly defined entrances and exits, other parts occur in behind-the-scenes areas where the objective is less clear.

The player must solve puzzles using the 'portal gun' which can create two portals connecting two distant surfaces depicted as matte white, continuous, and flat. Characters can use these portals to move between rooms or to "fling" objects or themselves across a distance. Outlines of placed portals are visible through walls and other obstacles for easy location.

The game includes a two-player cooperative mode. Two players can use the same console with a split screen, or can use a separate computer. Each player's portals are of a different color scheme, where one is blue and purple and the other is orange and red. A calibration chamber separates the characters to teach the players to use the communication tools and portals. Most later chambers are less structured and require players to use both sets of portals for laser or funnel redirection, launches, and other maneuvers. The game provides voice communication between players, and online players can temporarily enter a split-screen view to help coordinate actions. Players can "ping" to draw the other player's attention to walls or objects, start countdown timers for synchronized actions

Resident Evil 7 puts you in the shoes of Ethan. After his wife Mia disappears for almost three years he get's a disturbing message from her which contains a tearful goodbye. Wanting to find out what happened to his wife Ethan travels to Dulvey, Louisiana. Once there Ethan enters a seemingly abandoned house, but after some time he finds that the house is not abandoned and in fact is inhabited by the Bakers, a family of three, Jack, Lucas and Marguerite and Ethan is put in a fight for his life as he tries to save Mia and leave the Baker Residence. 

The story in itself is rather intriguing as it has a very mysterious feel to it. You don't know much about anything as the game doesn't flat out tell you the story. Most of it is told through paper clippings, photos, journals and VHS tapes which you can watch to find out what other souls went through when they wound up in the Baker residence. I found the story incredibly captivating which pushed me to keep playing until I figured out everything.

The voice acting for the characters I felt was alright. I liked Jack, Mia, Marguerite and Ethan, but the voice actor for Lucas truly over did it. Some of the lines he delivers are too over the top.

Gameplay:

Most fans have been annoyed by the fact that Resident Evil 7 was first person only, but to be honest ? This helps out the game to be even more scarier. The limited vision once you travel through the halls of the house and hear noises coming from seemingly every direction helps build tension which would have never been able to achieve with third person. But for those stating that this is not Resident Evil, it's more Resident Evil than the last 5 games in the series.

The most memorable stuff from previous RE games make a comeback in this game. Inventory management, safe rooms, limited resources. Even the puzzles are very RE like. Some of the puzzles include looking for pieces of a sculpture to open a door, which is very nice nod to previous games. 

The combat in this game is a bit different from the stuff you have seen in the previous RE games. Ammo and in general all resources are incredibly limited, so you must save your ammo and use it wisely and make every single shot count. The game gives you Pistols, Shotguns, SMG, Flamethrowers and Grenade Launchers to sink your teeth in, but again ammo for these guns are incredibly limited, so you'll mostly use Pistols and Shotguns.

Most of the fights tend to get incredibly violent and the game in general is incredibly violent. Probably even more violent than the other titles in the Resident Evil franchise.

Now for the enemies. Once the game starts, you're gonna be hunted by the Baker family. Unlike other enemies you can't kill Jack or Marguerite. They are faster and stronger than you so it's best you are not seen by them. But if you are spotted your options are to run away and hide or you can waste your ammo and stun them. They will go down, but will get back up again and will hunt you down. The only other type of enemies you see are the Molded, which are these black gooey monsters which are usually in groups, but fighting them is usually simple as a few well placed headshots will take them out.

Boss fight also make a return and the boss fights in this game are absolutely amazing. Intense would be an incredible understatement. Some of my favorite moments are the boss encounters in this game.

Graphics and Audio:

Graphically the game looks absolutely outstanding. The environments look incredibly and all of them are incredibly detailed. The game looks the best once the setting is night as some of the day textures are a bit mediocre. 

Audio design is absolutely phenomenal. Playing this game with a good pair of headphones is a must. Once the game starts and all the surrounding sounds kick in you are immersed in this world and in the later segments the audio design is phenomenal. When you wander through the houses and hear creeks, weird noises and the bakers shouting while they're stomping around looking for you make for an incredibly intense game.

Problems:

This game does suffer from some very minor issues which I will not deduct points for as I think these are just minor nitpicks of mine.

The game had one bug which I only encountered at one section of the game. I got stuck in a railing and I had to force shutdown the game to fix it. Until the end of the game it's the only bug I encountered.

The puzzles are all incredibly simple. It's usually pick something up and bring it to a specific location and that's basically it. I think more depth for the puzzles would have been nice, like the Happy Birthday puzzle. 

Length:

The game took me 8 hours to finish, but this game has tons of replay value. This game has two endings, the madhouse difficulty which gives you limited saves and resources are even more scarce and not to mention collectibles and stuff like that, so more or less you are looking at a 20+ hour game.

Closing remarks:

Resident Evil 7 is return to form. It's scary, intense, incredibly fun and all around an excellent game. Resident Evil 5 and 6 sold incredibly well and Capcom could have just made 7 into another action fest, but they took care and brought the series back to it's roots and the succeed in making one hell of a game. If you like Horror games this is a must, if you like Resident Evil this is a must, hell this is a must play in general. I would honestly say it's worth to get it as soon as possible.

Final Rating:
9.5/10

[h1]One game where I really wish Steam had an 'it's alright' button for the reviews![/h1]
I've been a long-standing fan of the Tomb Raider series from the beginning, right from the very first one. And I've enjoyed every instalment in the main series that I've played. (I'm excluding handheld-only versions for the purposes of this review). So when I saw that this was going to be a reboot and tell us how Lara became the tough adventurer that we know her as, I was excited.

The premise of the game is certainly an interesting one and certainly does have that Tomb Raider-esque vibe to it, and the game is delivered with a certain level of polish. It feels cinematic and has some tension in the right places, but it doesn't have the same feel as the past instalments in the TR series. I like the direction that they went with this one, making it more of a survivalist-style game, but there aren't enough tombs to raid (this is called TOMB raider after all, oh, and the tombs are side-quests). I do like the customising weapons and the slow introduction of new items and premises, though I would have preferred some more survivalism.

Maybe that's just me, but that is one thing that sticks out for me. However, the game doesn't come without its flaws. While the story is interesting enough, in parts it didn't feel like this was the precursor to the Lara Croft that I am used to seeing. I can understand that liberties were taken, but to me it seems that the writers didn't tie it in that well with the already-existing canon material. Admittedly the development of Lara in this game is okay, and as a reboot I can sort of let it off for the change in direction. But not completely.

Now, the multiplayer. Why oh why does it have multiplayer? The Tomb Raider series has pretty much always been single-player and the multiplayer modes are rather generic ones, which is disappointing. It would have been nice if the multiplayer modes had been a bit more TR-centric, but it felt like generic multiplayer modes with TR backdrops and characters. Again, that's probably me complaining.

[h1]In summary...[/h1]
All in all, this was an enjoyable experience, if slightly bland in places. But this is me coming in as someone who has played the previous games and making comparisons.

Pros:
+ Survivalist style makes sense for this sort of setting.
+ Cinematic experience at times.
+ General story premise was interesting.
+ Lara's character development, if looking at this from a standalone point of view.
+ Weapon customisation adds a certain amount of depth to the gameplay.
+ Controls are relatively easy to get to grips with.
+ RPG elements added but it still feels like an adventure game and not an RPG.

Cons:
- Story can occasionally be bland in places.
- Lara's character development, if considering ALL previous canon material.
- Multiplayer mode feels very tacked on.
- Multiplayer achievements.
- Would have been better with more survival elements.
- NEEDS. MORE. TOMBS.

[h1]To conclude...[/h1]
Whether I recommend this game or not is a difficult choice. As a standalone game it's okay, but as a Tomb Raider game it lacks something that I can't quite put my finger on. For fans of action/advanture games with a survivalist element, I would recommend it. For Tomb Raider fans who have been there since the beginning, I probably wouldn't. There was some enjoyment to be had with the game, yes. It has its merits, but it also has its flaws. I'm going to recommend it on the basis that it's an enjoyable cinematic adventure experience. As aTomb Raider game and a prequel to the old games, it still falls a bit short.

Definitely another Early Access star. Dead Cells is updated often, completely functional and polished (even though it's not content complete). As a 2D game, it's beautifully animated, with great combat mechanics, and very varied enemies. As a rogue-lite, it has a decent random level generator.

One note about the genre/gameplay loop though. Metroidvania seems to be an adjective people like to use to describe Dead Cells. This is completely untrue. Dead Cells is much more akin to Spelunky. It's meant to be completeable from start to end relatively quickly, and player progression comes in the form of unlocking things that you can encounter in later runs. There's no handcrafted map to explore and backtrack through. The few extra abilities you discover during the game are pretty much used only to open up alternate levels. This is very much a Rogue-lite game first and foremost.

Slay the Spire é um jogo que, na data deste overview, ainda está em Acesso Antecipado, mas já tem uma fundação sólida, e recebe updates semanais que, apesar de pequenos, são bem significantes.
O foco de ‘Spire está em seu gameplay dinâmico e com alta rejogabilidade, deixando um pouco de lado a narrativa e ambientação complexas, apesar de nunca negligenciar essas áreas. A narrativa de certa forma existe, mas é abstrata. Os elementos de world building estão ali, mas nada é explicado.
A apresentação é simples mas eficiente, com gráficos 2D bem trabalhados, e uma atenção à detalhes de cenário e animação que vários outros jogos desse estilo não costumam ter. Os efeitos sonoros e música fazem seu trabalho, mas não chegam a se sobressair. A interface e sua usabilidade, por outro lado, ficam melhores a cada novo update. Tudo flui muito bem, há ícones e tooltips para basicamente todos os elementos do jogo, é bem raro ficar perdido ou não conseguir ver alguma informação necessária da partida. Há um ou dois meses atrás haviam alguns problemas, mas aparentemente os desenvolvedores estão de olho na comunidade e arrumando essas coisas! Ainda há alguns poucos glitches, principalmente em relação a resoluções malucas ou modos de janela, mas até hoje nunca presenciei problemas que quebrassem o jogo.
Mas é no gameplay que Slay the Spire realmente brilha, implementando muito bem as dinâmicas vistas em jogos de Deck Building e Rogue-Lites. De forma resumida, o ciclo do jogo é simples: você deve seguir uma série de desafios que são gerados aleatoriamente, até chegar no fim do nível, onde há uma luta com um chefe. As lutas são feitas usando um baralho de cartas que começa fraco, mas entre uma luta e outra você pode conseguir novas cartas para melhorar ele. No meio do caminho também é possível encontrar tesouros, um mercador, e eventos aleatórios que podem ser muito bons, ou nem tanto… E, como quase todo rogue-lite, quando você morre, tem que recomeçar tudo do zero. 
Como nenhum jogo pode agradar todo mundo, é também no gameplay onde o jogo está incomodando mais seus jogadores, como dá pra perceber olhando os fóruns da comunidade na Steam. Muitas pessoas considerado o jogo injusto, muito difícil, e acreditam que se trata de um jogo de pura sorte. Mas isso é uma questão delicada, pois se em partes esses problemas podem, sim, ser erros de balanceamento que vão ser corrigidos ao longo do Acesso Antecipado, algumas características do jogo são deliberadas e realmente podem dividir as opiniões de quem joga. Para cada pessoa pedindo para nerfar uma carta, tem outra respondendo “git gud”...
Em resumo, acredito que Slay the Spire é um jogo que já está num nível de qualidade muito alto, considerando que é um Card Game indie que ainda está em Acesso Antecipado. Ele pode não agradar a todos, mas com certeza foi feito pra quem curte Rogue-Lites viciantes onde não é tão importante ganhar todas as partidas, mas sim aprender novas interações e combos o tempo todo pra se sentir recompensado quando a vitória chega. Pra ser melhor, só precisa de um pouco mais de conteúdo, e talvez um modo multiplayer cooperativo...

Oyunumuz Wildlands (Yaban Topraklar) serisinde de bu özellik var ve daha gelişmiş olarak karşımıza çıkıyor. Ama yapamaya da bilirsiniz, trollük yapıp tüm planı ve taktiği bozan insanlar da gelebilir.

Having full-cleared the achievements and played to high Alpha Mode levels, I can say that this is definitely a great game but also one that will leave you wanting more.  

The gameplay, graphics, introduction and interface are all terrific.  So much more, however, could have been done to improve interactivity with the girls and the dating-sim component of the game.  

Even something simple like 'poking' the girls with your mouse could have elicited some kind of unique response from each, consistent with their sparse but well-defined personalities.  While all the girls are uniquely characterized and memorable, they all share the same basic storyline and the gameplay and strategy is essentially identical for each.  You learn a little bit about the girls through the dozen or so multiple choice Q & A interactions, but there is no interplay between the girls and the Q & A gets repetitive after a while, especially if you do a couple of play-throughs to get all of the achievements.

This game is really begging for some DLC and I am shocked and disappointed there isn't any.  The same girls chasing down the player while s/he keeps them all satisfied using some new scheduling or deception mechanics in connection with the girls' monogamy preferences would have been an easy sell.

Also, it should go without saying, but Nikki = best girl.

---{Graphics}---
This game looks absolutely beautiful, especially the colors, character models, facial expressions and the lighting. The world is beautifully crafted. The graphics hold up pretty good compared to 2020 standards, the only thing that bothers me sometimes is low quality textures on objects e.g. crates, but there is a good mod that can improve this.

---{Gameplay}---
There is a giant amount of content, at the time that I'm writing this review, I've just beaten the main game (I've done a lot of sidequests too). There are a lot of epic moments in this game but sometimes the game can be a bit boring, for example, in a lot of the quests you have to do the same thing such as finding something, following something, slaying a monster. This isn't that big of a problem because the majority of the quests are exciting and unique. there is a ton of different things to explore in this beautiful world. Controls on the other hand... Combat can be a bit stiff, your horse feels unresponsive and it feels like Geralt is walking on ice when you stop moving.

---{Audio}---
This is some of the best voice acting I've seen in video games. The voice acting usually suits the characters and you can feel the emotion in their voices. The sound effects sound pretty good. The sound track is an absolute banger.

---{PC Requirements}---
This game is probably one of the best optimized video games (as long as you turn nvidia hairworks off), ubisoft can learn something from CD Projekt Red. I can run high settings with roughly 60fps on a 1050ti, 8gb single channel ram and an i5-7400.

---{Difficulity}---
The game was pretty easy for me, I played on the second hardest difficulty with enemy upscaling on. I could set the game to the hardest difficulty but I'm not the type that likes using potions and blade oils etc. If you don't like a game to be too easy for you then I'd recommend to just set it to the hardest difficulty.

---{Story}---
Straight up the best story in a video game. 10/10. Even a lot of sidequests are immersive and have a good story.

---{Game Time}---
If you don't like long games, then I unfortunately can't recommend the witcher 3. It will take you arround 50 hours to complete the main story and a few sidequests. Completing the game 100% takes arround 150 hours. But if you do like long games, then this game is perfect for you.

---{Price}---
It feels like you steal from the developers.

---{Bugs}---
There are quite a few annoying bugs such as not being able to swing your sword, not being able to summon your horse and just some visual bugs, but a quick reload of your save will fix them. The bugs don't ruin the game for me since everything else in the game is soooo amazing.

自从上古卷轴5在2011年发行以来已经过了五年，但是在这个时间我还是要完成我的测评，只是为了所有接触了或者想要接触它的玩家负责。如果光是谈到它对我的影响，那么可以说这是信仰级的。这并不是我第一个接触的沙盒类rpg，但的确是我最钟爱的。

那么就讨论到上古卷轴为何这么受到我的推崇。想必b社发布的steam原版老滚能免费获得高清版的消息已经众所周知。虽然对于pc版来说，材质包什么的全部打上或许比高清版都要更为耐看，但就诚意上来说b设的确是无可挑剔的。隔壁r星的gtaol服务器基本因为无脑封获得了一大批差评，育碧和卡婊又是明目张胆，无人不知的奸商。目前在游戏界这样良心的游戏大厂商真的不多了。我知道很多人对辐射4的制作有很多不满，的确，这么久的投入在辐射4里没有达到支持者的预期是b社的一大失误。但是就态度上，就诚意上，我们永远都可以看到b社真正做到好的地方。即使是辐射4，也依然有亮眼的地方。


讨论完厂商的业界良心，我们来具体说一说这个游戏的优劣


优点
1.自成庞大地图，有沙盒游戏最追求的探索空间。上古卷轴5全地图有成千上万的古墓，洞穴等空间，包括其dlc在内拥有两张主地图。如果光是探索性，上古卷轴5绝对是顶尖级别的。

2.完整合理的剧情，分布各个地域。在全地图的各个地方，你都有机会触发各种各样的剧情。小剧情零碎繁多，主线剧情庞大完整，主要支线剧情也是可玩度极高。在剧情方面，上古卷轴5绝对是不输给其他类型的rpg。

3.背景庞大，可探索性高。从初代的上古卷轴开始，b社就建立了庞大的世界观。不仅从主线，支线等剧情你可以深入了解这个世界。另外，各种各样的书籍秘籍都有上古卷轴设定的相关记载，让你体会到一个完整恍若真实的奈恩星。

4.元素众多，可选性强，真正的无拘无束。在其他的rpg中，一般你在游戏前就已经设定好人物的职业，技能等等，从而决定了你接下来的游戏步伐。但是上古卷轴5中，将不会给你任何的设定。所有的技能都由你来选择。当你练习弓箭高的时候，你很有可能成为弓箭手；当你单手武器厉害的时候，你就能自行点高这科技能树。没错，现实中不会有设定这种死板的东西，你的成长都源自于你的锻炼和强化，仅此而已。

5.mod多，可开发性强。上古卷轴也一直以mod而出名，他的不足，例如画质什么的也都可以由mod来补足。在有mod的下的上古卷轴，基本上可以说是无所不能。

缺点
1.即使是所谓的无所不能，但是这个游戏的战斗系统并不会如何出色。毕竟是沙盒类型的rpg，上古卷轴的战斗系统在初学者眼里简直是无法游戏。即使是mod，也没有什么能完全修改他的战斗系统的。因为上古卷轴没有手脚什么的判定，因此战斗中肢体等元素基本上是。。

2.mod对于新手稍有困难。mod的确几乎万能，但为了装上mod，新手起码要过一个月才能了解完所有的mod运行原理，冲突原因等等。这导致很多人开始时就放弃了，也丢失了上古卷轴最重要的游戏元素。

3.部分地图环境昏暗或者过大，让人无法苦不堪言。这个，也就三四个地图是这样的，其实好好跟着指引的话还是能够走出去的。


上古卷轴5是我觉得最近乎完美的沙盒游戏，无论是自由度还是任务链，都让人无法挑剔。mod也补足了游戏要素和画质等问题。为了我们的信仰，在我们期待上古卷轴6的时候，也珍惜当下吧。或许有很多人不屑于花钱买游戏，或者单机游戏。但是在steam上面的诸位应该不会有太多人持这种看法。大家都是为了自己真正热爱的游戏而来，是为了支持我们最喜欢的游戏，让它之后的续作更为惊艳。

There's so much I love about this game, and so much praise it deserves. Ultimately, I can't in all honesty recommend this game because of many broken aspects (mostly due to PC port) and that this game is ultimately a major step backwards for FROM Software in terms of not learning lessons from their previous titles.

FROM Software games have a well-earned reputation for being "tough, but fair", and while this tends to be exaggerated by many, I tend to agree overall with this sentiment. These games don't apologize for their difficulty, and their difficulty can be overcome with patience, learning, skill, and a bit of luck. Unfortunately, Sekiro betrays this entire formula. Granted, it's NOT in any way a Dark Souls game, and while that is a major lesson for a lot of people in terms of how to play the game after years of learning how to play Dark Souls, there's still a problem that goes beyond learning curve.

This is hard to simplify, but I'll try. Do you remember playing Guitar Hero back in the day? Remember when, to keep up with modern televisions and the delay of wireless controllers, they implemented an option about the sound and visual delay so that the screen would prompt your button hits around the same time the audio would prompt you to hit the button? Okay, well that is Sekiro. It's not an action RPG in the way that Dark Souls is, but rather a pure Action Platformer with a Rhythm game element for the battle system. Except in Sekiro, the Rhythm section is always off due to delays in both the game engine, and the computer.

Now, I'll admit that for the first 30 hours of playtime, this problem was my own fault. I thought I was just terrible at the game and realized after a LOT of trial and error, that the game was running at ~25-28 FPS. It's one of those things that is hard to realize until you fix it. The game looks beautiful and seems like it's running fine, but when I decided on a whim to lower the resolution (which shouldn't have been necessary when my computer is top of the line), the game suddenly ran way faster and I realized I was learning the game on a MAJOR delay. At full speed, the game seemed much easier after playing it in "broken hard mode", but even at full speed, there's several elements, particularly in the boss battles, where there's a noticeable delay that turns boss battles from "learn, practice, and overcome" to "cheese because the intended system doesn't work and just pray that you can trigger the boss to do the one move that allows you to respond over and over and over".

Let's go back to that Guitar Hero analogy for a second. You remember how frustrating it was when the visuals and sound were off by 2 or 3 frames per second, right? Suddenly, every note you play misses, and you end up learning to play ahead of the music because of the delay. Okay, now apply that to the rhythm in a Sekiro battle, except there's no notes (or in the case of Sekiro I guess the term would be 'prompts'), the notes are invisible, and if you miss ANY note in a song you lose and have to start over. That's the problem. It's like trying to learn a song that's in 4/4 but it's being played in 5/7 so you're never exactly on and the game will tell you it's YOUR fault.

There's so much to love about this game. It's gorgeous, it's ambitious, it's (overall) pretty fun. But it's so broken and so lacking as far as FROM Software game goes, that it's hard to recommend it. It has an extremely weak story compared to what we're used to from their previous titles (it's completely predictable start to finish), the characters are completely one-dimensional, the music is boring and repetitive, and then the gameplay punishes you for it's own mistakes.

If this is your first FROM Software game, I hope you aren't discouraged, Go try the Dark Souls series. They blow this game out of the water, and you'll see from the instant you start playing why this game is garbage in comparison.

Civilization is a series that holds a very dear place in my heart. I was extremely sick for the better part of two years and couldn't work. I didn't have internet or transportation. All I had was a macbook. I had heard about Civ but had never given it a shot, so I managed to get myself to McDonalds and pirate Civ V (I have since bought it, and every other Civ available). and was swept away with it. The immersion and replayability caused me to put countless hours into it, and made life somewhat bearable. Civilization saved my life

Civilization VI is a great successor to V, bringing a lot of the mechanics that worked and building upon them significantly but still maintaining it's own identity. Small things really give it charm, like the map being in an old style that evolves as you advance through the ages, to the small anecdotes from Boramir/Ned Stark (Sean Bean) Out of all the Civ games this one is definitely the most new-player friendly. Make sure to put aside a good chunk of time to play, a single campaign can take between 6-18 hours (depending on what speed you play at)

If you're new to 4X Strategy games and want to dip your toes in, this is the one to play. It's definitely the most user/noob-friendly one out there with a more limited and concise management system. Once you do check it out, I'd suggest trying out Civ IV and V. Each Civ game has it's own unique personality and style of gameplay, and each one shines in it's own way.

Man I was so excited for this game when it was announced. I loved the marketing for it. How it was set to release just shortly after E3 2015, after the first time ever Bethesda conference of E3. 

I woke up about 2 hours early, because I had a course to take for firearms, just so I could boot up this game and get a little playtime in. After spending probably an hour in the character creator, I realized that my character, despite a long time of editing, looks very close to the generic "Nate" face. This is kind of disappointing because I tweaked every possible thing, apart from hair color.

Seems to me the male models look relatively close in this game. I really don't like how everyone in the game is basically the same height. I understand average, but only the super mutants are towering over you (if you consider them human enough to compare heights)

The gunplay is definitely better than all of the previous "FPS" Fallout games, with notably better animations and behaviours (recoil, hit detection, hit response from enemies). Not a huge fan of the sounds though. Most weapons sound fairly generic. 

Combat really just varies to the difficulty you play on. Difficulty will determine if you play like a soldier in Call of Duty or like a slower and slightly more tactical version of Call of Duty. Not because the enemies deal lots of damage, or because you are being overwhelmed, but because of the survival save system. Do you remember the last time you fell asleep in game? Do you check your gamesaves to realize you have not slept in 30 minutes or more? Then not engaging in combat is the best strategy for you. I find that that mechanic is more of a gimmick (pointlessly harder), to  make a game that should always allow quicksaving/autosaving/manual saving. Every other difficulty is designed with function in mind, so why isn't survival?Because it needs to be more "immersive." As if you can save IRL, but whatever.

Enemies behave somewhat decently. Lot of them spend time peaking around a corner to line up a shot, then just empty their mag or, after a pre-determined amount of ammunition fired, go back into cover. Makes the combat more and more stale and not fluid, which becomes a problem as you continue to play the game. On higher difficulties be prepared for the grenade spam. It's a really cheap tactic to flush you out of cover and almost guarantee some damage to the player.

The settlement mechanic is a really good idea, just implemented in this game with mediocrity. There was a ton of potential for it, but of course it has to tedious. The idea of everything having some form of value is just a fancy way of saying; "you must loot everything, because you need crafting/building materials." The "snapping" functionality in this game is all over the place. Sometimes it goes where you want it to go. Lots of the times it rotated the object to snap it. Lots of times objects clip into eachother, showing you a horrid mess of textures fighting to be visible on screen. Settler management works okay, lots of times they are not working the stores if you fast travel back home. 

The varieties between the factions/races/species of enemies are very low. "Legendary" enemies just glow, have more stats and reset their health when near death. I would be okay with the health reset mechanic if you could "1 shot" them. You can't so it's unavoidable. Upon "mutation" (glows more red but with some cheap and almost B grade anime fire effect) they typically lose all sense of intelligence and often rush the player. This is really scary when you have low levels in damage perks, but after you get 3 or more (+60% damage) stars (representing a level of a perk) to a perk, it doesn't become much of a problem. This is even more true when you luck out and find some good gear early on, or, if you are a veteran of the wastes and have found some loot in your travels. Still mostly RNG but there are some pre-determined drops in the game.

Looting has been vastly improved in this game. With the loot menus being able to be accessed without pausing the game. But what's even better is that it still gives you the option to pause the game and examine the inventory of your fallen foe. Legendary enemies drop "legendary" items which is cool, but there are obvious and immediately apparent legendary effects that are vastly superior to others. For example, there is a perk that does +50% damage to animals. Including DLC's this affects 10 animals in the game. 3 of which are not hostile, 1 is neutral (doesn't usually attack you) and the remaining 6 are hostile. Then we have a legendary effect that increases your damage with each consecutive hit (on that target) by 15%. I don't know about you, but the legendaries in this game sound like another level of RNG that doesn't really need to be in games. The RNG in this game makes it mildly more interesting at best.

The story is about the expected Fallout by Bethesda quality. The ending(s) are not as good as previous Fallout games, because they don't give you a full picture of what happened. I am pretty sure most of the side content (not mainquest) is superior to the actual main quest. Your choices only effect what enemies and what allies are spawning in the end game content. 

End game is pretty lame in vanilla Fallout 4. Once you hit level 50, enemies get their min level increased, more of them spawn in the Commonwealth and you find what I like to call "roaming packs" of enemies. Basically a ton of false difficulty scaling. Just because they all behave the same, have a higher health pool and deal more damage does not make them harder. It turns a bullet spunge into a more lethal, larger bullet spunge. Bullet spunge density is based off of difficulty. I understand that this is an RPG with FPS (or TPS) mechanics, but my immersion breaks when I fire 300+ rounds (some enemies on survival post level 50 take several drums of minigun ammo to kill) into some dude (not in heavy armor, just was a raider with a level that was around 50), with a 5mm round (noted for having roughly 1/3 the joules of 5.56 ammuniton in real life). This is really comical when I use a weapon chambered in 5.56 and it only takes 10 ish rounds to kill him.

Graphics are nothing special for the year it was released, especially compared to the new DOOM, which came out 6 months later, with much better system performance. The godrays still have pixelation, despite this game being out for over 2 years. The water and volumetric lighting is much, much better than previous Fallout games. 

This game runs okay vanilla. There are some mods that may help performance (most of which are out of date, more on that later). Some mods may break the games performances or have frame cliffs, because drops are not enough. The game has some horrid load times, considering that you're going into a pre-rendered worldspace (interiors). The "Mass Effect elevator" makes many appearances in this game. 

The RPG elements (such as lower intelligence) regarding dialogue in this game have been dumbed down. This was done so that the main characters could have their own voice. I was excited thinking that they would have tons of lines of dialogue and really cool interactions. Instead, the buttons are almost dedicated to either being sarcastic, agreeing on doing something, disagreeing or asking for something (more caps/questions about what you're doing usually). Sometimes these options are swapped out for being a dick, being a little bit of a dick or being nice. Come to think of it, the main characters having dialogue pad out a small percentage of the game. I would wager (assuming you are doing lots of quests) roughly 4-5%. This number might be higher or lower based on how fast you select an option, if you skip it and the length of said dialogue.

Post-COD Blackout Beta Update:

Bluehole/PUBG Corp have had a year or more to address substantive issues with their engine, netcode and the game overall.

They took that time instead to focus developer resources on lootbox integration, attempts at e-sports tournaments and prizes and, most egregiously, their "battle pass" - a time-limited, paid DLC achievement-hunting mode that ultimately rewarded very few permanent unlocks.

They have now started a PR push behind their "Fix PUBG" roadmap. This, they claim, is their addressing concerns players have had with the game and improving PUBG overall. The tone of the FixPUBG page reads as if these issues are relatively recent, as if players haven't had the same concerns since Beta. It says a lot that their end date for these fixes is late October - when COD releases.

Frankly, they are getting around to substantive fixes now only because COD and Battlefield's battle royale modes are coming very soon and PUBG/Bluehole is in real danger of losing a lot of their playerbase.

Everything about this company points to a conscious decision to extract as much money from their playerbase as possible, as quickly as possible. Everything I have played of the COD BR beta points to it being in almost every possible way a superior product. The improvements to the PUBG UI/UX and the current improvements to load times and some behind the scenes performance are appreciated. But I have little doubt that the big ticket server/client issues will not be done on time. In fact, given their past performance I'm doubtful we'll ever even see them.

Unforunately, the game never stopped being a buggy, inconsistent, horribly performing mess. One had to fight the game to find the fun (but when you did, it could offer some truly memorable gaming moments). Bluehole/PUBG Corp, it is fair to say at this point, either could not figure out or chose not to invest in making their game technically better - better system performance, netcode, anti-cheat etc. and the game to this day is a frustrating experience almost every time you play it.

The new Call of Duty launches in less than a month of this updated review. Except for those people who are devoted to PUBG or in markets where options are limited, I simply cannot see this game's playerbase doing anything but cratering after COD releases. Even if you tradtionally hate call of duty, it is an undeniable fact that a first-look beta for their BR product performed and looked better than PUBG ever has.

If you somehow find this review and haven't tried PUBG yet, save your money and go play COD Blackout. Or Fornite. Or even PUBG mobile. This company doesn't deserve your money and in six months I anticipate you'll have much fewer people online to play with anyway.

The game is in Early Access so bugs and jankiness are to be expected. That's not what the negative review is for.

I cannot recommend this game after the lead developer stated explicitly there would be no paid DLC/cosmetic content during the early access period. Then, when the devs changed their minds about keeping that promise, handed out the pathetic excuse that they, "needed to test the loot crate system before it went live in the retail release."

Despite already having said they were introducing the paid crate system to fund a prize pool for the first PUBG esports event.

Despite there being no reason to need to charge real money for keys or crates in order to simply "test" the system.

Despite the mountain of actual bugs and features still needing work well in advance of allocating manpower to implementing a microtransaction system for cosmetics.

The game itself is equal parts pure frustration and hardcore test of skill. You will be shot from nowhere by people you had no chance of ever seeing. You will experience your bullets just not hit the other person and then get destroyed (thanks in part to calculations being done client-side). You will wonder about the hitboxes. You'll question why your "good" PC is chugging so hard.

But then you and your squad will launch a Dacia onto the roof of a house from the opposing hill, you'll pile out of the car and murder the guys on the ground below you who didnt' have a chance of reacting to your 1/100 stunt and everyone will laugh. Siege is a must buy for those people that like tactical shooters. It fearues 5v5 PvP multiplayer with an addition of a coop with you and 4 other people in which you probably won't spend too much time since the game shines in PvP. 

Each gamemode has an attacking and defending team, only the ultimate objective is different depending on the gamemode. The attacking and defending sides have their own operators, both sides have 13 operators each for now which means that in total there are 26 unique operators in the game and 2 more to come in a few months.

The biggest pro of the game is the somewhat destructable enviroment. By that I mean that some walls can be breached, some walls only partially breached while others are impenetrable. The same goes for floors and ceilings. 

The gameplay is extremely fun, switching constantly from slow paced to fast paced when the bullets start flying your way. The feeling of shooting guns is on point, when you kill someone you "feel" the feedback of the shot ifthat makes sense.

The game is best played with a communicative team that take operators that build on each other forming a synergy and luckily there are enough people in the community that do communicate and if you can't get a good team in the matchmaker then reddit has you covered on r/rainbow6. 

All operators in the game have an operator when together shine. A perfect example is Thatcher and Thermite. Thatcher has EMP grenades which can knock out jammers while Thermite has a thermite breach charge which can breach fortified walls.

There are currently 13 maps with one more on the way and map knowledge is essential in this game! It is recommended that you practice on casual way after you unlock ranked multiplayer (which you unlock at lvl 20) just so you can memorise all the angles where you or someone else can get a cheeky kill.

A good headset is a must for this game since you will be communicating with your team alot and there will be situations in the game where you will be the only one left and judging the direction of the sound will be paramount if you want to stay alive.

Now, the game is far from polished. Hitreg needs much work as the hitreg lags a bit behind the character model and basically that is my only major gripe with the game - the hitreg. I can't think of anything else at the moment. Ubi says it's their top priority now and allegedly, it will be fixed in the upcoming DLC (which is free as all DLCs in this game are) which is suppouse to go live in Novemeber or December. 

Anyhow, I wholeheartedly recommend this game for people that love tactical shooters, this is the next best tactical shooter since SWAT 4 minus the singleplayer.

With the release of 1.0, this marks the completion of a 15 year old project. Black Mesa is a reimagining of Valve's classic, Half-Life. It recreates the entire game in Half-Life 2's Source Engine with assets created specifically for this title. It stays faithful to the original game where it needs to and changes it up when it's appropriate. A couple of examples would be On a Rail and the entirety of Xen. On a Rail is considered one of the worst chapters in Half-Life mostly due to it being too drawn out. Black Mesa shortens it to a much more enjoyable section and makes it bearable. Xen is the opposite. It's considered one of the lows of Half-Life as well, but for different reasons. Black Mesa extended Xen to be at least a fourth of the game and completely reimagined it from the ground up, adding new story telling, puzzles, and revamped graphics, which are stunning. If you are the type who struggles to get into older games, Black Mesa is the best way for you to experience the glory of Half-Life.

[b]Deep Rock Galactic[/b]  es un juego de minería enana cooperativa. El adjetivo ‘enana’ es relevante pues sí, somos enanos mineros. Este hecho, que podría ser un simple detalle, aporta bastante diversión al juego a la vez que unas cuantas palabras malsonantes y divertidas. Pero, si nos centramos más en lo técnico, en Deep Rock Galactic tendremos diferentes misiones relacionadas con la minería, exploración, rescate y, en general, todo lo que se pueda hacer en una cueva.

El juego consta de 4 clases diferentes: ingeniero, artillero, explorador y perforador. Cada uno posee diferentes características que facilitarán la tarea de minar si se usa en combinación con tus amigos o entre los miles de usuarios que hay a diario en el juego (¡y eso que aún no había salido oficialmente!). Como ingeniero podremos colocar torretas y plataformas; el artillero contará con un lanzallamas para abrasar a esos enemigos; el explorador se encargará de iluminar nuestro camino; y el perforador contará con una útil herramienta para abrir el paso por las rocas.

Quizás la magia de este juego es que nunca tienes esa sensación de que estás repitiendo lo mismo veinte veces. Esto se da también por las diferentes regiones planetarias que muestran diferentes características y diferentes enemigos. Por ejemplo puedes enfrentarte a enemigos de magma en un mapa y en el siguiente a enemigos de hielo que te congelarán. Pero el peligro no está solo en los enemigos sino que también en el propio entorno.

[h1] Bomber Crew is great. Brilliant cartoony art style yet still manages to have tense moments when what seems like the whole goddamn Luftwaffe is chasing you and your plane is being held together by sticky tape and dreams. [/h1]

The progression system is good and you'll get really attached to your plane. Crew management is a huge part of the game. Every crew member is vital and you'll constantly have to move them around the bomber too keep your plane in the air. Sometimes you'll have to make the decision between saving a crew member or returning fire on the German fighters. This really brings out the most tense moments.

One criticism I have is that once you get the later stages in the game you won't be able to go straight into attacking the stage boss because your bomber won't be well enough upgraded. To get enough money to upgrade your plane the required amount you have to grind through the simple missions like [i] Bomb the enemy tank factory [/i], [i] Stop enemy Doodlebug launches [/i] or [i] Bomb the enemy U-Boats [/i]. But after there tenth time of bomb the factory you'll end up just messing with the special moves which will get you killed purely because your so bored. In my opinion they should have added more simple missions. But in the long term this doesn't really make a huge impact on your gaming experience. NOTE- This isn't a problem anymore as they have added more simple missions.

I'm not going to talk about the DLC because I haven't spent much time with it but it seems to add enough to be worth a purchase.
You should also note that even if your not overly into flight simulation this game isn't too heavy on simulation so it doesn't require a huge amount of knowledge in aircraft it's definitely more focused on an arcade style of play.

Overall, with this Summer Sale offer you can get Bomber Crew for an absolute steal of €5.
Just a brilliant game in total and even if it isn't on sale you should definitely add this to your Steam library.

However, (and you've already seen this i'm sure) the story, characters, lore are bad...especially if you loved previous borderlands stuff. There is little connection to previous stories foreshadowing and the story is overall boring and disjointed.
Compared, to previous Borderlands this game feels...sanitized. Most of the crazy erratic character of the previous games is gone, and the game feels almost pandering in its place.
One additional point is I also feel the level design is poor. Most areas have a very linear feel to them and there is rarely anything interesting off the beaten path. 
All that being said, the gameplay totally makes this game worth it. The new Vault Hunters have really fun abilities to play the game through with and the gunplay is even better than previous games.

This review is in direct response to the recent 2.4 update.

Half a year, and still no significant content updates yet. In a world where the most popular games are usually constantly evolving, a semi-competitive multiplayer game like Hunt: Showdown really suffers from a lack of replayability. Sure, I can level a hunter up for hours over and over again, but in the end, the mobs are all mindlessly easy to kill if you can aim better than a one-armed man, you run around to different waypoints without interacting with them in any way, find the bounty and kite it to death, defend the bounty from other hunters until you can collect it, then run off the side of the map with the bounty.

The mobs are so insignificant that even though they can spawn in different ways, it really doesn't impact gameplay. The waypoints/hints spawn in pretty much the same places and don't require you to do anything but find them. The Butcher is laughably easy to kite, and the Spider, while dangerous solo, can be dealt with by just running in and out of the building repeatedly. Defending the bounty is actually genuinely exciting if other Hunters show up, because the gunplay in this game is phenomenal. Usually, if you have a brain, and the other players don't have incredibly long range guns, running to the edge of the map is trivial, and defending yourself while escaping on the boat/stage coach is also typically pretty easy since the timer is so short.

The great gunplay isn't what makes Hunt: Showdown Hunt: Showdown. If you want good gunplay, you play a well-made first person shooter. You play Hunt: Showdown because it's a clever PvPvE formula that has multiple working parts to keep games non-linear. Unfortunately if the content in the game remains consistent for long periods of time, and the existing dynamic content can either be ignored or imposes little impact on the player when changing, the game becomes linear. The only things that are truly a wild-card in this game are the other players. At which point it just becomes a decent first person shooter with a relatively trivial objective.

I know this is more of a complaint about the way the game's development has been going, rather than an actual review, but seeing this patch when I got on today made me realize that I'm probably never going to enjoy this game enough to actually purchase a copy for my account. And that makes me sad, because I did truly have fun the times that I did play the game, but after I was done playing, I had no desire to go back and play more unless given a reason. Which is why I thought I'd put this here, in order to provoke you other steam users into asking the same questions I am. It's no secret Hunt: Showdown is struggling, given the recent f2p period, and I strongly believe that this is why. Aside, of course, from the large quantity of inconsistent playability problems some players are having.

Overall, I can 100% recommend playing this game. It's fun. I can't, however, recommend purchasing it for 30$. Unless you become addicted to it in some way and play it far more than it's worth, you won't get 30$ out of it. This might change after it leaves Early Access, but the stagnance I've seen so far does not leave me hopeful.

Side note: What the hell did they do this patch that fixed playability problems for a bunch of players that had them, and then also created playability issues for a bunch of other players that DIDN'T have them?

[h1]Overview[/h1]
[b]Black Mesa[/b] is a remake of the legendary FPS Half Life 1. Crowbar Collective took a very long time in rebuilding and improving the first chapter in Doctor Freeman's saga - and the result is extraordinary. In this game players will impersonate Gordon Freeman, assigned to work at the Black Mesa Facility as a researcher. An highly classified experiment goes wrong, tearing the very fabric of space and beginning a series of events with unimaginable consequences. 

🟩 [b]Pros[/b]
[list]
[*]An incredible remake: almost everything was remade from scratch or improved - HL1 never looked better.
[*]Excellent combat featuring interesting weapons, good enemy variety and great gunplay.
[*]Plenty of secrets and Easter eggs to discover, on top of amazing level design.
[*]Good variety of enemies and well designed boss fights.
[*]Great gameplay variety that alternates combat, exploration and puzzles (mostly) with the right pacing.
[*]Native modding support with Workshop integration.
[/list]
🟥 [b]Cons[/b]
[list]
[*]The "Interloper" chapter in Xen drags on too much, with uninspired filler puzzles and repetitive fights.
[*]Anti-aliasing doesn't work properly.
[/list]
[h3]Rating: Excellent[/h3]
[url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1989090445]Click here for the complete Rating Chart[/url]

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2038543627

Let's start with the many good sides of this incredible remake. First of all the complete overhaul of every HL1 section is stunning: texture, lighting, physics, animations, everything improved by a magnitude. This is even more impressive considering they used Source 1 engine - pushed at its technical limits. Combat feels meaty and satisfying with very good feedback on hits, well done weapon feeling, smart enemy AI that actively dodges and uses cover, grenades. 

Each level improves on the already great design of the original, with a myriad of secret areas and Easter eggs to find, some minor while other much greater. Exploration is rewarded constantly with additional resources and weapons. Enemy variety goes from classic headcrab zombies to military vehicles and plenty of exotic creatures from other dimensions - each with their own attack patterns and behaviors. Gameplay pacing is a masterpiece, as the alternation of puzzles, exploration and combat is done almost always in a flawless way. 

For the bad parts, Interloper, the final Xen chapter before the final boss, has been reworked for the worse, as it lasts considerably longer than the original and plays out much slower - with repetitive puzzle styles and enemies that soon get stale, in contrast to what seen before. It is a stain on an otherwise perfect remake. On another side note, the antialiasing doesn't seem to work properly, and it can be annoying.

[b]Overall Black Mesa is an amazing remake of an already legendary title, getting almost everything right but not without a few dents. It took me 15 hours to complete the game while being thorough in exploring - for the default price of 18€ and great overall quality, I can definitely recommend this game for full price.[/b]

[h1]In-Depth Breakdown[/h1]
🎮 [b]Gameplay Analysis[/b]
Gameplay is divided into Exploration, Combat and Puzzles.

[b]Exploration[/b]
Is performed on foot mostly, sometimes driving utility vehicles on rails, and later on with the aid of a jetpack allowing longer jumps. Despite being an FPS, exploration is actually the primary activity in Half Life and combines integrally with puzzles. Each level has plenty of side areas hiding secrets, Easter eggs or even items to obtain secret endings. Be prepared to some degree of platforming and jumps sometimes.

Exploring is very interesting because there is no explanation of the unfolding events outside of some dialogues, so from the environment players will have to understand things for themselves. Level design is sprawling and vertical, makes large use of ducts, passageways and physics to open up new paths in a realistic way consistently.

[b]Combat[/b]
Is not as fast paced as other FPS, but is equally interesting thanks to the realistic approach it has. Weapons all feel very diverse and "heavy", turning enemies into minced meat in case of high calibers or explosives - as it should be - and generally taking a realistic amount of shots to kill all but the most armored enemies. AI of opposing forces is excellent, especially regarding sentient enemies which use cover, suppression fire and grenades constantly to draw you out or flank. 

Boss fights rather than being a "classic bullet sponge" are instead different, often being multi-phased and tied to other actions to perform, sometimes elsewhere in the same level. Of course there also are classic arena bosses, namely the final boss being the prime example of this. They are not many but all very interesting and well done.

[b]Puzzles[/b]
Are varied and present throughout the adventure. Some are small-time things such as finding a spare part to activate machinery, while others span several areas and are much longer to finish. None of the puzzles is overly complex in the sense of difficulty but rather they want to make players feel like they accomplished something with a prolonged effort, and they hit the mark here. A pity the puzzles in the Interloper chapter are repetitive and boring.

[u]PC Specs: RTX2080Ti, Ryzen 3900X, 32GB RAM DDR4[/u]
There are no major issues or bugs to report. Menu interface can rarely bug and prevent the menu from displaying again, forcing a game restart to fix. Resolution reverts to monitor native each time the game is started, if it was set to a higher one for downsampling. The game runs well in 4K, 60FPS and thanks to the high scalability of the engine, good optimization, it should run also on older systems without trouble. 

[h1]Final Thoughts[/h1]
An amazing remake of one of the most iconic FPS in gaming history. A sure-fire purchase for Half Life fans, while also a great place for getting started with the series for those interested.
