// BeamNG.drive is a 3D Racing Simulator: //
// Schuitje82 - Extended Review //

When I made this review the game had been released in Early Access.
There is no influence from the maker due to a free key or any other reasons.

Title: BeamNG.drive
Genre: Race, Simulator,
Developer: BeamNG 	
Release date: 29 mei 2015 (Early Access)


Why I wanted it, and maybe you will too?
===============================
Personally I love race / car simulator video games.
If it's a racing game like Forza or a Sandbox simulator I want to play them all.
I've watched some movies and reviews about this game and wanted to know for myself what this game is all about.
Yes it's a simulator and oh yeah.... you can crash your car and it’sreally AWESOME!
Still, I wanted to try it myself and make a review about it.


Core Gameplay:
============
This is a pure simulator, so if you are looking for a racing game, maybe this is also something for you.
You have some different modes to choose from, like Scenarios such as Freeroaming.
Scenarios are  for the people who like to have a goal while they play around with the simulator.
I must say there are really very many modes made for you to try.
For example: Road Race, Jumps, Full Circuit Racing, Rally Croos Long Courses, Destruction Derby (multiplayer) and much more!
The Free roaming is really cool for the player who likes to drive around the levels the Dev's made for us.
You can choose already from 10 massive levels that you can drive and play through with all the cars that are ready to pickup from the car list.
If you think, “What kind of levels?’ for example:
You can choose from giant cliff, Derby Arena, Small Island, USA; and East Cost, USA as a Raceway to go high speed.
So these modes give you many hours of fun and in the future they will add campaigns for more ways to play.
Last option and I think the coolest is the "Add Content" option.
What makes this game really cool is that you can add your own levels and mods to it that other people have built for us.
Check the MOD section on the online website to see all the crazy and cool things other people have made for this awesome game.

http://www.beamng.com/resources/?ingame=2

I geot excited after every page seeing what all people have made for this great sanbox simulator !!


Graphics:
========
The first thing that makes this a nice simulator is the graphical part. (In my opinion.)
Everything looks really amazing and that was the first thing i noticed about the game that made me want to try it.
Not only the roads, but even the tree's a looking amazing. What appeals to me most is the car detail!
For example the car interior, engine, and everything else looks really amazing,.
aAnd let’s not forget about the damage that can be done to your car!
If you crash into a tree, your car’s hood folds like a piece of paper.
I think they did a really great job with this aspect of the game!
The onOnly thing I think is annoying sometimes: with a small crash even when there isn’t any huge physical damage, your car can get stuck and not be moved / driven.


Controls:
=======
I played the game with my keayboard as well as my Xbox 360 Wireless controller.
I can recommend the controller because you have more feeling with it.
For example, make sure to remember that  when you take a turn, sometimes your car brakes out and with a controller it is much easier to control and recover the car.
I'm happy with the dev's choice for controller support because many games I play in early access does not support this.
The cars feltels really weird in the beginning when I played the game, only after some time did I get used to it.
Every car feels slightly different, which and still makes it fun to play and try every car that I can choosice from.
They did a really good job with the different roads, likeand I mean is whean you go offroad racing.


Multiplayer:
=========
Still this is a early access game, but there are some crazy co-op local co-op things to do.
Like destructiiton derby, that is a lot of fune to play with up to 4 players local.
I hope the Dev's can add online multiplayer modesmode to this, so we can all drive all together!.


Overall:

This a really fun and well madegood and fun Car simulator where  you can have hours of fun!.
TheGame game wais only released infrom 2015 and there are allready so many community mods we can try out!.
It's a nice project with very much potential to it.... so Dev's keep up the good work.

An excellent indie game that's well worth the money. If you don't like hard games then you might want to steer clear, but even as a very difficult game there is plenty to enjoy. The difficulty can be both punishing and forgiving, as you die in one hit, but thankfully the game only restarts you back to the start of the area. The gameplay is fast-paced and suspenseful, keeping you on your toes for the whole game as you attempt to take out all the bad guys in one area without taking a hit. The game forces you to implement some strategy and stealth into the action, making an excellently balanced blend of fun which is surprisingly addictive as you try over and over again to pass the area.

The setting and story also help the game immensely. The Miami setting gives the game a great colour palette to work with, and makes the top-down world look vibrant and safe, a contrast to the actual gameplay. And the story....it's confusing, but done so well as to make you guess what is going on, and allows you to speculate on several things, like the guy who appears in every store you go to after each level, and acts oblivious to the fact. But you know there's something to him.

All in all, Hotline Miami is well worth the $10 pricetag, and you should definitely get it when it's on sale, even if you aren't interested.

幸运的是，我依然看到三上真司的恶灵附身一，Jason West 和 Vince Zampella的泰坦陨落，宫崎老贼的魂，小岛秀夫的死亡搁浅

into the breach
人如其名，突破，玩家所要做的只是一次又一次把自己置身敌众我寡的逆境中并且一次又一次突破，也是突破自己寻找最优解。
作为一款小品SLG，紧凑又精巧，三机五回合64格应付愈发困难应对无法彻底根除的虫群，一次又一次逼迫你去寻找最优解处理残局，更多的时候比起击杀你能做的仅仅只是挪开敌人甚至是把攻击方向改成自己去保护仅存的建筑物；置身逆境寻求突破既是游戏名称也是游戏的核心，玩家绝大多数情况下都是被动的，即便神装就位来势汹汹也仅仅是处于攻势防御罢，随着难度提升你能做到的事情愈发减少，贪图更多的收益成了奢望，万变不离其宗的依然是对综合利益的权衡与抉择，很可能接踵而来的就是满级穿越者机师的生命与最后一节电源之间的电车难题，一切的一切都是基于简单的游戏机制设计的，让人叹服。
与常见的SLG不一样的是，游戏中比拼的数值并不大，而游戏的目的更多的也是保护我方＞歼灭敌方，歼灭这一情况更多的是贪婪的奖励，这就带来了游戏机制上特别讨喜的两点：出于保护＞歼灭的情况游戏以干扰与位移阻挠虫群的攻势为主，而在满足了保护的前提下追求歼灭——游戏中的高伤害往往依托精妙的武器特性连携配合与地形相辅相成而不是单纯的堆砌数字。而保护和歼灭也是可以相结合的，那便是游戏中玩家所追求的利益最大化，也是无数场战斗中突破逆境的，丝血的建筑的护盾能在排挤敌人的同时部署，挪开偷袭研究所的敌人可以堵塞下回合的增援，潮汐与酸液、山脉与裂隙、旧式的军队也好先进的科学船也罢你要做的就是寻找当下他们物尽其用的有机结合。
全成就通关都有两年了，今天才发现这游戏前几个月出官中了，也不知道为什么以前没写过评测，我向来是对紧凑又精巧的游戏无法抗拒，有什么理由让我不给好评呢？
Um bom jogo de sobrevivência, muito enjoativo para quem procura novidade em games desse estilo. Recomendo pra quem quer competitividade e jogabilidade pegada.

Перед нами пазл, ориентированный на физические действия. То есть, не надо решать какие-то математические формулы в уме, вспоминать какие-то древние трактаты с цитатами и пытаться понять, что от нас хочет игра. Всё предельно просто: внимательно осматриваем каждую пядь окружающих предметов, находим другие предметы, применяем найденное в местах для этого предназначенных. Звучит скучно? Как бы не так! Игра интуитивно понятна, что позволяет пройти игру достаточно быстро и при этом почувствовать себя настоящим разгадывателем тайн и невероятных механизмов. Присутствует сюжет. А грамотный русификатор позволяет ещё больше погрузиться в атмосферу.

- графика; она чудесна
- музыка: загадочная, таинственная и периодически гнетущая
- логически правильные головоломки, ориентированные в большинстве своём на внимательность
- цена

划时代的神作。
小说，戏剧，动画，电影，都是不同艺术形式的载体。
而游戏，按照小岛的说法，它不是艺术，而是博物馆，专门陈列艺术。

这个话是小岛的过谦。在我看来，游戏即便是电影化，也还是和电影有所区别。和暴雨/阿兰醒来/底特律变人等真·电影化作品对比来说，游戏与电影最大的区别是，在操作中增加代入感。
为什么死亡搁浅（以下简称DS）发售时两极分化如此严重，因为本作不是立刻就能感受到内涵，也不是靠云游戏感受内涵的作品。它没有视觉的震撼，不像只狼乒乒乓乓拼刀。它是只有你体验过，才能明白的作品。
DS的剧情很简单，但是如果你云游戏看播片通关，你会觉得非常无聊。只有在雪地里送了那么久的货，你才能明白那份困难与孤独。此刻，你就是山姆。
你与山姆一起成长，从一开始对陌生人警惕，到开始原因搭把手，到最后肩负起联系他人的责任。这就是DS赋予我们的意义。

日本人的三途川。
希腊人的冥界。
中国人的黄泉。
DS的冥滩。
其实本作就是个披着科幻皮的神话故事。不过这个科幻世界搭建的能自治，很真实。

The game is just too buggy. The UI is just too painful. I wouldn't even mention it if it was still in EA, but it's supposed to be released.

Examples: 

- You'll frequently speed time forward, only to discover your characters weren't actually working for one reason or another. And the game gives you little to no indication.

- Characters can easily get stuck in a location. This requires you to let them die or start the game over.

- When you have one character running off to town, you get no meaningful indication that your other character is under attack. You frequenly switch back to your base to find you characters dead.

The major problem is that the game has a very unpolished UI. The game is also very grindy (which is good, imo) which necessitates frequent use of the fast-forward triple-speed button. Unfortunately, the game doesn't automatically slow down if you enter combat, someone starts starving, or anything else. It just keeps zipping forward at 3x, frequently resulting in the death of one or more of your characters.

If you're like me, and enjoy playing games on ironman mode (perma-death, no saving except when exiting the game) there is no way you can play the game in the current state without constantly saving the game to avoid frequent game-blocking bugs.

Now compare this with something like RimWorld which went through many iterations of it's notification/warning system to help players understand what was happening to their pawns before it became dire. Kenshi needs that level of attention if it's going to even come close to its full potential.

[b]Kdesi hluboko ve vesmíru..[/b]

[i]Hluboký vesmír. Nestabilní hvězda opodál se chystá k další emisi a vám již hoří nejen centrální ovladač dronů ale i kyslíkový generátor. Nepřátelé, kteří se vám teleportovali na palubu odvedli dobrou práci a teď se pomalu probojovávají k motorům. Jestli se k nim dostanou, je po vás. Generátor jede na poloviční výkon a vy se musíte rozhodnout, jestli necháte v provozu ošetřovnu, ve které se léčí dva členové vaší posádky, nebo zapnete štíty. Rebelská loď opodál už totiž nabíjí ionové kanóny. 
Jste jediná naděje federálního loďstva před rebelskou flotilou a jestli teď selžete, je konec.[/i] 
A to doopravdy. Tahle hra totiž nezná checkpointy ani ukládání pozic. Tahle hra vám nic neodpustí. Jste jen vy a vesmír. A když prohrajete, není návratu. O vašem osudu budou vyprávět jen němé trosky tiše plující vzduchoprázdnem. A vám nezbývá, než to zkusit znovu..a znovu..
Někomu by to mohlo přijít frustrující, obzvláště když dvakrát neletíte stejným vesmírem. Pokaždé potkáte jiné lodě, jiné vybavení, jinou posádku. Takže vaše cesta je určována i náhodou a občas se kazí vše, co se zkazit může. Ale v tom je její kouzlo. Když do toho šlápnete, můžete na konec doletět za pár desítek minut. Ale než se vám jí podaří poprvé dohrát, bude to chtít mnoho pokusů a mnoho nezdarů. Chybami se člověk učí a ve vesmíru to platí dvojnásob.

This review is on both campaign and multiplayer.
I have never bought a COD game in my life but have played a few COD games at friends houses, but until now i have decided to give the new COD ago as i was interested of the game going back to its roots. I will start off my thoughts for the campaign.

The campaign was decently good as it showed what WW2 was like, some of the campaign wasnt historically accurate but i believe the whole purpose of this game was ment to be fun. You play as a soldier named Daniels who volunteers to fight for his country and rid the Nazis from Europe. As you progress through the campaign Daniels begins to see that war was never a easy task, as the war has always been nightmare. I did like the campaign as there was some good and rare funny moments, but the campaign did have some problems. The campaign was short as it is only a 6 hour campaign. Some of the missions had stealth involved which was a bit boring honestly. And some of the missions just went too quick. Overall the campaign was decently good so i give it a 7/10.

To the multiplayer. The multiplayer is pretty fun as it now contains a new mode called War. It also has a thing called headquarters where you gather with other players either have a 1v1 with them, or show off your loot crates that you have collected. The leveling up system is pretty straight forward and you will occasionally get some goodies. Customizing your character, weapons and etc is pretty straight forward as well. And the hardcore modes are just fun. And its not paid to win. Overall multiplayer is decent as well and enjoyable to play most of the time. 7/10

Overall i do enjoy this game alot, the game is very well optimized and its great to play a WW2 game. And i am glad that Activision has heard from their community that they need to go back to their roots. Good game Activision.

I personally reccommend you don't buy No Man's Sky yet! Here is why!

My specs are:
GPU: Geforce GTX 1080
CPU: Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-4770K CPU @ 3.50GHz
24.00 GB RAM 
and I run at a resolution of 1920 x 1080 

I run the game at a good 40-60FPS (I use Vertical Sync) roughly, not only this but it also likes to have these absurd spikes of lag, not to mention it using up 60% sometimes 70% of my CPU depending on the environment, it's crazy. 

I record Let's Play videos on my channel, using OBS Studio to record at a clean 1080p 60fps whilst using another instance of the regular OBS to record my webcam at 1080p, Yet both instances of OBS where having massive trouble recording due to the insanely high CPU usage whilst playing this game, the stuttering became more apparent, and I ended up having to record just the gameplay for a small video I did on the PC version being broken (can be found here!: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8Vw_tKq8_SE ) 

I have played other games that have CPU intensive settings to see how bad it would get, and most of them have come out as around 55-60fps (again with Vertical Sync) with a CPU usage maximum of 40%!! 

All in all, for the game itself, I think it's great if you enjoy exploration, and I think that it's a game that has done a lot of things right, it also looks really beautiful and the atmosphere is amazing, besides performance issues, the only thing that annoys me is I can't find a reset or new save setting!

These performance issues don't do the game justice and it saddens me to admit that, hopefully we will see a patch incoming to make this game generally run smoother for everyone!

app_name: Total War Saga: Thrones of Britannia
review:
Well, being a fan of the TW Series since Medieval 1 and Viking Invasion onwards until todays Thrones of Britannia, I’m not totally disappointed by Thrones of Britannia, but also not really satisfied. It feels like a lot of potential was wasted. (I own all TW games and played them, including Warhammer, just skipped the Shogun titles, since my historical interest is rather eurocentric – I know, nowadays this causes silly outrage in the even more silly academic left *facepalm*) ToB could have been a great game to carry on the TW series, but the devs didn’t care much for in-depth atmosphere and interaction. It plays and feels very limited. Therefore I’d not recommend to buy it at full price. Essentially it’s an updated TW: Attila, nothing new, nothing ground-breaking. At least your girlfriend will appreciate, that you clearly won’t spent countless hours in front of the pc for this rather mediocre game… ;-)

Pros:
[list]
[*] I love the historical setting (it’s subjective, I know, but every review is in the end)
[*] beautiful graphics as usual (strategy map, tactical battle maps, units, etc. - all well done) 
[*] battle AI is ok for “very hard” (it used to be worse in previous titles an, so there is challenge on higher difficulty levels) 
[*] sea battles catch the historic flavor of the timeframe (it’s all about boarding, concrete: it’s a land battle on sea)
[*] a family tree is included (you can arrange marriages, reduce influence of generals and governors and try to convince your family members to be more loyal – there is always a chance, that disloyal ones revolt)
[*] role play elements exist, but are limited - nothing really new, compared to previous TW titles
[*] rival vikings arrive randomly from time to time at the shores of Britain to pillage & plunder
[*] emergent factions exist, the name of your kingdom might also change depending on your conquests (f.e. if you start as Dublin Seaking you might become Irish Vikings and later on Nordic-Gaelic Sea Faction)
[*] (excellent fanbase modding community) in brackets, since this is not really Creative Assembly’s merit
 [/list]

Cons:
[list]
[*] diplomacy sucks as usual (reasonable agreements are very hard to achieve, and as the game goes on and your conquests grow, it becomes impossible to get to terms with the AI via diplomacy)
[*] gameplay feels very restricted and limited (there is f.e. a max. 10 governors cap, why?! seriously? This doesn’t make sense. Just to make the game harder? I’m also not a fan of the very limited building place capabilities in your provinces, which makes every new building a tough choice)
[*] no spies, priests or assassins
[*] religion doesn’t matter much, you also can’t convert provinces f.e. as pagan Viking leader. You might get some penalities, when you decide to stay pagan as Viking, but that's pretty much it.

[h1]Middle-earth™: Shadow of War™, vastly improved and solidified -- is an appropriate next step into the franchise. [/h1]

[u]Introduction:[/u] Quite like it's predecessor, the game provides an role playing experience within the Middle-earth universe. Classical rpg mechanics such as customizable aesthetics through gear and individual character leveling makes this game more like I wanted it to be. [b]Short version of the review can be found at the bottem.[/b]

[u]Customization Options:[/u] Like most games on PC, you will have the ability to customize key bindings and sensitivities, however in comparision to Shadow of Mordor, you now have the ability customize your UI. The UI options are good within themselves, however I would've liked to have each individual aspect of the UI to be disableable -- instead of only being able to disable premeditated "segments" of the UI, regardless, decent option within the game. 

You can't natively alter the field of view within the game, which WB games are notorious for. You can check my guide which shows you an application which allows you to do so -- https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1191922623

[u]Graphics:[/u] The graphics are not mind blowing, but in no way shape or form disappointing. All things from more polygons in models, higher res textures blah blah blah -- you get the picture. Graphical options on the other hand are in order and isn't problematic. 

[u]Gameplay & Mechanics:[/u] [b]Gameplay[/b] is still incredibly repetitive and challengeless, but fun nonetheless. If you understand the system this game uses, you'll know that it's not something which you'll spend hours thinking of how to exploit effectively due to complexity, nor will you spend hours mastering mechanical skill because there is none. The is one very good thing about combat, it's incredibly satisfying, which takes the toll of it's repetitive nature. Everything from the animations, sounds and lore based abilities create an different experience not many games have done before. If anything, one aspect of gameplay which I personally have noticed, is that everything feels very automatic. 

Mechanics on the other hand is an completely different story, new varients of enemies, captain classes with indvidual strengths to change your approach to battle (Yes these changes of strategy are minuscule, while environment is still OP as hell, it's the variation of the experience which is the positive thing). Enemy captains, warchiefs and overlords definately have more personality to them, which is huge for me. Not only does it make the thing you're killing more interesting, it also is an immersive element. 

Exploration now uses the similar system of Witcher III: The Wild Hunt, in which you have main quests, side quests (from this game's perspective and points of interest within multiple sections of maps. While the previous installment has this, the new one has more than double the amount of sectioned maps, slightly smaller, but overall covering way more surface area. 

Gear has now become more advanced and customizable. An leveling system is used according to crates on the market, enemy leveling and level scaling. Challenges have been added to rare, epic and legendary gear, which once complete, allows the player to upgrade their gear to the predestinated level stated in the information section. Gear can also be upgraded with gems, which provides bonuses, which alter depending on two things; the type of gem and the type of loot it is being fused into. Gems also have an progression system which amplifies the effect. 

[u]Microtransactions:[/u] With the gaming industry going to shit, microtranscations within an single player RPG is one symptom of that. I will try to be as least self-rightous as I possibly can be in this next paragragh. Only someone who either likes to waste money or who has an incredibly shallow understanding for this game systematically speaking, would buy any of these microtranscations. If you like to spend time doing captain missions and doing everything on the map, you're going to level significantly faster than those who don't, even if you don't -- main quests provide a lot of XP. 

From an theoretical and realistic persective (I haven't bought any microtranscations), if bought two gold loot crates, granted you'll get very good loot, with exceptional qualities, 10 ish hours later you'll more than likely come accross better gear. Which then comes to my other point, there is an painfully obvious reason why they'd add XP boosts, because the loot system is specifcally designed to work like that so you keep buying crates. 

One good thing that is good about this microtranscation system, it's completely optional. It won't effect your gameplay in the slightest if you don't invest. If you wan't to buy them, go ahead but just remember you're endorsing something which is ruining the industry. 

[u]Story:[/u] I found that the story is more interesting than the previous games, especially when there is more characters and lore from the books directly involved. To some respects there can be small twists, which peak interests but aren't experience changing. I will keep this section short but as an concluion the story definately feels a lot more "Middle-earth" than the last game. 

[u]Concluion:[/u] To conclude this review, I must say that if you did enjoy Shadow of Mordor, you definately will enjoy this game, especially with the more immersive and advanced mechanics that have been added. At full price, totaling at 45 GBP, price for content ratio is good, however because of the repetitive nature, everyone will have an different tolerance to this. If you have assurance that you'll enjoy the game and get your moneys worth, i'd recommend this to you.

"Таааааак, что это такое? Хммм... Хорошая олдскульная графика, куча самых разных и неповторимых боссов, оригинальный геймплей... Дайте две!!! "- примерно так выглядел тот момент, когда среди тонн шлака я наконец нашел годноту! 

Что же можно сказать про эту инди игрулю?

1) Графика. Да, да, да. Вы все правильно поняли. Здесь действительно есть достойный графоний! Картинка очень занимательна тем, что все сделано под самое настоящее ретро. Аля хорошо забытое старое, но только красивее, ибо мне, как ярому фанату всего пиксельного реально понравилось играть именно с такой графикой. Она очень удобная и не колет глаза своей нереалистичностью, да и выглядит в сочетании с видом сверху           по-настоящему красиво, передавая не только детализацию монстров, но и ландшафта в целом.

2) Геймплей. Ну тут в принципе все предельно коротко и ясно. У вас есть аж одна стрела во всем колчане, которую вы можете притягивать обратно (спасибо Темной Силе). Также вы умираете от одного удара, что в общем совершенно логично во время битв с Титанами, ибо это вам не God of War. Благо есть чекпоинты поблизости с боссами. Таким образом, игра получается в меру хардовой. Не слишком казуально, но и нервных срывов быть тоже не должно. Однако, если вы действительно отбитый наглухо человек, то можете попробовать 3 особых режима, дабы призвать второй Чернобыль.

3) Сюжет. Как таковой сюжетной линии в игре не наблюдается. Единственное, что нужно знать, так это, что наш ГГ это еще не воспетый Геракл, которому нужно лишь убить всех Титанов (izi). По-настоящему печалит, что не рассказывается история каждого Титана в отдельности. Мы узнаем лишь общую сущность всех Титанов и то, что мы не первые, кто охотился на них (встретится легендарный рыцарь, перебивший туеву хучу монстров, который впоследствии сам стал титаном). В общем, чтобы пройти игру нам даже не требуется убить всех, но ради дополнительной концовки можно и поднапрячься.

4) Саундтрек. Достаточно просто сказать, что он очень даже неплох. Звучит как раз эпично во время битв и спокойно в остальное время. Слышны самые разнообразные мотивы на разных инструментах. Чувствуется некая атмосфера таинственности и жажда приключений.

В конечном итоге, этот продукт умелых рук получает от меня 9/10 лишь за отсутствие дерева навыков и возможностей торговли, как в тру РПГ.

--Edited, removes some things not relevant any more like Chinese language is finally supported. And oh my God, how good is the Norsca DLC?---
Long Review
I read a lot of reviews about this game and they are usually negative because the reviewer dislikes the DLC policy. Most of the fair reviews are usually positive. This game is far from being perfect but definitely does not deserve all this hate and unfortunately, it’s easier to find correct information in the positive reviews than in the negative.
I’ll try to summarize what I think of the game in a fair way but before I think I should introduce where I’m coming from. I’m not a Warhammer tabletop player (although I’m a big fan) and I like Total War series although haven’t played the latest versions. I love strategic games but when is about history I feel games like Europa Universalis are more my favourite. I was waiting for years to have a strategic fantasy game of this scale and depth. Also, I’m not against DLCs as long as they add content to the game and being a collector I may buy the aesthetic one once in heavy sale.  
And now to the review. Total War Warhammer is the latest installation of the epic strategy wargame series Total War. The first one not in a historical context and the first Warhammer Fantasy game of this type and scale. At the moment, not all factions from the original miniatures are available and the base game contains 5 of the 8 races currently developed, the other 3 being DLCs. CA plans are to create a trilogy and release all major races existing in the 8th Edition of Warhammer (plus some minor? Finger crossed) with each game focusing on a portion of the world. Having all three of them would allow for a grand campaign using all three portions of the map. While I was investigating about this game and if it was worth buying it or not, at this stage I was already hooked and was already in my cart.
The game can be divided in 2 different parts: the strategic map where you can control your armies, develop your provinces, contact other factions, etc. and the battle map where you control your units directly and you must fight your opponent mostly to the last blood. 
The strategic map presents all visible territories and armies moving through the beautiful landscape. I played the game both with medium to low settings with an old GeForce and now Ultra settings with a GeForce 1060 6GB and I have to say that while the game can still be enjoyed at lower settings, and Ultra settings are really demanding they are totally worth the price. In the strategic map you control also your buildings and are able to contact other factions to propose different agreements like trade, alliances or vassalage. Each race has also a specific characteristic that is important to control, for example the Dwarves have Grudges, be reconquering a just lost city or defeat an army that challenged us or reach a particular objective, ignoring them as terrible impact on the Empire giving global malus depending on how long the Grudge has been left unattended. The Wood Elves collect Amber that is coming from other cities or outposts and is used for research, powerful late game units or upgrading buildings. And so on making each race unique (Chaos Warriors and Beastmen look pretty similar in behaviour but have different strategies).  The armies are always led by a Lord, be it your Legendary Lord or another Lord that you can purchase when you have enough money. Each subsequent lord increases the upkeep of all your units therefore avoiding spamming too many of them. A special unit called Hero can be used mostly for sabotaging enemy lines and can be deployed separately from an army. Probably enemy Heroes are the most annoying part of the game but a really useful community mod restricts AI utilization to passive abilities (like spreading/removing corruption, etc.). Heroes cannot be attacked by armies and can be countered only by other Heroes. When an army meets another army (or it is ambushed or intercepted) you can decide to auto-resolve the battle or move to the battlefield.
In the battle map you control all your units and this is the part that most strategic player are more interested into. One thing I didn’t understand much, but seems related to the Warhammer lore, is the loss of unit formations, therefore you can’t control how the single models in a unit will be placed (more compact to resist melee impact or more spread for better resistance to enemy archers for example). There are keyboard combinations that allow you to keep a particular formation when you grouped your units together and I strongly recommend you learn them to avoid micromanaging every single unit. Yet I think this could have been done better and be more intuitive: if I group all my undead units in a tight line because they are extremely slow and they need constant use of my lord’s leadership to avoid crumbling, why if I press only the move button they keep spreading across the whole battlefield? The landscape makes for interesting strategic decisions, would you rush to conquer that hill so that your archers can have an advantage or will you ambush the enemy forces from the forest? My personal opinion is that most battles are boring and I auto-resolve them, but some (when the odds are against you) make for an interesting challenge. 
I realize that my review is already quite long and I could keep talking for hours, but if you reached up to here, thanks for reading and I hope you’ll enjoy the game should you give it a try. DLCs are not necessary (maybe except the Blood for the Blood God) but I would recommend the Wood Elves as they make for an interesting race with tough decisions in late game (amber is a quite rare resource and if you overextend you risk to be attacked from multiple fronts). And Norsca is just another level. A powerful new race the only defect is that makes you thing when Empire is going to get some love....

Погравши в DbD понад 147 годин можу зазначити, що задумка ігри цікава-чотирьом гравцям потрібно відремонтувати генератори і втекти від вбивці, попутно допомогаючи один одному знімати товариша з гака, лікуватися та інше, але гра побудована таким чином, що для просування свого рейтингу в рангах потрібно виконувати всі зазначені дії разом. Тобто  вам потрібно ремонтувати генератори, успішно тікати від вбивці, потім допомогти товаришу і зняти його з гака, вилікувати його, а може і декілька раз, а потім іще втекти через ворота або люк. В такому разі гра винагородить вас очками крові і ви отримаете "+" до рангу. Якщо ж, наприклад, вам з командою вдалося швидко відремонтувати генератори і вбивця нікого не спіймав або спіймав всього раз і вся команда успішно втекла через ворота, то вам, швидше за все, начислять мало рейтингу і можливо ви навіть отримает "-" ранг. Хоча, команда впоралася добре-все полагодила і втекла, а це, за логікою, основна задача з якою команда успішно впоралася. Таким чином гра змушує вас, наче, піддаватися вбиці для того, щоб отримати додаткові дії за які дають "+" до рангу. Буває, так що за результатами ви отримуєте багато очок крові (понад 20000), але гра все одно забирає у вас рейтинг. Гра за вижившего, начебто, командна, а в команді у кожного має бути своя роль під які набираються певні навики, один бере навики для швидкого ремонту, інший - щоб вміло тікати від вбивці, третій щоб швидше лікувати і таке інше, але гра наче каже вам що ви маєте робити це все, ви маєте бути універсалом і всі гравці набирають, приблизно одні і ті самі навики, які допомогають не "відлетіти" від вбивці першим, бо знову ж таки отримаєш "-" до рангу.  Також у грі багато "багів", які сильно дратують. Поблеми з пошуком нової гри, яка може шукатися до 10 хв. і з оптимізацією. Гра за вбивцю виявилася не цікавою. Його перевага над вижившими тотальна, складність виникає на початку ігри і пов'язана з розумінням механіки самої ігри. Вбивця, рухається від генерато до генератора, шукаає гравців, потім лове його і вішає свою жертву на гак. Завдання вбивці як можна швидше вбити першого гравця (через механіку триразового повішання або секретного підношення, коли можна вбити вже після першого повішання). Далі гра майже вирішена. Лишається завданням техніки довести гру до перемогу. Граю виключно через пошук гравців. Трапляються різні люди, які після першого падіння виходять з ігри, в такому разі гра  вже на 75 відсотків за вбивцею, а часто буває що і другий гравець теж виходе з ігри. І це після довгого пошуку ігри і завантаження. Буває так, що така ситуація повторюється декілька ігор підряд. І ви знову отримуєте "-" до рейтингу і сильну лють від ігри. Гравців які так вчиняють, гра не карає. а вони фактично псують ігру іншим. За шкалою в 5 пунктів гра на 3.

What's really amazing is how the only time you're not in control of your character is in the brief beginning cutscene.  Everything else is entirely under your control.  Ignore the big setpieces if you want; the game won't make you look.  But if you're looking, it's going to affect you emotionally because it's *you* looking, the control wasn't ripped away from you.  *You're* discovering things, *you're* making decisions, *you're* getting scared, *you're* triumphing over adversity.  This is so rare, and I'd recommend this game to anyone who enjoys major atmosphere and intense immersion.

Pick a car, set up the engine. Want a fast 4x4 truck with locked differentials? You can have that. Want a boosted street car that can drift for miles? That too! Want to drive an ambulance off-road? Yeah, me neither. 
You can slow down time and watch your rig destruct in slow motion. The destruction here is amazing. Engines will overheat, connecting rods will get damaged. Your radiator will leak if you cause frontal damage. You can break driveshafts or flatten tires. You can burn the clutch out. 
If you consider yourself a gearhead of any measure you will not hesitate to get this game. There is countless hours of fun and creativity inside.
Sincerely, DuramaxLover.

Ein großartiges Spiel für alle die anspruchvolle (und vor allem faire) Duelle a la Dark Souls mögen.
Der größte Teil der negativen Reviews scheint von schlechten Verlierern (in vierlerlei Hinsicht) geschrieben. 
Ich habe mit einem I3 3.Gen und einer GeForce 1060 auf maximaler Einstellung konstante 60 FPS. Die Ladezeiten sind selbst auf einer alten SATA II Platte mehr als akzeptabel. Verbindungsabbrüche habe ich bisher überhaupt nicht gehabt, allerdings ein bekannter von mir der über WLAN ins Netz geht. Hier treten je nach örtlicher Situation eben hin und wieder mal Paketverluste auf, das sollte man vll wissen bevor man sich beschwert. Aufgrund der kurzen Timeouts wird man hier schnell aus dem Spiel geworfen. Das macht einerseits bei einem SPiel wie diesem Sinn, da sofort ein (wirklich guter) KI-Bot einspringt , so dass das Team in der Unterzahlt das Match noch fair bis zum Ende bestreiten kann. Auf der anderen Seite könnte man hier vielleicht die Timeout-Toleranz ein wenig erhöhen um WLAN Nutzern etwas entgegen zu kommen.
Von schlechtem Balancing kann ich ebenfalls bisher nicht berichten. Nach 10,5 Stunden habe ich selbstverständlich noch nicht gegen alle Charaktere gespielt die es gibt, aber doch gegen die meisten auch Siege erringen können. Ähnlich wie in Mortal Kombat ist man hier gezwungen sich mit dem gespielten Charakter auseinander zu setzen und seine Kombos zu lernen. Im Gegensatz zu Mortal Kombat finde ich die Kombos aber deutlich einfacher (pro Char nicht zuviele und kürzere Abfolgen). Darüber hinaus muss man sowohl die Charaktere als Gegenspieler kennenlernen und Ihre Fähigkeiten einigermaßen einschätzen können, als auch den Spielstil seines menschlichen Kontrahenten schnell einschätzen und dementsprechend kontern.
Microtransactions ja, aber Pay2Win nein ! Es lässt sich nur ein schnellerer Fortschritt und jede Menge Accessoires kaufen, da das Matchmaking aber in meinen Augen super funktioniert bleibt es weiterhin ausbalanciert. Wer dann natürlich viel Geld für XP Bonis investiert hat steigt zwar schneller im Level auf, aber möglicherweise fehlt es dann auch an der entsprechenden Übung um mit entsprechend erfahrerenen Spielern mitzuhalten.

Fazit: nichts für Casual Gamer und kleine Mädchen!  

P.S.: Mehr als ich von UbiSoft erwartet hätte !

Main review
If you liked X-Com EW/EU then your going to love this, basically the same game.  There in lies my main complaint with this game.  Same stuff, minus alot of the cool stuff for EU (Gene Mods and MEC Trooper), from the previous game are here as well.  But, to me looking at the list side by side, this game contain quite a bit less than the first game and is incrediblly short for a xcom game.  I played on vetern and it started slowly till I hit the first few upgrades and it went be so fast I had all the story objectives queued up to accomplish in a matter of 20mins.  The combat way more easier than it was in the first game.  The main thing that got me killed is the new enemies (Codex, Gatekeeper, and Avatar) as I didnt know their ablities which hurt quite a bit.  

The combat seems to lean on the cheap side more than difficult side.  The codex and avatar can disable weapons, making you reload with an aoe attack AND Teleport even when hit (Codex make clones dividing HP b/w them each time) AND Teleport at will ANYWHERE which makes cover pointless in fighting them.  The gatekeeper is about the same as the cyberdisc, just cheaper with more AOE and reanimation.  Other than the Faceless, the game is quite easy to beat..  Sadly this takes alot of the charm out of the game for me at least.

Another Complaint I have and this is a complaint with alot of AAA titles is that they are not QAing the games anymore or at least half-assing QA.  They dont seem to test on multiple PC rigs.  The game launched with the SAME engine as EU/EW mind you and it still came in botched, at the time of writing this it is still desync and jerky in cutscenes and dialog, if they would have at least took one month to play on multiple platforms and different computer rigs, hell my computer is a beast of a system and I couldnt watch any of the cutscenes (gotta love Youtube for helping out on that), would have had a smoother launch.  Game companies as of late are becoming more and more lazy, but we still shell out the cash which tells them to keep doing it.

Final Thoughts
If you can get by the no cutscenes this is short and fun game, but not really worth the 60 bucks for it though.  If you see this on sale for less than 20 pick it otherwise wait.

Little more than 10 pgs of info on how to mod for the game.  This is why we ended up with the Corgi gun as the first mod for the game.  I planning on modding for this, but took one look at the documentation and said to hell with it.

So, I've been playing Rust since its Legacy days, and I've seen all the negative hype and bad press after so many changes. I just need to write this review because of the game in its current and up-coming status. 

Previously, Rust Legacy was a lot of fun. It had lag problems and some programming issues and other bugs that were bothersome... but overall, the game was a lot of fun. I had a blast playing it. Then, the devs started making changes. At one point the game became basically unplayable.  That sucked, and I was forced to take a long break from the game. I was disappointed in the devs and I took Rust off my Favorites list.

Now, with the more recent developer communication and with the more recent changes to the game, Rust is back on my Favorites! I'm very, very impressed with the devs now. I'm happy with the direction the game is going and I'm extremely excited about the future. It's been fun being a part of the development process and seeing all of the changes as well because I am interested in becoming a game developer and watching the process of development for this game has been intriguing. 

I expected to play a fun game when I bought Rust in early development, and I did. I didn't expect the roller coaster ride, but it's all working out OK. 

Lastly, let me make a comparison I'm sure 80% of the people reading this review will understand. World of Warcraft is one of the most well-known MMORPGs of all time. In some ways, it paved the way for the current MMO hype. It brought a lot of gamers together, and it brought a lot of people who weren't gamers into the gaming community. That being said, WoW has, at times, pissed a lot of gamers off. The devs at Blizzard made a lot of decisions that cost them players and gained them back. With WoW and with D3, Blizz has taken their fans on a roller coaster ride - just like the devs for Rust. If you're a gamer and you're pissed at buying Rust as an early access game and you're dealing with the disappointment and you're concerned about the game's future... be patient. Good things come to those who wait.

Facepunch isn't the biggest, wealthiest, best-staffed, world-wide phenomenon that Blizzard is... and yet, Blizzard took their gamers on some serious roller coasters just the same. As a Gamer you learn to deal with disappointment. There will never be a game that meets every single one of your criteria unless you make it yourself.

Only 9 hours in here, but I wanted to clear some air on a lot of peoples complaints and offer my insights.

And just to TL;DR - The game is pretty great if you can handle some bugs here and there. If you have ever played a day 1 release, or a Bethesda title, you will be absolutely fine. Plus, there are plenty of workarounds. If you want a 'no-fantasy' RPG...this is a definite buy!

Overall:
Really fun to play, and very time consuming (which is a good thing in my book!). The stories are great and can be on-par with the Witcher. Combat is challenging (For Honor but a touch clunkier/slower). Stat management is interesting and in-depth if you like that sort of thing. Lots of fun to be had here, and solid freedom of play-style. The in-game systems work together to create interesting results based on your activities. I'd say buy it now if you want to play a medieval/survival sim that doesn't hold your had. Otherwise, maybe give it a month or two. I am satisfied with my purchase, however, and have no regrets.

First: 
Yes, the save game thing is strenuous. Needing the Saviours Schnapps to save is a bit overwhelming, especially at the start when you A) Are broke and cannot afford it and B) Cannot make it.
The simple work around is to sleep in a bed of yours (some are given to you, or buy time in an inn).
If this doesn't solve your problems, just hit Nexus and grab the save mod...it's worth your time, and is just the addition of a file...super easy.
 
Second: 
Yep, there are bugs. And some are annoying. I haven't had anything that has 'broken' my gameplay in an unfixable way. And these are bearable if you've ever played a buggy game at all before...if you have survived Bethesda games, you will survive this.
Here are a few bugs I ran into, all marked as spoilers for safety:
[spoiler] Retrieving the ring for the Miller from the corpse/executioner: I dug up the grave, no ring. I went to the executioners house and was able to convince him to sell it but I was broke. So he freaked out and said to make up my mind. So I ran back to Miller who pretty much said 'figure it out'. I went back to executioner and he refuses to talk to me at all. I was left with 2 options: Steal it, or kill him. His path meant he ALWAYS saw me entering his home, and he would definitely hear me if I failed lock picking. I ended up having to kill him (which was against my play-style and really broke the vibe). Quest completed, but it still sucked that it came down to killing an innocent. [/spoiler]

[spoiler] Randomly, and not sure if related to killing the Executioner, considering no one was around, but my relationship with Rattay Citizens was -100 before I even entered the city. I have worked it up to -67 by following the quests, but this REALLY put a damper on finding this new great city to explore. Again, I am not killing randoms or stealing...so unsure how this happened. Not unlivable, it just means I've gotta work my way to positive rep.[/spoiler]

[spoiler] Another issue with the Miller. Pickpocketing training made zero sense to me at first so I kept failing. He ended up acting like I never showed up and walked away angrily in the middle of me trying, rather than just letting me try...weird.[/spoiler]

Some non spoiler bugs that are mostly just mechanics:
Citizens bump into you and yell at you like it's your fault. Not a bug, just annoying.
Occasional crashing but I have had this happen only 2x in ~10 hours. Not too bad and due to my regular saving, not detrimental. All games and apps crash some time, so I really shouldn't even mention it.
Some collision boxes could use fixing, like on stairs for battlements - this is where I get stuck most often.

Third:
Pretty much everything is hard. Combat, sneaking, lockpicking, pickpocketing...you WILL suck at this at first. This is not a detriment to gameplay, but rather, I believe, the intent. These skills aren't easy in reality, so why would they be in a game that is attempting a modicum of simulation? If you like a challenge, you should be satisfied here. Otherwise, mods and the console can help you out. Don't yell at the dev because you aren't good. Although, yeah, Lockpicking is a bit brutal. Definitely try the sectorial mod on Nexus to add a visual aid to lockpicking.

If anyone wants further insight, just let me know - I'd be happy to provide any details possible.

What I thought was going to be an awful, hard to understand, unnesscarily cryptic & vague, and "Meh." indie game...
Turned out to be a game that instead, I just can't stop bloody thinking about, even though I've been playing this religously lately.

Kenshi starts off like this: You pick one out of a few starters for your character(s): 
Be it just the basegame Zero in almost every stat, with nothing but rags and a wooden stick with your only true disadvantage being that literally everyone else is better than you. Unless if you work your butt off... Almost in the literal sense in some cases.
Or maybe you pick someone that starts off being chased by cannibals whilst missing an arm (Yes, there's proper limb loss in this game.) and are immediately forced to run for your life.
Maybe you pick the starter where your character lives in one of the major citities belonging to the [b]actual[/b] racist religious faction that has an... Interesting lacking in women.Who strictly only tolerate humans, and will try to murder & prosecute any other race who comes near no matter how human-like they are.
So as you can probably have guessed right now, the game just kinda throws a lot of you at once, but I think that's part of the fun.


As for the gameplay?
It's like this weird mix and mashing of Mount & Blade, Project Zomboid.
If you play it alone or in a small group, the game plays more like an RPG.
Eventually, you might decide to build an outpost that's got workers and all of your resources are fully automated.
And soon you have an army, and are now sort of playing in a psuedo RTS Mount & Blade esque game approach.
Melee is a huge thing in this game, and there are ranged weapons but it's limited to wall/fort turrets and hand-held crossbows. You don't actually control your swings and what not, it's pretty much dicerolls based on a LOAD of stats that I'm not going to mention because I'd be typing this up for way longer than I need to.

And... Well.
One of my friends disliked the game enough to compare it to "The You Testament" which, I would say does have similarities with Kenshi? But the major difference between these two games is that Kenshi isn't a nonsensical mess with NPCs that will attack you for made-up reasons out of nowhere like most of MD's games would have happen to you.

Kenshi is actually surprisingly fair if you play your cards right, and the world & NPCs will act in a pretty realistic manner. At least in regards to videogames. 
Of course if you meet starving bandits who haven't eaten in weeks, they're going to savagely attack you and rob your comatose/unconscious body of your food.
But if you're in a town that tolerates your race and gender? So long as you don't break the law, you should be good!

The only way the game really isn't 'fair' is through training two certain stats.
Toughness, and Melee Block chance. 

Those two stats, specifically require a "HURT ME MORE, SNAKE!" approach. As in, your character(s) literally will need to lose fights (which is a terrible idea usually.) and get hit a lot. 
Toughness determines your damage reduction, how much damage your organs can take before your character is comatose without aid from someone else, how much damage is needed in a single hit to stagger your character, how fast or slow you bleed out... It's such an important stat, but it's the most difficult one to raise since being unconscious in this game is such a huge risk... After all, if a carnivore be it animal or cannibal sees you comatose on the ground? They'll eat you, alive.
Unless if you're found by slavers. Who will kindly bandage you up! ...And then kidnap & shackle you, taking you away to work manual labor until you die of starvation and exhaustion.

Otherwise, your other stats train in pretty reasonable ways. Carrying someone over your shoulder with armor on & a backpack full of heavy gear? That's easily gonna raise your strength.
Want to raise your cooking? Cook some food, you ratbag! 
Want to get better at martial-arts? Don't use a weapon, only your fists.
Want to get better at repairing robots and prosthetic limbs? Get your noggin' joggin' with some science my dudes & dudettes.
REALLY need your character to get good with a specific weapon? Use that weapon class, and only that class for a very long time. Eventually you'll be so skilled that you can even stagger beasts with your sword or club, provided you have absurd strength & dexterity.

I would say more about the game, like the lore or how the outpost building works but...
I think leaving some things up to you to discover is better than me telling you EVERYTHING.

On the negative side, determining line of sight on maps with elevation differences can be a pain in the ass since the sight line tool which is very useful does not take elevation into account. Great game. The first has become a favorite of mine and this one seems to be improving upon in in a lot of ways. However, there are a few things that I think could use some work. As this is an early access game, I truly hope that the Dev's are looking into these reviews. I have no idea how to give them constructive criticism outside of this forum. I guess I will try their website next.

My issues: The new armor system is an awesome addition. It changes battle strategy in amazing ways. However, it is truly unfortunate that no status effects can be given to anyone who still has even a sliver of corresponding armour. This ruins the early battle efficiency of a number of spells and abilities, and unless you spend time wittling each enemies armour down before killing them off (a terrible tactical plan) most AOE skills (namely spells) have very little value. My suggestion to fix this would be to have each point in an armour type give a percentage resistance to corresponding status effects, rather than prevent them alltogether. This would still provide benefits for having the armour, but it would allow a chance for status effects to happen, increasing the usefulness of a lot of skills early in the battles.

Other than that, most of my issues are simple things that are undoubtedly going to get fixed through testing: permanent blindness issues that carry over into new battles, lack of companion options outside of original 4 (meaning no tank option without building into it), a beginning where I felt like I was running around talking to people for hours with no real direction and no winnable battles. 

All in all, this seems like a great improvement on an already amazing game. I can't wait for the final product.

最初评测是第一个DLC正是发售前写的，隔了三个月后再想想觉得差评还是不够公正。只从质量而言确实是非常好的游戏，所以还是改成了好评，但以前的评测就不改了放在下面：

游戏本体是质量过关的好游戏，但不好的或许在游戏外以及未来的DLC中。
八王之乱DLC从目前的介绍来看 CA似乎将其做成了八王分裂天下的全面战争-八国。
       晋书中所记载的八王之乱的主旋律是纷争，但更重要的是政争；不是欧洲罗马帝国崩溃后邦国林立的战争，跟三国时代的纷争也完全不一样。三国是中央权力已然崩溃、需要重新建立新的中央权力；八王之乱是八王先后在中央惠帝无能的状况前赴后继的争夺帝国执政权力的斗争，诸王或明战或暗谋，跟三国为了统一的战争是不一样的。这样的一段历史中朝堂的争斗其重要程度不亚于外部的战争，可以说在中央权力处的斗争决定了八王之乱中的诸多战争。全战一直以来运用的战争模拟引擎和与之配套的一套系统在我看来并不一定能够体现这段历史的复杂程度，极有可能弄巧成拙，弄成八个分裂晋王朝的邦国之间的战争。
      仔细查看这几天的诸王具体介绍，CA弄了个大错误。他把欧洲中世纪的邦国机械生硬的套到八王之乱DLC来了，它根本没搞清楚诸王的军事斗争的资本不是他们各自的封地，而是中央授予的都督诸州军事这一实权。所以，成都王司马颖的势力老巢不是他那个一辈子都没去的西蜀成都，而是在他都督的河北邺城；河间王司马颙的军事基地不在封地河间，是在他都督的关中；长沙王司马乂的军事控制范围根本不在封地长沙，他在八王之乱登场时控制的是首都洛阳的部队；汝南王司马亮楚王司马玮也从没有在封地起兵，他们更多的斗争在洛阳朝堂之内。诸王的势力范围不是他们的封地，而是他们掌握的天下哪个州的军队也就是都督军事的这个州。CA在这里犯了个及其愚蠢的错误！误把封地当做诸王的势力范围，按CA以往的考究，我不认为他们不知道这种基础知识。而这样的错误对于打着实际历史背景的策略游戏是很愚蠢的。这就像一款三国游戏，分别弄错魏蜀吴三国的起始位置。玩家粉丝可以说全战系列不是历史模拟游戏，甚至可以说不在乎。但我只说一句：知道这些历史后，你玩游戏的时候不感觉违和吗？
       在CA之前的考究前，这个错误更像是一个笑话。我不是说你CA不能选择八王之乱这段历史，但你作为策略游戏势力起始位置该考究的还是要考究。事实上正是因为这段历史里的斗争错综复杂不好还原，所以我才为CA捏了这一把汗。CA做的这个DLC，它的介绍给我的感觉就是别扭。中西方的历史还是有很多的不一样，你CA能做好中世纪的邦国林立，但却不一定能够做好八王之乱。你要不打着八王之乱的旗号，搞个虚拟背景的DLC，这些错误都不是错误；但你标题都是这个了，那就要强调历史的准确性。三国历史比较知名还没有这种错误，遇到八王之乱这种细节就套用CA想当然的欧洲中世纪封邦建国的那一套。那么其他DLC，你让我怎么相信这是全战-三国DLC，不是全战-欧洲换成中国地图DLC。
       这个话题可以就此打住了。我赞赏CA选择三国历史的精明，我甚至也赞赏选择八王之乱历史的勇气；我钦佩CA做这个游戏时的考究，我感动于CG和游戏本体的质量。后续DLC以及游戏改动质量过关的该好评还是好评。但我不为你的错误买单，我有权选择自己的评价。

       今天看到了CA与网易合作的消息。如果游戏本体的质量是优秀，DLC是毁誉参半，那么这步合作是不折不扣的臭棋。看到全战三国的火爆销量就已经这么迫不及待的来捞钱了吗？游戏独家发行商？忘了给你贡献百万销量的steam国区玩家是吧，还是说觉得Steam的30%抽成费太贵，网易给你带来更多好处？当然，作为中国玩家可以好心的可以给你们介绍一下网易这家中国公司，这是一家精致得没有下限，赚钱得没有良心，短视得如同他们的吉祥物，傲慢得如同你们CA自己一样的中国本土公司。哦不，我们或许现在才知道，你们CA和这家中国公司没有任何本质区别。

最后给CA个建议，锁区吧。这样Steam上所有差评都看不到了，你和新伙伴的合作才能亲密无间嘛。

hey all. my first review on a game! now im going to tear this game apart as i have played all total war games! and i have my faves.

first off i would like to add something about the DLC!!  how they can justify selling us something that should be part of the main game is mind boggling!!!   they have already hit us up for the full standard price of a full tripple AAA polished and complete game but only give us 4 playable factions out of an array of about 60 !!  this in my oppinion is down right unacceptable!!  but any way i bought the main game regardless and probably will not buy any DLC'S!

first off the way we upgrade cities is a sham!   unlike other total war titles where you have far more flexibility they give you just 4 build slots on small towns and 6 on the major cities!! this is just restricting as hell. also to save time building the game they have only listed the primary locations and left out many of the small surrounding villages which we should be able to visit! now i understand these villages in terms of lore are not really upgradable but visiting them should grant us special missions where we can do some good for the local community and kill of a green skin hord in return for a magic item or some much needed gold! or perhaps defending the village would result in a unique military unit becoming available to recruit into an army!

 secondly after several replays with the empire  i have to say its the same exact play each time..  you start the game you kill a few empire factions off the rest join you pretty much hassle free  then the chaos hordes come.. you beat them back conquer the lands and win the game!! its not dynamic and its not a great deal of fun.. empire troops are very weak meaning  tactics are the same thing every battle..  huge wall of sword and shields with some spear units on the flanks with crossbows in the rear protected so they can just keep reigning hell down on which ever enemy fights us!! simple easy and it works.. no real point in trying anything different because nothing else works.. as soon as you break the formation you  get slaughtered.  empire is an artiallry based defencive game style with the standard troops which are if i do say so also very limited and restrictive.   for a start they needed to include all the knightly orders! all the infantry units  and archers/crossbows!! different types of halberds and also colour code the regiments to match the province they come from.. 

also the fact they all become the empire is not lore either!  in the   warhammer world the individual provinces maintain their identity and their electors rule    but no! they all become reikland..   they should join with us but retain their individuality in each province so we the player can see and control the specific armies of each provicne.  

 the siege mode is feeble. too easy!   just blast the doors open the defenders leave the walls and then  we climb those walls with no problems.. wang the cavalry through the gate with great swords and put archers on their own walls and then sit and watch as they die out in the open with no where to run to..    not enough effort put into the strategy aspect of the game.

heroes are pointless and not needed at all!   waste of time and  troop space. 

vampires are too easy to beat!! just destroy the lords and watch the entire army crumble in seconds ??? kinda bad really. perhaps better AI to ensure vamps live longer.

  the biggest problem is definately the empire control aspects.. it just doesnt exist! you just build one of each military buildings in each province so you can recruit a large array of  troops then you just recruit and conquer.

Watch Dogs 2 is a massive improvement in every way over the first game and what the series should have been from the start.

Watch Dogs 1 was a self-serious and gormless games focused on a complete shithead that wasn’t even actually a real hacker that the writers thought was a hero even when he was anything but. 2 on the other hand actually has a sense of humor and a real a sense of character. 2’s spirit feels like a cross between a 90’s hacker movie and Jet Set Radio.  It’s much more colorful with a really neat punk aesthetic mixed with a modern Internet meme aesthetic. This could have all easily fallen into “How do you do fellow kids?” territory, but I feel that the game has such a genuine sincerity and charm to it that it never feels cringy, just endearingly and intentionally goofy. It really helps that the characters are fun and are intentionally a bunch of goofy dorks. Marcus is the protagonist the series needed and is the polar opposite to Aiden in every way. The game’s writing is good, as mentioned the cast is likable and the plot is solid, handling topical stuff with some deftness. My only real complaint is one of the cast dies and it feels completely out of place, it’s pretty disconnected from the main plot, doesn’t fit the tone of the rest of the game, and robs the game of the interesting interactions that character had with Marcus.

Gameplaywise the game actually feels like more like the hacker sandbox game it should have been from the get go. Aiden was just a GTA character with a magic phone, but Marcus has more tech in his arsenal such as drones that really add to the stealth elements, as well as non-lethal weapons which seem far more appropriate for him to use. It’s testament to how likable Marcus is that I tried to stay in character when I played story missions for the most part, I tried to keep casualties to a minimum and rarely stole cars. (It really helps that the game lets you spawn cars you own through your phone, because Marcus really doesn’t seem the type of guy to commit grand theft auto on the regular) I just wish melee takedowns weren’t all lethal.

As the PC port goes it’s not the best optimized. I’ve had three crashes and the game freaks out whenever I alt-tabbed. It obviously wasn’t close to being a deal breaker though if you look at how much I played.

Overall Watch Dogs 2 is a real good sandbox game and what the first game should have been to begin with.

[h1] A wonderful RPG experience! [/h1]

I went into this game, not having played many RPGs before, however, I still loved every minute I spent on "Grimm's Hollow". As a disclaimer, I played the story mode, especially because of my lack of experience with games like this , and the fights were very easy. In other words, if you want a challenge, do choose the other difficulty at the beginning.
For my review, let's try to start with aspects I did not like... Well, I honestly can't really complain about anything. Perhaps some might be bothered that this is a short game, yet I don't mind to be honest. While you won't spend that much time on this game, it is still crisp and the playtime is fairly fitting for the amount fo story.
With that, let's move over to me explaining why I [b]highly[/b] recommend you to give "Grimm's Hollow" a try.  The fighting system is easy to use and you will quickly catch on with how it works. Furthermore, with the little quick time events, it is quite fun in my opinion. There is a good variety of special attacks and some items as well, to offer you some diversity. As I noted before, I did not play the "advanced mode" so I can't say how fighting is there but I simply imagine the enemies to be a little stronger.
Next to the actual fights, we have a nice leveling system, where you can upgrade general skills like your attack damage or your defense. Aside from that, it also includes the special attacks, which you can unlock and enhance in there. Once again, this is extremely simple in a good way - it will only support the game experience.
What I also have to mention is the art style. The sprites are very adorable but some can also be a little creepy, which fits the atmosphere in certain parts of the game very well. [spoiler]Take Timmy's change of appearance at the end for example, if you lose against the baker. The way his sprite starts to look distorted is incredibly suitable for how horrible the "turning evil" for ghosts apparently is.[/spoiler] Moreover, the tiny animations (for example during the fights/attacks) are a very nice addition. The items also have cute designs, which personally made me actually want to try them in real life.
The music, of course, is part of the whole experience as well. It is used appropriately, always altering according to each situation you encounter. The same goes for sound effects. You can see that the developers/creators truly thought about what soundtracks would fit the game. It often sounds funny but can turn serious too.
The story was very touching as well. I loved the whole concept of death and ghosts/reapers that was introduced to us. My favorite character was Grimm by the way. [spoiler]He (?) was so endearing with how he deeply cared about the reapers, which was easy to recognize when watching the ending where Lavender loses against the baker and then does not pass on. It was incredibly heartbreaking but heartwarming too, seeing how sincerely hurt Grimm was by Lavender's suffering. Nevertheless, he still took care of her as best as possible.[/spoiler]
So what else can I say? Please do yourself a favor and [b]PLAY THIS GAME[/b] if you enjoy RPGs. You will not regret it (or at least I hope so). Thank you to the game developer and everyone who worked on this, for such an amazing free experience!
Btw, the skip button after you finished one ending was very much appreciated!

Easy to coordinate: little/no coordination required. Easy to play: difficult to master. From individual play, to the cooperative play, DRG doesn't demand much up front, but facilitates and rewards mastery of all it's elements.

I'm not big on pubs, but DRG is in an exclusive class of multiplayer games where it is not only pretty fun to play with strangers, but realistic to communicate and cooperate with each other; no voice chat required. At present that category is populated solely by Deep Rock.

If you like charming light hearted games that you can play at your own pace and still generally progress, (success or failure), you won't go wrong with DRG.
If you like challenging yourself to push farther and dig deeper, you won't go wrong with DRG.
If you like playing with friends versus CPU, you won't go wrong with DRG.
If you enjoy rapid-fire game genres where you can play a match within two minutes before moving on to something else... you could maybe go wrong with DRG.

Game is best multiplayer, but if you're stubbornly insistent on stranger danger, DRG is serviceable solo, if you're big on digging and exploration. The procedural caves are well done.

Con: Could stand for literally any other cheer/call out beyond "rock & stone". "Ice&Snow" when, Ghostship Games? You already have a frozen biome. I am very disappointed...

Played this game with three friends for many hours and we all experienced frequent inexplicable hit detection (or rather the lack thereof).  Most nights only one of us had problems, but some nights we all had difficulty getting kills despite seeing hits registered in our front end.  On the flip side it seemed like other players would just look at us and we'd die.  

Initially we wrote it off to hackers.  Unfortunately the problem seemed to get worse as time went on.

Eventually I did some online research and discovered that apparently from the beginning the developers found that the Unreal tournament engine that PUBG is based upon wasn't meant for MMOG and have been working around those limitations since  (desync issues).  There are plenty of YT videos documenting the problem too.

In addition to the unreliable hit detection there are other annoying aspects of the game.  There is a ton of emphasis on weapon accuracy - different weapons and attachments determine accuracy.  But what's glaringly absent is that getting hit by gunfire while firing does nothing to degrade the shooter's gunnery.  So if you're getting shot you can continue to shoot without penalty.

Another issue is the graphics draw distance.  Things like tall grasses block your visibility while prone so you might presume you're not visible to others, but if your opponent is far enough away he doesn't see you in the cover of grass - you're just lying in the open.

But it was the problems we experienced with wonky hit detection that eventually got so frustrating that we stopped playing.

If indeed the problem lies with limitations of the Unreal tournament engine there may not even be a fix.  If it's hackers then they're not doing enough to stop them.

Quite an improvement on Sniper Elite 3, which was really just "meh" for me.  They really opened the maps up quite a large amount, which allows you to actually get some ranged kills instead of 50m headshots and constant pistol and melee kills.

Some welcome additions include silenced ammo (logic, but whatever) that allow you to shoot normally very loud pistols or rifles quietly without alerting anyone, which is awesome for sneaky people.  Thankfully it's not super abundent so you can't just spam silent ammo the whole level.

I also liked how they fixed the ragdoll physics a little so that guys no longer do a flip and fly 10m away when you shoot them, which is nice.

Not really a gameplay thing but something for reading, they put in a Watch_Dogs style thing to the binoculars, where if you hover over a guy long enough it'll tell you their name and something about them.  Add to that how they have given some soldiers letters, so if you loot their bodies you can get a letter they were sending to family and friends.  Sometimes it kind of makes you feel bad when you learn that some sentry was a florist before being conscripted, and then blow his head off, and then take a letter off of him that details his sorrow at his childhood dog dying.

I did have some strange stuttering, the game would freeze every once in a while for a second or two, but I'm not sure if thats on my end or their end.

I'm not a fan of how much DLC is ALREADY in the game, and how most of the interesting things are behind paywalls.  For instance do you want a delisle (delysle?) silenced carbine as your sniper rifle, too bad, gotta pay.  Want an M3 grease gun? Pay up.  Want an M1 garand? PAY ME!  The only stuff you get for free is just the typical stuff, nothing really interesting.

       [i]尼尔：机械纪元[/i]  无疑是一款极为出色的日式ARPG游戏。不幸的是它似乎从登陆steam开始就陷入争议，老实说本人也是犹豫再三才决定入手的，但真正体验过这款游戏后，我只能说206收购一份感动是值得的。
      想必很多小伙伴和我一样都是从 [i]2B小姐姐[/i] 开始了解这款游戏的[spoiler]“2B姐姐是我的”[/spoiler]的确，2B出色的人设是这个游戏最大的亮点之一[spoiler]“舔爆”[/spoiler]。除了优秀的人设外，[spoiler]“总之你们先把这个人设（指2B）给我做出来，其它事之后再说”  据说这个游戏就是这么开始的[/spoiler]流畅的战斗系统，多样的战斗搭配，优美的原声音乐(买OST送游戏），丰富的收集元素（后期就像我这样钓鱼养老了）更是让人欲罢不能。但要说尼尔给我最深刻的印象，还是他的多周目系统。
       一周目结局乏善可陈，甚至让我觉得尼尔也不过如此；二周目操控9s似乎有点新意，但也不过是视角的变化；然而正当我觉得故事步入尾声时，我才猛然惊醒，原来故事远未结束，所有的悬念都将在三周目迎来终焉。在最终的弹幕游戏中，虽然我早知有这段剧情，但我还是哭了，只因忍不住泪水。那一刻的感受我很久后才回过味来，那是终焉的感觉，是一种故事结束时难言的感动。这样的感受我只在很久之前体会过，即在我看完【Air.真心为你】的时候。
    游戏最后，我选择[strike]删除了存档[/strike]，仿佛真正做完了一件事。我想，多年以后，我还会记得它曾带给我的感动，或许这就是SE期望达到的效果吧。

Parece cedo (40 horas), para emitir um comentário adequado, mas este jogo é uma releitura de um jogo do final do século, pelo qual desenvolvi um ótimo elo emocional, e nos primeiros momentos de jogo, senti o retorno das mesmas emoções anteriores, porém com detalhes pormenorizados quanto ao visual com melhor definição. 
A riqueza nos detalhes das locomotivas é apaixonante. Os cuidados com o resgate dos pormenores históricos conduzem a uma imersão na realidade, e levam a questionamentos sobre os rumos que teria a história tomado caso a escolha fosse por outro campo de desenvolvimento. 
O esquema das cadeias de suprimentos e suas intrincadas relações para apresentar o produto final ao mercado consumidor é uma das características que valorizam este jogo. A solução proposta na forma manual, que permite manter o vagão com a carga da estação anterior anterior, seguir viagem, amplia o realismo deste jogo para um nível acima ao quando colocado no modo automático.
A evolução dos aperfeiçoamentos, tanto para as locomotivas quanto para os estabelecimentos ferroviários, considero como um ponto inovador de grande valor, e historicamente rico por apresentar os detalhes e os motivos que levam àquele desenvolvimento. 
Outro aspecto, a meu ver positivo e de grande contribuição é as informações que se apresentam no próprio mapa de jogo, com um formato suave porém de maior precisão sobre o que e os motivos para ser realizado. De um aspecto pedagógico, o jogo apresenta um belo didatismo de como se desenrola seu funcionamento.
Suas campanhas trazem uma riqueza da história que marcou esta industria no alvorecer da Era Industrial, para o alvorecer da Era da Tecnologia e Informação. 
É um jogo simples, ou fácil de seguir em seu curso de desenvolvimento da partida. As possibilidades em ampliar os desafios a níveis maiores estão nas próprias definições de como o jogador prefere lidar com o que se apresenta diante da situação de cada partida. Em média consome de duas a quatro horas para concluir uma partida relacionada aos desafios apresentados, mas pode ser ampliado para muito mais tempo, tudo é uma questão de prioridade.
Este é outro aspecto a ser valorizado neste jogo, valorizar o aspecto de empreender, em desenvolver habilidades de antever  o  rumo do futuro e desenvolver empatia pela comunidade, para que se possa colaborar para que estas cresçam, independentemente de onde estejam, possam então desenvolverem seus sonhos.
Como disse inicialmente, sou suspeito para opinar, mas este se mostra um belo jogo de estratégia e simulação. (Aliás, este é o único ponto ainda falho, provavelmente devido a lidar com situações do mapa, no que se refere a construção da ferrovia, a ferramenta apresenta limites para arranjos durante a construção, mas fora isto, é prazeroso poder viajar pela via com a locomotiva.)
Considero este como um jogo que em breve o estaremos utilizando com Realidade Virtual e fazendo parte da partida, seja como um maquinista, foguista, guarda, chefe de estação, etc..

После года,потраченного на эту игру я решил переписать свой обзор.За эти  2 года игра притерпела столько изменений,что от прежнего PAYDAY 2 практически ничего не осталось.Из-за этого на игру и на то,какие транформации она притерпела за все это время, можно посмотреть с двух точек зрения,но давайте по-подробнее:
Сама игра представляет ко-оп fps про банду грабителей в клоунских масках.Геймплей не самый разообразный,в основном надо отстреливаться от бесконечной орды копов и время от времени перезапускать дрель.Но иногда нам дают действительно интересные для данного сеттинга вещи,вроде недавнего угона машин.Так что если вы не привыкли проходить один и тот же хейст 10 раз ради того,чтобы перейти на новый уровень или купить новую пушку,данная игра не сможет вам предоставить море веселья.И в этом заключается ММО часть игры.Вам придется потратить достаточно много времени,чтобы достигнуть 100 уровня и открыть все оружие.Но на этом дело не заканчивается.Если вам уж совсем некуда деть свое "драгоценное" время,то для вас есть infamy.Чтобы открыть последний уровень infamy (25-100)  вам потребуется несколько сотен часов вашей жизни.
Перейдем к ограблениям.В игре есть пара-десятков ограблений: начиная от ювелирки до национального банка.И в этом вся проблема:большая часть хейстов распространяется через DLC,а бесплатные ограбления выходят очень редко,так что если у вас кроме горы врмени есть гора денег,то готовьте ее для огромного количества дополнений,выходящих до сих пор.
Но не только ограблениями едины.Поскольку PAYDAY 2 является классическим представителем жанра MMOFPS,то все его аспекты здесь есть:
1.Оружия в игре предостаточно(по крайней мере для того,чтобы устоить революцию во имя Аллаха в какой-нибудь стране на Ближнем востоке).Но добрая половина доступна через DLC,вроде снайперских винтовок,пулеметов,гранат и прочих радостей жизни.Также,есть прокачка ваших стволов,вроде новых прицелов или увеличенного магазина(модификаций достаточно много даже без дополнений)
2.В оригинальном Payday было 4 главных героев:Даллас,Чейнс,Вульф и Хокстон.Теперь мы имеем ни 5,ни 6,а 10 персонажей,начиная от первого женского персонажа Кловер,до "хрен зная откуда он взялся" Джекета из Hotline miami.К счастью(а может и наоборот) большая часть доступна только через DLC.Но даже это является перебором,как мне кажется.Также,чтобы выделиться из толпы,тут мы имеем довльно большой арсенал масок и материалов для их кастомизации(Которые по большей части доступна через DLC).
3.Присутствует несколько дерев навыков(которые удивительно,доступны без DLC),заточенные под разные виды игры:хочешь с шумом вламываться в банк и щедро одаривать всех пулями,качай штурмовика,хочешь выполнять все тихо и не поднимать тревоги,призрак к вашим услугам.Четких разделений на классы нет,можно прокачивать все,что захочешь.Есть еще и перки,но про них лучше вообще не вспоминать.
В итоге мы имеем неплохую игру,заваленную кучей DLC(Даже в Sims 3 dlc меньше).Для кого то это минус,так как не каждый готов платить сумму,которая превышает стоимость игры в раз 10 на DLC.Казалось бы,не покупай,в чем проблема?Проблема в том,что даже за самую простую вешь,вроде снайперские винтовки или гранаты разработчики требуют денег,что не может не расстраивать.Тем не менее,Overkill заявили что собираются доить проэкт еще 2 года,так что посмотрим,к чему приведет жадность дядю Альмира,а пока что моя оценка игре 71 DLC из 100 возможных.

P.S.это все заговор,не покупайте dlc...ууу...серьезно,потратьте их лучше на мороженое,хотя там снайперские винтовки есть, и пулеметы...вот их и купите,а на все остальное купите мороженое.

As a huge fan of the classic Sim City games, I was really excited to pick this up during one of the summer sales. I totally enjoy and strongly recommend this game, but I also wanted to talk about some of the things I was disappointed about with the base game.

1. The traffic simulation is really challenging, and most of my efforts related to city planning involved trying to set up roads/avenues/highways in a way that encourages smooth traffic flow. This is harder then it sounds, as the sim dudes seldom find alternative routes to their destination if their current is experiencing heavy traffic. You often don't see the folly of your layout until its too late and you have hundreds of thousands of people living in your city, which makes me just want to start over entirely.

If you are into the idea of filling every map cell with RCI, be prepared to preemptively solve some of the most complex traffic problems I think I have ever encountered in a city builder. It's not my cup of tea as I am more interested in beautification, but the payoff is worth it for some I am sure.

2. Limited map selection. I remember in other city building games such as simcity 3000 or 4, you could select from entire regions of maps, or even randomly generate one from scratch. In this game (vanilla) you can select from maybe a dozen or so maps, each with pre-selected building types based on the region they represent. I tend to prefer classic city sims with lots of skyscrapers late game, so that limits my map choices further. Down to about maybe 6 or 7. If there is random map generation I certainly cannot find it in the menu.

3.  The "tweets" from citizens are kinda cool, as they give you hints on what it is you need to do from the perspective of average citizens, but up to a certain point these advice hints just kinda "stop". And what you are left with is a stagnant city and some repetitive tweets from content citizens. Late game, its up to you to read the data provided to get an understanding as to why your city is no longer growing, but I don't remember it being tutorialized. These could be traffic issues, lack of "adaquate" services to certain areas (even the kind that logically have no business in office areas like schools!), low demand, etc.

Keep in mind most of these gripes are either fixed with mods or a matter of preference. Personally though, I am not the type to spend hours researching and configuring mods to customize my experience.
