[b]La sana vida en el campo[/b]

El sector indie cada vez está cobrando más importancia dentro de la industria del videojuego, mes tras mes, son más los ejemplos de títulos que logran cotas de calidad que no tienen que envidiar a ningún AAA de su momento. No obstante, hay ciertos momentos en los que aparece un juego muy especial, que nace del cariño y la pasión más absolutas, pero digo más, incluso en más raras ocasiones surge algo de eso de la mano de una sola persona y son en estos momentos cuando uno se plantea muchas cosas seriamente. De esta manera nace Stardew Valley gracias a Eric Barone, una persona que cansado de ver en lo que se convertía su título favorito, Harvest Moon, decidió hacer su propio videojuego del estilo, pero añadiendo muchísimos más elementos que le dan identidad propia al juego y además, desde ya puedo afirmar que es lo mejor que hay tanto a nivel del género que aborda, como el mejor indie que ha aparecido en lo que va de 2016 (y de los últimos años, sin duda).

Pese a lo que pueda parecer en un principio, el juego guarda mucha, muchísima más profundidad de lo que pueda aparentar, en todos y cada uno de sus apartados. Pero la gran virtud no es solo eso, sino el hecho de, con maestría, nos introduce en todos ellos de forma paulatina, sin ninguna clase de presión y de una forma clara y sencilla. No es el típico juego que te obliga a hacer X cosas de forma casi desesperante, no... En Stardew Valley te puedes dedicar a lo que quieras, cuando quieras y el tiempo que quieras. ¿Que un día te apetece pescar? Lo haces, no pierdes nada, al contrario, subirás tu rama de pesca (pues tiene elementos RPG), ¿Que quieres picar y combatir en la mina? ¡A ello! O quizás te apetezca simplemente pasearte por el pueblo y conversar con sus habitantes para hacer amistades (y de paso alguna quest que te encomienden).

Hay muchísimo que decir de Stardew Valley, es como un micromundo muy bien entrelazado, en el que cada pieza está encajada perfectamente en su sitio, nada sobra y nada falta. Tan simple y la vez tan profundo como el hecho de que has heredado unas tierras de tu abuelo en un pueblo en el que la gente se dedica a la agricultura y ahora deseas vivir esa vida. Una vez llegas tienes tu granja, tus tierras y una enorme zona para explorar en la que vivir experiencias, aventuras y muchas y variadísimas sensaciones. Los días empiezan a pasar, con ciclos día/noche más climatología cambiante. Pero no se queda ahí, el año también va pasando y con él las estaciones y con la llegada de cada una de ellas todo el valle cambia, cambia su aspecto, sus frutos cultivables (o los que puedes encontrar por ahí) y hasta se van sucediendo festividades como las que podrías encontrarte en cualquier pueblo en la vida real.

Cada personaje que habita Pelican Town (el pueblo) tiene su vida, sus quehaceres diarios, su día de cumpleaños y siempre algo interesante que ofrecer, nadie está de relleno, con todos se puede interactuar y todos tienen algo que aportar. Puedes incluso tener una relación amorosa con algunos de ellos (sin importar el sexo de tu personaje y el del NPC), casarte ¡y hasta tener hijos! (adoptar si tienes una relación entre personajes del mismo sexo).

Francamente debo reconocer que el entusiasmo me puede a la hora de hablar de Stardew Valley, puesto que me sorprenden de el muchas cosas, desde el hecho de haber sido creado por una sola persona, pasando por el nivel casi enfermizo (en el buen sentido) de detalles jugables y estétitcos que tiene este juego y terminando por una realidad muy demoledora; Jamás me gustaron los juegos "de granjitas" y Stardew Valley me ha ENAMORADO.

PD: Encima ya hay traducción de la comunidad ¿Qué más se puede pedir? Lo recomiendo a cualquiera con los ojos cerrados.

app_name: Total War: ROME II - Emperor Edition
review:
Da sviluppatore di videogiochi posso ritenerlo un Ottimo gioco, un notevole miglioramento rispetto ai titoli precedenti. Curata la grafica e le animazioni di ogni singolo personaggio. L' IA è veramente di alto livello, una cosa da correggere è la cavalleria che carica i picchieri sempre frontalmente, probabilmente viene vista come normale fanteria. La campagna è molto bella con tutte le fazioni e andrebbe giocata con la massima difficoltà. Anche quella multiplayer è veramente ben fatta. E' il primo gioco in cui vedo fare bene una testuggine romana. Nonostante la grafica sia di alto livello, un ruolo determinante per le prestazioni lo gioca il LOD, riducendo drasticamente il numero dei poligoni degli oggetti lontani dalla camera, renderizzando come "High Poly" solo quelli ben visibili. Grazie a questo, abbassando un po' il dettaglio delle ombre, è possibile giocare bene anche con schede grafiche di fascia media.

Appassionato di Age of Empires questo gioco è si strategico, ma a volte le battaglie finiscono in un ammasso di soldati, cosa che gli antichi romani non avrebbero mai fatto.
L' unica frase in latino è "Roma Invicta" per il resto le conversazioni tra i personaggi sono tutte in inglese cosa che non mi piace.
Gli spartani e gli ateniesi dovevano essere inclusi nel gioco e non come DLC, poichè hanno giocato un ruolo chiave per la storia del mondo occidentale
Il fumo proveniente dagli edifici distrutti fa calare nettamente le prestazioni

The Elder Scrolls eine Reihe die jeden Gamer im RPG Franchise ein Name sein sollte. Und jeder der der sich nie mit RPG spielen auskennt wird auch hier kein Spaß haben aber für eingefleischt TES Fans oder RPG Fans werden hier ein würdigen Nachfolger sehen. Nach Arena Daggerfall Morrowind und Oblivion versucht hier Bethesda hier ein RPG der extra Klasse zu erstellen was ihnen auch voll gut gelungen ist. Mit Nexus und den Steam Workshop ist eine große Modvielfallt für jeden was dabei seis es Falskaar oder nur Begleiter. 

Die Positiven Seiten von Skyrim sind:

-Große Map und eine Abwechslungsreife Map 
-Eine gute auch dünne Hauptstory die sogar besser erzählt wird als bei CoD oder andere AAA Titeln 
-Eine Menge Nebenquest zB Die Dunkle Bruderschaft oder die Gefährten 
-3 DlC's die echt eine Extra klasse für sich sind 
-Hier merkt man das der Spieler und die Map eins sind d.h das man nicht linear von ein zum anderen Punkt muss sondern dies auch später erledigen kann 
-eine Modvielfalt die ständig erweitert wird
-die Soundtracks oder kurz OST sind fabelhaft un mann muss mit der Meldodie mitgehen 
-die Drachenkämpfe auch wenn die gleich sind hat jeder Kampf seine eigende Tücke 
-Grafik ist richtig gut gemacht und ist heute sogar sehr top 
-Lustige Easter Eggs haben die Leute auch verbaut also hop rein in Skyrim und sucht die alle :D 

Das sind die Punkte die mir nach 200 Stunden aufgefallen sind und zwar richtig und 200h zu erreichen ist nicht schwer denn Skyrim hat Suchtpontenzial und macht sehr schnell Abhängig ;D

Und Negatives ist mir kaum aufgefallen 

-Die Synchro das 2 leute die selbe haben ist aber in der Masse aber recht gut verkraftbar und kratzt nicht am Spielspaß 
-Manche Charaktäre sehen gleich aus 
Mehr fällt mir erstmal nicht auf von der Negativen Seite vielleicht noch die Hauptstory aber die wird durch die Erzählung schon ins Positive gerückt 

Nach 300 h finde ich bestimmt noch was Positives und was Negatives 

Aber mein Fazit ist bleibt ein Gelungendes RPG der besonderen Art 
Bethesda hat mit Skyrim eine Legende der Rollenspiele entwickelt und darauf sollten sie mit TES VI aufbauen auf die Stärken von Skyrim 

Es ist für RPG Einsteiger und für alte RPG Fans ein Have-Must und ich würde es jeden Gamer empfehlen

1) Ai is slightly better than Attila even in Diplomacy.

3) Archers finally mean something. Meaning their arrows do damage not like defending and the Archers have water pistols. Carefully placed Archers do damage. Which is great above all. 
4) Multiple Short,Medium and Long Victories to choose from.

Deceptive marketing from this company. This isn't a true part 2, this is essentially a standalone expansion / game update that they put up for sale as a part 2 to trick newcomers to the series. You think you can skip part 1, but this game is missing key features like a conquest mode and half the races unless you purchase the first one and all of its DLCs retroactively. 

Of course long time fans who have owned the first game all along don't mind, but this is a really dishonest way to make people think they can get into the series late and then ambush them with an entire extra game worth of DLC that doesn't show up on the store page. 

If they had simply released this as an expansion to Total War: Warhammer I wouldn't have an issue with it, you'd know that what you're really dealing with is one huge living game with a massive backlog of DLC and you'd know what to buy if you want to try the basics. But this makes you purchase a specialty campaign with only half the races in it, and doesn't tell you that the meat and potatoes of the game where you fight over the whole world and can play any race you want costs extra.

app_name: The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition
review:
It's a good game, but it's waaay better with mods.
Still, if you've not played Skyrim before I would recommend playing the main story through vanilla (without mods) first, but it can be kind of short if you only focus on the main story. This game intends for you to explore the region of skyrim, and go do your own thing, so don't be afraid to stray off the main quest.

The DLCs are great fun, I liked the dragonborn and vampire additions. They've got some more 'mini' dlcs in it's creation club, which you can get things like backpacks, goblin encounters, weapons, armour, quests, and other such things. 

I would recommend with mods and/or the dlcs once you've completed the guilds and main story. I personally  get bored of the game once that happens, mainly because it's just pure exploration after that, but I would recommend the Apocalypse and Ordinator or whatever mods, which adds a heck ton of new perks. Makes magic a lot more worth it, I especially like running around as a necromancer with an awesome army of skeletons behind me.

If you have any mods you'd like to suggest to me or the other people reading this, then feel free to comment on this review. I just use Skyrim's in-game mod thing because nexus mods is too confusing for me (I'm a bit dumb) but yeah. Suggest any mods you enjoy.

新伦敦，541人。
充分发挥社会主义制度的优越性
在打垮“伦敦帮”的过程中，我从一个单纯的、热心的“组织者”变成了一个真正坚强的城市领导。
警察、监狱、宣传部建立起来之后，一切都有序而高效地进行着。
此时，有人怂恿我签署最终的《效忠法案》，它可以让人民永远”满意“，不管你做什么。
我毫不犹豫地拒绝了：集中权力是为了克服困难，但它仍然有边界，让温情和人性有生存的空间。

在以我为核心的党中央坚强领导下，生产规模和效率都得到了迅速的发展，人民生活水平得到了实实在在的提高。
“安居工程”让所有的人民都住上了最温暖的房子；温室和飞行猎人让人民的伙食从稀糖提升为了干货；
三家蒸汽医疗所和四个诊所能让50人同时就医；三所科研机构同时运作让技术更新突飞猛进；
机器人的广泛运用既提高了效率又节约了人力；四家儿童活动中心既保护了孩子又让医院获得了额外的人力；

就在一切蒸蒸日上时，最后的挑战来了。我们坚强地迎接了挑战。
400多人7天的食物，要储备2800份口粮。考虑到可能还有新居民加入，我把目标定在了3500份，动员一切可以动员的力量，工程师干苦力，节约出工人当猎人，最终同志们超额完成任务，收集了4500份！
3个受困地点的群众全部救出，尽管很多人抱怨不该接收这些“负担”，因为他们全都重病在身。
迅速研发科技，在暴风雪到来前把保温科技全部点亮，机器人效率100%，各类设施保温基本完成。
在此过程中，同志们表现出了极高的工作热情和奉献精神，被抽调来紧急加班的研发中心工程师毫无怨言，斗志昂扬。

暴风雪来了，吃饭不是问题，难点在于供热和就医。
能量塔即使开到最高，在零下100度的低温下还是难以支持，只能通过过载来加温。但是过载只能持续约15个小时。
因此，只能晚上过载，白天恢复。为此，我把因暴雪闲赋在家的猎人们全部安排进了警察局、派出所、监狱和国有企业。
因为我知道，如果让他们白天待在家里，很可能冻死。而单位里面都有三级加热器和各种保温设施，不至于太冷。
生病是难免的，提高就医容量势在必行。由于没有蒸汽核心，因此一口气建立了8个诊所。
”党员干部（工程师“）冲在了第一线，机关里、国企里的工程师几乎都被派到了诊所。
关键时刻，面对恐慌和谣言，宣传部和派出所发挥了稳定器的作用，两天一次巡逻，三天一次宣传，人民的信心有效提振。
最后一天，气温骤降至零下120度，整个城市都冻住了，过载运行的能量核心也没法让人民摆脱严寒。
似乎一切都完了，设施都无法运行，好像没有希望了。
然而我鼓励着大家要保持信心。
因为我们已经做了一切可以做的，这种极端的天气不可能持久，否则不管你怎么做都无法通关，这个游戏就没有意义了。
不！游戏的设计者不会这么脑残！

终于，在早上八点，太阳出来了，大地回暖，一切都好起来了。
长吁一口气，甚至还有一点意犹未尽。
唯二比较遗憾的，一是没有在风暴来临前及时撤出先遣队和一只探险队，导致15人死亡。
二是三波来投靠的难民，只有第一波被全部接收，第二和第三波都只接收了健康者。
好游戏！

This is the mmo using the name of the greatest single player series made that is standing in the way of a 6th installment to the series. Nuf said.

As far as mmo's go, it is a pretty good game. Realistically though, there is no such thing as free to play. Expect to pay to get  more than a passing glimpse at the game because of storage and a few other issues. It is an mmo so you should know ahead of time say goodbye to your spending money and most of your free time if not all to get much out of it.

One of the great points to the single player series is that you level a character based on skills you use and there are (at least before skyrim er oblivion or whatever a lot of skills.) This one has classes with a few skills. The end. It winds up being more of a gear grinder, which is ok if that is what your game is... like say... diablo. As far as character progression on it's own goes this one feels really shallow.

It has quite a bit of crafting, but see paragraph 2 about storage. My biggest peave about the crafting is alchemy just is meh. In the single player it is the go to OP skill. 

If you aren't extremely active don't expect to be in a guild that gets a store bid every week so you can actually sell things and have money. In some cases you can get away with only logging in once a week for a few hours and still sell the minimum required by the guilds that successfully bid locations with stores that actually sell anything. There is no auction house so expect to spend a lot of time searching for that one piece to finish a set every few levels. 

The game has its good points. The combat is pretty good and there are lots of areas to explore. Some of the boss battles are innovative and fun. They leave you feeling like you accomplished something and sometimes even drop something useful. There is a great variety of enemies. It is story and lore rich. 

All in all if you know what you're getting into with an mmo it is worth it, but because of paragraph one and its many other  faults I can't give it a positive recommendation.

Ah, Hotline Miami.
It's a top-down shooter with lots of gore, lots of action, lots of badass music, and lots of confusing plot. But that's okay.

You're a guy (who is named Jacket by the fans and eventually by everyone) who lives in an alternate 1989 Miami who suddenly starts to get phone calls and a rooster mask. Totally not weird at all.
So, you obey the voices, and end up going on a slaughter spree that costs 307 Russian mobsters their lives. (I got the kill count from the Hotline Miami wiki, by the way.)
Along the way, you rescue some hooker who then becomes your girlfriend, you lucky bastard, an old friend of yours with a nice beard gives you free movies, pizzas, and drinks, and you find three people with animal masks; Richard, Don Juan, and Rasmus.
Richard's a cryptic sonuvabitch, Don Juan is actually nice to you sometimes, but Rasmus hates you. That's okay, because I don't like Rasmus either.
Richard asks you four questions, makes three predictions, and then eventually tells you that none of your actions matter because you're a bloody idiot. At least he sticks with you until the end.
Some assclown named Richter eventually shows up but I'm not spoiling anymore. Play for yourself.

Combat. Whew, this part's the best. You've got a pretty big variety of weapons to use, but not all guns are found on some levels. For example, you probably won't find the Silenced Pistol until the chapter Deadline. However, if you get crazy good scores on levels, you'll unlock more and more weapons, from hammers, to Skorpion SMGs, to beer cans that you can throw at people.
You die incredibly fast in Hotline Miami. But so do your enemies. One stray bullet from an Uzi can mean certain death, so rushing into rooms with an assault rifle really isn't a good idea. Guns make lots of noise, too. Melee weapons are much, much quieter.
You'll have to use guns sometimes, though. Just manage your ammo, but you may want to use the Peter mask if you love guns but don't want to have the entire map flocking to you.
There are boss fights every few chapters, and of course there's one at the end of Jacket's storyline.

Surprise, surprise, though, you get to play as Biker, who's actually the first boss fight in Jacket's story. Neither Biker nor Jacket die, by the way.
Biker just so happens to be in the same masked maniac boat as Jacket, and was trying to find the source of the phone calls. There are actually two endings to Biker's story but there will be no spoilers of that here.

This game excels tremendously with its atmosphere, visuals and sound design. I have never seen an open world game look so absolutely beautiful before. Wondering aimlessly in the woods is very, very satisfying for some reason. I'm only like 3 story missions in -- story isn't the greatest and I read that the ending of this game sucks, but honestly I could care less. The free roam aspects of FC5 are what stand out on top for me. 

When it comes to the weapons, the guns sound Battlefield-level of incredible quality. They have a really nice pop, are loud af as they are IRL, and have a strong low-end, which happens IRL, too. Too many games can't get gun sounds down. I'm a huge fan of the Metro series, but the guns sound weak and horrible in those games. FC5 is borderline God-tier when it comes to weapon sfx. Reloading could sound a little better, but it is still above acceptable. 

I know a lot of gamers want a good story in a game, but I am typically not one of those gamers. However I can appreciate a really good story, like The Last of Us or Bioshock, etc. Generally, in an open world game, I just want to f around, explore and have fun without following a story. The story in FC5, so far, is a bit weak. But like I said before, it doesn't bother me. The main thing I want out of a game is to be entertained and FC5 does that very well for me, even without the story. 

Atmosphere and visuals are so stunning. I can't get over it. Not only that, but the game seems to be optimized and runs quite well, even on my older GPU (R9 290). I get around 60fps on high. Visuals aren't even maxed out and I am still blown away. Ubisoft's environmental artists have improved dramatically over FC4 and 3, which saw huge performance losses in heavy vegetation. This was a huge issue in GTA V too outside of the city. But through advancements in graphics and related tech, this game is able to stream complicated and rich vegetation without huge performance losses. Kudos to Ubi for making that happen, since this game heavily relies on vegetation propagation. 

My complaints: wild animal AI and their animations are a bit weak, though it is improved over FC4. Friendly AI could be improved too. Enemy AI is hit or miss. Also, even though there are a few desolate areas, I do feel a lot of the map seems to be crammed with too much stuff, and too much of the same stuff. I wish things were spread out more, is basically what I am saying. Furthermore, I wish it got darker at night time. The moonlight is too bright. Lastly, some major wild animals don't feel like much of a threat like they did in FC3 (FC4 had this issue too). I wish the animals were more sneaky and quiet like they are IRL. A cougar isn't gonna growl at you a few seconds before it attacks to warn you. That mf is gonna sneak up on you, rush you and attack in under a second or 2. I am of course ignoring the fact that humans are not generally pray for cougars. Let's just assume we are common cougar snacks. I would love to be scared out of my skin from a surprise wild animal attack in the woods. Just doesn't really happen in this game. They all tend to give you a heads up before attacking. We all know the joke about drop bears. Put that in the game. Make these angry mf's drop from the treetops and slash your face open without you knowing just once or twice to keep you on edge in the future. That would be amazing and an unforgettable experience. Remember those eagle attacks in FC4? Where's stuff like that in FC5? Lack of surprise attacks is a big loss for this game.  

Overall, still, an amazing title. I can understand the complaints gamers have. I just personally don't relate to them. For $15 it was steal. Wait for the next sale and pick it up if you like open world shooters.

Conan exiles es un juego de supervivencia con tematica medieval basada a las obras de Robert E. Howard donde podremos encontrar un lore rico en su historía, mapa muy bien ambientado en el mundo de conan, nieve, desiertos, playas, bosques, junglas, todo podremos encontrar en este maravilloso juego.

Conan exiles tiene 3 modalidades de juego, el single player o juego local que nos permite jugar con amigos o tú solo, el modo pve donde puede entrar en servidores hasta 70 jugadores para construir y hacer tu cuidad, modo pvp que te permite atacar bases, destruirlas, robar todo lo que tienen y volverte un barbaro en su totalidad.

Elementos positivos:
- Un sistema climatico digno de un gran sandbox donde podremos tener lluvias en zonas humedas, nieve en zonas congeladas, tormentas de arenas en el desierto, sistema de día y noche con atardeceres hermosos y amaneceres igual de hermosos y todo estos nos afectara para sobrevivir en este mundo hostil lleno de fauna que nos atacara cada vez que nos acerquemos a una creatura.
- Lore
- Muchisimos jefes y mazmorras con diseño MMO
- la posibilidad de cambiar estadisticas que te permite ser tanque, asesino o un arquero.
- mucho contenido que se actualiza constantemente gracias al apoyo de la desarrolladora

Elementos Negativas:
- una gran cantidad de bugs que en servidores pvp son una molestia ya que se aprovechan para hacer trampas en el juego.
- Esto no es negativo del todo pero la realidad des que el juego en su modo pvp es cruel, puedes crear una base gigantesca pero llegar dos personas y destruirtela solo por que se quiere, no es malo ya que de esos se trata el modo pvp pero hay muchos que odian tanto eso que dejan el juego por dicho motivo.

Mało jest gier do których można się nie przyczepić. Taką właściwie jest TW Warhammer. Gra jest przede wszystkim innowacyjna, nie kopiuje jedynie elementów z poprzednich totalwarów, ale widać, że rozwija się. Różnorodność bohaterów, ich poziomowanie i ich bardzo duży wpływ na pole walki imponująca. Każdą nacją gra się inaczej, co jest niesamowite. Inaczej gramy krasnaludami, inaczej imperium, goblinami, nieumarłymi, inaczej chaosem. AI też nie jest aż tak złe - owszem mogłoby być nieco czasem lepsze, ale i tak biorąc pod uwagę masę wychodzących obecnie gier, to radzi sobie. Fajny motyw to, to że część miast ma oryginalne budowle, co aż kusi aby je zdobyć. Z gry wylewa się aż klimat warhammera. Twórcom udało się coś co wydawałoby się niemożliwe - przenieśli prawie że idealnie świat WH w ramy totalwara. Chciałbym aby nieco questów dla bohaterów i ogólnie questów było nieco więcej i bardziej różnorodnych, ale gra się rozwija i liczę, że z czasem będzie jeszcze lepsza. Polecam gorąco, bo gra wystarcza na wiele wieczorów. A właśnie jedna rzecz - gra jest prosta gdy wciskamy automatyczne bitwy, gdyż coś chyba algorytm zbyt mocno oblicza wynik automatycznej potyczki na korzyść gracza. To moim zdaniem mocno ułatwa rozgrywkę, więc polecam jak już gracie nie psujcie sobie zabawy i rozwiązujcie bitwy samodzielnie :)

app_name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
review:
相对于一作来说，增加了很多新的元素。
优点：
地图：感觉挺像空洞骑士的，不过比空洞骑士人性化很多（由于空洞的恶心跑图机制弃游了（才不是因为菜，手动滑稽））。
难度：相对于一作也下降了很多，也许是我变厉害了？看了下记录只死了200多次，在一作的大银树都死了一百多次，一作一共死了500多次吧。
剧情：中规中矩，没什么让人惊喜的地方，不过不影响打分。
画面：我tm吹爆！明明是2D的游戏，玩起来一点也没有2D的僵硬感。画面层次细节很多，算是我见过的2D游戏的巅峰了。
游戏内容：还算比较丰富的，28小时通关，但是从开始到结束一只有新的东西出现，并没有感觉到太明显重复性，可见制作团队是下了大功夫的。
手感：一个字，绝。从得到猛击开始，对于玩过一作的人来说，游戏应该才刚有一切尽在掌握的流畅感觉。滞空时的手感更是让人欲罢不能。而最后的炮弹跳跃更是让奥日的灵活度上了一个等级，一套行云流水的跑图简直是让强迫症患者无比舒适。也算是我心目中这个游戏最成功的地方了。
缺点：
翻译：呵□，□□□，但是□□，□□这么□□，□□□□□□。作为一个做了5年的游戏，汉化做成这个样子，真的让人挺失望的。
BUG：遇到过两个bug，一个是打祭坛的时候打着打着画面没了，声音还在。另一个是载入存到后不是原来存档的地方，而是在空中一只往下落。还好去网上查了下，发现有备份，回档了几分钟前的节点。
总的来说，还是不错的，应该支持。希望以后能继续有这种优秀的作品出现！

I don't really care much about the Creation Club because of the Nexus mod sites (and I'm a mod author myself) but I really hate what Fallout 4 has done to the Fallout genre. A voiced protaganist is a BIG NO NO for a true RPG (Mass Effect and other Bioware games do not count as they're Action games with RPG elements, the story won't change much in Mass Effect from what you do unlike Fallout). You can't immerse yourself in this game. The SPECIAL system is super weird now and to top off the problems with this game there wasn't even a HOLSTER animation! Are you joking? Is this 1995? The guns you holster just vanish!!! I don't know if this problem was fixed, I stopped playing about a month after this game came out.

What I did like was how you were able to talk and the world around you wouldn't stop (but this would prove to cause problems sometimes). VATS being in slow-mo rather than full time stop was cool too because it fixed the problems that existed with Fallout 3 (and a bit of NV). Aside that there is nothing memorable from this game and I've come to dispise Bethesda for what they've done. They've traded in their game identities in an attempt to mass market this game. The amount of hype this game got was stupidly over the limit. I saw way too many "fans" who never played any of the old games and called this the best Fallout there ever was. While I don't have a problem with those who haven't played any of the other fallouts I can tell you that I would rather play Fallout Tactics over this because there were more RPG elements assosicated with Tactics than this (for those of you who don't know Tactics was pretty much a turn-based shooter). 

Oh and how about the stupid fact that you don't know what your character is going to say in the chat menu? Or how about how you're only limited to Yes, No, Maybe later, and "sarcastic response"? What a pathetic excuse for an RPG, not even Mass Effect did something like that. While Mass Effect wasn't a true RPG at least the converastion trees were very interesting to the point that I would make extra save files so that I could try to experience them all.

Furthermore I hate what Fallout has done to the lore. In Fallout 3 and New Vegas they established that in order to effectively use Power Armor you would need to have training. Why does the female protaganist have the ability to USE POWER ARMOR? Why do the NPCs in your stupid first city get into your Power Armor and have the ability to use them? WHAT?!?! It's like they took it all out. Also for some reason Sarah Lyons *spoilers?* ended up dying by some super mutant attack or something? Idk about you but I would suspect she was backstabbed or something, they should not have killed her off like that and give more explanation to her story. *end of spoilers* But hey I don't know because I haven't touched this game since 2015.

What made the Fallout games good was how they were unique in their own way. Bethesda doesn't need to go out and copy Bioware, what they need to do is not throw Obsidian out on the curb and let them come back for Fallout 5. New Vegas was an INSANSELY good game and far superior to Fallout 3. While the world map of Fallout 3 was cooler than New Vegas, New Vegas's gameplay was so good that I still replay that game fully every year or so (with a bunch of mods of course) although I do replay Fallout 3 as well (mostly for the Mothership Zeta Crew mod).

Shame on Bethesda for throwing away the Fallout identity, I pray to the lords of gaming that they do NOT do this with The Elder Scrolls. Finally, get rid of that creation club nonsense, I can still find mods for FALLOUT ONE for FREE. They made mods for this game before I was even born and they were FREE. The microtransaction stuff is destroying the gaming community (reference Battlefront II) and I was hoping Bethesda was going to be better than that but it doesn't seem like it. 

I would NOT recommend buying this game. Go buy Fallout New Vegas (or Fallout 1 & 2 if you don't care about graphics, FO2 is a good amount of fun) and load it up with mods (Project Nevada and FOOK to start with, make sure to get the convergance mod). Obsidian knew how to make GOOD DLC (OWB was silly-stupid though and GRA may not be your cup of tea) so do give Dead Money, Honest Hearts, and Lonesome Road a try. Dead Money has survival-horror (especially if you have Project Nevada tossed in), Honest Hearts has an extremely interesting character (Grahm), and the Lonesome Road is downright amazing.

The developers behind this game, quit your job and work somewhere else (try Bioware since you seem to love trying to copy from them) OR play the old Fallouts and stop trying to steal from other game series. Fallout is its own game with its own identity, it should not try to steal from other game series.

This game is always going to be very divisive when it comes to reviews so I will try to give my honest assessment on the basic pros and cons as someone who was skeptical and very wary of this game until I saw it was on deep sale and got it on a whim and not as a fanboy.

-PROS-
>The art style is amazing, hands down. Learning that a team of ~6 people made this is astounding given how much thought is put into each character, enemy, and animation. It has a unique color pallete that conveys the darkness and hopelessness of the game world while not being too bland and full of browns and greys (looking at you Fallout 3).
>The narrator who plays the ancestor is out of this world, even after beating the game and going back for round 2 I still do not get tired of his lines.
>Once you get the hang of the gameplay it becomes very addictive mid-to-late game. Jumping into dungeons and challenging yourself by going torchless or shaking up your party to something outside your comfort zone is refreshing once you have mastered the basics of the game.
>The stress system is a really cool take on dungeon crawling, and although it adds difficulty on top of an already hard game, it really does make sense. If you were exploring dank dungeons all day crawling with eldritch horrors, your sanity would definitely be in question after a few slimy tentacle swipes from a Cthulian horror or two.
>Stat/RNG nerds will have a field day here. There are literal spreadsheets that exist to crunch numbers for your SPD, CRT chance, optimal trinkets, etc. and it really does feel like you are playing an interactive game of DnD with a lovecraftian twist. On the flipside to that...

-CONS-
>Stat/RNG...you either love it or hate it and since the entire gameplay system is based around it, if numbers based combat isn't for you, you will hate this game with a passion. All your heroes will miss, the enemies will simultaneously crit your weakest hero one after the other, your healer will roll a zero and inflict bleeding instead...I could go on. It's all part of the experience however, and this is the reason most people seem to dislike this game. Whether or not the enemies get better RNG than you through intentional design is up for debate.
>Early game is kind of a mess. The game explains almost nothing aside from a couple super basic actions in the tutorial. Once you get to the estate, it throws you to the wolves without a clue on what you should upgrade first, how to manage your heroes optimally, the trinket system...nothing. For a first playthrough it is pretty rough, even compared to the likes of Dark Souls. Would recommend skimming a beginners guide online if you don't want to have to wipe on your first attempt and start over. 
>The story is underwhelming, mediocre at best. Without going into too many spoilers, most significant things happen in the endgame and the entire early/mid period will just be you grinding procedurally generated dungeons to level up heroes and hoard heirlooms and gold to upgrade your town. There is a twist at the very end that saves the plot from total disappointment, however lore will be few and far between up until then, mostly found through trinket descriptions and boss dungeon intros explaining the origin behind the creatures. 

So that is the basic gist of this game coming from someone who loves hard games but was hesitant to buy this one due to unfavorable reviews lambasting the "unfairness" of the game and how it just punishes you without rhyme or reason. I will recommend this game with a caveat-it's not for everyone, and if you are someone who can't stand failure you will not enjoy constantly having hero wipes from brutal RNG that is totally outside your control. If it's your first roguelike then I would approach with some caution as there is a lot of menu scrolling and number crunching involved that is just not present in other types of games. Otherwise, a cool game overall with a lot of unique takes on the genre that have never been seen before along with a great art style and atmosphere. 

-OVERALL-
8/10, would recommend only to players more on the hardcore side.

Joguei o jogo com um grupo de amigos cada um fazendo sua parte, sendo a minha explorar a dungeon do jogo, devido as minhas constantes explorações acabava chegando muito tarde em casa, uma vida dificil contudo honesta.
sempre que conseguia algo interessante na dungeon guardava para a haley, posso dizer que minhas varias horas de jogo foram em grande parte dedicadas a ela.
Agora vem a parte curiosa, sempre que eu ia atras da haley eu encontrava outra pessoa nas redondezas, linus o mendigo talarico, de inicio eu pensei "deve ser apenas uma coincidencia" o tipico pensamento de um corno. Linus estava sempre perto da haley oq por si so ja pode ser considerado estranho, contudo eu so fui capaz de conectar esses pontos no dia que iria me declarar para haley, nesse dia sai cedo da dungeon e fui atras dela, ao chegar perto da casa dela, ele apareceu o falso amigo, o mendigo talarico, o mal antigo, Linus, apos seu aparecimento uma cutscene começou o que me impediu de me declarar naquele dia.
Devido a esse triste incidente eu percebi a proximidade entre o amor da minha vida haley e o mendigo talarico linus.
Stardew valley foi uma lição de vida para mim, percebi que devemos ficar sempre atentos a nossos ditos "amigos" e que devemos dedicar mais tempo para nos mesmos, apos aquele triste incidente eu pude juntar dinheiro reformar minha casa aumentar minha plantação e parti rumo a riqueza, espero que na proxima atualização nos seja revelado esse relacionamento secreto entre o linus e a haley.

Valve did it again.

This game set a new course for gaming as a whole.
I'm calling it now : the PS5 and Xbox Series X are the last console generation before VR goes mainstream.

Mark my words.



DETAILS :

The first thing i saw when opening the game was a "low GPU memory warning", saying i should shut down other programs to be able to play properly. They were right. My GTX1070's 8Go of VRAM were consistently used at >85%, but the game still held 120Hz on medium-high settings.

And that's freaking black magic considering the thing basically looked photorealistic on my Valve Index. The controls are pretty much perfected to the extreme. VR games usually come with their fair share of jank, like trying to put things in your backpack and they just fall on the ground behind you, or physics objects kind of freaking out when you push them against others, ...

Not. Even. Once. Items ALWAYS land in my backpack, objects ALWAYS behave the way you'd expect and best and most surprising of all, this game induces VR sickness at like 5% the usual rate. Seriously, i played VR for the first time in over a month and played this 3h straight and was completely fine after that which is unusual for me. I don't have a clue of how they do it. They pretty much have cleared the uncanny valley and manage to fool my brain.

So, the technical implementation of VR is perfect. Good, but how's the actual game ?
It's a Half Life game. Everything looks and sounds beautiful, the game design constantly challenges you and makes you think, the attention to detail is just unprecedented. I'll come back when i've finished it and edit this review to comment about the story, but right now i've got nothing to be disappointed about.

Actually, there is ONE thing. You can enable continuous movement in the options, but not continuous rotation, which i would have liked, but that's completely a nitpick.




This game lives up to the Half Life name and paves the way for what's to come.

What a time to be alive.


EDIT : They added smooth turning within 48h of release because the community asked for it. The madlads are still at it. Guys, take a break, you've earned it ! XD

EDIT 2 : THE STORY. Oh boy. It starts out slow, the game just gives you a reason to push forward and then...

Let's just say it's worth it. Don't get spoiled.

Put in countless hours on PS4, and now some on PC. I LOVE this game.

GOOD
-You can customize any of your soldiers, and even set up a soldier pool of customized soldiers for you to recruit. For example, I recruited a DOOM Slayer, the crew from Firefly, and other custom soldiers.
-You can progress. Each soldier upgrades to a class from 'Rookie'. Then, they specialize around certain playstyles (big guns, gadgets, sniper, etc.) You can choose from one of two ability choices each time the soldier levels up. So you may, for example, spec your sniper to actually utilize his sidearm more usefully, or focus on his long-range abilities.
-Custom soldiers makes a real sense of loss when your soldiers die.
-The strategy and tactics are fun. Trying to arrange my soldier in a perfect ambush setup, or taking high ground for my sniper while way-too-many enemies close in. You can really use strategy to take control in the battlefield, and you'll find yourself getting much better at this as you go.
-Sound design and voice acting is not prominent, but is good. You're in a battle and you hear fire, or a panicked soldier yell, or a building collapse from a fire you started. It all sounds good.
-Graphics are great - zero complaints. I'd like more customization options, but you can find these for free in Workshop.

BADS
-It's a meme but percentages really seem to screw you over. 97% - MISS. But this is just something you need to get used to. I've learned to sometimes risk taking the shot with 40% chance of hit, and it can pay off. But it sometimes feels like a huge blow.
-Not enough autosaves. You have three autosaves that trigger each turn (this turn, last turn, two turns ago). Sometimes, it takes 10 turns before you realize you have no chance of winning this way. Nothing to do but restart or take the L, because rewinding three turns is just not enough.
-The UI at your hub isn't terrible, but it isn't good. Scrolling can be annoying. But you are only here between missions.

gta5的经典性与开创性毋庸置疑，它为新世代大型开放游戏的制作提供了很多崭新的思路或者说是创举。仅就我个人而言，我最欣赏它其中偌大的故事结构、超凡的叙事方式、自然和谐的统一性以及做到极致的细节，可以说这些内容对于一个6年前的“老”游戏是不可思议的，即使放在开放世界层出不穷、丰富任务无穷无尽的大型游戏比比皆是的今天，gta5中流畅的运行模式和尽力避免单调刻板的某些细节手段都是令人称赞的。我们仍可以看到，直到今天R星仍在gta5内容的拓展与创新上投入着巨大精力和成本，无数的新兴玩家仍在延续着这部经典之作的传奇热销，不少人的硬盘里压着这样一个令人充满回忆的箱底。
即使这样，gta5仍有许多难以忽视的问题。像故事剧情的大部分暴力血腥与主人公若隐若现的亲情友情等一些生活基本情感之间的相融，在较短的叙述和极大的开放性当中难以平衡，一些涉及到正面情愫的故事场景略显多余或是不适。当然在以犯罪为主题的gta系列当中，这样的纠结也似乎不值一提，对于大部分玩家来说，享受游戏打来的快感与满足已是发掘出该作的价值。且不谈游戏中绝大多数房屋无法探索，就是某些经典建筑内部的场景也缺乏细化，尤其是房屋内与人物的互动太过偏向于公式化，远不及在街头漫步带来的随机故事触发。提高游戏ai的智能性是大部分玩家也是开放游戏必然面对的诉求，在充实游戏自由度上，像某些游戏的多过程多结局性就值得借鉴，很希望R星能在保持游戏高画质的方向上为游戏增添一些策略性，在单纯的打杀中建立新的更加注重过程的游玩机制。由于我线上模式玩的时间很少，没有勇气对线上模式指点一二，还是要说gta5真的是一个很好很好的游戏！

Auch Leuten, die nichts mit Res anfangen können??? Und dies war hier der Fall! Die Idee dies in Ego Perspektive zu machen war das beste, was die Entwickler hätten machen können!!! Zu den Entwicklern:
Es ist finde ich extrem wichtig, dass sich Spiele wie dieses hier gut verkaufen, damit die Entwickler merken, dass die Spieler mehr hiervon haben wollen! Wir brauchen mehr AAA+ Horrorgames auf dem Markt und weniger von diesen billigen Indiespielen, wo man so richtig merkt, dass die Entwickler sich keine Mühe gegeben haben oder einfach zu wenig Zeit gelassen haben. My first impressions (coming from other Paradox games like EU-IV and CK2):

#1: The UI is somewhat messy. Anything new takes time to learn, but in this case I feel like there are genuine issues in Stellaris. After CK2, Paradox seemed to realize that the UI they put out is sometimes needlessly complex or even sometimes redudant in sections. Hence, EU-IV did a decent job of presenting tons of info in a simple manner, and HoI-IV, whatever its other issues, made info extremely easy to get at. Then Stellaris comes along and throws info at me from every which direction, sometimes without sufficient tool-tips (and yes, I left the beginner's stuff on and didn't skip over it). Again, part of it is just me being new, but the default map screen, the way subscreens are accessed, etc., is all a bit clunkier than the last couple games.

#2: Surprisingly, then, I have to admit: the screens for setting up the game and choosing universe size and so on, are actually perfect. I can choose my empire or build a new one; if I build a new empire, I can elect to have it be forbidden from being played by the CPU; I can choose the percentage of planets that will be habitable. The options are concise, include anything I could think of that really matters that much. For one of the few games Paradox has done that has procedural generation for elements, I'm pleasantly surprised that they nailed it straight out of the gates as far as settings.

#3: Early game has a lot to do, but is strangely slow. Probably just me, but I'm used to immediately having enemy countries at my door, or the Spanish Civil War to send a Panzer or two at in order to intervene. It took a decent chunk of time just to spot any other factions, though this could be luck-of-the-draw for my first game.

#4: I just got this on sale, and picked up all content-adding DLC along with it. So keep in mind that my reaction is based on everything, not just the vanilla game. 


Overall, recommending thus far, but really have to get a dozen hours or so in on it to make any suggestion worth bothering to read.

Das Spiel macht zu Beginn noch Spaß, aber irgendwann macht man immer nur noch dasselbe (Forschung, Divisionen etc.). Das Spielgefühl ist mit jedem Land eigentlich genau gleich, es fühlt sich nicht historisch an, außerdem stören die unhistorischen "Zahlen": Die USA hatten Ende des Zweiten Weltkrieges ungefähr 100 Divisionen. In Hearts of Iron IV kann man mit den Vereinigten Staaten aber ohne viel Aufwand 400 Divisionen ausbilden.  Dass man eine Welteroberung mit Ländern wie Luxemburg und/oder Tanu Tuwa machen kann stört auch sehr. Sandbox ist gut, aber dennoch braucht es Grenzen. Die Luftwaffe, welche sehr wichtig während des Zweiten Weltkrieges war, ist kaum von Bedeutung. Wenn man genügend Divisionen hat, ist die Luftwaffe nicht ausschlaggebend. Dasselbe gilt für die Marine und auch für Panzer. Geschichte ist kaum vorhanden und das Spiel fühlt sich wie eine leere Hülle an, bei Paradox ist das ein Hinweis auf eine Menge DLCs. Das (für mich) interessanteste Land des Zweiten Weltkrieges, Manchukuo (Marionettenstaat von Japan, wo der letzte Qing Kaiser von China, Puyi, das Staatsoberhaupt stellt), gibt es nicht. Die Kriegsführung ist eintönig, Ressourcen in Afrika und und im Nahen Osten sind nicht vorhanden. Dies macht die Eroberung von europäischen Kolonien sinnlos. Dennoch muss ich sagen, dass der Industrieteil des Spieles sehr gelungen ist. Fazit: kastriertes HoI3, nett zum ansehen, aber kein Strategiespiel (aufgrund unfähiger KI)

É difícil falar sobre um jogo quando a experiência com ele é tão pessoal e cada um é livre pra ter a própria interpretação do que vê, mas ainda posso afirmar que apesar de ser divertido e necessário usar a lógica para sair de alguns pontos particularmente difíceis, é impossível não lidar com um misto de emoções durante a jornada de Gris, principalmente quando entramos no tema da perda, do luto e da superação.

Gris é uma garota que, aparentemente, sofreu uma perda trágica e agora não está sabendo lidar com essa terrível situação. Ela está quebrada em milhões de pedaços, não tem mais forças, não tem mais voz, está perdida e se encontra num vazio total, sem vida e sem cor. Sendo assim, Gris vai abordar o luto e seus cinco estágios de uma forma tão sutil quanto sublime, por isso, se forem embarcar nessa (o que recomendo muito), preparem os lencinhos.

O cenário em si representa a própria mente e os sentimentos de Gris, e a medida que ela avança, vai mudando de cor, toma forma mas se quebra novamente, se afunda num abismo escuro e sombrio cada vez mais fundo, vira de cabeça pra baixo, mas sempre existe aquela luz, aquela estrela que está escondida em algum lugar que vai dar a ela forças e abrir o caminho, basta que ela se esforce pra encontrá-la e, assim, poder escapar dessa escuridão que está literalmente a engolindo. E enquanto Gris enfrenta alguns desafios, ela vai se recompondo enquanto adquire ou recupera habilidades que haviam sido perdidas nesse processo. O mais incrível é que às vezes ela precisa usar ou enfrentar exatamente aquilo que a assusta ou a persegue para conseguir superar um determinado desafio e conseguir avançar.

O intuito do jogo não é fazer com que a protagonista passe por perigos a ponto dela morrer ou coisa do tipo, mesmo que ela caia da maior altura que existe ou se enfie no buraco mais fundo ever. Não há nenhum fator aqui que faça com que Gris perca a vida ou fique presa sem ter como escapar, mesmo que a gente dê mil voltas, sempre vai ter uma saída, basta ter atenção pra resolver o quebra-cabeças. Talvez o ponto que não agrade tanto seja o fato de não haver muitos caminhos a serem explorados e o jogo ser bastante linear, ou seja, você vai pra frente, pra trás, pra cima ou pra baixo, o lugar onde se deve chegar sempre vai ser o mesmo, mas ainda assim, a arte faz com que todos os sentimentos dela sejam bastante evidentes e a jornada seja incrível.

Não dá pra deixar de falar da trilha sonora desse jogo. Sem ela eu tenho certeza que a experiência e a imersão não seriam as mesmas. As músicas se adaptam linda e perfeitamente ao cenário e vão se transformando conforme o progresso, e quando Gris finalmente recupera a voz e consegue cantar, minha gente, é difícil controlar as emoções...

Eu finalizei esse jogo emocionada, cheia de lágrimas nos olhos, tanto pela arte que passei contemplando durante essa jornada quanto pela forma sensível de superação de todas essas adversidades. E talvez essa experiência ainda seja mais intensa caso o jogador já tenha passado por algo do tipo. Em diversos momentos eu enxerguei a mim mesma e acredito que esse tenha sido o motivo de ter mexido tanto comigo.

Gris é uma obra de arte, a experiência é única, e a sensação que vai aflorar aqui vai fazer desse jogo algo simplesmente inesquecível.

I Einleitung

Civ V ist die Fortsetzung der glorreichen Civilization Reihe von Sid Meier.. Es ist primär ein Rundenbasiertes Strategiespiel. 
Als Langjähriger Spieler dieser Reie werde ich mich hier stärker auf unterschiede zu den Vorausgegangenen Teil Civ IV Konzentieren. Für Civ Neulinge wird daher dieser Review nur bendingt nützlich sein. 

II Die Story,
Das Spiel beginnt wie schon im ersten Teil, die Erde ist Wüst und leer.. Doch irgendwann finden sich die Menschen zusammen und Organsiieren sich zu einer Zivilisation.. Nun kommst du ins Spiel als der Herrscher, wird ein Volk über die Zeiten überdauern? Welche Herausforderungen wird die Reise über die Jarhunderte bringen? Lass uns nun die Reise im Jahr 4000 v. Chr. beginnen. 

III Das Gameplay,
Civilization bietet verschiedene Spielmodi. Neben einigen vordefinierten Szenarios wird ein Single Player Modus mit Zufällig generierbaren Karten und Spieleparametern einem Multiplayer Modus. Der Multiplayer kann sowol über Lan wie Internet stattfinden so wie auch über E-Mail oder HotSeat also 2 Spieler an einem Computer. Der Übersichtlichkeit halber gehe ich jedoch hier auf dem Einzelspielermodus auf einer Zufällig generierten Karte. 

Single Player
Das Spiel beginnt irgendwo auf einem Fleck der Karte umgeben von unerkundeter Gegend die vom Nebel verschleiert ist. Zum Anfang werden je nach Schwierigkeits Grad einen Einheiten zur verfügung gestellt. Normalerweise ein Siedler, für die erste Stadt und ein Krieger als Militäreinheit. 
Dann geht es los, die erste Stadt gründen und dabei folgenschwehre entscheidungen für die weiterendwicklung deiner Zivilisation fällen, also wo gründe ich die Stadt, welche Resurcen möchte ich erschließen, welche Einrichtungen bzw. Einheiten möche ich bauen?
Neben den besiedeln der Karte und bauen von Einheiten, kann der Spieler sein Reich durch Straßen und einrichtungen auf dem Land ausbessern, desweiteren gibt es Wissenschaft, Kulur, Religion, etc.. das Überschaubare Spiel wird mit der Zeit immer Komplexer.. Wenn die Runden anfänglich nur wenige Sekunden gedauert haben werden sie hin zum Spielende immer länger.
Natürlich seid ihr nicht auf der Karte allein. Es gibt Computergegner, entweder als Barbaren, Staatstaaten und natürlich andere Zivilisationen. Je nach euerer Vorstellung könnt ihr z.B. durch die Unterwerfung der kompletten Welt das Spiel gewinnen. 

Mulit Player..
Der Mulitplayer von Civ V ist ähnlich wie der SP nur das es diesmal weniger Animationen z.B. bei Einheitenkämpfen gibt.. Je nach Modus z.B. durch Simultane Bewegungen in der Spielrunde kann es sein das deine Einheiten vom Gegner getötet werden bevor du sie wegbewegen konntest. Vom feeling spielt sich Civ V im Mulitplayer wie CIV II von 1996.

IV Unterschiede von Civ V zu Civ IV

Auf dem ersten Blick erscheint Civ V aufgeräumter und übersichtlicher als sein Vorgänger. Es gibt weniger Details, auch weniger Animationen z.B. bei Weltwundern. Die Karte ist nicht mehr in Kästchen sondern in Hexfelder unterteilt. Desweiteren gibt es viele kleine Spielerreihen wie z.B. die Wegzoom Ansicht mit der Weltkugel nicht mehr. Die Klassische bedinenung der Spiels über die Tastatur und Num Tastenfeld funktioniert bedingt. 

Nach dem ersten schnellen durchspielen einer Partie stellt man fest dass das Spiel an vielen Punkten vereinfacht wurde, damitt der Einstieg für neue Spieler leichter ist. So hatte ich den eindruck das Barbaren weniger agressiv sind. Die KI ebenfalls weniger auf Krieg ausgerichtet ist, habe nur einmal erlebt das mich ein Gegner unangekündigt angegriffen hat. 

Hier sind noch einige weitere Punkte die mir aufgefallen sind, (Kein anspruch auf Vollständigkeit)

- Transportschiffe fallen Weg, da sich Einheiten nun mit der Passenden Technologie sowohl über Land wie Wasser bewegen können.
- Weniger Einheiten insgesamt bzw. und auch keine Möglichkeit mehr beliebig viele Einheiten auf einem Feld zu plazieren. (auch in Städten)
- Es ist leichter wieder die ganze Karte mit Städten voll zu klotzen..
- Städte können sich nun selbst verteidigen.
- Weniger Technologien und kürzere Zitate zu den Technologien 
- Die Regierungen und die Religionen werden nun individuell aus dem Baukasten zusammengebaut.
- Es gibt keine Kapitalgesellschaften mehr.
- Neben Geld und Wissenschaft gibt es jetzt Freue, Kultur, Tourismus und Glauben die ausgebaut werden können. 
- Wieele Weltwunder... 
- Staatstaaten als kleine Zivilisation

Insgesamt hatte ich den Eindruck das der Schwehrpunkt von CIV V weniger im Kriegerrischen als in der Diplomatie und Kultur liegt. Durch z.B. die Kleinen Staatstaaten steht man ständig in Interessenskonflikten. 

V Grafik, Sound etc..

Die Grafik war noch die die Stärke der Civ reihe, so ist es auch in Civ V, auf mich wirkt die Grafik wie ein Facelift vom alten Civ  IV dabei sind die Texutren etwas höher auflösend aber ansonsten nichts was einem vom Hocker reicht. Ich Spiele Civ wegen den Kopfkino wie ein gutes Brettspiel weniger wegen der Grafik. 
Auch das ganze Spielgeschehen ist etwas Statisch, daher sind längere Runden sogar recht für die Augen ermüdend. Es gibt weder Tag/Nacht Rytmus noch Jahreszeiten die auf dem Bildschirm zwischen Blau, Grün und Blau für etwas abwechslung sorgen könnten. 
Die Performance, ist naja.. Trotz der recht simplen Grafik zieht das Spiel in der späteren Phase ordentich Leistung, so kann sein das manchmal die Menüs etwas träge reagieren. 
Soundtechnisch, gibt es miestens eine Musikalische Untermalung passend zur Zivilisation und Epoche in welcher man spielt. Wenn man z.B. Klassik mag kann es ganz entpsannend sein. Der Sondtrack ist aber zum Glück nicht so eintönig wie in Civ IV. Bei Krieg ändert sich etwas die Soundkulisse sie wird ernster, und auch die panischen Schreie z.B. bei der Belagerung einer Stadt wirken recht bedrückend. 

VI Fazit:
Ich denke das CIV V schon im Angebot oder als gesamtpaket sein Geld wert ist, daher würde ich von einem Kauf nicht abraten, jedoch bietet das Spiel für den Stammspieler nicht viel neues. Ich hatte den Eindruck das es das Beste ein bischen von allen Civ Teilen ist: also weniger ist mehr und nur ganz vorischtig versucht neuerungen einzuführen, euch wenn ich denke das ein Rundrum redesign der Spielreihe sehr gut tun würde.
Firaxis hat es damals mit Civ IV bewiesen das es noch ein brauchbares Civ Spiel liefern kann, ingegensatz zu Civ III wleches eine Katastrophe war. Jedoch bietet Civ V eine vorsichtige Evolution aber keine Revolution. Fesselnd ist das Spiel torzdem wie jedes Civ von anfang an. Vom gefühl spielt es sich ähnlich entspannend wie Civ II.. also wer ein bischen die Welt nach Feierabend erobern will warum nicht?
Was mir aber Fehlt sind Inovation und Humor.. wie griffige Sprüche bei den Technologien, oder Elemente wie Kapitalgesellschafen mit so sinnlosen Namen wie Sid Sushi & Co.

[u]Short version[/u]
Getting started is easy. Piecing things together is captivating. Continued discovery will easily put your playtime in the hundreds of hours.

[u]Long version[/u]
[h1]Presentation[/h1]
Isaac is a game of feces, blood, urine, and so many tears. The graphical ichor and squishy sound effects are a polished iteration of their Flash origins, which works just fine. Creature sprites are twisted and endlessly creative, while level aesthetics set a distinct mood. What's truly impressive here is that each of the >100 unlockable items will add its own aesthetic to your character, meaning that your randomized collection of pickups is quickly going to result in an entirely unique (and often grotesque) appearance.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The game starts off simply, and builds to a staggering height of complexity and strategy. At first you might be reminded of a dungeon from the original Legend of Zelda, with top-down perspective rooms and basic enemy patterns. As you proceed through randomized iterations of this concept, you'll gradually unlock items which improve your attacks and attributes, or sometimes completely change the way you approach the run. This game is at its absolute best when you discover an amazing combination of items, like one that turns your basic shot into a huge laser, and another that fires that shot in every direction at once. There's also plenty of opportunity to learn the game's rules, and squeeze every bit of advantage possible out of a level by deciding a meticulous order in which to activate your discoveries.

[h1]Story[/h1]
What little story this game has to tell is narrated during startup. You won't be watching cutscenes until the end of your run, and even those won't offer much insight or closure to the tale. That being said, there is a rich "implied" lore here, drawing significance from character and item names, much of which originates in biblical mythology. You might enjoy reading what other users piece together from subtle hints, but the in-game experience has little to do with this resulting tale.

[h1]Meta[/h1]
There is a lot to do in this game, and new players are going to die a lot. The luck of the item drops will determine much of the run's challenge, but you'll definitely find yourself growing in skill and memorizing enemy behavior over time. Losing can be infuriating, but that means your victories feel earned. If you're a completionist like me, be aware that the game's deepest secrets were intended for communal exploration, and that it's unrealistic to seek them on your own. Discovery is the heart of what makes this game great, but don't strain your brain trying to solve the final puzzle - I rarely offer such advice, but just check a guide and spoil it for yourself once you've accomplished most everything else.

This is a game that might take a minute to get used to, but it is by far worth the effort. I wasn't sold at first, while I was getting used to the systems in place and learning the ropes, but over time I've come to really cherish the co-op gameplay that can be had here. Weirdly enough, it's still in early development but I feel that there is already a full game's worth of content. Definitely for a 25 dollar game anyway, and they're still hard at work expanding the content to be had. The biomes are varied, distinguished, and interesting; they aren't just a different color set, they all behave differently and provide unique challenges in and of themselves. The bugs (or whatever they're called) are also a lot of fun to shoot and have a bunch of different archtypes to keep things interesting. Anything from armoured opponents, to little flying bastards that shoot you with acid globs, to swarms of little ankle biters that can overrun a poorly coordinated team or isolated player. The sound design, in terms of shooting and mining, is meaty and very satisfying. The minigun in full roar, as well as the other guns, sound as they should sound and the metallic 'ting' of collecting minerals all seems very fitting, and adds to the addictive nature of a 'minecraft-meets-L4D' game.  

As far as teamwork goes, each class seems to work seamlessly with the other, creating a co-op environment that can support a large variety of 'meta' teams based on the mission objective/game mode (of which there are a bunch to pick from; surprising for an EA game). As an aside in terms of the co-op nature of the game, the community is also amazingly receptive to new players and is, in my experience, very laid back and willing to help new players out. I will be playing this game for a long time to come and look forward to the updates as we get closer to an official 1.0 release.  

All in all I highly recommend this game. As a veteran of L4D, L4D2 and Vermintide 1 & 2, this is some of the best 4 player co-op fun to be had but in a highly unique setting. Especially for the pricetag, even if you don't have friends to play with, it is well worth a shot.

As many have stated before, HOI4 is a fun game to play if you are relatively new to the series and just want to mess around. However, when you really look at the gmae closely, you tend to notice a lot of issues that have yet to be fixed or even added to the game a year after its release.

Cons
-The AI is laughable. So bad that CIV VI AI looks good. Grand battle plan just doesn't work. The units that you have carefully placed along the French border? All decided to come together at one district, or just hopscotch between districts because AI doesn't know what "forward advance" means, thus leaving an entire front wide open for flanking. Or better yet, the AI will reorganize its army to have reinforcements go to a part of the front that does not require any reinforncements, thus leaving the crucial part of the front that actually needs reinforcement, wide open for being overrun.

-Bordergore. If you want to see some art..er I mean...unfathomable and illogical map carving, I encoruage you to check it on Reddit or simply Google it.

-Lots of minor nations are just meh, and not entirely enjoyable to play. It'd help if they had some interesting focus trees that does not require me to shell out $10-$15 just to "enhance" my gameplay

-Some of the major powers don't feel exciting to play, especiialy when you comapre the focus trees to what the Community offers (Look at Vanilla Gemrany focus tree and then look at Edelweiß's "Germany Techtree overhaul. It offers way more focuses that are logically and fun to use, rather than some lackuluster focuses.)

-DLCs are overpriced for what they barely offer. I don't understand why I should pay $10-$15 for game features that should have been in the game Day 1, as well as play nations that should have had their focus tree fleshed out from the start. Seriously, just to play any other Commenwealth nation (Australia, New Zealand, Canada, South Africa, and India), have the concept of Autonomy (become an independant nation) in play, as well as Battle Combat Logs, One new tactical attack option, and Tech sharing, you need to cough up $15. Paradox...dude, you're like EA now.

Pros:
-I honestly can't think of a postitive thing since the things that I like about this game, is greatly overshadowed by the amount of trouble and bugs that this game has. Maybe the workshop and the mods that are offered? Yeah that's the actual good thing about this game. The modding cumminuty that actually fixes the game and makes it interesting.

TL:DR
-Game is fun if you never played HOI before, and do not give a crap about some missing features. However, if you want said features (that should've been present since Day 1), expect to pay up half the price of a AAA title just for some few lines of codes to work in your game, and maybe some interesting/lackluster nations to play.

EDIT: Oh and they also jacked the price up in some regions, thus nullifying the benefit of a Summer Sale. Expect Jim F-ing Sterling-son to make a video about this.

I recently downloaded FTL from Steam; it caught my eye because I’ve always liked the idea of being the captain of my own space ship. This game is highly addictive when I first started playing I continued playing for several hours. The graphics of the game feel a little retro but for a $9 they don’t feel cheap.  You get a top view of your spaceship as you tell your crew where to go, allocate power, chose augments and weaponry for your vessel.  
	You play as a Federation captain running from the rebel fleet in an ever increasing right hand direction with vital information about the rebels. I thought it was a nice touch to not be a member of the rebel force. Each solar system has a Dungeons and Dragons feeling encounter where you can make decisions to help ships, investigate asteroid fields and debate whether or not to fight slavers and pirates or buy their wares.
	The flaws in the gameplay can also be one of the things that make it so addicting which is the randomness in the gameplay.  Some aliens are better at fighting or repairing but you may play through the entire campaign without encountering them, the same thing with the weaponry. Some weapons can cut through several rooms or cause breaches but you might never see them. Randomness in core gameplay just doesn’t work it forces the game to walk the line of emersion and frustration; I kept playing trying to find different routes just to unlock new ships and layouts.
	If you’re a fan of real time strategy, sci-fi, and inexpensive games that are still fun than give FTL a try.

[h1]Meine ausführliche Review zu Rainbow Six Siege[/h1]

[h1]PRO:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Gute Grafik
[*]Hochwertige Optimierung
[*]Angenehme Waffen Dynamik
[*]Viele Maps
[*]Kurze Ladescreens (bis auf den INS Spiel)
[*]Viele taktische Elemente (Aufspreng- und aufschießbare Wände, blend Möglichkeiten, Mobile Schilde ...)
[*]Viele Funktionen, Operator & Waffen
[*]Das Menü ist Angenehm.
[*]Teamplay ist endlich wirklich wichtig
[*]Der sound ist mir zwar VIEL zu unklar (wie unten erläutert), aber man kann ALLES hören was der Gegner macht. Alle Waffen unterscheiden sich vom Schussgeräusch, auch die Schrittgeräusche unterscheiden sich von den Operator. Man kann unterscheiden ob es ein 1,2 oder 3 Speed Operator ist. EGAL WAS, du kannst es unterscheiden und zuordnen was er macht.
[*]Zerstörung; Diese sieht ziemlich gut aus, es gibt weiche und harte wände und man kann durch Boden und weiche wände z.B. schießen.
[/list]

[h1]KONTRA:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Als erstes mal die Bugs die seit Jahren im Spiel sind und bis heute nicht behoben wurden. Drohnen die direkt vor der Bombe stehen können die Bombe trotzdem nicht spoten erst wenn man zwischen den Drohnen hin und her switched. Nervig. Gegnerische tote Spieler haben den Kopf in der Wand usw. könnte meine ganze Review nur mit der Erwähnung von irgendwelchen Bugs füllen. (Habe auch bildfehler gescreenshoted)
[*]Die Spieler sind oft echt Lächerlich scheiße, vor allem im RANKED. Ich freue mich immer über gesprächige Personen die mir oder dem Team helfen(gibt auch korrekte Personen), aber diese dummen Kinder die sich freuen wenn sie jemanden mit der Pistole töten und sich dann im Chat feiern oder Personen die nichts als Beleidigungen bringen, nerven nicht nur, sondern Zerstören einem das ganze Spielerlebnis. Vor allem die Konzentration im Ranked lässt gerade dann nach. Lustig auch, das im "Schnelles Spiel/Casual" man sowas kaum hat aber im "RANKED" fast nur. Das melden der Spieler sollte vor allem im Ranked genauer untersucht werden. Diese "Meldungen" sollten generell einfach anfangen was zu bewirken, denn so fühlt sich diese Funktion mehr wie ne Deko an ohne das sie jemals was bringt. Das hat sich auch bis heute nicht geändert. Die Community entspricht einem haufen stück scheiße zu ungefähr 90%.
[*]Manchmal funktioniert die hitbox/hitreg nicht wie sie soll, habe einen 12ms ping (der Gegner 50ms) und trotzdem kommen meine Schüsse obwohl ich vor ihm geschossen habe nicht an und mehr als mit meinem Visier auf seinen Kopf zu gehen kann ich auch nicht machen, wie oft hatte ich diese Situation und ich weiß nicht einmal ob es an der Engine liegt fühlt sich aber extrem scheiße an, an der Physik des Spiels zu sterben.
[*]Das Matchmaking ist außerdem auch Lächerlich, man spielt nicht mit Spielern auf gleichem Level sondern durchaus gegen Spieler gegen denen man keine Chance hat. Als Gold 3 Spieler gegen Platin 3 oder kräftigeren Gegnern zu Spielen ist echt mies (Platin 3 ist immer noch in der 1000er ELO differenz). Kein wunder das die Quitt rate im locker so hoch ist, keiner hat Spaß dran von Platin oder Diamant Spielern auf die fresse zu bekommen. Im Ranked will man wenigstens Ebenbürtige Gegner bekommen, ist jedoch selten der Fall. Es hat sich zwar mit der neuen Änderung gebessert das man jetzt nur gegen & mit Spielern mit einer ELO oder auch "MMR" (welche den Skill einer Person als Zahl darstellt) mit einer maximalen Differenz von 1000 beträgt die sowas mittlerweile einigermaßen bessert, das Problem bleibt trotzdem bestehen da mit diesem "fix" das nur im Ranked behoben wurde, und selbst da nicht wirklich. Im locker hatte ich es trotzdem schon einmal das ich mit Gold 3 gegen einen Champion 26 gespielt habe. Ein solches System führt dazu, das man seinen Noob Kollegen auf z.B. Bronze X mitnimmt damit man in Ranked niemand besseres als Gold X bekommt, und man somit das ganze Team hochranked, für mich und meine Kollegen eine Win-win situation, aber ich kann mir vorstellen das sich die Gegner dann genauso beschissen vorkommen wie ich, wenn ich alleine spiele.
[*]Der Sound ist mir nicht Scharf genug. Der Sound ist viel zu verschwommen und meist extrem leise, wenn die nicht direkt vor einem stehen, weshalb man die Lautstärke anhebt und feststellt das man jetzt mit 70 AUFJEDENFALL ein Hörgerät braucht. Ein Sound Update für VIEL klareren Sound wäre echt gut. Das habe ich auch nachdem ich mehrfach meine Audio Einstellungen überarbeitet habe, der klang ist in anderen Spielen viel Schärfer. Bei Shifting Tides hätte ich mir eine Bohrinsel als Map übrigens auch ganz cool vorgestellt. Was Maps betrifft, gibt es also noch gut Luft nach oben.

Considering it's lowered price tag, you should defenitely pick this game up, NOW!

I can't believe I have never written a review for this, and I find this unacceptable since this has been one of THE most satisfying gameplay experiences I have had in my life of gaming. Definitely in the top 10. There is a reason the reviews are overwhelmingly positive.

The base game has an exceptionally written storyline with accompanying voice acting. The background music is very atmospheric for the setting as are the sound effects of the enemies and miscillaneous ambient noises. The great graphics together with the day/night cycle further adds to  the already amazing immersive feel.

The character has a solid progression system for your character and makes you feel like you are progressing along with the pace of the storyline and feels like it ties in very well with it, going from a newbie just on the scene to becoming somebody more experienced in the world or Haran.

The game mechanics seem balanced. No real feeling of things being overpowered or nerfed as such, although I will admit sometimes it felt as though your bladed weapons were like a hammer at times even at maximum durability, but in the end it kind of balances off and makes the danger of dealing with those inevitable, seemingly inane zombies, real.

The game also really knows how to keep you on edge with it's ambiance... You really feel drawn into the game and the current situation. Especially at night :) You will definitely feel the fear in certain points.... sometimes even more quickly than you thought heh heh.

So, with your trusty rock in hand, you begin to hack away at the resource piles in front of you. As you gather your stone, you hear footprints from in front of you. You stop hacking at the rock, and peek around ever so slowly to see a man in full kevlar staring at you, with a dangerous object resembling a gun pointed straight at your head. He says to you - "Go away. Stay away from my base, or I will kill you."
So you run, and you run, and you run some more. Then BAM an M4 shot sounds and you hear a bullet ping off the ground from next to you. You turn around at the last second to see the same person shoot you in the face.
You respawn in a peacefull valley next to a concrete bunker. You decide to explore. As you happily run up to a weapon crate, you hear footsteps from behind you - "probably just a deer" you say to yourself. You open the box to see an MP5A4! You are so happ tp get your first gun, but then a voice comes from behind you - "Thats mine B***H!"
You turn around to see a man slam the blunt surface of a rock into your skull, and you lose your first gun.

TIPS!!
-if you are new, join a rather unpopulated server. Just learn how the game works.
-When looting, always check your surroundings. 
-When you hear footsteps, you should probably run.
-Dont go for the airdrop.
-Rock is your friend

很好玩的一款挂机类游戏，我玩了90个小时，整理出一些东西，希望对你们有帮助：
1.中期刷钱可以用木剑和布衣，材料少，而且价格不低，应该是性价比最高的了，而且时间上也差不多。（我吃过这个亏）
2.探索出来后，左边的码头，可以多造2个船，而且探索页面的左边，有一个自动探索。（手点了2个小时才发现）
3.城镇大厅右上角有2个东西，按那个时钟进去可以吧传说和远古的留下来，而且上面的加成是有上限的，鼠标划上去可以看。
4.任务叫你去打的副本，里面怪物都是有加成的，有些大幅度降低物理伤害，有些大幅度降低魔法伤害，最好配多个阵容。（我自己是（纯魔法+肉盾+牧师），（纯物理+肉盾+牧师），（一个物理+一个魔法+一个辅助+一个肉盾+一个牧师）3套阵容刚刚好）
5.这个游戏巨占内存，建议不用电脑时在挂机（不然会和我一样想砸电脑）
6.这个游戏必须点保存后才能退出，不然不留存档（右下角保存并回到主菜单）
7.变速齿轮用了会直接掉游戏（本人亲测）
8.探索的时候最好什么技能都放点，不然很亏。
9.前期不建议开活动，后期建议一直开着活动。
10.熔炉对于7级以及以前的装备合成不需要钱，对于8级的装备就要很多很多钱。（记得看清楚再合成，不然血亏）
11.戒指在前后期也会有属性上的差异。
12.冒险家每5级得到一点属性点，第一第三层都是强化自己，第二层强化技能，第四层强化战法。
13.建筑物升级全靠任务，人物装备也要及时更换，不然连任务都打不过。
14.中间拿到的一些杂的东西都是增加你熔炉打出来的东西的好坏以及战斗方面的。
15.实在打不过就氪秘药和血药，这个帮助很大。

This game is truly amazing. It's coming close to my favorite game of all time, and that should say something as I am an old guy that is playing since the early 90's. I don't write many reviews, the reason I write one here (besides I find this game a piece of art) is to counter some badly argumented reviews that call out the bad side of RNG. Too many players can not handle the loss of heroes when a chain of bad events happen. It's a big part of the charm of this game. Good RNG is never called out, most players don't notice a 4 hero dodge chain but when a 4 enemy dodge chain happens they go look for the review button. 
Just imagine everything going as expected, how boring would a game become? Anyways that might just be my opinion but the RNG is the cherry on the cake in this game. The atmosphere is hands down the best I have ever felt in a game. Obviously the narrator is amazing but the artstyle and soundtrack are just perfect.

The Crimson Court DLC just adds on what I call the 'survival chaos'. The race for finishing courtyard quests is so tense that you just feel it in the town screen ! "Will someone die of the curse because I didn't bring back enough blood?" "Should I take my best Highwayman even though he is wasting or craving and I have no blood left?". The tension feels so good. The curse can feel frustrating when heroes just decide to pass or attack one of your heroes at the wrong time, but oh boy does this make you feel stick to you monitor.

10 euro/dollar for this game in a sale is a crime, nothing this good should ever be so cheap. The one single hint I can give new players is : just accept heroes will die and are replacable, you will need this mindset to fully grasp this piece of art.

[h1] Что еще за SoulCalibur? [/h1]

Во многом эта серия схожа с другой популярной японской линейкой Street Fighter. Первая часть зародилась на игровых автоматах, а позже перекочевала на консоли, где постепенно мутировала и менялась, конкурируя с другими файтингами. К слову, оригинальная Soul Blade, прародитель серии — это один из первых трехмерных файтингов вообще.
тличительными особенностями серии является сильный упор на сюжетную составляющую и акцент на использование холодного оружия. В центре истории всегда находится проклятый меч «Грань души» (Soul Edge) и его противоположность под названием «Соулкалибур». На протяжении пяти номерных частей оба артефакта сменили множество хозяев, а в рамках серии сложилась большая вселенная.
Настолько большая, что она стала препятствием для новичков, ведь разобраться в происходящем им довольно проблематично. Именно поэтому SoulCalibur 6 нельзя назвать продолжением. Наоборот, создатели игры решили вернуть игроков туда, где все началось, а именно в 16 век альтернативной истории. Вот так легко и просто студия Project Soul перезапустила серию.
Основная сюжетная линия развивается параллельно уже известным по другим частям событиям. Главный герой становится жертвой очередного хозяина «Грани души», но выживает, после чего начинает длинный путь мести новому владельцу проклятого клинка. Поначалу кажется, что на такой жизнеутверждающей завязке все и закончится, однако SoulCalibur 6 далеко не так проста.
Обзор SoulCalibur 6 — концептуально, дорого, с Геральтом
Собственно, от файтинга тут только сами бои, все остальное запросто можно увидеть в какой-нибудь JRPG. Перед началом игры можно создать собственного персонажа, при этом выбор большой: есть 16 рас, которые определяют стартовые параметры бойца, множество стилей боя и другие элементы кастомизации, в том числе и чисто-визуальные.
Среди оружия, например, есть комбинация щита и меча, а также всякая экзотика вроде мечей-пистолетов, топоров, парных дубинок. Можно вооружиться косой!
Обзор SoulCalibur 6 — концептуально, дорого, с Геральтом
Оружие определяет не только внешний вид, но также анимации и числовые показатели атак, прямо как в Souls-играх. Очень необычно видеть такое в файтинге, да еще и с такой длинной историей.
А потом начинается и вовсе что-то странное. SoulCalibur 6 не стесняется щеголять глобальной картой с основными и побочными квестами, ролевой системой с «лутом» и «прокачкой», наймом дополнительных бойцов и диалогами с несколькими вариантами выбора ответа. Место нашлось даже системе репутации «добрый-злой», которая впоследствии влияет на концовку всей кампании.
Может сложиться впечатление, что SoulCalibur 6 — это не совсем файтинг, однако все сомнения пропадают, стоит лишь зайти в мультиплеер. Вот где игровая механика раскрывается на все 100%, ведь, как ни крути, «боты» не могут передать всю остроту ожесточенного поединка. К тому же именно в PvP больше всего заметны новшества боевой системы.

Обзор SoulCalibur 6 — концептуально, дорого, с Геральтом
Главное из них — это появление блока и контратаки. Эти движения повсеместно используются в современных файтингах, но прошлая часть серии вышла 6 лет назад, так что для SoulCalibur они действительно новые. Еще бойцы получили способности-усилители, действующие в течение ограниченного времени. Все это сделало бои более тактичными и менее аркадными.

Еще одна уникальная черта мультиплеера SoulCalibur 6 — это возможность создать собственного персонажа с уникальным внешним видом, стилем боя и характеристиками. Тут выбор точно такой же, как и в одиночной кампании, а значит простор для проектирования идеального бойца действительно широкий. Где еще такое есть? Разве что в WWE, но эту игру можно назвать файтингом с натяжкой.


А в чем подвох?
Определенно, SoulCalibur 6 является одной из самых необычных игр в своем жанре. Там, где конкуренты давят на PvP и соревновательность, этот проект преподносит любопытный одиночный опыт, и лишь потом приглашает окунуться в мультиплеер с редактором персонажа и обновленной «боевкой». Казалось бы, это отличное решение, ведь игра как бы метит в немного другую нишу.
И это правильно, потому что если начать сравнивать с популярными файтингами, то становится ясно, что детище коллектива Project Soul смотрится не слишком выгодно. Во-первых, многое в игре сделано крайне бюджетно. Трехмерные заставки можно пересчитать по пальцам, почти весь сюжет разворачивается на статичных экранах с лицами персонажей. Поэтому на красоту приходится любоваться исключительно в движении, когда в бою участвуют женские персонажи.

Если оценивать SoulCalibur 6 с точки зрения продолжения легендарной серии файтингов, то никаких претензий нет. Игра сохранила все, за что любят «Соулкалибур»: интересный одиночный режим, нестандартный подход, гибкий редактор персонажа и крепкий мультиплеер. Девелоперы Project Soul верны своим корням, и потому фанаты серии наверняка будут довольны.

Things that I would love in a update/Stardew 2.0: More villagers (I know it's meant to be a sleepy village but a busier atmosphere could be nice) & dog/cat pet to be more interactive (finds a new item every day? mini game opportunities?).

My one criticism is that some things aren't intuitive (like using a hoe to dig up and move scarecrows and sprinklers) and there's no help/lessons page for stuff like that so anytime I had questions I had to search online, but hey, I guess that's what Steam's for!
