Given the upcoming release of Binding of Issac: Rebirth, I have decided to update my review of The Binding of Issac + The Wrath of Lamb. Having doubled my playtime in the past couple of weeks i have come to the conclusion that my initial response to the game was premature.

     For those unfamiliar with Issac, the game is a Rougelike Dual Analogue Shooter. this means you controll Issac (or one of his unlocakble alternates) who fights randomly spawned monsters in a procedurely generated dungeon using his own tears as bullets. Issac is heavially inspired by retro titles, especially the original Legend of Zelda, as can be seen in the way each room is a seperate yet in many ways similar mirror of each other with some room s designated as treasure or boss rooms, and the heart based life meter.

     The presentation of Issac is that of a Newgrounds flash game on steriods. To be fair that description is fairly apt. the game is built on the flash engine and if it hadn't had the time, creativity, and vision applied to it that is what it would likely have ended up as. That flash comment is not meant in the derrogative though, the game looks and sounds beautiful (Mostly thanks to Danny Baranowsky). Because it sticks to the limitations of the engine rather than attempt more realistic graphics the game looks perfect for what it is.

     Gameplay is where Issac truly shines. The controls are simple and tight, keeping the already difficult gameplay from becoming frustrating. The best part of the gameplay though is the items. The randomly generated items ensure that no two runs are the same. These items are most awesome when they work together (Protip-Polyphimus+Technology =Awesome.). The enemies have unique attack and movement patterns that are easy to learn but will always be able to throw you for a loop.

     The only problem I have with the game is the same as it was before. The random nature of the item drops and boss spawns can make some playthroughs almost instant throwaways. This is aliviated by the sortness of the game and the rapidity of the respawn but if a few games in a row with a bad start and even I get frustrated. 

8/10. Worthy of a checkout before Rebirth comes out.

I have another 100+ hours on switch and 30+ on my other steam account, so I would say that I have an adequate amount of experience with this game, to the point where i can give a fair critique of it.

Basically, what you need to know is that anyone can find this game interesting and entertaining, but its true value lies in the multiplayer gameplay. I had experience with the game prior to multiplayer being introduced, but I have heard that having the game open up to you with someone who knows what they're doing is the best way to experience it. So if you have a friend who already knows how to play properly and can carry you through the early game, you will be set and able to experience the game in the most pure way possible. There will be consequences to your mistakes, and as a new player you definitely will make some mistakes, but the point of those is to learn from them. If you can do that, then your experience will improve as time goes on and eventually you can tutor other people into the game. It will take some patience, but the game mechanics are simple yet numerous and complex when they interact with each other. There is a level of learning that must be done before you understand the game fully, yet there is never one best strategy for you to take.
Not to spoil some of the mechanics, but one example is the leveling system. There are 5 categories that you can directly effect with increasing your participation in their activities, and these will make participation easier and more beneficial as time goes on. For example, early game fishing is extremely lucrative, but even with your increasing levels it will become increasingly difficult to level up in fishing unless if you do other things around the other categories, and get money. Eventually you will come across items and other mechanics that will make fishing easier and quicker, but only if you stop the lonesome fishing grind and look into the other aspects of the game. What makes it so excellently balanced is this matching between all the different options for you to pursue, and how they positively impact your other experiences in the game.

All in all, this game is an experience intended to be played with friends. That is the ideal way to initially experience it, yet you will still have an amazing time if you simply play alone and learn as you go. Did I mention that the main point of the game is to farm? Well yeah that's something to mention. Have fun

Kenshi，一款集星际争霸，模拟人生，骑马与砍杀于一体的开放世界沙盒游戏。这款游戏没有绝对的主角，只要你的人手足够，你可以操控任何招募的小弟成为游戏的主角。在游戏中发展的方法也很多：成为商人在各个城市之间进行贸易，或是从零开始在野外建造村庄并成为世界中新崛起的势力，抑或是凭借自己的人数优势成为打手等等...

不难看出这款游戏试图吸收上文提到的那些游戏的精髓，但可能由于制作的人手不够，这些精髓只学了个皮毛，并没有学习到内核：作为RTS来讲，你虽然能爆兵，但是每个士兵并没有自己独特的技能，只能用他们来实现十分简单的战术；作为模拟人生来讲，游戏只能达到随意摆放家具随意建造房屋的阶段，其他的什么也做不了。因此换句话来讲的话，游戏覆盖的面很广，但是深度并不是很深。

所以怎么形容这款游戏最为贴切？

它很像被子里的舒服，但确实又像风一样捉摸不住。

最后期待一波打磨得更好的Kenshi2.

Bioshock, and Bioshock 2, were easily two of my favourite games ever prior to playing Infinite. Everything about them is awesome, but it was so awesome that I never though Infinite would be anything more than a generic sequel, that adds nothing.

Infinite is hands down the best video game I have ever played. It's story ranks up there among the best fictional story I have ever been subject to. I loved every minute of it, and have since replayed it twice on PC, and a few times among other consoles. But I had the same feeling towards Burial at Sea as I did towards Infinite originally; I couldn't envision how they could tie it in. Especially with Infinites' ending. Blown away is all I can say after playing it.

The Bioshock trilogy deserves to go down as the best video game trilogy of all time as it is, but Bioshock Infinite (Plus Burial at Sea) needs to be recognised as the best video game of all time. Nothing feels out of place, it is a seamless exploration. 

I can't recommend this game (plus DLC) any more than I already do. Play it, you won't regret it.

Great game. DLCs are cool too. But if I had to recommend specifics, it'd be Industries DLC and Mass Transit. 

If you suddenly double the size of your city, look out for death waves some years later.  "Difficulty tuning mod" makes you take care and pace yourself.  I am currently playing on Ultra+ difficulty. This mod is recommended after you start getting bored of the regular mechanics. 

There are also many, many, many more mods which make the game amazing. One even micromanages your budget for you, so you don't fully fund giant capital projects (like universities) when below use capacity.  

There are mods other than that single Quality of Life mod I just mentioned. There are actually modded buildings, which are functional public works.  For example, piggybacking off of both Difficulty tuning and budget manager, a good example would be the "Faculty" structure, which functions as a smaller university, with less price, less, upkeep, and less capacity.  The catch is it's about 20% less efficient than the full blown university, but it's desirable early-game when you only have a few sims you want to college educate. 

So this game is complex, and mod-able, and provides many hours.   But if you get mods, the more you get, the less optimized the game is.  RAM is key, and you have to pick and choose what you really want.

I would tentatively recommend this game based on what your expectation for this game is. 

If you want to re-live the childhood memory where you sit besides your dad and watch the cavemen on screen slowly evolve into genocidal maniacs then by all means please grab it.  The game remains largely the same, but modernized slightly with some much needed QoL changes (such as idle vilies button, walkable farms and auto re-seeding), graphical improvement (not a complete overhaul, more like hi-res textures with high fidelity) and minor balance tweaks. The feeling of the game is preserved perfectly and you could instantly recognize almost everything in game if you have played the original. Also, some "authentic" annoyances got carried over (the most glaring problems being unit pathing and weird hit boxes). The soundtrack also got remastered with live orchestra, which is pretty neat.

However, if what you want is a total reboot of AoE 1 with modern game design philosophies then you might want to wait for sale or give it a pass. Peeling away the nostalgia, the game really does feel like it's more than 20 years old. It feels clumsy in terms of design yet sparse when comes to features. After all the underlying engine stays the same as it was 20 years ago. Playing this game makes me appreciate AoE2 (and 3 to some degree) more, seeing how much more enjoyable they actually are compared to AoE1.

So as I said, I tentatively recommend this game because fortunately (or maybe the opposite) I am of the first camp. Soooo...... rogan?

Если вы находитесь в начале игры недалеко от османа, то вам звездец. Этот парень имба на протяжении половины игры. Игра длится от 1444 по 1821 года. В первой половине, турок это ВЕЛИКИЙ ОСМАН дающий люлей всем вокруг, а европейские государства дружно подставляют свои жирные щеки. НО. Во второй половине Осман превращается в Сосмана и как вы уже догадались сосет похлеще ЗРИ на ее закате. Ибо на арену выходит МОСКОУ-РАША. Парниша, которого никто не трогал и он все это время тусовался с ордой и Новгородом, становится весьма неприятным противником идущим на запад(на востоке просто никого не останется(сори за спойлер)) и сметающим на своем пути Печь Росполитую (если поляк в начале возьмет в унию литву) или то что осталось от литвы и польши. 
Такс такс такс.. кто тут у нас? 
Священная Римская Империя ну или в простонародье СРИ.
Соберет ли австриец СРИ? НЕТ. Тут все как в жизни. Европейцы все время срутся и не могут придти к общему соглашению. Венгрия это груша для битья и на ней тренируются все кому не лень, тут и поляк улыбаясь лупасит с востока, осман с закрытыми глазами пинает с юга, богемия залетает на эту мега пати с севера, ну и в некоторых случаях австрия с запада. Идем на север и мы видим Бранденбург. Еще одна имба которой нельзя давать превратиться в Пруссию. Если  же вы этого не сделали то мне вас жаль. Все бафы у нее на на пехоту и армию в целом. Если это новая имба которая затмит сосмана на земле, то великобритания затмит в море, не трудно догадаться что у брита бафы на флот и на все что с ним связано. Stellaris is a game for an aquired taste. Its a massive 4X real time space strategy game. Here are my thoughts on good and bad:

Pros
+Vast maps with a lot of starsystems to explore.
+Research is different than most games, and takes forever to complete.
+Different ways to form your empire/democracy. You can even be machines.
+You can upgrade and outfit your ships with new weapons and equipment.
+Good replayability

Cons
-Wars can be tedious due to a warscore system (basically limits how much you can conquer each war).
-Space combat is a big part of the game, but the fights themselves are more or less automatic.
-Lacks more options in deplomacy (also this part of the game needs an upgrade, though its cool you can make federations)

All in all, Stellaris is a game that has a slow phase and focuses a lot on exploration (at least at the beginning and mid game). You have to enjoy the "Grand campaign" style where it will take a long time to win, which I personally do. Although there are some negative things to be said, I still think its one of the better 4X space games out there right now.

I recommend it.

Call of Duty вернулась к истокам... Но насколько хороши истоки? 

После десятилетия непрекращающейся штамповки современных войн и кривосделанного будущего, Call of Duty наконец-то решила вернуться в те времена, откуда началась ее былая слава, а именно во Вторую мировую. Прежде всего, разочарую тех, кто ожидал увидеть дедов, бравших Берлин - их здесь нет. С одной стороны, это плохо, с другой - наблюдать очередную ядренную клюкву тоже сомнительное удовольствие. Вся игра целиком и полностью посвящена американцам (за исключением миссии в Париже, где мы играем за француженку из Сопротивления, которая похожа на стелс-миссии с проникновением из Medal of Honor Allied Assault), а наш боевый путь пройдет от мясорубки на побережье Нормандии до взятия последнего моста через Рейн. 

При создании игры, Sledgehammer Games явно вдохновлялись фильмами Спилберга и игрой Brothers in Arms, однако им не хватило запала, чтобы сделать одиночную кампанию запоминающейся. Все выглядит как-то скучно и сумбурно, а актеры чересчур переигрывают. Несмотря на кажущуюся на первый взгляд серьезность действа, Call of Duty: WWII выглядит по-прежнему, т.е. галопом по Европам. В одной миссии штурмовали укрепления немцев при поддержке танков, во второй нас уже засылают для диверсионной работы, в третьей мы опять ведем жаркие перестрелки с немцами. Должен признать, что авторы пытались сделать драму, но никакого чувства переживания за персонажами не возникает. Даже в Brothers in Arms во время таких сцен иногда пробивало на скупую слезу. Кроме того, само поведение героев выглядит так, как будто война им по нраву (опять же, достаточно сравнить с Brothers in Arms, где все устали от происходящего). Зато разработчики не забыли о типичных сценах из индийского кино, только вместо машин у нас летают вагоны поезда, пущенного под откос... машиной. Впрочем, сами увидите. 

И, самый идиотский момент игры. Как оказалось, Sledgehammer Games забили и все свастики во всех без исключения версиях заменили крестами. По-началу решил, что это косяк русской версии, но как оказалось нет. Хотя изначально было оговорено, что цензура коснется лишь мультиплеера.

Геймплей описывать смысла нет. Одним словом, Call of Duty. Никакое оружие с убогим звуком, тупейший ИИ как союзников, так и врагов, и не менее тупой дизайн уровней с расстановкой чекпоинтов в отрыве от "горячих точек". Из инноваций (хотя знаю, для Call of Duty это слово выглядит смешным) - в игру впервые с выхода самой первой части, вернули аптечки! Правда это касается лишь синглплеер, в мультиплеере все по-старому. В итоге, напролом бежать не получится плюс придеться часто сидеть в укрытиях, особенно на ветеране, поскольку у вражеских ботов, по традиции, включается 100% точность и повышенный в несколько раз урон. 

Отдельным абзацем хочу упомянуть "шедевры" местного геймдизайна, а именно две миссии, где нам предстоит на танке прорываться к окруженным союзникам и прикрывать бомбардировщики на истребителе. В первом случае, какому-то гению пришла в голову мысль сделать поворот башни одновременно с корпусом. Но это еще цветочи. Ягодки - это уничтожение немецких танков. Ладно, "Тигр" нельзя пробить в лоб, но блин, чтобы подбить Pz.IVG надо играть в прятки, и зарядить ему в борт или тыл, при этом наш "Шерман" могут спокойно коцать в лоб. И как оказалось, пули тоже наносят ему урон... В этот момент я воспроизвел знаменитую позу Пикарда из "Стар Трека". Что же касается самолета, то это корыто, просто корыто, причем управление одинаково дубовое, что на геймпаде, что на мышке. Ускорение на стик, при поворотах не дай бог не туда дернешь, и опять выискивай цель. Спасибо, что додумались фиксацию прицела на враге сделать.

Je dois dire que ce Just Cause 3 est à l'heure actuelle l'apogée de la série car il a su extraire les bonnes idées des premiers opus en incorporant encore plus de liberté et de sentiment de puissance grâce à:
- La wingsuit
- Aux destructions et effets "boule neige" vraiment réussies et extrêmement jouissif
- Et à l'utilisation du grappin plus aboutie, nous laissant l'imagination comme seul limite.

On joue à ce jeu car l'on souhaite avant tout du fun, des destructions à la Michael Bay et des déplacements en rase motte avec la Wingsuit. Et je dois dire que l'on est servit. Le décor Méditerranéen planté, avec ses toits plats, ses champs de tulipes et ses petits villages en borde de mer est un vrai plaisir à découvrir avec une topographie intéressante.

Graphiquement jolie sans être transcendant, le jeu fait un bon en avant par rapport au 2. 

La répétitivité reste malgré tout au coeur de cet opus, les missions secondaires sont du même accabis que le 2 et les missions principales ne gagnent malheureusement pas en maturité, ni en finesse d'écriture. 

On reste néanmoins très addict avec ce jeu et on y revient facilement grâce à son mode bac à sable, ses destructions, son dépaysement et sa liberté de déplacement qui fait la force des Just Cause.

Human: Fall Flat is definitely fun with friends but I'm not sure if it's worth full price, if you're interested I suggest you read the short lists below and check it out when it's on sale.

COOL: 
+ Easy to start, understand and play co-up experience. You can play solo, but is simply quite boring.
+ Surprisingly funny and engaging for such simple mechanics. At least with friends.
+ Stylized graphics and design are a'ight. Nothing amazing but works for what it's trying to do.
+ Achievements and other minor challenges are introduced to add some spice to the game, but still has limited replay value.
+ Music is rather surprising. Sometimes doesn't fit the mood, but it might be the most professional-seeming part of this indie game.
+ There are apparently ideas to have a Workshop where people could share levels and avatars they made themselves, this could greatly increase the game's lifespan.

NOT-SO-COOL:
- Without any friends to play with it's simply a rather slow-paced walking simulator with some puzzles and parkour mixed in.
- Everythnig is physics based with no real challenges. Just small chores that are hard to do due to the nature of the controls. This was funny in "Octodad" for example, but not so much here since there is no narrative to make it funny, only your friends.
- It's also really easy to go out-of-bounds or sequence break. Half the times the intended path is less obvious then the alternate ones, meaning level design is a bit rubbish.
- A far better experience with a controller then keyboard and mouse but inputs seems to lag quite easily when you're playing with a lot of people.
- For a game that is so easy to break and get stuck in, there isn't an /unstuck command or anything like that. You can only "reset to checkpoint" the ENTIRE server when one person is stuck. 


So all in all, it seems this game has a solid idea but fails a bit at the excecution. Maybe a bit more time in development could've given it a bit more character to work with. I think 15 bucks for less then 10 hours of rather limited fun might be a bit much for some people so I recommend to grab it on sale as long as you've got some friends to fool around with.

I hope this helped, if you have any question please leave a comment.
Cheers!

Далее: спустя около часа я прошёл 4-5 гонок, покатался по сгенерированным трассам США и не получил никакого экстаза от вождения, хотя была выбрана "полная симуляция" вождения с отключением всех видов помощников, плюсом словил 3 вылета за это время. Следующая номерная часть после DIRT 3 делает огромный откат назад. 

Я не заметил какой-то крутой графики в сравнении с Dirt Rally, ведь, игра вышла позже неё, значит должна же она быть в чём-то лучше(?!)

И главное, зачем мы в этой игре - "погружение" в автомобиль и ощущение драйва, скорости и страха перед поворотом - этого нет. Ты летишь по трассе без малейшей опасности, без опасения, что потеряешь секунду или две, тебе начихать на штурмана и настройку подвески с балансом тормозов или распределением сил дифференциала(ов)... 
И как я писал в самом начале, если вы получаете кайф от "реализма" в Dirt Rally, то здесь его нет, здесь всё аркадное от начала и до конца. Эта игра мне напомнила CMR 2005, в которой было легче, чем в 2004. Не могу упомянуть одну вещь, что ощущения с видом от руля в этой игре напрочь железные : если в Rally только от руля можно выиграть гонку и чувствовать автомобиль, то здесь, наверное, это можно сделать от третьего лица; если в Rally с клавиатурой делать вообще нечего, то тут можно с джойстиком от Денди выиграть.

И понять не могу, как люди, сделавшие Dirt Rally, догнавную по симуляции Richard Burn's Rally, сделали это...

Didn't play a long time but the fact that if you die you lose your geos (currency) and if you die another time without getting back your ghost/soul means you lose them permanently sucks. Personally, whenever I'm fighting a new enemy I try to find the optimal way to deal damage to them, that means being risky at times and consequently dying which I don't mind per se, but the punishment is very annoying. 

The checkpoints (benches) are too spread out, which means a lot of travel time to get back where you were, even more so if you were exploring or fighting a boss. Furthermore, the jumping feels awkward at ledges. At points where I thought I should be able to jump from, I can't, and I just fall into a hazard that I cannot see to begin with.

As for the rest of the game, I never really understood what the purpose of the protagonist was, I guess that's part of the storyline but it felt very weird for the player not knowing at all what the goal was. Gameplay was OK. Map should be baseline for all areas, it just makes things annoying to not have it and I can't imagine it being a "fun" aspect. 

The game's price is quite low so something can be said about that but I still wouldn't recommend.

EDIT: After playing Hollow Knight, I doubt I'll be buying Hollow Knight: Silksong.

It's hard to know where to begin when providing a review for this game, and it's not often that when a game loads and you first start that the first sounds of out my mouth are "Wow". That's what happened with Hollow Knight.

The game is visually impressive, highly detailed, and the environments are just beautiful.  There is a large amount of variety throughout the game, with characters, enemies, and stylisation to keep anyone happy.

The audio was nice, with good music that suited the game and the levels and incidental sounds keeps the player immersed.

My only gripe for the game ?  It's not designed for casual players.  This game is tough. It starts out easy enough, and really enjoyable, then ramps up the difficulty to high levels very quickly.  I watched a number of Youtube videos on boss battles and found that even when playing on easy (or easier difficulty) that I struggled to perform as well as some of the Youtube players.  The other minor downside - the game is quite literally huge. That's good in the sense that there is a huge amount to explore, but it also means going over and over the same portions of the game.

[h1]ゲームについて[/h1]
[b]10/10[/b]
素晴らしく、そして儚い友情まで シュールな笑いを兼ねているSteamの最高傑作といえます。
ルートは３つあり、それによって主人公が体験する内容が異なります。
とあるルートでは心が痛んだり、またとあるルートではハンカチを要することもあるでしょう。
[b]笑いあり涙あり 人生を知ることのできるゲームだと私個人では思います。[/b]

[h1]操作性について[/h1]
[b]9/10[/b]
最初は少し戸惑うかもしれませんが、とっても簡単な操作性です。
移動や戦闘では十字キーを使います。
私自身も最初は「どこがイベントリを開くボタンなんだろう？」と戸惑いましたが、やはり[b]慣れ[/b]です。
強いて言うなら、全画面モードに常にするという項目がほしかったなぁとは思いました。
※F4で全画面にすることはできます。

[h1]BGM、SEについて[/h1]
[b]10/10[/b]
とても満足しています。
某動画サイトでもRemixなどがアップロードされており、その人気ぶりが分かります。
私個人の好みとしては、「Hope And Dreams」と「Death by Glamour」が好きです。

[h1]描写、キャラクターについて[/h1]
[b]10/10[/b]
昔ながらのレトロなドット絵が特徴です。
何故、近未来的なゲームがたくさん出てきてこの描写なのか・・・・。
その答えは、プレイすればきっとわかると思います。
とても愛着の湧く、可愛らしい描写です。

[h1]言語について[/h1]
[b]10/10[/b]
デフォルトは英語です。
「まったく英語がわからない！」という人は、[b]日本語化パッチ[/b]が配布されているのでそれを使えば日本語でプレイできます。
ただ、日本語でプレイしただけでは味わえないものが英語版ではあります。
両方試されてもいいかと思います。

[h1]最後に[/h1]
色々な小ネタがこの作品の中に凝縮されており、980円では勿体無いほどです。
人生とは何なのか、友情とは何なのか、いいギャグとは何なのか　これらの投げかけにこたえてくれる作品だと思います。
人それぞれですが、買って損はないと思います。
セール中だと、定価よりもすごく安くなっているときもあるのでそれを狙うといいかもしれません。

Outlast was a decent game. It's good points were it's ability to invoke a sense that you were being chased. Most of it's fear came from this. With the remainder being an equal mix of suspense and startle.

The game cripples itself though with a created depenancy on batteries for your night vision camera. It creates a system where you aren't so much worried about hiding, as you are busy scavanging for batteries. Even to the point where dying is a welcome reset, as you now know exactly where the batteries are and don't have to waste time trying to find them.

On top of that, when you are forced into a position where you get chased because of rail roading, the chase is too... Frantic. You don't have time to take literally two seconds to look left and right at the junction and decide which direction to run.

Which ends up boiling down to this: You spawn and immediately grab the batteries under the bed (you already knew they were there), you run down the hall, you turn left because you know right is a dead end. You open the door into the locker room, but don't try to hide in the lockers because you already know you are guarenteed to get caught. You run to the far end of the room where there is another door. You open the door and die. A 'monster' was waiting there. Maybe you're suppose to try to jump out of the windows? You spawn and immediately grab the batteries...

I don't usually review games but I gotta give my two cents on this one because some of the reviews are unfair to this game.

     It takes inspiration from dark souls. I understand the first 2 games were more forgiving in combat but the combat in Darksiders 3 is more refined and demanding. Dodge isn't some get out of a bad situation for nothing ability, it's actually timing your dodge and paying attention to your enemies on which direction you should dodge to avoid the blow if you can't get that perfect dodge timing. I like how this game increased the difficulty, it's a nice change of pace.

     I did like playing the other Darksiders and feeling like a boss with no equal but this game feels more a challenge because it's the growth of a character. Fury isn't some badass like War or Death start out. She actually grows and becomes that living weapon that the other 2 started out as. After playing through the game she starts out rough but by the end of the game she can take damage as well as dish it out. So I believe this game is more about the growth of a character than about the lore like the other 2 games which, again, is great to me because the other 2 games we were just told that War is an honor bound badass and Death is the resourceful badass who values family above all.

     I love the level design and character design of the Seven Sins. Each Sin feels really well placed in their environment and actually evokes some awe because of the creativity that went into their designs. The game also wraps around itself and you find new routes in familiar places because you got a new ability or solved a puzzle to open up a path. Basic enemies are more of a challenge this time around and keep the tension in the game high versus the past games where basic enemies sometimes felt like a chore or a grind. Fury's design is awesome with each new ability giving her a new look and different fighting style so that when you find that form that suits you it feels comfortable and combat comes more easily.

     The one thing I wish this game had was a map. I understand they wanted to give you that feeling of exploration but I wanted to go back to other places and use my new abilities to find secrets or treasures. I couldn't remember where each and every path lead which would limit me in exploration unless I mapped it out myself to remind that I could use that ability here or there. So in the end I just kept moving forward and exploring as much of the area around me as I could and forgot places that opened up to me because I never went back unless the game/compass brought me there.

     Overall, I loved this game and recommend it for fans of games with a challenge and good character development. I do however recommend that you catch yourself up on the lore of the previous 2 games because it only enhances the story of this one and there are many videos out there that do this exact thing for you if you don't want to buy or play the previous games. Thanks for reading this review and thanks THQ for this game and here's to Darksiders 4 because I love the lore of this series!

Ich bin ein riesen Fan von Civ5, daher stand ich Civ6 eher skeptisch gegenüber. Die Grafik ist rein technisch besser als beim Vorgänger, klar da das Spiel ja auch neuer ist. Was mich persönlich daran stört ist, dass es an einen Cartoon erinnert und alles so ein wenig "weicher" wirkt. Die Animationen, vor allem bei Fertigstellung eines Wunders ist spitze, sowie die von Einheiten.

Das neue Bezirk-System ist einfach zu verstehen, man braucht allerdings einige Zeit um sich aller Tricks und Strategien zu ermächtigen. Die neuen Einheiten und Möglichkeiten bieten vielseitige neue Features, z.B Landebahnen, Raketensilos sind ne super Sache, da man damit auch weiter entfernte Städte nun auch bombardieren kann.
Was mich noch stört ist das Diplomatie System, erinnert mich an das Civ5 Basisspiel (also ohne DLCs), die Charaktere sind sehr unterschiedlich auch die Idee, dass jede Civ eine Agenda hat ist gut, dennoch finde ich das Punkte System für den Beziehungs-Status schlecht. Einerseits kann man so viel besser nachvollziehen welche Aktion welchen Einfluss auf die Beziehung hatte, andererseits ist die Balance bzw die Vergabe von Punkten für eine Aktion nicht sehr gut gelungen. So bekommt man z.b recht wenig Beziehungspunkte für wichtige oder bedeutende Dinge (Botschaft, Freundschafts-Erklärung, im Krieg unterstützt) und die Agenda wird viel zu stark gewichtet, sprich deutlich mehr - Punkte nur weil man z.B auf dem gleichen Kontinent wie eine Civ beheimatet ist. Ergibt meiner Meinung nach nicht viel Sinn.

Im Großen und Ganzen eine gelungene Fortsetzung die viel Potenzial hat.

YES!! I grew up with Doom and Doom 2 and before Doom (4) came out, I decided to replay them and what a great decision that was. Doom 1, coming after Wolfenstein 3D and Blake Stone, introduced the z-axis to the FPS genre, and they made well use of it. Level design is where Doom shined, combining complicated sprawling labrynths with demon hordes in a convincely dark atmosphere. Doom 2 updated the engine to allow even more demons on screen and even more complex awesome levels. Nearly a decade later we were given Doom 3, which was also awesome, but highly relied on jump scares and darkness, while level design was relatively linear. It was a good game, but different from original Doom. Now again about a decade later we have been blessed with Doom (4). I was nervous. Was it going to recreate the feeling of the old Doom? Maze-like levels that test your navigation skills while throwing demons at your face with fire in the depths of hell? I became more nervous when I heard about skill trees and upgrading. I became terrified when I tried the multiplayer open beta. It was awful, slow, boring, and the brightly colored player/weapon skins were just slap in the face. People were like "yeah I was old school Doom multiplayer like CTF and DM!" Umm, you mean Unreal Tournament and Quake III? But the MP part was not made by id, it was by the CoD people. Ugh why Bethesda why?? But whatever, Doom is about singe player. So got the game and WOW. This. Is. PERFECTION!! The level design is complex and interesting and great use of z-axis like what Doom 1 was all about. The demons, the weapons, the fast paced enemies in your face explosion is all so great. The brutal gore, the f*cking heavy metal music, it's all perfect and gave me the same feeling as playing the old Dooms, well more specifically Doom 2. And if you thought the glory kill thing was brutal, jesus the berserker powerup will make your grandparents vomit and weep for the future of society, just like they did back with old Doom! The weapon/armor upgrades actually add a bit of variety and I loved searching for all the secrets. Took me about 30 hours to complete the whole game having found all items and secrets, and that's longer than Doom 1, 2, and 3 combined. My only qualm would be that the health and ammo from glory kills makes the game a bit easy, but I'll soon replay the whole game on nightmare. And if you thought the SP game was all, SnapMap is actually pretty awesome. The tutorial is fun and well made, and you can play with that, but there are plenty of crazy obsessed people out there making some impressive and pretty awesome maps. It can be difficult to find a good map since there's no real search function or way to preview a map but the rating system is a start. In the end, Doom (4) exceeded my already extremely high expectations!

After 500+ hours of Payday, I’ve had a blast with this game. But not without it’s problems. The balancing is awful. I primarily was a Death Sentence player. But it’s so hard to get my other friends to play it with me because it’s a cheap mess. And I agree with them. Keep in mind it led to one of my friends quitting the game entirely because of the sheer damage the cops do on Death Sentence. And on anything below it, it feels TOO EASY. Deathwish feels pretty easy when you sunk 200+ hours into high crime spree and death sentence. Don’t say that I’m crying about me sucking because I have my One Down Mask legit. (I HATE LAB RATS) Perks are also pretty limited in higher difficulties. If you try hard enough Every perk can be used on Death Sentence but some are way better than others. The Queen of DS perks is Anarchist. As much as is my favorite perk next to Kingpin. It gets very boring using it all the time. I tried experimenting with grinder and Gambler and it works but you have to be super super cautious. It’s not very fun. Pair that with the over abundance of cops and damage being flung around, it’s a mess. It really is. 

There’s three gamemodes in the game all with a huge amount of maps to play with, so you won’t run out of content for a few hundred hours. That’s a plus from me. Even though I bought a lot of these DLCs individually. 

Optimization? Not here. The magical engine called Diesel doesn’t allow for that. However there’s a lot of performance mods to fix that.

Skin Economy? It exists, however there isn’t much trading as there is in CSGO and TF2 but they’re there and there’s some really nice skins to be had. 

Community? Eh, I don’t know how the community is right now but when I played it was a 50/50 chance of me getting an asshole who someone who was really cool. I exclusively play Pubs. You’ll find a lot of toxicity when you’re a new player. Especially when you’re just starting out. Don’t let that bring you down if you really want to get into the game.

Mods? The main reason I sunk a lot of hours is because of the quality of life mods there are available like Hud Mods and sound mods. 

Recommended? Yes, despite all the issues, all the left over bugs (Like losing lines in the middle of a successful stealth hiest) toxic-ish community. It’s still a blast to play with your friends and a treat for completionists since there’s so many achievements to do.

Is it 100% perfect and bug free? Of course not. But it's a lot closer to that ideal than any other game of this complexity and scope ever was on day one. And most importantly it's additive immersive and fun.

The interface is the biggest improvement from CK2. You know what's going on and you can find out what to do about it.

Are there things that lack from CK2? Of course, but on the whole the game has been chopped to a lean but complete core. I've been playing as Sweden. Not as detailed as CK2 vikings, possibly a little easy at this point. But I'm sucked in by the events, the pets! The murder! Avoiding my cousin because he's developed horrifying pox! Being blackmailed by my own vassals!

Much as I'm looking forward to this getting built on, it isn't a stellaris like hope that the hollow core gets built into a better game. But rather a new concern that adding to this complete feeling game won't bog down the experience! Of course I look forward to the early patches to clean it up a bit as well, but it's not a bug ridden mess in need of complete system changes, as can happen with PDS!

Never written a steam review before, but I feel I have to after all the Negative reviews here. TL,DR at the end.

 Some reviews complain about hords of Chinese hackers on Games, which i've seen videos of, but have not seen any in my own playtime (EU servers). Some complain about a 'myrad of technical issues', but do not elaborate beyond it taking up ALOT of RAM and VRAM, which may be true, since with 16gigs ram iv'e no issues. Rubberbanding has never happened except for the time the entire house had shitty internet because my country has a data cable from the 1970s or something, and hackers are nowhere as prevalant as some people say. Not encountered any blatant hacking yet, and the inclusion of the Death Cam is a great help in finding hackers, especially with aim, wall, and recoil hacks.

IMHO, this is an incredibly fun game to play, transitioning from relaxed looting to suddenly tense and almost panicky moments as another player/squad find you, or you realize the blue circle is closing in on you and youy have no car. Playing with friends is an absolute blast, especially if you all have a similar sense of humor, as after every gunfight or funny mishap while driving you can all make a few good jokes about it.

TL,DR:
Extremely fun game to play, alone or with friends, with funny, calm and tense moments all over. It is also one of the few games I've played where I do not feel crushing dissapointment when I don't win, as long as YOU think you did well, you have fun.

Loads of fun, bring friends, and enjoy the massacres.

I haven't checked out the multiplayer yet, but the campaign as a whole is decent, like 7/10. The plot is ridiculous, as if D44M's lore didn't hint at it getting worse, and the dialogue is pretty painful to hear at times. The "evil cult's" lair is like a cartoon villain's hideout, and the Hell Priest keeps goading you like Snidely Whiplash. There are MANY more goofy things than necessary, that made me wonder if Randy Pitchford had been involved some how (no where near BL's 5th grade shit). A good example is the "weakness" of the Cacodaemon, where you fire a grenade shell into its mouth and it cartoonishly expands a bit, followed by a glory kill where you pull out its eye to the sound of stretching rubber with a distinct "pop" at the end. That almost makes the Serious Sam games seem subtle.
 But what makes up for all of that trash is the gameplay. I've seen alot of people complain that ammo is scarce, and I was under that impression as well, until I discovered that the chainsaw regenerates 1 bar of fuel over time. After that I couldn't dream of running out of ammo, unlike D44M, and that allowed me to basically ignore resource management. That, paired with the "faster" gameplay (the dashes), really brought the game together for me. Granted, its nothing like Quake (which is the closest approximation for an original 3D DOOM) where you're allowed to freely explore the map and aren't being trapped in an arena constantly, but for what it is, its fun. Also, for those of you that think the platforming and swimming are foreign, remember that Quake 1 & 2 both had these, and they were done well.
 Also, the enemy design is much better than the previous installment, mirroring DOOM II's sprites. The environments were hit or miss, as some areas looked straight out of Darksiders II (not to mention the plot resembling Darksiders II's), whereas Hell looked MUCH more on point than D44M's. The soundtrack somehow was worse than D44M's, which was original and had some charm, (not to mention all the weird equipment Mick Gordon used/made) but this felt like a shitty remix of those themes that was less coherent. 

Overall, its a good shooter that looks like DOOM, but isn't really.

I'd recommend it, at $30.

Viele haben es abgelehnt, weil es nicht sich nicht exakt wie Skyrim spielt, aber wenn man es abseits von Skyrim betrachtet, ist es eines der umfangreichsten und komplexesten Elder Scrolls Spiele überhaupt.

- mega gute Quests (Vertonung, Storywriting, Umfang, Komplexitä) In diesem Punkt kann eigentlich fast kein MMORPG mit ESO mithalten.
- enorm große Welt (nach hunderten Stunden hab ich jetzt vielleicht ca 30% Welt erkundet)
- kein Zwangs-PVP (für mich als reiner PVE Spieler wichtig), aber trotzdem gutes Massen-PVP
- sehr komplexes Item-System und Crafting-System
- dauernde Updates verbessern das Spiel und erweitern es
- Kein Pay2Win Itemshop
- Sehr komplexes Charakter-Entwicklungs-System (Hier kann man auch exotische Dinge tun, wie einen Magier zum Tank drehen, oder mit dem Heiler damage machen)

Klare Kaufempfehlung für jeden Elder Scrolls und MMORPG Fan, aber wie gesagt, geht nicht mit der Erwartung ran, dass es sich wie Skyrim spielt, das tut es nicht.

OVERALL REVIEW Masterpiece [9/10] 
This is one of the best RPG games ever made not just of the isometric genre but of all time. It would be a crime not to pick up and give it a play through. The game allows you to play as you wish without forcing you to play in one way. Each quest can be completed in a number of ways. This game rewards those who can think outside of the box so problems solvers will be very satisfied. I have received over 80 hours of gameplay in one complete play through without even finishing all the content, I missed so much content that I am now started a 2nd play through.

GAMEPLAY
Gameplay is very fun and satisfying, it is turn based with environmental battles. Drop oil on the floor then use fire to light your enemy you can then proceed to administer water upon the fire to create steam or freeze the water to cause your enemy to slip and fire upon the ice would create water which can be electrocuted. You have many combination of abilities and environmental elements that cause each battle to be a little bit different and exciting. There is are a lot of abilities that can be mixed and matched to create powerful builds as well as each team member can assume a specific role.

DIFFICULTY
The game can be quiet difficult your first play through as you will not know how to properly spec your character and not know how to distribute attribute points across your team. The first act starts with both you and enemies having low health and is not much a challenge especially when you understand how to play. The 2nd act gets much harder and the 3rd act is insanely difficult the fight truly become tough to the point you have to carefully plan out how to win fights, victory wont be given easily and you may die a few time before figuring out how defeat a foe. The game also features puzzles some of which I could not help but think "How would I even know that". Some of the puzzle feel they were put only to be difficult for no reason at all other than being difficult.

RPG ELEMENTS
The game is extremely strong in story telling and assuming the role of an imprisoned sorcerer. You truly encounter choices that are tough to make as you will see toward the end of the game the weight of the world starts to build on your shoulders. At the end of the game I truly felt I had come far and was sad to see it end as not many games of quality as this one is. You are given the ability to choose between many races, some of them are premade characters with already made back stories others are clean slates so that you may create their stories. Each race has its own strengths and weaknesses and effects gameplay so choosing a race actually does effect the way you can play. The undead experience is not like the elf both have cool exclusive abilities.

Critique
The first few hours of this game is a bit slow as you do not know where you are or what to do and can bore some people but once you get past that the game truly opens up and becomes amazing. The game gets extremely hard late gate and some enemies are just outright obnoxious to fight against. The quest journal leaves much to be desired its not very clear or detailed as to what has been completed and what needs to be done next. The movement speed is painfully slow but this can be fixed through mods. Over all there is not a lot of complaints of this game and most of them can be solved trough mods.

L'un de mes jeux préférés sur Steam, tout simplement. 

Terraria est l'un de mes premiers jeux achetés sur Steam, en 2011, soit déjà environ 8 ans à l'heure où j'écris cette review... en 2019 (ouch le coup de vieux). Je me souviens à l'époque que j'avais un peu joué à Minecraft mais que je trouvais qu'il manquait un peu un aspect RPG (armes et armures plus variées, plus de combats, plus d'objets, des boss, etc)... chose que Minecraft ne proposait pas encore à l'époque. Si je me souviens Minecraft venait tout juste de décoller et n'avait pas eu de mise à jour pour rajouter l'XP et n'avait pas encore de vraie fin. Je me suis donc demandé s'il existait un équivalent avec un poil plus de RPG... et j'ai découvert Terraria, qui était encore au stade d'Early Access... et n'était disponible qu'en anglais (rassurez-vous le jeu propose aujourd'hui du français)

J'ai tout de suite accroché à Terraria. La 2D minimaliste mais sympa, les animations des persos à la FF1-6, pouvoir massacrer des lapins ou des oiseaux à coup d'épée... Le minage, les ressources à récolter, le craft, les armes et armures diversifiées, les boss, les ennemis, les invasions de monstres... déjà à l'époque c'était du lourd. J'ai relancé le jeu à chaque grosse mise à jour, et à chaque fois j'ai redécouvert le jeu. Car oui le jeu a eu de nombreuses mises à jours, avec beaucoup d'ajouts divers et variés, au point qu'entre le moment où le jeu était en Early Access et aujourd'hui le contenu à été très largement augmenté et amélioré. A l'heure où j'écris ces lignes la dernière MàJ a été annoncée à l'E3, j'ai hâte de me replonger dans le jeu.  

Le jeu est vraiment riche en contenu, je recommande vivement de consulter un wiki. Pour ma part je consulte celui-ci :
https://terraria.fandom.com/wiki/Terraria_Wiki
C'est un wiki en anglais mais il est très très complet. Vu que j'ai découvert le jeu en anglais je m'y suis habitué et ne joue qu'en anglais sur le jeu donc c'est plus facile pour retrouver les noms des objets.
En cherchant vite fait je vois qu'il y a un wiki FR qui a l'air assez complet :
https://terraria-fr.gamepedia.com/Terraria_Wiki

Si je devais citer les qualités / défauts :
+ beaucoup de contenu (environ 40-50h pour aller à l'essentiel, plus du double ou du triple pour tout compléter)
+ la diversité des armes, armures, styles de jeu (corps à corps, arc / fusil, magies) 
+ le système de minage, simple et efficace
+ la diversité du craft
+ la diversité des ennemis 
+ les invasions de monstres
+ les boss, qui demandent très souvent une bonne préparation sinon c'est le KO assuré
+ la difficulté globale, relativement bien faite dans son ensemble (malgré un pic de difficulté passé un certain boss du jeu), avec de quoi offrir du challenge pour ceux qui veulent
- les musiques sont correctes mais on fini par s'en lasser, surtout car le jeu est assez long et les musiques assez répétitives si on reste dans les mêmes zones
- on prend parfois trop facilement des coups de la part des ennemis, à tel point qu'on peut se retrouver à prendre constamment des dégâts et c'est parfois difficile à gérer, pour ne pas dire mortel. C'est d'autant plus flagrant quand on passe en mode Hard (après avoir battu l'un des boss du jeu) et que les ennemis se mettent à infliger beaucoup plus de dégâts.
- le pic de difficulté lorsqu'on arrive en mode Hard. Pour faire simple l'un des boss qui sert à faire progresser le jeu fait passer le monde en mode Hard quand on le tue, faisant apparaître de nouveaux biomes, de nouveaux ennemis et de nouvelles mécaniques. Pourquoi le pic de difficulté? Je m'explique : quand vous faites le jeu normalement, vous êtes amenés à explorer le monde verticalement, notamment vers le sud en creusant le sol / explorant les cavernes. Lorsque vous arrivez tout en bas de la carte vous avez normalement creusé pas mal de galeries et exploré pas mal de biomes en long et en large. Et bien lorsque le jeu passe en mode Hard, les nouveaux biomes qui vont apparaître vont partiellement changer les biomes que vous avez déjà visités, dont vos galeries, et certains endroits peuvent devenir très dangereux (surtout juste après le boss). La plupart des ennemis seront trop puissants. Il faut plus ou moins reprendre la progression du début du jeu : explorer les galeries peu profondes, trouver les matériaux pour créer les nouveaux sets d'armes / armures, aller plus profond, trouver les minerais suivants, etc. En faite la difficulté tiens du fait qu'il faut bien se préparer avant le boss, être sûr de soi et se dire qu'il n'y a pas de retour en arrière. Pour ma part il m'a fallu pas mal de temps avant de terminer le jeu au complet à cause de ce pic de difficulté. Bon malgré tout ce n'est pas un défaut rédhibitoire, globalement le jeu reste excellent et la difficulté bien dosée (d'où mon "+" un peu plus haut).

Bref, globalement Terraria est un très bon jeu.

Resident Evil 7 который мы заслужили

Честно сказать, я не любитель серии Resident Evil из-за кривой анимации, достаточно скудного геимплея, устаревшей механики и просто надоедливой тематики "зомби-Umbrella-старые герои". Седьмая часть изначально мне казалась подобием P.T. или в народе Silent Hills, где место действия происходило в доме/особняке. Но Resident Evil 7 это совсем другое.

СТРАХ ВНУТРИ

Я начал игру на "легкой" сложности и слава богу, это помогло мне сконцентрироваться на атмосфере, сюжете и героях. Это помогло мне пройти игру подобно просмотру фильма и за это я очень благодарен разработчикам. Каждый босс был своего рода этапом, который проходился быстро и зрелищно. Но зато нагнетание обстановки было запредельным, я боялся звуков, монстров которые внезапно выползали из люка или другого отверстия, открывать очередную дверь. Я давно такого не ощущал, я играл в Outlast который многие считают лучшим кирпичным заводом, но мне он отвратителен за свои бездарные скримеры и пустоту во врагах. В Resident Evil 7 в какой-то момент даже начинаешь сочувствовать злодеям и стараешься их оправдывать.

Считаю, что разработчикам удалось добраться до души игроков и не только напугать их и сыграть на фобиях но и создать по настоящему интересный хоррор со времен (не побоюсь этой серии) Silent Hill. 

ПРАВИЛЬНОЕ НАПРАВЛЕНИЕ

Многие посчитали, что Resident Evil уже не тот и вообще, что это за игра от первого лица? Но это необходимая мера для того, чтобы оживить сериал и дать ему глоток свежего воздуха. Это всё тот же Resident Evil но в новом обертке, здесь есть и аналог печаткой машинки для сохранения, типичные для серии головоломки и двери с ключами, даже сюжет сильно схож с общей серией. 

Новый уровень достигнутый Resident Evil 7 стоит развивать дальше, это действительно что-то новое и интересное. Но даже в этой части разработчики смогли порадовать любителей первой части и даже не забыть про Resident Evil Revelations. 

ОБЩАЯ РЕАЛИЗАЦИЯ

У меня есть претензии только к общей картинке, если взять по отдельности некоторые моменты то они выглядят просто потрясающе - игра актеров, озвучка, модели персонажей, темные помещения, общие планы дома и местности. Но иногда зайдешь в комнату, а там свет не правильно лежит или шейдеры выглядят убого. Иногда картинка совсем ужасно играет с цветами и мне непонятны в данном случае мотивы художника и в целом дизайнера локации.

ИТОГ

Это тот Resident Evil 7 которого мы заслуживаем. За столько лет, пора забыть про успех Resident Evil 4 и принять что-то новое. Возможно это совсем не то, чего ждали фанаты, но это именно то, что нужно серии. Тем более в конце игры есть приятный подарок для фанатов серии.

[h1] We live… again [/h1] 
[b] These words could be heard from all old-school shooters, while you are playing Dusk [/b]
Sometimes I question myself: “Why do I always want to play Blood, Quake or Doom?” The progress went pretty far, nowadays every shooter has decent graphics, kind of plot, cutscenes, soap opera, tons of abilities and X-ray vision. So it is hard to state why do I keep returning to the origins? The reason is not in a simple nostalgia, but in fact that you do not need to watch cutscenes, play tutorial, remind all skills and perks or finish active quests in order to start playing the game. In old-style shooters like Dusk you simply select the level and start destroying everything you see. There are no long sections which dilute the gameplay or quite complex puzzles, it’s a pure shooter. Dusk is a brilliant example of such mechanic, it seems that the game orients on two grandfathers Blood (in case of environment) and Quake (overall gameplay core). Dusk is a perfect choice in case of reliving forgotten experience in the world of modern gaming. 
[h1] Story [/h1] 
Like in most of old FPS the game does not care to tell player anything. So you simply have to guess what is going on or to read it in Internet (I do not know whether Dusk has any txt file with the summary). However, the game bases on the Lovecraft’s mythology and also is greatly influenced by a Blood universe, especially 1 Episode. So the main story is about having your revenge and the goal is to find that mysterious cult leader. In addition, like in old days the protagonist literally rises from the dead. Caleb rises from the grave and Duskdude was attached to meat hooks, these hooks appeared in the heads of poor cultist in the end. 
[h1] Environment and level design [/h1] 
In Dusk the player will be able to visit various locations through three episodes. In the first Episode Duskdude will fight in rural landscapes such as farms, mines and worst levels in video games – sewers. Here player fights against cultists, corrupted goats and chainsaw massacre guys. I think this episode takes a middle place in terms of the quality, as locations are pretty mediocre. Moreover, the idea of such level concept is not very innovative and highly reminds Blood.  The second Chapter is the best in the whole game, if you ask me. Here player has to fight in industrial areas with some infernal machines, among these locations – factories, bases, labs. Enemies are represented by corrupted soldiers, monsters and laboratory experiments. I would like to state that most of maps are unique and have really interesting and creative sections. This episode reminds me Quake 2 and this is a positive correlation. Final chapter demonstrates an underground mysterious city which is a reference to a Lovecraft stories compilation and at some point reminded me Heretic. Here player has to fight various creatures and visit temples among with some dark magic. The problem with this episode lies in the second half of levels. First ones were pretty good, but then maps became like a last Doom 2 levels – large arenas with tons of enemies. So it is essential that these sections could have been placed in one level, but it takes too much of a player time. To sum up, Dusk has a decent level design and it is an interesting experience, in addition, it brings something new to the industry. 
[h1] Arsenal [/h1]
Dusk demonstrates a classical selection of weapons such as meat hooks, magic swords, pistols, shotguns, assault rifle, sniper rifle, crossbow, rocket and grenade launcher. The funny thing is that you simply pick up a gun and you intuitively know what it does.  There are not any complex mechanics, which is a plus – gameplay is not diluted with a tutorial sections. And yeah, here is present a weapon of ultimate destruction – the double-barreled shotgun and it is fantastic. Every weapon’s sound and its impact are brilliant, so you feel the power in character’s hands. However, the design of weapons is not so attractive, as it is quite simple, you have a feeling that you hold a combination of cubes, not a grenade launcher. So a bit more of details would have been nice. Finally, there is no middle-power rifle, like Energy rifle in Doom, which is sad at some point. 
[h1] Gameplay [/h1] 
Two words – classical FPS. Fast paced combat with toms of enemies. In addition, with a right combination of movement keys you are able to gain a speed of a light. Enemies differ and re	quire a specific approach. Apart from that, in my opinion the addition of bosses is a positive solution, even despite the fact that some of them are pretty easy. Dusk carefully saved an old-school FPS experience, yeah, there are no autoaim or X-ray vision. 
[h1] Soundtrack [/h1] 
It is just fantastic, every mission has its own theme and Dusk does not belong to these cases where only a few compositions are good. In Dusk every track is ultimately good and correlates with events on the screen. Composer made a great job on this one. 
[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
If you love Doom, Heretic, Quake and Blood – buy Dusk without a hesitation. If you have already bought it – buy it a second time. If you bought it twice then call your friend and buy him a copy of Dusk. But if you are from you8ng generation of gamers I would recommend you to think twice. The animation is clunky, simple mechanics and the total absence of perks and X-ray vision. The game bases on the old-school shooters, so it is like watching black & white comedies in 2018. The question is - are you willing to dive into a game of dinosaurs? My personal rating is 9 out of 10 (Fantastic game), despite some flaws, Dusk recreates a forgotten style and shows these AAA titles how things should be done.

Очень интересная программа, в которой можно поставить живые обои или создать свои.
ДОСТОИНСТВА:
Большая библиотека обоев, Доступная цена, Возможность создавать собственные работы.
НЕДОСТАТКИ:
Программа всегда запущена, Небольшая нагрузка на компьютер.
Наткнулся на неё еще давно, было интересно побаловаться с рабочем столом и его минимальным изменением
Функционал:
Огромное количество обоев, анимаций и подобного контента в одной программе, которая может изменить фон рабочего стола, как вы именно хотите. Обширная библиотека и мастерская, где люди делятся своими шедеврами. Простоя установка обоев, пару кликов и у вас уже другие обои.
Визуал:
Как по мне, все анимации сделаны качественно и добротно. Если не брать в учет вырезки из фильмов, видео, мультиков.

Интерфейс управления:
Всё на русском языке, при желании его можно сменить. Удобно понятно и по делу. Множество ползунов, которые дают возможность регулировать обоями как я хочу.
Себе лично поставил подобное, картинка не статична. Множественные гличи, выглядит очень даже ничего.
Итог:
Советую если хотите разнообразить обычные свои обои. Цена приемлема.

If you enjoy survival games, hybrid MMO's, and the chance to build a kingdom of wood planks and metal scraps, this game is definately worth a looksee. You start off as a bare naked man with a rock, a torch, some medical kits and frigid nipples as you attempt to survive the countless nights of this seemingly untouched forest. Hit your rock upon a tree or rock to obtain resources; resources to create an amalgamation of weapons or shelter pieces needed to survive the wilds... or possibly your neighbors...

On a serious note, this game can be either the best thing since sliced bread or the most frustraiting thing since urinary tract infections. The game has a beautiful sense of sandbox and complete up-to-you, take-this-have-fun aspect to it, and gives YOU the steering wheel as to what to do. You can be simple; build a small house, make a fire inside and only go out to hunt or gather. You can also be complex, and not leave an inch of your land untouched by leaving a 10 ft wall, barracades everywhere and a tower big enough to give the clouds pleasure.

You see how you progress in the game as you go, going from rock to bow, bow to boomstick handcannon, onto rifles and machine guns, and when you get to the point, you feel REALLY accomplished, but it's there when the frustraiting parts start.

The game is VERY unforgiving, and rightly tells you so with a hail of bullets to your face. Let's say you spent 12 hours building this awesome house, it's got walls and barracades galore. You're very proud of it, and as you walk back into it and close the wooden gate, you hear footsteps outside the walls. You ready your .45 pistol and get ready for anything, but nothing happens. No voices, no gunshots, nothing but the barely audible sound of... ticking? BOOM! Your walls are down, you're filled with more holes than a Senator's brain and they begin to blow up your house, to take everything you just spent your 12 hours on. Gone in less than 15 seconds. THAT is what I mean by unforgiving.

I don't complain about this, because the same happened to me, to everyone else before, and you can only get better at it to avoid it. 

Yes, this game has a huge grief-friendly system.
Yes, this game is buggy as hell.
Yes, this game has a few hackers.
Yes, I recommend this game. 

A few bad apples spoil the bunch; give it a try. You might like it.

Castle Crashers, das kurzweilige Sofavergnügen.

Ich habe Castle Crashers gespielt, als es auf der XBox 360 auf den digitalen Markt kam. Als mein Zwillingsbruder und ich die Demo gespielt haben, waren wir so fasziniert (geflasht, wäre der moderne Ausdruck), dass wir sofort bereitwillig Geld in Microsoft Punkte investiert haben, um dieses Spiel zu kaufen. Und es war jeden Cent wert. 

Geschichte
Eines schönen, schrecklichen Tages entführt ein böser Magier die Töchter des Königs und zusätzlich klaut er auch noch den großen Stein desselbigen. Der König darüber erbost sendet seine Ritter aus zu denen die Spieler auch gehören, um seine geliebten Schätze zurückzugewinnen. Dabei treffen die Helden (wir) auf kuriose Gegner und Gestalten.

Spielweise
Castle Crashers ist in wenigen Zügen zu verstehen. Man haut alles zu klump, was angreifbar ist und versucht dabei möglichst wenig eigene Treffer einzustecken. Dabei stehen einem hauptsächlich zwei Arten zur Verfügung. Physische Angriffe und magische Angriffe. Das klingt nach einfachem Knöpfedrücken, ist es anfangs auch, aber wer sich einmal mit den richtigen Techniken auseinandergesetzt hat, um Gegner möglichst lang in der Luft zu halten, um genügend Schaden zu verursachen und selber nicht getroffen zu werden, der wird merken, dass es alles gar nicht so einfach ist. Besonders bestimmte Bossgegner verlangen wirklich perfektes Teamwork und das Wissen, in welchen Intervallen man Sterben sollte.
Ja der Tod gehört auch mit zu der Partie/Party. Aber solange man Freunde hat, die einem eine gute Herzmassage verpassen können, ist man auch bald wieder gut auf den Beinen. Meistens habe ich am längsten überlebt, weil ich mich darauf spezialisiert habe.

Ja man kann "Skillpunkte" verteilen. Castle Crashers ist durch und durch ein Rollenspiel in dieser Hinsicht. Nicht nur dies. Man kann auch neue Waffen kaufen, kleine Extras sich besorgen und Haustiere führen, die allesamt spezielle Fähigkeiten besitzen.

Technik
Ich nenne diese Abteilung nicht Grafik, weil Castle Crashers jetzt keine Augenweide, aber ein stimmes Gesamtbild ist. Man versteht die Gestiken, lacht über die ulkigen Mimiken und kann sich ganz in dieser humorvollen Welt verlieren. 
Die Steuerung des XBox-360-Controllers (der beste meiner Meinung nach) ist präzise und gut belegt.
Der Soundtrack packt einen sofort und schon der Startbildschirm verheißt ein episches Abenteuer.

Fazit
Castle Crashers ist etwas für einen langen Abend, eine LAN-Partie, als kleines Projekt für Zwischendurch. Mit 4-5 Stunden Spielzeit ist es nicht lange, aber jede Minute kostet man gerne aus und auch beim wiederholten Spielen mit meinen Freunden hat Castle Crashers Spaß gemacht. Natürlich gibt es noch einen Game+ Modus und viele Sachen zum Freispielen, aber das hat mich nie gereizt. 
Wer Freunde hat, einen schönen Abend verbringen möchte und nicht zum wiederholten Male irgendeine Triologie sich auf dem Fernsehr anschauen möchte, der ist mit Castle-Crashers gut bedient (Sowie jeder mit einem guten Funken Humor).

The best things in life don't come easy.  You value it more , if you need to work for it.  I purchased this game in June and couldn't get it to run on my laptop but I had invested $20 and I wanted to play the game so I spent the first few hours troubleshooting, Googling and ended up installing a bunch of software to upgrade my drivers and I got the game to run!

Next, I logged on to a private PVE server and then spent 30 min, running around and dieing every time I ran into a new dino.  My heart pumped every time something dangerous jumped out at me. I swung wildly, I punched, I tried to fight back, I lost all my stuff over and over again.  All this time I was learning, picking up valualbe survival knowledge.  I developed a blood grudge against Megaladons, I spent an entire afternoon trying to stab them from a rock on the beach.  I couldn't get them at level 8 but I didn't forget and I came back later and went to town on them :)

Next, I tried a PVP server, I logged on and was frightened of the people immediately, I was soft and plushy, they had flak armour.  Luckily, the first people I met were friendly.  They took me in, offered some friendly advice and invited me to thier clan.  I accepted because I figured, if I didn't they might turn on me.  They showed me their impressive stone and metal base, it felt safe.  They had been building it since day 1 of the game release.  A few hours later, I was there to witness their complete destruction when a rival clan came and used C4 to demolish them.  At level 6, I could only watch and bare witness.  I felt terrible for them though.  I learned PVP isn't my thing.  I prefer PVE servers.  

Then came survival of the fittest and I tested all that I had learned against other players.  Top finish so far, third, I still mean to win one these days!

After 280 hours of emotional ups and downs and heart pounding survival momements - this game is still a thrill and the first few hours of troubleshooting to get it to run ain't nothing.  Glad I stuck with it.

I run this game on a Laptop
Intel i7 2.8Ghz
16 Gb Ram
AMD Radeon HD 7700
I run it on mostly low with some medium settings.  The graphics in the trailer are epic and I would love to be able to run it on epic but the thrill of the game is in the gameplay - the epic graphics would be gravy.

Developers, thanks for working your buns off, I love this game.  Would love to know about your SDLC,  I work in a corp dev shop and would love to find out how you get as much content out, as fas as you do, with 10 devs.

Euro Truck Simulator 2, não é só um simulador de direção, além das missões de fazer entregas, você passa por condições reais de transito, como multas por excesso de velocidade, ultrapassagens indevidas, sinal vermelho, fora também abastecer o Truck, conserta-lo, melhorar seu desempenho, quanto mais entregas fizer, aumenta sua reputação, podendo assim, comprar Trucks mais fortes e irados, contratar outros motoristas para trabalhar para você, enfim é o melhor, fora ainda os gráficos são ótimos, comprem vocês não se arrependeram ! Que dire, le jeu provoque soit une haine indicible, soit un plaisir fou. Spoiler, je fais parti des gens qui ont aimé.

Le jeu est à faire comme on fait un RPG à l'ancienne. Prévoir du temps pour préparer ses personnages comme un RPG papier,
ou déleguer se travail aux très bon tutoriels qui existent sur le net pour monter ses perso level après level.(cherchez neoseeker-Pathfinder)

Si vous y allez comme des bourrins,  sans monter vos personnages en réfléchissant (ou par tuto), vous allez vous casser les dents. ce jeu est respectueux des règles du jeu papier. l'exemple le plus frappant? vous pouvez rater un event parce que vous n'avez pas une corde dans votre sac ! Vous ne pouvez vous reposer en donjon sans rations etc.... c'est super <3

j'ai pris 102 heures à finir le jeu, avec un ending presque parfait. level 18/20 à la fin. 

Point forts : Très bonne durée de vie, Des quêtes passionnantes, un bestiaire interessant. Une vrai difficulté par moment. Gros coup de coeur pour la quantité de ligne de dialogue, et le lore très bien foutu.

Point faible : 
- Vous pouvez arriver à la fin du jeu et perdre tout vos compagnons si vous ne faites pas ce qu'il faut durant leurs quêtes. Les finir ne suffit pas, il faut les finir COMME LE DECIDE OWLCAT. (chercher comment sauver ses compagnons avant de commencer le jeu).

-Gros moments sans grand chose à faire a part les quêtes "royaume". Pas un problème en soit, mais passer deux heures à passer les jours avant la prochaine malédiction...moyen.

- le dernier donjon est horriblement ******* sans soluce. sérieusement. Regardez une soluce avant.

Conclusion : j'ai adoré, c'était super, et frustrant par moment. Un digne héritier des baldur's , malgré des moments creux, et une fin horrible si non préparé en amont.

PS : si vous développez correctement votre royaume et votre argent vous n'aurez aucun problème. J'ai fini a 6000+BP et 2Millions de Gils. (127BP par semaine)

Le jeu s'étale sur plusieurs années ingame, faites en priorité les quêtes principales, et ensuite explorez !

Bon courage, vous pouvez le faire !

Well, now it is a release game, I must admit it is not a game with a release quality, so if I had some hope during its early access, now it's done. This game is totally unfinished, broken.
The only things that works some are the landscape, which is beautifull with several bioms like snow, desert, swamp, forest, and some (but not all) dinos are well made too, in design and animation. The main music is quite good too. 
There's two distinctive modes in the game : pvp (player vs player), you will die quickly by snipers or by T-Rex tamed by players, and pve (player vs dinos), on wich you will safely take all your time to tame and raise dinos and to build your base, but the game mechanics are broken : 

- players put PILLARS everywhere to claim lands, so you can not build your base,

- you must tame and breed lots of dinos to fight other players or to fight some dinos boss, but it will take you A LOT of your REAL TIME to manage and take care of them, giving them food, breeding them, if not your dinos will die, and your base will be erased,

- you must FARM A LOT of material to construct a decent base, in metal in pvp, at least in stone in pve, that take lot of time, and there's a timer that destroy your base if you don't connect to the game,

- then if you go away for a week, all your glass constructions will be LOST because of this TIMER that destroy your stuff if you are not connected in a short period of time, so you will be litterally enslaved by the game, if you want to keep to maintain your great base, 

- on a non-isolated server (there's isolated - server to server transerfs are disabled - and non-isolated servers), tribes can transfers and travels to other servers, so in pvp your base will be raid soon or late, and you will loose all your stuff, even if you got the best defenses,

- lot of dinos are too badly rendered, like in a bad indy game, there's no real AI, big dinos will be stuck in the landscape, on a rock, in a tree... 

- linux version sucks, with lot of glitch and missing textures,

- pve mode is really boring after a while, when you have finished to build your base, and pvp mode is unplayable when some players are overpowered (op) and don't let you play,

- this game will waste a lot of your time. You can not safely put time in it, on official servers, but you can buy your own server, if you like to pay a monthly fee and to play alone or with your friends only. 

So the overall review for this released game is it doesn't worth the price, because the quality is not there. It lack at least 2 years of developpement, compare with some other AAA games of the same price. Lot of review are positive, but they don't have look this game in his broken deepness. 

I had lot of fun during first periods of the game though, in early access, one year ago, when pvp was playable, when tribes couldn't rush others servers, I enjoy lot of hours on it, but it wasn't the same game. In current state of play, don't invest all your time in it, you will regret it.

Great game if you have a friend to play with. I think it is pretty important that you play this with the same person through the whole game, specially the first time you finish it. It is a wonderful experience of trying to understand each others descriptions, something we don't usually do anymore since if we are having a hard time describing something, we just google it or show the other person an image of the thing we are speaking. 

If you really want to live the experience, I recommend you not to use guides at all. Try to figure things out, if you get stuck, give it a pause and try again the next day. It will give you a different approach to the problem you're facing.

Replayability: There is some randomness in the order certain elements are presented (which are key to the game) which gives a certain element of replayability, but the really difficult part of the game is getting to an agreement on the descriptions you make. So basically once you have established with a friend that the weird looking figure that has a "sort of head" is going the be named by you and the other player the "fish" it is easier to figure things.

Recommended even on full plrice.

I could not be happier with how this game turned out! Granted, a few things could be improved, but overall it's fantastic. The graphics are incredible and runs very smoothly, the coaster creation is incredible and quite easy to get a hang of and the scenery options are vast! The amount of detail in this game is just mind boggling. Now, I would like to see more variety of rides in the future as there aren't really all that much here (not as much as previous 'Frontier' games). Now, the one gripe I have with Planet Coaster is the management side of things...it's not a deal breaker for me because the main reason I play games like this is for the creative aspect, but I can see how that if you enjoy management, this could be a problem. The management is not as in depth as the older RCT games and the menus are tedious. You can't change wages of all staff from one screen, you have to select each staff member individually to adjust. And the same applies to prices of food and drink etc. I would love to see Frontier expand on this! 
But as I said, for me the most important aspect of a game like this is the ability to create wonderful looking parks and exciting rollercoasters, and Planet Coaster does this incredibly well.

Et bien c'est l'une des plus amples simulations militaire (pour l'heure !), complexe, punitive, dynamique comme passive.

Ce n'est pas une licence Blockbusterisée ou vous sauterez sur les murs en tuant tout ce qui passe devant votre gatling pour avoir un score de 100 frags pour 3 vies perdues ! Non, vous allez faire se que vous dit les QG, vous allez marcher, courir, repérer, ramper, et sans doute mourir plusieurs fois avant de comprendre qu'un tir se calcule, et qu'une balle perdue est vite arrivée ! 

Ce n'est pas un jeu pour tout le monde, il faut le reconnaître, comme dit plus haut, il y faudra du temps et de la patience, et un long passage par l'apprentissage des nombreuses mécaniques de gameplay que peut fournir ce soft. 

En outre de campagnes qui vous feront faire votre sport de la semaine, le jeu dispose d'un énorme mode "bac à sable" qui vous permet de créer aussi bien vos missions que de vous amuser à créer des batailles épiques ! Sans compter le multijoueur, car malgré la jouabilité infinie, pour celui qui se satisfait de ses propres conceptions mais aussi de celle de la multitude de mods et scénarios fournie par la communauté mondiale de ce jeu, l'IA ne vous apportera au final que très peu d'intérêt, étant soumise à des scripts basiques les rendant parfois soit "trop intélligent" et vous collant une balle à 300 mètres, soit débile et s'allongeant au sol devant une fenêtre en faisant des cibles trop faciles et incompréhensibles. 

Donc le multi : Join the army, et opérez ensemble, de manière tactique en stressant au moindre coup de feu de l'opposition, qui peut être évité grace à une reconnaissance efficace et à une unité coordonnée.

En bref, un très bon jeu, avec ses défauts, comme des graphismes qui prennent du coup dans les dents à chaque nouvelles sorties, des mécaniques parfois (trop) complexes, une IA qui manque d'humanité (lulz).

I feel kind of bad saying I recommend this game, not because I dislike it, but because I disagree with the overall design. The character, music and presentation are excellent, and as a Sokoban-type game it's a nice, clever and engaging member of that genre. However, the game starts off being something you can be patient with and take your time solving and even skip puzzles, but then for the last part of the game it decides it actually wants to be a punishing reflex-based game about dodging obstacles that flash in very quickly and that really isn't what it presented itself as.

I don't have anything against the type of game Helltaker became at the end, and I think the genre bait-and-switch could have been done well, but the problem for me was that the game kept the same single move in one direction control scheme from the puzzle sections- that form of control is designed for precise measured movement in a stationary position, so suddenly having to use it to navigate in multiple directions while on a moving conveyor belt in a hurry is very confusing and annoying, and since you only have four hit-points it just turns into a bunch of deaths and a very tedious, IMO unfun finale. 

Again, I don't mind that sort of game trick, but I think it could have been done better and as someone who was enjoying the sokoban puzzles I was pretty annoyed.

Still, this is a good game and it's free, so I can't not recommend it as a whole. It's fun, inviting and I'm sure most people will probably enjoy the switch of genre anyway. I'm definitely not a majority here. It's free, so download it and make up your own mind I guess.

[u] What changed compared to the 2016 version : [/u]
- A lot of new abilities were added like climbing walls and the dash, that really help increasing the verticality of the game
- New game mechanics like chainsaw for ammo, glory kill for health and fire for armor. Those three little things really add a lot of action into the game
- New designs for the demons,  they look a lot more like the originals 
- The story is longer ( Finished the game in 15-20h ) and you get more details about the Slayer himself..

[u] The + [/u]
- The codex allows you to know more about the story and the different characters
- A lot of different ennemies (much more than the 2016 game)
- Once you finish the campaign, you can still replay missions and try to find items or secrets you missed, complete milestones or play the new Battlemode multiplayer, which is basically 2 demons vs 1 slayer.
- Your Slayer skin appears in cutscenes, that is still a nice detail
- Good optimization. Minimum specs said I would only be able to run in low settings but I can actually run it in high with some stuff on higher settings.
-If your game crashes you still get your progression saved, even in UltraNightmare mode, I crashed in a boss fight because I forgot stuff were running in the background, when I opened the game, my save wasn't deleted and I could resume.

- Game sometimes crashes in the menu
- Some skins are not displayed in the Battlemode Lobby
-Peer to Peer, so everyone lags, all the time in multiplayer, impossible to play
-Matches aren't balanced at all, I always play against lvl 200+ slayers but with a lvl 4-10 teammate...
