Being able to ride the monsters, swing around environments and jump off walls/ledges makes me feel like I'm doing parkour while fighting these beasts. WARNING this game is challenging if you are not familiar with Monster Hunter games. It does have some repetition to it but just enough to make it worthwhile and not frustrating. Alright, so this is my review on Doki Doki Literature Club.

I'm gonna try my damndest to not spoil a single thing, but it's kinda hard not to when all the memes for the game are direct spoilers for they key moments in the game.

So whats the plot? The plot is as follows: it's 4 days before a school festival, and the protagonist (he is the name you give to him) hasn't joined a club yet. His childhood friend Sayori goes and convinces him to join the literature club with 3 other students. The club is ran by Monika, with Sayori being vice president, along with the 2 members of the club being Yuri and Natsuki. On the first day, Monika assigns everyone with the task of writing a poem, and this is where the choices come into play where you select words that allign with the character's personalities. After a few days, it is brought up that they need to prepare for the festival, and you get to choose a girl to help out in the preperations of the festival.

It as at this point, regretably, where the plot cannot be discussed. on the 4th and final days result is plot heavy events that if I were to state what happens would spoil the game and the overall experience.

So, what does the game have going for itself? Well, It has a metanarative that goes on throughout the game, and weird glitches and oddities all within the game causes strange events to occur. The gameplay is stupidly simple, due to the game being a dating sim with no real effort needed.

So what do I not like about the game? Well, the whole metanarative isn't as fleshed out as I think it should. It is there and entertaining for what it is, but from an experimental perspective where various things hint to the game being more versatile than what it actually is results in a disapointing ARG-like game. Alright, just a small spoiler, but when you install the game and look inside the game's folders, you find a folder labeled "Characters" with every character's name in the literature club. This has more relevancy later on within the game, it's just that it isn't that great when you have a mechanic that has so much potential used in such a limited way to convey storytelling. I get that would've made the game take long to make, but I think the extra effort of making the characters alterable would be a neat medium of storytelling.

Do I recommend the game? Well yes, I think you should play it. It's free, so the only price is the time you spend playing it, and if you like to experience shock and awe, then this game will be the game for you.

[h1][b]The Better Sequel[/b][/h1]

I was a newcomer to the XCOM series, picking up Enemy Within during the summer sale last year. I was quickly engrossed by the game's mechanics, and when I found out a sequel had been announced I knew I'd have to jump on it. With a massive expansion pack and some other add-ons released now, as well as several patches to fix up the problems, I believe it's just about time to take an in-depth look at the latest product of Firaxis Games.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
The most immediately apparent improvement in XCOM 2 is the visual design. XCOM: Enemy Unknown had a distinct art style, but it didn't appeal much to me and the game itself also just didn't look that great because of its low level of detail. There are almost no such issues here. Your troops have relatively realistic proportions, their weapons are properly sized, and the models and textures themselves have improved greatly. This extends to your opponents, as well; each of which receive a fantastic face-lift. The animations are relatively fluid, and XCOM 2 also offers a host of new customization options for making every XCOM trooper feel just a little more unique and personal. The environments are also much more detailed than they were before. Utopian cityscapes maintain an eerie sterility, which contrasts with the wilderness of the cold wastelands of Siberia and the unbearable heat of the Sahara. XCOM 2 definitely earns itself some praise here, and really raises the bar in its genre, even if it isn't groundbreaking.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2180877183

[h1]Audio[/h1]
Another big improvement in presentation over Enemy Unknown for XCOM 2, audio design has been greatly enhanced. Each environment features appropriate ambient sounds, adding to the suspense before you engage. Your enemies all have unique responses to whatever situation they're presented with, from the hiss of a Sectoid to the Earth-shattering stomp of a Sectopod. XCOM's own weapons all sound satisfying, and there are a variety of options for your troopers' voices. Voice acting is of similar quality to that found in Enemy Unknown; while I hoped for an improvement it is still perfectly acceptable. One of my favorite parts of Enemy Unknown's audiovisual presentation was the soundtrack, and I am once again impressed by XCOM 2. The base game's music is good, and one of the most recent updates adds an optional suite of synth music as well - and [i]that[/i] music is great.

[h1]Performance[/h1]
I'm afraid that this is going to have to be the low point of the review. XCOM 2 still doesn't perform great, even on a PC that exceeds the recommended requirements by a great deal. It's very unfortunate that this game suffers from such lackluster performance, as it drags down an otherwise well-rounded performance from Firaxis Games. With that said, I haven't had many issues with crashing, but there are some bugs and glitches that have yet to be officially fixed. These aren't game-breaking in my experience, but they are very annoying. Fortunately, there are a variety of modifications on the Workshop which address almost all of these issues, but I would expect an official patch to have fixed these things by now.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
XCOM 2 shares many gameplay elements with its predecessor, Enemy Unknown, as you might expect. It is a turn-based tactics game focusing on the control of multiple troopers, and each of them have their own unique equipment and abilities. The game uses a two-moves-per-turn system; every unit has two available actions, and moving any amount within a radial area consumes one movement point; typically, activating abilities consumes one or two movement points, and firing always ends that unit's turn. This comes together very well, and makes for a game that is in-depth enough to excite while not being overly complex. There is a line-of-sight system which is used to reveal enemies and parts of the map, and a variety of units to choose from. These include ordinary humans, cloned government troopers, XCOM's own version of the krogan, xenomorph-like arachnoids, and massive bipedal robots. With this variety, it will take some time before one becomes bored of the game's cast.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2180877289

[h1]Singleplayer[/h1]
The singleplayer campaign of XCOM 2 places you in the shoes of the illusive Commander, a faceless strategic genius in charge of the XCOM organization. This time around, you eschew the underground command center in favor of a massive VTOL supply spacecraft, the Avenger. This mobile base completely overhauls the strategic world map, known as the Geoscape, forcing you to manage your resources carefully since the nations of the world have capitulated to the alien menace, ADVENT. You'll face these human enemies more often than not, but after you escalate and take the fight to ADVENT's strongholds, you'll encounter aliens more and more. Missions are similar to those of Enemy Unknown, but some enforce a turn limit before the mission fails, which is both challenging and aggravating. There are more ways to customize troops than before, as the classes from Enemy Unknown are replaced by five new ones. New technology and stat-boosting items provide various bonuses to troopers, giving players the edge they need to destroy ADVENT and incite a worldwide uprising. The singleplayer keeps you on your toes and threatens you with destruction, from start to finish. Most players will spend most of their time here, as it is the focus of the game.

[h1]Multiplayer[/h1]
XCOM 2 also features multiplayer, which allows for players to assemble a cadre of troops from both ADVENT, alien, and XCOM forces, with similar abilities to those of singleplayer units. There are a handful of map types to choose from, but the big issue with multiplayer is the lack of options. The adversarial gamemode quickly becomes uninteresting, and other ways to play would greatly improve the game. One idea is singleplayer gamemodes being introduced to multiplayer; one player must defend an objective, the other must destroy it; perhaps one player is attempting to defend a stronghold of civilian units against another. No matter how you look at it, more variety is needed for multiplayer, and as a result you probably won't spend a ton of time on it.

[h1]Community Content[/h1]
XCOM 2 earns fantastic praise here. A full suite of development tools, workshop integration, and bringing the Long War modding team in to work with Firaxis on XCOM 2 modding features shows how dedicated the developers were in their integration of community content support. Take one look at the workshop and you can already see a fantastic variety of modifications: New enemies to give you an even bigger challenge. A total overhaul to how the game is played, making it more like the previous XCOM games. A new weapon tier, or new weapon classes. And a host of new trooper voices and customization options, to scratch whatever science fiction itch you have. This plays a big part in my recommendation of the game.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2180877359

[h1]Verdict[/h1]
XCOM 2 is definitely a worthy sequel to the previous reboot, Enemy Unknown. While it takes a few steps back in some areas, its community content support takes many more steps forward. It changes enough to justify its purchase without changing too much from the XCOM formula, and once again sets the standard for the turn-based tactics genre. Though they might be put off by the performance issues, fans of strategy and tactics are sure to enjoy this title. I would just advise waiting for a sale, so you can pick this game up alongside its impressive expansion pack, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/593380/XCOM_2_War_of_the_Chosen/]War of the Chosen.[/url]

[b]I would recommend XCOM 2, but would suggest waiting for a sale.[/b]

Spring has come to the valley. The air smells of pine and jasmine. I walk out into my fields, the buds not quite ripened, but promising a good harvest in mere months. I hear my wife call my name from the steps of my house, my daughter clasped in her arms. I breathe in the air of this glorious life, and feel peaceful, serene, complete. Welcome to the Valley.

Okay, it is a romanticized, metaphorical experience, but in all truthfulness, Stardew Valley is one of the greatest games on Steam, if not in recent memory. On the surface, it is much like the classic Harvest Moon farming simulators of yesteryear, with a generous helping of the wondrous Rune Factory. One part marketing game, one part dating sim, one part action adventure. Together, these elements create a unique experience which has seldom, if ever, been matched. What I find most fascinating is the narrative interaction between your character and the townspeople. Their stories are surprisingly poignant, at times even dark, setting the stage for an evolving soap opera-esque story which unfolds depending on your choices. 

The reviews speak for themselves. Stardew Valley is both calming and exciting. An adventure in commerce, companionship, and courage. Sometimes, to escape the drudgery of daily life, you have to go back to basics. This game belongs in every Steam library. I'll see you in Stardew Valley!

I played first Insurgency, and I liked it. Fast time to kill, combination of sneaking and rushing, and satisfying weapons were nice change and a more "realistic" fast paced shooter.

It didn't drag me in and after around 80 hours I didn't come back. I ignored Sandstorm after nice comments from youtubers and nice reviews, and I can now say I was right.

This game is frustrating, there is zero team play, VoiP is only used to shout at the end of a round, weapons are imbalanced, you can't customize while waiting for map to change and numerous other frustrations.

They made some aspects realistic, like getting up from prone takes lots of time like you are carring a lot of equipment, or a heavy backpack, switching weapons takes ages, taking out and throwing a frag takes like 5 seconds, and you better have 2 guys covering for you while you do it.

Other things like running, jumping out of tall 2nd story windows, firing in quick succession with little to no recoil and other important things are just too arcadey and don't merge well with other aspects of gameplay.

Sound is off, only thing good about it is that the footsteps are loud but you can't orient yourself when someone is shooting at you and missing you.

Teammate recognition is slow and hard, and new players are teamkilling all the time.

The game is simply not worth it, unless it was free. I can't believe some people actually sink 1k or more hours into this shit.

r6 siege is far better game for instance, cs:go more balanced with similar trashtalking no teamplay community, SQUAD is much more realistic... there is no reason to play this game.

Игра с дикой динамикой и невероятной способностью поджаривать ж*пы. Как свои, так и противников. Играю, чтоб расслабиться и в волю нашпиговать патронами членов других команд. Периодически делаю это со своими тимейтами. Чисто случайно, честно.

Есть команда защитников, есть команда атакеров. Есть три режима игры. Захват контейнера, защита заложника и деактивация заряда. Есть три вида самой игры: рейтинг, анранкет и обычная игра. Есть еще и новичковая игра, которая будет недоступна после получения 50 уровня. У каждого оперативника есть свое оружие, свои вспомогательные гаджеты, как второстепенные и во многом схожие с другими оперативниками, так и основные, которые имеются только у определенные оперов. При защите, тебе дается время укрепить точку так, чтобы было удобно твоей команде и так, чтобы можно было задержать противников для атаки точки. Когда ты играешь за атакующую сторону, у тебя есть разведывательный дрон, который поможет сориентироваться тебе по карте и найти точку защитников. Так же в игре имеются камеры, местоположение которых тебе нужно будет запомнить. Понимать какие стены можно пробить, как и не укрепленные люки. Сложность игры в том, когда ты еще только знакомишься с ней у тебя будет люто пригорать (вообще, даже у людей, кто играет в эту игру уже давно тоже пригорает). Тебе будет ничего не понятно. Не волнуйся, игра подкинет тебе возможность посмотреть видео с обучением и лучше тебе его посмотреть, чтоб заработать дополнительную валюту для покупки новых оперативников.
Помимо опыта и валюты после окончания катки, тебе может выпасть пакет со скинами на оружие/шлем/костюм.

Вроде все, что нужно я объяснила, там на самом деле больше всяких тонкостей, но новичкам пока это не нужно. Однозначно советую!

Bardzo fajna gra, jak dla mnie najlepsza survivalowa gra. Kreskówkowa grafika która nadaje grze wyjątkowy klimat oraz równie klimatyczny soundtrack. W Don't Starve trafiamy do świata stworzonego przez mrocznego Maxwella, w którym czycha na nas wiele niebezpieczeństw od zwykłych psów gończych po giganty jak np. jelenicyklop. Najważniejszym celem gry jak wzkazuje na to sam tytuł jest nie umrzeć z głodu. Musiemy więc zdobywać pożywienie zbierając jagody, zabijając dzikie stworzenia itp. Zdobyte jedzenie można również przetwarzać aby zwiększyć jego atrybuty albo przedłużyć termin przydatności do spożycia co można uzyskać przechowując jedzenie w lodówce. Musimy również dbać o dwa pozostałe współczynniki czyli zdrowie i zdrowie psychiczne. Możemy również eksplorować podziemne jaskinie i ruiny w poszukiwaniu nowych potworów, przedmiotów i przygód. Podsumowując, dla każdego kto lubi gry survivalowe Don't Starve to pozycja obowiązkowa. Podczas obecnie niemalże stu godzin rozgrywki nie dopatrzyłem się żadnych większych wad. Jedyną wadą może być to że na samym początku póki nie zdobędziemy doświadczenia gra może wydawać się bardzo trudna jednak z czasem stanie się tylko trudna :) Serdecznie polecam!

For the sceptics out there... I had literally 0 problems with the setup or performance of the game. I dont have an over the top gaming PC (Specs: GPU GTX 680, CPU i7-4960k, Memory 16GB) and the game is running at 60-85 fps for the most part (sometimes 50 fps in extremely highly concentrated areas).

For the gameplay, I find it extremely intriguing. If you expected a survival garther exploration game with an element of possible multiplayer, you WILL NOT be disappointed. The gameplay feels extremely smooth, and the tasks that you get dont feel meaningless or boring. Each planet is extremely unique and some beautiful and some ugly. 

Overall this game has only disappointed me in the fact that all my friends are complaining that they cant get above 30 fps, which in a covex voxel game is unheard.. Paying 60€ for something that literally runs like a fat guy who realised there were donuts for only 1.99$..

Dont buy the game if:
-You have a very low end pc
-You arent very patient, or dont find scenery and lore interesting
-You cannot handle losing some of your stuff in a heated space battle
-You do not want to follow the story, if you want to just explore then it might get boring pretty quickly.

Overall I would recommend it to someone like me, but if you fall under the 5 points above, dont buy it.
